# Lucia 0.8B v1.2-nc: Qwen3.5-0.8B, think symbolic image (non-commercial)

**Lucia 0.8B v1.2-nc** is the non-commercial sibling of [Lucia 0.8B v1.2](https://huggingface.co/AbstractPhil/qwen3.5-0.8b-think-symbolic-image): a LoRA adapter of
[Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B) that looks at a picture and writes a reading of it, a short chain of
plain-language thoughts, one named step per line, then the wordings (a caption, a prompt, tags, a critique, by depth), then the
questions a careful looker would still ask, each with its answer and what settles it. She is the smallest of the Lucia family. Version 1.2-nc is the recipe of
[Lucia 4B v1.2-nc](https://huggingface.co/AbstractPhil/qwen3.5-4b-think-symbolic-image-nc) at 0.8B: the same rows, taught
once, with a second objective that keeps her near her base model.

**One bar missed: she finishes fewer of her other answers.** Of the bars set for this release before she was read, she missed one: the share of her answers to ordinary questions and text requests that end. Of 328 such held-out requests, she finishes 283 (86.3%) within 512 new tokens, where the bar asks for 291 (the base model's 90.5%, less 2 points). 8 of her answers fall into a repetition loop (7 of them answers to text requests; the base model: 1; Lucia 0.8B v1.2: 2) and 37 run to the 512-token limit while still writing (the base model: 30); with the adapter at half strength (its weights scaled by 0.5), 288 finish. What it means for use: on some general questions, most of them text requests, she can repeat herself until the limit, so set `max_new_tokens` to what the answer needs when you ask her anything other than a reading: a limit ends a loop, it does not prevent one. Her readings end: asked in the same read for a reading of each of 185 held-out pictures, she ended every one within the 800 new tokens it allows. Beside the miss, what the non-commercial rows bring her: her long look names a word the picture shows for 176 of 245 held-out pictures with readable lettering, 0.72 of them (Lucia 0.8B v1.2: 103, 0.42; the base model: 20, 0.08).

- **More than eight times the rows.** She was taught 184,562 rows (version 1: 20,836), the rows Lucia 4B v1.2-nc was taught:
  [release 5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned/tree/cac40b93d7b063aafd0cb70d3c1b1a7a100562ef) of [thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned),
  its Apache-2.0 part and its non-commercial part together (185,356 rows), less 660 rows on the pictures the
  reads below hold out and 134 rows whose pictures no store holds. The non-commercial part holds readings written
  with the picture in view: COCO 2017 photographs (each under its Flickr author's license, most of them non-commercial), FFHQ
  photographs (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and DeepFashion-MultiModal pictures (non-commercial research use). The rows were written by
  OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek models and admitted by a blind review; 41,231 of them are long looks. No row she was taught
  was written by a Claude model, or by any model of this project trained on rows a Claude model wrote.
- **One pass.** She was taught her rows once (21,815 steps); version 1 was taught hers twice (2,724 steps).
- **The base model kept**, as in Lucia 0.8B v1.2: a second objective in training holds her next-word choices near
  Qwen3.5-0.8B's on ordinary requests that Qwen3.5-0.8B answered itself for version 1.2, so the adapter changes how she
  answers when asked for a reading and little else, though fewer of her other answers end (the caveat above). On held-out ordinary requests she stays close to the base
  model, and of the questions and text requests among them she answers none in the reading's form; version 1, trained without it, answers
  267 of the 328 that way.
- **Lettering in the long look.** Of 300 held-out pictures with readable lettering, a screen found no person's name, credit or
  web address in the lettering of 245. Of those 245, her long look names a word the picture shows for 176
  (Lucia 0.8B v1.2: 103; version 1: 95; the base model, which copies the request's question line: 20). Her closer look names one for
  62 (Lucia 0.8B v1.2: 61), and for 86 when the request asks for the visible text (below). Asked
  directly what the lettering says, for 214 of those 245, her answer names it more often than the base model's does
  (0.87 of them against 0.82).

# MiniMax-H3（视频 Ref2VA）NVFP4 W4A4 量化权重 —— RTX 50 系

MiniMax H3 视频主干（Ref2VA transformer）的**离线 NVFP4(E2M1) W4A4** 量化版：
BF16 **66.28GB → 37.48GB**，配合 NVFP4 张量核在 **RTX 5070 12GB** 上跑通参考图生视频（含音轨）。

- 引擎 / 使用手册 / 实测样片：**https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Xanyiyan/H3-FP4-5070**
- 源码：https://github.com/xuanyiyanyuyin/ai-pipeline/tree/main/h3_fp4
- 仅适用于 **NVIDIA Blackwell（sm120，RTX 50 系）**；40 系及更早、AMD 无 FP4 张量核

> 本仓库是官方权重的**量化衍生版（Model Derivatives）**，按 MiniMax H3 社区许可分发（见 LICENSE 与 NOTICE）。
> 本仓库**不包含**：文本编码器（Qwen3-VL，63GB）、video_vae、audio_vae、tokenizer/processor/scheduler ——
> 这些请从官方 `MiniMax/MiniMax-H3` 获取（合计约 10.4GB + 文本编码器 63GB）。

## 文件

```
transformer/
  model-00001-of-00013.safetensors ... model-00013-of-00013.safetensors   # ≈36GB
  adaln_cache.safetensors        # 默认档
  adaln_cache_s2/s4/s8/s20.safetensors   # 对应 steps 的 AdaLN t 键缓存
  fp4_manifest.json              # 量化清单（哪些张量被量化/保留）
```

## 量化口径

- 量化：FFN fc1/fc2 + attn qkv/out；per-16 block scale（FP8）+ tensor-wise global scale
- 保留 BF16/FP32：AdaLN / norm / embed / 输出头 / patchify（26GB 保留权重）
- 实际 FP4 核心仅 **11.3GB**；AdaLN 预计算后每步实际流式读取 ≈**11.5GB**
- 量化损失（往返 relL2）：k1 9.4–9.6%（E2M1 固有地板）；k2 套娃 0.86%；k3 0.078%

## 用法

1. 官方权重就位：`models/MiniMax-H3/Ref2VA/{video_vae,audio_vae,text_encoder,processor,tokenizer,scheduler,audio_scheduler}`
2. 本仓库放到：`models/MiniMax-H3-FP4/transformer/`（14 个文件原样）
3. 跑：

```bash
# turbo8（124 帧 / 512²）
python code/h3_video_job.py --ref ref.png --cond h3_cond_ref.pt --steps 8 --turbo 8 --frames 124 --size 512 --out out.mp4

# 标准 20 步
python code/h3_video_job.py --ref ref.png --cond h3_cond_ref.pt --steps 20 --frames 124 --size 512 --out out.mp4
```

**steps 必须与 adaLN 缓存档位匹配**（2/4/8/20）；引擎会按实际 `--steps` 自动建/复用缓存，错配（用别的 steps 配旧缓存）会出 confetti 垃圾。

## 实测（RTX 5070 12GB，2026-11）

| 配置 | 时间 |
|---|---|
| 124f / 512² turbo8（8 步） | ≈203s/条（首帧锁定，L1 0.037） |
| 124f / 512² 20 步 | ≈284s（单步 11.88s：quant 10.5% / attn 60.3%） |
| 2K 22f tile1024 ov0 | 单步 51s |
| 4K 22f tile1024 ov0 | 单步 173s + VAE 解码 ~945s |
| BF16 对照（同配置 20 步） | ≈30 分钟 ⇒ FP4 ≈6× |

16GB / ≥24GB 卡：显存越大驻留越高、速度越快（32GB 卡可全驻留，2K/4K 免降档）。

# MiniMax-H3 Prompt Rewriter (FL2VA)

This model rewrites prompts for MiniMax-H3 video and audio generation. It supports
text-only prompts and optional first/last-frame images.

This model was trained through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of
[Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B).

## Setup

Use a Python environment with vLLM and GPU support on the server:

```bash
pip install vllm requests pillow qwen-vl-utils
```

All scripts use `python` from the active environment. The writing guide is included
in this directory.

## Run

1. Check `MODEL_PATH` and GPU settings in `vllm_server.sh`, then start the server:

   ```bash
   bash vllm_server.sh
   ```

2. In another terminal, edit `post_vllm.sh`: set `PROMPT`, `TASK_TYPE`, `DURATION`,
   and any image paths, then run:

   ```bash
   bash post_vllm.sh
   ```

| Task | Required images |
| --- | --- |
| `T2VA` | None |
| `I2VA` | `FIRST_IMAGE` |
| `L2VA` | `LAST_IMAGE` |
| `FL2VA` | `FIRST_IMAGE` and `LAST_IMAGE` |

Image paths must be absolute. Keep client `MODEL` and `SERVER_URL` aligned with
the server's `MODEL_NAME`, `HOST`, and `PORT`. Commands above assume this directory
is the working directory; the scripts also accept absolute paths from elsewhere.

Both example servers use GPU 0 and port 8000. To run both models at once, assign
separate GPUs and ports and update each client's `SERVER_URL`.
The 32768-token context includes the input and output; the output limit is 16384.

The client saves the enhanced prompt, reasoning, input, generation parameters,
usage, and timing to `infer_outputs/result.json`, overwriting an existing file.
Run `python post_vllm.py --help` for all options.

## Latest release: Episode MA50 v2

**What changed:** Same 50/50 FL-Singularity blend. V2 uses stock FL timestep conditioning in place of Singularity’s.

**What improved:** In LoRA tests with Pika Flex FL and DMAD H3 8-step, v2 followed the trained action more closely and produced cleaner, more natural-looking footage with fewer gritty artifacts than v1.

---

# MiniMax H3 FL-Singularity

An experimental, reference-capable MiniMax H3 merge. It pairs the visual clarity and quality of FL’s original CFG distillation with Singularity’s natural lighting and textures, more expressive movement, and better facial detail in medium and long shots. The aim is less waxiness than FL and less blur than standalone Singularity. The merge supports reference-conditioned generation and first/last-frame workflows.

These are modified weights assembled from existing checkpoints, not a separately trained model.

## What changed

**Attention and MLPs:** All 50 main transformer blocks use a 50/50 blend of FL and Singularity for these four projection weights:

```text
blocks.<0..49>.attn.qkv_proj.weight
blocks.<0..49>.attn.out_proj.weight
blocks.<0..49>.mlp.fc1.weight
blocks.<0..49>.mlp.fc2.weight
```

The blend is `FL + 0.5 × (Singularity − FL)`, calculated in FP32 and rounded to BF16 before quantization. Native tensor ordering is retained. Singularity’s leading `model.diffusion_model.` key prefix is removed to match the FL tensor names.

**Retained from FL:** The conditioning projection, both token-refiner blocks, normalization gains, video and audio input/output projections, and rotary frequencies are copied unchanged from stock FL.

Two variants are offered. They differ only in which model supplies the timestep conditioning (AdaLN).

### MA50 v2 FL AdaLN

- `episode-h3-fl-singularity-ma50-v2-fl-adaln-int8.safetensors`
- `episode-h3-fl-singularity-ma50-v2-fl-adaln-w6a8.safetensors`

Retains stock FL’s timestep table and AdaLN projections, making it a closer match for LoRA stacks that expect FL conditioning.

### MA50 v1 Singularity AdaLN

- `episode-h3-fl-singularity-ma50-v1-sing-adaln-int8.safetensors`
- `episode-h3-fl-singularity-ma50-v1-sing-adaln-w6a8.safetensors`

The original MA50 release keeps Singularity’s timestep conditioning, making it a closer match for LoRAs trained on Singularity.

**Turbo adapters:** Pika Flex FL and [DMAD H3 8-step](https://huggingface.co/ZhengmingYu/DMAD/blob/main/minimax_h3/dmad_minimax_h3_8step_full_critic_comfyui.safetensors) worked well on both versions.

## Sources

From [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 at the build revision](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/54472221d27c695fca9621b0c3ed52f06c4af707/diffusion_models):

- `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_bf16.safetensors` — floating FL weights for the blend.
- `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` — deployment base. Untouched tensors are retained byte-for-byte.

From [WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity at the build revision](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity/tree/1259cf16cd0b655ba691a32fb46a409142762972):

- `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_bf16.safetensors` — floating attention and MLP donor.
- `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_pruned_int8.safetensors` — timestep conditioning for MA50 v1.

## Checkpoint naming

`episode-h3-fl-singularity-maNN-vN-{fl|sing}-adaln-{int8|w6a8}.safetensors`

- `maNN` gives the Singularity percentage in the main MLP and attention projections. For example, `ma50` means 50% Singularity and 50% FL.
- `vN` numbers weight releases within that blend. A new ratio starts its own `v1`. README edits and preference changes do not bump the weight version.
- `fl-adaln` or `sing-adaln` identifies the timestep-conditioning source. Checkpoint files are available in both INT8 and W6A8. ConvRot details are documented below rather than repeated in the filename.

## Weight construction

Only the 200 blended main-block projection matrices are converted to INT8 ConvRot, replacing their weights and per-row scales in the deployed FL base. The conversion uses [Comfy-Org’s quantizer at this revision](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-model-tools/blob/d6797787e6bdb1a1fb0094d588a26f8e71a1c757/quant_int8_convrot.py): group size 256, per-row absmax scaling, CPU FP32 arithmetic, 256 complete rows per chunk, and `mseclip=False`.

MA50 v2 retains FL’s `adaln_t_table` and matching projections. MA50 v1 copies all 103 timestep-conditioning tensors from Singularity: the timestep table, all 50 blocks’ `adaln_proj.linear.weight` and `.bias`, and the final layer’s corresponding weight and bias. The donor values and dtypes are preserved.

# Lucia 0.8B v1.2: Qwen3.5-0.8B, think symbolic image

**Lucia 0.8B v1.2** is a LoRA adapter of [Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B) that looks at a picture
and writes a reading of it: a short chain of plain-language thoughts, one named step per line, then the wordings (a caption, a
prompt, tags, a critique, by depth), then the questions a careful looker would still ask, each with its answer and what settles
it. She is the smallest of the Lucia family. Version 1.2 is the recipe of
[Lucia 4B v1.2](https://huggingface.co/AbstractPhil/qwen3.5-4b-think-symbolic-image) at 0.8B: the same rows, taught once, with a
second objective that keeps her near her base model.

- **More than four times the rows.** She was taught 91,138 rows (version 1: 20,836), the rows Lucia 4B v1.2 was taught:
  the Apache-2.0 part of [release 5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned/tree/cac40b93d7b063aafd0cb70d3c1b1a7a100562ef) of [thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned)
  as anyone can read it there (95,481 rows), less 3,718 rows on COCO 2017 photographs under other licenses,
  609 rows on the pictures the reads below hold out and 16 rows whose pictures no store holds.
  They are readings of DOCCI and COCO 2017 photographs, of National Gallery of Art pictures and of drawn specifications, written
  by OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek models and admitted by a blind review; 30,250 of them are long looks. No row she was
  taught was written by a Claude model, or by any model of this project trained on rows a Claude model wrote. Training shows her
  the picture of every row about a picture (the drawn specifications have none), so the COCO 2017 photographs she saw are only
  those whose Flickr authors gave them the Attribution license or that carry no known copyright restrictions, in her rows and in
  the ordinary requests below alike.
- **One pass.** She was taught her rows once (10,137 steps); version 1 was taught hers twice (2,724 steps).
- **The base model kept**, new at 0.8B: a second objective in training holds her next-word choices near Qwen3.5-0.8B's on
  ordinary requests that Qwen3.5-0.8B answered itself for this version, so the adapter changes how she answers when asked for a
  reading and little else. On held-out ordinary requests she stays close to the base model, and of the questions and text
  requests among them she answers none in the reading's form; version 1, trained without it, answers 267 of the 328 that way.
- **Lettering seldom in the closer look.** Of 300 held-out pictures with readable lettering, a screen found no person's name,
  credit or web address in the lettering of 245. Of those 245, her closer look names a word the picture shows for
  61, where the base model, which given the same request copies the request's question line instead of describing the picture, names one for 13; her long look names one for
  103. Asked directly what the lettering says, for 214 of those 245, her answer names it about as often as the
  base model's does (0.84 of them against 0.82).

Version 1 stays in this repository at the tag `lucia-v1`.

What she writes for a closer look at a held-out COCO 2017 photograph ([376084](https://cocodataset.org/#explore?id=376084), its author's Attribution license), verbatim:

```
see: One yellow truck is parked at the center of the frame, with orange cones around it.
relate: The truck is left of the fence, and the fence is right of the motorcycle.
mood: The truck's parked state suggests a gentle pause.
caption: A yellow truck is parked at the center of the frame, left of a fence and right of a motorcycle.
prompt: yellow truck parked at center, orange cones around the truck, fence to the right of the motorcycle, photograph
tags: yellow truck, orange traffic cones, fence, motorcycle, photograph
question: thing name -> truck [record]
question: thing position -> centre [record]
question: rel1 b -> fence [record]
question: scene layout -> unknown [unknown]
```

The steps a chain may use, in the order a careful looker takes them: `see`, `name`, `place`, `count`, `relate`, `form`,
`light`, `colour`, `mood`, `mean`, `intend`, `story`, `compare`, `change`, `check`, `say`. A quick look holds 1 to 2 thoughts,
a closer look 3 to 5, a long look 6 to 10. Questions end in `[record]` (the answer is a fact of the picture), `[chain]` (the
chain worked it out) or `[unknown]`. The prompt line often opens with the kind of picture (a close-up photograph, an overhead
photograph); unlike version 1, she was not taught to open it that way every time.

# MiniMax-H3-Tiny for ComfyUI

[![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Page-2f6feb)](https://fuyi25.github.io/MiniMax-H3-Tiny/) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-MiniMax--H3--Tiny-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/fuyi25/MiniMax-H3-Tiny) [![Collection](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Collection-H3--Tiny-ffcc4d)](https://huggingface.co/collections/H3-Tiny/h3-tiny-v01-6afeea67147c27cf3b80820a)

H3-Tiny transformers repackaged as single-file checkpoints for ComfyUI's native MiniMax H3 support.
Part of **[H3-Tiny](https://github.com/fuyi25/MiniMax-H3-Tiny)**: structured pruning of MiniMax-H3 for joint video + audio
generation.

| Model | Workflow | Params | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| [MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-Pruned-Ref2VA](https://huggingface.co/H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-Pruned-Ref2VA) | Ref2VA | 17.05B | `minimax_h3_tiny_17b_ref2va_bf16.safetensors` · 34.2 GB |
| [MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-Pruned-FL2VA](https://huggingface.co/H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-Pruned-FL2VA) | FL2VA / T2VA | 17.05B | `minimax_h3_tiny_17b_fl2va_bf16.safetensors` · 34.2 GB |
| [MiniMax-H3-Tiny-14B-OKD-Ref2VA-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-14B-OKD-Ref2VA-v0.1) | Ref2VA | 13.98B | `minimax_h3_tiny_14b_okd_ref2va_bf16.safetensors` · 28.1 GB |
| [MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-FewStep-Ref2VA-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-FewStep-Ref2VA-v0.1) | Ref2VA | 17.08B | `minimax_h3_tiny_17b_fewstep_ref2va_bf16.safetensors` · 34.2 GB |

FewStep samples in 6 steps (4 or more work) and needs our nodes, see below; the others use 50 steps with stock ComfyUI.

These are the same weights as the diffusers checkpoints, in ComfyUI's key layout. ComfyUI reads the pruned depth and
FFN width from the tensors, so no custom node is needed.

## Usage

1. Put a file in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`.
2. Get the text encoder and VAEs from [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3):
   `text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_*.safetensors` → `models/text_encoders/`,
   `vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors` and `vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors` → `models/vae/`.
3. Open ComfyUI's MiniMax H3 workflow (`MiniMax H3 Image to Video` for FL2VA / T2VA, `MiniMax H3 Reference to Video`
   for Ref2VA) and select the H3-Tiny file in **Load Diffusion Model**.
4. Sample without the turbo LoRA: 50 steps, `simple` scheduler, guider without CFG (`BasicGuider`). We tested
   `euler`.

Use the `ref2va` file with the Reference to Video node and the `fl2va` file with the Image to Video node (with first
and last frames for FL2VA, without for T2VA).

We tested these files on ComfyUI commit `afcb984` (2026-11-21) at 1344×768 and 243 frames on one H200: the outputs
match our diffusers pipeline. The Comfy-Org turbo LoRAs were trained on the
33B model and are untested with H3-Tiny.

The files were made with [`scripts/convert_comfyui.py`](https://github.com/fuyi25/MiniMax-H3-Tiny/blob/main/scripts/convert_comfyui.py).
It writes AdaLN in ComfyUI's curve form (`adaln_t_table`), which reproduces the diffusers AdaLN to about 1e-10
relative error.

### FewStep

The few-step checkpoint also needs the step endpoint, which stock ComfyUI does not pass to the model. Install the
H3-Tiny nodes:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fuyi25/MiniMax-H3-Tiny
ln -s "$PWD/MiniMax-H3-Tiny/comfyui" ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Tiny
```

In the Reference to Video workflow, load the file with **H3-Tiny Few-Step Loader** instead of Load Diffusion Model,
and feed **H3-Tiny Few-Step Sigmas** (6 steps by default) to `SamplerCustomAdvanced`, with the `euler` sampler and
`BasicGuider`.

[![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Page-2f6feb)](https://fuyi25.github.io/MiniMax-H3-Tiny/) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-MiniMax--H3--Tiny-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/fuyi25/MiniMax-H3-Tiny) [![Collection](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Collection-H3--Tiny-ffcc4d)](https://huggingface.co/collections/H3-Tiny/h3-tiny-v01-6afeea67147c27cf3b80820a) [![ComfyUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/ComfyUI-Weights-f0883e)](https://huggingface.co/H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-ComfyUI)

Part of **[H3-Tiny](https://github.com/fuyi25/MiniMax-H3-Tiny)**: structured pruning of MiniMax-H3 for joint video + audio
generation. This checkpoint is the pruned version of the H3 transformer used for **FL2VA** (first + last frame to
video + audio) and **T2VA** (text to video + audio).

🧩 **Using ComfyUI?** Get the single-file version of this checkpoint from [MiniMax-H3-Tiny-ComfyUI](https://huggingface.co/H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-ComfyUI).

|---|---|

| Workflows | FL2VA, T2VA |
| Sampling steps | 50 |

MiniMax H3 ships two transformers with the same architecture: one for Ref2VA and one shared by T2VA and FL2VA.
[`MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-Pruned-Ref2VA`](https://huggingface.co/H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-17B-Pruned-Ref2VA) is pruned from the Ref2VA one; this
repository is pruned from the other with the same recipe, calibrated on FL2VA and T2VA samples. The depth search
removes the same blocks, `[6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15]`, for both transformers.

This repository holds the **transformer only** (diffusers layout: `config.json` + sharded safetensors). The text encoder,
VAEs and processors come from the official MiniMax H3 checkpoint in diffusers format.

# MiniMax-H3 FP8 (TP4 / TP1 prepared weights)

**Modified files.** This repository contains Model Derivatives of [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3):
the original weights were converted and quantised. They are NOT the original files.

MiniMax H3 is licensed under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement (see `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`), and so are these
weights. Read it before use: among other things it limits use, reproduction and distribution to its "Applicable
Territory" (worldwide excluding the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea and the United States),
requires machine-generated content to be disclosed, and has an Acceptable Use Policy (Exhibit A).

## Contents
| folder | what | size |
|---|---|---|
| `base-fp8/` | base text-to-video/audio DiT, FP8 E4M3 weights (codes capped at 224) + per-output-channel f32 scales, tensor-parallel 4 shards (`rank0..3`), bf16 token refiner, full-form AdaLN in `host/` | 44 GB |
| `base-fp8-tp1/` | the same DiT for one GPU (block scales [K/128, N]) | 20 GB |
| `ref2va-fp8/` | Ref2VA (reference-to-video) DiT, same format as `base-fp8/` | 44 GB |
| `text-encoder-fp8/` | text encoder (Qwen3-VL based, 50 layers), FP8, TP4 | 25 GB |
| `vision/` | vision tower for reference images, extracted from the Ref2VA text-encoder shard (bf16) | 1.2 GB |
| `vae-bf16/` | video VAE decoder, bf16 | 4.6 GB |

Not included (use the original repo): audio VAE, Ref2VA video-VAE encoder, tokenizer / processor / scheduler configs.

## Format
These are engine-specific prepared layouts (per-rank tensor files + `meta.json`), produced by the Minimax-neuron
`prepare_weights` tools (fp8 mode: per-channel minmax E4M3, max code 224; interleaved per-head qkv layout,
fc1 = [gate; value]). They load in that engine's Vulkan backend (KHR / NV cooperative matrix, TP over several GPUs)
and Neuron backend; they are not a diffusers / safetensors drop-in.

Measured with the Vulkan backend on 4 x RTX 5090 (TP4): 5.2 s 1344x768 text-to-video in ~2.5 min at 20 steps + FSampler;
per-tensor quantisation error 2.6e-2; one real-width DiT block vs an fp32 reference: rel. L2 ~1e-2.

Generated videos must be disclosed as machine-generated (license, Exhibit A item 12).

## Generate with LoRAVideoTrainer

1. Install [LoRAVideoTrainer](https://github.com/dreamsartificial648-sketch/LoRAVideoTrainer#install) and set up the Wan 2.1 T2V 1.3B base model.
2. Download one adapter from the table and put the individual Safetensors file directly in LoRAVideoTrainer's `output/` folder.
3. Select **Wan 2.1 T2V 1.3B** in the model selector. Open **Generate**, click **Refresh** beside the checkpoint selector, and select the downloaded file.
4. Start your prompt with the trigger word and click **Generate Video**.

You can also load a downloaded adapter in [ADAM](https://huggingface.co/SyntheticMDProductions/AI_Development_Automation_Manager#wan-video-lora) through **Video LoRA / Generate / Browse** after setting up its Wan backend.

# ADAM Video LoRAs for LTX-Video 2B 0.9.6 Dev

**By SyntheticMDProductions**

These video-only attention LoRAs were trained with ADAM for LTX-Video 2B 0.9.6 Dev. Use the exact [base checkpoint and revision](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-Video/blob/8984fa25007f376c1a299016d0957a37a2f797bb/ltxv-2b-0.9.6-dev-04-25.safetensors). The adapter format is ADAM PEFT Attention v1.

## Download an adapter

| Adapter | Trigger word | Download |
|---|---|---|
| Backrooms Footage | `Backrooms_Footage` | [Safetensors](./backrooms-footage/Backrooms_Footage.safetensors) |
| Looping the Rooms | `Looping_the_Rooms` | [Safetensors](./looping-the-rooms/Looping_the_Rooms.safetensors) |
| Minecraft | `Minecraft` | [Safetensors](./minecraft/Minecraft.safetensors) |
| Nikocado Avocado | `nikocado_avocado` | [Safetensors](./nikocado-avocado/Nikocado_Avocado.safetensors) |
| Roblox Fun Obby | `Roblox_Fun_Obby` | [Safetensors](./roblox-fun-obby/Roblox_Fun_Obby.safetensors) |
| SyntheticMDProductions | `SMDP` | [Safetensors](./smdp/SMDP.safetensors) |
| Spooky Swings | `Spooky_Swings` | [Safetensors](./spooky-swings/Spooky_Swings.safetensors) |
| Subnautica | `Subnautica` | [Safetensors](./subnautica/Subnautica.safetensors) |

| Ultrakill | `Ultrakill` | [Safetensors](./ultrakill/Ultrakill.safetensors) |

## Generate with LoRAVideoTrainer

1. Open [LoRAVideoTrainer](https://github.com/dreamsartificial648-sketch/LoRAVideoTrainer#modelscope-and-ltx-video-2b), select **LTX-Video 2B 0.9.6 dev**, then install the backend and download the model files.
2. Save the downloaded Safetensors file in the trainer's `output/ltx_video/` folder.
3. In **Generate**, refresh the checkpoint selector and select the file. Include its trigger word in the prompt.

The trainer documents the ADAM attention format. Generation with these release copies on a fresh install is still to be verified.

## License and notices

Use and redistribution are subject to the included [LTX-Video Open Weights License](./LTX-Video-Open-Weights-License-0.X.txt), including the use restrictions in Section 4 and Attachment A. The adapters are fine-tuned additions created by SyntheticMDProductions for the upstream model. The base weights are available from Lightricks.

# MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-heretic-NVFP4

This is a decensored version of [`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE`](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE), made using [Heretic](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic) and [`VINAY-UMRETHE/Refusal-Classifier-v2`](https://huggingface.co/VINAY-UMRETHE/Refusal-Classifier-v2).

This repo contains the **NVFP4 (ModelOpt) safetensors** checkpoint. A single-file NVFP4 **GGUF** for llama.cpp is available at [`narzh49/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-heretic-NVFP4-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/narzh49/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-heretic-NVFP4-GGUF).

| Parameter | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| `start_layer_index` | `25` |
| `end_layer_index` | `55` |

## Performance

| Metric | This model | Original model (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| KL divergence (`harmless_alpaca`) | `0.332` | `0` (by definition) |
| Refusals & Evasions (`Refusal-Classifier-v2`) | `34/100` | `95/100` |

# ChatR Labs Uncensored Omni — Quantized

[![Try the Playground](https://img.shields.io/badge/Playground-Try_it_live-2563eb?style=for-the-badge)](https://thechatr.ai/playground)
[![Base model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hugging_Face-Base_model-ffcc4d?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)
[![Chatr AI](https://img.shields.io/static/v1?label=CHATR%20AI&message=SUPPORT%20OUR%20RESEARCH&color=8B5CF6&labelColor=555555&style=for-the-badge)](https://thechatr.ai)

> **A special thank-you to [Chatr AI](https://thechatr.ai).** Training models requires significant computing resources, and Chatr AI generously provided the GPU infrastructure that made this release possible. If you would like to help us release more open-weight models, please support Chatr AI—their support directly powers our research and future community releases.

**Quantized builds at adapter weight 1.0, for text-to-image generation and image editing.**

This repository ships **quantized transformer weights only**. The model is our rank-128 Omni adapter merged into
[Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) at **LoRA strength 1.0**, then quantized.
The text encoder, processor and VAE are not included; take them from the base repository.

> **New: Turbo LoRA — 8 steps, CFG 1.0.** Add the few-step [Turbo LoRA](https://huggingface.co/chatrlabs/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Omni-LoRA-v0.1/blob/main/chatrlabs-omni-turbo-8step-fp32.safetensors) on top of any build here to generate in **8 steps without CFG**, about **6–7× faster** than the standard 35-step, CFG 5.0 setting, with comparable quality. See [Turbo LoRA](#turbo-lora-8-steps-cfg-10).

File integrity information is in [SHA256SUMS](./SHA256SUMS).

### Which build should I use?

- **ComfyUI, one file, both workflows** -> any **GGUF**. It also loads in Diffusers via `from_single_file`.
- **ComfyUI, native quant ops** -> **FP8**, **INT8 ConvRot** or **NVFP4**.
- **Diffusers, smallest download** -> **NF4** (needs `bitsandbytes`).
- **Diffusers, best fidelity** -> **FP8 (torchao)** (needs `torchao`).
- **Maximum fidelity overall** -> **BF16 GGUF**, **BF16 safetensors** or **Q8_0**.
- **Diffusers without the `gguf` package** -> the **BF16** folder (plain `from_pretrained`).

The `297` and `265` layouts use different MLP representations: `265` uses the fused `img_mlp.gate_up`
projection; `297` keeps the separate `gate_layer` / `proj` pair. A loader must support the selected layout.
The BF16 ComfyUI workflow below was verified with the `297`-tensor safetensors file and the native
`UNETLoader` in ComfyUI 0.39.0; support should not be assumed for older or different loaders.

# black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein

문장으로 512×512 또는 1024×1024 이미지를 만듭니다. Furiosa RNGD에서 실행하며, 가중치 사본 없이 원본 체크포인트를 그대로 읽습니다.

```bash
fxbx run flux-3-image-klein --sample -o result.json
```

[설치·내 문장으로 실행·검증 결과](releases/2026.4.0-flux3-fxbx1/USAGE.md)

## 모델 정보

- **NPU 실행:** FuryNo5로 만든 실행 계획 다섯 개(텍스트 인코더, 해상도별 트랜스포머 스텝과 VAE)와 병합 실행 묶음으로 동작합니다. 16스텝, guidance 없음.
- **속도(텍스트 인코더 제외):** 512×512 약 9.7초, 1024×1024 약 14.4초. 단계별 실행(46.7초, 35.7초)보다 각각 4.8배, 2.5배 빠릅니다.
- **정확도:** CPU 기준 파이프라인과 같은 문장·초기 노이즈로 비교한 PSNR은 512에서 27.31 dB, 1024에서 29.88 dB입니다. 1024는 병합 실행의 BF16 반올림 차이로 단계별 실행(33.0 dB)보다 약 3 dB 낮습니다.
- **가중치:** 원본 [`black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/3b767ff9b5261d71645e2ec49d87d298d955238d)의 safetensors를 첫 실행 때 내려받고 SHA-256을 확인합니다. 원본 저장소는 동의가 필요하므로, Hugging Face에서 FLUX Kommunity License에 동의하고 로그인해야 합니다.
- **입력:** 장면 전체를 묘사하는 문장(프롬프트 확장기 없음, 240토큰까지), 해상도, 시드.
- **필요 환경:** fxbx 0.9.5 이상, Furiosa Torch/TCC 2026.4.0, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, Transformers 5.20 이상, Python 3.11.

## 라이선스

원본 모델과 그 파생물은 [FLUX Kommunity License v1.0](licenses/LICENSE.md)을 따릅니다. 비상업적·비생산 용도로 쓸 수 있고, 상업적 이용은 라이선스가 정한 Qualifying User에 한합니다. 사용 전에 라이선스와 [NOTICE](licenses/NOTICE.md)를 확인하세요. 이 패키지는 Black Forest Labs와 관계가 없으며, 가중치를 재배포하지 않습니다.

# MiniMax H3 Duo for AI Pod

当前修复版本 **0.2.1**，配套 **AI Pod / Agent 2.3.304**，修复部署释放旧模型时的目录缺失错误；模型权重、推理镜像和驱动缓存沿用已验收的 0.2.0 制品。

0.2.1 与配套 AI Pod 2.3.304 已提交应用商店，审核单分别为 **23111 / 23110**，提交时均为审核中；官方接口返回的版本、大小及 SHA256 与真机验收包一致。见 [商店提交回执](evidence/appstore-stop-fix-release.json) 和 [0.2.1 最终安装验收](evidence/release-0.2.1.json)。

将 GaryLauLGY/MinimaxH3-Dual-Dgx-Spark 的双机序列并行路径移植到两台 Jetson AGX Thor，通过四条 25Gbps 光口通信。没有 RDMA 的 Thor 使用经过 CUDA 数据一致性验证的四链路 TCP 适配器。100Gbps 是四口理论总速率；性能报告按实际测量区分链路、集体通信和端到端生成。

部署停在“释放已确认的模型资源”，并出现 `docker-compose down ... chdir ... no such file or directory` 时，需修复主应用 Agent 的选择性停止逻辑：外部 Compose 项目及部署目录已删除的模型按容器身份停止，正常托管服务继续使用 Compose。补丁与回归测试保存在 [Agent 修复](integration/agent-selective-process-stop-fix.patch)，双机修复前后接口、完整重部署及视频生成结果见 [真机验证记录](evidence/agent-selective-process-stop.json)。补丁同时识别两台验收设备上由 Nsight 启动的历史 Pika H3 推理容器。

**0.2.0 最终LPK已完成双源与真机安装验收**。 已提交应用商店，审核状态未宣称通过。冻结方案完整生成中位数 **39.14秒**，其中20步采样 **33.70秒**（832×480、56帧、24fps，视频时长约2.33秒）。固定输入及另外两组输入的像素、音频、MP4 SHA256均与原生参考相同；全新双机进程独立复测为 **39.38秒完整生成 / 33.94秒采样**。本轮已测试实现完成实际收敛审核，无编译器生产镜像也已通过真机生成，最终LPK已通过双源安装、生命周期、统计与恢复检查。全部历史最佳和失败实验继续保留。

生产镜像三次热运行中位数 **38.23秒完整生成 / 33.84秒采样**，重复提示词条件缓存命中；独立关闭该缓存的输出一致性检查已通过。空CUDA缓存首请求为222.66秒，按Agent权限恢复约7MB的纯驱动缓存后降至 **91.62秒**，仍保持像素、音频及MP4一致；模型加载就绪32.27秒另计。首次请求、热运行及条件缓存口径分别记录，不能混用。两台设备实际重启后还观察到约522秒首请求（期间做过只读线程诊断），最终输出一致；该冷态长等待未完成单独归因，不作为热运行成绩。详见性能报告、`evidence/runtime-production-acceptance.json` 和 `evidence/driver-cache-acceptance.json`。

测试方法、全部候选与保留方案见 [性能报告](docs/PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md)。源码仓库保留实现、参数与汇总证据；权重及发布制品使用锁定的双源快照，原始CUDA trace与完整实验产物保留在本地实验记录及发布证据中。

最终安装LPK的三次热运行完整生成分别为37.7873、37.6816、37.7707秒，中位数 **37.77秒**，其中20步采样中位数 **33.38秒**；HTTP等待中位数40.39秒。重复提示词条件缓存命中，832×480、56帧、24fps，视频时长约2.33秒。10个完整画幅安装验收视频的原始像素、音频和实际下载MP4均与参考完全一致；两个来源、数据删除重建、两种卸载重装、Agent和设备重启、四光口及9分钟空闲保持检查均通过。仅登录态图形界面和HTTPS统计展示按用户指定免验，设备累计统计已实测。

# H3 Character Swap Lora

[![Follow @akatz_ai on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/Follow-%40akatz__ai-111111?style=flat-square&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/akatz_ai)
[![Patreon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support-Patreon-FF424D?style=flat-square&logo=patreon&logoColor=white)](https://www.patreon.com/Akatz)
[![GitHub Sponsors](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-GitHub-EA4AAA?style=flat-square&logo=githubsponsors&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sponsors/akatz-ai)
[![Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tip-Ko--fi-FF5E5B?style=flat-square&logo=kofi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/akatz)

![Character Swap: original video, character reference, and swapped result](assets/character-swap-showcase.gif)

**Original → Reference → Character swap.** Four selected examples.

**V1.5 is the recommended checkpoint for new character swaps.** It replaces a
selected person in a source performance with a character from an image reference.

- **[Download V1.5](h3_character_swap_v1.5.safetensors)** — recommended, strength 1.0.
- **[Download V1](h3_character_swap_pro4500_1000.safetensors)** — retained for
  existing workflows and reproducible comparisons.

## Versions

| Version | File | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H3 Character Swap V1.5 | `h3_character_swap_v1.5.safetensors` | Recommended |
| H3 Character Swap V1 | `h3_character_swap_pro4500_1000.safetensors` | Previous release |

## Native workflow with H3 Relay 2.0

[Download the canvas workflow](examples/H3-Character-Swap-Relay-V2.json) or
[the API prompt](examples/H3-Character-Swap-Relay-V2.api.json). These use the
recommended V1.5 adapter, native ComfyUI model loading, reference conditioning,
SAM masking, sampling, loops and saving, plus reusable Relay timeline helpers.
The model weights are unchanged by this workflow update.

Install [H3 Relay 2.0](https://github.com/akatz-ai/h3-relay) and follow
[the workflow guide](examples/README.md) for models, runtime and input paths.

## Use in ComfyUI

1. Obtain the H3 Ref2VA base model, text encoder and VAEs separately.
2. Place `h3_character_swap_v1.5.safetensors` in your configured LoRA directory
   and select it in a compatible model-only LoRA loader at strength **1.0**.
3. Provide the source performance as `<Video 1>` and character reference as
   `<Picture 1>`. Describe the person to replace and the reference identity.
4. Begin with a short continuous shot at 24 fps. Use your runtime's supported H3
   frame grid and review identity, motion, expressions and joins before extending.

Example:

> Replace the selected person in <Video 1> with the character in <Picture 1>.
> Keep the reference character's face, hair and clothing. Follow the source
> performance's pose, gaze, expression and movement. Preserve the scene and the
> other people.

The H3 Character Swap tool handles masks, optional scene anchors, source-audio
conditioning and continuation history. Its tested recipe uses the Ref2VA INT8
base, this character adapter at strength 1.0, and the separate
`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_768p_comfyui_bf16.safetensors` at strength 1.0:
8 steps, CFG 1, `er_sde`, `normal`. The LoRA itself is not a standalone model
and does not include the base, training assistant, VAEs or Turbo weights.

## V1 vs V1.5 comparison

<video controls playsinline src="https://huggingface.co/akatz-ai/MiniMax-H3-Character-Swap-LoRA/resolve/main/assets/character-swap-lora_v1-vs-v1-5.mp4" width="100%"></video>

[Download the comparison video](assets/character-swap-lora_v1-vs-v1-5.mp4).
V1 is on the left; V1.5 is on the right. These selected examples show cases
where V1 loses the reference identity or returns to the source appearance,
while V1.5 retains more of the character. They illustrate improvements on
these shots, rather than an aggregate benchmark.

## Examples and limitations

This remains an experimental character-swap model. Identity, source timing,
expressions, occlusions and cuts can still drift. A recommended default does not
mean every shot improves over V1. Selected comparisons show improved retention
of stylized faces, hair and character identity. Broad evaluation is still in
progress; these observations are not a claim of uniform improvement.

The accompanying tool retains the original source soundtrack in its export.
That is an application feature, not evidence that the LoRA reproduces audio
accurately or that lip sync is exact. Long segment controls in the tool are not
a guarantee of long-shot quality or suitability for every GPU.

The existing showcase and examples below are **V1 results and workflows**.

# LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Mixed-Calibrated

![LTX-2.5 BF16 42GB to Mixed Calibrated 13.2GB](hero.jpg)

Diffusion-calibrated mixed-precision MLX quant of the `Lightricks/LTX-2.5` 22B distilled DiT (`transformer-distilled.safetensors`), packing `MXFP4`, `Q6`, and `Q8` layers into one 13.20 GB safetensors file for `ltx-2-mlx`.

If you prefer uniform 6-bit for strictest frame-for-frame layout parity with Q8, see the companion release: [yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Q6](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Q6) (`15.96 GB`).

## Method

1. **BF16 activation calibration:** Ran 24 BF16 `Lightricks/LTX-2.5` (`49b093a39c19`) DiT forwards across 8 out-of-sample audiovisual prompts (no overlap with the benchmark set) at early (`sigma=0.90`), mid (`0.50`), and late (`0.15`) timesteps, accumulating diagonal second moments `H_diag = E[x^2]` for all 1,632 `transformer_blocks` linears.
2. **Greedy budget allocation (13.20 GB target):** Starting from uniform `MXFP4` (`bits=4, group_size=32`, uint8 scales, no `.biases`), upgraded layers (`mxfp4 -> q6 -> q8`) by highest `H_diag`-weighted error reduction per byte:
   - 584 layers at `mxfp4` (`bits=4, group_size=32`)
   - 807 layers at `q6` (`bits=6, group_size=64, affine`)
   - 241 layers at `q8` (`bits=8, group_size=64, affine`)
   - Boundary embeddings, norms, AdaLN/timestep modulations, and output projections kept in BF16.
3. **Affine clipping refinement:** Per-group range grid search (`alpha in {1.0, 0.98, 0.95, 0.92}`) reduced weighted error on 19 affine layers before standard MLX packing. Runs on stock `nn.QuantizedLinear` Metal kernels with no custom dequantizer.

Total `H_diag`-weighted quantization error dropped from `6.400e5` (uniform `MXFP4`) and `2.421e4` (uniform `Q6`) down to `1.664e4` (-31% vs Q6 while 2.76 GB smaller). Full layer map is in `quantization_policy.json`.

## Benchmarks

Measured on Apple M5 Pro (64 GiB unified RAM), macOS 27.2.1, Python 3.13.18, `mlx 0.32.2`, with non-DiT components locked to `dgrauet/ltx-2.5-mlx-q8`.

### Single-pass DiT parity vs BF16

| Variant | DiT Size | Video Cos | Video RMSE | Audio Cos | Audio RMSE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Q8` (affine g64) | 20.59 GB | 0.999805 | 0.02390 | 0.999681 | 0.01574 |
| `MXFP8` (g32) | 20.02 GB | 0.992870 | 0.14793 | 0.994663 | 0.06530 |
| **Mixed Calibrated (this repo)** | **13.20 GB** | **0.987724** | **0.21676** | **0.989421** | **0.09092** |
| [Q6 (affine g64)](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Q6) | 15.96 GB | 0.986826 | 0.20015 | 0.996734 | 0.05065 |
| `MXFP4` (g32) | 10.74 GB | 0.984554 | 0.21650 | 0.970633 | 0.15176 |
| `Q4` (affine g64) | 11.32 GB | 0.816431 | 0.71769 | 0.968157 | 0.15504 |

### End-to-end 48-clip benchmark (6 scenarios x 2 seeds, 12 clips per variant)

| Variant | Avg Wall | Avg Denoise | Sec/Step | Peak MLX | Max Swap Delta | Silent Clips |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Mixed Calibrated (this repo)** | **70.28s** | **57.38s** | **5.216s** | **29.45 GB** | **0.0 MB** | **0** |
| `Q8` | 74.19s | 60.88s | 5.535s | 29.45 GB | 0.0 MB | 0 |
| [Q6](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Q6) | 74.69s | 61.12s | 5.557s | 29.45 GB | 0.0 MB | 0 |
| `Q4` | 75.17s | 61.32s | 5.575s | 29.45 GB | 0.0 MB | 0 |

### Visual notes

Compared side by side against Q4, Q6, and Q8 on fixed seeds: Mixed Calibrated is sharper than Q4 across skin, eyes, and wet surfaces, and keeps Q6/Q8 scene layout and hand structure on dialogue shots where Q4 smears hands and changes the background. On some seeds it can still shift framing or subject orientation relative to Q8; pick [Q6](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Q6) if exact seed parity with Q8 matters more than speed and RAM.

## Usage

Drop `transformer-distilled.safetensors` into an existing LTX-2.5 MLX pack (such as `dgrauet/ltx-2.5-mlx-q8`), then run:

```bash
ltx-2-mlx generate \
  --distilled \
  --low-ram \
  --nag \
  --negative-prompt "background music, soundtrack, piano, score, plastic smooth skin" \
  --model /path/to/ltx25-mixed-pack \
  --width 768 --height 512 --frames 97 --frame-rate 24 --seed 42 \
  --prompt "A close-up portrait near a sunlit window with natural room tone." \
  --output output_mixed.mp4
```

Notes from testing on M5 Pro 64 GB:
- Requires `ltx-2-mlx` with per-layer mixed-precision and `MXFP4` loader + `BlockStreamer` support.
- `--nag --negative-prompt` on `--distilled` suppresses unwanted score reliably without putting "no music" in the positive prompt.
- `--video-decoder diffusion` ran with 0.0 MB swap at `768x512x97` (162.5s, untiled), `1280x704x97` (416.1s, 2 tiles), and `1152x768x121` (551.6s, 3 tiles).

# LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Q6

6-bit affine (`bits=6, group_size=64`) MLX quant of the `Lightricks/LTX-2.5` 22B distilled DiT (`transformer-distilled.safetensors`) for `ltx-2-mlx`.

If you want a smaller and faster ~13 GB checkpoint, check the companion mixed-precision release: [yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Mixed-Calibrated](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Mixed-Calibrated) (`13.20 GB`, `MXFP4 + Q6 + Q8`).

## Comparison

All numbers measured on Apple M5 Pro (64 GiB unified RAM), macOS 27.2.1, Python 3.13.18, `mlx 0.32.2`, with non-DiT components locked to `dgrauet/ltx-2.5-mlx-q8`.

### Single-pass DiT parity vs BF16

| Variant | DiT Size | Video Cos | Video RMSE | Audio Cos | Audio RMSE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Q8` (affine g64) | 20.59 GB | 0.999805 | 0.02390 | 0.999681 | 0.01574 |
| `MXFP8` (g32) | 20.02 GB | 0.992870 | 0.14793 | 0.994663 | 0.06530 |
| [Mixed Calibrated](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Mixed-Calibrated) | 13.20 GB | 0.987724 | 0.21676 | 0.989421 | 0.09092 |
| **Q6 (this repo)** | **15.96 GB** | **0.986826** | **0.20015** | **0.996734** | **0.05065** |
| `MXFP4` (g32) | 10.74 GB | 0.984554 | 0.21650 | 0.970633 | 0.15176 |
| `Q4` (affine g64) | 11.32 GB | 0.816431 | 0.71769 | 0.968157 | 0.15504 |

### End-to-end 48-clip benchmark (6 scenarios x 2 seeds, 12 clips per variant)

| Variant | Avg Wall | Avg Denoise | Sec/Step | Peak MLX | Max Swap Delta | Silent Clips |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [Mixed Calibrated](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Mixed-Calibrated) | 70.28s | 57.38s | 5.216s | 29.45 GB | 0.0 MB | 0 |
| `Q8` | 74.19s | 60.88s | 5.535s | 29.45 GB | 0.0 MB | 0 |
| **Q6 (this repo)** | **74.69s** | **61.12s** | **5.557s** | **29.45 GB** | **0.0 MB** | **0** |
| `Q4` | 75.17s | 61.32s | 5.575s | 29.45 GB | 0.0 MB | 0 |

Q6 trims 4.63 GB off Q8 (22.5% smaller) while staying visually close to Q8 frame for frame on faces, hands, lighting, and background geometry. Uniform affine Q4 drifts visibly on the same seeds. If you want the smallest and fastest option and don't need strict seed-for-seed layout parity with Q8, use [Mixed Calibrated](https://huggingface.co/yuribarreira/LTX-2.5-Distilled-MLX-Mixed-Calibrated) instead.

## Recipe

- Source: `Lightricks/LTX-2.5` (`49b093a39c19`, `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-bf16.safetensors`)
- Quantized: all 1,632 2D `.weight` linears inside `transformer_blocks` at `bits=6, group_size=64, mode="affine"` (0 packability exceptions)
- Kept in BF16: boundary embeddings, norms, AdaLN/timestep modulations, output projections
- Output: 7,355 tensors, 15.958 GB (`quantization_policy.json` has the full per-tensor map)

## Usage

This is a drop-in DiT file. Place `transformer-distilled.safetensors` alongside the VAE, vocoder, upscalers, connector, and Gemma text encoder from an LTX-2.5 MLX pack (e.g. `dgrauet/ltx-2.5-mlx-q8`), then run:

```bash
ltx-2-mlx generate \
  --distilled \
  --low-ram \
  --nag \
  --negative-prompt "background music, soundtrack, piano, score, plastic smooth skin" \
  --model /path/to/ltx25-q6-pack \
  --width 768 --height 512 --frames 97 --frame-rate 24 --seed 42 \
  --prompt "A close-up portrait near a sunlit window with natural room tone." \
  --output output_q6.mp4
```

Notes from testing on M5 Pro 64 GB:
- Requires `ltx-2-mlx` with native 6-bit / per-layer quantization support.
- Passing `--nag --negative-prompt` on `--distilled` suppresses unwanted background music much more reliably than writing "no music" in the positive prompt.
- Adding `--video-decoder diffusion` improves fine skin and fabric sharpness at higher decode time (verified with 0.0 MB swap at `768x512x97` in 162.5s untiled, `1280x704x97` in 416.1s with 2 tiles, and `1152x768x121` in 551.6s with 3 tiles).

## License

Derived from `Lightricks/LTX-2.5` under the LTX-2.x Community License (see `LICENSE`). When paired with the Gemma text encoder from an LTX-2.5 pack, Gemma's Terms of Use and Prohibited Use Policy also apply.

# MiniMax-H3 INT8 FLF, R2V, Bridge & TTS Workflows Collection

Optimized **ComfyUI workflows** for MiniMax-H3, featuring INT8 inference, native Block Sparse Attention, Veda Sparse Attention, Spectrum, Lightx2v Turbo LoRA, native Extend, Fun ControlNet Union V2V control, Face Refine, TTS, Latent Upscaler, Bridge, and Group Bypass.

**Veda Sparse Attention is supported by both the I2V and R2V workflows** as an optional attention optimization.

These workflows are designed to provide flexible local video and audio generation, with optional acceleration and refinement stages that can be enabled or bypassed as needed.

## Workflows

| Workflow | File | Description |
|---|---|---|
| First-Last-Frame (FLF) | `MiniMax_int8_I2V-javanoYYMM.x.json` | FLF/I2V video generation with Extend, ControlNet Union V2V, Latent Upscaler, and optional Veda Sparse Attention. |
| Reference-to-Video (R2V) | `MiniMax_int8_R2V-javanoYYMM.x.json` | Reference-guided video generation with Reference LoRA, ControlNet Union V2V, Extend, Latent Upscaler, and optional Veda Sparse Attention. |
| Bridge | `MiniMax_int8_Bridge-javanoYYMM.x.json` | Generates a transition between Video A and Video B. |
| Face Refine | `MiniMax_int8_FR-javanoYYMM.x.json` | Face refinement for generated video. |
| Text-to-Speech (TTS) | `MiniMax_int8_TTS-javanoYYMM.x.json` | Audio-only speech generation. |

**Base model:** https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3

## Features

### INT8 Inference

The workflows use INT8 MiniMax-H3 model weights to reduce memory requirements and improve local inference efficiency.

- Reduced model memory requirements compared with higher-precision weights.
- Improved memory efficiency for local inference.
- Suitable for systems with limited VRAM relative to full-precision configurations.

Actual generation speed and output quality depend on the GPU, attention backend, sampling configuration, and enabled optimizations.

### Native Block Sparse Attention

The FLF / I2V and R2V workflows use ComfyUI's native **Block Sparse Attention** node for optimized attention processing.

This is separate from Veda Sparse Attention, which is an additional optional attention optimization.

Native Block Sparse Attention does not require an additional custom node.

### Spectrum

**Repository:** https://github.com/xmarre/ComfyUI-Spectrum-MiniMax-H3

Spectrum provides additional MiniMax-H3 sampling optimization.

The workflows support Spectrum alongside other compatible acceleration methods. Sampling steps and LoRA strengths may require adjustment to balance speed and quality.

### Lightx2v Turbo LoRA

**Model:** https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo

An acceleration LoRA intended to reduce the number of sampling steps.

The appropriate LoRA strength and sampling configuration depend on the selected workflow and output requirements.

### Veda Sparse Attention — I2V and R2V

**Model:** https://huggingface.co/Veda-Sparse/Minimax-H3-R2VA-Veda-Preview

**ComfyUI implementation:** https://github.com/veda-sparse/Veda-on-ComfyUI

Veda Sparse Attention is an optional attention optimization for MiniMax-H3 video generation. It is available in both the I2V and R2V workflows.

It uses a learned predictor to identify relevant visual attention tiles and reduce attention computation.

- Available for both I2V and R2V workflows.
- Requires the Veda-on-ComfyUI custom node and a compatible predictor checkpoint.
- Separate from the native ComfyUI Block Sparse Attention implementation.
- Does not replace the MiniMax-H3 base model or the R2V Reference LoRA.
- Optional; the workflows can be used without enabling Veda Sparse Attention.

The published R2VA Preview is an experimental configuration associated with a Turbo-LoRA setup. Compatibility with other model, LoRA, and sampling configurations should not be assumed.

Follow the official repository instructions for installation, model placement, and supported inference backends.

### Native Extend

MiniMax-H3 supports native video extension for continuing existing video content.

The workflows use native Extend functionality rather than requiring the former Motion Context custom node.

### Fun ControlNet Union — V2V Control

**Model repository:** https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3-experimental/tree/main/controlnet

Integrated into the I2V and R2V workflows.

Supported control types:

- OpenPose
- Canny
- Depth

Available models:

- `minimax_h3_fun_controlnet_union_pruned_bf16.safetensors`
- `minimax_h3_fun_controlnet_union_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`

Use the model variant compatible with your workf

# MiniMax H3 files for mmh3

Model files for [mmh3](https://github.com/niw/mmh3), an inference engine dedicated to
[MiniMax H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3). They follow the layout of mmh3's models
directory. Each file is a Model Derivative of MiniMax H3, and its section says what it was modified
from and how.

## patches/minimax_h3_fasth3_vsa_datafree_patch_rank64.safetensors

A patch that turns the pruned INT8 ConvRot FL2VA DiT,
`diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` of
[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3), into FastVideo's
[FastH3 VSA-DataFree](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastVideo-FastH3-4-step-Preview-v1-VSA-DataFree),
which generates in four steps with video sparse attention. mmh3 applies it on top of that DiT:

```sh
mmh3 generate --models /path/to/models --prompt-file prompt.txt --out out.mp4 \
  --steps 4 --attention-precision int8-fp8 \
  --patch /path/to/minimax_h3_fasth3_vsa_datafree_patch_rank64.safetensors
```

The patch holds a rank-64 LoRA and the tensors that a LoRA cannot carry, such as the VSA gates and
the fine-tuned AdaLN, so tools other than mmh3 may not load it.

Modifications: it is modified from MiniMax H3 and from FastVideo's FastH3 VSA-DataFree checkpoint.
The differences between the FastH3 and MiniMax H3 weights were reduced to a low-rank LoRA, and the
other tensors that FastH3 changed or added were converted to the layout of the pruned INT8 DiT. It
was built with `tools/models/fasth3_vsa_patch.py` of mmh3.

SHA-256: `5577a30b1a443c5f6d0ba923e11a0b5ae57cbf73aa64ae8d458d1c2feff16903`

## vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors

The video VAE of MiniMax H3 with the linear layers of its decoder blocks in INT8 ConvRot, in the
layout of ComfyUI's INT8 ConvRot checkpoints, so ComfyUI loads it too. mmh3 decodes with it when
its models directory has it. Against the FP16 VAE's decode, its pixels reach about 60.9 dB PSNR over
five FastH3 latents outside the calibration, where rounding the weights to nearest gives 58.2 dB.

Modifications: it is modified from MiniMax H3, from `vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors` of
[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3). Its decoder was rescaled per
input channel, with the inverse folded into the neighboring weights so that its function does not
change, and its linear layers were quantized to INT8 with GPTQ on calibration latents. It was built
with `tools/models/video_vae_int8.py` of mmh3.

SHA-256: `7c0b2e270d4b04923c7bbc07358a842b19255635fb08792210f36355e2c6adfd`

## loras/minimax_h3_taomate_3step_lora_rank128_bf16.safetensors

The [TaoMate-H3](https://huggingface.co/TaoLiveAIGC/TaoMate-H3) adapter, the step-3000 generator EMA
of rank 128, as a LoRA under ComfyUI's names in BF16, so mmh3 and ComfyUI load it. It generates in
three steps, states 0, 16, 33 and 49 of the 50-step schedule, which mmh3 runs with
`--schedule taomate`:

```sh
mmh3 generate --models /path/to/models --prompt-file prompt.txt --out out.mp4 \
  --schedule taomate --attention sol --attention-precision int8-fp8 --sparse-start 0 \
  --lora /path/to/minimax_h3_taomate_3step_lora_rank128_bf16.safetensors
```

Modifications: it is modified from the TaoMate-H3 adapter. Its low-rank updates were factored again
by their SVD at the full rank, renamed to ComfyUI's LoRA names and rounded from FP32 to BF16. It was
built with `tools/models/taomate_lora.py` of mmh3.

SHA-256: `eaad4eeebc5eb2db1ca1d492b93f6cacb52bf6cc3c4d2a13b3c6e493b9ce16b8`

## loras/minimax_h3_pdmd_2step_lora_rank128_bf16.safetensors

The [PDMD 2-NFE LoRA](https://huggingface.co/pdmd2026/pdmd_2NFE_lora), the step-4000 student of rank
128 distilled from MiniMax H3 with Projected Distribution Matching Distillation, as a LoRA under
ComfyUI's names in BF16, so mmh3 and ComfyUI load it. It generates in two steps with the video and
audio shifts 12 and 3:

```sh
mmh3 generate --models /path/to/models --prompt-file prompt.txt --out out.mp4 \
  --steps 2 --shift-video 12 --shift-audio 3 --attention sol \
  --attention-precision int8-fp8 --sparse-start 0 \
  --lora /path/to/minimax_h3_pdmd_2step_lora_rank128_bf16.safetensors
```

update and cut from rank 384 to 128, which keeps 97% of their energy on average, and the halves of
its feed-forward input update were swapped to the DiT's order. Each update was factored again by its
SVD, renamed to ComfyUI's LoRA names and rounded to BF16. The other layers keep their full rank. It

# MiniMax H3 Temporal Latent Upscaler for ComfyUI

Fix fast-motion smear, ghosting, and frame stepping in MiniMax H3 videos—and optionally upscale resolution in the same pass—directly in latent space.

Instead of decoding to pixels and re-encoding like pixel De-RoPE, this pack takes the **latent output of your first H3 sampler**, detects which 17-frame blocks have fast motion, stretches only those moments to 2× or 3× frames during Pass 2 so H3 can redraw them cleanly, and recovers your exact original frame count, 24 fps timing, and untouched Pass-1 audio.

---

## See the Difference

[![Looping backflip comparison. Left, the H3 source. Right, joint spatial and temporal repair.](demos/backflip-preview.webp)](demos/README.md#backflip--spatial-and-temporal-repair)

**Watch the trailing leg during the flip.** Left is the raw H3 Pass-1 output (ghosted/smeared limb). Right is Pass-2 adaptive temporal repair + 1.5× spatial latent upscaling, playing at the exact same speed and duration.
👉 [Full comparison gallery (backflip, basketball pixel-vs-latent, anime slash)](demos/README.md)

---

## Updates

### v2.0 — Speed, Quality & Unified Workflow Overhaul (Nov 2026)

A full code audit, RTX 4060 8 GB benchmark sweep, and workflow cleanup resolved several hidden bugs and simplified the whole repo down to **one toggleable production workflow**:

- **1.81× faster temporal upscaler, -32% VRAM, zero OOM:** Rewrote `temporal_checkpoint.py` onto ComfyUI core's optimized `MiniMaxH3LatentUpscaler` path (`channels_last_3d` convolutions, fused `comfy_kitchen` GroupNorm3D + SiLU, `SLAB=16` chunking, dynamic VRAM via `CoreModelPatcher`, and mtime caching). Removed forced `unload_all_models()` calls. (`3× + 1.5× spatial` dropped from OOM / `5.60s` down to **`3.10s / 1.16 GiB`**.)
- **Fixed Pass-2 schedule bug (`H3RepairSchedule`):** Previously, `inject` was compared against sigma values instead of step counts, silently running only 1 Pass-2 step instead of 5. The new built-in `H3RepairSchedule` matches `H3InjectSchedule` bit-for-bit (true 5 steps on masked clips) **and automatically skips Pass 2 in `0.02s`** on calm 1× clips when no motion blocks need repair.
- **Fixed FL2V first-frame drift:** Spatial upscaling of single-frame I2V/FL2V keyframe latents now takes the symmetric center token (`2:3`) instead of an edge token, bringing first-frame fidelity (`first_mae`) in line with the end frame.
- **Fixed 5-frame edge-case crash & tail over-dilation:** Fixed a crash on 5-frame clips in motion scoring and tightened the short-tail gate so quiet endings don't waste Pass-2 compute.
- **Added `H3ExactVAEDecode`:** Combines H3 video VAE decoding and exact hold-map frame recovery in one node, skips trailing snap-pad chunks (bit-exact vs `VAEDecode + H3ExactRecover`), and cleanly falls back to normal decoding if Pass 2 is bypassed.
- **Replaced 4 separate JSON graphs with 1 unified workflow:** T2V, I2V, FL2V, Ref2V, 8 GB Low-VRAM, FirstBlockCache (Pass 1 only), Sol-Attn INT8 (Pass 2 only), H3DyRoPE, Turbo LoRA, and RTX VSR 2× are now all one-click toggles in [`workflows/H3_Unified_Production_Workflow.json`](workflows/H3_Unified_Production_Workflow.json).
- **Quality-verified speedups (rejected anything that blurred output):** Benchmarks showed sparse attention hurts sharpness at low token counts (Pass 1) and core `BlockSparseAttention` conflicts with KJ Low-VRAM / `H3DyRoPE`. Pass 1 therefore uses **FirstBlockCache H3 Safe** (`-11%` time, matching quality), while Pass 2 uses **Triton Sol-Attn INT8** (`min_tokens=12288`, `-21%` time, *higher* measured sharpness than dense).

---

## One Workflow for Everything

Open **[`workflows/H3_Unified_Production_Workflow.json`](workflows/H3_Unified_Production_Workflow.json)** in ComfyUI. Use the **3 toggle panels on the left**—no rewiring needed:

### Panel 1 — Generation Mode *(Cyan · pick one)*
- **FL2VA (T2V / I2V / FL2V)** *(Default ON)*: Standard text-to-video, image-to-video, and first+last-frame video.
- **REF2VA (Reference to Video)** *(Default OFF)*: Character/scene/voice reference video using `<Picture 1..3>` and `<Audio 1>`.

### Panel 2 — Optional Media Inputs *(Yellow · all OFF = T2V)*
- **A. Image 1:** First frame (FL2VA) or `<Picture 1>` (REF2VA).
- **B. Image 2:** Last frame (FL2VA) or `<Picture 2>` (REF2VA).
- **C. Image 3:** `<Picture 3>` (REF2VA only).
- **D. Ref Audio:** `<Audio 1>` (REF2VA only).

### Panel 3 — Hardware, Speedups & Finish *(Brown)*
| Toggle | Default | What it does |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| **1. Low VRAM 8GB (KJ Attn + FFN)** | **ON** | Keeps 8 GB GPUs comfortable without OOM. Turn **OFF** on 16–24 GB+ GPUs. |
| **2. Pass-1 FirstBlockCache** | **ON** | ~11% faster Pass 1 (`H3 Safe`). Wired strictly to Pass 1—never affects Pass 2. Turn OFF for 100% dense Pass 1. |
| **3. Turbo 4-Step LoRA** | OFF | Fast previews—turn ON and set Pass-1 steps to `4`–`6`. |
| **4. Pass-2 Sol-Attn INT8** | **ON** | ~21% faster & sharper Pass 2 when upscaling (`min_tokens=12288`, auto-bypa

# MiniMax H3 INT4 ConvRot + Mixed FP16/FP32 Video VAE

This repository contains a collection of MiniMax H3 model components intended for lower-memory local inference.

The original MiniMax H3 model and architecture were released by **MiniMaxAI**:

https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3

MiniMax H3 is an omni-modal video generation model capable of generating synchronized video and stereo audio. The official release supports text-to-audio-video, first/last-frame-to-audio-video, and multimodal reference-to-audio-video generation, depending on the selected model variant.

The original MiniMax H3 release, documentation, architecture information, usage instructions and licensing information can be found in the official repository linked above.


# September 19 2026 : updated with another Hybrid model version

This can replace both the rf2va and the ref2va model and allows using start image + reference in one job
Hybrid model one : all credits to berryber09, go here for all info :

For more info go to https://civitai.com/models/2900456/minimax-h3sparseref15hybrid


## INT4 ConvRot model files


The following three quantized model files included in this repository were copied from the MiniMax H3 INT4 ConvRot release by **Winnougan**:

https://huggingface.co/Winnougan/MiniMax-H3-INT4_Convrot_ComfyUI

- `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-w4a8_convrot_pruned.safetensors`
- `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-w4a8_convrot_pruned.safetensors`
- `minimax_h3_te_w4a8_convrot.safetensors`

These files use the W4A8 / ConvRot quantization format.

The FL2VA and Ref2VA transformer checkpoints are pruned and W4A8 ConvRot quantized versions of the MiniMax H3 diffusion transformers. The text encoder is also provided in W4A8 ConvRot format, while its visual component remains at higher precision as in the source conversion.

All credit for these INT4 ConvRot conversions belongs to **Winnougan** and the respective contributors to the ConvRot/W4A8 tooling.

For additional technical information about the quantization format, requirements and original converted files, see the Winnougan repository linked above.

## Mixed-precision Video VAE

This repository also contains a modified version of the MiniMax H3 Video / Visual VAE.

The original Video VAE weights originate from the official MiniMax H3 release.

For this repository, I converted the majority of the Video VAE tensors from FP32 to **FP16** in order to substantially reduce its memory and storage requirements.

Instead of blindly converting the entire VAE to FP16, selected small and precision-sensitive blocks were intentionally retained in **FP32**.

The resulting file is therefore a **mixed FP16/FP32 Video VAE**:

- Large weight tensors are stored in FP16.
- Selected smaller / precision-sensitive tensors remain FP32.
- The goal is to reduce memory usage while preserving as much reconstruction quality and numerical stability as possible.
- The model architecture itself was not retrained or fine-tuned.


## MiniMax H3 Tubo 4 step loras

Newest Turbo lora step600 was copied from  https://huggingface.co/larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora


## Model components


- FL2VA INT4/W4A8 ConvRot transformer
- Ref2VA INT4/W4A8 ConvRot transformer
- INT4/W4A8 ConvRot MiniMax H3 text encoder
- Mixed FP16/FP32 Video VAE
- MiniMax H3 FP32 Audio VAE
- Supporting configuration files where required


## Intended use

The purpose of this repository is to provide a more practical MiniMax H3 model set for local inference, particularly on consumer GPUs where loading the original full-precision model components can require a very large amount of VRAM and system memory.

The quantized components trade some numerical precision for substantially reduced memory requirements.

The mixed-precision Video VAE is intended to further reduce memory consumption compared with the original FP32 VAE while retaining FP32 precision where it may matter most.

Officially created for use with Comfyui. With some work and the correct (comfyui) loader these also work standalone in other setups.

# NEXORA H3

**NEXORA H3** is a community-created merged MiniMax H3 Ref2VA checkpoint for reference-guided video generation, including audio-video and motion-oriented use cases. I researched and tested different approaches to improve reference consistency, image quality, motion, natural-looking skin, and a restrained cinematic look, then brought those experiments together in one checkpoint. The model is designed to balance these qualities; results still depend on the prompt, references, and workflow.

Access to repository files is controlled by the Hugging Face manual access gate; gated files require owner approval.

## Preview videos

These examples were generated with NEXORA H3. They illustrate several motion and audio-video use cases. They are examples, not controlled benchmark results. The clips are also stored in the repository under the examples folder.

## Recommended prompt-writing guide

For writing scene prompts for this checkpoint, use [NEXORA H3 Ref2VA Motion-Enhanced Prompt Guide](https://huggingface.co/Asirus/MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-NEXORA/blob/main/NEXORA_H3_Ref2VA_Motion_Prompt_Guide_EN.md). It is the closest match among the six reviewed documents: it is written for MiniMax H3 Ref2VA, uses the six-section Full-Reference CIR format, and gives detailed guidance for reference identity, coherent action, camera choreography, continuity, and audio. The guide is an LLM prompt-writing aid, not a guarantee of model behavior or a replacement for the ComfyUI workflow settings.
## Model development

The starting point was the clean Comfy-Org MiniMax H3 Ref2VA INT8 ConvRot diffusion checkpoint. I built NEXORA H3 by merging complementary weight-level changes into this base checkpoint. It is a merged model checkpoint, not a full-parameter fine-tune or a model trained from scratch.

The merge preserved the base architecture and tensor layout. The structural audit found no unmatched targets or shape errors. The INT8 requantization audit measured a median relative error of about 0.549%, a 95th percentile of about 0.679%, and a maximum of about 0.809%. These are tensor-level numerical measurements, not a perceptual benchmark or a guarantee of visual quality.

NEXORA H3 brings these research goals together in one ready-to-use checkpoint. This model card describes the goals and intended use at a high level. The original terms for the base model and any third-party material continue to apply; this project does not grant additional rights.

- Load the checkpoint as a diffusion model from the ComfyUI models/diffusion_models folder.
- Keep the compatible MiniMax H3 text encoder, VAE, and reference/audio workflow components installed separately; they are not bundled into this diffusion checkpoint.
- Recorded sampler: **Euler SDE**.
- Recorded scheduler: **Simple**.
- Recorded sigma shift: **12.3**.
- For the best result observed by the creator, use a **two-pass workflow**. Exact pass settings depend on the workflow and target resolution.

# Lucia v1.2: Qwen3.5-9B, think symbolic image

**Lucia v1.2** is a LoRA adapter of [Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B) that looks at a picture and
writes a reading of it: a short chain of plain-language thoughts, one named step per line, then the wordings (a caption, a
prompt, tags, a critique, by depth), then the questions a careful looker would still ask, each with its answer and what settles
it. She is the largest of the Lucia family. Version 1.2 is version 1.1's recipe taught once on nearly ten times the rows, the
recipe and the rows of [Lucia 4B v1.2](https://huggingface.co/AbstractPhil/qwen3.5-4b-think-symbolic-image) at 9B.

- **Nearly ten times the rows.** She was taught 91,138 rows (version 1.1: 9,261), the rows Lucia 4B v1.2 was taught:
  the Apache-2.0 part of [release 5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned/tree/cac40b93d7b063aafd0cb70d3c1b1a7a100562ef) of [thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned)
  as anyone can read it there (95,481 rows), less 3,718 rows on COCO 2017 photographs under other licenses,
  609 rows on the pictures the reads below hold out and 16 rows whose pictures no store holds.
  They are readings of DOCCI and COCO 2017 photographs, of National Gallery of Art pictures and of drawn specifications, written
  by OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek models and admitted by a blind review; 30,250 of them are long looks. No row she was
  taught was written by a Claude model, or by any model of this project trained on rows a Claude model wrote. Training shows her
  the picture of every row about a picture (the drawn specifications have none), so the COCO 2017 photographs she saw are only
  those whose Flickr authors gave them the Attribution license or that carry no known copyright restrictions, in her rows and in
  the ordinary requests below alike.
- **One pass.** She was taught her rows once (10,137 steps); version 1.1 was taught hers twice (2,102 steps).
- **The base model kept**, as in version 1.1: a second objective in training holds her next-word choices near Qwen3.5-9B's on
  ordinary requests that Qwen3.5-9B answered itself, so the adapter changes how she answers when asked for a reading and little
  else. On held-out ordinary requests she stays close to the base model, and of the questions and text requests among them she
  answers none in the reading's form; version 1, trained without it, answers 157 of the 328 that way.
- **Lettering left out of the closer look.** Of 300 held-out pictures with readable lettering, a screen found no person's name,
  credit or web address in the lettering of 245. Of those 245, her closer look names a word the picture shows for
  50, where the base model's free description names one for 226; her long look names one for
  97. Asked directly what the lettering says, for 234 of those 245, her answer names it as often as the
  base model's does (0.91 of them against 0.91).

Versions 1.1 and 1 stay in this repository at the tags `lucia-v1.1` and `lucia-v1`, and the original release at
`legacy-e-all-2ep`. Her non-commercial sibling,
[qwen3.5-9b-think-symbolic-image-nc](https://huggingface.co/AbstractPhil/qwen3.5-9b-think-symbolic-image-nc), holds version
1.1-nc: version 1.1's recipe on the Apache-2.0 rows and on the readings written with COCO 2017, FFHQ and DeepFashion-MultiModal
pictures in view, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

What she writes for a closer look at a held-out COCO 2017 photograph ([376084](https://cocodataset.org/#explore?id=376084), its author's Attribution license), verbatim:

```
see: One yellow truck sits at the center of the frame, with traffic cones around it.
relate: The truck is to the right of a person, while the person is to the left of a chair.
mood: The truck's parked state suggests a gentle pause.
caption: A yellow truck is parked at the center of the frame, to the right of a person, with traffic cones around it.
prompt: yellow truck, parked truck, traffic cones around the truck, truck to the right of a person, person to the left of a chair
tags: yellow truck, traffic cones, person, chair, photograph
question: thing name -> truck [record]
question: thing colour -> yellow [record]
question: rel1 rel -> right of [record]
question: form space -> unknown [unknown]
```

`light`, `colour`, `mood`, `mean`, `intend`, `story`, `compare`, `change`, `check`, `say`. A quick look holds 1 to 2 thoughts,

# Qwen 3.5 Natural Language Image Captioning Adapter

This is an adapter model for the Qwen 3.5 4B Abliterated model  DreamFast/Qwen3.5-4B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive-Safetensor-Benchmark .

The adapter is trained on image captioning using natural language output.

When using this adapter on the Qwen 4B model , we can do batches of 30 captions at a time on a single T4 , roughly 7 seconds per caption. 

Its trained on my own prompts , natural lanugage captions of images from sankaku complex using a mix of gemini flash and joycaption beta , and prompts from (NSFW) posts on civitai
The main goal of this project is to create a fast, compact natural language captioning model that can be used to generate training captions for image-to-text and image-generation models.

This is the current dataset distribution

![ffff](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/65d7326229af34543a0f4fd0/AQhmCKzi_6LQgYGWSF3P-.webp)

## Testing the adapter

You can test the adapter using the Google Colab notebook provided in this repository:

[qwen35_sankaku_captioning.ipynb](https://huggingface.co/codeShare/qwen35_image_captioning_adapter/blob/main/qwen35_sankaku_captioning.ipynb)

The notebook provides an interface for testing image caption generation using the adapter. 

## Training

The adapter was trained on 2,000 images using:

| Parameter | Details |
|---|---|
| Base model | DreamFast/Qwen3.5-4B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive-Safetensor-Benchmark |
| Training images | 10,000 |
| Dataset source | Sankaku Complex Database |
| Training hardware | 2 × NVIDIA T4 GPUs (Kaggle) |
| Training duration | 24 hours |
| Training steps | 13000 |

### Training methodology

The dataset preparation involved an initial captioning and summarization stage.

During the first training run, the base Qwen 3.5 model was used to caption the images. Its generated descriptions were then summarized by the model itself.

The adapter was subsequently trained on these summaries rather than the original, longer model responses.

This approach was intended to remove unnecessary preambles and verbose introductory text from the captioning output, producing more direct and compact natural language descriptions.

An important distinction: this process does not add new visual understanding or knowledge to the underlying model. It primarily teaches the model to produce a more concise version of its existing captioning capabilities.

## Performance

Inference speed is one of the most promising aspects of this adapter.

On an NVIDIA T4 (16 GB), the model can process approximately 40 image items in a batch, with an average caption processing time of approximately 6–7 seconds per image.

These are observed performance figures and may vary depending on image resolution, generation settings, software configuration and available GPU memory.

The combination of relatively fast inference and access to the Sankaku database opens up interesting possibilities for on-the-fly dataset preparation.

### Potential applications

One particularly interesting possibility is integrating natural language caption generation directly into an image model training session.

For example:

1. Fetch candidate images from the Sankaku database.
2. Generate natural language captions using this adapter.
3. Use the resulting image-caption pairs to train a LoRA.
4. Repeat the process to continuously expand the training dataset.

This could reduce the need to prepare and manually caption large datasets in advance.

For LoRA training on GPUs with 16 GB of VRAM, MOSS Image is one of the first model families I would like to explore for this approach.

## Limitations and future development

The current adapter is primarily optimized for concise natural language captioning.

Because the training dataset was generated through a caption-and-summarization process, the resulting descriptions can lack some of the detail and depth that would be desirable for more demanding image understanding and image-generation training tasks.

My next step is to manually edit and improve the dataset, focusing on more detailed and informative descriptions.

The intention is to move beyond simply removing unnecessary verbosity and towards genuinely richer natural language image descriptions.

- [x] Generate initial natural language captions.
- [x] Summarize the original model responses.
- [x] Train the fir
