# Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo for the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 neural unit

Built with Qwen. A phone conversion of [Qwen-Image 2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) Turbo (as
packaged in [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1)), compiled as QNN
context binaries for the Hexagon v81 neural unit (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5). It draws 768x768 pictures from
a prompt in 8 steps, and edits a 768x768 picture from an instruction. The files for the Snapdragon 8 Elite
(Hexagon v79) are in [qwen-image-2.1-qnn-8elite](https://huggingface.co/sebekblessing/qwen-image-2.1-qnn-8elite); the
ones for the graphics chip of either phone are in
[qwen-image-2.1-gpu](https://huggingface.co/sebekblessing/qwen-image-2.1-gpu).

**Non-commercial use only** (Qwen RESEARCH LICENSE AGREEMENT, see LICENSE and NOTICE).

## What is in it

| Files | What they do |
|---|---|
| `r0.bin` ... `r3.bin`, `qwen_table_q8.raw`, `qwen_tokenizer.json` | the prompt reader (Qwen3-VL-8B's language model, 8-bit weights) |
| `vis.bin` | the reader's vision tower, for edits (8-bit weights) |
| `sp0.bin` ... `sp31.bin` | the drawing model, one block per file (4-bit weights in blocks of 32) |
| `enc.bin`, `dec.bin` | taeqi2_1 picture encoder and decoder |
| `sigmas.txt` | the 8 noise levels |
| `manifest.json` | file list with sizes and SHA-256, used by the app's download |

One download (about 14 GB). The files are loaded one at a time, so drawing needs about 2.6 GB of memory.

## Changes from the original models

The weights were converted to ONNX, quantized (4-bit blocks for the drawing model, 8-bit per channel with a
Hadamard rotation for the reader) and compiled for the neural unit. Pictures may differ slightly from the
original models'.

## The app, and building these files yourself

These files are made for the [Anima app](https://github.com/adiirfan/anima-android), which downloads them itself.
The scripts that build them from the original model weights, with a step-by-step guide, are in
[`build/`](build/README.md) in this repo.

# MiniMax-H3-Image for the AMD Ryzen AI NPU

AMD Ryzen AI NPU (XDNA 2) model files for the [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) six-step text-to-image model. The same files generate 1024×1024 images and portrait or landscape sizes up to the same pixel count. The files hold the diffusion transformer, the decoder projections and the token refiner, converted with Ryzen AI Software 1.8.0. Unofficial; see `NOTICE`.

Code, setup and usage: **https://github.com/tomhda/minimax-h3-image-ryzen-ai-npu**

![Three images generated with these files: a rainy neon street, an anime neon city and a handwritten message card](images/gallery.jpg)

![Four images generated with these files](images/samples.jpg)

`cafe-board`, `neon-open`, `station-board` and `birthday-card` from left to right, all with seed 1234.

## Contents

| Folder | What | Size |
|---|---|---:|
| `dit/` | 50 diffusion transformer layers: four int4 projections, a compiled attention graph and host scale tensors per layer | 18.04 GB |
| `vae/` | 24 decoder layers: four packed int4 projections and bias tensors per layer | 1.89 GB |
| `vae-common/` | Shared decoder tensors and the compiled DynamicDispatch attention graph | 0.04 GB |
| `outer/` | CPU projections, six output heads, timestep and modulation tensors, sampling schedule | 0.25 GB |
| `refiner/` | Condition projection and token refiner tensors in their original dtypes | 1.60 GB |
| `casts/` | Two ONNX graphs for the host casts | 266 bytes |
| `manifest.json` | Size and SHA256 of every file, upstream revisions, Ryzen AI version | |

The files total 21.81 GB. The text encoder, tokenizer and original VAE files are not in this repository; the GitHub setup downloads them from the MiniMax repositories at pinned revisions (56.04 GB).

## Changes from MiniMax-H3-Image

- The four linear projections in each DiT and VAE layer use asymmetric int4 weights with bf16 inputs and outputs. The DiT projections are split by width and zero-padded to shapes the NPU kernels support.
- DiT attention runs as a 24-head DynamicDispatch graph in a fixed 1,280-row frame. Three calls cover the 56 heads. An attention pass on validity marks accounts for the padding.
- The CPU streams text encoder layers 0–49 and runs the token refiner. The decoder works on overlapping 256×256 tiles, 25 at 1024×1024, and computes its attention on the CPU.

## Requirements

- Windows 11 on an AMD Ryzen AI processor with an XDNA 2 NPU and its driver
- [Ryzen AI Software 1.8.0](https://ryzenai.docs.amd.com/en/1.8/inst.html)
- The scripts from the GitHub repository

## Quick start

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/tomhda/minimax-h3-image-ryzen-ai-npu
cd minimax-h3-image-ryzen-ai-npu
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\setup.ps1
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\doctor.ps1
pwsh -NoProfile -File .\gen.ps1 -Items .\examples\one.json -Out .\outputs\first
```

## Measured on a Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350 (32 GB, NPU driver 32.0.203.329, NPU power mode Turbo, AC)

- Transformer projections and attention on the NPU; decoder projections on the NPU; text encoder on the CPU. GPU engine utilization of the generation processes 0%.
- 1024×1024, 6 steps: 368 s end to end per image (median of six back-to-back executions; mean 369 s, 352–389 s). DiT inference 28.6 s/step. Every image also includes 105 s of DiT session creation.
- CPU time / wall time 0.92: about one logical processor busy on average.
- Memory for one image: the generation processes peak at 3.86 GB of private bytes (text encoder stage) and 1.92 GB of NPU shared memory, 4.33 GB at the same moment. Free physical memory fell by 4.05 GB. Generation stops when free physical memory falls below 5 GB (configurable).
- Other sizes: `width` and `height` per item, multiples of 32, at least 256, `width` × `height` between 589,824 and 1,048,576. 768×1344 took 341 s and 1344×768 took 361 s, one execution each. A smaller image takes about as long as 1024×1024.
- Text in images: five of the six prompts show the requested text. `price-tag` shows りんど where the prompt asks for りんご; the fp32 CPU implementation of the official equations shows the same りんど.
- The same prompt and seed do not always give the same latent: in 27 runs, 20 final latents matched an earlier run bit for bit and 7 did not. The cause is unknown.

Full tables and technical notes are in the GitHub repository.

# MiniMax-H3-Image-Exp-Comfy

**完整未裁剪 BF16/FP32 发布主干 + 多步材质近似修正实验 / ComfyUI。**

## 快速开始：50 步工作流先装节点

> **必装自定义节点：[H3 Image Single Head · T8（GitHub）](https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8)。** 只下载模型和 LoRA 不会自动安装节点。工作流里 `H3ImageSingleHead` 显示红叉时，请先安装节点并重启 ComfyUI。
>
> **只跑原生 6 步 CFG1？** 用 [原生六步工作流](workflows/native_pdd6)，不装此节点，也不加载 direct MLP100。

**EN:** The supplied 50-step direct MLP100 workflows require the [H3 Image Single Head node](https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8). The native 6-step workflows do not.

1. **安装节点：**[查看 GitHub 安装说明](https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8#安装) 或 [下载节点 ZIP](https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8/archive/refs/heads/main.zip)，解压到 `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/`，然后重启。
2. **放好模型：**按下方表格放置完整主干、direct MLP100、文本编码器和 VAE。
3. **导入一个工作流：**第一次用就选 [推荐文生图 JSON](workflows/direct_mlp/violin_maker.json)；有参考图再选 [图生图 / 编辑 JSON](workflows/direct_mlp/shop_wall_edit.json)。

```text
UNETLoader → H3ImageSingleHead → LoraLoaderBypassModelOnly (+1) → CFGGuider (3)
```

推荐工作流已连好，使用 Euler 50 步和内置 shift 3 采样表。[查看完整效果对照](EXAMPLES.md)。

Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image。这是 t8star 的第三方研究与打包仓库，不是 MiniMax 官方新版本，不是 FineView 权重，也不是已剥离 PDD 的原版教师。

## 先说结论：什么值得用？

1. **要完整发布模型：**下载 `diffusion_models/minimax_h3_image_full_bf16_comfy_qkvfix-T8.safetensors`。66.29 GB，保留完整 AdaLN 与发布精度，不是 INT8 反量化，也不是 pruned 模型。**它仍然含 PDD，正常六步路线没有被去掉。**
2. **要试多步下更自然的材质：**使用上面的主干 + 本仓库单头节点 + `loras/experimental_direct_mlp100_rank16-T8.safetensors`。这是目前本项目优先尝试的近似修正候选。实测设置为 **Euler 50 步、CFG 3、shift 3、LoRA 正强度 +1**。不是六步 CFG1，也不是简单调整 SHIFT。
3. **不要把最新日期当成最好：**`experimental/rejected/REJECTED_edit_preservation_mlp100_rank16_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY.safetensors` 未通过训练数值预算检查，实图也没有证明整体优于前一版。仅供失败诊断，**不推荐替换 direct MLP100**。

没有找到匹配的原始图像 PDD 主干增量，也没有未知教师权重可供对照；不能声称“剥离完成”“99% 原版还原”。8/10 是这批固定样本的人工联合检查计数，不是教师相似度，不是大规模盲测成绩。

## 下载什么、放在哪里？

|文件/目录|用途|安装位置|建议|
|---|---|---|---|
|[完整主干](diffusion_models/minimax_h3_image_full_bf16_comfy_qkvfix-T8.safetensors)|完整发布权重的 ComfyUI 格式转换，66.29 GB|`ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`|基础必需|
|[direct MLP100](loras/experimental_direct_mlp100_rank16-T8.safetensors)|独立训练的材质近似补偿，172.07 MB|`ComfyUI/models/loras/`|多步实验优先尝试|
|[文本编码器](text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors)|测试使用的 INT8 文本编码器，27.14 GB|`ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/`|已有同文件可复用|
|[VAE](vae/minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors)|测试使用的 FP16 图像 VAE，1.17 GB|`ComfyUI/models/vae/`|已有同文件可复用|
|[单头节点 · GitHub](https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8)|`__init__.py` 和 `mean_head.safetensors` 必须一起保留|整个目录放入 `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/`|50 步必装；原生六步不使用|
|[历史模型清单](MODEL_INDEX.md)|全部已整理的独立推理导出、历史训练适配器和诊断权重|按各条说明|不要一次性叠加|

完整主干是 **BF16 + FP32 混合存储**；文本编码器是 INT8，VAE 是 FP16。这里**不是全链路 BF16**。未重新上传官方原始十二分片、视频全模型、优化器状态或训练缓存；完整转换主干与本研究的独立模型导出集中在本仓库，第三方文件来源分别标注。

文件大小、SHA256、来源、修改状态见 [模型清单](MODEL_INDEX.md) 和 [机器可读清单](MODEL_MANIFEST.json)。体积单位 GB/MB 为十进制。不要直接下载整个历史实验目录当成一个模型。

## 安装与复现

线上主干和 direct MLP100 文件名带 `-T8`，权重内容不变。若你已下载旧名文件，无需重下；在工作流中从加载器下拉菜单重新选择本地文件即可。

使用支持 MiniMax H3 Image 的 ComfyUI。研究环境基于 ComfyUI `989d93d0d`；需要原生 `MiniMaxH3ImageConditioning`、`LoraLoaderBypassModelOnly`、`ManualSigmas` 和 `CFGGuider`。如果节点不存在，请更新到包含这些节点的版本；不要用普通 LoRA 合并加载器替代旁路加载器。

1. 按上表放置主干、文本编码器、VAE、direct MLP100。
2. 安装 [H3 Image Single Head · T8](https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8)，然后重启 ComfyUI。节点仓库已包含所需头资产，无需另下；安装命令见下方。如果已安装旧的 `h3_image_single_head`，请移出旧目录，避免重复加载。
3. 导入 [workflows/direct_mlp](workflows/direct_mlp) 下普通 `.json`；`.api.json` 是程序提交格式，不是普通界面工作流。
4. 照片编辑示例先将 [inputs/prepared.png](inputs/prepared.png) 保存到 `ComfyUI/input/prepared.png`，然后在 LoadImage 中选中它。可以换自己的图片，但不应把换图结果当成本仓库固定样本复现。
5. 使用工作流保存的显式 51 点 sigma 表，不需要再叠加 SHIFT 节点；保留正条件与单独的空文本负条件。图像编辑时正负分支均携带同一参考图。

在 ComfyUI 根目录执行以下命令安装节点（也可下载 GitHub ZIP 解压至 `custom_nodes`）：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8.git custom_nodes/Comfyui-h3-image-single-head-T8
```

搜索节点 **H3 Image 单头多步（实验）**，节点 ID 为 `H3ImageSingleHead`。[Hugging Face 节点镜像](custom_nodes/h3_image_single_head) 与 GitHub 二选一安装，不要同时安装。

多步加载顺序：

```text
UNETLoader → H3ImageSingleHead → LoraLoaderBypassModelOnly → CFGGuider
```

单头节点必须紧接未经 LoRA 修改的主干。均值头只是发布六组 PDD 头按区间加权得到的单头，不是蒸馏前教师头；节点只修改内存中的克隆，不覆盖主干文件。修正 LoRA 用 **+1，不是 -1**。不要叠加旧 v2、PAI 或其它实验补偿。

文生图九项为 2048×2048，照片编辑为 2048×1344。实际运行硬件是 RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB / 128 GB RAM；66 GB 权重需要大量系统内存与卸载，16 GB 显存实测能跑不代表低内存机器同样可跑，也不保证速度。不同硬件、算子和 ComfyUI 版本不保证逐像素一致。

[workflows/native_pdd6](workflows/native_pdd6) 保留完整发布模型的六步生成/编辑示例。使用发布 PDD 日程与 BasicGuider（等效 CFG1），**不接单头节点、不加载修正 LoRA**。这一路线用于原发布模型验证，不是去蒸馏。

# MiniMax H3 Ref2VA (pruned) Q8_0 GGUF for Nightmare Mobile

The MiniMax H3 reference-to-video denoiser (Ref2VA, Comfy-Org's pruned build) as Q8_0 GGUFs for the Hexagon NPU path
of [Nightmare Mobile](https://github.com/AbrahamPaulJ/nightmare-mobile), an on-device image and video generation app
for Android. Built with MiniMax H3. Test builds: the app's catalogue does not offer them yet.

| file | what | size |
|---|---|---|
| `h3_ref2va_pruned_q8_0.gguf` | the base model; use with Comfy-Org's ref2v turbo 4-step LoRA v0.1 at run time | 21,583,324,256 B |
| `h3_ref2va_pruned_turbo_q8_0.gguf` | the same with that LoRA merged in before quantizing; no LoRA at run time | 21,583,324,256 B |

## What was changed

These are modified files, not upstream releases. The layout, header and 324 F32 tensors (the AdaLN curve table, the
per-block AdaLN projections at its knots, norms, patch and condition projections) are those of our Q4_0 Ref2VA GGUF,
copied unchanged. The 208 large linear layers are quantized to Q8_0 straight from Comfy-Org's pruned bf16 Ref2VA
safetensors. Relative error against the bf16 weights: about 0.0055 (our Q4_0: about 0.11).

The turbo file adds `scale * B @ A` of `minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors` to each of those
linears first, scale = alpha / rank = 0.0625 (the LoRA's own training scale).

## Use

Four Euler steps, CFG 1, with H3's video VAE and audio VAE, the reference pictures as Ref2VA conditions; in the app the
text encoder is Qwen3-VL-4B with [NicoLab28's ClipProj](https://huggingface.co/NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3).

# MiniMax-H3-Image ## Online API Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via API. - Global: [platform.minimax.io](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/image-generation) | CN: [platform.minimax.cn](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/guides/image-generation) API docs: - Text-to-image: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations) - Image editing: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits) - Prompt expansion: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir) ## Online App Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via App. - WebApp Global: [hailuoai.video](https://hailuoai.video/) | CN: [hailuoai.com](https://hailuoai.com/) - Desktop Global: [agent.minimax.io](https://agent.minimax.io/) | CN: [agent.minimax.cn](https://agent.minimax.cn) ## Introduction MiniMax-H3-Image is a state-of-the-art open-source model for image generation and editing from the [MiniMax H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) family. It combines intelligent understanding of creative intent with the ability to build visual worlds: with precise instruction following, it develops a creative concept into concrete characters, scenes and atmosphere. Generation and editing are unified in one checkpoint, which generates images from text (text-to-image) and edits one or more reference images (image editing), giving creators and developers a flexible and controllable way to create images. It generates images of about 16 megapixels at every aspect ratio, from 4096x4096 (1:1) to 6272x2688 (21:9), directly and without an upscaler (see [Sizes](#sizes)). The checkpoint is distilled to 6 sampling steps (6 NFEs) with no classifier-free guidance. Its diffusion transformer (DiT) has the H3 architecture without the audio layers, and it uses the MiniMax-H3 text encoder unchanged. ![Fifteen MiniMax-H3-Image text-to-image results in landscape and portrait formats: a 3D fantasy battle, a blue-green landscape painting, a tree frog, an indigo-dyed rabbit, a 3D white-haired girl, a portrait among flowers, a sci-fi city, dumplings, a highland cow, a mirror portrait, a 3D otter and sheep, a pixel art cat, a jewel beetle, giant cherries and a fisheye selfie](assets/showcase_hero.jpg) **Highlights** MiniMax-H3-Image brings together three core strengths: speed, image quality, and instruction following. 1. **16-megapixel images at a practical computational cost.** Compared with the 1–4 MP outputs common today, 16 MP (4096 × 4096) images offer far more detail but typically require substantially more computation. # FLUX.3-image-klein NPU BFP16 weights

**Run with VigenFlow:** [GitHub repository](https://github.com/jia1217/vigenflow) · [Installation guide](https://github.com/jia1217/vigenflow#-quick-install) · [Latest release](https://github.com/jia1217/vigenflow/releases/latest)

Pre-converted weights for **text-to-image** (and, in a later release, image editing) with
[VigenFlow](https://github.com/jia1217/vigenflow) on AMD Ryzen AI 300-series processors (XDNA2).

The upstream model is [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein),
converted from revision `09561231f44e41381c461caf53d5452005a60ac9`.

**License:** these weights are a Derivative of a FLUX Model and are distributed under the
[FLUX Kommunity License v.1.0](LICENSE) of Black Forest Labs Inc. Non-commercial use only, except
that Qualifying Users (under US$5 million annual revenue, including affiliates) may use Outputs
commercially as the license describes. Read the license before downloading or using the weights.

## Performance

Measured with VigenFlow for one **1024 × 1024** image on an **AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370**,
using CPU + XDNA 2 NPU inference and BFP16 weights.

| Task | VigenFlow model ID | Denoising steps | Approx. inference time |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text-to-image | `flux3-klein` | 16 | ~32 s |

These approximate inference-stage timings exclude model loading, process startup/shutdown,
queue wait and network transfer; the full request takes longer. Results vary with
the prompt, image size, runtime version and system configuration.

## Package

- Format: `vgf-npu-weights-1`.
- 3 safetensors shards, approximately 10.6 GiB in total.
- 984 packed file entries, including `LICENSE`, `Notice` and `prepare_manifest.json`.
- Local model folder: `all_model_weights/flux3_image_klein/`.

| Folder | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `dit/` | FLUX.3 transformer: BFP16 NPU matrices and bf16 CPU tensors |
| `text/` | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct language-model layers (the FLUX.3 text encoder), BFP16 NPU matrices |
| `vae_decoder_packed_weights/`, `vae_encoder_packed_weights/` | the autoencoder in NPU layouts |

Each shard entry is a flat U8 byte vector named by a relative path inside the prepared model folder.
Matrix weights use BFP16 and the memory layout required by the NPU kernels; other tensors retain
the formats required by the runtime. These archives are not directly loadable as Diffusers or
PyTorch checkpoints.

## Download with VigenFlow

Use a VigenFlow release that includes FLUX.3 (v0.2.0-beta.6 or newer); its
`prepare/prepare_models.jsonc` already lists this repository. From the release directory:

```bash
# Ubuntu: download and unpack this model
./prepare/prepare_base.exe --only flux3_image_klein
```

```powershell
# Windows: download and unpack this model
.\prepare\prepare_base.exe --only flux3_image_klein
```

`prepare_base.exe` prints the FLUX Kommunity License link and downloads only after you type
`I agree`; `--accept_license` accepts it for unattended runs. The preparer resumes downloads and
removes downloaded shards after unpacking unless `--keep_sources` is supplied. NPU binaries and the
application are provided by the VigenFlow release, separately from these weights.

For a custom configuration, add the entry from
[prepare_models.jsonc](https://huggingface.co/Kelsey1217/FLUX.3-image-klein-NPU-BFP16/resolve/main/prepare_models.jsonc?download=true)
to your `models` list.

BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH USE OF THIS MODEL.

These weights have been modified: matrix weights are converted to BFP16, arranged in NPU memory
layouts, and transposed or zero-padded where required; the converted files are packed as U8
safetensors entries. See [NOTICE](NOTICE). This is an independent conversion, not an official

# ClipProj for MiniMax-H3 — GGUF

These projection weights let a smaller Qwen3-VL text encoder replace the Qwen3-VL-32B encoder across the MiniMax-H3 family. MiniMax-H3 video, MiniMax-H3-Image and P-H3-Image share the same 5,120-dimensional text conditioning, so one matrix works with all three. They are not standalone generation models. The diffusion model, matching text encoder and VAEs are not included.

## Files

| File | Matching encoder | Projection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mmh3-4b-ClipProj-v3.1.gguf` | Qwen3-VL-4B | Ridge |
| `mmh3-4b-ClipProj-v3.1-mlp.gguf` | Qwen3-VL-4B | MLP |
| `mmh3-8b-ClipProj-v3.1.gguf` | Qwen3-VL-8B | Ridge |
| `mmh3-8b-ClipProj-v3.1-mlp.gguf` | Qwen3-VL-8B | MLP |
| `mmh3-2b-ClipProj-v1.gguf` | Qwen3-VL-2B | Legacy v1 |
| `mmh3-2b-ClipProj-v1-mlp.gguf` | Qwen3-VL-2B | Legacy v1, MLP |

Start with a v3.1 file that matches your encoder size. The `-mlp` files are larger. The 2B files are included as legacy variants; their runtime compatibility and exact source revision have not been verified here.

## Usage

Build the [Romara Labs fork of stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/romara-labs/stable-diffusion.cpp) using its [patch build instructions](https://github.com/romara-labs/stable-diffusion.cpp/tree/master/patch). Add these flags to any MiniMax-H3 generation command, video or image:

```sh
--llm /path/to/qwen3-vl-4b.gguf \
--cliproj /path/to/mmh3-4b-ClipProj-v3.1.gguf
```

Works with MiniMax-H3 video, MiniMax-H3-Image and P-H3-Image. On P-H3-Image, `--cliproj` takes precedence over the P-H3 text connector when both are present. Use the matching vision tower with `--llm_vision` if your encoder stores it separately. The custom `clipproj` GGUF architecture is not a standalone `llama.cpp` model.

The matrices were calibrated on video prompts. Text-to-image works with the same matrices, but image quality has not been systematically validated, and reference-image or reference-video workflows are not validated here.

## Source and licensing

The v3.1 files are GGUF conversions of the projection weights from [NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3). Credit goes to the original project. The conversion preserves tensor precision and does not add quantization. The legacy v1 files predate the v3.1 series; their exact source revision on the original repository could not be confirmed here.

The license is the same for v1 and v3.1: these projections are calibrated for and bound to the MiniMax-H3 research. Use and redistribution of every file in this repository follow the [MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/LICENSE), as declared in this repo's license metadata.

# EZVR Flash V1 · SeedVR2 3B INT8 DiT

此仓库发布 EZVideoRepair 使用的量化 DiT 权重。210 个线性层矩阵采用逐输出通道对称 INT8，量化值范围为 −127 至 127，每行配一个 BF16 比例因子。其余张量保持源精度。VAE 和后处理沿用基础仓库的文件。

`dit-1.safetensors` 使用 EZVR 专用打包格式。量化张量在 safetensors 头中声明为 BF16 容器，实际载荷顺序为全部行的 INT8 数据，再接所有行的 BF16 比例因子。推理需要匹配的 DiT 图及 `ezvr_demo::w8linear` 算子。基础权重版本及其 VAE 见[固定版本](https://huggingface.co/whitelok/seedvr2-hybricprecision-3b/tree/4aedb55b384131a3a475dbed228110a510f4a85b)。

This repository distributes the quantized DiT weights used by EZVideoRepair. The converter quantized 210 linear weight matrices to symmetric, per-output-channel INT8 in the range −127 to 127, with one BF16 scale per row. Other tensors retain their source precision. The VAE and postprocessing weights are available in the base repository.

The EZVR packing format uses BF16 containers in the safetensors header. Each quantized matrix stores all signed INT8 rows followed by their BF16 scales. Inference requires the matching DiT graph and the `ezvr_demo::w8linear` operator. See the [pinned source revision](https://huggingface.co/whitelok/seedvr2-hybricprecision-3b/tree/4aedb55b384131a3a475dbed228110a510f4a85b) for the base weights and VAE.

# MMH3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-NVFP4A16

Weight-only **NVFP4A16** (`nvfp4-pack-quantized`, W4A16) quantization of [lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA), created with `llm-compressor`.

## Notes
Hey.  This is a basic repackage/quant of light2x's excellent model.
It was quanted with very basic instructions/settings.
If there are ways to improve it, please let me know and I'll be happy to re-repackage it.

This was set with Grace Blackwell / GB10 stuff in mind.  DGX Spark, specifically.
The overall footprint was squashed from ~55 GB to ~ 19GB in VRAM requirements.
This allows it to run much more comfortably in a ComfyUI environment, allowing a
bit more breathing room for tertiary model-parking and all that.

Notes on Serving on GB10 (SM121)
On GB10 (SM121), NVFP4A16 executes through vLLM's Marlin / CUTLASS W4A16 GEMM 
path automatically. 

So sayeth the S2: Fight in the shade, my friends.


## Quantization Details
- **Scheme:** `NVFP4A16` (4-bit FP4 weights, 16-bit BF16 activations)
- **Scope:** Language model backbone `Linear` layers quantized; `lm_head`, vision tower (`visual`), audio/projector modules, and `mtp` kept in native `bfloat16`.
- **Footprint:** ~18.8 GiB VRAM in vLLM (down from ~55.6 GB in BF16).

## Serving with vLLM
```bash
vllm serve 4kun/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-NVFP4A16 \
  --served-model-name MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":50,"video":0}' \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true,"reasoning_effort":"xhigh"}' \
  --override-generation-config '{"temperature":0.7,"top_p":0.8,"top_k":20,"max_new_tokens":16384}'

GGUF for MiniMax-H3, compatible on most platforms including stablediffusion.cpp and Unsloth. # Run MiniMax-H3 locally You can run MiniMax-H3 via Unsloth: https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/ GGUF quantizations of [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) MiniMax H3 is an omni-modal generative system that produces video with native stereo audio, up to 15 seconds at 24 FPS with 32 kHz stereo audio. Both halves of the runtime are in this repo: the denoisers and the Qwen3-VL text encoder they need. H3 ships two denoisers, and which one you load decides what the model can be given: - **`fl2va_pruned`**, the H3-Base first-and-last-frame variant. Text, plus zero, one or two frames. - **`ref2va_pruned`**, the reference variant. Text, plus reference pictures, videos and audio. They are separate checkpoints, not settings, so pick the one that matches the task. Both are quantized here at the same rungs, so a given quant costs about the same either way. ## Example `UD-Q2_K_XL`, the smallest rung here, at 960x544, 124 frames, 24 FPS, 8 steps, guidance 1.0, seed 11, on a single card. > a red panda stepping along a mossy log in a misty forest, cinematic The GIF is downsampled and silent. For the full 960x544 clip with its native 32 kHz stereo audio track, play [`assets/h3_gguf_ud_q2_k_xl.mp4`](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/blob/main/assets/h3_gguf_ud_q2_k_xl.mp4). H3 generates the audio jointly with the video, so the audio is part of the model output rather than something added afterwards. ## Files Text and frames, `fl2va_pruned`: | File | Size | |---|---| | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q2_K.gguf` | 6.26 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-UD-Q2_K_XL.gguf` | 7.51 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q3_K.gguf` | 8.16 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf` | 8.90 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q4_K.gguf` | 10.64 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q5_0.gguf` | 12.97 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q6_K.gguf` | 15.45 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q8_0.gguf` | 19.97 GiB | References, `ref2va_pruned`: | File | Size | |---|---| | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q2_K.gguf` | 6.22 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q3_K.gguf` | 8.12 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q4_K.gguf` | 10.60 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q5_0.gguf` | 12.94 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q6_K.gguf` | 15.42 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q8_0.gguf` | 19.94 GiB | Text encoder, shared by both: | File | Size | |---|---| | `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q2_K_M.gguf` | 12.20 GiB | | `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 16.97 GiB | The `UD-` rungs are dynamic, mixed-precision builds. The uniform rungs hold one type throughout. Pair the `Q2_K_M` text encoder with the two smallest denoisers and the `Q4_K_M` one with everything else. The text encoder and the VAEs are shared, so switching between the two denoisers costs one denoiser download and nothing else. The VAEs are not duplicated here, take them from [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3). ```bash sd-cli --mode vid_gen \ --diffusion-model minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-UD-Q2_K_XL.gguf \ --llm qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q2_K_M.gguf \ --vae minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors \ --audio-vae minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors \ --prompt "a red fox trotting through falling snow, cinematic" \ --width 640 --height 384 --video-frames 25 --steps 4 --cfg-scale 1.0 \ --backend te=cpu --diffusion-fa \ --output out.webm ``` Three flags are not optional. `--mode vid_gen`, or H3 takes the image path and aborts. Explicit `--cfg-scale 1.0`, because H3 is distilled and cfg-free and aborts above 1.0 while the default is 7.0. And `--backend te=cpu`, which keeps the 12 GB text encoder off the card. Add `--offload-to-cpu` to fit a smaller GPU. # MiniMax-H3-Image MLX

MLX builds of [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), made by Moonbox for Apple Silicon Macs. Each precision is a folder that holds the
whole text-to-image pipeline: the transformer, the text encoder, the VAE decoder and `mlx_model.py`, the one file
that runs them. Keep a folder's files together.

## What is in a folder

| Folder | Transformer | Whole folder | First step vs bf16 | Worst block | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `8bit/` | 8 bits, 21.4 GB | 37.2 GB | 0.015 - 0.026 | 0.9998 | passes |
| `6bit/` | 6 bits, 16.4 GB | 32.2 GB | 0.025 - 0.057 | 0.9993 | passes |
| `4bit/` | 4 bits, the last 18 of its 50 blocks at 6 bits: 13.2 GB | 28.9 GB | 0.055 - 0.094 | 0.9972 | passes the two marks; pictures drift from `6bit/` (see below) |

Every folder also holds the same text encoder (`text_encoder/`, 14.2 GB: the first 50 layers of Qwen3-VL-32B at
4 bits) and the same VAE decoder (`vae/`, 1.6 GB, float32), so one folder is everything a picture needs.

- **First step vs bf16**: relative L2 distance of the velocity the build predicts at the first of the six sampling
  steps from the unquantized model's, same prompt and noise, over four cases (three prompts at 1024 x 1024, one at
  512 x 512). Our mark is 0.10.
- **Worst block**: each of the 50 blocks is fed the unquantized model's input and its output compared (cosine).
  Our mark is 0.995.
- **Why `4bit/` is not 4 bits throughout.** At 4 bits everywhere the first step is 0.09 - 0.20 from bf16 and the
  worst block at 0.9947: under both marks. The damage is in the last blocks (each of blocks 2 - 16 alone stays within
  0.5 % of bf16; blocks 34 - 38 are 8 % off), so `4bit/` keeps 4 bits for blocks 0 - 31 and uses the 6-bit weights
  for blocks 32 - 49: 1.9 GB more, and both marks are met. `config.json` lists the bits of every block
  (`mlx_quantization.block_bits`).
- The unquantized model (40 GB) doesn't fit a 24 GB Mac, so there is no bf16 picture to compare with: the numbers
  above were taken while the bf16 weights passed through memory during conversion, and repeated on the finished
  `6bit/` and `4bit/` files. Then the same three prompts were rendered from the same noise at 1024 x 1024 with
  `6bit/` and `4bit/`, and looked at: both make correct pictures of the prompts with the same composition. Against
  the `6bit/` pictures, `4bit/` is at LPIPS 0.16 on average and 0.24 at worst (PSNR 20.7 dB); 4 bits throughout
  would be at 0.26 / 0.28 (17.6 dB). Our mark for pictures is 0.15 against a reference, so count `4bit/` as the
  small build whose details differ, not as a copy of `6bit/`.
- `8bit/` was larger than the disk space we had free during conversion: its numbers come from the conversion pass
  and its files were checked by size and sha256 on upload. Afterwards it was downloaded again and two
  1024 x 1024 pictures of one prompt were rendered with `stream=True`: correct pictures, the lettering the prompt
  asks for included. They were looked at, not measured against the `6bit/` pictures.

## How to run

Needs `mlx`, `numpy`, `tokenizers` and `pillow` (no PyTorch). Download one folder and use the `mlx_model.py` in it:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
folder = snapshot_download("moonbox-dev/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX", allow_patterns="4bit/*") + "/4bit"

import sys; sys.path.insert(0, folder)
from mlx_model import Pipeline

pipe = Pipeline(folder)                       # Pipeline(folder, stream=True): one transformer block in memory at a time
image = pipe.generate("a red fox in fresh snow at sunrise, photo", width=1024, height=1024, seed=0)
image.save("fox.png")
```

# Lucia 2B v1.2: Qwen3.5-2B, think symbolic image

**Lucia 2B v1.2** is a LoRA adapter of [Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B) that looks at a picture and
writes a reading of it: a short chain of plain-language thoughts, one named step per line, then the wordings (a caption, a
prompt, tags, a critique, by depth), then the questions a careful looker would still ask, each with its answer and what settles
it. Version 1.2 is the recipe of [Lucia 4B v1.2](https://huggingface.co/AbstractPhil/qwen3.5-4b-think-symbolic-image) at 2B:
the same rows, taught once, with a second objective that keeps her near her base model.

- **More than four times the rows.** She was taught 91,138 rows (version 1: 20,836), the rows Lucia 4B v1.2 was taught:
  the Apache-2.0 part of [release 5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned/tree/cac40b93d7b063aafd0cb70d3c1b1a7a100562ef) of [thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned)
  as anyone can read it there (95,481 rows), less 3,718 rows on COCO 2017 photographs under other licenses,
  609 rows on the pictures the reads below hold out and 16 rows whose pictures no store holds.
  They are readings of DOCCI and COCO 2017 photographs, of National Gallery of Art pictures and of drawn specifications, written
  by OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek models and admitted by a blind review; 30,250 of them are long looks. No row she was
  taught was written by a Claude model, or by any model of this project trained on rows a Claude model wrote. Training shows her
  the picture of every row about a picture (the drawn specifications have none), so the COCO 2017 photographs she saw are only
  those whose Flickr authors gave them the Attribution license or that carry no known copyright restrictions, in her rows and in
  the ordinary requests below alike.
- **One pass.** She was taught her rows once (10,137 steps); version 1 was taught hers twice (2,724 steps).
- **The base model kept**, new at 2B: a second objective in training holds her next-word choices near Qwen3.5-2B's on ordinary
  requests that Qwen3.5-2B answered itself for this version, so the adapter changes how she answers when asked for a reading
  and little else. On held-out ordinary requests she stays close to the base model, and of the questions and text requests
  among them she answers none in the reading's form; version 1, trained without it, answers 270 of the 326 that way.
- **Lettering left out of the closer look.** Of 300 held-out pictures with readable lettering, 245 have no person's name, credit
  or web address in their lettering. Of those 245, her closer look names a word the picture shows for 57, where the
  base model's free description names one for 160; her long look names one for 119. Asked directly what the
  lettering says, her answer names it about as often as the base model's does (0.93 of the pictures against
  0.88).

Version 1 stays in this repository at the tag `lucia-v1`.

What she writes for a closer look at a held-out COCO 2017 photograph ([376084](https://cocodataset.org/#explore?id=376084), its author's Attribution license), verbatim:

```
see: One yellow truck sits at the center of the frame, alone as the picture's single subject.
place: The truck is parked on a road, with grass and trees around it.
mood: Its parked state suggests a gentle pause, with the truck held still on the road.
caption: A yellow truck is parked at the center of the frame on a road, with grass and trees around it.
prompt: yellow truck, parked on a road, grass and trees, single subject, photograph
tags: yellow truck, parked truck, road, grass, trees, photograph
question: thing name -> truck [record]
question: thing colour -> yellow [record]
question: thing state -> parked [record]
question: scene layout -> single subject [record]
question: form rhythm -> unknown [unknown]
```

The steps a chain may use, in the order a careful looker takes them: `see`, `name`, `place`, `count`, `relate`, `form`,
`light`, `colour`, `mood`, `mean`, `intend`, `story`, `compare`, `change`, `check`, `say`. A quick look holds 1 to 2 thoughts,
a closer look 3 to 5, a long look 6 to 10. Questions end in `[record]` (the answer is a fact of the picture), `[chain]` (the
chain worked it out) or `[unknown]`. The prompt line often opens with the kind of picture (a close-up photograph, an overhead
photograph); unlike version 1, she was not taught to open it that way every time.

# MiniMax H3 Image: ComfyUI workflows for 8, 12 and 16 GB VRAM

Three versions of one ComfyUI workflow for **MiniMax H3 Image**. **All three make full 16 MP images** (3:4 = 3552x4736, 16:9 = 5472x3072), even on an 8 GB card. ComfyUI streams the model through the card in parts, so a smaller card gives **the same image, only slower**. Pick the file that matches your VRAM and drag it into ComfyUI.

| File | For | Final image | Draft | VAE decode | Reference pictures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minimax_h3_image_8gb_vram.json` | 8 GB cards | 16 MP | 4 MP | Tiled (512) | 10 slots, 4 or fewer is fastest |
| `minimax_h3_image_12gb_vram.json` | 12 GB cards | 16 MP | 4 MP | Tiled (768) | 10 slots, 4 or fewer is fastest |
| `minimax_h3_image_16gb_vram.json` | 16 GB+ cards | 16 MP | 4 MP | Normal | 10 slots |

### What you need for an 8 GB card

- **GPU:** NVIDIA with 8 GB VRAM (tested: ComfyUI used at most 3.7 GB VRAM for a 16 MP image).
- **System RAM:** 24 GB or more (tested with 24 GB), 32 GB is safer. The models are bigger than the card, so ComfyUI keeps them in RAM and streams them in parts.
- **Disk:** about 38 GB free, on an SSD.
- **ComfyUI:** a recent version (MiniMax H3 nodes are built in, no custom nodes).
- **3 model files**, the same full-quality files as the 16 GB version, **no GGUF**: the image model (21 GB), the main text encoder `nvfp4` (15.7 GB) and the VAE (1.2 GB). Links are in [Model files](#model-files).
- **Not needed:** the prompt upsampler `qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors`. It is switched off in the 8 GB workflow because it makes images very slow on 8 GB.

### Measured render times

Tested on an RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB) with 24 GB of system RAM. For 12 GB and 8 GB, part of the card's memory was filled by a dummy program, so ComfyUI only had the VRAM a real 12 GB or 8 GB card has free. With the same seed, all three gave **pixel-for-pixel the same image**.

| Job | 16 GB | 12 GB | 8 GB |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text-to-image, 16 MP | 66 s | 63 s | 60 s |
| Time per step (6 steps) | 4.4 s | 4.8 s | 5.7 s |
| 4 reference pictures, 16 MP | - | - | 228 s (about 4 min) |
| 4 reference pictures, 8 MP | - | - | 156 s (about 2.5 min) |

Real 8 GB and 12 GB cards (RTX 4060, 3060, 4070 ...) have slower chips than the test card, so expect longer times. The memory limit itself is not a problem.

## Example images

Made with this workflow, straight out of ComfyUI with no editing or upscaling. Click an image to open the full-size original PNG (5472x3072, 16 MP). All originals are in the [`examples`](https://huggingface.co/vyrekai/minimax-h3-image-comfyui-workflows/tree/main/examples) folder.

| | |
|---|---|
| [![Tortoise island](examples/previews/01_tortoise_island.jpg)](examples/01_tortoise_island.png) | [![Teacup tsunami](examples/previews/02_teacup_tsunami.jpg)](examples/02_teacup_tsunami.png) |
| [![Book canyon](examples/previews/03_book_canyon.jpg)](examples/03_book_canyon.png) | [![Moon hatching](examples/previews/04_moon_hatching.jpg)](examples/04_moon_hatching.png) |
| [![Lightbulb orchard](examples/previews/05_lightbulb_orchard.jpg)](examples/05_lightbulb_orchard.png) | [![Mirror desert](examples/previews/06_mirror_desert.jpg)](examples/06_mirror_desert.png) |
| [![Octopus pizza](examples/previews/07_octopus_pizza.jpg)](examples/07_octopus_pizza.png) | [![Bathroom mirror](examples/previews/08_bathroom_mirror.jpg)](examples/08_bathroom_mirror.png) |

The octopus pizza is 3840x2176 (8 MP); all others are 5472x3072 (16 MP).

## Prompt guide: let any AI write your prompts

[`MINIMAX_H3_IMAGE_PROMPT_GUIDE.md`](MINIMAX_H3_IMAGE_PROMPT_GUIDE.md) teaches an AI chatbot how to write prompts for this model. Drop the file into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or a local model, then ask for what you want, for example:

- *"Using this guide, write me a prompt for a rainy Tokyo street at night with a woman holding a red umbrella."*
- *"Using this guide, write an edit prompt: Picture 1 is my living room, make it sunset and add a cat on the sofa."*
- *"Using this guide, put the man from Picture 1 into the café from Picture 2."*

It answers with a finished prompt plus the settings to use (aspect ratio, draft or full size). Paste the prompt into the **PROMPT** box and leave *Enhance prompt* off, because the prompt is already long.

The guide covers text-to-image, single-picture edits and multi-reference scenes, plus realistic skin, hands, body direction, text in images, and fixes for common problems.

## What is in the workflow

- **Prompt box** with an optional **Enhance prompt** switch: a Qwen3.5 9B upsampler rewrites a short idea into a long, detailed caption (text-to-image only).
- **Aspect ratio picker** (1:1, 3:4, 4:3, 2:3, 3:2, 9:16, 16:9, 21:9) and a **full / draft switch**. Use the draft size to test prompts quickly.
- **Ten reference picture slots** for editing and multi-image prompts. They are all bypassed by de

# Qwen Image 2.1 Anime FUSAL

[![Try in Spaces](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Try%20in%20Spaces-FUSAL%20Anime%20Playground-blue)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/MicksHF/Qwen-Image-2.1-Anime-Fusal-Playground)

> [!TIP]
> **Update — Original (Non-Turbo) V3 Released (`fusal-qwen-image-2.1-v3-exact-r80.safetensors`)!**
> - **Cardboard / rough paper texture fixed:** V3 eliminates the unintended toothy cardboard/sandpaper grain ("cardboard smudge") that previously leaked onto smooth skin and cel-shaded surfaces in V2 by locking late text-blind pixel-decoder `img_mlp` blocks and routing style adaptation through front/mid text-aware attention layers.
> - **Five controllable anime rendering styles:** V3 now supports **5 distinct style trigger phrases** — **Flat Cel**, **Clean Modern Cel**, **Polished Semi-Impasto**, **Heavy Painterly / Gouache**, and **Watercolor Wash & Ink Sketch** (see [Five style triggers in V3](#five-style-triggers-in-v3) below).
> - **Standard (Non-Turbo) vs. Turbo notice:** **All showcase and comparison images in this README are generated with the Standard (Non-Turbo / Original) model (`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`).** The **Turbo LoRA is an experimental preview only** and incurs **significant quality and capability loss** because step-distilled Turbo models struggle to learn nuanced art styles and domain knowledge. Use **Original R80 V3** for full style fidelity and control (see [Standard (Non-Turbo) vs. Turbo — why they differ](#standard-non-turbo-vs-turbo--why-they-differ)).

[![Original R80 V2 example — view prompt and inference parameters](images/example-prompt.png)](#example-prompt-and-inference-parameters)

[View this image’s prompt and inference parameters ↓](#example-prompt-and-inference-parameters)

### Please read before generating

> **Prompt format:** Please follow the structured [Prompt format](#prompt-format) and examples below rather than using only a free-form, chat-style instruction. Start with `fusal style.`, then organize your description under `[TASK: ...]`, `[Subject]`, `[Appearance]`, `[Pose]`, `[Composition]`, `[Environment]`, `[Lighting]`, and `[Style]` as appropriate. Natural-language descriptions belong inside these sections; omit sections that are not relevant.
>
> **LoRA strength: start at 0.7.** For either FUSAL adapter on its matching base model, start at **0.7** (also the public Playground default), then adjust within **0.7–1.0** according to the result. Increase toward **1.0** if you want a stronger effect (or crisp 5-style separation on V3). This is the **LoRA/model strength**, not CFG; keep CFG / true CFG at **1.0**.
>
> **Sampling steps:** Start with **25 steps** for the Original (non-Turbo) base + LoRA; this is also the public Playground default. In the author's testing, **20 steps** can already give good results for anime illustrations with simple layouts. For complex compositions or reference-heavy scenes, try **30–40** if needed and compare results. More steps are not a guarantee of better quality. **Turbo remains fixed at 8 steps** with its matching base and sampling schedule.

**Built with Qwen. For adults and research use only.**

This repository publishes **two separate FUSAL Anime LoRA families for two different base checkpoints**. Choose the adapter that matches your base model; they are not interchangeable.

| LoRA | Required base model | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Original Base: Exact R80 V3 (Recommended)** | [`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) | **Latest primary Original-Base release — cardboard texture fixed + 5 style triggers** |
| Original Base: Exact R80 V2 (Legacy) | [`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) | Retained earlier Original-Base release for existing workflows |
| **Turbo E6 Preview R128** | [`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) | **Experimental preview only — significant style & knowledge loss vs. Original** |

**Do not load an original-Base LoRA on Turbo, and do not load the Turbo LoRA on the original Base. Do not stack V3 with V2 or with Turbo.** Replace V2 directly with V3 on `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`.

The matching BF16 Heretic text encoder **is included**, because training cached prompt and reference embeddings with that encoder. **All showcase images, Base-vs-LoRA comparisons, and examples in this README were generated using the Standard (non-Turbo) Original Base model — never the Turbo preview.**

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

Native transparent image generation

GGUF for MiniMax-H3, compatible on most platforms including stablediffusion.cpp and Unsloth. # Run MiniMax-H3 locally You can run MiniMax-H3 via Unsloth: https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/ GGUF quantizations of [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) MiniMax H3 is an omni-modal generative system that produces video with native stereo audio, up to 15 seconds at 24 FPS with 32 kHz stereo audio. Both halves of the runtime are in this repo: the denoisers and the Qwen3-VL text encoder they need. H3 ships two denoisers, and which one you load decides what the model can be given: - **`fl2va_pruned`**, the H3-Base first-and-last-frame variant. Text, plus zero, one or two frames. - **`ref2va_pruned`**, the reference variant. Text, plus reference pictures, videos and audio. They are separate checkpoints, not settings, so pick the one that matches the task. Both are quantized here at the same rungs, so a given quant costs about the same either way. ## Example `UD-Q2_K_XL`, the smallest rung here, at 960x544, 124 frames, 24 FPS, 8 steps, guidance 1.0, seed 11, on a single card. > a red panda stepping along a mossy log in a misty forest, cinematic The GIF is downsampled and silent. For the full 960x544 clip with its native 32 kHz stereo audio track, play [`assets/h3_gguf_ud_q2_k_xl.mp4`](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/blob/main/assets/h3_gguf_ud_q2_k_xl.mp4). H3 generates the audio jointly with the video, so the audio is part of the model output rather than something added afterwards. ## Files Text and frames, `fl2va_pruned`: | File | Size | |---|---| | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q2_K.gguf` | 6.26 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-UD-Q2_K_XL.gguf` | 7.51 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q3_K.gguf` | 8.16 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf` | 8.90 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q4_K.gguf` | 10.64 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q5_0.gguf` | 12.97 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q6_K.gguf` | 15.45 GiB | | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-Q8_0.gguf` | 19.97 GiB | References, `ref2va_pruned`: | File | Size | |---|---| | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q2_K.gguf` | 6.22 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q3_K.gguf` | 8.12 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q4_K.gguf` | 10.60 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q5_0.gguf` | 12.94 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q6_K.gguf` | 15.42 GiB | | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned-Q8_0.gguf` | 19.94 GiB | Text encoder, shared by both: | File | Size | |---|---| | `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q2_K_M.gguf` | 12.20 GiB | | `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 16.97 GiB | The `UD-` rungs are dynamic, mixed-precision builds. The uniform rungs hold one type throughout. Pair the `Q2_K_M` text encoder with the two smallest denoisers and the `Q4_K_M` one with everything else. The text encoder and the VAEs are shared, so switching between the two denoisers costs one denoiser download and nothing else. The VAEs are not duplicated here, take them from [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3). ```bash sd-cli --mode vid_gen \ --diffusion-model minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned-UD-Q2_K_XL.gguf \ --llm qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q2_K_M.gguf \ --vae minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors \ --audio-vae minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors \ --prompt "a red fox trotting through falling snow, cinematic" \ --width 640 --height 384 --video-frames 25 --steps 4 --cfg-scale 1.0 \ --backend te=cpu --diffusion-fa \ --output out.webm ``` Three flags are not optional. `--mode vid_gen`, or H3 takes the image path and aborts. Explicit `--cfg-scale 1.0`, because H3 is distilled and cfg-free and aborts above 1.0 while the default is 7.0. And `--backend te=cpu`, which keeps the 12 GB text encoder off the card. Add `--offload-to-cpu` to fit a smaller GPU. The pre-quantized PyTorch checkpoints are in [unsloth/MiniMax-H3-FP8](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/MiniMax-H3-FP8). ## Licence MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement, from MiniMax-H3. # MiniMax-H3-Image ## Online API Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via API. - Global: [platform.minimax.io](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/image-generation) | CN: [platform.minimax.cn](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/guides/image-generation) API docs: - Text-to-image: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-generations) - Image editing: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-edits) - Prompt expansion: [EN-docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir), [CN-docs](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/api-reference/image-generation-h3-context-ir) ## Online App Use MiniMax-H3-Image directly via App. - WebApp Global: [hailuoai.video](https://hailuoai.video/) | CN: [hailuoai.com](https://hailuoai.com/) - Desktop Global: [agent.minimax.io](https://agent.minimax.io/) | CN: [agent.minimax.cn](https://agent.minimax.cn) ## Introduction MiniMax-H3-Image is a state-of-the-art open-source model for image generation and editing from the [MiniMax H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) family. It combines intelligent understanding of creative intent with the ability to build visual worlds: with precise instruction following, it develops a creative concept into concrete characters, scenes and atmosphere. Generation and editing are unified in one checkpoint, which generates images from text (text-to-image) and edits one or more reference images (image editing), giving creators and developers a flexible and controllable way to create images. It generates images of about 16 megapixels at every aspect ratio, from 4096x4096 (1:1) to 6272x2688 (21:9), directly and without an upscaler (see [Sizes](#sizes)). The checkpoint is distilled to 6 sampling steps (6 NFEs) with no classifier-free guidance. Its diffusion transformer (DiT) has the H3 architecture without the audio layers, and it uses the MiniMax-H3 text encoder unchanged. ![Fifteen MiniMax-H3-Image text-to-image results in landscape and portrait formats: a 3D fantasy battle, a blue-green landscape painting, a tree frog, an indigo-dyed rabbit, a 3D white-haired girl, a portrait among flowers, a sci-fi city, dumplings, a highland cow, a mirror portrait, a 3D otter and sheep, a pixel art cat, a jewel beetle, giant cherries and a fisheye selfie](assets/showcase_hero.jpg) **Highlights** MiniMax-H3-Image brings together three core strengths: speed, image quality, and instruction following. 1. **16-megapixel images at a practical computational cost.** Compared with the 1–4 MP outputs common today, 16 MP (4096 × 4096) images offer far more detail but typically require substantially more computation. Replace a person in a still image with a character from a reference sheet. I trained this LoRA to bring over the character’s face, costume, and style while following the pose, framing, and lighting in the source.

[![Four matched character swaps in a 2×2 grid. Rain Rosette and Copper Eel Archivist are above Green Reptilian Adventurer and Rattler Rail Marshal. Each comparison shows the source, V1 LoRA, base H3 Image, and character reference.](assets/character-swap-comparisons.webp)](assets/character-swap-comparisons.webp)

Each comparison uses the same source, character reference, prompt, seed, and sampling settings. The V1 panel adds the LoRA at strength **1.0**. These are selected examples. Source footage for Rain Rosette comes from Blender Institute’s *Tears of Steel*, © Blender Foundation. [Project credits](https://mango.blender.org/about/) · [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/)

Source footage for Copper Eel Archivist comes from Lacoste’s *Crocodile Inside*. Rattler Rail Marshal uses footage from *When the potion seller runs out of ingredients*. [Copper Eel source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CHapY4muRRQ) · [Rattler source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qin8q_sOANo)

**[Download V1 LoRA](https://huggingface.co/akatz-ai/MiniMax-H3-Image-Character-Swap-LoRA/resolve/main/h3_image_character_swap_v1.safetensors)** · Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image

## Use in ComfyUI

1. Install the files below and open the [H3 Image Character Swap V1 workflow](examples/H3-Image-Character-Swap-V1.json) in ComfyUI. The V1 LoRA is already connected at strength **1.0**.
2. To replay Rain Rosette, put the [source frame](examples/rain-rosette-source.webp) and [Rain Rosette character sheet](examples/rain-rosette-character.webp) in `ComfyUI/input/`, or upload them through the two **Load Image** nodes. Queue the workflow with the included prompt and fixed seed.
3. For your own swap, load the source into **Image 1** and the character reference into **Image 2**. Use `<Picture 1>` and `<Picture 2>` in the prompt. If the shot has multiple people, identify the target by position, clothing, or what they are doing. Set the output dimensions to around **1 megapixel** and match the source aspect ratio.

The workflow uses native nodes and was tested in ComfyUI **0.45.0** on an RTX 4090 with dynamic VRAM. It is adapted from the [official MiniMax H3 Image Edit template](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/c8e48bdcfc7241d7af588d20d4f924caf9d9d953/templates/image_minimax_h3_image_edit.json). Place the **Licon H3 INT8 Backend** node after your model and LoRA loaders and select **Legacy INT8 (Kitchen 0.2.35)** to use the legacy comfy-kitchen backend. ## Overview **Licon VBVR** is an image-to-video LoRA for **MiniMax-H3**, trained on VBVR data rebuilt and reprocessed specifically for H3. It improves object consistency and character action logic, reducing unintended object duplication, clipping, and interpenetration during motion and interactions. ## Key Improvements - **Reduced object duplication:** fewer unintended copies of objects during generation. - **Reduced clipping and interpenetration:** improved spatial interactions between characters, objects, and surfaces. - **Improved character action logic:** more coherent movement sequences and interactions. ## Training Data The training data is derived from **[VBVR-Pro-SFT-Video](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Video-Reason/VBVR-Pro-SFT-Video)**. I rebuilt the VBVR training data around H3's characteristics, adapting data preparation and preprocessing to its training pipeline. # LTX-2.5 ComfyUI Quants by DDB

Community quantizations of the official split-weight
[`Lightricks/LTX-2.5`](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) release for
ComfyUI. The repository contains matching Dev and Distilled diffusion
transformers, the LTX-specific Gemma-4 12B text encoder with projection, and an
experimental quantized Distilled LoRA.

These are community conversions, not official Lightricks or ComfyOrg releases.

> **Pre-release validation boundary:** all 10 current artifacts passed structural and
> deep DDB-qanalyse validation. The four final transformer files were recognized
> by ComfyUI on a physical RTX 4090, the NVFP4 Gemma-4/LTX text encoder passed
> a real tokenize + forward + dual-projection smoke, and the quantized-LoRA
> runtime passed a real GPU tensor-dequantization smoke. Equal-seed
> prompt-to-decoded-video and audio quality A/B tests are still pending, so no
> perceptual-quality ranking is claimed yet.

## Naming

- `dev` is the regular configurable LTX-2.5 route.
- `distilled` is the official fixed **8-step / CFG 1** route.
- Transformer `int8-convrot` is the quality-retaining INT8 profile: 1,435
  searched INT8 matrices, ConvRot/Hadamard group size 256, and five BF16
  sensitivity islands selected by DDB-qanalyse.
- Transformer `nvfp4` is the compact profile: 1,425 searched NVFP4 matrices
  and fifteen BF16 sensitivity islands. Ada uses the supported fallback path;
  native NVFP4 acceleration is a Blackwell path.
- The transformer lineup now has only these two profiles. Existing
  text-encoder and LoRA profile names are unchanged.
- Quantized LoRAs use a DDB descriptor/runtime; stock ComfyUI LoRA loading is
  **not** claimed for them.

## Choose a profile

Choose one transformer row. Dev and Distilled use the same two-profile
layout; download only the route you intend to use.

| Profile | Dev transformer | Distilled transformer | Matching existing TE | Optional existing Distilled LoRA | Intended route |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **int8-convrot** | [20.152 GiB](https://huggingface.co/DmitryDB/LTX-2.5-ComfyUI-Quants/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.5-22b-dev-transformer-int8-convrot.safetensors?download=true) | [20.152 GiB](https://huggingface.co/DmitryDB/LTX-2.5-ComfyUI-Quants/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-int8-convrot.safetensors?download=true) | [`int8`](https://huggingface.co/DmitryDB/LTX-2.5-ComfyUI-Quants/resolve/main/text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-int8.safetensors?download=true) | [`int8`](https://huggingface.co/DmitryDB/LTX-2.5-ComfyUI-Quants/resolve/main/loras/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-lora-450-int8.safetensors?download=true) | Highest retained transformer precision; use ComfyUI offload on a 24 GiB GPU. |

The retired transformer Lean profile saved only about 127.9 MiB by quantizing
five matrices which the source analysis marked as sensitivity islands, so it
was removed. File size is not complete-workflow peak VRAM; resolution, frame
count, audio, attention, TE, VAEs, upscalers, and offload also matter.

## Dev v2 searched rebuild

Both **Dev and Distilled** transformers were rebuilt from their exact
official BF16 bytes. The v2 rebuild preserves separate Q/K/V and replaces the
old fixed/simple scale path with exhaustive FP32 MSE scale selection:

- `int8-convrot`: 101 scale candidates from 1.00 to 0.80 per selected matrix,
  then stock-compatible INT8 ConvRot g256 storage;
- `nvfp4`: 101 scale candidates from 1.00 to 0.50 per 16-value block, stored in
  the stock Comfy NVFP4 wire format.

Every final transformer is bound to its source SHA-256, tensor-schema digest,
policy digest, kernel digest, Qfabrik build lock, output SHA-256, and a real
stock-ComfyUI load plus quantized-projection smoke on an RTX 4090.

# RelayVSR_X2

We trained this RelayVSR model for **native, fixed 2× video super-resolution**.
It doubles the input video's width and height.

We found that RelayVSR's model design is effective at suppressing temporal flicker
in upscaled videos. This is particularly useful for videos produced by generative
video models: the generated video may occasionally contain subtle flicker, which
super-resolution algorithms can amplify.

The [original RelayVSR model](https://huggingface.co/kopper/RelayVSR) uses a fixed
4× super-resolution scale, which incurs substantial inference time. To reduce this
cost, we modified the model architecture and continued training to obtain a
**fixed 2× RelayVSR model**, with inference supported by
[LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V).

We recommend RelayVSR as a super-resolution post-processing model for video
generators such as **MiniMax-H3**. For example, a MiniMax-H3 video generated at
**768 × 1344** can be upscaled by 2× to **1536 × 2688**.

For inference instructions, see the
[LightX2V RelayVSR documentation](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/tree/main/scripts/relayvsr).

| Model | Native scale | Output dimensions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Original RelayVSR](https://huggingface.co/kopper/RelayVSR) | 4× | 4W × 4H |
| [RelayVSR X2](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/RelayVSR_X2) | 2× | 2W × 2H |

## Inference Benchmark

On the tested clip, **RelayVSR X2 with LightX2V processes 243 frames in 5.348 seconds
(45.44 inference FPS)** on a single NVIDIA H100 80GB.

Using the same
[drone rooftop input video](assets/benchmark/originals/input.mp4):
**1024 × 768**, **243 frames**, **24 fps**, **10.125 seconds**.

The input video was generated by **MiniMax-H3** and contains some mild temporal
flicker. This flicker is already present in the source video before super-resolution.

All cases ran sequentially on one **NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3** with
**PyTorch 2.11.0 + CUDA 13.0**. Each row reports **one measured run after
same-resolution warmup**.

| Model / implementation | Scale | Output resolution | Inference time (s) | Inference FPS | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [SeedVR2-3B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B) | 2× | 2048 × 1536 | 352.820 | 0.69 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/seedvr2_3b_x2.mp4) |
| [FlashVSR+ Turbo](https://huggingface.co/ruchangyao/FlashVSR_plus) | 2× | 2048 × 1536 | 54.024 | 4.50 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/flashvsr_plus_turbo_x2.mp4) |
| [Open-H3-Regenerate-2K](https://huggingface.co/Efficient-Large-Model/Open-H3-Regenerate-2K) | 2× | 2048 × 1536 | 784.954 | 0.31 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/open_h3_regenerate_x2.mp4) |
| [SwiftVR](https://huggingface.co/H-oliday/SwiftVR) | 2× | 2048 × 1536 | 7.252 | 33.51 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/swiftvr_x2.mp4) |
| [SwiftVR (LightX2V)](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/tree/main/scripts/swiftvr) | 2× | 2048 × 1536 | 6.399 | 37.98 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/swiftvr_lightx2v_x2.mp4) |
| [RelayVSR](https://huggingface.co/kopper/RelayVSR) | 4× | 4096 × 3072 | 26.332 | 9.23 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/relayvsr_x4.mp4) |
| [RelayVSR (LightX2V)](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/tree/main/scripts/relayvsr) | 4× | 4096 × 3072 | 19.304 | 12.59 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/relayvsr_x4_lightx2v.mp4) |
| **[RelayVSR X2 (LightX2V)](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/RelayVSR_X2)** | 2× | 2048 × 1536 | **5.348** 🚀 | **45.44** 🚀 | [MP4](assets/benchmark/originals/relayvsr_x2_lightx2v.mp4) |

## Video Comparison

<video controls src="https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/RelayVSR_X2/resolve/main/assets/benchmark/comparison_grid.mp4"></video>

Many super-resolution methods can amplify the temporal flicker already present in
AI-generated input videos. **RelayVSR can substantially alleviate this flicker**,
producing more temporally consistent results.

The original RelayVSR model is limited to fixed **4× upscaling**, which incurs a
higher computational cost and slower inference. To reduce this cost, we trained a
**native 2× super-resolution model based on RelayVSR**. Our **RelayVSR X2** model
combines effective temporal-flicker suppression with **fast inference**, making it
suited to upscaling AI-generated videos.

# H3 Video Upsampler

> Code: [GitHub](https://github.com/sandpies/ComfyUI-H3-Video-Upsampler). The Regen2K LoRA is in [`lora/`](./lora).

Make a finished MiniMax H3 video (or any video) bigger and sharper in ComfyUI.
Faces, motion, mouths and the soundtrack stay your clip's own.

## Quick start

1. Clone this repo into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes` and restart ComfyUI.
2. Download the files below into the folders shown.
3. Load `example_workflows/H3_Video_Upsampler_File.json`, pick your video, press Queue.
   The MP4 lands in `ComfyUI/output/video/`.

Needs **ComfyUI v0.38.0 or newer**.

## Two ways to re-draw: `method`

- **`regen2k`** (default): fast, and good for most clips.
- **`ic`**: keeps the original frames in view while it re-draws, so faces, writing
  on signs and mouths stay closest to your clip. About 1.7x slower.

`ic` needs these extra files:

| File | Put it in | Size |
|---|---|---|

| [`minimax_h3_open_regenerate_2k_ic_lora_avg_rank_21_bf16`](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3-experimental/blob/main/loras/minimax_h3_open_regenerate_2k_ic_lora_avg_rank_21_bf16.safetensors) | `models/loras` | 0.2 GB |

| *optional:* [`minimax_h3_lms_v1.0_r64`](https://huggingface.co/Alissonerdx/Minimax-H3-ComfyUI/blob/main/loras/minimax_h3_lms_v1.0_r64.safetensors) (a little extra sharpness) | `models/loras` | 1.2 GB |

To switch: set `method` to `ic` and load `minimax_h3_ref2va_int8_convrot` in the model loader.
If something is missing, the node stops straight away and tells you which file.
The `clip` input can stay empty: wiring the text encoder (27 GB) looked the same in our tests.

## Settings worth knowing

Hover any setting in ComfyUI for a short explanation. The ones you might change:

| Setting | What to do |
|---|---|
| `megapixels` | Output size. **2** is about 1080p. It must be bigger than your clip. |
| `redraw_steps` | **3** is the normal recipe. **2** is a third faster and looked the same in our tests. |
| `redraw_start` | How much the re-draw may change (`regen2k`; under `ic` the face close-ups only). **0.6** keeps faces close; 0.8 is sharper but faces can change. |
| `denoise` | **0** only enlarges, with no re-draw. |
| `sharpness` | Only with the 2D latent upscaler: **1** stays closest to your clip, **6** is sharpest. The 3D upscaler ignores it. |
| `conditioning` | Optional text describing the look, e.g. *"2D anime, flat cel shading"*. Helps animation. |

Leave the rest at their defaults: they adjust themselves to your graphics card.

# MiniMax-H3-Image (Pruned DiT) — GGUF Quantizations

Quantized **GGUF** weights for **[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)**, converted directly from the structurally pruned BF16 master checkpoint provided by **[Comfy-Org](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image)** (`minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16.safetensors`).

MiniMax-H3-Image is a state-of-the-art **33.1B parameter single-stream Diffusion Transformer (DiT)** designed for ultra-high-resolution text-to-image generation and multi-reference image editing (up to 16 MP / 4096 × 4096) in just **6 distilled sampling steps**.

All GGUFs in this repository have sensitive layers (the 24-channel input patchifier `video_patch_proj`, the 6-step PDD output head `final_layer`, and the low-rank AdaLN modulation basis `adaln_basis` / `adaln_t_table`) strictly preserved in **unquantized FP32** to eliminate quantization noise and grid artifacts.

> **✅ Update — Native Stock ComfyUI-GGUF Support:** All GGUF files in this repository now include the embedded `config` (`pdd_sigmas` 6-step schedule) header metadata and load natively out of the box in stock **ComfyUI-GGUF (`Unet Loader (GGUF)`)** with zero custom scripts or patches required! *(Note: [`minimax_h3_image_gguf_fix.py`](./minimax_h3_image_gguf_fix.py) is kept in the repository solely as an optional fallback for users on older versions of ComfyUI-GGUF).*

# Lucia 4B v1.2: Qwen3.5-4B, think symbolic image

**Lucia 4B v1.2** is a LoRA adapter of [Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B) that looks at a picture and
writes a reading of it: a short chain of plain-language thoughts, one named step per line, then the wordings (a caption, a
prompt, tags, a critique, by depth), then the questions a careful looker would still ask, each with its answer and what settles
it. Version 1.2 is version 1.1's recipe taught on nearly ten times the rows.

- **Nearly ten times the rows.** She was taught 91,138 rows (version 1.1: 9,261): the Apache-2.0 part of
  [release 5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned/tree/cac40b93d7b063aafd0cb70d3c1b1a7a100562ef) of [thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-recaptioned)
  as anyone can read it there (95,481 rows), less 3,718 rows on COCO 2017 photographs under other licenses,
  609 rows on the pictures the reads below hold out and 16 rows whose pictures no store holds.
  They are readings of DOCCI and COCO 2017 photographs, of National Gallery of Art pictures and of drawn specifications, written
  by OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek models and admitted by a blind review; 30,250 of them are long looks. No row she was
  taught was written by a Claude model, or by any model of this project trained on rows a Claude model wrote. Training shows her
  the picture of every row, so the COCO 2017 photographs she saw are only those whose Flickr authors gave them the Attribution
  license or that carry no known copyright restrictions, in her rows and in the ordinary requests below alike.
- **One pass.** She was taught her rows once (10,137 steps); version 1.1 was taught hers twice (2,102 steps).
- **The base model kept**, as in version 1.1: a second objective in training holds her next-word choices near Qwen3.5-4B's on
  ordinary requests, so the adapter changes how she answers when asked for a reading and little else. On held-out ordinary
  requests she stays close to the base model, and of the questions and text requests among them she answers none in the reading's form.
- **Lettering still left out.** She seldom writes the lettering a picture shows into her reading: her closer look names a word
  the picture shows for 56 of 245 held-out pictures with readable lettering, where the base model's free description
  names one for 227. Asked directly what the lettering says, her answer names it as often as the base model's does
  (0.92 of the pictures against 0.91).

Versions 1.1 and 1 stay in this repository at the tags `lucia-v1.1` and `lucia-v1`. Her non-commercial sibling,
[qwen3.5-4b-think-symbolic-image-nc](https://huggingface.co/AbstractPhil/qwen3.5-4b-think-symbolic-image-nc), holds version
1.2-nc (version 1.1-nc at its tag `lucia-v1.1`), trained the same way on the Apache-2.0 rows and on the readings written with
COCO 2017, FFHQ and DeepFashion-MultiModal pictures in view, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

What she writes for a closer look at a held-out COCO 2017 photograph ([376084](https://cocodataset.org/#explore?id=376084), its author's Attribution license), verbatim:

```
see: One yellow truck sits at the center of the frame, its bright body making it the clear focal point.
relate: The truck is parked on a road, with traffic cones and a grassy field nearby.
mood: Its parked state suggests a gentle pause, as the truck seems momentarily at rest.
caption: A yellow truck is parked at the center of the frame, with traffic cones and a grassy field nearby.
prompt: yellow truck parked on a road, traffic cones, grassy field, centered composition
tags: yellow truck, traffic cones, grass, road, photograph
question: thing name -> truck [record]
question: thing count -> 1 [record]
question: thing colour -> yellow [record]
question: thing state -> parked [record]
question: scene time -> unknown [unknown]
```

The steps a chain may use, in the order a careful looker takes them: `see`, `name`, `place`, `count`, `relate`, `form`,
`light`, `colour`, `mood`, `mean`, `intend`, `story`, `compare`, `change`, `check`, `say`. A quick look holds 1 to 2 thoughts,
a closer look 3 to 5, a long look 6 to 10. Questions end in `[record]` (the answer is a fact of the picture), `[chain]` (the
chain worked it out) or `[unknown]`. The prompt line often opens with the kind of picture (a close-up photograph, an overhead
photograph); unlike version 1, she was not taught to open it that way every time.

**Quantized builds at adapter weight 1.0, for text-to-image generation and image editing.**

### Which build should I use?

- **ComfyUI, one file, both workflows** -> any **GGUF**. It also loads in Diffusers via `from_single_file`.
- **ComfyUI, native quant ops** -> **FP8**, **INT8 ConvRot** or **NVFP4**.

# LTX-2.5 for Moonbox

The files the [Moonbox](https://moonbox.dev) desktop app downloads for these models:

- **LTX-2.5** (Lightricks): Clips with sound from words or from a first frame, 2 to 10 seconds, at every size up to HD.
- **LTX-2.5 (4-bit encoder)** (Lightricks): The same LTX-2.5 model with a lighter text encoder, for computers with less memory: clips at the Draft and Small sizes.
- **LTX-2.5 edits** (Lightricks): Sixteen edits for a clip or a still: relight, restore, colourise, reframe and more.

They are the LTX-2.5 22B distilled transformer converted to MLX for Apple silicon and quantized to 6-bit, its text encoder (8-bit, and a 4-bit build for computers with less memory), VAEs, vocoder and upscaler, and the Lightricks LoRAs behind the app's video edits. Moonbox checks every file against a signed list before using it. You do not need this repository to use Moonbox, and it is not an official release of the original models.
