# VDN-H3 Edge

Prepared FP8 weights and portable AdaLN constants for [FreeVideo](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeVideo). Powered by MiniMax H3.

Two FP8 formats live in this repository. **FreeVideo downloads only the matching format**, about **22.9 GB / 21.4 GiB**, plus the separately installed text encoder and decoders. It does not download both variants or the original transformer weights.

## Formats

| Directory | Quantization | FreeVideo automatic route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cache/` | Per-tensor FP8 | Blackwell, including RTX 50 |
| `rowwise/cache/` | Per-channel FP8 weights | Ada / RTX 40 and Hopper / SM90; Ampere / RTX 30 uses this storage with BF16 compute |

These routes preserve the engine's existing arithmetic. Ada also supports per-tensor FP8; keeping its current rowwise policy is a software/output compatibility choice. Windows rowwise uses FreeVideo's scalar FP8 GEMM plus fused row/column scaling, because the pinned PyTorch Windows build excludes its native rowwise implementation. Linux uses the native rowwise path. SM90's favorable rowwise dispatch does not establish equal performance on every architecture or shape.

The per-tensor model files are unchanged. Each format has its own immutable installer pin, so adding rowwise does not move or redownload an existing per-tensor installation. The repositories on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3-edge) and [ModelScope](https://modelscope.ai/models/OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3-edge) contain the same payload. Setup selects a working source and resumes interrupted files.

## Use

Install [FreeVideo](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeVideo), open its launcher and start setup. The installer detects the GPU architecture and operating system, downloads the matching prepared files and checks the selected kernels on the machine. **Users do not choose a quantization format or download both variants.**

The model is public; no Hugging Face login is needed. Existing compatible local models are reused. The same automatic selection applies to FreeVideo's ComfyUI integration and command-line setup.

## Portable AdaLN constants

Both formats contain the same two table sets: standard eight-step text-to-video and visual-keyframe schedules. I2VA, L2VA, FL2VA and visual-reference requests share the visual schedule where the engine's exact timestep contract matches. Prompt, seed, dimensions, duration, GPU model and Torch/CUDA versions do not require regenerating these stored constants.

Original AdaLN projections are omitted, saving approximately 26.02 GB per installation. Unsupported schedules or modulation-changing LoRAs can use the optional original projections from the pinned [historical revision](https://huggingface.co/OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3-edge/tree/4f16eb1066d96592b84be0de532069f5d69fcfa9). Ordinary attention/FF LoRAs retain the tables.

## Validation and provenance

The formats derive from the same 101 merged BF16 groups. Rowwise packaging copies all 363 previously prepared FP8 matrices without requantization; modification notices change headers only. Original projection identities and time-embedding tensors match the portable assets. All 50 text-only tables are byte-identical to the earlier rowwise generation cache.

The earlier rowwise native/Windows-compatibility comparison completed an eight-step 1344×768, 243-frame request on Linux SM120 with bit-identical video/audio latents, decoded RGB and audio. The existing per-tensor slim package was checked against the full prepared model on a complete 1344×768, 362-frame request, also bit-identically. This publication adds a byte-preserving rowwise package; it adds no new physical Hopper, Ada or Windows benchmark.

Individual cache format: `freevideo-fp8-slim-v1`; portable tables: `freevideo-adaln-v2`. These are FreeVideo engine packages. The source is `OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3@751739ee5b9e3ac802dca5d5111075fdaeb47885`; no additional training was performed. `bundle.json`, `rowwise/cache/publication.json`, `SHA256SUMS` and `READY.json` record source identities and publication verification. [MODIFICATIONS.md](MODIFICATIONS.md) describes the changes; [NOTICE](NOTICE) retains attribution.

# Qwen-Image 2.1 · MFlux Q4

This is a **Q4** **MFlux** version of [**Qwen-Image-2.1**](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1).

[**MFlux**](https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux) runs the latest state-of-the-art generative image models locally on your Mac in native MLX. MFlux is open source and free.

> [!NOTE]
> Community conversion by [MFlux-Community](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community) -- not an official release from the original model's authors. The original model's license applies unchanged, see [License](#license).

### MFlux versions of Qwen-Image-2.1
|   QUANT   | GB  | Repo |
| :--: | :-: | --- |
| BF16 | 33.1 | [mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-bf16](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-bf16) |
| Q8 | 18.5 | [mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q8](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q8) |
| Q6 | 14.5 | [mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q6](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q6) |
| Q5 | 12.6 | [mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q5](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q5) |
| **Q4** | 10.6 | this repo |
| Q3 | 8.7 | [mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q3](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q3) |

Converted with MFlux 0.24.0 on 2026-10-31.

Standard MFlux quantization uses MLX affine quantization (4-bit) across the text encoder, transformer and VAE. The quantization level is stored in the weights, so no `--quantize` flag is needed.

## Usage

**Install MFlux**
```bash
uv tool install --upgrade mflux
```

**Generate an image using Qwen-Image-2.1 Q4:**
```bash
mflux-generate-qwen-2.1 \
  --model mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q4 \
  --base-model qwen-image-2.1 \
  --prompt "A puffin standing on a cliff" \
  --width 1024 \
  --height 1024 \
  --seed 42 \
  --output image.png
```

The weights are downloaded from this repo on first use. To keep a local copy instead:
```bash
hf download mflux-community/qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q4 --local-dir ./qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q4
```
then pass `--model ./qwen-image-2-1-mflux-q4`.

This repo inherits the license of the original model: **qwen-research**. See the [original model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) for the full terms and any usage restrictions. The weights here were modified from the original release only by conversion to MLX and quantization.

# MiniMax-H3-Image — MLX-Serve 8-bit

![Six 2048x2048 samples from this pack: a jewel beetle, a highland cow, a bakery sign, a fisherman, pixel art and dumplings](assets/samples.jpg)

8-bit affine (group size 64) conversion of
[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) for
[mlx-serve](https://github.com/ddalcu/mlx-serve), running natively on Apple Silicon: text to image
and editing with up to 16 reference images, in six transformer forwards and no classifier-free
guidance.

Self-contained: the DiT with its six per-step output heads, the MiniMax-H3 text encoder (which the
upstream release loads from MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3), the image VAE and the tokenizer in one directory.

This is the higher-fidelity pack: side by side with the 4-bit one at the same seeds it is a little cleaner on small structures (insect legs and antennae, candy shapes in an edit, knit texture). It needs a 48 GB Mac. The mlx-serve app lists the 4-bit pack; this one appears under On This Mac once it is in your models folder.

## At a glance

| | 4-bit | 8-bit |
|---|---|---|
| Repo | [ddalcu/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Serve-4bit](https://huggingface.co/ddalcu/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Serve-4bit) | [ddalcu/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Serve-8bit](https://huggingface.co/ddalcu/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Serve-8bit) |
| Download | 36.9 GB | 65.8 GB |
| Peak memory, M1 to M4 | 15.9 GB | 27.4 GB |
| Peak memory, M5 with 64 GB or more | 22.7 GB | 27.6 GB |
| Recommended Mac | 32 GB or more | 48 GB or more |
| 2048x2048 text to image, M5 Ultra | 13 s | 15 s |
| Edit with one reference, M5 Ultra | 22 s | 24 s |

Peak memory is MLX's own peak over one 2048x2048 image and one edit (`/props` `peak_bytes`). On an
M5 with 64 GB or more, mlx-serve runs the DiT as int8 by default, which is why that row differs;
everywhere else the 8-bit weights run as they are. The stages load one at a time (text encoder,
then DiT, then VAE), so the peak is the largest stage, not the sum.

## Files

| File | Size | Precision |
|---|---|---|
| `transformer.safetensors` | 35.3 GB | 8-bit affine, group size 64 (260 matrices); 271 small tensors dense |
| `text_encoder.safetensors` | 28.2 GB | 8-bit affine, group size 64; the 50 layers the DiT reads |
| `image_vae.safetensors` | 2.3 GB | original f32 |

## Use it

In the mlx-serve app: Create ▸ Image, pick MiniMax-H3-Image, Download, then Generate. Add a source
image to edit it.

From the command line:

```bash
mlx-serve pull ddalcu/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Serve-8bit
mlx-serve --model ~/.mlx-serve/models/ddalcu/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Serve-8bit --serve --port 8080

# text to image
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/images/generations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "A highland cow in misty hills at golden hour, photorealistic", "size": "2048x2048", "seed": 7}'

# edit: the source is <Picture 1>, references follow as <Picture 2>, <Picture 3>, ...
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/images/generations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "Make the bicycle in <Picture 1> bright yellow", "mode": "edit", "image": "<base64>"}'
```

The answer is OpenAI's images shape (`data[0].b64_json`, a PNG).

- Six sampling steps, fixed: omit `steps`. `guidance_scale`, LoRAs and variations are refused by name.
- `size`: each side 16 to 6272. A request smaller than `min_generation_area` (default 2048x2048) is
  generated on a canvas of that area at its aspect and resized back, as the upstream pipeline does.
  The model is trained up to about 16 megapixels (4096x4096, 6272x2688).
- Edits: `image` plus up to 15 `ref_images`, 16 pictures in all; the result keeps the source's size.

# ClipProj — MiniMax H3 conditioning from a Qwen3-VL-4B or 8B

**Projection matrices that let a small Qwen3-VL replace the Qwen3-VL-32B text encoder of MiniMax H3.**

**15.7 GB → 4.5 GB of VRAM**, with no change to the diffusion model, the VAEs or the sampler.

---

## v3.1 — better multilingual speech

**No measurable gain in image over v3 — the whole gain is in speech.** The image scores of the two generations overlap entirely, and nothing measured here separates either of them from the 32B, which is not the same as saying they are identical to it: the cosine is blind to countable attributes. What v3.1 improves is pronunciation in the ten languages that are not English — **29 %% fewer phoneme errors overall, 60 to 74 %% fewer in Spanish, French, German and Italian.**

<video controls width="360" src="https://huggingface.co/NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/bench3.1/video/clipproj-v3.1-eleven-languages.mp4"></video>

*Eleven languages, 88 seconds. For each one the **smallest** file that matches the 32B — not the best one. Nine of the eleven run on a 4B. [Direct link](https://huggingface.co/NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/bench3.1/video/clipproj-v3.1-eleven-languages.mp4)*

> ⚠️ **The video looks and sounds rough, on purpose.** 0.3 MP, 6 sampling steps — the settings that made 297 renders affordable — then upscaled. The audio is tinny for the same reason, **identically so on the 32B**, with the same 19 dB dip between 1 and 3 kHz. This is a pronunciation test, not a showcase: it exists to let you hear *which words come out*.

**Four new files:** `mmh3-4b-ClipProj-v3.1`, `mmh3-4b-ClipProj-v3.1-mlp`, `mmh3-8b-ClipProj-v3.1`, `mmh3-8b-ClipProj-v3.1-mlp`. They load on node **0.1.13** with no code change — same base as v3. Start with **`mmh3-4b-ClipProj-v3.1`**: 26 MB of projection, 4.6 GB with its encoder.

**What changed:** the calibration corpus now gives every writing system a comparable share instead of being overwhelmingly English, with raw Arabic text added. Phoneme errors drop **29 % overall**, 60 to 74 % on the European languages.

**What it is measured against:** the 32B does not reproduce itself. Change nothing but the seed and it re-pronounces **5.8 phonemes out of 75** differently. The four v3.1 files sit at 6.4 to 7.0 — so swapping the encoder costs about what re-rolling the seed costs. Every figure is normalised against that variance rather than against zero, and on that scale nothing separates 4B from 8B, or ridge from residual.

**Full report** — three seeds, 297 speech renders, 405 image renders, method, limitations and all the raw data: **[bench3.1/README.md](./bench3.1/README.md)**

---


> ⚠️ **Proof of concept — working, but a proof of concept.** It runs and produces good video, and every number below was measured on real hardware. Built and tested on a single setup (Windows 11, NVIDIA, ComfyUI 0.31.0) with deliberately limited exploration.

> **Arriving from a tutorial or an article?** Anything published before 11 August names files that have moved. `h3_qwen3vl_4b_tap24`, `h3_control_zero` and `h3_control_identity` are still here, one folder down in `obsolete/`, so nothing is lost. But take the current set instead: **`mmh3-4b-ClipProj-celeb-mlp`** for a Qwen3-VL-4B, **`mmh3-8b-ClipProj-celeb-mlp`** for an 8B. They are better on every measurement below, and they need node **0.1.4 or later**.

These files are useless on their own. They require the custom node:
**[github.com/nicolab28/ComfyUI-ClipProj](https://github.com/nicolab28/ComfyUI-ClipProj)**

## Where this came from

I am not an ML researcher. I work in imaging, and programming is a tool and a hobby rather than my trade. This started as something to tinker with: I wanted to understand how a diffusion model actually uses its text encoder, and the only way I know how to understand something is to take it apart and see whether it still runs afterwards.

So the question was never "how do I save VRAM". It was "is this even possible at all". I expected it to fail. A linear map between two models that were never trained together, fitted in a single pass with no gradients and no learning rate, has no business producing usable video.

It did, and the first results were good enough that keeping them on my own disk seemed silly. That is the whole story, and it is why this is labelled a proof of concept rather than a tool: it was never designed as one.

It is also why there are so many measurements on the model card. Before showing this to anyone I had to convince myself I was not fooling myself, and most of what I tried along the way turned out to be wrong. Those attempts are written down as well, in [MEASUREMENTS.md](https://github.com/nicolab28/ComfyUI-ClipProj/blob/main/MEASURE

# Qwen-Image 2.1 for WebGPU (2-step, int4 ONNX)

Built with Qwen. [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) with the
[2-step DMD2 LoRA](https://huggingface.co/linoyts/Qwen-Image-2.1-DMD2-2steps) fused in, exported to ONNX and quantized
to int4 to run in the browser with onnxruntime-web on WebGPU. It does text-to-image and image editing in 2 denoising steps
with no CFG. Text-to-image downloads about 7.4 GB; the first edit adds the 1.2 GB vision encoder.

Try it: [linoyts/Qwen-Image-2.1-WebGPU](https://huggingface.co/spaces/linoyts/Qwen-Image-2.1-WebGPU). It needs a
WebGPU browser (desktop Chrome or Edge) and a GPU with `shader-f16` and about 8 GB of memory.

## Files

| Folder | Contents | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `text_encoder/onnx/` | Qwen3-VL-8B text path: int4 embedding table, 36 layer graphs, final norm | 3.7 GB |
| `text_encoder/onnx/vision_encoder_fp16.onnx` | Qwen3-VL vision tower with DeepStack mergers, fp16 (editing only) | 1.2 GB |
| `transformer/onnx/` | DiT: `text_proj`, `step_embed`, 32 block graphs, `head` | 3.7 GB |
| `vae/onnx/` | [TAEQI2.1](https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/taeqi2_1) tiny encoder and decoder, fp16 | 30 MB |
| `tokenizer/`, `scheduler/` | Tokenizer and FlowMatch Euler config (static shift 1.0) | |

- Linear layers are int4 `MatMulNBits` (block 128, asymmetric). Norms, embedders, modulation and the output head stay fp16.
  The vision tower stays fp16: int4 weights move its output by 58% (int8: 9%, fp16: 1%).
- Every graph is under 2 GB and loads as its own session.
- Each component's `config.json` lists the inputs and outputs of its graphs, the RoPE settings and the prompt template.

## How it runs

1. **Encode the prompt.** Wrap it in the chat template, run the embedding, the 36 layers and the norm, then drop the first
   14 tokens. The result is the prompt embeddings, `[1, L, 4096]`.
2. **Prefill the text.** Run `text_proj`, then each of the 32 blocks with the t=0 modulation row and a causal mask.
   Keep every block's `present_key`/`present_value`. Text tokens are modulated from t=0 (`causal_condition`), so
   their K/V are the same at every step. This is the KV-cache path the diffusers pipeline uses.
3. **Denoise for 2 steps, σ = 1.0 then 0.5.** At each step:
   1. `step_embed` turns the latents `[1, S, 64]` into image tokens and modulation.
   2. The 32 blocks run on the image tokens only, each attending to its cached text K/V.
   3. `head` returns the velocity, and the Euler step is `x += (σ_next - σ) · v`.
4. **Decode.** Reshape the latents to `[1, 64, H/16, W/16]` and run the TAEQI2.1 decoder, which outputs RGBA in [0, 1].

### Editing

Resize the input to about the output area at its own aspect ratio (multiples of 32). Then:

- **Text encoder.** The prompt uses the template with `Picture 1: <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>`. The vision
  encoder output replaces the `<|image_pad|>` embeddings, and the 3 DeepStack features are added to those positions after
  layers 0, 1 and 2. Positions use Qwen3-VL's interleaved mRoPE.
- **Transformer.** The TAEQI2.1 encoder turns the image into condition latents. Their `step_embed` tokens replace the
  `<|image_pad|>` run in the prefix. The prefix is block-causal (the image block sees itself), uses the t=0 modulation and
  is cached like the text, so each step still runs only the target image tokens.

## Verification (ONNX Runtime CPU vs PyTorch)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| One DiT block, fp32 export | relative error 5e-7 |
| Full DiT, 2 steps, same int4 weights and noise, vs fp32 PyTorch | relative latent error 0.155 (diffusers bf16 vs fp32: 0.187) |
| Text encoder embeddings vs the bf16 pipeline | cosine similarity 0.955 to 0.967 (edit prompts with an image: 0.90 to 0.91) |
| Edit, DiT on the pipeline's embeddings, vs diffusers bf16 with TAEQI2.1 | relative latent error 0.12 to 0.14 |

## License

The Qwen-Image 2.1 weights are under the Qwen Research License (non-commercial); see `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`. The files in
`transformer/` and `text_encoder/` are modified forms of those weights: LoRA fused, converted to ONNX, quantized and
split. The encoder and decoder in `vae/` are from madebyollin/taeqi2_1 (MIT).

A [Loom](https://github.com/ROCm/hrx-system) package (`.loom` programs and a `model.json` card) for the unmodified GGUF checkpoint [unsloth/flux-3-image-klein-pup-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/flux-3-image-klein-pup-GGUF) (`flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q4_K_M.gguf`), for the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" and AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 GPUs, generated with [loom-next](https://github.com/loom-fun/loom-next) (the generator alone, no LLM in the loop). Learn more on the [Loom ecosystem website](https://loom-fun.github.io/loom-dev/).

## Quick start

Open your GPU and copy its commands.

<details>
<summary>AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" (gfx1151)</summary>

```bash
pipx install "hrx-loom[hf]==0.2.0"
loom-fetch huggingface:loom-draft/unsloth-flux-3-image-klein-pup-loom:chat --materialize=copy --output=flux-3-image-klein-pup
loom-serve --model=flux-3-image-klein-pup '--device=amdgpu://?completion_spin_ns=4294967295' --pool_backing=fixed --parameter_mode=preload
```

- `--materialize=copy` puts copies of the fetched package files in the output directory.
- `completion_spin_ns=4294967295` enables active waiting for GPU completions (uses CPU while GPU work is in flight); the card's performance measurements use this setting.
- `--pool_backing=fixed` commits the preset's memory pool up front instead of growing elastic backing.
- `--parameter_mode=preload` only changes how the weights are loaded on the host, so the performance rows were measured without it unless their job served with it.

</details>

# Flux.3-Image-Klein · MFlux Q4

This is a **Q4** **MFlux** version of [**flux-3-image-klein**](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein).

[**MFlux**](https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux) runs the latest state-of-the-art generative image models locally on your Mac in native MLX. MFlux is open source and free.

> [!NOTE]
> Community conversion by [MFlux-Community](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community) -- not an official release from the original model's authors. The original model's license applies unchanged, see [License](#license).

### MFlux versions of flux-3-image-klein

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

# MOSS-Image Qwen3.5-9B text encoder, INT8 (W8A8, ConvRot)

The Qwen3.5-9B text encoder of [MOSS-Image](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base)
in one 9.2 GB file instead of the 16.8 GB bf16 shards, in ComfyUI's mixed-precision
`int8_tensorwise` + `convrot` format. Its matmuls run in int8 (weights and activations),
about 1.7× the encode speed of the [fp8 file](https://huggingface.co/sorryhyun/MOSS-Image-Qwen3.5-9B-fp8)
at the same VRAM and nearly the same error.

| | |
|---|---|
| Files | `qwen35_9b_int8_convrot.safetensors` (9.20 GiB), `config.json` (the Qwen3.5-9B config, for transformers) |
| Quantized | the 248 decoder-layer linears (attention, gated-DeltaNet projections, MLP): each weight rotated per 256-column group by a Hadamard matrix (ConvRot), int8 with one fp32 `weight_scale` per output row |
| Kept as-is | token embedding, GDN `conv1d` / `A_log` / `dt_bias`, the vision tower |
| Changed | the decoder layers' RMSNorm weights (fp32) carry SmoothQuant scales (below); they belong to this file's linears and don't mix with the bf16 ones |
| Matmul | W8A8: the input is rotated by the same Hadamard and rounded to int8 per token (`comfy_kitchen.int8_linear`). The weight can also be dequantized for a bf16 matmul (weight-only) |

## anima_lora

The default text encoder for MOSS caching and generation (`text_encoder=int8`,
`--text_encoder int8`): fetched on first use (`make download-model ARGS=moss-te-int8`),
all 32 decoder layers stay on a 16 GB card. The tokenizer still comes from MOSS-Image-Base.
`text_encoder=bf16` / `fp8` select the reference shards or the fp8 file.

## ComfyUI

Put the file in `models/text_encoders/` and load it with **MOSS-Image Load Qwen3.5**
(the `moss-image` node); ComfyUI's mixed-precision loader reads `comfy_quant` per layer.

## Measured

RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, against the bf16 encoder. Speed and VRAM (`bench/moss_te_fp8`, 34 prompts,
same format and kernel):

| | bf16 | fp8 (weight-only) | INT8 W8A8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encode, tokens/s | 2250 (2 layers paged) | 1467 | 2459 |
| Peak VRAM, decoder layers resident | 12.59 GiB | 6.69 GiB | 6.54 GiB |

Embedding relative L2 error on the held-out split of the calibration set (121 entries;
image rows are manga / colorize pages through the vision tower):

| | fp8 GPTQ | INT8 (this file) |
|---|---|---|
| tags | 0.039 | 0.042 |
| position clauses | 0.040 | 0.046 |
| natural language | 0.044 | 0.043 |
| layout JSON | 0.039 | 0.047 |
| OCR captions | 0.051 | 0.053 |
| JA / KO / ZH | 0.054 | 0.053 |
| page + caption (image rows) | 0.10 | 0.10 |
| all | 0.095 | 0.097 |

Plain INT8 GPTQ (no smoothing) reads 0.105 overall in the same W8A8 mode; round-to-nearest
is worse again.

## How it was made

`project/moss_lora/src/te_gptq.py --grid int8_convrot --smooth 0.5 --act_aware` in
[anima_lora](https://github.com/sorryhyun/anima_lora), on MOSS text-encoder inputs (tag
captions, layout JSON, English and JA/KO/ZH prompts, manga and colorize pages through the
vision tower; `te_calib.py`), layer by layer:

1. **SmoothQuant** (α 0.5): per input channel, activation outliers are moved into the
   weight; the scales are folded into the preceding RMSNorm (`(1 + w) / s − 1`) and,
   for `down_proj`, into `up_proj`'s rows.
2. **Activation-aware GPTQ**: the Hessian comes from the rotated, int8-rounded inputs the
   W8A8 kernel actually sees, and the rounding targets the least-squares weight for those
   inputs. Each layer is calibrated on the previous layers' W8A8 outputs.

## License

Apache-2.0, as MOSS-Image and Qwen3.5. Weights derived from

# ReCaVSR video upscaler: ComfyUI workflows for 8, 12 and 16 GB VRAM

Three versions of one ComfyUI workflow for **ReCaVSR**, a one-step video super-resolution model (built on Wan 2.2) that upscales **any video**: AI video (MiniMax H3 and others), anime, 3D or real footage. Load your video, press **Run**. That's it.

Each workflow **reads your video's size and picks the biggest output your card can hold** (up to 4x, up to 4K). You never have to set the scale yourself, and it stays inside your card's memory.

| File | For | 720p video becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `recavsr_upscale_8gb_vram.json` | 8 GB cards (also 10 and 11 GB) | **1920x1080** (Full HD) |
| `recavsr_upscale_12gb_vram.json` | 12 GB cards | **2560x1440** (2K) |
| `recavsr_upscale_16gb_vram.json` | 16 GB cards and bigger | **3840x2160** (4K) |

**Same model, same quality per pixel in all three.** A bigger card only allows a bigger output. Pick the file that matches your card. Don't use a smaller card's file on a bigger card: the size picking is worked out for that card's memory.

## Output sizes

| Your video | 8 GB | 12 GB | 16 GB |
|---|---|---|---|
| 480p 854x480 | 1922x1080 | 2562x1440 | 2776x1560 |
| 720p 1280x720 | 1920x1080 | 2560x1440 | **3840x2160** |
| MiniMax H3 1248x704 | 1872x1056 | 2496x1408 | 3744x2112 |
| 720p vertical 720x1280 | 1080x1920 | 1440x2560 | **2160x3840** |
| 1080p 1920x1080 | 1920x1080 (cleaned, same size) | 3360x1890 | **3840x2160** |
| 1080p vertical 1080x1920 | 1080x1920 (cleaned, same size) | 1890x3360 | **2160x3840** |

For other shapes, the two boxes **Output width** and **Output height** in the workflow show what you will get.

## Setup

**1. Install the custom node** with ComfyUI Manager (search "ReCaVSR"), or:

```
cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/PedroMarinhoDev/ComfyUI-ReCaVSR
```

**2. Download 3 model files into `ComfyUI/models/recavsr/`** (the same files for all three workflows):

| File | Size | Download |
|---|---|---|
| `transformer_int8_convrot.safetensors` | 6.3 GB | [PedroMarinhoDev/ReCaVSR-ComfyUI](https://huggingface.co/PedroMarinhoDev/ReCaVSR-ComfyUI/blob/main/recavsr/transformer_int8_convrot.safetensors) |
| `prompt.safetensors` | 4 MB | [kopper/ReCaVSR](https://huggingface.co/kopper/ReCaVSR/blob/main/prompt.safetensors) |
| `flashdecoder.safetensors` | 229 MB | [kopper/ReCaVSR](https://huggingface.co/kopper/ReCaVSR/blob/main/flashdecoder.safetensors) |

**3. Drag the workflow for your card into ComfyUI**, pick your video in **Load Video**, press **Run**. The upscaled video is saved in `ComfyUI/output/recavsr/`, with the original audio and frame rate.

## What you need

- **GPU:** NVIDIA, RTX 20 series or newer (RTX 30 series or newer for the fastest kernels).
- **ComfyUI:** a recent version (0.44 or newer). The workflow uses only ComfyUI's built-in nodes plus ReCaVSR.
- **System RAM:** 16 GB minimum for the 8 GB version, 24 GB+ for 12 and 16 GB (32 GB recommended for 4K). Part of the work is kept in RAM so the output fits the card.
- **Disk:** about 7 GB for the models.

## How it works

- **Auto size** (the grey group): reads the first frames of your video, takes its width and height, and works out the scale. It uses the memory numbers from the ReCaVSR node itself, with a safety margin, and only uses sizes with even width and height so the video encoder accepts them.
- **kv_offload is on** in all three: the attention history is kept in RAM instead of VRAM. The output is bit-for-bit the same; it only makes room on the card for a bigger output.
- **Long videos are fine.** The video is upscaled 8 frames at a time and written to the file as it goes, so a longer clip costs time and disk space, not VRAM.

## Tested

All three tested on an RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB) with 24 GB of system RAM. For 8 GB and 12 GB, a dummy program held the rest of the card's memory **and** ComfyUI was told the card's total was 8 or 12 GB, so ReCaVSR behaved exactly as on a real 8 or 12 GB card. In both tests **2.4 GB of VRAM was used by the desktop** (browser, Discord ...), more than a typical setup, and nothing ran out of memory.

| Version | Test video | Output | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 GB | 1376x768 | 2064x1152 | 5 s clip in 49 s |
| 12 GB | 1080x1920 (vertical) | 1890x3360 | 5 s clip in 80 s |
| 16 GB | 720p | 3840x2160 (4K) | 15 s clip in about 3 min |

Real 8 GB and 12 GB cards (RTX 4060, 3060, 4070 ...) have slower chips than the test card, so expect longer times. The memory limit itself was tested.

## Tips

- **Close other apps that use the GPU** before you run (games, OBS preview, video in the browser), especially on 8 GB.
- **Colours drift from the original?** Set `color_fix` to `wavelet` in the ReCaVSR Upscale node.
- **Scene cuts:** ReCaVSR treats a clip as one shot, so you may see

# LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 for ComfyUI: bf16, int8, W6A8, W4A8

The DiT of **[LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video-Avatar-1.6)** (Meituan
LongCat) as single ComfyUI files, for the native ComfyUI nodes of **[ComfyUI-LongCat-Avatar](https://github.com/PedroMarinhoDev/ComfyUI-LongCat-Avatar)**. The bf16 file is the
release's `base_model/` shards merged into one file, keys unchanged. The three smaller files are ComfyUI's own int8
ConvRot, W6A8 and W4A8 layouts (Comfy Kitchen kernels), made from it by plain round-to-nearest: no GPTQ, no
calibration.

| File | Size | Layer output error (random inputs) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`longcat_video_avatar_1.6_bf16.safetensors`](diffusion_models/longcat-video-avatar/longcat_video_avatar_1.6_bf16.safetensors) | 29.5 GiB | - |
| [`longcat_video_avatar_1.6_int8_convrot.safetensors`](diffusion_models/longcat-video-avatar/longcat_video_avatar_1.6_int8_convrot.safetensors) | 14.9 GiB | 1.4% |
| [`longcat_video_avatar_1.6_w6a8.safetensors`](diffusion_models/longcat-video-avatar/longcat_video_avatar_1.6_w6a8.safetensors) | 12.3 GiB | 2.1% |
| [`longcat_video_avatar_1.6_w4a8.safetensors`](diffusion_models/longcat-video-avatar/longcat_video_avatar_1.6_w4a8.safetensors) | 8.8 GiB | 6.4% |

Block linears are in the named format, the adaLN modulation layers in int8 ConvRot, and the embedders, audio
projection and final layer in bf16.

The int8 file is the one the nodes were tested with: on an RTX 4090 with `--use-ck-attention`, the distilled 8-step
mode runs at 5.1 to 5.7 s per step at 768x512, 93 frames. W6A8 and W4A8 have not been timed with the current nodes,
and no file's video quality has been measured against bf16 beyond the layer error above.

## Use

The folders here mirror `ComfyUI/models/`. Take one transformer and the three files below it:

| Folder | File | Size | |

# MiniMax-H3-Image Exact-adaLN NVFP4

A **12.61 GB** (`11.74 GiB`) Blackwell **NVFP4** checkpoint of [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) (33.1B DiT) for ComfyUI, paired with a **zero-ULP-error 7-step one-hot `adaLN` lookup table** in ComfyUI's native curve format (no ComfyUI patches or custom nodes required).

Governed by the [MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement](LICENSE-MODEL.md) (note the upstream territory exclusions in Section I.5: EU, UK, Republic of Korea, and USA). Not an official MiniMax release.

**Implementation details, build scripts & ComfyUI workflows:** [GitHub (`lepetitprince716-prog/minimax-h3-image-exact-adaln-nvfp4`)](https://github.com/lepetitprince716-prog/minimax-h3-image-exact-adaln-nvfp4).

![Sample 01](samples/01-alpine-knight-sunrise.jpg)

## What Was Changed

1. **Exact 7-Step One-Hot `adaLN` Lookup Table (`0` BF16 ULP Error):**
   - Upstream `MiniMax-H3-Image` spends **26.0 GB** (`39.5%` of the `66.28 GB` DiT) on per-block `adaLN` MLPs (`2688 -> 96768` across 50 blocks).
   - Standard pruned checkpoints compress those MLPs into an 8-dimensional `F16` basis curve (`adaln_t_table` `[1025, 8]`), introducing **`p99 = 5` BF16 ULP** error across blocks (`7` ULP on step 0 and `9` ULP on `t = 0.999` visual reference rows).
   - Because H3-Image's 6-step PDD solver only ever queries the DiT at **7 fixed timesteps** (`t = 0.0, 0.0324763, 0.1124515, 0.25, 0.4672261, 0.7679911` plus `0.999` for reference images), we pack a `F32 [1025, 7]` nearest-neighbor one-hot table and exact `FP64`-accumulated official modulation vectors (`~136 MB` total) directly into ComfyUI's curve format — **0 BF16 ULP error** across all 50 blocks with zero code changes to ComfyUI.

2. **Blackwell Native `NVFP4` DiT Projections (`comfy-kitchen`):**
   - Quantizes the 200 heavy DiT block linear projections (`blocks.0..49.{attn.qkv_proj, attn.out_proj, mlp.fc1, mlp.fc2}`) to `NVFP4` (`E2M1` packed `U8` weights + `F8_E4M3` per-16 block scales + `F32` per-tensor scale via `TensorCoreNVFP4Layout.quantize`).
   - Keeps `token_refiner.*`, `condition_proj`, `video_patch_proj`, `final_layer.video_out` (6-step PDD head bank), all `q_norm` / `k_norm` / `norm1` / `norm2` layers, and the exact `adaLN` table unquantized in `BF16` / `FP32`.

| `minimax_h3_image_exact_adaln_nvfp4.safetensors` | `12,605,496,924` | `e5a9122b14dc31ab4da67b1a7513041afb3ced7d31dd81f501c1aa16b958aa2a` |

## Speed and Memory (ComfyUI `0.45.0`, 4 MP, 6 Steps)

| Variant | File Size | Resident DiT Weights | Peak DiT VRAM (4 MP T2I) | Peak DiT VRAM (4 MP Dual-Ref Edit) | 6-Step DiT Time (4 MP T2I) | 6-Step DiT Time (4 MP Dual-Ref) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Exact-adaLN `BF16` | `40.30 GB` | `37.53 GiB` | `38.11 GiB` | `40.78 GiB` | `15.02 s` (`1.00x`) | `30.38 s` (`1.00x`) |
| Exact-adaLN `INT8 ConvRot` | `21.05 GB` | `19.62 GiB` | `20.06 GiB` | `21.59 GiB` | `12.09 s` (`1.24x`) | `31.36 s` (`0.97x`) |
| **Exact-adaLN `NVFP4` (this)** | **`12.61 GB`** | **`11.75 GiB`** | **`12.34 GiB`** | **`14.00 GiB`** | **`10.55 s` (`1.42x`)** | **`20.97 s` (`1.45x`)** |

![Exact-adaLN BF16 (left) vs Exact-adaLN NVFP4 (right)](samples/ab-bf16-vs-nvfp4.jpg)

| ![](samples/05-autumn-gorge-viaduct.jpg) | ![](samples/06-basalt-coastal-lighthouse.jpg) | |

## ComfyUI Usage

- **Requirements:** ComfyUI `>= 0.45.0`, `comfy-kitchen >= 0.2.41`, PyTorch with `cu130+`. Native 4-bit Tensor Core acceleration requires NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (RTX 50-series / GB-series); older GPUs dequantize weights on the fly.
- **Text Encoder (`CLIPLoader`, `type: minimax`):** `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_bf16.safetensors` from [`Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image) (pass `--bf16-text-enc`), or `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors`.
- **VAE (`VAELoader`):** `minimax_h3_image_vae_fp32.safetensors` (`--fp32-vae`) or `minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors`.
- **Exact PDD `ManualSigmas` (`SamplerCustomAdvanced` + `KSamplerSelect(euler)` + `BasicGuider`):**
  ```text
  1.0, 0.9675236940383911, 0.8875485062599182, 0.75, 0.5327739119529724, 0.23200887441635132, 0.0
  ```
  Ready-to-load workflows (`workflows/minimax-h3-image-exact-adaln-nvfp4-t2i.json` and `workflows/minimax-h3-image-exact-adaln-nvfp4-edit.json`) are included in this repo and on [GitHub](https://github.com/lepetitprince716-prog/minimax-h3-image-exact-adaln-nvfp4).

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

# MiniMax-H3-Image-PE: SceneWorks converted tiers (bf16 / q8 / q4)

> **Modified files.** Every file under `bf16/`, `q8/`, `q4/`, `candle-q8/` and `candle-q4/` was
> **modified by SceneWorks**. Each one was converted from, or copied out of, MiniMax's
> [`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE`](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE) at
> revision `35603d4b63949afa12cb098227fffefedf081afa`. This notice is the one Section III.2 of the
> MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement requires. This is **not** an official MiniMax
> distribution.

MiniMax-H3-Image-PE is the prompt expander for
[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), a fine-tune of
Qwen3.8-27B (`qwen3_5`, with its vision tower). It turns a short prompt, or an edit instruction
with its `<Picture N>` references, into the long caption MiniMax-H3-Image was trained on, and
proposes an aspect ratio.

MiniMax publishes it only as a ModelOpt **NVFP4** checkpoint, which runs natively only on
Blackwell NVIDIA GPUs. This repository holds converted tiers for Apple Silicon (MLX) and for
other CUDA GPUs and CPUs (Candle), as used by [SceneWorks](https://github.com/SceneWorks).

## License

Governed by the **MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement** (November 10, 2026), carried
verbatim as [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). The notice Section III.4 requires is in [`NOTICE`](NOTICE).

- **No improving other models** (Section V.3). Neither the model nor its outputs, expanded

  Model Derivatives.

Read the full Agreement before downloading.

## Tiers

Each tier directory is a complete, standalone snapshot (weights, `config.json`, tokenizer, chat
template, processor and generation config). Download only the tier you need.

| directory | backend | format | size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bf16/` | MLX and Candle | dense bf16, sharded safetensors | 54.7 GB |
| `q8/` | MLX (macOS) | MLX affine 8-bit, group size 64 | 31.9 GB |
| `q4/` | MLX (macOS) | MLX affine 4-bit, group size 64 | 19.8 GB |
| `candle-q8/` | Candle (Windows / Linux) | GGML Q8_0 | 31.9 GB |
| `candle-q4/` | Candle (Windows / Linux) | GGML Q4_K | 19.8 GB |

On a Blackwell GPU, use MiniMax's original NVFP4 checkpoint instead.

### What was changed

- **`bf16/`**: each ModelOpt NVFP4 projection was dequantized to a dense bf16 `.weight`, and its
  `weight_scale`, `weight_scale_2` and `input_scale` were dropped. Every other tensor was copied
  byte for byte. `config.json` lost its `quantization_config` and declares `dtype: bfloat16`.
  `hf_quant_config.json` and the source index were removed, and a new
  `model.safetensors.index.json` was written. The tokenizer, chat template, processor and
  generation config are unchanged copies.
- **`q8/`, `q4/`, `candle-q8/`, `candle-q4/`**: quantized from the `bf16/` snapshot above. The
  `config.json` `quantization` block records the bit width and storage format.

### What is not here

MiniMax's `prompt/` directory, which holds the system and task prompts the expander needs, is
**not** redistributed here. Download it from the upstream repository at the same revision.
SceneWorks reads it from there at run time and checks every file against the upstream
`prompt/manifest.json`. Without those prompts, the expander does not produce MiniMax-H3-Image
captions.

## Quality vs. NVFP4

Each tier was run on a fixed set of 8 prompts (text-to-image, and edit with reference images)
and compared with the native NVFP4 output from a Blackwell GPU (SceneWorks Inference run
[43028135206](https://github.com/SceneWorks/inference/actions/runs/43028135206)). Every tier
returned valid JSON for all 8 prompts.

| tier | backend | mean chrF vs NVFP4 | aspect ratio matches NVFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | Candle | 55.3 | 6 / 8 |
| q8 | Candle | 54.7 | 6 / 8

Undistills MiniMax-H3-Image, making it act more similar to a base model. Designed mainly for training. Unlike Ostris's V1 adapter, this one is trained using a continuous timestep distribution, rather than a discrete timestep schedule. You should train on top of it like any other base model, without additional tricks or special configuration. Works well for training in diffusion-pipe. AI-Toolkit might be hardcoded for Ostris's adapter and the discrete timestep schedule, so it may not work properly there.

Trained on 10k diverse images with Gemma-4-31b captions for 15 epochs. Equal mix of 512 and 1024 resolution. The model was trained without architecture modifications: it still selects a PDD head based on the timestep, following the ComfyUI implementation, but it is trained to accept any continuous timestep between 0 and 1.

Weights are in ComfyUI format.

supports one cached repository per endpoint.

A Q4_0 GGUF of the MiniMax-H3-Image diffusion transformer, made from Comfy-Org's

[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) is MiniMax's image model:

This repository holds smaller quantized tiers of the image transformer only, for

### What was changed

- The attention and feed-forward projections of the 50 transformer blocks and the 2 token-refiner
  blocks, plus each transformer block's `adaln_proj`, are packed at the tier width (MLX
  group-wise affine quantization, group size 64).
- The six per-step output heads (`pdd_proj_out`), the input projection (`proj_in`), the text

  other norm stay dense.
- The output heads, which upstream ships separately as `pdd_fused_heads.safetensors`, are stored
  inside the shards.
- `config.json` is upstream's transformer config plus a `quantization` block recording the bit
  width and group size.

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

Native transparent image generation

Group photograph generated from six portrait references

# One model for camera traps and Galápagos animals (LoRA), LLaVA-OneVision 0.5B

One model for two jobs: camera traps, and the Galápagos animals Google's SpeciesNet has no label for. It scores **93.33%** on mockingbird versus brown noddy, **91.69%** on marine iguana versus green iguana and **87.58%** on land iguana versus green iguana, and names **88.20%** of invasive rats as rats, while holding camera traps at **79.22%** (64.09% unedited). Frontier AI started from the camera-trap edit (an earlier direct edit of the weights for camera-trap answers), built this model and a direct-edit rival from the same 2,902 labelled practice photos, and measured both. This one is a standard LoRA fine-tune (a small trained add-on to the weights, merged back in), trained in about three hours on one desktop computer.

[Explainer](https://andrewxhill.com/frontier-model-weight-edits/) · [Paper](https://andrewxhill.com/frontier-model-weight-edits/paper.pdf) · [Code, data and results](https://github.com/andrewxhill/frontier-model-weight-edits)

## Results

| Model | Mockingbird vs brown noddy | Land iguana vs green iguana | Marine iguana vs green iguana | Invasive rats found | Camera traps |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Island edit | 98.33% | 81.22% | 80.37% | 81.23% | 72.14% |
| One model for both jobs (LoRA) | 93.33% | 87.58% | 91.69% | 88.20% | 79.22% |
| One model for both jobs (direct edit) | 90.83% | 55.49% | 55.49% | 17.70% | 80.70% |
| Camera-trap edit | 91.67% | 51.83% | 51.83% | 13.75% | 81.76% |
| Unedited LLaVA-OneVision 0.5B | 70.83% | 50.00% | 50.00% | 2.96% | 64.09% |
| SpeciesNet (standard output) | 3.33% | 12.44% | 12.44% | 8.11% | — |

Island scores come from 697 test crops from places not used to build any model. Each native-versus-look-alike score averages two shares, natives named as natives and look-alikes named as look-alikes, with each photo location counting equally; rat recall also weights locations equally. The camera-trap column is balanced accuracy on 1,611 crops from 45 cameras, each with its own list of names, with every camera and every animal within it counted equally. SpeciesNet has no label for the natives, and its standard output rarely names the look-alikes, so it scores below 50%, the score of guessing. SpeciesNet was scored on the island test only.

## How it was made

A LoRA fine-tune of the camera-trap edit, merged into full weights. Rank-8 updates (alpha 16) were trained on the attention query and value matrices of all 24 language blocks: 540,672 parameters. One seeded pass covered 2,902 labelled practice crops, 2,095 from camera traps and 807 island photos, with each domain carrying half the loss. There was one fixed recipe and no search over settings. Training took about three hours on one Mac Studio. The Codex research assistant (OpenAI GPT) built and evaluated it. A direct edit for both jobs, built in about an hour from the same crops, scored 80.70% on camera traps, 1.48 points above this model, within the test's noise (95% interval −2.54 to +5.80), but lost most of the island gains.

## How to use it

```python
import torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoProcessor, LlavaOnevisionForConditionalGeneration

repo = "andrewxhill/camera-island-lora"
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(repo)
model = LlavaOnevisionForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(repo, dtype=torch.float32).eval()

names = ["Galapagos land iguana", "Santa Fe land iguana", "Galapagos pink land iguana",
         "marine iguana", "common green iguana", "black rat", "house mouse",
         "domestic cat", "domestic goat", "pig", "European rabbit"]
question = ("Which animal is shown in this crop?\n"
            + "\n".join(f"{chr(65 + i)}. {n}" for i, n in enumerate(names))
            + "\nAnswer with the animal's name from the choices, and no other text.")
messages = [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
            {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": Image.open("crop.jpg").convert("RGB")},
                                         {"type": "text", "text": question}]}]
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True,
                                       return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt")
out = model.generate(**inputs, do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=1024, repetition_penalty=1.1)
print(processor.decode(out[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

Give it a crop around one animal. The reply may be a name, a letter or both; the study's parser, [`code/eval/parser.py`](https://github.com/andrewxhill/frontier-model-weight-edits/blob/main/code/eval/parser.py), accepts either. The study used three fixed 11-name lists, for iguanas, birds and rodents; all

# MiniMax-H3 Seamless Chain

A ComfyUI node pack and two workflows that render a multi-shot MiniMax-H3 scene
as **one continuous take**: no visible cut at the shot boundaries, no colour
shift between shots, and continuous audio across the whole piece.

MiniMax-H3 natively generates blocks of roughly 10-15 seconds. This pack chains
those blocks into arbitrarily long scenes and hands back a single master video
with a single master audio track.

Released as **v2.7.0** of the ComfyUI-H3-Multishot pack.

## v2.7.0 - per-subject voices, flf_chain fixed, chain leveller, ComfyUI 0.34

- **Per-subject voice refs** (`voice_ref_2` / `voice_ref_3`, both samplers):
  each character keeps their own voice across a chained scene - verified blind
  across a full chain, no cross-speaker bleed.
- **flf_chain fix:** the memory bank stood in flf chains and pinned a clip of
  shot 1 (which opens on boundary plate 0) into every later shot as an unbound
  reference - PLATE0 bled back in from shot 2 onward. The bank now stands down
  automatically in flf_chain; plates alone carry the continuity there.
- **H3ChainNormalize:** post-chain texture + colour leveller - the 2.6.0
  long-take ratchet limit is addressed.
- **refresh_pin splice alignment**, **x0 clamp dial** (`x0_clamp_window`,
  dose cap 0.30), in-loop latent upscale + `refresh_renoise` +
  `pin_noise_ramp` + `auto_chunk_ffn`.
- **ComfyUI 0.34 supported:** native interior keyframe anchors detected; the
  pack's layout patch stands down automatically on 0.34, unchanged on older
  cores.
- **Engine-aware writer:** separate H3 (`<d>[English] ...</d>`) and LTX
  (quoted dialogue) system prompts for every mode via an appended `engine`
  widget.

## v2.6.0 adds the extend take: one prompt, one continuous speech, as long as you want

Set **`take_seconds`** on MASTER CONTROLS (or open `H3_Extend_Take`, now the
main workflow, shipped at 1280x736 with a 30-second take) and give the writer
one premise. The panel sizes a window for your
card and the number of windows that fills the time; the writer's new
**extend take** join style writes ONE continuous speech and cuts it across
the windows at sentence boundaries; the chain continues it under
`context_pin` in H3's own voice — no TTS, no airlock, no per-shot dialogue
budgeting. Verified before shipping: seven writer-driven renders including a
65-second, 7-window take, every join continued the speech, reviewed blind as
one uninterrupted take. Also in 2.6.0: reference photographs now win over the
writer's prose (the writer points at the photos instead of describing a face -
same-seed measured), auto refs reach the sampler on their own (a second gate
downstream used to discard them silently), three
reserve-planning fixes from the 24 GB test lab and a writer fix for silent
shots echoing the voice anchor. Full notes in the changelog below.

**Known limit (2.6.0):** the chain's texture ratchet is not fully solved for long takes - measured about +13% fine texture per join at 736x1280 with the anti-drift set on. Under ~4 windows (~30-40 s) it is slight; at 7 windows it is visible sharpening. Keep extend takes to ~4 windows for now; a pin-side fix is in progress for 2.6.1.

## v2.5 is the memory release

Four new memory systems, all measured, two of them fully automatic:

- **The driver-headroom rule (automatic).** High-resolution renders used to
  take anywhere from 27 minutes to 3 hours for identical work — a lottery
  caused by the Windows driver demoting GPU memory when the card fills past
  roughly 95%. The pack now detects that zone and deliberately streams a few
  GB of weights instead of riding the ceiling. The lottery render became 15
  minutes, every time. Nothing to configure.
- **`low_ram_master`.** Long chains used to hold every finished shot in
  system RAM until the final join — tens of GB at the very last step. Switch
  it on and shots stream to lossless disk staging as they finish; peak RAM
  becomes about two shots regardless of chain length, with verified-identical
  output (42.8 dB against the RAM path — codec noise).
- **Remote text encoder.** The text encoder runs for seconds per shot and
  holds 15+ GB the rest of the time. Point the new node at any second PC
  running ComfyUI with this pack and that memory leaves your render card —
  identical results, verified across machines, with a local cache so repeated
  text never touches the network. One flag on the switches panel turns it
  on; it ships off.
- **`H3 TAE Decode`.** 2-second full-resolution draft previews from a 9 MB
  tiny decoder, versus about a minute per shot through the real VAE. For seed
  hunts and batch triage, never finals.

Plus a Speed Boosters panel (Spectrum, TeaCache, block cache, EasyCache —
each measured and eye-tested, with honest notes about which distort people),
and new defaults tuned for 16

# SeedVR2-3B for VigenFlow on AMD Ryzen AI

This package contains the SeedVR2-3B weights in the BF16 and BFP16 layouts
used by [VigenFlow](https://github.com/jia1217/vigenflow)'s single-image NPU upscaler. It includes the DiT, VAE encoder,
VAE decoder, and fixed text embedding. The safetensors archive uses the
`vgf-npu-weights-1` format.

Use VigenFlow's updated `prepare_base.exe` to install the archive:

```sh
./prepare_base.exe --only seedvr2 --weights_root /path/to/all_model_weights
```

Run the SeedVR2 worker with an input image and point it at the installed
`seedvr2` folder using `-w`. The worker and its compiled NPU program bundle
are distributed separately.

The weights were converted from [ByteDance Seed's SeedVR2-3B
checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B/tree/37255ff8cccfb01071b87f635a5948ca8d53117c).

It is a **Full Q4 quantized distribution** based on [Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit) with the official 4-step distillation adapter [lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning) **pre-fused (baked) directly into the 4-bit transformer weights**. --- ### ⚡ Why This Model is a Game Changer for Apple Silicon (16 GB): 1. **11x Speedup (5 Minutes instead of 1 Hour)**: - Standard Qwen-Image Edit requires **20 steps** at guidance 4.0 (~180s per step, total **59 min 35 s** on an Apple Silicon M1 16 GB). - This Lightning model converges in only **4 steps at guidance 1.0**, finishing in **5 min 20 s (320s)** with identical visual fidelity! 2. **Zero LoRA Overhead & Zero Memory Spike**: - Instead of loading the 849 MB adapter dynamically or attempting on-the-fly dequantization (which inflates memory to 20+ GB and causes disk swap thrashing), the 720 transformer layers are **pre-fused and quantized to 4-bit (`QuantizedLinear`, group_size=64)**. - Loads in **1.47 seconds** and generates with native Apple Silicon hardware quantization kernels. 3. **Pre-Quantized 4-Bit Text Encoder**: - The multimodal Qwen 2.5 7B text encoder is also fully quantized to 4-bit (**4.25 GB** instead of the original 14.5 GB BF16), keeping total unified memory consumption under 12 GB. --- ## 🎨 Reproducible Demonstration: "Bear in a Red Suit" Below is a 100% reproducible test comparing the original reference image and the edited output generated on Apple Silicon in 4 steps using this exact checkpoint: | 1. Lightning LoRA (`bake_lora=True`)** | 4 steps, CFG 1.0 | 19.56 GB RAM, 19.75 GB Swap | **12 min 14 s** | ~178 s / step | **~5x faster** | | **4. Lightning LoRA (`bake_lora=False`)** | 4 steps, CFG 1.0 | ~12.5 GB RAM, 0 GB Swap | **6 min 17 s** | ~83 s / step | **~9.5x faster** | | **🚀 5. This Model (Pre-Fused Native Q4)** | **4 steps, CFG 1.0** | **~11.5 GB RAM, 0 GB Swap** | **5 min 20 s (320 s)** | **~75 s / step** | **~11.2x faster !** | #### Why the differences on a 16 GB machine? - **Version 1 (Crash):** Standard distributions ship the text encoder in BF16 (14.5 GB) alongside the transformer and VAE. # MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA — few-step audio-video generation

A LoRA for [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3) that renders
joint **video + synchronized stereo audio** in as few as **4 sampling steps**
instead of the usual ~20 — a ~5× sampling speedup — and keeps getting better as
you add steps.

## Which checkpoint — `v4` (step 600) or `v1` (850)?

For **most** work, use **`minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors`**. It's the
strongest checkpoint we've released: much better static and small-motion shots,
markedly better micro-detail (faces, fingers, fine texture), and the
over-sharpening / plastic look of the earlier `v1` (~850) line is **fully
resolved**.

v4 introduced a **static-frame enhancement** — a big win for static and
small-motion content. The one trade-off shows up **only at 4 steps with large,
fast motion**, where v4 can produce **motion-smear / trailing ghosting** (we're
actively fixing this). Two things address it:

- **Use 6–8 steps.** This **largely removes the smear** and is where v4 looks its
  best. v4 also tolerates higher step counts better than v1, which tends to
  over-sharpen at high steps + strength 1.0.
- For the specific case of **4 steps *and* heavy motion**, the older **`v1` ~850**
  checkpoint can still be the friendlier pick.

```
Using 6–8 steps?        ── yes ──►  v4-600  (recommended)
   │ no (4 steps)
   ▼
Heavy / fast motion?    ── no  ──►  v4-600  (recommended)
   │ yes
   ▼
                                    v1-850  (friendlier at 4-step heavy motion)
```

Still a preview — training continues; the two areas still being improved are
**audio** and **behaviour under fast, intense motion**.

## Steps and strength — read this

- **4 steps is the recommended *minimum*; 4–8 is the useful range.** 6–8 steps
  look noticeably better than 4, so add steps if you can afford them. Past **8
  steps** it stops helping and can start to introduce **over-sharp artifacts** —
  there's no benefit to going higher, so stay in **4–8**.
- **Keep strength at `1.0`.** It's tuned for 1.0 and holds up well across the 4–8
  step range. Only reach for the strength dial if a *specific* clip misbehaves —
  then **blurry ghosting / smear → nudge up** (`~1.05–1.2`), **over-sharp grain →
  nudge down** (`~0.8–0.95`).
- Keep the scheduler on `simple`.

## Use it in ComfyUI (recommended)

Custom nodes: **[Larryvrh/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo](https://github.com/Larryvrh/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo)**
— or search **"MiniMax-H3 Turbo"** in ComfyUI-Manager. (Keep the node updated; it
evolves alongside these weights.)

1. Install the nodes (Manager, or `git clone` into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes`) and put
   a `.safetensors` from this repo into `ComfyUI/models/loras/`. You also need the
   base MiniMax-H3 model, VAEs and text encoder — see the
   [MiniMax-H3 tutorial](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3).
2. Start from the official MiniMax-H3 workflow (t2v or i2v) and make two changes:
   - insert **MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA** between the model loader and the sampler;
   - feed `SamplerCustomAdvanced` from **MiniMax-H3 Turbo Sampler**, and set the
     scheduler to `simple` at **≥ 4 steps**.

Everything else stays as in the official graph, so both text-to-video and
image-to-video work. A ready-made t2v workflow ships in the
[node repo](https://github.com/Larryvrh/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo/tree/main/example_workflows)
(and here as `minimax_h3_t2v_turbo.json`) — drag it in.

- **Base model**: any MiniMax-H3 base — full (`bf16`, `int8_convrot`) **and the
  pruned/curve variants** (`pruned_int8`, `pruned_fp8`). The node auto-detects a
  pruned base and re-injects the time-conditioning at run time, so **one LoRA file
  covers every base**.
- **`low_vram`** switch: **off** applies the LoRA at run time (sharpest,
  recommended); **on** merges it into the weights for the lowest peak VRAM (a bit
  softer on quantized bases). Turn it on only if you run out of memory.
- The custom sampler **auto-adapts to your ComfyUI version**: MiniMax-H3 runs
  video and audio on two different flow schedules; recent ComfyUI handles that
  natively (`ModelSamplingAV`) and older ComfyUI doesn't — the Turbo Sampler
  detects which and does the right thing either way, so nothing to change when you
  update ComfyUI.

## Weights

All bf16, ~744 MB, applied as a plain low-rank update
(`W_eff = W + lora_B @ lora_A`, alpha = rank, so no extra scaling). **Prefer the
EMA files**; the non-EMA ones are for comparison.

| file | notes |
|---|---|
| **`minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors`** | **recommended — current best.** Strong static/small-motion, good micro-detail, no over-sharpening. |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600.safetensors` | v4-600 non-EMA (comparison). |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step150_ema.safetensors` | earlier v4 checkp

# Teriks/MiniMax-H3-Qwen3VL-text-encoder

ComfyUI safetensors int8_tensorwise and nvfp4 quantization of [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3), written by [dgenerate](https://github.com/Teriks/dgenerate) 6.0.0.

The license of the source model applies to these weights.

Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 and Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image publish qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_bf16.safetensors, qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors, and qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors without lm_head.weight. The MiniMax Qwen3-VL config sets tie_word_embeddings to false, so those files cannot rewrite a prompt with --pipeline-prompt-enhance. These files were quantized from MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 text_encoder, which includes lm_head.weight. int8 is ConvRot INT8. nvfp4 covers every linear that fits. The Comfy NVFP4 file also sets full_precision_matrix_mult.

## Source

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` |
| Pipeline | `MiniMaxH3ModularPipeline` |
| Components | `text_encoder` (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`) |
| Formats | `int8`, `nvfp4` |

## Quantization

Keep the original repository as the model and pass the quant file with the matching component option, so the config still comes from the repository.

Tensor names are the ones the component stored.

| Format | File |
| --- | --- |
| `int8_tensorwise` | ComfyUI safetensors quant |
| `nvfp4` | ComfyUI safetensors quant |

`--formats` accepts short names and presets. `q4` is Q4_K. `q8` is Q8_0. `fp8` is float8_e4m3fn.

## Command

```bash
dgenerate --sub-command quantize MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 --subfolders text_encoder --formats int8 nvfp4 --output 'D:\dgenerate-quants\minimax-h3-qwen3vl' --hf-upload Teriks/MiniMax-H3-Qwen3VL-text-encoder --hf-upload-card 'extra:Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 and Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image publish qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_bf16.safetensors, qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors, and qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors without lm_head.weight. The MiniMax Qwen3-VL config sets tie_word_embeddings to false, so those files cannot rewrite a prompt with --pipeline-prompt-enhance. These files were quantized from MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 text_encoder, which includes lm_head.weight. int8 is ConvRot INT8. nvfp4 covers every linear that fits. The Comfy NVFP4 file also sets full_precision_matrix_mult.'
```

| `config.json` | 1.4 KB |
| `text_encoder-int8_tensorwise.safetensors` | 31.8 GB |
| `text_encoder-nvfp4.safetensors` | 18.5 GB |

[**MiniMax-H3 PE**](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) is a prompt enhancement model fine-tuned from [Gemma4-12B-IT](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it) for MiniMax-H3 audio and video generation. The model is **jointly trained to enhance prompts for the FL2VA / Ref2VA input formats using a single set of PE weights**. It uses user instructions and task context to organize audiovisual descriptions for H3 generation. This repository provides **two independent ComfyUI workflows, one for FL2VA and one for Ref2VA**, along with **standard and quantized model versions**. ## Input Formats and Use Cases | H3 input format | Use cases | Prompt enhancement focus | | --- | --- | --- | | **FL2VA** | T2VA (text only), I2VA (first frame), L2VA (last frame), and FL2VA (first and last frames) | Organize scenes, actions, camera movement, changes over time, and sound descriptions; incorporate frame constraints when provided | | **Ref2VA** | Reference-conditioned generation | Organize subject definitions, reference relationships, content retention, actions, camera movement, and sound descriptions | Here, **FL2VA refers to an input format used by MiniMax-H3**, covering T2VA, I2VA, and FL2VA modes. Choose the independent **FL2VA / Ref2VA** workflow that matches your generation task. ## Interactive Demo [![MiniMax-H3 prompt enhancement comparison preview — click to open the interactive demo](https://cdn.wuli.art/image/open_bench_20261109_fiveway_pick8_showcase/model-card-demo-preview.jpg)](https://cdn.wuli.art/image/open_bench_20261109_fiveway_pick8_showcase/index.html) [**Explore the MiniMax-H3 prompt enhancement comparison →**](https://cdn.wuli.art/image/open_bench_20261109_fiveway_pick8_showcase/index.html) Compare **Raw (No PE), Gemma4 base, MiniMax-H3 Official PE, lightx2v Rewriter, and Ours** across **9 selected cases and 45 videos**. The showcase covers text-to-video, image-to-video, and multi-reference generation, with synchronized playback, two-column comparisons, selectable audio, and expandable original and enhanced prompts. ## Workflow Overview ```text User instructions + task context ↓ ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐ ↓ ↓ FL2VA Workflow Ref2VA Workflow │ │ └───────────────────┬───────────────────┘ ↓ Ours Prompt Rewriter (BF16 / FP8 / Int8) ↓ Enhanced prompt ↓ MiniMax-H3 (FL2VA / Ref2VA) ↓ Video and audio ``` The two workflows are **alternative options**. PE produces an enhanced prompt, which the corresponding H3 generation pipeline uses with the required assets to generate video and audio. ## ComfyUI Workflows Two independent workflows are available. import torch

negative_prompt = ''

model_output = pipeline(

    guidance_scale=1.0,
).images[0]

model_output.save("output.png", format="PNG")

```

gguf - minimax-h3 - text-to-video - image-to-video - audio-video-generation --- # MiniMax-H3 GGUF [English](https://huggingface.co/yasutoshi-lab/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/blob/main/README_EN.md) | 日本語 [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)（revision `0919fb6`）を、[stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp) 用の GGUF に量子化したものです。MiniMax 公式の配布物ではありません。 > **ライセンスと利用できる地域**：MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement（`LICENSE`）に従います。 ## ファイルの構成 フォルダの名前は公式のリポジトリに合わせています。stable-diffusion.cpp で動かすのに要るファイルは、すべてこのリポジトリにあります。 ``` transformer/DiT-fl2va-{量子化}.gguf T2VA・I2VA・FL2VA 用の DiT transformer_ref/DiT-ref2va-{量子化}.gguf Ref2VA 用の DiT text_encoder/TE-{量子化}.gguf テキストエンコーダー（Qwen3-VL-32B、50 層） text_encoder/mmproj-F16.gguf そのビジョン部（Ref2VA で使う） text_encoder_tail/TE-{量子化}-tail.gguf TE から削った層 50〜63（動画の生成には使わない） vae/source/model.safetensors 動画 VAE（F32） vae/VAE-{F16,Q8_0,Q4_0}.gguf 動画 VAE（F16・Q8_0・Q4_0） audio_vae/audio_vae.safetensors 音声 VAE（F32） audio_vae/audio_vae-F16.safetensors 音声 VAE（F16） vae/・audio_vae/ の設定、scheduler/、audio_scheduler/、docs/ 公式のファイル（参照用） ``` 量子化：BF16・Q8_0_M・Q8_0・Q6_K_M・Q6_K・Q5_K_M・Q4_K_M・Q4_K_S・IQ4_XS・IQ3_S・IQ3_XS・IQ3_XXS・IQ2_S・IQ2_XS `Q8_0_M` と `Q6_K_M` は、このリポジトリ独自の構成です。それぞれ Q8_0・Q6_K を既定にし、Q5_K_M・Q4_K_M で精度を上げているのと同じ場所（DiT は qkv の全層と FFN の down の 25 層、TE は attention の v と FFN の down の 25 層）だけを、BF16・Q8_0 にしています。`Q8_0_M` の DiT は、AdaLN の射影も BF16 です（96GB の GPU 1 枚に、DiT・TE・VAE がちょうど収まる大きさにしています）。 ## 元のモデルから変更した点 ライセンス III.2 による表示です。学習による重みの変更はしていません。 - **DiT**：シャードを 1 ファイルにまとめ、`attn.qkv_proj.weight` の行を [heads, (q,k,v), head_dim] から [(q,k,v), heads, head_dim] に並べ替えて、量子化しました。AdaLN の射影は幅が K-quant・IQ 系に合わないため、Q8_0（Q6_K_M・Q6_K）・Q5_1（Q5_K_M）・Q5_0（Q4_K_M・Q4_K_S）・IQ4_NL（IQ 系）にしています。Q4_K_S と IQ3_XS の混ぜ方は llama.cpp の規則に合わせました。IQ 系は imatrix を使いました。 - **TE**：使われる 50 層に切り（層 50〜63 を削除）、[llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) で量子化しました。IQ 系は imatrix を使いました。 - **音声 VAE**：weight_norm の `weight_g`・`weight_v` を 1 本の `weight` にまとめ、`latents_mean`・`latents_std` をテンソルとして加えました（F32 のまま）。F16 版は、2 次元以上の重みを F16 にしたものです。 - **動画 VAE**：`vae/source/model.safetensors` は公式のままです。F16 版は重みを F16 に、Q8_0 版・Q4_0 版はデコーダーの線形層を Q8_0・Q4_0、畳み込みを F16 にしたものです。 - **設定ファイル・`docs/`**：公式のまま、変更していません。 ハッシュは `SHA256SUMS` にあります。 ## TE の残層（`text_encoder_tail/`） `text_encoder/TE-{量子化}.gguf` から削った層 50〜63 を、量子化ごとに `text_encoder_tail/TE-{量子化}-tail.gguf` として配置しています。動画の生成には不要です。 同じ量子化の `TE-{量子化}.gguf` に `TE-{量子化}-tail.gguf` のテンソルを足し、`qwen3vl.block_count` を 64 にすると、元の 64 層の TE に戻ります。量子化し直す必要はありません。 ## 組み合わせたときの合計容量 DiT と TE を同じ量子化で組み合わせたときの、ファイルの合計です（GB = 10^9 バイト）。DiT の容量は FL2VA・Ref2VA とも同じです。VAE は、量子化の強さに合わせて次の精度のものを組み合わせます。 | DiT・TE | DiT (GB) | TE (GB) | 動画 VAE (GB) | 音声 VAE (GB) | 合計 (GB) | Ref2VA の合計 (GB)

（DiT + TE + VAE） | 画像編集時の合計 (GB)
（+ `mmproj-F16.gguf`） | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 | BF16 | 40.32 | 51.88 | 94.54 | 95.73 | | Q8_0 | Q8_0 | 21.54 | 27.56 | 51.44 | 52.63 | | Q6_K | Q6_K | 16.68 | 21.28 | 40.30 | 41.50 | | Q5_K_M | Q5_K_M | 15.08 | 18.39 | 35.81 | 37.00 | | Q4_K_M | Q4_K_M | 12.77 | 15.68 | 30.78 | 31.97 | | IQ4_XS | IQ4_XS | 10.89 | 14.05 | 27.28 | 28.48 | | IQ3_S | IQ3_S | 8.86 | 11.49 | 22.68 | 23.88 | | IQ3_XXS | IQ3_XXS | 7.92 | 10.21 | 20.46 | 21.66 | | IQ2_S | IQ2_S | 6.66 | 8.40 | 17.40 | 18.60 | | IQ2_XS | IQ2_XS | 6.04 | 7.95 | 16.32 | 17.52 | - 画像編集（参照画像あり）では、TE のビジョン部 `text_encoder/mmproj-F16.gguf`（1.20 GB）も読み込みます。 - 実行時のメモリ使用量は、ファイルの容量とは一致しません。 > **低精度の量子化について**：Q8_0〜Q4_K_M は BF16 と同じ構図を保ちます。IQ4_XS・IQ3 系は構図が変わりやすくなります。IQ2 系は文字からの生成が崩れます（画像編集は IQ2_S までおおむね保たれます）。劣化は主に DiT の量子化によるもので、TE は Q5_K_M まで画質にほとんど影響しません。 ## 使い方の例（stable-diffusion.cpp） DiT と TE を Q4_K_M にした例です。stable-diffusion.cpp `32d516c` で確かめました。 ```bash hf download yasutoshi-lab/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF \ transformer/DiT-Q4_K_M.gguf text_encoder/TE-Q4_K_M.gguf text_encoder/mmproj-F16.gguf \ vae/config.json vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors --local-dir h3-image-gguf G=h3-image-gguf # 文字から画像を作る sd-cli --diffusion-model $G/transformer/DiT-Q4_K_M.gguf --llm $G/text_encoder/TE-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --vae $G/vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors \ -p "A red apple on a wooden table, soft window light, photorealistic" \ --sigmas minimax-h3-image --steps 6 --cfg-scale 1.0 --sampling-method euler \ -W 1024 -H 1024 -o apple.png # 画像を編集する（TE のビジョン部 mmproj と参照画像 -r を足す） sd-cli --diffusion-model $G/transformer/DiT-Q4_K_M.gguf --llm $G/text_encoder/TE-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --llm_vision $G/text_encoder/mmproj-F16.gguf --vae $G/vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors \ -r apple.png -p "Edit . Replace the red apple with a green pear. Keep everything else unchanged." \ --sigmas minimax-h3-image --steps 6 --cfg-scale 1.0 --sampling-method euler \ -W 1024 -H 1024 -o pear.png ``` - ステップ数は 6 から変えられません（AdaLN を 6 ステップの時刻だけの表にしているため）。 ## 動作確認 DiT 10 種 × TE 10 種のうち 28 構成で、文字からの生成と画像編集を stable-diffusion.cpp で行い、すべて画像が出ることを確かめました。 - GPU：NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96GB - stable-diffusion.cpp `32d516c`、llama.cpp `aa75ff323` 以下は公式のモデルカード（[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)、revision `5f90473`）の引用です。 ---
