# Qwen-Image 2.1 NF4 for LoRA Training

Pre-quantized [Qwen-Image 2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) packaged for
**AcademiaSD Qwen-Image 2.1 LoRAlab**, a LoRA trainer for consumer GPUs (8 GB and up).
It is downloaded automatically by the LoRAlab; you do not need to fetch it by hand.

> **This is not an inference checkpoint.** The transformer is stored as a per-layer NF4 cache
> that the LoRAlab rebuilds directly; it does not load with `from_pretrained`. For generation,
> use the original model or its ComfyUI release.

## What is inside

| Folder | Size | Content |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `transformer/` | 3.87 GB | 7B DiT as an NF4 cache: 224 NF4 layers + 8 precision-critical layers in BF16 + norms (`others.safetensors`) |
| `text_encoder_BF16/` | 16.29 GB | Qwen3-VL-8B in BF16, exact. `lm_head` is not stored (only hidden states are used) |
| `text_encoder_INT8/` | 8.78 GB | Qwen3-VL-8B in LLM.int8 |
| `text_encoder_NF4/` | 5.45 GB | Qwen3-VL-8B in NF4, with `lm_head`: also used as the dataset **auto-captioner** |
| `vae/` | 1.35 GB | Original 64-channel RGBA VAE, unchanged |
| `scheduler/`, `processor/`, `model_index.json` | — | Original files, unchanged |
| `LoRAs/` | 0.34 GB | [Viggle Turbo LoRA](https://huggingface.co/Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo) (4 steps), used for fast training previews |

The LoRAlab downloads only the text encoder variant you select.

### Transformer (NF4)

- Every attention and MLP linear of the 32 blocks is NF4 (bitsandbytes, double quantization).
- `img_in`, `txt_in`, the shared `modulation`, the timestep embedder, `norm_out` and `proj_out`
  stay in BF16: they are small and every block depends on them.
- Measured against the BF16 transformer on the same inputs: cosine similarity **0.998–0.9996**
  on the predicted velocity, with practically identical loss.
- Loads in ~2 s and takes **~3.9 GB of VRAM**, with no BF16 copy of the model needed.

### Text encoder variants

The text encoder of Qwen-Image 2.1 is exactly **Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct** (verified tensor by tensor
against the official repository). It is only used during pre-caching, never while training.

| Variant | Peak VRAM | Error per token vs BF16 | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| BF16 CPU offload | adapts to free VRAM | 0% | **Default.** Layers that do not fit run from RAM |
| BF16 | ~15.5 GB | 0% | Needs 16+ GB |
| INT8 | ~8.5 GB | ~9% | |
| NF4 | ~5.5 GB | ~24% | Also the auto-captioner (~6 GB peak) |

Error measured on real captions against the BF16 text encoder, which is what ComfyUI uses at
inference. Pre-caching with an exact encoder means the LoRA trains on the same conditioning it
will see when you generate.

## What the LoRAlab trains with it

- **Characters, objects and styles**: one image + caption per sample.
- **Edit LoRAs**: `name_before` / `name_after` pairs with an imperative instruction
  (e.g. *"make it TOSTIOK style"*). The "before" is encoded by Qwen3-VL together with the
  instruction and prepended as clean latents, exactly as the ComfyUI `TextEncodeQwenImage21` node does.

Exported LoRAs use the diffusers/PEFT key format with per-layer `alpha` and load directly in
ComfyUI (verified with ComfyUI's own LoRA loader).

## License

Qwen-Image 2.1 and its derivatives are released under the **Qwen Research License**
(see `LICENSE`): **non-commercial use only (research or evaluation)**. The same license applies
to this conversion and to the Viggle Turbo LoRA included in `LoRAs/`. By downloading these files
you accept the terms of that license.

## Credits

- [Qwen](https://huggingface.co/Qwen) for Qwen-Image 2.1 and Qwen3-VL.
- [Viggle](https://huggingface.co/Viggle) for the Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo LoRA.
- NF4 conversion and LoRAlab by **AcademiaSD**:
  [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Academia_SD) ·
  [X](https://twitter.com/Academia_S_D) ·
  [Discord](https://discord.gg/Syuaduy678) ·
  [Ko-Fi](https://ko-fi.com/academiasd)

---

### Resumen en español

Qwen-Image 2.1 cuantizado a NF4 para el **LoRAlab de AcademiaSD**, que lo descarga solo.
Transformer de 7B en NF4 (~3,9 GB de VRAM), text encoder Qwen3-VL-8B en tres variantes
(BF16 exacto, INT8, NF4; solo se usa en el pre-caché), VAE original y el Turbo LoRA de Viggle
para previews rápidas. Sirve para entrenar LoRAs de personajes, objetos, estilos y de edición
(pares antes/después). No es un checkpoint de inferencia. Licencia Qwen Research:
**solo uso no comercial**.

# H3 Character Swap Lora

[![Follow @akatz_ai on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/Follow-%40akatz__ai-111111?style=flat-square&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/akatz_ai)
[![Patreon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support-Patreon-FF424D?style=flat-square&logo=patreon&logoColor=white)](https://www.patreon.com/Akatz)
[![GitHub Sponsors](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-GitHub-EA4AAA?style=flat-square&logo=githubsponsors&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sponsors/akatz-ai)
[![Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tip-Ko--fi-FF5E5B?style=flat-square&logo=kofi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/akatz)

![Character Swap: original video, character reference, and swapped result](assets/character-swap-showcase.gif)

**Original → Reference → Character swap.** Four selected examples.

**V1.5 is the recommended checkpoint for new character swaps.** It replaces a
selected person in a source performance with a character from an image reference.

- **[Download V1.5](h3_character_swap_v1.5.safetensors)** — recommended, strength 1.0.
- **[Download V1](h3_character_swap_pro4500_1000.safetensors)** — retained for
  existing workflows and reproducible comparisons.

## Versions

| Version | File | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H3 Character Swap V1.5 | `h3_character_swap_v1.5.safetensors` | Recommended |
| H3 Character Swap V1 | `h3_character_swap_pro4500_1000.safetensors` | Previous release |

## Native workflow with H3 Relay 2.0

[Download the canvas workflow](examples/H3-Character-Swap-Relay-V2.json) or
[the API prompt](examples/H3-Character-Swap-Relay-V2.api.json). These use the
recommended V1.5 adapter, native ComfyUI model loading, reference conditioning,
SAM masking, sampling, loops and saving, plus reusable Relay timeline helpers.
The model weights are unchanged by this workflow update.

Install [H3 Relay 2.0](https://github.com/akatz-ai/h3-relay) and follow
[the workflow guide](examples/README.md) for models, runtime and input paths.

## Use in ComfyUI

1. Obtain the H3 Ref2VA base model, text encoder and VAEs separately.
2. Place `h3_character_swap_v1.5.safetensors` in your configured LoRA directory
   and select it in a compatible model-only LoRA loader at strength **1.0**.
3. Provide the source performance as `<Video 1>` and character reference as
   `<Picture 1>`. Describe the person to replace and the reference identity.
4. Begin with a short continuous shot at 24 fps. Use your runtime's supported H3
   frame grid and review identity, motion, expressions and joins before extending.

Example:

> Replace the selected person in <Video 1> with the character in <Picture 1>.
> Keep the reference character's face, hair and clothing. Follow the source
> performance's pose, gaze, expression and movement. Preserve the scene and the
> other people.

The H3 Character Swap tool handles masks, optional scene anchors, source-audio
conditioning and continuation history. Its tested recipe uses the Ref2VA INT8
base, this character adapter at strength 1.0, and the separate
`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_768p_comfyui_bf16.safetensors` at strength 1.0:
8 steps, CFG 1, `er_sde`, `normal`. The LoRA itself is not a standalone model
and does not include the base, training assistant, VAEs or Turbo weights.

## V1 vs V1.5 comparison

<video controls playsinline src="https://huggingface.co/akatz-ai/MiniMax-H3-Character-Swap-LoRA/resolve/main/assets/character-swap-lora_v1-vs-v1-5.mp4" width="100%"></video>

[Download the comparison video](assets/character-swap-lora_v1-vs-v1-5.mp4).
V1 is on the left; V1.5 is on the right. These selected examples show cases
where V1 loses the reference identity or returns to the source appearance,
while V1.5 retains more of the character. They illustrate improvements on
these shots, rather than an aggregate benchmark.

## Examples and limitations

This remains an experimental character-swap model. Identity, source timing,
expressions, occlusions and cuts can still drift. A recommended default does not
mean every shot improves over V1. Selected comparisons show improved retention
of stylized faces, hair and character identity. Broad evaluation is still in
progress; these observations are not a claim of uniform improvement.

The accompanying tool retains the original source soundtrack in its export.
That is an application feature, not evidence that the LoRA reproduces audio
accurately or that lip sync is exact. Long segment controls in the tool are not
a guarantee of long-shot quality or suitability for every GPU.

The existing showcase and examples below are **V1 results and workflows**.

# SeedVR2 causal 3-D VAE (fastforks safetensors)

Weights by ByteDance Seed: Wang et al., SeedVR2: One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training (2025), converted to safetensors (see Source), hosted for [fastforks](https://github.com/kleinicke/fastforks). This repo is named after the weights,
not after a model: every fastforks model that uses these exact bytes (same SHA-256) points here.

## Files

| file | size | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `seedvr2-vae.safetensors` | 478.1 MiB (501325110 bytes) | `bcf7f47d490efcfdce05659510baec78e6bb8301ae6b2dee584a09bdfa54cd4a` |

## Source

- Upstream: https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B/tree/37255ff8cccfb01071b87f635a5948ca8d53117c
- Original file: ema_vae.pth (SHA-256 c7df8a67e68b7f9aca3d5d2153d2ce8ab4373687741a0f9ce87cb356ace51cac; the same file in ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B and -7B)
- Converted by fastforks with `tools/convert_seedvr2.py vae ema_vae.pth`: every tensor in bfloat16 (upstream runs the VAE with `vae.dtype = bfloat16`), upstream's keys. No retraining.
- Precision: bfloat16 (every tensor).
- Conversion script: `convert_seedvr2.py` in this repo (also `tools/convert_seedvr2.py` in fastforks).

## Licence

Apache-2.0, the authors' licence: https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B/blob/37255ff8cccfb01071b87f635a5948ca8d53117c/README.md

Evidence that it covers the weights: Model card front matter of ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B and -7B: "license: apache-2.0"; code: https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR/blob/e4de8c24441a67e1b7df56abea10645059bb1185/LICENSE (Apache-2.0).

`LICENSE` in this repo: the upstream licence text, kept as the licence requires; `NOTICE`: what we changed.
Copyright stays with the authors. Converted by the fastforks maintainers; fastforks is not affiliated with the authors.

## Used by

| fastforks model | family |
|---|---|
| `seedvr2-3b@1` | seedvr2 |
| `seedvr2-7b@1` | seedvr2 |

## How fastforks downloads it

fastforks downloads the file on first use and checks it against the SHA-256 above (nothing unverified is
loaded); `fastforks download MODEL` fetches it ahead of time.
These converted files exist only here, so this repo is the download URL in the model cards.
Without fastforks: `hf download fastforks/seedvr2-vae-bf16 seedvr2-vae.safetensors`.

# LTX-2.5 FP8 for Paiton on RDNA4

These are weights of [Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) (22B distilled, video with
audio) converted for one AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB). The transformer and the Gemma 4 text encoder are in
FP8 in layouts that Paiton's native HIP kernels read. The files only run with the Paiton container; they do not load in
diffusers, ComfyUI or Lightricks' `ltx-pipelines`.

## Speed

| Request (121 frames, 5 s at 24 fps) | Paiton, this repository | Stock LTX-2.5, BF16 | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| text to video, 1280 x 704 | 18.1 s | 128.6 s | 7.1x |
| image to video, 1280 x 704 | 21.1 s | - | - |
| text to video, 1920 x 1088 | 48.8 s | 420.5 s | 8.6x |
| image to video, 1920 x 1088 | 51.9 s | - | - |

One R9700 at its 300 W limit. Paiton: server time from HTTP request to mp4 with a warm server (median of 3 runs), peak
VRAM use on the card 26.6 GiB at 1280 x 704 and 27.4 GiB at 1920 x 1088. Stock: Lightricks' `ltx-pipelines` distilled
pipeline in BF16 on the same card, warm, with `--offload cpu` because the BF16 weights do not fit in 32 GB. With
`--quantization fp8-cast` the stock pipeline is slower on this card (156.7 s and 488.5 s): its matrix products still
run in BF16.

## Run

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Eliovp-BV/paiton-vllm-plugin.git
cd paiton-vllm-plugin
export HF_TOKEN=<your Hugging Face read token>
./models/LTX-2.5/launch.sh
```

```bash
./models/LTX-2.5/run.sh generate "A street drummer plays a fast rhythm on a city sidewalk at dusk while the crowd claps and cheers" --out drummer.mp4
```

Accept the license terms on this page first and use a token of the same account. The first start downloads this
repository (38 GB) at the revision pinned in the container and checks every file
against its SHA-256. The server answers `POST /v1/videos/generations` on port 30000 with an mp4 (H.264 video, AAC
audio). The [guide](https://github.com/Eliovp-BV/paiton-vllm-plugin/blob/main/models/LTX-2.5/README.md) lists the
request fields and limits.

## Quality

Any quantized version of this 11-step sampler, the stock pipeline's FP8 cast mode included, follows a different path
from the BF16 one after small numeric changes, so its frames differ from the BF16 video in layout and detail. PSNR and
SSIM against a BF16 run with the same noise therefore measure how far the sampler drifted from that run, not how good
the video looks. With the current FP8 weights (round to nearest):

| Case, 121 frames | This build, PSNR / SSIM | Stock `--quantization fp8-cast`, PSNR / SSIM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| text to video, 1280 x 704 | 25.7 dB / 0.918 | 25.3 dB / 0.90 |
| image to video, 1280 x 704 | 24.5 dB / 0.881 | - |
| text to video, 1920 x 1088 | 18.9 dB / 0.724 | 18.7 dB / 0.726 |
| 4 more prompts, 1920 x 1088 | 18.0 to 25.5 dB | 19.4 to 26.4 dB |
| mean of the 5 prompts at 1920 x 1088 | 21.25 dB / 0.726 | 22.35 dB / 0.759 |
| audio of the same 5 prompts, mean log-spectral distance (lower is closer) | 4.69 dB | 4.75 dB |

At 1280 x 704 this build is as close to the BF16 run as the stock FP8 cast mode. At 1920 x 1088 it drifts about as
much: 1.1 dB lower on the mean of five prompts, with two prompts lower (by 1.9 and 4.1 dB) and three equal or higher.
Side by side, the frames of the two FP8 runs show different camera paths and positions, with no blocking, banding or
noise. We also tried GPTQ rounding for the transformer weights; the videos showed no consistent gain, so this release
keeps round to nearest.

| `te/` | Gemma 4 12B t

# MiniMax H3 Ref2VA in FP8: video with sound on one R9700

Send a prompt and 1 to 9 reference pictures (or one reference video), and get back a 5.2-second 864×480 clip with
stereo sound in **30 seconds**, on one Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32 GB, 300 W).

These are the weights for the native MiniMax H3 Ref2VA runner in
[paiton-vllm-plugin](https://github.com/Eliovp-BV/paiton-vllm-plugin/tree/main/models/MiniMax-H3) (v1.2). The runner is
compiled HIP code for RDNA4, with no PyTorch, diffusers or ComfyUI inside. You call it over HTTP or from a ComfyUI node.

## Numbers

The original BF16 release is 144 GB, and its transformer alone (66.3 GB) is twice the memory of the card. This build
needs 50.9 GB on disk for one preset and peaks at 24.7 to 26.8 GiB of VRAM.

Time per request on one R9700 with the 4-step preset (Turbo4), 124 frames at 24 fps, from the prepared inputs to the
finished MP4. v1.1.0 is our earlier ComfyUI build with a W4A8 denoiser
([EliovpAI/MiniMax-H3-W4A8-Paiton-RDNA4](https://huggingface.co/EliovpAI/MiniMax-H3-W4A8-Paiton-RDNA4)) on the same
card.

| Request | v1.2 (these weights) | v1.1.0 | Faster by |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 864×480, 1 picture | **30.4 s** | 50.6 s | 1.7× |
| 864×480, 3 pictures | **33.4 s** | 85.3 s | 2.6× |
| 864×480, 9 pictures | **44.3 s** | 178.7 s | 4.0× |
| 1344×768, 9 pictures | **114.1 s** | 258.4 s | 2.3× |
| 864×480, 1 video with its soundtrack | **203.8 s** | not measured | |
| 864×480, 1 picture, 8 steps (Turbo8) | **51.4 s** | 109.2 s | 2.1× |

Peak VRAM for one picture at 864×480 went from 30.6 GiB (v1.1.0) to 24.8 GiB. The server loads the weights once when
it starts (76 s in our test, including a SHA-256 check of every file) and keeps them in memory between requests.

Quality, compared with the BF16 model in diffusers (MI355X, same prompts, references, seed and starting noise). CLIP-T
scores how well the clip matches its prompt:

| Request | CLIP-T, BF16 | CLIP-T, these weights |
|---|---:|---:|
| 864×480, 1 picture | 29.52 | 29.77 |
| 864×480, 3 pictures | 34.68 | 34.35 |
| 864×480, 9 pictures | 26.31 | 25.70 |
| 1344×768, 9 pictures | 25.80 | 25.71 |
| 864×480, 1 video | 29.87 | 29.86 |

Over 15 clips (two seeds, both presets) the frames have a mean similarity of 0.932 (CLIP-I) and 0.871 (DINOv2) to the
same frames of the BF16 clip, where 1.0 is the same image. With nine references the subjects are all there but can
stand in other places than in the BF16 clip. Method and limits:
[BENCHMARKS.md](https://github.com/Eliovp-BV/paiton-vllm-plugin/blob/main/models/MiniMax-H3/BENCHMARKS.md#quality-against-the-bf16-model).

## Run it

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Eliovp-BV/paiton-vllm-plugin.git
cd paiton-vllm-plugin
PAITON_DETACH=1 ./models/MiniMax-H3/native/launch.sh http
docker logs -f paiton-minimax-h3-v12        # wait for "READY http://..."; the first start downloads the weights
curl -o panda.mp4 -F image=@panda.png \
  -F prompt='The red panda from <Picture 1> walks through a sunlit forest. Audio: birds and a stream.' \
  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/videos/generations
```

The runner downloads these files on first use and checks each one against the SHA-256 in its `checkpoints.lock.json`,
so you don't need to download anything by hand. For ComfyUI, copy the `paiton_h3v_client` node from the plugin into
`custom_nodes`; it sends the job to the server, so ComfyUI itself can run on the CPU.

You need one R9700 with nothing else on it, Docker, 51 GB of disk for one preset, and about 41 GB of free host RAM for
the fastest text-encoder path (with less, the runner reads the text encoder from disk instead).

## Files

The files only work with this runner: they are packed for its kernels, not for diffusers or ComfyUI.

| Folder | Content | Size |
|---|---|---:|
| `weights/turbo4/` | transformer, 4 steps (Turbo LoRA merged, FP8) | 20.3 GB |
| `weights/turbo8/` | transformer, 8 steps (Turbo LoRA merged, FP8) | 20.5 GB |
| `dec8.bin`, `enc.bin`, `audio.bin` | video VAE decoder (INT8), video VAE encoder (BF16), audio VAE (FP32) | 3.4 GB |
| `model/tokenizer/` | tokenizer | 7 MB |

The text encoder (Qwen3-VL-32B, layers 0 to 49 in FP8, and the vision tower, 27.2 GB) is the same as the one of
MiniMax H3 Image, so it is not stored twice: the runner downloads it from the `te/` folder of
[EliovpAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-FP8-Paiton-RDNA4](https://huggingface.co/EliovpAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-FP8-Paiton-RDNA4/tree/b33b88f27c8919ca05632ccde801087796d603dd/te), pinned by revision and SHA-256.
The changes to each file are in `MODIFICATIONS.md`.

This repository contains a **9.82 GiB** (`3.31×` compressed from `32.45 GiB` BF16) **`W4A16-HGPTQ`** quantization of [`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) (`d26bb61231c349cf6b7896fa83353113880e1ba3`) produced with [`warp-quant`](https://github.com/nchapman/warp34-quant-lab).

| `vae/` | `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21` | Unmodified `BF16` | `0.63 GiB` |

# MOSS-Image Text Encoder for Apple Silicon: Qwen 3.5 9B (MLX Q8-G64) Apple MLX 8-bit affine (`group_size=64`) conversion of the **Qwen 3.5 9B** text encoder from [`OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT`](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT). Built for **[DiffusionBear](https://github.com/OuincheWinch/DiffusionBear)** to run MOSS-Image natively on 16 GB Apple Silicon Macs. ### Engineering Summary - **Problem:** The official BF16 text encoder is ~19 GB. On 16 GB unified memory Macs, running the text encoder alongside the 5B DiT (~10 GB) and VAE exceeds Metal wired limits, forcing slow PyTorch CPU fallback (~61 s/prompt). - **Architecture:** Hybrid MLX conversion. Heavy MLP projections, full-attention matrices, and embeddings are quantized to 8-bit. **All Gated DeltaNet recurrent projections (`in_proj_*`, `out_proj`, `conv1d`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`, `RMSNorm`) remain in `bfloat16`** to preserve delta-rule state recurrence across 32 layers. - **Results:** Prompt encoding in **17 s cold / ~4 s warm** on Apple GPU (vs 61 s CPU), peak memory **10 GB** (vs 19 GB), cosine similarity **0.9995** vs BF16 ground truth. --- ## Sample Generations & Benchmarks (Apple Silicon M1, 16 GB RAM) All samples generated locally on a **MacBook Pro M1 (16 GB Unified Memory)** using DiffusionBear and this quantized text encoder. ### 🏆 Hero Sample: 50-Step Full CFG Trajectory

# Qwen-Image Edit — MLX 4-bit Full (Pre-Quantized Text Encoder) This repository provides an all-in-one, fully 4-bit quantized distribution of **Qwen-Image Edit** for Apple Silicon using [MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx) and [mflux](https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux). Input Reference (`bear_reference.png`) | 2. Edited Output (`output_edit.png`) | |:---:|:---:| | | | | *Original image: Grizzly bear with classic dark sunglasses* | *Result: "replace the sunglasses with glowing blue aviator goggles"* | ### 📋 Generation Metadata & Benchmark #### Phase 1: Reference Generation (Qwen-Image 2.1 + DMD2) - **Model**: `mlx-community/Qwen-Image-2.1-mflux-q4` - **Adapter**: `qwen-image-2.1-dmd2-2steps-v1.5` - **Prompt**: `"A cinematic portrait of a cool grizzly bear wearing dark sunglasses and a stylish casual red suit jacket with open collar, detailed fur, professional studio lighting, vibrant colors, 8k"` - **Dimensions**: 768 × 768 - **Steps**: 2 - **Seed**: `42` - **Output**: `bear_reference.png` #### Phase 2: Instruction-Based Edit (Qwen-Image Edit 4-bit Full) - **Model**: `Ouinche/qwen-image-edit-mflux-q4-full` - **Prompt**: `"Picture 1: replace the sunglasses with glowing blue aviator goggles"` - **Reference Image**: `bear_reference.png` - **Dimensions**: 768 × 768 - **Steps**: 20 - **Guidance Scale**: 4.0 - **Scheduler**: linear - **Seed**: `42` - **Output**: `output_edit.png` --- ## 💻 Python Quickstart ```python from mflux.models.qwen.variants.edit.qwen_image_edit import QwenImageEdit # Load the model directly from this repository: pipe = QwenImageEdit(model_path="Ouinche/qwen-image-edit-mflux-q4-full") # Generate the edited image: image = pipe.generate_image( prompt="Picture 1: replace the sunglasses with glowing blue aviator goggles", image_paths=["bear_reference.png"], num_inference_steps=20, width=768, height=768, seed=42, ) image.save("output_edit.png") ``` > **Tip for 16 GB Mac users**: Before denoising, you can set `pipe.tiling_config` and evict `pipe.text_encoder` via `pipe.callbacks.before_loop` to keep peak memory under 12 GB. --- ### 📦 Components in this Repository: - # Qwen Image Edit 2509 Lightning 4-Step Nunchaku Lite NVFP4 r32

This directory is a Diffusers-loadable conversion of:

- Base Diffusers model: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509`
- Source Nunchaku checkpoint repo: `nunchaku-ai/nunchaku-qwen-image-edit-2509`
- Source safetensors checkpoint: `lightning-251115/svdq-fp4_r32-qwen-image-edit-2509-lightning-4steps-251115.safetensors`
- Lightning LoRA fused by source checkpoint: `Qwen-Image-Edit-2509-Lightning-4steps-V1.0`

The transformer is packaged for the Diffusers Nunchaku Lite loader:

- `quant_method`: `nunchaku_lite`
- SVDQ precision: `nvfp4`
- SVDQ rank: `32`
- SVDQ targets: `720`
- AWQ targets: `120`

The text encoder is saved with BitsAndBytes 4-bit NF4:

- `quant_method`: `bitsandbytes`
- `load_in_4bit`: `true`
- `bnb_4bit_quant_type`: `nf4`
- `bnb_4bit_compute_dtype`: `bfloat16`

The scheduler config is the lightning scheduler used by the Nunchaku 4/8-step example, with `base_shift = max_shift = log(3)`.

## Benchmark

Measured with 4 inference steps on a 1248x832 input image. Latency is the mean of 3 measured runs after 1 warmup. Max VRAM is peak CUDA allocated memory during generation.

| Checkpoint | Latency | Max VRAM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Converted Diffusers Nunchaku Lite NVFP4 r32 + BNB4 text encoder | 6.06 s | 21.54 GiB |
| Original Nunchaku FP4 r32 safetensors | 4.93 s | 35.44 GiB |

Original baseline: `nunchaku-ai/nunchaku-qwen-image-edit-2509/lightning-251115/svdq-fp4_r32-qwen-image-edit-2509-lightning-4steps-251115.safetensors` loaded through the native Nunchaku transformer.

## Output Comparison

![Lightning watercolor edit comparison](output_comparison.png)

The comparison uses the same input image, prompt, seed, scheduler, and 4-step settings for this converted checkpoint and its original Nunchaku safetensors baseline.

## Run

```python
import torch
from PIL import Image
from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline

model_path = "lite-infer/qwen-image-edit-2509-lightning-4steps-nunchaku-lite-nvfp4-r32"
image_path = "input.png"
output_path = "output.png"

pipe = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained(model_path, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
pipe.to("cuda")

image = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
prompt = "Change the image to watercolor style."

result = pipe(
    image=image,
    prompt=prompt,
    generator=torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1),
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    num_inference_steps=4,
    num_images_per_prompt=1,
)

result.images[0].save(output_path)
```

# SeedVR2-3B for Core ML (one 512 px frame, int4 DiT)

A Core ML conversion of **SeedVR2-3B** ([SeedVR2: One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05301); [code](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR), [weights](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B)), a one-step diffusion transformer for video and image restoration. The iOS app *Still (한컷)* downloads it on demand as a developer-menu experiment for maximum quality, and uses it on single frames.

SeedVR2 synthesises detail. **Restored detail is a prediction, not evidence of captured detail.**

## Files

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `SeedVR2Encoder.mlpackage/` | VAE encoder, ML Program (iOS 18+), FP16 weights |
| `SeedVR2DiT0.mlpackage/` … `SeedVR2DiT6.mlpackage/` | The 32 DiT blocks in seven chunks (0–2, 3–5, 6–8, 9–14, 15–20, 21–26, 27–31), ML Program (iOS 18+), 4-bit weights in 32-weight blocks |
| `SeedVR2Decoder.mlpackage/` | VAE decoder, ML Program (iOS 18+), FP16 weights |
| `manifest.json` | Size and SHA-256 of every file in the packages |
| `LICENSE` | Apache License 2.0 |

## Interface

All inputs and outputs are float16. Every package is fixed at one 512 × 512 output frame.

| Package | Inputs | Outputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SeedVR2Encoder` | `image` `[1, 3, 512, 512]`, RGB in `[-1, 1]` | `latent` `[4096, 16]` |
| `SeedVR2DiT0` | `latent` `[4096, 16]` | `vid_out` `[1024, 2560]`, `txt_out` `[58, 2560]` |
| `SeedVR2DiT1` … `SeedVR2DiT5` | `vid` `[1024, 2560]`, `txt` `[58, 2560]` | `vid_out`, `txt_out` |
| `SeedVR2DiT6` | `vid`, `txt` | `x0` `[4096, 16]` |
| `SeedVR2Decoder` | `x0` `[4096, 16]` | `image` `[1, 3, 512, 512]`, RGB in about `[-1, 1]` |

- **Encoder input.** The low-quality frame enlarged to the output size. The reference CLI uses bilinear interpolation on Apple GPUs.
- **Encoder output.** The posterior mode × 0.9152, channels last. It is the DiT's conditioning latent.
- **Decoder output.** Taken before the CLI's clamp and color correction. The app keeps the decoded detail and takes color and light below about 16 px from the input.
- **Larger images.** The app cuts larger areas into 512 px tiles that overlap by 64 px. Neighbouring tiles cross in a 32 px seam in the middle of their overlap.

Measured on iPhone 14 Pro (A16, iOS 18.4), second run, one model resident at a time:

| | Load | Run per frame |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Encoder (Neural Engine) | 0.3 s | 1.7 s |
| DiT, seven chunks (GPU) | 2.8 s | 5.0 s |
| Decoder (Neural Engine) | 0.1 s | 2.0 s |

- **Memory.** A four-tile capture peaked at 0.6 GiB for the whole app. The decoder before this revision took 13–15 s to load every time,
  also a second time in one launch, held 1.4 GB once loaded, and the capture peaked at 1.8 GiB.
- **Encoder on newer Neural Engines.** The encoder before this revision did not compile for the Neural Engine of an M4 Mac or, by its load times, an A18 iPhone: Core ML reported `ANECCompile() FAILED` at every load, never cached the failure, and took 13–22 s to load on the M4 (14–52 s on an iPhone 16 Pro) and 0.70 s a frame. This one loads in 0.07 s after its first compile and runs a frame in 0.12 s on the M4. It has not been measured on an iPhone 14 Pro, where the earlier one compiled.
- **Run the DiT on the GPU** (`.cpuAndGPU`). The A16 Neural Engine computed these iOS 18 compressed weights wrongly. FP16 and the VAE were correct there, and the same packages were correct on an M4 Mac's Neural Engine.

## Changes from the original weights

Notice of modifications under section 4(b) of the Apache License 2.0. The source was `numz/SeedVR2_comfyUI` at revision `09ced71023636e9bc8cdf9cdecfb2625d1e691e8`, an FP16 repackaging of `ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B` under Apache 2.0:

- `seedvr2_ema_3b_fp16.safetensors`, SHA-256 `2fd0e03a3dad24e07086750360727ca437de4ecd456f769856e960ae93e2b304`
- `ema_vae_fp16.safetensors`, SHA-256 `20678548f420d98d26f11442d3528f8b8c94e57ee046ef93dbb7633da8612ca1`

The following were changed:

1. **Conversion.** Converted from PyTorch to Core ML ML Programs for one 512 × 512 output frame. Window indices and rotary positions became constants of that size.
2. **Split.** Split the DiT into the seven chunks listed above. The last chunk also takes the single Euler step (x0 = noise − v).
3. **Precomputed constants.** Some inputs are fixed in one-step restoration, so they were computed once and stored:
   - the timestep embedding for t = 1000;
   - the text conditioning: the published positive prompt embedding (`pos_emb.pt`) after `txt_in`;
   - the noise, from seed 42.
4. **FP16 and size changes.**
   - RMSNorm divides each token by its largest magnitude before squaring. The text stream reaches 28,640, and x² overflows FP16.
   - The timestep modulation is broadcast instead of rep

# MiniMax H3 AI Pod inference runtimes

Verified ARM64 runtime archives for Thor T5000 (JetPack 7) and AGX Orin 64GB (JetPack 6). These contain inference code and dependencies, not model weights. Weights are downloaded separately from OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3 and Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3. LPK 0.7.2 pins these runtime images. The Thor archive includes both the video and reference runtimes.

| Target | Archive | Bytes | SHA256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| thor | `minimax-h3-thor-vllm-0.7.2-runtime.tar` | 14293082624 | `7a6edcbb3be59db792beb880313b06736a5260cdb89d126143c52aa835dc8daa` |
| orin-64g | `minimax-h3-orin-vllm-0.7.0-runtime.tar.gz` | 9868845237 | `5db7528981ce6c146216f32398406d3ff0b735788614e45aab983171d8ffec47` |

# MiniMax-H3 People & Vehicle Removal LoRA

[中文](README_zh.md)

A **MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA LoRA for removing people and vehicles from perspective and 360° panoramic scenes**. Supply scene references in temporal order and a removal prompt to generate a background video with people and vehicles removed.

Joint training on panoramic video reconstruction and perspective removal pairs transfers removal capability to panoramic scenes while retaining panoramic video generation capability.

Released as a **free, non-commercial research contribution to the community**. The author does not commercialize this project.

## Download

[**Download v1**](MiniMax-H3-People-Vehicle-Removal-Ref2VA-v1-step1000.safetensors) · BF16 · rank 32 · 125 MiB

## Usage

Load the **BF16 Ref2VA** base with the [DiffSynth-Studio H3 inference examples](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio/tree/main/examples/minimax_h3), then add the LoRA:

```python
from diffsynth.pipelines.minimax_h3_audio_video import ModelConfig

pipe.load_lora(
    pipe.dit,
    ModelConfig(path="MiniMax-H3-People-Vehicle-Removal-Ref2VA-v1-step1000.safetensors"),
    alpha=1.0,
)
```

| Setting | Recommended value |
|---|---|
| Base | MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA, BF16 |
| LoRA strength | 1.0 |
| References | Supplied in temporal order to both Qwen and VAE |
| Inference CFG / sampling steps | **1.0 / 50** |
| Frames / frame rate | 107 / 24 fps |
| Panorama output / reference short edge | 960 × 480 / 960 |
| Perspective output / reference short edge | 832 × 480 / 768 |
| Video / audio flow shift | 12 / 3 |
| Image-video / audio conditioning noise augmentation | 0.999 / 1.0 |
| Output audio | Off |

The [panoramic street prompt](prompts/removal_360_street.txt) and [perspective street prompt](prompts/removal_pv_street.txt) are the full task prompts used in evaluation, not trigger words. Adapt the scene description and camera motion to your input while retaining the removal instructions. Panorama reference frames are 0/35/106; perspective reference frames are 0/53/106. Reported results use the BF16 base.

## Video comparisons

**Perspective people and vehicle removal**

![Perspective people and vehicle removal](media/pv_street_03_seed123.webp)

[Full-rate MP4](media/pv_street_03_seed123.mp4) · [Actual prompt](media/pv_street_03_prompt.txt)

Base retains a foreground car at the start and vehicles on the right near the end; these vehicles are removed in the LoRA output.

**360° near-camera body and nadir capture artifact removal**

![360 near-camera body and nadir capture artifact removal](media/pano_street_05_seed42.webp)

[Full panoramic MP4](media/pano_street_05_seed42.mp4) · [Actual prompt](media/pano_street_05_prompt.txt)

Base leaves the camera operator’s head, shoulders, and arm prominently visible at the bottom of the panorama. The LoRA removes these nearby body parts. This example highlights body-part removal and nadir cleanup, with the difference visible directly in the full panorama.

Top: the actual three reference images. Bottom, left to right: **Source video | Base H3 | This LoRA**. The full source video is shown only for comparison; the model input is three sparse images. Each pair uses identical prompt, references, seed and BF16 settings; the only difference is whether the LoRA is loaded. MP4 files retain all 107 frames at 24 fps; animated previews are 8 fps.

## Results

Five panoramic and five perspective street scenes, seeds 42 / 123, with identical inputs and BF16 inference settings in each comparison:

| Metric | Base | This LoRA |
|---|---:|---:|
| Panorama sampled frames with people/vehicle detections ↓ | 81.9% | **25.7%** |
| Perspective sampled frames with people/vehicle detections ↓ | 15.7% | **0.0%** |
| Perspective SSIM against pseudo-clean targets ↑ | 0.325 | **0.392** |

Detection rates are measured with SAM3 on 21 sampled frames per output.

# qwen-image-2.1-p150 on Tenstorrent p150

> Derived from [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) by the Qwen team (Alibaba), with unmodified weights at commit `790c926`. Upstream code: [QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1). See the original model card for training and evaluation details.

Qwen-Image-2.1, a text-to-image diffusion model: a 7B-parameter single-stream DiT (32 layers), the Qwen3-VL-8B language model as text encoder and a 64-channel RGBA VAE decoder, all three running on the device. One request takes a text prompt and returns one 1024×1024 PNG image (RGB composited over white, and optionally the RGBA image with its alpha channel), sampled with 40 FlowMatch Euler steps by default and no classifier-free guidance. The text encoder runs with bfp8 weights, the DiT with bf16 weights. This package serves text-to-image only; the image editing mode of Qwen-Image-2.1 is not included.

Runs on Tenstorrent **p150** (mesh `P150`).

Packaged and published with [tt-model-manager](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-model-manager) 0.1.0 (manifest schema 5.1).

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | p150 |
| License | Qwen Research |

## Intended use

Non-commercial research and evaluation of text-to-image generation, within the terms of the Qwen Research License Agreement.

## Prerequisites

- The [Tenstorrent CLI](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-cli/blob/main/docs/prerequisites.md), `tt`: `uv tool install tenstorrent` (or use tt-model alone, see the Quickstart)
- Docker
- Tenstorrent hardware: **p150**
- About 41 GB of free disk: the image (4.1 GB, downloaded as 0.9 GB), the pinned weights (33.1 GB, in your
  Hugging Face cache) and the compile cache that the first start writes (3.3 GB)
- About 33 GB of free host RAM: the resident memory of the server process peaks at 32.1 GB (29.9 GiB) while it
  loads the weights

## Quickstart

```bash
tt serve changh95/qwen-image-2.1-p150
```

`tt serve` downloads the Docker image and the [`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) at `790c92633540aa0cb11d9abf19eb46d861714758` weights (into your HF cache; they are not in the image), then starts the model's own HTTP server on port 20000 (or the next free port, if that one is busy). The first start compiles kernels for your device, which takes several minutes; the server is ready when it logs `Application startup complete`.

Without tt-cli: `tt-model serve changh95/qwen-image-2.1-p150`.

Generate the demo image on the port `tt serve` reported and save it as `llama.png`:

```bash
curl -s localhost:20000/predict -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "White furry llama with black sunglasses, smiling and happy, jumping", "seed": 42}' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys, json, base64; d = json.load(sys.stdin); open("llama.png", "wb").write(base64.b64decode(d["image"])); print(d["timing_ms"])'
```

## Capabilities

This package exposes the model's own HTTP server on port 20000, **not** an OpenAI-compatible chat API — its request and response shapes are the model's own. See the author's notes for the payload it expects.

`POST /predict` generates one image from a text prompt; `GET /health` and `GET /info` report readiness and the
device configuration; `GET /v1/models` is a stub, not a chat API. Requests are queued and run one at a time on
the chip. While several wait, a request whose prompt is one of the 4 most recently used prompts can be served before
older requests; a request that has waited 120 s is served next.

| request field | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt` | the text prompt, 1 to 2,000 characters; prompts of up to 256 tokens use the pre-compiled path |
| `seed` (optional) | integer seed of the initial noise; default 42. The same prompt, seed and step count give the same image |
| `num_steps` (optional) | denoising steps, 1 to 100; default 40 |
| `return_rgba` (optional) | `true` adds the RGBA image (with the model's alpha channel) as `image_rgba`; default `false` |

Response for the quickstart request (image data elided):

```json
{
  "image": "<base64 PNG elided>",
  "image_rgba": null,
  "width": 1024,
  "height": 1024,
  "seed": 42,
  "num_steps": 40,
  "timing_ms": {"encode_s": 0.0, "prefix_s": 0.0, "denoise_s": 16160.8, "decode_s": 12.5,
                "total_s": 16173.3, "total_ms": 16173.3}
}
```

- `image` is a base64 PNG, 1024×1024 RGB, composited over a white background; `image_rgba` is `null` unless
  requested.
- `timing_ms` gives the server-side time of each stage in milliseconds, under the stage names of the Python API
  (`encode_s`, `prefix_s`, `denoise_s`, `decode_s`, `total_s`); `total_m

# MiniMax H3 Image: ComfyUI workflows for 8, 12 and 16 GB VRAM

Three versions of one ComfyUI workflow for **MiniMax H3 Image**. **All three make full 16 MP images** (3:4 = 3552x4736, 16:9 = 5472x3072), even on an 8 GB card. ComfyUI streams the model through the card in parts, so a smaller card gives **the same image, only slower**. Pick the file that matches your VRAM and drag it into ComfyUI.

| File | For | Final image | Draft | VAE decode | Reference pictures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minimax_h3_image_8gb_vram.json` | 8 GB cards | 16 MP | 4 MP | Tiled (512) | 10 slots, 4 or fewer is fastest |
| `minimax_h3_image_12gb_vram.json` | 12 GB cards | 16 MP | 4 MP | Tiled (768) | 10 slots, 4 or fewer is fastest |
| `minimax_h3_image_16gb_vram.json` | 16 GB+ cards | 16 MP | 4 MP | Normal | 10 slots |

### What you need for an 8 GB card

- **GPU:** NVIDIA with 8 GB VRAM (tested: ComfyUI used at most 3.7 GB VRAM for a 16 MP image).
- **System RAM:** 24 GB or more (tested with 24 GB), 32 GB is safer. The models are bigger than the card, so ComfyUI keeps them in RAM and streams them in parts.
- **Disk:** about 38 GB free, on an SSD.
- **ComfyUI:** a recent version (MiniMax H3 nodes are built in, no custom nodes).
- **3 model files**, the same full-quality files as the 16 GB version, **no GGUF**: the image model (21 GB), the main text encoder `nvfp4` (15.7 GB) and the VAE (1.2 GB). Links are in [Model files](#model-files).
- **Not needed:** the prompt upsampler `qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors`. It is switched off in the 8 GB workflow because it makes images very slow on 8 GB.

### Measured render times

Tested on an RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB) with 24 GB of system RAM. For 12 GB and 8 GB, part of the card's memory was filled by a dummy program, so ComfyUI only had the VRAM a real 12 GB or 8 GB card has free. With the same seed, all three gave **pixel-for-pixel the same image**.

| Job | 16 GB | 12 GB | 8 GB |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text-to-image, 16 MP | 66 s | 63 s | 60 s |
| Time per step (6 steps) | 4.4 s | 4.8 s | 5.7 s |
| 4 reference pictures, 16 MP | - | - | 228 s (about 4 min) |
| 4 reference pictures, 8 MP | - | - | 156 s (about 2.5 min) |

Real 8 GB and 12 GB cards (RTX 4060, 3060, 4070 ...) have slower chips than the test card, so expect longer times. The memory limit itself is not a problem.

## Example images

Made with this workflow, straight out of ComfyUI with no editing or upscaling. Click an image to open the full-size original PNG (5472x3072, 16 MP). All originals are in the [`examples`](https://huggingface.co/vyrekai/minimax-h3-image-comfyui-workflows/tree/main/examples) folder.

| | |
|---|---|
| [![Tortoise island](examples/previews/01_tortoise_island.jpg)](examples/01_tortoise_island.png) | [![Teacup tsunami](examples/previews/02_teacup_tsunami.jpg)](examples/02_teacup_tsunami.png) |
| [![Book canyon](examples/previews/03_book_canyon.jpg)](examples/03_book_canyon.png) | [![Moon hatching](examples/previews/04_moon_hatching.jpg)](examples/04_moon_hatching.png) |
| [![Lightbulb orchard](examples/previews/05_lightbulb_orchard.jpg)](examples/05_lightbulb_orchard.png) | [![Mirror desert](examples/previews/06_mirror_desert.jpg)](examples/06_mirror_desert.png) |
| [![Octopus pizza](examples/previews/07_octopus_pizza.jpg)](examples/07_octopus_pizza.png) | [![Bathroom mirror](examples/previews/08_bathroom_mirror.jpg)](examples/08_bathroom_mirror.png) |

The octopus pizza is 3840x2176 (8 MP); all others are 5472x3072 (16 MP).

## Prompt guide: let any AI write your prompts

[`MINIMAX_H3_IMAGE_PROMPT_GUIDE.md`](MINIMAX_H3_IMAGE_PROMPT_GUIDE.md) teaches an AI chatbot how to write prompts for this model. Drop the file into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or a local model, then ask for what you want, for example:

- *"Using this guide, write me a prompt for a rainy Tokyo street at night with a woman holding a red umbrella."*
- *"Using this guide, write an edit prompt: Picture 1 is my living room, make it sunset and add a cat on the sofa."*
- *"Using this guide, put the man from Picture 1 into the café from Picture 2."*

It answers with a finished prompt plus the settings to use (aspect ratio, draft or full size). Paste the prompt into the **PROMPT** box and leave *Enhance prompt* off, because the prompt is already long.

The guide covers text-to-image, single-picture edits and multi-reference scenes, plus realistic skin, hands, body direction, text in images, and fixes for common problems.

## What is in the workflow

- **Prompt box** with an optional **Enhance prompt** switch: a Qwen3.5 9B upsampler rewrites a short idea into a long, detailed caption (text-to-image only).
- **Aspect ratio picker** (1:1, 3:4, 4:3, 2:3, 3:2, 9:16, 16:9, 21:9) and a **full / draft switch**. Use the draft size to test prompts quickly.
- **Ten reference picture slots** for editing and multi-image prompts. They are all bypassed by de

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

Native transparent image generation

No LoRA files, no key remapping, no ComfyUI graph: load the pipeline and swap. Feed it a scene photo as `` and a character reference as ``, name who to replace, and it swaps the person while preserving the background, the lighting, the other people and the pose — including **cross-style swaps (anime/illustrated character → photoreal scene) that the base image model fails on**. ## Showcase *Original scene (``) · character reference (``) · character swap — all single-seed, straight out of the merged model.* ![Anime character swapped into a side-profile bookstore scene — the case native H3-Image fails on every seed](assets/showcase_profile.jpg) ![Photoreal hiker character swapped into a café conversation](assets/showcase_cafe.jpg) ![Anime character swapped into a full-body jogging scene](assets/showcase_fullbody.jpg) ## The case that motivated this repo Native MiniMax-H3-Image is a strong multi-reference editor, but it **systematically fails** cross-style swaps onto non-frontal faces: given an anime character and a strict side-profile photo, it kept the original face on 3 out of 3 seeds (producing a hybrid, pasting the character into the newspaper, or ignoring the swap). # MiniDF pixel map — Qwen Image 2.1 LoRA (final A)

Turns an oblique 3D map render of Brasília into the isometric pixel-art look of the [MiniDF map](https://cadeoflavio.marceloeduardo.com/), which Codex paints frame by frame. Image-to-image LoRA; winner of the first training round (7 Nov 2026). Training log: [marceloeduardo.com/pixel-lora-training.html](https://marceloeduardo.com/pixel-lora-training.html).

## Use

```python
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline
from PIL import Image

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda")
pipe.load_lora_weights("handful/mndf-pixel-qwen-image-2.1")
render = Image.open("render.jpg").convert("RGB")          # 1024x1024 oblique 3D render
out = pipe(image=render, prompt="Repaint this 3D map render as mndfstyle isometric pixel-art map of Brasília, keeping every road, building and tree in place",
           width=1024, height=1024, num_inference_steps=28).images[0]   # no guidance (pipeline default)
```

## Training

diffusers `train_dreambooth_lora_qwenimage21_img2img.py` · rank 16 · alpha 16 · lr 1e-4 constant · random flip · 1024 px · batch 1 · 3,750 steps (~100 min on one RTX PRO 6000) · 188 Brasília pairs.

## Evaluation

Round-1 judge (32 held-out Brasília frames): LPIPS 0.416. On the later five-group test set: 0.410 (Brasília 0.401, landmarks 0.409, São Paulo 0.396, Rio 0.412, world 0.429).

## Limitations and data

- **Training data:** ~2,000 pairs of (oblique 3D render of a 1024 px map frame → Codex painting of the same frame), mostly Brasília, plus São Paulo, water/shorelines and 42 world-landmark frames. The 3D inputs are renders of **Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles**; Google's Map Tiles terms do not allow using their content to train models. This LoRA is shared as a research experiment; check those terms before using it for anything beyond that.
- **Look:** water comes out brighter than the target's deep teal; very fine lattices (e.g. the Torre de TV) only appear when the 3D render shows them.
- **Input:** works best on renders like the training ones: 1024×1024, ~30° oblique, ~3.4 px per metre.

# Minimax H3 Latent Upscaler > ### 🆕 2026-11-10 — 2D v1 released > > Added **`minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_2d_conv_v1`**: > > - **Half the parameters** — 182,140,312 params, **52.8%** of the 3D release (345,280,216), with checkpoint files roughly half the size. > - **Beats the 3D release on most scales** — lower latent MSE on **32 of 36** scales; across all scales it cuts latent MSE by **84.7%** versus trilinear (3D v1: 61.1%). > - **6-step adjustable sharpness** — `tier` 1 is the most faithful, 6 the sharpest. The 3D release has no such control (its sharpness sits at roughly 2D tier 1). Neural latent-space upscaler for **Minimax H3** video generation. Works directly on Minimax H3's **24-channel VAE latents** to upscale spatial resolution (H×W) while preserving the time dimension. ## Purpose This model is designed to **accelerate high-resolution H3 video generation**: 1. Generate video at low resolution — far fewer latent tokens, much faster. 2. Upscale the latent in-place with this learned upscaler. 3. Re-sample / refine at the target resolution to recover detail. By skipping the expensive `decode → pixel upscale → encode` round-trip through Minimax H3's heavy ~5B-parameter VAE, this pipeline saves a significant amount of generation time. It also avoids the **ghosting / double-image artifacts** that naive latent interpolation (bilinear/bicubic) introduces. ## 📸 Examples **Video upscale comparison** — click to play: *(If the player doesn't render, [download the video here](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler/resolve/main/examples/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler_001.mp4).)* **Image upscale comparison**: ![Minimax H3 latent upscale comparison](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler/resolve/main/examples/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler_002.jpg) ## 2D v1 vs 3D v1 **Test setup**: 2,500 validation pairs (the same frozen split used during training); latent-domain metrics computed on the normalized latents; pixel metrics decoded through the actual Minimax H3 VAE. Coverage is **36 scales from 1.1× to 4.0×** (reference report generated 2026-11-06; 3D v1 degrades noticeably below 1.5×, see the per-range table). ![Per-scale latent MSE across all 36 scales](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler/resolve/main/examples/3D_Conv_v1_vs_2D_Conv_v1.png) > **Above** (Part A of the full report): raw latent MSE at each of the 36 scales from 1.1× to 4.0× > — grey is trilinear, orange is 3D_Conv_v1, blue is 2D_Conv_v1 at tier 1. > 2D sits at the bottom for almost every scale; 3D only pulls back ahead at the four scales it was > natively trained on (2×, 2.25×, 2.5×, 4×), which is why the orange line is so jagged. 📊 **Full comparison report**: [`examples/3D_Conv_v1_vs_2D_Conv_v1.html`](/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler/blob/main/examples/3D_Conv_v1_vs_2D_Conv_v1.html) — per-scale data for all 36 scales, side-by-side images, the sharpness ladder and temporal consistency. (HTML file, 9.3 MB; Hugging Face does not render HTML inline, so download it from that page and open it locally in a browser to see the full charts.) ### Overall | Metric | Trilinear | 3D_Conv_v1 | 2D_Conv_v1 | | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Latent MSE (mean improvement over trilinear, 36 scales) | baseline | **+61.1%** | **+84.7%** | | Decoded PSNR (mean over 36 scales, higher is better) | 23.54 | 29.30 | **30.47** | | Sharpness (gradient ratio, 1.0 = matches ground truth) | 1.429 ¹ | 0.869 | **0.897** | | Chroma shift (lower is better) | 28.3% | 17.9% | **16.4%** | | Parameters | — | 345,280,216 | **182,140,312 (52.8%)** | | Adjustable sharpness tiers | — | none | **6 (t1–t6)** | ¹ Trilinear's sharpness is usually

# ChatR Labs Uncensored Omni — Quantized

[![Base model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hugging_Face-Base_model-ffcc4d?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)

**Quantized builds at adapter weight 1.0, for text-to-image generation and image editing.**

This repository ships **quantized transformer weights only**. The model is our rank-128 Omni adapter merged into
[Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) at **LoRA strength 1.0**, then quantized.
The text encoder, processor and VAE are not included; take them from the base repository.

## Download

File integrity information is in [SHA256SUMS](./SHA256SUMS).

### Which build should I use?

- **ComfyUI, one file, both workflows** -> any **GGUF**. It also loads in Diffusers via `from_single_file`.
- **ComfyUI, native quant ops** -> **FP8**, **INT8 ConvRot** or **NVFP4**.
- **Diffusers, smallest download** -> **NF4** (needs `bitsandbytes`).
- **Diffusers, best fidelity** -> **FP8 (torchao)** (needs `torchao`).
- **Maximum fidelity overall** -> **BF16 GGUF**, **BF16 safetensors** or **Q8_0**.
- **Diffusers without the `gguf` package** -> the **BF16** folder (plain `from_pretrained`).

The `297` and `265` layouts use different MLP representations: `265` uses the fused `img_mlp.gate_up`
projection; `297` keeps the separate `gate_layer` / `proj` pair. A loader must support the selected layout.
The BF16 ComfyUI workflow below was verified with the `297`-tensor safetensors file and the native
`UNETLoader` in ComfyUI 0.39.0; support should not be assumed for older or different loaders.

## Recommended settings

These are the values from our inference grid search for the non-distilled model.

| Setting | Starting value |
| --- | --- |
| Base components | Text encoder, processor and VAE from `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` |
| Sampling steps | **35** |
| True CFG scale | **5.0** (both text-to-image and editing) |
| Sampler | `er_sde` with the `simple` scheduler (ComfyUI) |
| Negative prompt | A single space: `" "` |

# DiT-Reward: Qwen-Image (Heavy)

Anonymous model release for Submission 7366. This model assigns a scalar reward to an image and its text prompt; it is **not an image-generation pipeline**. Higher scores indicate greater predicted preference **within this model**; scores from different reward models are not calibrated against each other.

The Qwen-derived weights are distributed under Apache-2.0; see `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`.

## Checkpoint and settings

- Backbone: `Qwen/Qwen-Image`.
- Feature blocks (zero-indexed): `[29, 39, 49, 59]`.
- Flow-matching noise coefficient: **0.005**. The released models retain this setting at inference; these are not the new noise-ablation checkpoints.
- Checkpoint provenance: `{"merge_method":"linear_parameter_interpolation_fp32_3way","source_checkpoint_steps":[13400,14000,13800],"weights":[0.5,0.4,0.1]}`.
- Image processing: bicubic resize of the shorter edge to 512, center crop to 512×512, RGB, tensor normalization to [-1, 1].
- Real text conditioning is required; no silent vision-only fallback is permitted.
- Reward MLP: concatenated pooled features → 1536 → 384 → 1, with GELU and training-time dropout.

Weights are sharded without tensor re-encoding. Tensor names, dtypes, shapes and bytes are retained. Only identifying file-header metadata was removed; `checkpoint_provenance.json` records anonymous source/payload hashes. Optimizer states, original training arguments, run logs, personal paths and credentials are not included.

## Quick start

Use a separate Python 3.10+ environment with CUDA-compatible PyTorch/torchvision, then install `requirements-inference.txt`. Download the repository (including its Python files) with:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
snapshot_download("iclr2027-7366/DiT-Reward-Qwen-Image", local_dir="reward-model")
```

```bash
python -m pip install -r reward-model/requirements-inference.txt
python reward-model/inference.py --repo-dir reward-model --image example.png --prompt "A red bicycle next to a tree." --device cuda --seed 0
```

This release includes all checkpoint tensors: transformer, VAE, Qwen text encoder, normalization and reward head. Tokenizer/configuration assets are bundled. No original Qwen base-model weight download is needed.

Programmatic usage, from the downloaded directory:

```python
import torch
from inference import DiTReward
torch.manual_seed(0)
model = DiTReward(".", device="cuda")
scores = model.score(["example.png"], ["A red bicycle next to a tree."], batch_size=1)
print(scores)
```

The CLI also accepts `--input-jsonl pairs.jsonl` with one `{"image":"example.png","prompt":"..."}` record per line and `--batch-size`. Start with batch size 1; VRAM depends on backbone and prompt lengths. It rejects incomplete/shape-mismatched checkpoints and non-finite weights/scores. Use `--verify-hashes` to check every shard against the SHA-256 manifest.

## Reproduction notes

The scorer preserves the original VAE posterior **sampling**, flow noise, full prompt encoding, feature hooks, pooling/normalization and reward-head forward path. Fix a seed and record batch size, evaluation order, device and dependency versions: stochastic latent/noise draws and GPU kernels mean independently rerun scores need not be bitwise identical. No new benchmark result is claimed by releasing the checkpoint.

`qwen_reward_model.py` is the isolated reward-forward implementation. Changes for release are limited to path-free component initialization from bundled configs, full checked checkpoint materialization, optional Qwen `txt_seq_lens` compatibility and removal of debug printing. Loading from empty config initialization avoids downloading an unused pretrained transformer before replacing it with reward weights. The reward computation itself is unchanged.

Model weights retain their upstream license. Python code has the separate MIT license in `LICENSE-code`. See `verification.json` for the exact tested runtime and small inference verification, not a complete benchmark re-evaluation.

# **Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Ultra-Realistic-Portrait**

> Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Ultra-Realistic-Portrait is an adapter LoRA developed for Qwen’s Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 image-to-image model, designed to generate ultra-realistic glamour-style portraits with strict identity preservation. The model focuses on high-end fashion realism by combining cinematic directional lighting, refined makeup aesthetics, and detailed epidermal textures. It enhances micropores, microhairs, subtle oil sheen, soft wrinkles, and subsurface scattering while preserving the subject’s natural facial structure and original details. Visual consistency is maintained across lighting, shadows, skin tones, and composition, delivering a luxury fashion-magazine look without artificial smoothing or excessive retouching. This makes the model well suited for premium portrait generation where realism, identity fidelity, and cinematic polish are essential. Above are example outputs demonstrating the model’s ability to produce high-quality, visually cohesive ultra-realistic portrait results.


## **Quick Start with Diffusers**

> Compatible with versions 2509 and 2511.

```bash
pip install -U diffusers transformers accelerate
```

```python
import torch
from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline
from diffusers.utils import load_image

# Switch to "mps" for Apple devices
pipe = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511",
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map="cuda"
)

pipe.load_lora_weights("prithivMLmods/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Ultra-Realistic-Portrait")

prompt = "ultra-realistic portrait"

input_image = load_image(
    "https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/diffusers/cat.png"
)

image = pipe(image=input_image, prompt=prompt).images[0]
```

## **Core Prompt**

```
Transform the image into an ultra-realistic glamour portrait while strictly preserving the subject’s identity. Apply a close-up composition with a slight head tilt and a hand near the face, enhance cinematic directional lighting with dramatic fashion-style highlights, and refine makeup details including glowing skin, glossy lips, luminous highlighter, and defined eyes. Increase skin realism with detailed epidermal textures such as micropores, microhairs, subtle oil sheen, natural highlights, soft wrinkles, and subsurface scattering. Maintain a luxury fashion-magazine look in a 9:16 aspect ratio, preserving realism, facial structure, and original details without over-smoothing or retouching.
```

## **Trigger Prompt**

Use the following prompt to activate the ultra-realistic portrait effect:

```
ultra-realistic portrait
```

Compared with Qwen-Image-Edit released in August, the main improvements of Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 include: * **Multi-image Editing Support**: For multi-image inputs, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 builds upon the Qwen-Image-Edit architecture and is further trained via image concatenation to enable multi-image editing. It supports various combinations such as "person + person," "person + product," and "person + scene." Optimal performance is currently achieved with 1 to 3 input images. * **Enhanced Single-image Consistency**: For single-image inputs, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 significantly improves editing consistency, specifically in the following areas: - **Improved Person Editing Consistency**: Better preservation of facial identity, supporting various portrait styles and pose transformations; - **Improved Product Editing Consistency**: Better preservation of product identity, supporting product poster editing； - **Improved Text Editing Consistency**: In addition to modifying text content, it also supports editing text fonts, colors, and materials； * **Native Support for ControlNet**: Including depth maps, edge maps, keypoint maps, and more. ## Quick Start Install the latest version of diffusers ``` pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers ``` The following contains a code snippet illustrating how to use `Qwen-Image-Edit-2509`: ```python import os import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline pipeline = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16) print("pipeline loaded") pipeline.to('cuda') pipeline.set_progress_bar_config(disable=None) image1 = Image.open("input1.png") image2 = Image.open("input2.png") prompt = "The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square." inputs = { "image": [image1, image2], "prompt": prompt, "generator": torch.manual_seed(0), "true_cfg_scale": 4.0, "negative_prompt": " ", "num_inference_steps": 40, "guidance_scale": 1.0, "num_images_per_prompt": 1, } with torch.inference_mode(): output = pipeline(**inputs) output_image = output.images[0] output_image.save("output_image_edit_plus.png") print("image saved at", os.path.abspath("output_image_edit_plus.png")) ``` ## Showcase **The primary update in Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 is support for multi-image inputs.** Let’s first look at a "person + person" example: ![Person + Person Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8719.JPG#center) Here is a "person + scene" example: ![Person + Scene Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8720.JPG#center) Below is a "person + object" example: ![Person + Object Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8721.JPG#center) In fact, multi-image input also supports commonly used ControlNet keypoint maps—for example, changing a person’s pose: ![ControlNet Keypoint Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8722.JPG#center) Similarly, the following examples demonstrate results using three input images: ![Three Images Example 1](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8723.JPG#center) ![Three Images Example 2](htt

# Qwen3-VL-32B Heretic (MiniMax-H3) 鈥?BF16, transformers format

The uncensored MiniMax-H3 text encoder in **plain bfloat16, transformers layout**, converted from
[`Momoking/Qwen3-VL-32B-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/Momoking/Qwen3-VL-32B-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-NVFP4)
(ComfyUI NVFP4, 15.7 GB).

## Why this repo exists

The NVFP4 source is a ComfyUI `comfy_quant` checkpoint 鈥?ComfyUI loads it, but the transformers/diffusers
MiniMax-H3 pipeline cannot. This repo ships the same weights dequantized to bfloat16 (62.14 GiB, the same
footprint as the official encoder) under the exact file layout of the official
[`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) `text_encoder/`, so any tooling built
for the official encoder can point at this repo instead:

- **diffusers modular loading** (`load_components` / `modular_model_index.json`): point `MODEL_REPO` here.
- **transformers**: `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("<this-repo>", subfolder="text_encoder")`.
- **ComfyUI**: keep using the NVFP4 source repo; this repo is for non-Comfy tooling.

Only `text_encoder/`, `tokenizer/` and `processor/` are shipped 鈥?the H3 transformer and VAEs are not here.

## Conversion notes (the ConvRot trap, done right)

The upstream Heretic INT8-ConvRot stores ConvRot-rotated weights; re-quantizing without un-rotating yields
garbage conditioning (see the source repo's README). The NVFP4 source here was already un-rotated by its
author, so dequantization is exact. The file's quantized tensors are `nvfp4` (block-scaled E2M1, 350
linear layers) plus one `int8_tensorwise` embedding table; every tensor was dequantized with the same
`comfy_kitchen` layout ComfyUI itself uses (`TensorCoreNVFP4Layout.dequantize`).

The source checkpoint carries layers 0鈥?9 only 鈥?MiniMax-H3 reads the hidden state after 50 decoder
layers, so layers 50鈥?3 and `lm_head` are never used for conditioning. To keep the checkpoint complete
(and the optional prompt-rewrite path functional), those 156 tensors are filled from the official
`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` encoder. All weights the pipeline actually reads are Heretic.

## Files

```
text_encoder/   config + 14 脳 model-*.safetensors (bfloat16) + index
tokenizer/      Qwen2TokenizerFast files
processor/      Qwen3VLProcessor files
modular_model_index.json
```

## Usage with the demo Spaces

Paired deployment (ZeroGPU, free tier):

- conditioner Space: [`SXIAOYAN/qwen3vl-heretic-h3-conditioner`](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SXIAOYAN/qwen3vl-heretic-h3-conditioner) 鈥?`MODEL_REPO` defaults to this repo.
- generator Space: [`SXIAOYAN/minimax-h3-heretic-turbo`](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SXIAOYAN/minimax-h3-heretic-turbo) 鈥?4-step video+audio, conditions via the conditioner above.

## Credits

- Weights: [Momoking/Qwen3-VL-32B-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/Momoking/Qwen3-VL-32B-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-NVFP4), a re-quantization of [ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-32B-Ultra-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-ComfyUI-INT8-ConvRot](https://huggingface.co/ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-32B-Ultra-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-ComfyUI-INT8-ConvRot).
- Layout/config files: [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3).

# darksidewalker/MiniMaxH3

**Official repository for the GRAVITON weight-space fusion architecture and merged MiniMax H3 audio-video DiT checkpoints.**

* **GRAVITON Architecture, Mathematical Specification & Engine Author:** **Darksidewalker**
* **Official Reference Implementation:** [darksidewalker/dasiwa-quant-station](https://github.com/darksidewalker/dasiwa-quant-station) (`core/model_merge_engine.py`, commit `69412c0+`)
* **Engine & Workbench License:** [GPL-3.0-or-later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html)
* **Specification & Whitepaper License:** [CC-BY-SA-4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) (Attribution + ShareAlike required)

---

## Evolution of MiniMax H3 Merge Architectures

This repository encompasses three generations of model-level H3 fusion recipes implemented in **DaSiWa Quant Station**. While earlier approaches targeted specific conditioning unifications (`fl2va` + `ref2va`), **GRAVITON**—designed and engineered by **Darksidewalker**—provides a mathematically rigorous, calibration-free spectral and polar geodesic framework for arbitrary DiT pairings.

| Recipe | Engine ID | Primary Use Case | Core Mechanism | Key Limitation Solved by Next Generation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Hybrid H3** | `h3_hybrid` | Grafting `ref2va` conditioning onto `fl2va` | Hard block/row splicing of AdaLN weights & biases (default blocks 30–49) + optional `final_layer.audio_out` swap. | Zero interpolation; hard boundaries between block regimes; requires unquantized matching layouts. |
| **2. Delta-Fused H3** | `h3_delta` | Single checkpoint serving both keyframe & reference paths | Linear delta injection (`W = fl2va + s · Δ`) with optional fixed-rank (`N`) randomized SVD truncation on 2-D trunk matrices. | Fixed rank ignores aspect ratios; linear interpolation on heterogeneous finetunes/turbos causes variance collapse. |
| **3. GRAVITON** | `h3_graviton` | Merging any two H3 models (Base, Turbo, Finetunes, W6A8) | Full-spectrum RMT filtering (Gavish-Donoho) + pre-geodesic TIES/EMR sign mediation + row-wise polar SLERP & RegMean norm re-anchoring. | *Current architecture* — prevents variance drift, spectral tail noise, post-SLERP trajectory warping, and AdaLN black-frame collapse. |

---

## 1. GRAVITON (`h3_graviton`)

![GRAVITON Event Horizon Pipeline](assets/graviton_poster.png)

**Geodesic Rank-Adaptive Variance-Isolated Tensor Orthogonal Normalization**  
*Designed and authored by **Darksidewalker**.*

### Authorship & Architectural Lineage

While originally motivated by an unimplemented, four-step community recipe description (`OliviaRossi/Minimax-h3_Singularity-x-10Eros-Max_PRISM`, which had no published code or formal paper), **GRAVITON** is an original mathematical formulation and systems implementation by **Darksidewalker** (`core/model_merge_engine.py`, commit `69412c0+`) that corrects fundamental geometric flaws in prior descriptions and introduces:
1. **Pre-Geodesic Sign Mediation Ordering:** Moves TIES/EMR sign-conflict resolution *before* spherical interpolation so post-rotation sign flips never knock rows off the geodesic hypersphere.
2. **Exact Full-Spectrum RMT & Gavish-Donoho Auto-Rank:** Replaces arbitrary fixed-rank cutoffs with aspect-ratio-adaptive optimal hard thresholding via exact Gram-matrix eigendecomposition.
3. **Analytical Marchenko-Pastur Quantization Floor (`tau_quant`) & Comfy-Kitchen W6A8 Bridge:** Derives exact uniform step-noise variance from QuantStation `W6A8` scale companions and blocks quantization grid staircases from entering the structural subspace ($L$) or diffuse residual ($R$).
4. **AdaLN Anti-Alignment Protection & Structural Preservation:** Prevents the black-video variance collapse caused by per-row SLERP on anti-aligned AdaLN modulation weights or mismatched community coordinate tables.
5. **Decoupled Float Output:** Emits clean floating-point artifacts (`BF16`/`F16`/`F32`) rather than risking inline quantization packer corruption.

### Why GRAVITON?

Merging step-distilled accelerators (8-step Turbo/DMD/LCM), diverse community finetunes, or group-quantized checkpoints into base DiT models triggers four primary failure modes:
1. **Spectral Tail Contamination:** Step distillation concentrates structural trajectory changes into top singular vectors while leaving discretization artifacts in the spectral tail. Fixed-rank truncation (e.g., rank-64) under-fits wide layers and leaks noise from narrow projections.
2. **Post-Geodesic Trajectory Warping:** Applying element-wise sign mediation *after* spherical interpolation flips components off the hypersphere and destroys the interpolated angle.

# Qwen Image 2.1 Mosaic Mate LoRA

> Remove the semi-transparent mosaic overlay and faithfully restore the underlying details.

This lightweight LoRA adds inverse alpha-blend restoration capability to Qwen-Image 2.1, enabling it to remove light to moderately heavy ***semi-transparent*** (opacity up to 0.9) mosaic overlays from images.

We did not train it on specific body parts, viewing angles, or texture details, and it does not explicitly inject a new style or introduce new concepts. It is intended to handle semi-transparent mosaic overlays across a broad range of body parts/regions, texture details, cell sizes, and areas, although performance may vary depending on the input.

It should be emphasized that Qwen-Image 2.1 already has some capability to remove mosaic occlusion. This adapter is intended to improve the precision of semi-transparent mosaic removal by encouraging the model to reconstruct occluded details primarily from texture and structure cues preserved under the semi-transparent overlay, rather than relying mainly on prior-driven guessing. 

## Usage

To save processing time, keep the model focused, and avoid degrading quality in other regions, we recommend cropping the image to the approximate region of mosaic before processing.
Once you have loaded the LoRA and configured your workflow as usual, spell:

`Remove the semi-transparent mosaic`

Recommend settings:
- **Strength**: 1.0
- **CFG**: 1.0
- **Sampler**: euler / simple
- **Steps**: 10-20 (Base) | 4-8 (Turbo)
- No trigger word

## Results

| Mosaic / Original | Base Model / DIFF | + This LoRA / DIFF |
|-------------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| ![](images/mermaid_eye.png) | ![](images/mermaid_eye_base.png) | ![](images/mermaid_eye_lora.png) |
| ![](images/mermaid_eye_original.png) | ![](images/mermaid_eye_base_diff.png) | ![](images/mermaid_eye_lora_diff.png) |
| ![](images/mermaid_full.png) | ![](images/mermaid_full_base.png) | ![](images/mermaid_full_lora.png) |
| ![](images/mermaid_full_original.png) | ![](images/mermaid_full_base_diff.png) | ![](images/mermaid_full_lora_diff.png) |

> The example images are not in the training data.

## Limits

Since semi-transparent overlays still cause information loss, the adapter does not guarantee pixel-exact recovery of the original content. Results depend on the base model, overlay opacity, and input image; heavily degraded regions may not be faithfully recovered.

This is our first LoRA with real practical value. It was trained using only Fizgig’s recommended preset settings and already produces satisfactory results. Any comments or suggestions are welcome.

If you are aiming for pixel-perfect restoration and don’t mind performing some manual touch-ups, you might want to try our [dedicated tool](https://github.com/Schwi-AI/MosaicMate).

## Training

|---------|-------|
| Base Model | Qwen Image 2.1 |
| Type | LoRA (Standard) |
| Trainer | Fizgig v8.9.93 |
| Preset | Qwen 2.1 Edit (rank 8, adaptive LR) |
| Modules | fizgig.families (qwen_image21, lora) |
| Alpha | 8 |
| Resolution | 0.5 MP |
| Data | 52 image pairs |
