# MiniMax-H3 (pruned) — NVFP4

NVFP4 (TensorCore block-scaled FP4) **weight-only** quantization of both **pruned MiniMax-H3**
transformers — FL2VA and Ref2VA. MiniMax-H3 is a 33 B omni-modal video model that generates
video **and native stereo audio in a single forward pass**: dialogue, sound effects and score
come out with the picture, not from a separate stage.

**11.67 GiB per transformer instead of 19.53 GiB, and slightly faster** on Blackwell.

✅ **Everything you need for H3 is in here as of 2026-09-13.** Both transformers, the text
encoder, both VAEs and the two 4-step turbo LoRAs, laid out as ComfyUI's `models/` tree, so a
single `hf download` is enough to start generating. The only thing you fetch elsewhere is LTX-2.5, and only
if you want the two-stage refine workflow (different license, so it is linked, not mirrored).

📝 **Full write-up, benchmarks & the gotchas in detail:**
[Running MiniMax-H3 on one RTX 5090](https://ai-muninn.com/en/blog/minimax-h3-nvfp4-rtx5090)
· [繁體中文版](https://ai-muninn.com/zh-TW/blog/minimax-h3-nvfp4-rtx5090)

🖥 **Both Blackwell machines use this same repo.** An RTX 5090 (sm_120) and a DGX Spark /
GB10 (sm_121) load the exact same files and run the exact same graphs — nothing here is
per-machine. The only difference is how much fits at once: the Spark's 121 GiB of unified memory
holds both stages of the refine pipeline, while a 32 GB 5090 has to evict and reload between them.

📝 **On a DGX Spark:**
[MiniMax H3 Super Acceleration on a DGX Spark](https://ai-muninn.com/en/blog/h3-ltx-two-stage-dgx-spark)
(H3 draft + LTX-2.5 refine: 118.8 s vs 237.7 s native, 73.3 s warm)
· [繁體中文版](https://ai-muninn.com/zh-TW/blog/h3-ltx-two-stage-dgx-spark)

## What this is

- **Format:** NVFP4 weight-only. 200 linear layers are packed FP4 (4-bit) with per-block FP8
  (E4M3) scales and per-tensor FP32 global scales — the standard NVFP4 layout. Norms,
  embeddings, biases and the pruned model's `adaln_t_table` stay at their original precision.
  (Header dtype profile: 1,132 tensors — 200 U8 packed-FP4 + 200 F8_E4M3 block scales +
  200 F32 global scales, alongside 219 BF16 / 51 F16 / 4 F32 left untouched.)
- **Base:** the **pruned** Comfy-Org repack of
  [`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3). The pruned checkpoint
  matters here: most of its ~13 B-parameter AdaLN projection has been replaced by an
  equivalent timestep lookup table (13,039,369,728 → 43,642,368 parameters, ~299×; reduced
  `adaln_proj` tensors remain rather than being removed outright), so quantization never
  touches it. MiniMax document this themselves — the model card notes the AdaLN modulation
  outputs can be precomputed and cached and "do not need to be loaded for inference-only
  deployment". AdaLN emits the
  scale/shift applied to every residual stream and its error compounds across every block and
  every sampling step — the pruned base removes that risk instead of trying to survive it.
- **Size:** 11.67 GiB per transformer, down from 19.53 GiB. The two transformers are
  alternative task checkpoints and are never loaded together, so what has to fit is one
  transformer plus the text encoder: measured peak is 26,914 MiB on a 32 GB card.

## Honest caveats (read these)

**1. Blackwell only. On anything older this is a size play with no speed.**
NVFP4 has tensor-core support only on sm_120+. On Turing/Ampere/Ada, ComfyUI lists `nvfp4`
under `emulated ops`: the file loads and runs, but weights are expanded before the matmul, so
you get the smaller download and none of the benefit. For those cards, use INT8-ConvRot or a
W4A4-ConvRot build instead.

**2. A different quantization does not give you the same clip faster — it gives you a
different clip.**
Quantization changes the numerics, the denoising trajectory diverges, and a fixed seed lands
somewhere else. `samples/nvfp4_vs_int8_sidebyside.mp4` shows NVFP4 next to INT8-ConvRot from
the same seed and prompt: both are coherent — m

No validation prompt was used during training.

Note: The validation settings are not necessarily the same as the [training settings](#training-settings).

You can find some example images in the following gallery:

<Gallery />


The text encoder **was not** trained.
You may reuse the base model text encoder for inference.


## Training settings

- Training epochs: 27
- Training steps: 500
- Learning rate: 0.0001
  - Learning rate schedule: constant_with_warmup
  - Warmup steps: 25
- Max grad norm: 1.0
- Effective batch size: 1
  - Micro-batch size: 1
  - Gradient accumulation steps: 1
  - Number of GPUs: 1
- Gradient checkpointing: True
- Prediction type: flow_matching[]

- Optimizer: adamw_bf16
- Trainable parameter precision: Pure BF16
- Base model precision: `no_change`
- Caption dropout probability: 0.0%



- LoRA Rank: 32
- LoRA Alpha: 32.0
- LoRA Dropout: 0.0
- LoRA initialisation style: default
- LoRA mode: Standard
    


## Datasets



## Inference


```python
import torch
from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline

model_id = 'MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image'
adapter_id = 'SimpleTuner/minimax-h3-image-domokun-2048'
pipeline = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(model_id, torch_dtype=None) # loading directly in bf16
pipeline.load_lora_weights(adapter_id)

prompt = "An astronaut is riding a horse through the jungles of Thailand."
negative_prompt = ''

## Optional: quantise the model to save on vram.
## Note: The model was not quantised during training, so it is not necessary to quantise it during inference time.
#from optimum.quanto import quantize, freeze, qint8
#quantize(pipeline.transformer, weights=qint8)
#freeze(pipeline.transformer)
    
pipeline.to('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else 'cpu') # the pipeline is already in its target precision level
model_output = pipeline(
    prompt=prompt,
    negative_prompt=negative_prompt,
    num_inference_steps=6,
    generator=torch.Generator(device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else 'cpu').manual_seed(42),
    width=2048,
    height=2048,
    guidance_scale=1.0,
).images[0]

model_output.save("output.png", format="PNG")

```

# MiniMax H3 two-track mixed resolution (MPEG-Diffusion)

> [!WARNING]
> **Research weights, help wanted.** Working now, no DiT fine-tune: the fitted K/V maps ([`kv_maps/`](kv_maps)) and region head v3 ([`region_head_v3/`](region_head_v3)) give sharp subjects on 22-frame 1344×768 video at **1.94×** the speed of full resolution (RTX 5090). The LoRA is not published: its 500-step run changes the whole picture. Help and results: [scrya-com/mpeg-diffusion issue #2](https://github.com/scrya-com/mpeg-diffusion/issues/2).

> [!CAUTION]
> **License and territory.** Derived from MiniMax H3 under the [MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement](LICENSE) (see [`NOTICE`](NOTICE)). Use and redistribution are allowed **only outside the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea and the United States of America**. Commercial use above US$20M yearly revenue needs MiniMax's written authorization. Do not use these weights to impersonate anyone, and disclose machine-generated output.

Weights for two-track mixed-resolution sampling on the MiniMax H3 DiT. The method is MPEG-Diffusion: Mixed-Resolution Video Generation by Dennis Menn, Tianpei Gu, Guande He, Aryan V S, Yanke Song, Nan Liu, Desai Xie, Xun Huang, Chenfeng Xu and Diana Marculescu (UT Austin and Roblox), [arXiv 2611.12069](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12069). This repository is an independent port to H3, not their release.

How it works: the unmodified H3 renders the whole frame at half resolution. A region, such as the face, gets full-resolution tokens. Dual-resolution attention lets every query read keys and values at its own resolution. The paper fine-tunes the model so the full-resolution track can start earlier and redraw detail. These weights are that fine-tune, made affordable as a rank-16 LoRA plus the K/V up-maps and two resolution vectors.

| Folder | What |
|---|---|
| [`kv_maps/`](kv_maps) | Fitted `f_up` K/V maps (rank 128, 50 blocks). They remove the diamond-grid grain of copied keys in the full-resolution region. Use with `render --preset quality` or the ComfyUI node's `maps` input. |
| [`region_head_v3/`](region_head_v3) | Region head v3 (see its card); the one the quality recipe uses. |
| [`region_head/`](region_head) | The self-selected region head: one linear layer on block 25 of the frozen DiT that marks the subject partway through sampling, and so sets the full-resolution region and the Level-of-Token layout. Trained on 2,354 pictures with YOLOE subject labels; held-out mIoU 0.468. It favours the centre of the frame (see its card). |
| LoRA (not published) | Lets the full-resolution track start earlier. First run (2,346 pairs, RTX 5090) stopped at step 500 with held-out loss down 21% (half resolution) and 26% (full resolution). |

- Code, sampler and training pipeline: [scrya-com/mpeg-diffusion](https://github.com/scrya-com/mpeg-diffusion) (`lot/two_track_h3.py`, `lot/train_tt.py`, one command: `lot/train_tt_all.sh`).
- Precomputed caption embeddings for the Pexels photos, which skip the 32B text encoder: [johndpope/MiniMax-H3-pexels-people-text](https://huggingface.co/datasets/johndpope/MiniMax-H3-pexels-people-text).
- Write-up: [scrya.com/mpeg_diffusion](https://scrya.com/mpeg_diffusion).
- The earlier Level-of-Token adapters are in [johndpope/MiniMax-H3-LoT](https://huggingface.co/johndpope/MiniMax-H3-LoT).

# MiniMax-H3-Image 2-step pDMD LoRA

A **2-step** distillation LoRA for [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), trained with **pDMD** (DMD2 with the pDMD projection, Distribution Matching Distillation). It turns the base model's 6-step sampling into 2 forward passes while keeping text-to-image and reference-image editing close to the full 6-step model, which makes it suitable for real-time and interactive pipelines.

- **Base model:** MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image
- **Method:** pDMD (DMD2 with the pDMD projection), the base model's 6-step sampler as the teacher
- **LoRA:** rank 128, alpha 128, attention and feed-forward (`to_q`, `to_k`, `to_v`, `to_out.0`, `ff.net.0.proj`, `ff.net.2`)
- **Inference:** 2 steps, `sample_sigmas=[1.0, 12/13, 0.0]`, about 1 megapixel
- **Training:** 1000 steps on a single H100, multi-aspect (1024x1024, 768x1344, 1344x768), on prompts expanded by [MiniMax-H3-Image-PE](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE)

## Usage

MiniMax-H3-Image is supported in `diffusers` 0.43.0 and later, as Modular Diffusers blocks (Python 3.11+):

```bash
pip install -U "diffusers>=0.43.0" transformers accelerate safetensors
```

The transformer and the text encoder are about 62 GB each in bfloat16, so this uses automatic offloading (about 140 GB of CPU RAM).

```python
import torch
from diffusers import ComponentsManager, ModularPipeline
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from safetensors.torch import load_file

manager = ComponentsManager()
manager.enable_auto_cpu_offload(device="cuda")
pipe = ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image", components_manager=manager)
pipe.load_components(dtype=torch.bfloat16)


def fuse_lora(transformer, path, scale=1.0):
    """Merge a LoRA (rank 128, alpha 128) into the transformer weights."""
    state = load_file(path)
    params = dict(transformer.named_parameters())
    for key in state:
        if key.endswith(".lora_A.weight"):
            name = key.removeprefix("transformer.").removesuffix(".lora_A.weight")
            weight = params[name + ".weight"]
            delta = state[key.replace("lora_A", "lora_B")].float() @ state[key].float()
            weight.data += (scale * delta).to(weight.device, weight.dtype)


lora_path = hf_hub_download("linoyts/MiniMax-H3-Image-pDMD-2steps", "pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors")
fuse_lora(pipe.transformer, lora_path)
pipe.register_to_config(sample_sigmas=[1.0, 12 / 13, 0.0])  # 2 steps, one transformer head per step
```

### Text to image

```python
prompt = (
    "A cozy wooden cabin in a snowy pine forest at dusk, warm yellow light glowing from its small square "
    "windows, smoke curling from a stone chimney, deep blue sky with the first stars, fresh snow on the roof."
)
image = pipe(
    prompt=prompt,
    height=1024,
    width=1024,
    min_generation_area=1024,  # generate at the requested size instead of upscaling to 4 MP
    generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(0),
    output="images",
)[0]
image.save("cabin.png")
```

### Image editing

Pass reference images as `image` and refer to them as `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, ... in the prompt:

```python
from diffusers.utils import load_image

reference = load_image("https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image/resolve/main/examples/reference1.png")
image = pipe(
    prompt="Keep everything in <Picture 1> as it is, but remove the headphones and have the two hosts fist bump.",
    image=reference,
    height=1024,
    width=1024,
    min_generation_area=1024,
    generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(1234),
    output="images",
)[0]
```

## Notes

- **Use long prompts.** The LoRA was trained on prompts rewritten by [MiniMax-H3-Image-PE](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE), the format the base model expects. Short prompts work, and detailed descriptions (or prompts run through the PE model first) work best. The [diffusers PE blocks](https://huggingface.co/diffusers/minimax-h3-image-pe-blocks) run the expansion as a pipeline of its own.
- **Resolution.** The LoRA was trained around 1 megapixel (1024x1024, 768x1344, 1344x768). Pass `min_generation_area=1024` so the pipeline generates at the size you ask for; by default it generates on a canvas of at least 4 megapixels, which this LoRA was not trained at.
- **Schedule.** `[1.0, 12/13, 0.0]` is the 2-step schedule the LoRA was trained on (a shift-12 midpoint). The transformer has one output head per step, and the pipeline uses the heads in order, so the first two heads are used.
- **No guidance.** The base model is guidance-distilled, so there is no `guidance_scale` or `negative_prompt`.

# MiniMax-H3-Image NF4 for LoRA Training

Pre-quantized [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) packaged for
**AcademiaSD MiniMax-H3 Image LoRAlab**, part of
[AcademiaSD LoRAlab Trainer Studio](https://github.com/AcademiaSD/AcademiaSD_LoRAlab-TrainerStudio),
a LoRA trainer for consumer GPUs. It is downloaded automatically by the LoRAlab; you do not need to
fetch it by hand.

> **This is not an inference checkpoint.** The transformer is stored as a per-layer NF4 cache
> that the LoRAlab rebuilds directly; it does not load with `from_pretrained`. For generation,
> use the original model or its ComfyUI release.

## What is inside

| Folder | Size | Content |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `transformers/` | 17.23 GB | 33B single-stream DiT as an NF4 cache, one file per layer (66.3 GB in BF16) |
| `vae/` | 2.34 GB | Original image VAE (CNN encoder, 2D ViT decoder, 24 channels), diffusers format, unchanged |
| `scheduler/`, `pdd_config.json`, `modular_model_index.json` | — | Original files, unchanged |
| `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` | — | MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement and the notice it requires |

**Two folders come from [AcademiaSD/MiniMax-H3-NF4](https://huggingface.co/AcademiaSD/MiniMax-H3-NF4),
not from here**, and the LoRAlab downloads only those two (35.6 GB of the 41.4 GB repo; nothing if
you already train MiniMax-H3 video LoRAs):

- `text_encoder/` (18.4 GB): MiniMax-H3-Image conditions on the unchanged Qwen3-VL text encoder of
  MiniMax-H3. Used by the pre-cache only.
- `transformers/` (17.2 GB): the MiniMax-H3 DiT the LoRA is trained on (see below).

### Transformer (NF4)

- Every linear of the 50 blocks and of the 2 token-refiner blocks is NF4 (bitsandbytes, double
  quantization, BF16 compute): 373 layers.
- `proj_in`, the timestep embedder, `norm_out` and the **six per-step output heads**
  (`pdd_proj_out.0`–`5`) are also stored unquantized (`pc-*` files): the model declares them
  precision-critical, and the heads are what make the 6-step distillation work.
- Norms and other non-linear parameters are kept as in the original (`other-*` files).
- Measured weight error of the NF4 layers: 7–9 % relative to BF16. The precision-critical copies
  are bit-identical to the original.
- Generation from this cache, on an RTX 5080 with 16 GB: 1024×1024 in 6 steps in ~33 s, with a
  VRAM peak of 1.8 GB.

### VAE

`vae/` is the official `vae_diffusers/` folder, byte-identical (verified by SHA-256). The LoRAlab
encodes every training image with it, never with the MiniMax-H3 video VAE, using the same pixel
normalization as the released pipeline.

## What the LoRAlab trains with it

- **Characters, objects and styles**: one image + caption per sample.
- **Trained on MiniMax-H3, made for MiniMax-H3-Image.** MiniMax-H3-Image is distilled to 6
  sampling steps with one output head per step and no CFG, and fine-tuning it directly fails: in
  our tests plain flow matching turned its high-noise heads into the dataset's average within
  ~100 steps (blurred, blotchy images, even at lr 1e-4), and anchoring those heads kept the images
  sharp but learned no likeness. MiniMax-H3-Image was fine-tuned from MiniMax-H3, which is not
  distilled and shares its latent space and every module a LoRA touches. So the LoRAlab trains the
  LoRA on the MiniMax-H3 DiT, with latents from **this** repository's VAE, and renders the training
  previews with MiniMax-H3-Image (6 steps, CFG 1) with the LoRA attached. Measured: previews stay
  sharp and pick up the dataset from the first few hundred steps.
- **Low VRAM**: transformer blocks are streamed to the GPU on demand. Measured on a 16 GB card:
  30 of the 50 blocks resident, 13.9 GB peak with previews included, ~4.5 s per step at ~1 MP.

Exported LoRAs use the key layout of the original checkpoints (fused `qkv_proj`, interleaved per
attention head; `mlp.fc1` with its SwiGLU halves in the original order), verified row by row
against the official MiniMax-H3-Image `transformer/` and MiniMax-H3 `FL2VA/transformer`. The same
file applies to both models.

# MiniMax-H3-Image (Pruned DiT) — GGUF Quantizations

Quantized **GGUF** weights for **[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)**, converted directly from the structurally pruned BF16 master checkpoint provided by **[Comfy-Org](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image)** (`minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16.safetensors`).

MiniMax-H3-Image is a state-of-the-art **33.1B parameter single-stream Diffusion Transformer (DiT)** designed for ultra-high-resolution text-to-image generation and multi-reference image editing (up to 16 MP / 4096 × 4096) in just **6 distilled sampling steps**.

All GGUFs in this repository have sensitive layers (the 24-channel input patchifier `video_patch_proj`, the 6-step PDD output head `final_layer`, and the low-rank AdaLN modulation basis `adaln_basis` / `adaln_t_table`) strictly preserved in **unquantized FP32** to eliminate quantization noise and grid artifacts.

> **✅ Update — Native Stock ComfyUI-GGUF Support:** All GGUF files in this repository now include the embedded `config` (`pdd_sigmas` 6-step schedule) header metadata and load natively out of the box in stock **ComfyUI-GGUF (`Unet Loader (GGUF)`)** with zero custom scripts or patches required! *(Note: [`minimax_h3_image_gguf_fix.py`](./minimax_h3_image_gguf_fix.py) is kept in the repository solely as an optional fallback for users on older versions of ComfyUI-GGUF).*
---

## Model Files & Quantization Overview

| File Name | Size | Quant Type | Recommended Hardware / VRAM | Quality / Use Case |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q2_K.gguf`** | **6.88 GB** | `Q2_K` | 8 GB – 10 GB VRAM | Maximum memory savings. Fits easily on consumer laptops & entry GPUs. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q3_K_M.gguf`** | **8.91 GB** | `Q3_K_M` | 12 GB VRAM | High efficiency with significantly lower quantization loss than 2-bit. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q4_K_S.gguf`** | **11.60 GB** | `Q4_K_S` | 12 GB – 16 GB VRAM | Fast 4-bit small variant. Well-balanced footprint. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q4_K_M.gguf`** | **11.60 GB** | `Q4_K_M` | 16 GB VRAM | **Recommended sweet spot.** Near-lossless visual quality for standard GPUs. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q5_K_M.gguf`** | **14.10 GB** | `Q5_K_M` | 16 GB – 24 GB VRAM | Maximum fidelity. Indistinguishable from full BF16. |

---

## Required Companion Files

MiniMax-H3-Image requires a dedicated **24-channel Image VAE** and the **Qwen3-VL-32B** text encoder (reading layer 50 hidden states).

### 1. Image VAE (24-Channel)
* **Official / Comfy-Org FP16 VAE:** [`minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image/tree/main/vae)  
  *(Place inside `ComfyUI/models/vae/`)*

> **Note:** The Image VAE uses 24 latent channels with a 2D ViT decoder. Do **not** use standard 4-channel SD/Flux VAEs or the 16-channel video VAE from earlier H3 releases.

### 2. Text Encoder (Qwen3-VL-32B)
You can choose between pre-quantized safetensors or standalone GGUF text encoders:

* **GGUF Text Encoders (by Abiray):**

*(Place inside `ComfyUI/models/clip/` or `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/`)*

Ultra-compact 4-bit ConvRot text encoder & prompt enhancer weights for ComfyUI

--- ## Overview Ultra-compact **INT4 ConvRot** single-file `.safetensors` weights for **[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)** in **ComfyUI**. **`-15.2%`** vs `nvfp4_awq` (`15.69 GB`) | | **`qwen3.5_9b_int4_convrot.safetensors`** | **Prompt Enhancer** (`Qwen3.5-9B`, optional) | `convrot_w4a4` + `int8` / `bf16` | **5.42 GB** (`5.05 GiB`) | **`-26.2%`** vs `qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq` (`7.34 GB`) | --- ## ComfyUI Usage ### 1. Workflow Setup 1. **Text Encoder:** In **CLIPLoader**, select `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int4_convrot.safetensors` with **`type = minimax`** and connect it to **MiniMaxH3ImageConditioning**. 2. **Prompt Enhancer *(optional)*:** In **CLIPLoader**, select `qwen3.5_9b_int4_convrot.safetensors` with **`type = minimax`** and connect it to **Generate Text** (`TextGenerateV2`). 3. **Templates:** Works as a direct drop-in replacement inside ComfyUI's official MiniMax-H3-Image [Text-to-Image](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/image_minimax_h3_image_t2i.json) and [Image Edit](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/image_minimax_h3_image_edit.json) workflows. > **Requirements:** Up-to-date **ComfyUI** with **`comfy_kitchen`** kernels supporting `convrot_w4a4` and `nvfp4` on CUDA GPUs. --- ## Quantization Details ### `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int4_convrot.safetensors` (`727` tensors) Formatted to MiniMax-H3-Image's exact 50-layer extraction spec (`minimax_h3_te: {"num_hidden_layers": 50, "output": "unnormalized_hidden_after_layer_50"}`): - **LM & Merger Linears (`358` layers):** `convrot_w4a4` (`convrot_groupsize=256`, `quant_group_size=64`). - **Vision Projections (`81` layers):** `convrot_w4a4` (`convrot_groupsize=64`). - **Vision MLP Down (`fc2`, `27` layers):** `nvfp4` fallback (`K = 4304` is not divisible by `64` for `convrot_w4a4`). - **Embeddings & Sensitive Layers:** `embed_tokens` in ConvRot `int8_tensorwise` (`gs=256`); RMSNorms, vision biases, `patch_embed`, and `pos_embed` preserved in `BF16`. > **Why viewers show `I8` on 4-bit layers:** Safetensors has no native `int4` tensor dtype, so two 4-bit weights are packed per byte in `I8` (`int8`) containers. # MiniMax H3 Image · ARA1 GGUF

**Q8_0 diffusion transformer and conditioning encoder, with the original VAE,
tokenizers, processor and six PDD heads. Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image.**

Independent community conversion by [Devin Lai](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai).
This experimental release includes the published nine `o_proj` ARA edits in
encoder layers 31–39 at strength 1.0. No new training was performed.

## Download

Request access on this page, read the retained model agreements and sign in.
The complete weight bundle is **66.33 GB (61.77 GiB)** before the included runtime
source and documentation. Disk size is not the host RAM or GPU memory requirement.

```bash
python -m pip install 'huggingface-hub>=0.36.2'
hf auth login
hf download devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-ARA1-GGUF \
  --revision v1.0.0 --local-dir MiniMax-H3-Image-ARA1-GGUF
cd MiniMax-H3-Image-ARA1-GGUF
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

| Component | File | Bytes |
|---|---|---:|
| DiT | `transformer/MiniMax-H3-Image-DiT-Q8_0.gguf` | 36,022,938,432 |
| Encoder | `text_encoder/MiniMax-H3-TextEncoder-ARA1-Q8_0.gguf` | 27,921,295,104 |
| Original VAE | `vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors` | 2,336,964,672 |

The encoder contains the 50 language layers consumed by H3 conditioning and
the complete source-precision vision tower. The DiT uses the audited native QKV
row layout. Both component manifests record every tensor's shape, type and hash;
`bundle.json` records the packaged files. The GGUF weight bytes match the
previously validated local bundle exactly.

## Run with the included Linux / NVIDIA runtime

`runtime-source.tar.gz` contains the patched SGLang backend, SageAttention
source, pinned dependencies and GGUF inference launchers. The GGUF loader fixes
are included; a generic SGLang installation may not contain them. This snapshot
contains inference sources, without the custom model export tools.

On Linux x86_64 with an allocated NVIDIA GPU, a C++ compiler, sufficient host RAM
and a CUDA 13.0 compatible driver:

```bash
# Run from the downloaded model directory.
tar -xzf runtime-source.tar.gz
bash runtime/bin/install.sh
runtime/.venv/bin/python runtime/bin/serve_h3_gguf.py \
  --bundle "$PWD" --gpu 0 --port 33000
```

In a second terminal, from the same model directory:

```bash
runtime/.venv/bin/python runtime/bin/generate.py \
  'A watercolor fox under a snowy pine tree' \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:33000 --profile six --quality exact \
  --size 2048x2048 --seed 731 --output generated/fox.png
```

The service binds localhost. Keep ports 33000, 33001 and 33010 available. Weights
stream from host RAM, with 12 DiT layers resident by default. Installation also
needs scratch space for the pinned CUDA toolchain and compiled dependencies.
The packaged sources correspond to the validated runtime; a new installation
has not been rerun on a GPU as part of this upload.

Compatibility with ComfyUI and llama.cpp is untested. The GGUFs use H3-specific
tensor names and metadata; the `.gguf` extension alone does not establish loader
compatibility. The public [MLX conversion scripts](https://github.com/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx-convert)
document a separate storage-preserving repacking workflow for Apple silicon.

## Validation and limits

Historical L20 tests used 24 prompts × two seeds at native 2K with all six PDD
passes. Against the original BF16 image pipeline, mean LPIPS was **0.1798** and
mean CLIP image cosine was **0.9784**. The general-quality subset measured
LPIPS 0.1448 and cosine 0.9848. These metrics do not establish perceptual or pixel
equivalence; compositions can change substantially.

All three arms (original BF16, original Q8 control and edited Q8) generated 48/48
images with zero visually observed refusals. Refusal reduction was not
demonstrated. The source language-model refusal figures are not image-generation
results. Visual review was by Codex, without an independent human panel; the
custom suite does not cover explicit sexual imagery or arbitrary prompts.

Standalone loading, 2K editing and native 4K generation were tested o

# ChatR Labs Uncensored Omni — Quantized

[![Try the Playground](https://img.shields.io/badge/Playground-Try_it_live-2563eb?style=for-the-badge)](https://chatrlabs.com/)
[![Base model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hugging_Face-Base_model-ffcc4d?style=for-the-badge)](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)

**Quantized builds at adapter weight 1.0, for text-to-image generation and image editing.**

This repository ships **quantized transformer weights only**. The model is our rank-128 Omni adapter merged into
[Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) at **LoRA strength 1.0**, then quantized.
The text encoder, processor and VAE are not included; take them from the base repository.

## Download

| File | Format | Layout | Size | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-BF16.gguf`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-BF16.gguf) | GGUF BF16 | 297 | 14.23 GB | ComfyUI, Diffusers |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q8_0.gguf`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q8_0.gguf) | GGUF Q8_0 | 297 | 7.69 GB | ComfyUI, Diffusers |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q6_K.gguf`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q6_K.gguf) | GGUF Q6_K | 297 | 6.00 GB | ComfyUI, Diffusers |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q5_K_M.gguf`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q5_K_M.gguf) | GGUF Q5_K_M | 297 | 5.21 GB | ComfyUI, Diffusers |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q4_K_M.gguf`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q4_K_M.gguf) | GGUF Q4_K_M | 297 | 4.47 GB | ComfyUI, Diffusers |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q4_0.gguf`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q4_0.gguf) | GGUF Q4_0 | 297 | 4.20 GB | ComfyUI, Diffusers |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-FP8-comfy.safetensors`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-FP8-comfy.safetensors) | FP8 E4M3 | 265 | 7.12 GB | ComfyUI only |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-INT8-ConvRot-comfy.safetensors`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-INT8-ConvRot-comfy.safetensors) | INT8 ConvRot | 265 | 7.26 GB | ComfyUI only |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-NVFP4-comfy.safetensors`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-NVFP4-comfy.safetensors) | NVFP4 | 265 | 4.20 GB | ComfyUI only |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-FP8-torchao/`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-FP8-torchao) | FP8 (torchao) | 297 | 7.12 GB | Diffusers only |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-NF4-bnb/`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-NF4-bnb) | NF4 (bitsandbytes) | 297 | 3.67 GB | Diffusers only |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-INT8-bnb/`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-INT8-bnb) | INT8 (bitsandbytes) | 297 | 7.12 GB | Diffusers only |
| [`qwen-image-2.1-step90000-BF16/`](./qwen-image-2.1-step90000-BF16) | BF16 safetensors | 297 | 14.23 GB | Diffusers; ComfyUI (see BF16 workflow below) |

File integrity information is in [SHA256SUMS](./SHA256SUMS).

### Which build should I use?

- **ComfyUI, one file, both workflows** -> any **GGUF**. It also loads in Diffusers via `from_single_file`.
- **ComfyUI, native quant ops** -> **FP8**, **INT8 ConvRot** or **NVFP4**.
- **Diffusers, smallest download** -> **NF4** (needs `bitsandbytes`).
- **Diffusers, best fidelity** -> **FP8 (torchao)** (needs `torchao`).
- **Maximum fidelity overall** -> **BF16 GGUF**, **BF16 safetensors** or **Q8_0**.
- **Diffusers without the `gguf` package** -> the **BF16** folder (plain `from_pretrained`).

The `297` and `265` layouts use different MLP representations: `265` uses the fused `img_mlp.gate_up`
projection; `297` keeps the separate `gate_layer` / `proj` pair. A loader must support the selected layout.
The BF16 ComfyUI workflow below was verified with the `297`-tensor safetensors file and the native
`UNETLoader` in ComfyUI 0.39.0; support should not be assumed for older or different loaders.

## Recommended settings

These are the values from our inference grid search for the non-distilled model.

| Setting | Starting value |
| --- | --- |
| Base components | Text encoder, processor and VAE from `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` |
| Sampling steps | **35** |
| True CFG scale | **5.0** (both text-to-image and editing) |
| Sampler | `er_sde` with the `simple` scheduler (ComfyUI) |
| Negative prompt | A single space: `" "` |
| Output resolution | `768 x 1152` or `1024 x 1024` |
| KV cache | Enabled |

An omitted or empty negative prompt disables true CFG even when `true_cfg_scale` is greater than 1. Use a single
space if you do not need a specific negative prompt. This is a regular LoRA merge; it does not provide few-step
distillation.

## Usage with ComfyUI

```
ComfyUI/models/
|-- diffusion_models/    qwen-image-2.1-step90000-Q5_K_M.gguf
|-- text_encoders/       <Qwen-Image-2.1 text encoder>
`-- vae/                 <Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE>
```

- **GGUF:** `Unet Loader (GGUF)` -> pick the file. Works

# MiniMax H3 Image on Apple silicon

**Generate and edit images locally with MLX. Choose one weight variant; reuse the shared components.**

**Measured on M5 Pro / 64 GiB:** tuned warm 2048 × 2048 generation took
**62.49 s with BF16** or **64.05 s with lossless packed BF16**. These are
historical tests with cached conditioning and resident weights; see the
[measurement details](#measured-on-m5-pro--64-gib).

[View the generated showcase and comparisons](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx-examples)

*The gallery contains AI-generated images from recorded local runs. It uses
manual access review under the model license. [Prompts, seeds and precision
settings](examples/README.md) are also documented here.*

A community port of [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)
by [Devin Lai](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai). Native MLX/Metal inference,
all six distilled PDD steps, reference-image editing, lossless BF16 packing
and optional Q8/Q4 weights. Model operators run locally on your Mac.

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Choose weights](#choose-your-download) ·
[Usage](USAGE.md) · [Benchmarks](BENCHMARKS.md) ·
[Collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/devin-lai/minimax-h3-image-apple-silicon-mlx-6af64fcd11d7d7a3b17e11d8) · [Repository map](MODEL_INDEX.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Start with packed12 on a sufficiently large Mac.** It reconstructs the
original BF16 weight bits before computation. It is storage compression,
not quantization. The tested machine is an **M5 Pro with 64 GiB**;
smaller-memory Macs have not been qualified.

## Choose your download

The main repository contains inference code, documentation and comparison
records. Generated images are in the separately gated example gallery. Each
linked model repository contains one weight choice.
The downloader fetches that choice and its required shared files, then reuses
the same pinned upstream text encoder across variants.

| Variant | Variant weights¹ | Choose it for |
|---|---:|---|
| **[Lossless packed BF16](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx-packed12)** | **27.23 GiB** | Recommended exact storage choice; original BF16 payloads |
| [Original BF16](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx-bf16) | 61.73 GiB | Unmodified complete transformer storage |
| [Q8](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx-q8) | 19.83 GiB | Smaller core; image and detail changes |
| [Q4](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx-q4) | 10.50 GiB | Smallest core; stronger fidelity tradeoffs |

¹ Excludes [shared VAE, support tensors, heads and tables](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx-shared),
the separate **roughly 62 GiB text encoder**, Python dependencies and runtime
memory. BF16 already includes native support; the downloader omits its redundant
shared copy.
Download sizes are not RAM requirements. Q8/Q4 quantize main and refiner
attention/MLP weights with MLX affine groups of 64; FP32 precision islands stay
native. Quantization has not established a generation-speed advantage here.

**License and access:** model weights retain MiniMax's community agreements,
including territory and commercial restrictions; they are not unrestricted
open-source weights. Model components use manual access review.
[Status and license details](RELEASE.md).

| Measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Q4 variant payload | **10.50 GiB** |
| One historical warm product trial: denoising | 67.71 s |
| Same trial: peak MLX allocation | 12.51 GiB |

The variant payload excludes approximately 3.86 GiB of shared components and the roughly 62 GiB text encoder. The historical trial was one 2048 × 2048, six-step product run with cached conditioning and resident weights, using online Q4 on an M5 Pro / 64 GiB. Denoising is not end-to-end time; MLX allocation is not total process or system memory and does not establish minimum RAM. This was not a fresh performance test of the downloadable export. # MiniMax H3 Image MLX · Original BF16 transformer

Unchanged BF16/FP32 transformer files from the pinned image checkpoint. This is the unmodified storage control; it includes the large timestep modulation matrices. The shared downloader omits its redundant support copy.

Community adaptation by **Devin Lai**. Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image.

[Start here: install and quick start](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx) · [Compare variants](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx/blob/main/MODEL_INDEX.md) · [Evidence and limitations](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md)

## Measured performance · M5 Pro / 64 GiB

| Measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Warm 2048 × 2048 image, tuned | **62.49 s** |
| Matched BF16 control → tuned | 65.83 s → 62.49 s (**5.07% lower**) |
| Maximum sampled parent footprint | 40.50 GiB |
| Transformer repository payload | 61.73 GiB |

The repository payload excludes the separately downloaded shared files and roughly 62 GiB text encoder. The BF16 transformer includes native support, so the downloader omits its redundant shared copy.

Warm 2048 × 2048 generation with all six steps, cached conditioning and resident weights. The result is the geometric mean of product and portrait medians, each with three alternating repeats. Startup and downloads are excluded. Peak is sampled parent-process physical footprint across four candidate cases, not a minimum memory requirement. The tested device was an M5 Pro with 16 GPU cores and 64 GiB, running MLX 0.32.4.

The optimized settings are optional and a new CLI process includes loading. [Tuning flags](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx/blob/main/USAGE.md#measured-exact-tuning) · [Method and receipts](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/MiniMax-H3-Image-mlx/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md#exact-tuning-results).

## Download only this variant

After installing the main runtime and obtaining the required access:

```bash
h3-mlx download --variant bf16 --model-dir models/bf16
h3-mlx generate --model models/bf16 \
  --text-encoder models/bf16/text_encoder \
  'An editorial photograph of a cobalt perfume bottle on pale stone' \
  --seed 731 --output outputs/bottle.png
```

This fetches this variant, required shared components and the separately pinned
native text encoder (roughly 62 GiB). It does not fetch other variants. Use
`--text-encoder-path /path/to/text_encoder` to reuse an existing encoder.
All image variants retain the six original PDD heads and native FP32 islands.
The published compact format requires this runtime, not a generic Diffusers
or mlx-lm loader. Tested on M5 Pro / 64 GiB; smaller Macs are unqualified.

This is an inference port of `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image` at revision
`6534ea1c979a5f8cb00c2bd1025d5ca4ee8d8901`, not a newly trained model.
No new training dataset is introduced. Training provenance, potential biases,
intended uses and upstream limitations remain those of the original model.

# Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo for the Snapdragon 8 Elite neural unit

Built with Qwen. A phone conversion of [Qwen-Image 2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) Turbo (as
packaged in [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1)), compiled as QNN
context binaries for the Hexagon v79 neural unit (Snapdragon 8 Elite, e.g. iQOO 13). It draws 768x768 pictures from
a prompt in 8 steps, and edits a 768x768 picture from an instruction.

**Non-commercial use only** (Qwen RESEARCH LICENSE AGREEMENT, see LICENSE and NOTICE).

## What is in it

| Files | What they do |
|---|---|
| `r0.bin` ... `r3.bin`, `qwen_table_q8.raw`, `qwen_tokenizer.json` | the prompt reader (Qwen3-VL-8B's language model, 8-bit weights) |
| `vis.bin` | the reader's vision tower, for edits (8-bit weights) |
| `sp0.bin` ... `sp31.bin` | the drawing model, one block per file (4-bit weights in blocks of 32) |
| `s0.bin`, `s1.bin`, `qwen2b_table_q8.raw` | the Small prompt reader (Qwen3-VL-2B's language model, 8-bit weights) |
| `proj.bin` | the Small reader's translator: maps the 2B's features to the 8B's (trained on 35k prompts) |
| `enc.bin`, `dec.bin` | taeqi2_1 picture encoder and decoder |
| `sigmas.txt` | the 8 noise levels |
| `manifest.json` | file list with sizes and SHA-256, used by the app's download |

Two downloads share the drawing model: **Standard** (the 8B reader, picture editing, 14.9 GB) and **Small** (the 2B
reader + translator, prompts only, 8.2 GB; pictures very close to Standard's, the prompt read in ~2 s instead of ~7 s).
On the phone a picture takes about 2½ minutes and an edit about 5; the files are loaded one at a time, so it
needs about 2.6 GB of memory while drawing.

## Changes from the original models

The weights were converted to ONNX, quantized (4-bit blocks for the drawing model, 8-bit per channel with a
Hadamard rotation for the reader) and compiled for the neural unit. Pictures may differ slightly from the
original models'. Before November 2026 this repo held a 4-step build (the base model with Viggle's turbo LoRA merged
in); the build guide explains how to make it again.

## The app, and building these files yourself

These files are made for the [Anima app](https://github.com/adiirfan/anima-android), which downloads them itself.
The scripts that build them from the original model weights, with a step-by-step guide, are in
[`build/`](build/README.md) in this repo.

# Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-CMF

A verified, single-file **CMF** build of the Qwen-Image-2.1 pipeline for local image generation with [Cortiq](https://github.com/infosave2007/cmf).

**12.745 GB · 15.59B parameters · one file · CPU, native Metal, Vulkan and CUDA runtime paths**

The file contains the DiT, text/vision encoders, VAE, tokenizer, and recipe. Its production layout is retained from the validated CMF base: **q4tp DiT + q8_2f encoders + f16 VAE**. This is a runtime-oriented layout, not a raw BF16 dump.

## Get started

Download `qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf` and its matching
`qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf.sha256` file from the **Files** tab, then verify
the download:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf.sha256
```

To download both files from a terminal instead, use the Hugging Face CLI:

```bash
hf download infosave/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-CMF \
  qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf.sha256 \
  --local-dir ./image-2.1-uc
```

| File | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Artifact | `qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf` |
| Exact size | 12,745,219,006 bytes (11.870 GiB) |
| SHA-256 | `44317a2e7ebe4a520ba2e701ff099f8faaeafe065972395c3ac53ae32f99aada` |
| Tested runtime | `cortiq 0.8.2` |

## Generate an image

```bash
cargo install cortiq-cli --locked

cortiq imagine qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf \
  --prompt "A red fox in fresh snow at golden hour" \
  --out fox.png
```

The artifact was tested with `cortiq 0.8.2`. The embedded recipe defaults to 1024×1024 and 40 steps. For a fast installation check:

```bash
cortiq verify qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf
cortiq imagine qwen-image-2.1-uncensored.cmf \
  --prompt "A red fox in fresh snow at golden hour" \
  --width 512 --height 512 --steps 4 --seed 42 --out smoke.png
```

## Examples

![A red fox in fresh snow at golden hour](examples/fox-vulkan-1024.png)

`1024×1024` · 40 steps · cfg=1 · seed=42  
Prompt: `A red fox in fresh snow at golden hour`

![A futuristic botanical observatory above the ocean](examples/observatory-vulkan-1024.png)

`1024×1024` · 40 steps · cfg=1 · seed=271828  
Prompt: `A futuristic botanical observatory built into a cliff above a calm ocean at sunrise, glass domes, lush bioluminescent plants, cinematic wide-angle architectural visualization`

Both images were generated from this exact artifact on the RTX 4090 Vulkan f16-fallback path.

## Hardware paths

| Platform | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU | `CMF_GPU=0 cortiq imagine …` | Tested. Use `CMF_THREADS` to tune the host. |
| NVIDIA / Vulkan | `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan CMF_GPU=1 cortiq imagine …` | Tested on RTX 4090. |
| NVIDIA / CUDA | `CMF_GPU=cuda cortiq imagine …` (a binary built with `cargo install cortiq-cli --features cuda`, 0.8.82 or later) | Tested on RTX A5000. |
| Apple silicon / Metal | `CMF_GPU=1 CMF_QI21_METAL_PROF=1 cortiq imagine …` | Native resident path is retained by this layout. Measure on the target Mac before publishing a Metal number. |

For headless RunPod-style containers, install the Vulkan userspace once before testing:

```bash
apt-get update && apt-get install -y libglvnd0 libgl1 libegl1 libvulkan1 vulkan-tools
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName
```

### Measured Vulkan result

This is a run of **this exact artifact**, not a number copied from another Qwen model:

| Host | Workload | Path | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 4090, driver 570.195.03, Vulkan | 1024×1024, 40 steps, cfg=1, seed=42 | Vulkan f16 fallback | **29.13 s** end to end; **0.527 s** median DiT step |

The run held 13.96 GB of DiT planes on the device; the 1024² VAE decode reported 4.8 GB activations and 0.81 s decode time. The driver exposed no float8 matrix extension (`fp8 mma false`), so this is honestly labeled **f16 fallback**, not FP8.

CPU tuning on AMD EPYC 7642 (96 logical CPUs), using 256×256 / 2 steps / the same fixed prompt and seed:

| `CMF_THREADS` | Total | Median DiT step |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 48 | 86.70 s | 32.720 s |
| 32 | 66.05 s | 24.317 s |
| 12 | **43.54 s** | **15.806 s** |

For this host and workload, 12 threads beat the default-like 32-thread configuration by about 34% end to end. This is a tuning result, not a universal CPU claim. Repeating the 12-thread run produced the identical PNG SHA-256.

See [BENCHMARKS.md](./BENCHMARKS.md) for the reproducible protocol and limitations.


### Measured CUDA result

| Host | Workload | Path | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX A5000 (24 GB), cortiq 0.8.82 | 1024×1024, 40 steps, default settings, seed 7 | CUDA | **53.1 s** end to end; **1.14 s** median DiT step |

**Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image.**

Quantized files of [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), MiniMax's text-to-image and
image-editing model (6-step distilled, no CFG), for [stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp).
Each file is the diffusion transformer only. The text encoder and the VAE are the usual downloads (see [Run](#run)).

> **Licence and territory.** MiniMax-H3-Image is distributed under the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement
> (`LICENSE`, `NOTICE`). It grants rights **only outside the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea
> and the United States of America**. Do not download, use or share these files, or anything generated with them, in
> those territories. Use must also follow the Acceptable Use Policy in `LICENSE`. Annualized revenue above 1 million USD
> or offering the model as a hosted service needs MiniMax's prior written permission.

> Not made, sponsored or endorsed by MiniMax.

> **These files have not been tested on AMD hardware yet.** Please report speed and quality in the Community tab.
>
> The `ROCMFPX` and `ROCMFP4` files need stable-diffusion.cpp built on the ROCmFPX fork of ggml with the small patch
> in this repo (`sdcpp-rocmfpx.patch`). The `Q6_K` and `Q5_K` files are stock llama.cpp weight types and load in
> stable-diffusion.cpp from commit `32d516c` (MiniMax-H3-Image support) on.

## Files

| File | Size | LPIPS | PSNR | SSIM | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `MiniMax-H3-Image-Q8_0_ROCMFPX.gguf` | 20.8 GB | **0.032** | 31.05 | 0.957 | 8-bit, closest to BF16 |
| `MiniMax-H3-Image-Q6_K.gguf` | 16.6 GB | 0.060 | 25.48 | 0.916 | 6-bit, stock type, our importance matrix |
| `MiniMax-H3-Image-Q5_K.gguf` | 13.9 GB | 0.113 | 22.30 | 0.847 | 5-bit, stock type, our importance matrix |
| `MiniMax-H3-Image-Q4_0_ROCMFP4.gguf` | 11.4 GB | 0.193 | 19.52 | 0.757 | 4-bit, smallest |

Compared with GGUFs already on the Hub and with stock files, measured the same way:

| Not published | Size | LPIPS | PSNR | SSIM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [Hearthscale](https://huggingface.co/Hearthscale/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF) Q8_0 | 21.4 GB | 0.041 | 30.34 | 0.945 |
| Stock Q8_0 (stable-diffusion.cpp convert) | 21.4 GB | 0.043 | 30.07 | 0.940 |
| ROCmFPX 6-bit | 16.4 GB | 0.085 | 24.43 | 0.883 |
| Stock Q6_K without importance matrix | 16.6 GB | 0.080 | 24.25 | 0.891 |
| [Hearthscale](https://huggingface.co/Hearthscale/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF) Q5_K_M | 13.9 GB | 0.124 | 21.65 | 0.834 |
| [Hearthscale](https://huggingface.co/Hearthscale/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF) Q4_K_M | 11.4 GB | 0.202 | 18.54 | 0.740 |
| Stock Q4_K, our importance matrix | 11.4 GB | 0.218 | 18.46 | 0.730 |

At every size the files here are closer to BF16 than the Hub GGUFs of the same size. The ROCmFPX 8-bit file is also
0.6 GB smaller than a Q8_0. At 6-bit the stock `Q6_K` with our importance matrix beat the ROCmFPX 6-bit type, so the
`Q6_K` is the one here. Abiray's GGUFs could not be compared: they store the output head in a ComfyUI-specific layout
that stable-diffusion.cpp does not load.

**How this was measured:** 12 prompts (portrait, text on signs, watercolor, still life, animals, aerial, night market and
others) at 512x512, seed 1, 6 Euler steps with the MiniMax-H3-Image sigma schedule, rendered with stable-diffusion.cpp on
an NVIDIA GB10 GPU after expanding each file to F16, and compared image by image with the same render from the BF16
model. LPIPS is how different two images look to a neural network (lower is better); PSNR and SSIM compare the pixels
(higher is better). A 6-step model turns small weight differences into small changes of composition, so these numbers
measure how far each file drifts from BF16 rather than how good its images look.

# Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 CMF

[Qwen-Image-Edit-2509](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509) for native Rust image editing with [cortiq](https://github.com/infosave2007/cmf). The ready file includes the transformer, Qwen2.5-VL text/vision encoder, tokenizer, processor, VAE and scheduler. Separate components remain available.

Native editing is available; image-quality validation is incomplete.

[English](#speed) · [Русский](#русский) · [中文](#中文说明)

## Files

- qwen-image-edit-2509-q4tp.cmf — ready single-file pipeline
- transformer.cmf — Q4TP diffusion transformer
- text_encoder.cmf — Qwen2.5-VL encoder, tokenizer and processor
- vae.cmf — Qwen Image VAE
- scheduler_config.json — scheduler for separate components

## Usage

Install [cortiq 0.8.80](https://github.com/infosave2007/cmf/releases/tag/v0.8.80) or newer, then run:

    cortiq imagine qwen-image-edit-2509-q4tp.cmf \
      --image input.png --prompt "Add a blue knitted scarf." \
      --height 1024 --width 1024 --steps 40 --cfg 4 --seed 7 \
      --reference-size 1024 --out edited.png

For separate components, pass their folder instead of the single file:

    cortiq imagine qwen-image-parts \
      --image input.png --prompt "Add a blue knitted scarf." \
      --height 1024 --width 1024 --steps 40 --cfg 4 --seed 7 \
      --reference-size 1024 --out edited.png

--text-encoder, --vae and --scheduler select explicit component overrides.

## Speed

`cortiq` 0.8.80 keeps every transformer block of a step on the card in one call, over CUDA and over Vulkan;
the VAE's convolutions and attention run on the card too. NVIDIA RTX A5000 (24 GB), a 1024 × 1024 edit,
8 steps, CFG 4, seed 7, release build, single runs:

| Backend | Time | Before 0.8.80 |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA (`CMF_GPU=cuda`) | **105.8 s** | 464 s |
| Vulkan (`CMF_GPU=1`) | **148.1 s** | 442.5 s |

On CUDA the edit fits an 8 GB card: `CMF_GPU_VRAM_MB=8000` keeps the first blocks on the card and passes the
rest through it every step (115.1 s, peak 7.4 GB). The card's 40-step recipe takes 371.6 s on CUDA. The CUDA
backend is a build feature; the prebuilt release binaries do not include it:

    cargo install cortiq-cli --features cuda     # needs the driver and the CUDA 12.x libraries
    CMF_GPU=cuda cortiq imagine qwen-image-edit-2509-q4tp.cmf --image input.png \
      --prompt "Add a blue knitted scarf." --height 1024 --width 1024 --steps 40 --cfg 4 \
      --reference-size 1024 --out edited.png

## Sources

The transformer was converted from [QuantStack's Q6_K GGUF](https://huggingface.co/QuantStack/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509-GGUF); other components come from [Qwen](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509). Apache-2.0.

## Русский

процессором, VAE и планировщиком. Нужен cortiq 0.8.80 или новее:

# MiniMax-H3-Image GGUF

GGUF builds of [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), made by Moonbox for on-device use. Each precision is one file at the root of
this repository; pick one by the memory you have. Only the model's own weights are converted: the other parts of the
pipeline (text encoder, VAE, tokenizer) come from the original repository unless the section below says otherwise.

## Files

The last column is how far each file is from the original BF16 weights: the relative RMS error of its dequantized
weights, averaged over all parameters. Image-quality scores against BF16 outputs are
added as each precision passes the image eval.

| Precision | File | Size | sha256 | Checked against BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F16 | [`minimax-h3-image-F16.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/moonbox-ai/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF/blob/main/minimax-h3-image-F16.gguf) | 40.25 GB | `df57ab8cf074` | 0.0000001 % (8.8e-10) |
| BF16 | [`minimax-h3-image-BF16.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/moonbox-ai/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF/blob/main/minimax-h3-image-BF16.gguf) | 40.25 GB | `66bb7109a073` | exact |
| Q8_0 | [`minimax-h3-image-Q8_0.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/moonbox-ai/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF/blob/main/minimax-h3-image-Q8_0.gguf) | 21.46 GB | `142134608dde` | 0.56 % |
| Q6_K | [`minimax-h3-image-Q6_K.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/moonbox-ai/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF/blob/main/minimax-h3-image-Q6_K.gguf) | 16.61 GB | `cbedcf9a5f46` | 1.9 % |
| Q5_K_M | [`minimax-h3-image-Q5_K_M.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/moonbox-ai/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF/blob/main/minimax-h3-image-Q5_K_M.gguf) | 14.05 GB | `d6571e57f992` | 3.7 % |
| Q4_K_M | [`minimax-h3-image-Q4_K_M.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/moonbox-ai/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF/blob/main/minimax-h3-image-Q4_K_M.gguf) | 11.54 GB | `bf51152afb00` | 7.2 % |

## How to run

These files are the MiniMax-H3-Image diffusion transformer only (20.1 B parameters as stable-diffusion.cpp and
ComfyUI run it), made from Comfy-Org's single-file repackage of MiniMax's weights
(`minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16.safetensors`: the six per-step output heads included and the time-embedding
modulation folded into 8 time curves; we checked it against the official weights). Text encoder and VAE are separate:

- **VAE:** `minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors` from [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image/tree/main/vae).
- **Text encoder:** MiniMax-H3's Qwen3-VL-32B, e.g. `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q4_K_M.gguf` (18 GB) from
  [leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF), or the much smaller P-H3-Image text
  encoder (Qwen3-VL-4B with its connector, 5 GB) from [PrunaAI/P-H3-Image-Comfy](https://huggingface.co/PrunaAI/P-H3-Image-Comfy/tree/main/text_encoders).

**stable-diffusion.cpp** (MiniMax-H3-Image support from master-1088; we ran master-1091, commit b9d7176):

```
sd-cli --diffusion-model minimax-h3-image-Q4_K_M.gguf --vae minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors \
  --llm qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q4_K_M.gguf -p "a lovely cat holding a sign says 'moonbox'" \
  --cfg-scale 1.0 --steps 6 --sampling-method euler --sigmas minimax-h3-image -W 1024 -H 1024 \
  --offload-to-cpu --diffusion-fa --vae-tiling
```

Tested here: Q4_K_M with the P-H3-Image text encoder renders 1024 × 1024 in 13.4 s end to end on an RTX 3080
Laptop GPU (16 GB), adding `--max-vram 14 --mmap --params-backend te=disk` to the command above in place of
`--offload-to-cpu`. Q8_0 (21.5 GB) did not run on that 16 GB card with 32 GB of RAM; the files above Q4_K_M are
for GPUs with 24 GB or more.

# 🚀 Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo - NVFP4 for ComfyUI

![Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo NVFP4, for ComfyUI, by BennyDaBall](banner.png)

**Follow me on X [@BennyDaBall_OG](https://x.com/BennyDaBall_OG) !**

## New file 2026-11-12: `qwen_image_2.1_turbo_nvfp4_BdB_SR.safetensors`

**Same 5.69 GB. Same speed. Closer to full-precision Turbo.**

A second transformer file, built with the next version of my quantization solver stack instead of plain round-to-nearest. It is calibrated on real ComfyUI denoiser runs, and this time that covers **image editing** as well as text-to-image. **BdB_SR** is my tag for files built this way.

- **Drop-in swap:** same 144 NVFP4 matrices, same 48 protected BF16 matrices, same kernels, no custom nodes.
- **Closer on text-to-image:** 21% lower error per denoiser step than the original file (320 held-out calls, closer on 298).
- **Closer on edits:** 25% lower error per denoiser step (240 held-out edit calls, closer on all 240).
- **The original stays put:** the first file further down this page is unchanged. Run whichever you like.

### The numbers

Measured on my RTX 5090 in one sitting on ComfyUI 0.45.0: 12 prompts x 6 seeds, the official 8-sigma schedule, euler, CFG 1, BF16 text encoder. Every render is scored against the BF16 render of the same seed.

| Transformer file | LPIPS vs BF16 (lower = closer) | Median LPIPS | PSNR | Warm s/img |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Official INT8 ConvRot (7.26 GB) | 0.057 | 0.035 | 28.3 dB | 2.17 |
| Original `qwen_image_2.1_turbo_nvfp4.safetensors` | 0.166 | 0.144 | 20.5 dB | 2.25 |
| **New `qwen_image_2.1_turbo_nvfp4_BdB_SR.safetensors`** | **0.136** | **0.111** | **21.3 dB** | 2.27 |

Paired on the same seeds, the new file lands closer to BF16 on 45 of 72 renders (mean LPIPS -0.030, 95% CI -0.050 to -0.011, PSNR +0.8 dB). The per-step numbers above run through the stock loader and the real NVFP4 kernels, scored against the full-precision model.

### Use it

Drop the file into `models/diffusion_models/` and load [01_Text_to_Image_BdB_SR.json](workflows/01_Text_to_Image_BdB_SR.json), or pick it in any workflow below.

Eight steps. Less baggage. More attitude.

**Quantized by BennyDaBall. Built and tested on a single RTX 5090.**

Native ComfyUI weights, a selectively quantized image transformer and encoder, and seven ready-to-load workflows. Fashion, casual photography, editing, multiple references, typography, illustration, and transparent PNGs.

![Native eight-step fashion image generated with the released NVFP4 transformer and encoder on regular ComfyUI](assets/hero.png)

## Download and run

# ACEdit on Qwen-Image-2.1 — student LoRA Reproduction of **ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning** ([arXiv 2610.22328](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22328)) applied to the Qwen-Image-2.1 family. - **Student** = [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) (8-step, CFG=1) + this rank-16 LoRA - **Teacher** = [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1), frozen, CFG 2, asymmetric conditioning (source image + compound instruction) - **Aux editor** = base 2.1 + its own rank-16 LoRA (`aux_lora.safetensors`), trained jointly (DMD fake-score model) ## Recipe (paper §4–§5.1) 10-turn latent rollouts without VAE decode; exit step s~U{1..8}; DMD gradient w(τ)(v̂φ^γ − v̂ψ) evaluated at z_τ(x̂ˢ) with τ~U[0,1); asymmetric conditioning on (I₀, h_e); 5 warmup iters (aux only) + aux every iter / student every 5th; AdamW(0, 0.999), wd 0.01, clip 10, bf16; lr 4e-5 (student) / 8e-6 (aux). Training data: 96 synthetic 1024² scenes with 10-edit chains (dataset [acedit-qwen-image-2.1-chains](https://huggingface.co/datasets/linoyts/acedit-qwen-image-2.1-chains)), generated with the student itself. ## ⚠️ Result: the paper's stability gain did NOT reproduce at this scale This run is a **half run: 250 training iters = 50 student updates** (paper: 500 iters / 100 updates, ~4.4 B200-hours). Losses were healthy (aux FM 3.7→0.16; student DMD loss low and stable), the LoRA verifiably attaches and affects outputs — but the multi-turn stability effect was not measured: | Eval (16 held-out chains ×10 turns, fixed seed, full-image proxies) | base Turbo | trained | note | |---|---|---|---| | Edit chains: LPIPS vs source @10 | 0.727 | 0.720 | saturated by legitimate edits | | Edit chains: DINO cos vs source @10 | 0.622 | 0.615 | same | | **No-op chains** (10× "keep as is"): LPIPS @10 | 0.706 | **0.697** | ~1% — within per-chain noise | | No-op chains: DINO cos @10 | 0.762 | 0.762 | identical to 4 decimals | The no-op test is the paper-sensitive proxy (its Fig. 3), and it shows **no measurable stability gain**. Full artifacts: `EVALUATION.md`, `noop_summary.json`, `noop_per_chain.json`, per-turn PNGs in this repo. Stated deviations beyond the half run (each a candidate explanation, untested here): edit chains from a template bank, not LLM-written; compound instructions h_e built by fluent-join templates, not LLM rewrites; w(τ)=1/max(τ,0.05) chosen for the paper's unspecified normalization; student is the 8-step Turbo checkpoint rather than 4-step FLUX.2-klein-9B; evaluation uses full-image proxies instead of background-masked LPIPS / anchor DINOv2 (GroundingDINO) and no VLM judge. ## Usage Manual peft attach (verified path): ```python from peft import LoraConfig from safetensors.torch import load_file transformer.add_adapter(LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=["to_k","to_q","to_v","to_out.0"])) sd = load_file("student_lora.safetensors") # raw peft keys; strip a "transformer." prefix if present mapped = {k.removeprefix("transformer.").replace(".lora_A.", ".lora_A.default.").replace(".lora_B.", ".lora_B.default."): v for k, v in sd.items()} transformer.load_state_dict(mapped, strict=False) ``` `pipe.load_lora_weights` on this file is not guaranteed (verified inconsistent) — the key metadata format that diffusers' loader expects was not fully reproduced.

> **The clips above are silent GIFs. The videos are not.** The same 48 blocks > denoise the soundtrack alongside the picture — hear it in > [`examples/`](./tree/main/examples): six mp4s with audio, their raw 48 kHz > stereo wavs, and the exact command that made each one. **Every frame above was produced by `cortiq`** — a single Rust binary with no PyTorch, no diffusers, no CUDA toolkit and no Python anywhere in the process — reading one memory-mapped [CMF](https://github.com/infosave2007/cmf) file. On an RTX A5000 a 384×256 clip of 49 frames **with its soundtrack** takes **22.3 s on CUDA and 28.9 s over Vulkan** once the prompt is encoded (it is cached; the first take of a prompt adds 35–45 s). **All nine modes run from this one file**: text → video, text → sound, text → video + sound, image + text → video, video → video, video → sound, sound → video, sound → sound, and image + sound → video. Both VAE encoders are packed alongside the decoders, so conditioning needs nothing else — see [the table below](#every-mode-the-model-has). The `pipeline_tag` says `text-to-video` because that is the one tag Hugging Face lets a model carry and it is where people look for this; the rest are in `tags`. [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) renders video **and its soundtrack** from one prompt: a 21 B audio-video diffusion transformer that denoises picture and sound in the same 48 blocks, a Gemma-4 12 B prompt encoder, a 3-D video VAE, an audio VAE, two latent upscalers and a duration head. The reference checkout is **71.35 GB across six safetensors** plus a PyTorch stack. Here it is **one file of 22.07 GB** — every component, the Gemma-4 tokenizer and every config inside it. | | reference | this file | |---|---|---| | files | 6 safetensors + configs + tokenizer | **1** | | bytes | 71.35 GB | **22.07 GB** (3.2× smaller) | | weights | 35.65 B | 35.65 B — all of them | | loader | diffusers / ComfyUI + PyTorch | `mmap` | | renderer | Python | **one Rust binary** | ## Quick start ```bash # 1 — the runtime (Rust 1.85+; nothing else) cargo install cortiq-cli # 2 — the model hf download infosave/LTX-2.5-cmf ltx25-q4tp.cmf --local-dir . cortiq verify ltx25-q4tp.cmf # every tensor is hashed in the directory # 3 — a video cortiq ltx-video --model ltx25-q4tp.cmf \ --prompt "A corgi in a chef hat flips a pancake in a sunlit kitchen. \ Warm morning light, static camera." \ --height 256 --width 384 --frames 49 --fps 24 --seed 42 \ --out corgi.y4m ffmpeg -i corgi.y4m -pix_fmt yuv420p corgi.mp4 ``` That is the whole thing: prompt in, frames out, one process, one file. The GPU is found at run time — Vulkan on Linux and Windows, Metal on Apple silicon — and everything falls back to the CPU when there is none. On an NVIDIA card the native CUDA backend is faster still. It is a build feature (stable Rust, nothing is linked against CUDA at build time; the prebuilt release binaries do not include it) and needs the card's driver with the CUDA 12.x libraries `libnvrtc.so.12` and `libcublas.so.12` on the loader's path: ```bash cargo install cortiq-cli --features cuda CMF_GPU=cuda cortiq ltx-video --model ltx25-q4tp.cmf --prompt "…" --out clip.y4m ``` On CUDA and over Vulkan the 48 blocks of a step run as one resident chain on the card and the video VAE decodes there too; `CMF_GPU_VRAM_MB` caps what the process holds on the card (the table under [Measured](#measured)). These speeds need `cortiq` 0.8.77 or later. > **Keep the file on local storage.** It is memory-mapped, so every weight is > a page fault. This is a randomly initialized tiny model based on [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) for testing and debugging.

| Feature | Source | This repo |
|---|---|---|
| Checkpoint tensor elements | 66.46B BF16, 604.20M F32 | 3.55M BF16, 1.13M F32 |
| Safetensors weight files | 135.34 GB (28 files) | 11.71 MB (3 files) |
| Diffusion transformer layers / refiner layers | 50 / 2 | 4 / 2 |
| Transformer width / heads / head dimension | 5,376 / 56 / 128 | 64 / 4 / 32 |
| Transformer FFN width | 14,336 | 128 |
| Per-step output heads (PDD) | 6 | Same |
| Image transformer image / text width | 24 / 5,120 | 8 / 8 |
| Text encoder layers / width / head dimension | 64 / 5,120 / 128 | 51 / 8 / 32 |
| Text encoder vision tower layers / width | 27 / 1,152 | 2 / 64 |
| Tokenizer / processor vocabulary rows | 151,936 | Same |
| Image VAE stages / residual blocks | 6 / 2 | Same |
| Image VAE stage widths | 128 / 256 / 256 / 512 / 512 / 1024 | 32 at every stage |
| Image VAE latent channels / compression | 24 / 16x | 8 / 16x |
| ViT decoder layers / heads / head dimension | 24 / 16 / 64 | 4 / 2 / 32 |
| Transformer precision | BF16 blocks, FP32 patch/timestep/output heads | Same |
| Image VAE precision | FP32 | Same |
| Inputs / output | Text, optional reference images -> image | Same |

The DiT conditions on `hidden_states[50]` of its Qwen3-VL conditioner, so the tiny text encoder keeps 51 decoder layers and shrinks only its width. Six VAE stages keep the source's 16x spatial compression, and the transformer keeps the full 2x2 latent patch and six-step PDD schedule that replaces the base output layer. The text condition width is reduced to 8 columns.

| File path | Size |
|------|------|
| text_encoder/model.safetensors | 6.2MB |
| transformer/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors | 1.1MB |
| vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors | 4.5MB |

### Example usage

#### Diffusers (✅ verified)

Requires Diffusers 0.43.0 or newer, which ships the MiniMax-H3-Image integration, and Torchvision for the Qwen3-VL video processor.

```python
def run_diffusers(model_id: str):
    import torch
    from PIL import Image
    from diffusers import ModularPipeline

    pipe = ModularPipeline.from_pretrained(model_id)
    # The index stores the components relative to the repo root (`.`) so the same
    # checkpoint loads from a local directory and from the Hub.
    pipe.load_components(
        pretrained_model_name_or_path=model_id, dtype={"default": torch.bfloat16, "vae": torch.float32}
    )
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    pipe.to(device)

    image = pipe(
        prompt="A red fox trotting through a snowy pine forest.",
        height=64,
        width=64,
        min_generation_area=1024,
        generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(42),
        output="images",
    )[0]
    image.save("minimax-h3-image-t2i.png")
    print("text-to-image", image.size)

    reference = Image.new("RGB", (64, 64), "blue")
    image = pipe(
        prompt="Keep everything in <Picture 1> as it is, but turn the square green.",
        image=reference,
        height=64,
        width=64,
        min_generation_area=1024,
        generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(1234),
        output="images",
    )[0]
    image.save("minimax-h3-image-edit.png")
    print("image editing", image.size)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_diffusers(model_id="scratch/minimax-h3-image")
```

```python
    from PIL import Image
    from diffusers import ModularPipeline

    pipe = ModularPipeline.from_pretrained(model_id)
    # The index stores the components relative to the repo root (`.`) so the same
    # checkpoint loads from a local directory and from the Hub.
    pipe.load_components(
        pretrained_model_name_or_path=model_id, dtype={"default": torch.bfloat16, "vae": torch.float32}
    )
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    pipe.to(device)

    image = pipe(
        prompt="A red fox trotting through a snowy pine forest.",
        height=64,
        width=64,
        min_generation_area=1024,
        generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(42),
        output="images",
    )[0]
    image.save("minimax-h3-image-t2i.png")
    print("text-to-image", image.size)

    reference = Image.new("RGB", (64, 64), "blue")
    image = pipe(
        prompt="Keep everything in <Picture 1> as it is, but turn the square green.",
        image=reference,
        height=64,
        width=64,
        min_generation_area=1024,
        generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(1234),
        output="images",
    )[0]
    image.save("minimax-h3-image-edit.png")
    print("image editing", image.size)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_diffusers(model_id="scratch/minimax-h3-image")
```

# MiniMax-H3 Turbo — one file, no Python

[MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3) renders video and
synchronized stereo audio from one prompt, in one transformer, on two flow
schedules. [larryvrh's Turbo LoRA](https://huggingface.co/larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora)
brings it to four sampling steps. This is both of them in the
[CMF container](https://github.com/infosave2007/cmf) — the DiT, the Qwen3-VL
prompt encoder, the video VAE decoder and the audio vocoder in a single
memory-mapped file — running on `cortiq`, a Rust binary with no ML framework
underneath. On an RTX A5000 a 512×288 clip of 39 frames renders in **19.5 s on
CUDA and 25.8 s over Vulkan**, and within 4 GB of the card's memory in 22.4 s.

The reference checkout is 124.4 GB across four files plus a ComfyUI install.
Here it is **one file between 13.2 and 23.9 GB**, and which one you take is
decided by your VRAM.

## Same prompt, three files

*"A corgi in a chef hat flipping a pancake, sizzling sounds and a cheerful bark."*
— 512×288, 39 frames, seed 42, four steps, nothing but the prompt.

| ![32B](https://huggingface.co/infosave/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-cmf/resolve/main/samples/ab_q4tp.gif) | ![ClipProj](https://huggingface.co/infosave/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-cmf/resolve/main/samples/ab_clipproj.gif) | ![two bits](https://huggingface.co/infosave/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-cmf/resolve/main/samples/ab_q2tp.gif) |
|---|---|---|
| **23.9 GB** — full 32B prompt encoder | **13.2 GB** — 4B encoder + ClipProj | **18.7 GB** — two-bit encoder |
| the reference | same scene, plainer set | a different animal, no pan |

The 13.2 GB file is the one to take if you have 16–20 GB of VRAM: it holds the
whole run resident instead of paging, and it is still four bits everywhere.
Two bits is published as a dead end, not a choice —
[why, with numbers](#making-it-smaller).

The GIFs are silent and the audio is half the model, so take an
**[mp4](https://huggingface.co/infosave/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-cmf/resolve/main/samples/ab_clipproj.mp4)**.
One transformer denoises picture and sound together in one packed sequence.

### Which file

| file | size | VRAM | keyframes | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mmh3-turbo-fl2va-q4tp.cmf` | 23.94 GB | 24 GB+ | yes | **the default** |
| `mmh3-turbo-q4tp.cmf` | 23.47 GB | 24 GB+ | no | same, without the vision tower |
| **`mmh3-turbo-clipproj4b-q4tp.cmf`** | **13.16 GB** | **16–20 GB** | no | **the small one**, peaks at 15.1 GB |
| **`mmh3-turbo-clipproj4b-fl2va-q4tp.cmf`** | **14.48 GB** | **16–24 GB** | **yes** | the small one WITH start/end frames — the 4B vision tower and the VAE encoder join the compact build |
| **`mmh3-turbo-clipproj4b-fl2va-v2-q8_2f.cmf`** | **26.90 GB** | **32 GB+** | **yes** | **eight bits**: the two-field int8, `w = q·row[o]·col[i]`. More weight fidelity, and it runs on the card as of 0.5.94 — still without the fused kernels q4tp has |
| `mmh3-turbo-fl2va-q2tp.cmf` | 18.74 GB | — | yes | don't render with this |

Text-to-video everywhere; the `fl2va` files also take a first and/or last frame
(`--first-frame`/`--last-frame`, binary P6 PPM). The compact
`clipproj4b-fl2va` file was verified frame-for-frame: the conditioning
image comes back as frame 0 of the render. One honest caveat: its
ClipProj projection was fitted on text-only encoder activations, so with
a picture in the prompt the conditioning quality on complex scenes is
still being compared against the full-encoder fl2va files — report what
you see in the discussions.
([keyframes](#keyframe-to-video)). The release's third path, `ref2va`, is not
ported. The Turbo LoRA is merged into the weights, so the file IS the 4-step
model — nothing else to download. 47.83 B parameters, 2 361 tensors,
`cortiq verify` clean.

## Keyframe to video

![The corgi flipping the pancake, started from one frame](https://huggingface.co/infosave/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-cmf/resolve/main/samples/i2v_corgi_flip.gif)

```bash
cortiq animate mmh3-turbo-fl2va-q4tp.cmf \
  --prompt "the corgi lifts the pan and flips the pancake high, sizzling" \
  --first-frame keyframe.ppm --out flip.avi
```

One picture conditions the run twice, and both halves matter. Its VAE latent
becomes a row the DiT holds at a timestep of its own near 1 — a condition, not
noise being removed — and never denoises. The picture ITSELF goes to the prompt
encoder through Qwen3-VL's vision tower, as `"<Picture 1>: "` and a vision
block: at 512×288 that is 144 tokens of the 168 the prompt above carries.
Leave one out and the model is conditioned on something the reference never
conditions on.

`--last-frame` anchors the other end. The first frame is a geometry anchor and
is stretched to the canvas; the last one follows and is cover-cropped, which is
what the reference does w
