# MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Q4

Affine **4-bit / group 64** conversion of MiniMax-H3-Image, published by **zimageapp**. Includes the Q4 diffusion model, the H3-specific Qwen3-VL32B Q4 text/vision encoder with embedded tokenizer, and the original FP16 Image VAE. Supports the **original six-step** model, text-to-image and ordered-reference image editing.

**Runtime compatibility:** packed affine matrices follow the MLX quantization convention, but the checkpoint uses native H3/Locraft tensor names and embedded configuration. The tested end-to-end runtime is **Locraft C++/Metal with BF16 compute**. A complete Swift/MLX H3 Image implementation is not included or validated. This repository is not a drop-in `mlx-lm`, MFlux or Diffusers pipeline; the name describes the Q4 weight packaging, not a ready-made loader.

## Components

| File | Storage | Size |
|---|---|---:|
| `diffusion_models/minimax_h3_image_int4.safetensors` | Q4/g64, selected original BF16/FP32 tensors retained | 11.39 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int4.safetensors` | Q4/g64 text/vision encoder; embedded tokenizer/config | 16.47 GB |
| `vae/minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors` | Original dedicated Image VAE, unchanged | 1.17 GB |

Total weights: **29.02 GB / 27.03 GiB**. Exact byte counts, SHA-256 hashes and source URLs are in [`q4_components.json`](q4_components.json). The Image VAE has a 24-layer 2D decoder; do not replace it with the H3 video VAE.

The diffusion conversion quantizes 209 matrices. Packed weights are `uint32`, eight 4-bit values per word, lowest nibble first, with BF16 scales/biases; `w = q * scale + bias`. The FP32 time basis, patch projection and final PDD-head tensors are preserved. Native tensor names and six original PDD heads are retained. Configuration, tokenizer and reproducible diffusion conversion tools are included. The encoder publication copy removes 864 bytes of inter-tensor padding from the local native file; all 1,602 tensor payloads and metadata are byte-identical and the published file passes standard safetensors validation. Local source weights are not overwritten.

## Download

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
snapshot_download("zimageapp/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-Q4", local_dir="models/MiniMax-H3-Image")
```

With a Locraft build supporting H3 Image, pass the component paths explicitly (this also supports older catalog entries for the padded encoder):

```sh
locraft image generate --model h3-image \
  --models-root /absolute/path/models \
  --dit /absolute/path/models/MiniMax-H3-Image/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_image_int4.safetensors \
  --text-encoder /absolute/path/models/MiniMax-H3-Image/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int4.safetensors \
  --vae /absolute/path/models/MiniMax-H3-Image/vae/minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors \
  --prompt "A cat reading beside a sunlit window, detailed watercolor illustration." \
  --size 2048x1536 --seed 42 --out /absolute/path/new-output --json
```

For edits, add `--ref /absolute/path/input.png` (repeat in Picture order, up to nine). References supply image conditioning rather than pinned output frames. Native prompts use `Edit <Picture 1>.` for edits; Locraft supplies this prefix when absent. The six evaluations use the published seven-point grid in [`pdd_config.json`](pdd_config.json), guidance 1, no negative prompt, no extra LoRA. The removed experimental two-step adapter is not included. Reducing the step count arbitrarily is unsupported.

The publication encoder also passed a fresh 1024 × 768 six-step smoke in 22.3 s; its output pixels exactly match the historical aligned-encoder result for that prompt/seed. See [`publication-validation.json`](publication-validation.json).

## Local evidence

Apple M5 Pro / 24 GB; native C++/Metal, six evaluations, one food prompt and seed 42:

| Canvas | Total generation time |
|---|---:|
| 1024 × 768 | 24.2 s |
| 2048 × 1536 | 60.5 s |
| 3072 × 2304 | 124.0 s |
| 4096 × 3072 | 236.8 s |

These are direct generations, not upscales. Different canvas sizes change noise and composition. Timings are single measured runs, not universal speed or quality guarantees. See [`benchmarks.json`](benchmarks.json) and the exact [food prompt](examples/food.json).

![AI-generated food sample, 2K generation shown as a reduced preview](examples/food-2k-preview.jpg)

The local six-step samples show coherent food/material detail, but Q4 is not pixel-identical to the dense model. Image edits can repaint faces and fine geometry. The native CLI does not include the official hosted endpoint's prompt enhancer: exact short input text can differ in style from the hosted API result. A small native Image

# MiniMax-H3-Image for Mac (MLX, 8-bit)

**Run it in one click with [Phosphene](https://phosphene.video): a free, open-source Mac app for offline AI pictures, video, speech and songs.**

**Will it run on your Mac?** See which models run on your memory size and how long a clip takes: [phosphene.video/mac-requirements](https://phosphene.video/mac-requirements/?utm_source=huggingface&utm_medium=model_card).

Download Phosphene at **[phosphene.video](https://phosphene.video)** (Mac app, or one-click install through Pinokio), open **Images** and pick **MiniMax-H3-Image**.

This is [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) converted to run natively on Apple Silicon with MLX: the image transformer in 8-bit (group size 64), with its per-block timestep projections precomputed for the model's six steps. About 22 GB instead of 66 GB. Everything runs on your Mac; nothing is sent anywhere.

## Benchmark (M4 Max, 64 GB)

Whole picture, wall clock, including model load:

| Size | Time | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|
| 4 MP | about 2 min (119 s) | 27.5 GB |
| 8 MP | about 4 min (227 s) | 27.5 GB |
| 16 MP | about 8.5 min (513 s) | 27.5 GB |

6 steps, no guidance. Needs a Mac with 48 GB of memory or more. Strong at hands, skin and exact text on posters. Longer, detailed English prompts work best.

## Edit and combine pictures

Since Phosphene 5.0.19 the same weights also edit your own pictures:

- **Edit one picture**: give it a photo and say what to change ("make it night", "put her in a red coat"). The rest of the picture stays.
- **Combine pictures**: give it two or more pictures (up to 16) and describe the result, for example a person from one photo in the place from another.
- **Match the reference**: keep the layout and framing of your picture while restyling it.

Measured on the same Mac (M4 Max, 64 GB), 4 MP, whole picture including model load:

| Job | Time | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|
| Text only | about 2 min (119 s) | 27.5 GB |
| Edit one picture | about 5 min (277 to 291 s) | 29.3 GB |
| Combine two pictures | about 8 min (493 s) | 29.3 GB |

In Phosphene: open **Images**, pick **MiniMax-H3-Image**, add your pictures, write what you want and press Generate.

## Files

- `dit/`: the image transformer, 8-bit MLX, 12 shards, sha256 per file in `dit/ASSET_SHA256.json`
- `vae/`: the image decoder
- `pdd_fused_heads.safetensors`, `pdd_config.json`: the per-step output heads and schedule from the original release
- `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`: the original licence and notice

The text encoder is the one from MiniMax-H3 (Qwen3-VL-32B); Phosphene's H3 install already includes it.

## Licence

MiniMax-H3-Image is licensed under the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement, Copyright (c) 2026 MiniMax. All Rights Reserved. The full licence is in `LICENSE`, and it applies to these files and to anything you make with them, including the Acceptable Use Policy in its Exhibit A. The licence does not cover the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea or the United States of America.

The transformer and decoder files here were modified from the original (8-bit quantisation, precomputed timestep projections); each modified file says so in its metadata.

Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image (MiniMax). Pictures made with this model are AI-generated; please label them when you publish them.

# MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-GGUF

GGUF conversions of [lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA).
The model rewrites user requests into structured MiniMax-H3 video and audio prompts.
These are complete model weights with a separate vision projector. Load the language
file with `-m` and the projector with `--mmproj`.

**Tasks:** Ref2VA with ordered image references, sampled video frames and explicit audio descriptions.

**Output:** `subject_definitions`, `summary`, `retention_analysis`, `detailed_description`, `overall_soundscape`, `non_diegetic_music`.

## Files

| File | Download size | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| [MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-Q5_K_M.gguf](MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-Q5_K_M.gguf) | 19.231 GB | Q5_K_M |
| [MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-Q4_K_M.gguf](MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-Q4_K_M.gguf) | 16.547 GB | Q4_K_M |
| [mmproj-MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-F16.gguf](mmproj-MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-F16.gguf) | 0.928 GB | Vision projector, F16 |

Sizes are decimal GB of files on disk. Runtime memory also includes the context,
vision processing and backend allocations. Both quantizations use the same F16
projector extracted from this checkpoint.

`conversion.json` records source/output SHA-256 hashes and the conversion tools.
The BF16 control used for validation is not required to run these files.

## ComfyUI

Install [MiniMax-H3 Prompt Rewriter](https://github.com/pytraveler/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-ComfyUI)
and add **MiniMax-H3 Qwen Rewriter** with **Qwen Rewriter Options**. Choose this
checkpoint in **Model list**, or put the model and projector together under
`ComfyUI/models/LLM/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-GGUF/` for local discovery.

The node provides input checkboxes, the ordered reference strip, **+ instr**,
aspect ratio, duration, bypass/repeat and the prompt library. Its `references`
output carries the original enabled conditioning to Reference Slots or Reference
Encode. Select a task supported by this checkpoint.

## llama.cpp

Use a build that supports `qwen35` and its Qwen3-VL vision projector. Conversion
used llama.cpp commit `cb26014d965036f0eacdab7387b222d28d36b9e6` (`b10310`).

```bash
hf download pytraveler/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-GGUF --include '*Q5_K_M.gguf' 'mmproj-*.gguf' --local-dir .
llama-server -m MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-Q5_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA-F16.gguf --jinja \
  --ctx-size 32768 --n-gpu-layers 999 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081
```

Supply the matching official writing guide and task request, as in the
[upstream inference example](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA/blob/ca617d2f9bf7ec98818a7e536a7817c01ae9bcda/post_vllm.py).
Image parts must stay interleaved with their labels. Video references are sampled
images with source timestamps. The ComfyUI node builds this request automatically.

The upstream defaults are `temperature=0.7`, `top_p=0.8`, `top_k=20` and
`max_tokens=16384`, with thinking enabled. A smaller budget can be used with
thinking disabled through `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`.

**Audio:** this checkpoint has no audio encoder. Provide an explicit description
of the reference sound. The original Ref2VA helper labels audio but does not send
its waveform; these conversions do not add a hearing capability.

## Validation

Q5_K_M and Q4_K_M loaded on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 and returned all six Ref2VA sections from an image reference. The original SFT also completed a smoke test in NF4. Exact settings, timings and H3 findings are recorded in validation.json.

Quantization changes the weights and can change the wording. A successful smoke
test checks loading, media input and output structure; it is not a quality score.

Source: [lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA at ca617d2f9bf7ec98818a7e536a7817c01ae9bcda](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA/tree/ca617d2f9bf7ec98818a7e536a7817c01ae9bcda).

directory. `llama-quantize` pr

**Tasks:** T2VA, I2VA, L2VA and FL2VA. Use first/last frames in the order required by the task.

**Output:** `integrated_multimodal_description`, `overall_soundscape`, `non_diegetic_music`, plus frame alignment for image tasks.

## Files

| File | Download size | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| [MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-Q4_K_M.gguf](MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-Q4_K_M.gguf) | 5.629 GB | Q4_K_M |
| [MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-Q5_K_M.gguf](MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-Q5_K_M.gguf) | 6.468 GB | Q5_K_M |
| [mmproj-MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-F16.gguf](mmproj-MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-F16.gguf) | 0.918 GB | Vision projector, F16 |

Sizes are decimal GB of files on disk. Runtime memory also includes the context,
vision processing and backend allocations. Both quantizations use the same F16
projector extracted from this checkpoint.

`conversion.json` records source/output SHA-256 hashes and the conversion tools.
The BF16 control used for validation is not required to run these files.

## ComfyUI

Install [MiniMax-H3 Prompt Rewriter](https://github.com/pytraveler/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-ComfyUI)
and add **MiniMax-H3 Qwen Rewriter** with **Qwen Rewriter Options**. Choose this
checkpoint in **Model list**, or put the model and projector together under
`ComfyUI/models/LLM/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-GGUF/` for local discovery.

The node provides input checkboxes, the ordered reference strip, **+ instr**,
aspect ratio, duration, bypass/repeat and the prompt library. Its `references`
output carries the original enabled conditioning to Reference Slots or Reference
Encode. Select a task supported by this checkpoint.

## llama.cpp

Use a build that supports `qwen35` and its Qwen3-VL vision projector. Conversion
used llama.cpp commit `cb26014d965036f0eacdab7387b222d28d36b9e6` (`b10310`).

```bash
hf download pytraveler/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-GGUF --include '*Q5_K_M.gguf' 'mmproj-*.gguf' --local-dir .
llama-server -m MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-Q5_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA-F16.gguf --jinja \
  --ctx-size 32768 --n-gpu-layers 999 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081
```

Supply the matching official writing guide and task request, as in the
[upstream inference example](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA/blob/ea2a677e0597831a992a400224d98dde4c405fe6/post_vllm.py).
Image parts must stay interleaved with their labels. Video references are sampled
images with source timestamps. The ComfyUI node builds this request automatically.

The upstream defaults are `temperature=0.7`, `top_p=0.8`, `top_k=20` and
`max_tokens=16384`, with thinking enabled. A smaller budget can be used with
thinking disabled through `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`.

**Audio:** this checkpoint has no audio encoder. Provide an explicit description
of the reference sound. The original Ref2VA helper labels audio but does not send
its waveform; these conversions do not add a hearing capability.

## Validation

Q5_K_M and Q4_K_M loaded on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 and returned the task sections from image references. The original SFT also completed a smoke test (BF16 for 9B, NF4 for 27B). Exact settings, timings and H3 findings are recorded in validation.json.

Quantization changes the weights and can change the wording. A successful smoke
test checks loading, media input and output structure; it is not a quality score.

## Conversion and source

Source: [lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA at ea2a677e0597831a992a400224d98dde4c405fe6](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.5-9B-FL2VA/tree/ea2a677e0597831a992a400224d98dde4c405fe6).
The official `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` produced a BF16 language-model control with
`--no-nextn` and an F16 vision projector with `--mmproj` from the same SFT
directory. `llama-quantize` produced Q5_K_M and Q4_K_M language files. The vision
projector was kept at F16; no additional LoRA is needed.

The writing guides are fetched from their original source by the node and are
not redis

# PGH MiniMax-H3 HOT3D ControlNet

日期：2026-10-24

- 模型：MiniMax-H3 FL2VA 的 Fun-ControlNet-Union 分支（5 个注入块，3.40B 参数）从 PAI 权重全量继续训练，同时训练 DiT LoRA（rank 32，`attn.qkv_proj, attn.out_proj, mlp.fc1, mlp.fc2`）。
- 控制输入：物理通道图，打包成一个 RGB 视频：R = 深度（近亮远暗），G = 手 255 / 物体 128 / 背景 0，B = 接触强度。
- 数据：HOT3D train_aria 全部 1516 个 clip 渲染的（真实视频, 通道图）配对，1441 训练 / 75 验证；832×480，24 fps，124 帧。视频无音频，音频损失权重为 0。
- 训练：5 个 epoch，LR 1e-4，AdamW（weight decay 0.01），有效 batch 8（4 卡 × 梯度累积 2）。
- 配置：4×H200，BF16，DeepSpeed ZeRO-2，梯度检查点开启，DiffSynth-Studio 6b3c254；每个 epoch 约 66 分钟，峰值显存约 110 GB/卡。
- 状态：训练完成；尚未用训练后的权重做推理评测。

## 文件

每个 epoch 两个文件，sha256 见 `training_config.json`：

| epoch | ControlNet | DiT LoRA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `epoch-0-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-0-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 1 | `epoch-1-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-1-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 2 | `epoch-2-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-2-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 3 | `epoch-3-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-3-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 4 | `epoch-4-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-4-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |

## 加载

ControlNet 是 DiffSynth 的内部格式（q/k/v 已融合为 `qkv_proj`），不是 PAI 原始格式。先照常加载 PAI ControlNet（经 DiffSynth 转换），再用这里的权重覆盖；开启显存管理时 norm 层的键名会多一层 `.module.`，需要映射：

```python
import torch
from diffsynth import load_state_dict

# pipe = MiniMaxH3Pipeline.from_pretrained(..., model_configs=[...,
#     ModelConfig(model_id="PAI/MiniMax-H3-Fun-Controlnet-Union", origin_file_pattern="MiniMax-H3-Fun-Controlnet-Union.safetensors", **vram_config)])
trained = load_state_dict("epoch-4-controlnet.safetensors", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cpu")
names = {k: k.replace(".module.", ".") for k in pipe.controlnet.state_dict()}
pipe.controlnet.load_state_dict({k: trained[v] for k, v in names.items()}, assign=True)
pipe.load_lora(pipe.dit, "epoch-4-lora.safetensors")
```

首帧条件（FL2VA 关键帧）与 ControlNet 同时使用时需要 DiffSynth 的一行补丁。代码、补丁和数据渲染见 the PGH code repository (private) 的 `cvm-physics-proxy` 分支（`scripts/cvm_hand/`，`scripts/reproduce/run_h3_scenarios.py`）。

# SadikAI Video — Wan 2.2 I2V (14B) Fast ⚡

![SadikAI Video — Wan 2.2 I2V Fast](https://huggingface.co/SadikNawazAI/sadik-ai-video-wan2.2-fast/resolve/main/cover.jpg)

**SadikAI Video** is the video branch of [SadikAI](https://huggingface.co/SadikNawazAI), a project by **Sadik Nawaz**.

This repository packages a **fast, ComfyUI-ready build** of
[Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B)
accelerated with the **LightX2V 4-step LoRAs**. It turns one image plus a text
prompt into a short video in **4 sampling steps** instead of the usual 20+.

> **Honest note:** this is a **repackaged fast build**, not a SadikAI
> fine-tune. The base weights and LoRAs are the official Apache-2.0 releases.
> A SadikAI LoRA fine-tune is planned for a future version — read the
> [fine-tune plan](FINE_TUNE.md). Full credit to Wan-AI, LightX2V and
> Comfy-Org — see [License & attribution](#license--attribution).

## What's inside

| Folder | File | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `diffusion_models/` | `wan2.2_i2v_high_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors` | 13.31 GiB |
| `diffusion_models/` | `wan2.2_i2v_low_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors` | 13.31 GiB |
| `loras/` | `wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_high_noise.safetensors` | 1.14 GiB |
| `loras/` | `wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_low_noise.safetensors` | 1.14 GiB |
| `text_encoders/` | `umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors` | 6.27 GiB |
| `vae/` | `wan_2.1_vae.safetensors` | 242 MiB |

**Total: ~35.4 GiB.** Everything a ComfyUI Wan 2.2 I2V Fast workflow needs.

## Quick start (ComfyUI)

### 1. Download

```bash
hf download SadikNawazAI/sadik-ai-video-wan2.2-fast --local-dir SadikAI-Video-Fast
```

Or download only the files you need from the **Files** tab.

### 2. Put them in the right folders

```text
ComfyUI/models/
├── diffusion_models/
│   ├── wan2.2_i2v_high_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors
│   └── wan2.2_i2v_low_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors
├── loras/
│   ├── wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_high_noise.safetensors
│   └── wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_low_noise.safetensors
├── text_encoders/
│   └── umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors
└── vae/
    └── wan_2.1_vae.safetensors
```

### 3. Load the workflow

Download [`workflows/sadik-ai-video-wan2.2-i2v-fast.json`](workflows/sadik-ai-video-wan2.2-i2v-fast.json)
and drag it into ComfyUI.

Also copy
[`workflows/video_wan2_2_14B_i2v_input_image.jpg`](workflows/video_wan2_2_14B_i2v_input_image.jpg)
into `ComfyUI/input/` so the example image loads, or simply upload your own
image in the **Load Image** node.

### 4. Generate

1. Load your image.
2. Write a prompt describing the motion and camera move.
3. Press **Run**.

The example prompt from the official template:

> The white dragon warrior stands still, eyes full of determination and
> strength. The camera slowly moves closer or circles around the warrior,
> highlighting the powerful presence and heroic spirit of the character.

## Recommended settings

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Steps | **4** |
| CFG | **1.0** |
| Sampler | **euler** |
| Scheduler | **simple** |
| Shift | **5.0** |
| Frames | **81** (≈5 s at 16 fps) |
| Resolution | 640×640, 832×480, or 1280×720 |
| LoRA strength | 1.0 on both high- and low-noise LoRAs |

The high-noise model handles the first 2 steps and the low-noise model the last
2 steps; the workflow wires this automatically with two `KSamplerAdvanced`
nodes.

### Prompt tips

- Describe **motion**, not just the scene: "she turns her head slowly",
  "the camera pushes in", "hair moves in the wind".
- Keep the first frame close to your input image; Wan 2.2 I2V works best when
  the prompt agrees with the photo.
- 81 frames is the standard 5-second clip. Longer clips need more VRAM and time.

## Hardware

- Official ComfyUI benchmark: **~97 s** for a 640×640 clip on an **RTX 4090
  24 GB** with fp8_scaled + 4-step LoRAs.
- **24 GB VRAM** recommended; 32 GB+ is comfortable.
- **CPU-only is not supported.** Use a cloud GPU if your PC has no NVIDIA card.
- ComfyUI can offload to system RAM, but generation will be much slower.

# P-H3-Image Prompt Upsampler — Heretic

Heretic-modified versions of the [P-H3-Image prompt upsampler](https://huggingface.co/PrunaAI/P-H3-Image-Comfy), provided as ComfyUI single-file checkpoints in INT8 ConvRot and W4A8 formats. The upsampler is based on [Qwen3.5-9B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B). It turns a short image request into a fuller prompt for P-H3-Image text-to-image generation or an edit brief for image editing. It is **not** the P-H3-Image diffusion model or its main image text encoder.

## Files

| File | Format | Local file size |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `p-h3-image_prompt_upsampler_heretic_int8_convrot.safetensors` | INT8 ConvRot | 11.46 GB |
| `p-h3-image_prompt_upsampler_heretic_w4a8.safetensors` | W4A8 | 7.46 GB |

Choose one file for a workflow. These are alternative quantizations of the Heretic-modified upsampler, not separate prompt stages. The listed sizes are the files on disk, in decimal GB; they are not measured peak VRAM requirements.

## What was changed

The prompt upsampler was modified with [Heretic](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic), using the default refusal-suppression configuration and the ARA (Arbitrary-Rank Ablation) modifier. The selected result is **Trial 424**, from a 450-trial optimization run.

### Heretic evaluation results

| Measure | Original model | Selected Trial 424 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Refusals on Heretic's harmful-behavior evaluation prompts | 95/100 | 6/100 |
| KL divergence on Heretic's harmless Alpaca prompts | 0 (baseline) | 0.0069 |

Heretic's log reports 100 prompts for each evaluation measure and 400 prompts per category for optimization. These are Heretic's internal selection metrics, not independent safety, prompt-quality, or image-quality benchmarks. The results describe this evaluation run and do not guarantee how the model will respond to other prompts. The original source includes 450 optimization trials; Trial 424 was selected from the resulting Pareto-optimal options.

## Use in ComfyUI

1. Put either safetensors file in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` and refresh ComfyUI's model list.
2. Open a current [P-H3-Image ComfyUI workflow](https://huggingface.co/PrunaAI/P-H3-Image-Comfy/tree/main/workflows).
3. In the **Load CLIP** node used for the *prompt upsampler*, select this file and keep the loader type set to `minimax`. This is separate from the Load CLIP node for P-H3-Image's main text encoder.
4. Keep the upsampler's **Generate Text** output connected to the prompt input of the P-H3-Image conditioning node, as in the upstream workflow.

For text-to-image, the upstream workflow supplies a short request with an aspect ratio, for example:

```text
Aspect ratio: 1:1
Request: A candid street photograph of a rainy market at dusk.
```

For image editing, use the upstream edit workflow's image inputs and request format. The upsampler does not generate images by itself; the P-H3-Image diffusion model, main text encoder, VAE, and conditioning workflow are separate downloads.

## Limitations

- Heretic's default settings aim to reduce refusals; they do not guarantee that every request will be accepted or that an expanded prompt will preserve every detail of the request.
- Prompt expansion can add or alter scene details. Review the generated prompt before relying on exact text, identity, or edit instructions.
- Quantization can change generated text. Neither file has a published comparison against the original BF16 upsampler in this release.
- No performance, VRAM, safety, or image-quality benchmark is claimed for these modified files.

## Provenance and license

The source component is the prompt upsampler in [PrunaAI/P-H3-Image-Comfy](https://huggingface.co/PrunaAI/P-H3-Image-Comfy), which is based on Qwen3.5-9B. [Pruna AI's model card](https://huggingface.co/PrunaAI/P-H3-Image) identifies the prompt upsampler as Apache 2.0 licensed. The **P-H3-Image diffusion model** has separate MiniMax H3 Community License terms. This card's Apache 2.0 metadata applies to the prompt upsampler files in this repository, not to the full image model.

# MiniMax H3 Image — GGUF Quantizations
**Low-VRAM GGUF quantizations of MiniMax H3 Image, by [Rebel AI](https://huggingface.co/realrebelai).** This repository provides quantized versions of MiniMax H3 Image, designed to reduce model storage and memory requirements while preserving image generation quality. The quantizations are produced from a pruned BF16 checkpoint using mixed-precision GGUF conversion. ## Available Quantizations | Format | Description | |---|---| | Q2_K | Maximum compression, lowest memory requirements | | Q3_K_M | Lightweight option balancing size and quality | | Q4_K_M | Recommended balance of quality and compression | | Q5_K_M | Higher precision with reduced quantization loss | | Q6_K | Quality-focused quantization | | Q8_0 | Highest precision in the standard quantized ladder | *Availability depends on the files uploaded to this repository. Individual formats may require additional compatibility testing.* ## Quantization Details - **Source:** MiniMax H3 Image, pruned BF16 checkpoint - **Container:** GGUF - **Method:** Mixed-precision weight quantization - **Target:** ComfyUI with GGUF support - **Focus:** Lower memory requirements and accessible local image generation Selected sensitive tensors are preserved at higher precision to help minimize quality degradation. ## ComfyUI Installation 1. Install [ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF). 2. Download your preferred GGUF quantization from the **Files and versions** tab. 3. Place the GGUF file in: `ComfyUI/models/unet/` 4. Load the model using the appropriate GGUF loader and a compatible MiniMax H3 Image workflow. **Note:** GGUF support depends on the loader implementation and model architecture. Compatibility should be verified for your specific ComfyUI setup. ## Recommended Format **Q4_K_M** is the recommended starting point for users seeking a practical balance between compression and image quality. For systems with more available memory, Q5_K_M, Q6_K, and Q8_0 offer progressively higher weight precision. Actual VRAM usage depends on resolution, workflow, offloading configuration, and supporting model components. ## Credits - **Original model:** MiniMax - **GGUF quantizations:** [Rebel AI](https://huggingface.co/realrebelai) - **ComfyUI-GGUF:** [city96](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF) ## License These quantizations are derivative works of MiniMax H3 Image. Usage and redistribution remain subject to the applicable original model license and any additional authorization requirements. Please review the original model's licensing terms before commercial use or redistribution. --- **Created by Rebel AI** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/realrebelai) · [YouTube](https://youtube.com/@realrebelai) · [X / Twitter](https://x.com/realrebelai)

# MiniMax-H3-Image FP8 for Paiton on RDNA4

FP8 weights of [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) for the Paiton native runtime
on one AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32 GB). Use them with the container in
[Eliovp-BV/paiton-vllm-plugin](https://github.com/Eliovp-BV/paiton-vllm-plugin) under `models/MiniMax-H3-Image`, which
downloads this repository on its first start.

These are runtime weights for Paiton, not a general FP8 checkpoint. They are stored in our own container formats:
the transformer modulation (AdaLN) is precomputed into tables for the fixed 6-step schedule, and the projection
layouts are reordered for the Paiton kernels. Only the Paiton image for the R9700 (gfx1201) loads them; diffusers,
vLLM-Omni and ComfyUI cannot. That is why the name ends in RDNA4.

MiniMax-H3-Image is MiniMax's 33B image model for text to image and image editing with up to 16 reference images, at
4 to 16 MP and 6 sampling steps. With these weights it runs on a single 32 GB R9700.

## Speed

| Request | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| text to image, 2048 x 2048 | 6.9 s |
| text to image, 1024 x 1024 (made at 2048 x 2048, then resized) | 7.1 s |
| text to image, 4096 x 4096 | 33.4 s |
| edit, 4096 x 4096, one 1024 x 1024 reference | 39.9 s |
| edit, 4736 x 3552, one 4736 x 3552 reference | 50.1 s |
| edit, 4096 x 4096, two references | 66.9 s |
| edit, 4096 x 4096, three references | 88.5 s |

Server time per request, from the HTTP request to the finished PNG, with a warm server in the Paiton container on
11 Nov 2026. It includes the text encoder, all 6 steps, the VAE decode and PNG encoding. The 2048 and 4096
text-to-image rows are rounded from three runs each (6.87 to 6.99 s and 33.40 to 33.44 s); the other rows are one
run each. The card ran at its 300 W power limit
and used at most 27.6 GiB of its 32 GB.

# Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 LowRankMod

[Qwen-Image-Edit-2511](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511) with its AdaLN modulation layers replaced by one shared low-rank projection (rank 128) and small per-layer heads. This shrinks the modulation layers from 6.8B params to 284M, and the output stays as close to the original as bf16 rounding allows.

**These files need the custom loader [ComfyUI-QwenImage-LowRankMod](https://github.com/sab76/ComfyUI-QwenImage-LowRankMod).** The built-in Load Diffusion Model node can't load them.

## Files

| File | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen_image_edit_2511_int8_convrot_lowrankmod_r128.safetensors` | 14.8 GB | int8 convrot (original int8 convrot: 20.5 GB) |
| `qwen_image_edit_2511_int8_convrot_lowrankmod_r128_lightning8s.safetensors` | 14.8 GB | int8 convrot, [Lightning 8-step V2.0](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning) LoRA baked in |
| `qwen_image_edit_2511_lowrankmod_r128.safetensors` | 28.4 GB | bf16 (original bf16: 40.9 GB) |

The modulation factors are stored in fp32 in every file. The int8 files need a recent ComfyUI with mixed-precision quantization support.

## Usage

1. Install [ComfyUI-QwenImage-LowRankMod](https://github.com/sab76/ComfyUI-QwenImage-LowRankMod) into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/`.
2. Put a file in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`.
3. Swap **Load Diffusion Model** for **Load Qwen-Image (Low-Rank AdaLN)**. Text encoder, VAE and the rest of the Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 workflow stay the same. For the Lightning file, use 8 steps and CFG 1.

## Accuracy

Modulation error vs exact fp32 math, held-out timesteps (relative to each layer's variation over timesteps):

| | dense bf16 | rank 128, fp32 factors |
|---|---|---|
| Average | 1.008% | 1.008% |
| Worst layer | 1.094% | 1.094% |
| `t = 0` (reference images) | 0.196% | 0.196% |

## Limitations

- LoRAs that target `img_mod`, `txt_mod` or `norm_out.linear` don't apply. Attention and MLP LoRAs work.

## Credits

- Base model: [Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511) (Apache-2.0).
- Lightning LoRA: [lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning) (Apache-2.0).
- Compression method based on [bluvoll/ComfyUI-MageFlow-Compressed](https://github.com/bluvoll/ComfyUI-MageFlow-Compressed).

# Fizgig MiniMax-H3-Image Training Adapter

A training adapter for [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), made for [Fizgig](https://github.com/shootthesound/Fizgig). Keep it on, frozen at strength 1.0, while you train a LoRA on MiniMax-H3-Image, and leave it off when you use the LoRA. Without it, a LoRA trained straight on MiniMax-H3-Image turns faces into caricatures; with it, the LoRA learns the person with photographic skin and the model's own quality.

Fizgig downloads and uses it for you. It's a standard LoRA file (kohya keys, rank 16, attention and MLP of all 50 blocks), so ComfyUI loads it too.

**Training:** real photos plus MiniMax-H3-Image's own renders, about 1 MP, the model's 6 distilled noise levels each through its own head, AdamW at 1e-4, EMA 0.998, 4,000 steps. Only the adapter is published here, not the training images.

# MiniMax-H3-Image (Pruned DiT) — GGUF Quantizations

Quantized **GGUF** weights for **[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)**, converted directly from the structurally pruned BF16 master checkpoint provided by **[Comfy-Org](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image)** (`minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16.safetensors`).

MiniMax-H3-Image is a state-of-the-art **33.1B parameter single-stream Diffusion Transformer (DiT)** designed for ultra-high-resolution text-to-image generation and multi-reference image editing (up to 16 MP / 4096 × 4096) in just **6 distilled sampling steps**.

All GGUFs in this repository have sensitive layers (the 24-channel input patchifier `video_patch_proj`, the 6-step PDD output head `final_layer`, and the low-rank AdaLN modulation basis `adaln_basis` / `adaln_t_table`) strictly preserved in **unquantized FP32** to eliminate quantization noise and grid artifacts.

> **✅ Update — Native Stock ComfyUI-GGUF Support:** All GGUF files in this repository now include the embedded `config` (`pdd_sigmas` 6-step schedule) header metadata and load natively out of the box in stock **ComfyUI-GGUF (`Unet Loader (GGUF)`)** with zero custom scripts or patches required! *(Note: [`minimax_h3_image_gguf_fix.py`](./minimax_h3_image_gguf_fix.py) is kept in the repository solely as an optional fallback for users on older versions of ComfyUI-GGUF).*
---

| File Name | Size | Quant Type | Recommended Hardware / VRAM | Quality / Use Case |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q2_K.gguf`** | **6.88 GB** | `Q2_K` | 8 GB – 10 GB VRAM | Maximum memory savings. Fits easily on consumer laptops & entry GPUs. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q3_K_M.gguf`** | **8.91 GB** | `Q3_K_M` | 12 GB VRAM | High efficiency with significantly lower quantization loss than 2-bit. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q4_K_S.gguf`** | **11.60 GB** | `Q4_K_S` | 12 GB – 16 GB VRAM | Fast 4-bit small variant. Well-balanced footprint. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q4_K_M.gguf`** | **11.60 GB** | `Q4_K_M` | 16 GB VRAM | **Recommended sweet spot.** Near-lossless visual quality for standard GPUs. |
| **`MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned-Q5_K_M.gguf`** | **14.10 GB** | `Q5_K_M` | 16 GB – 24 GB VRAM | Maximum fidelity. Indistinguishable from full BF16. |

## Required Companion Files

MiniMax-H3-Image requires a dedicated **24-channel Image VAE** and the **Qwen3-VL-32B** text encoder (reading layer 50 hidden states).

### 1. Image VAE (24-Channel)
* **Official / Comfy-Org FP16 VAE:** [`minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image/tree/main/vae)  
  *(Place inside `ComfyUI/models/vae/`)*

> **Note:** The Image VAE uses 24 latent channels with a 2D ViT decoder. Do **not** use standard 4-channel SD/Flux VAEs or the 16-channel video VAE from earlier H3 releases.

### 2. Text Encoder (Qwen3-VL-32B)
You can choose between pre-quantized safetensors or standalone GGUF text encoders:

* **GGUF Text Encoders (by Abiray):**
  * **Q4_K_M (14.6 GB):** [`qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q4_K_M.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/Abiray/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3-Q4_K_M.gguf)

* **Official / Comfy-Org Text Encoders:**
  * **NVFP4 / AWQ / BF16:** Available in the [Comfy-Org Text Encoders directory](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image/tree/main/text_encoders) (`qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors` or `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors`)

# **MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-GGUF**

> **MiniMax-H3-Image-PE** is MiniMax's prompt-expansion model for its MiniMax-H3-Image image generator. It is fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B and released in FP4. It turns a short request into a detailed image description and recommends an aspect ratio, returned as JSON with `expanded_caption` and `aspect_ratio`, with the output constrained to a schema by XGrammar. It runs with thinking on by default (`reasoning_effort` xhigh, 4,096 max tokens including reasoning), and the reasoning is returned separately. The weights cover text-to-image expansion. For image editing, the release provides only a task prompt and a message-assembly example for a vision-language model of your choice, and the card says editing support is still under development. In editing mode the model describes what is preserved and changed and returns a `target_aspect_ratio`. It can be served with SGLang (0.5.23 or later) or run locally through the Modular Diffusers blocks, where the FP4 weights use about 19 GiB of GPU memory. The Diffusers path runs activations in bf16, so its outputs differ slightly from the SGLang deployment. The card gives no benchmarks. The license is the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement, not Apache 2.0, and some uses need separate written authorization from MiniMax. The Qwen3.8-27B base is Apache 2.0.

Highly optimized for **NVIDIA Blackwell** hardware accelerators **(e.g., RTX Pro 6000, RTX 50-series, B200, B300)**, offering native hardware-accelerated FP4 Tensor Core speeds and a strong balance of size and performance. |
| MiniMax-H3-Image-PE.mmproj.gguf | mmproj | 931 MB | [Link](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-GGUF/blob/main/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE.mmproj.gguf) | Multimodal projection file. Used for vision/image capabilities. |

Sawfwair's native MLX export of MiniMax-H3-Image for mere.run. This export uses
affine 8-bit weights with groups of 64, exact AdaLN outputs for the six-step PDD
schedule, and the text encoder layers needed for image conditioning. It retains
the original FP32 VAE, sampler, and fused PDD output heads. The weights and
runtime files occupy about 52 GB.

Max covered 2K and 4K text-to-image output with one prompt and seed. The fastest
observed warm 4K request took 229.5 seconds at a 26.1 GiB session peak. The
benchmark report includes the settings, timings, and machine-generated previews.

With a mere.run build that includes the Q8 catalog entry, install and select the
model by ID.

```bash
mere.run model pull image-minimax-h3-q8 --accept-model-license

  --prompt "A detailed studio photograph of a brass camera on a walnut desk." \
  --width 4096 --height 4096 --seed 42 --output ./camera-q8.png
```

For a manually downloaded copy, point the image command at the export folder.

```bash
mere.run image generate --model ./MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-8bit \
```

This is a dynamic 8-bit quantized version of [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) using [SDNQ](https://github.com/Disty0/sdnq) with Hadamard rotation. The transformer and the text encoder are quantized, and the text encoder keeps only the 51 layers the model uses. The VAE is not quantized.

Note: You need SDNQ v0.2.8 or superior and diffusers installed from source.

## Usage

For prompting and recommended sizes, see the [original model card](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image).

## Sample image

The INT8 image above was generated with the following prompt and settings (seed `7`):

```python
import sdnq  # noqa: F401
import torch
from diffusers import ModularPipeline


pipe = ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("OzzyGT/minimax_h3_image_sdnq_dynamic_8bit")
pipe.load_components(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
pipe.to("cuda")

prompt = """a photo of two real cows racing towards the camera and kicking up dirt, one white cow with black patches has a shaggy yellow wig with a small black bowler hat on top, the other cow has brown color and is wearing a chunky knitted grey wool sweater and rectangular glasses, the background is a farm with a white barn and a green hill, with multiple farmers in caps and work jackets standing along both sides of the dirt track watching the race"""

image = pipe(
    prompt=prompt,
    height=3360,
    width=5024,
    generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(7),
    output="images",
)[0]
image.save("minimax_h3_image_int8.png")
```

# Introduction
FlagOS is a fully open-source system software stack for heterogeneous AI chips. It unifies the model–system–chip layers to enable a "develop once, run anywhere" workflow, eliminating the fragmentation among vendor-specific software stacks and substantially lowering the cost of porting AI workloads across accelerators.
In this release, Qwen-Image-2.1 leverages the FlagOS software stack to provide direct multi-chip support. By integrating the Triton-based operator library FlagGems via the Torch-FL plugin, FlagOS enables seamless adaptation of the Diffusers library across chip platforms; the usage experience remains identical to that on NVIDIA, requiring zero code modifications. Inference accuracy across all platforms has been aligned with the official implementation.

### Integrated Deployment
- Out-of-the-box inference scripts with pre-configured hardware and software parameters
- Released **FlagOS-Metax** container image supporting deployment within minutes
### Consistency Validation
- Rigorously evaluated through benchmark testing: Performance and results from the FlagOS software stack are compared against native stacks on multiple public.

# Evaluation Results
## Benchmark Result
| Metrics      | Qwen-Image-2.1-Nvidia-Origin | Qwen-Image-2.1-Metax-FlagOS |
|--------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| T2I-100 (ClipScore) | 33.66                              | 33.75                                  |
| Coco-Image (ClipScore) | 25.34                              | 25.11                              |


### Download Open-source Model Weights
```bash

modelscope download --model FlagRelease/Qwen-Image-2.1-BF16-metax-FlagOS --local_dir /data/Qwen-Image-2.1
```

### Start the Container
```bash
sudo docker run -dit --privileged --ipc=host \
  --entrypoint sleep \
  -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  -v /data/Qwen-Image-2.1:/models/Qwen-Image-2.1:ro \
  -v /data/qwen-image-out:/out \

```
### Start the Server

```bash
# 1. text encoder: prompt -> prompt_embeds + mask + img_mask

# 2. one transformer forward at fixed latents

# 3. VAE decode of fixed latents -> PNG
sudo docker exec qwen-image $RUN infer --device flagos --devices flagos:0 --stage vae

# 4. the whole pipeline: 1024x1024, 40 steps, one PNG
sudo docker exec qwen-image $RUN infer --device flagos --devices flagos:0 --stage full --steps 40

```

## Service Invocation
### Invocation Script

```bash
sudo docker exec qwen-image \

  --device flagos --devices flagos:0 --stage full \
  --prompt "A small cactus with a red flower in a clay pot." \
```

# MiniMax-H3-Image for MLX (4-bit)

A 4-bit quantization of [VisualInference/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-bf16](https://huggingface.co/VisualInference/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-bf16)
(the MLX port of [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)). It runs with the same runner,
[felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx](https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx), and was made with its own exporter.
Text-to-image and image editing, 33B DiT, 6 steps. Unofficial; not affiliated with MiniMax or with the port's author.
Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image.

**Compact, not faithful.** 4-bit drifts from the float32 result 1.1–6.4× further than bf16 does at 2048×2048, and 5–8× at 512×384. In practice the composition can change (pose, framing, small objects), much like a different seed. Every image in the tests below stayed clean, with correct text, and showed no grain or banding. Use it if disk space matters most. Use 8-bit if you want bf16-level fidelity.

| | bf16 (source) | **4-bit (this repo)** |
|---|---|---|
| Download | 94 GB | **31.4 GB** |
| Memory and time, weights streamed from disk | 3.4 GB, 185 s | **2.8 GB, 235 s** |
| Memory and time, weights kept in memory | 40.4 GB, 197 s | **13.5 GB, 204 s** |

All timings are for one 2048×2048 image on an M4 Pro (64 GB), with the weights on an external PCIe SSD. Quantized
matmuls are a little slower than bf16 on Apple Silicon, so the gain here is the download size, not speed. The other
tier is [8bit](https://huggingface.co/cguldogan/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-8bit).

## Usage

Accept the licence on this page, then:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx@31cc9a9173d8013f14f22024b056f64e27fd763c
hf auth login
minimax-h3-mlx @prompt.txt --size 2048x2048 --seed 42 --weights cguldogan/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-4bit -o out.png
minimax-h3-mlx @edit.txt --image ref.png --size 2048x2048 --seed 1234 --weights cguldogan/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-4bit -o edit.png
```

The CLI keeps a quantized tier fully in memory (13.5 GB peak). On a Mac with less memory, stream
it from disk instead (same pixels, about 2.8 GB peak):

```python
from minimax_h3_mlx.pipeline import Pipeline
from minimax_h3_mlx.weights import resolve

pipe = Pipeline(resolve("cguldogan/MiniMax-H3-Image-MLX-4bit"), stream=True)
pipe(open("prompt.txt").read(), height=2048, width=2048, seed=42).image.save("out.png")
```

This commit is the runner version these tiers were tested with. If the original repository is ever unavailable, the same commit is mirrored at [cguldogan/minimax-h3-image-mlx](https://github.com/cguldogan/minimax-h3-image-mlx) (`pip install git+https://github.com/cguldogan/minimax-h3-image-mlx@31cc9a9173d8013f14f22024b056f64e27fd763c`) and archived by [Software Heritage](https://archive.softwareheritage.org/browse/origin/?origin_url=https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx).

The model expects long, detailed English prompts. See the runner's
[examples](https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/tree/31cc9a9173d8013f14f22024b056f64e27fd763c/examples/prompts).

## Quality checks

The method follows the port's own [validation](https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/blob/31cc9a9173d8013f14f22024b056f64e27fd763c/docs/VALIDATION.md).
bf16 inference of this model is chaotic: tiny rounding differences grow over the 6 steps, so bf16 itself does not
reproduce the float32 image. A quantized tier passes if it stays as close to the float32 result as bf16 does. That
float32 result is the MLX port run in float32, which matches PyTorch float32 to 3e-5.
"Drift" is ‖latent − float32 latent‖ / ‖float32 latent‖ after the last step (lower is better).

**2048×2048, seed 42, drift from float32:**

| prompt | bf16 | 8-b

Wuli MiniMax-H3 Turbo — 8-Step Ref2VA and 4/6/8-Step T2VA/FL2VA

   

**Update — 2026-10-23:** Added `ref2va-turbo-8step` for reference-conditioned video generation with audio, along with `run_ref2va.py` and usage examples. Ref2VA is now supported in ComfyUI; load the [8-step Ref workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wuli-art/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-ComfyUI/main/example_workflows/ref2va_8step.json). All variants generate video and audio together. This repository contains four variants: - `turbo-4step/`: four-step LoRA with fused video and audio output projections. - `turbo-8step/`: eight denoising steps. - `turbo-6step/`: six denoising steps. - `ref2va-turbo-8step/`: eight-step reference-conditioned video generation with audio. The 6- and 8-step variants, including Ref, store a complete Diffusers-format transformer. The 4-step variant stores a compact adapter for the official transformer, including a backbone LoRA and fused video/audio output projections. The demo downloads the remaining components from `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`. # Qwen-Image-2.1 text encoder — NF4 pre-quantized

This repository is a **derived** artifact, not an upstream release. It publishes the
`text_encoder/` component of [`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)
as a bitsandbytes NF4 4-bit double-quantized checkpoint, so a Diffusers pipeline can load a
~6 GB encoder instead of the 17.5 GB BF16 shards.

## Provenance

- Source repository: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`
- Source revision: `d26bb61231c349cf6b7896fa83353113880e1ba3`
- Source subfolder: `text_encoder`

| Source shard | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model-00001-of-00004.safetensors` | 4998056552 | `dde00291b5f7fb92013895310a3da0ddba78674df9f10d505d375243dc01fc6f` |
| `model-00002-of-00004.safetensors` | 4915962464 | `9047faccc0a6d98496a52d55f27be1c94a9c259d1e283fbea0128d054a948d42` |

Each shard was loaded with the quantization config below on a CUDA device
(`device_map={"": "cuda"}`, `torch_dtype=bfloat16`) and saved with
`transformers` `save_pretrained`. The `quantization_config` in `config.json` is what makes
a plain `from_pretrained` load this checkpoint already quantized.

## Quantization

```json
{
  "load_in_4bit": true,
  "bnb_4bit_quant_type": "nf4",
  "bnb_4bit_use_double_quant": true,
  "bnb_4bit_compute_dtype": "bfloat16",
  "bnb_4bit_quant_storage": "uint8"
}
```

`processor/` holds the tokenizer and processor files from the same source
revision, so the pair can be used without the full base repository.

## Licence and intended use

The base model is research-only; this derived checkpoint carries the same restriction. It
is published to cut download size for a local, single-GPU research deployment. No weights
were fine-tuned, merged, or altered apart from the quantization above.

unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF uses [Unsloth Dynamic 2.0](https://docs.unsloth.ai/basics/unsloth-dynamic-2.0-ggufs) methodology for SOTA performance. - Important layers are upcasted to higher precision, per tensor, from a measured sensitivity scan. Every file uses the same per-tensor layout as the matching file in [unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-GGUF), built and checked on Turbo itself at its own 8-step schedule. - Run these with [Unsloth Desktop](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth), ComfyUI (ComfyUI-GGUF), stable-diffusion.cpp and more. A GGUF is the denoiser only, so it needs the VAE and the Qwen3-VL text encoder alongside it. Turbo uses the same text encoder and VAE as Qwen-Image-2.1. - VAE: [unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-FP8](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-FP8) `vae/qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors`. Text encoder: [unsloth/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF) `Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf`, the Dynamic 2.0 4-bit rung rather than the uniform `Q4_K_M`. - Turbo is meant for **8 steps at CFG 1** with the sampling schedule it ships (`sample_sigmas` in [model_index.json](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo/blob/main/model_index.json)). Unsloth Desktop applies it automatically.

# FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler GGUF

GGUF conversions of [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup), the prompt upsampler for [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein). It is a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B by Black Forest Labs that expands a short image request (and, for edits, the reference images) into the detailed caption FLUX 3 Image Klein is trained on.

FLUX 3 Image Klein is meant to run with a prompt upsampler in front of it. Short prompts sent to the image model as typed often give generic images and broken poses (backflips, handstands, tangled arms); the upsampled caption describes the pose and every limb explicitly and fixes most of those.

Unsloth Desktop and Unsloth Studio download and run this upsampler automatically for FLUX 3 Image Klein through the "Enhance prompt" option.

## Files

| File | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `flux-3-image-klein-pup-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` | 6.0 GB | Unsloth Dynamic 4-bit, closest to BF16 among the 4-bit files. Default in Unsloth Desktop, about 7.5 GB of VRAM with the mmproj |
| `flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 5.6 GB | 4-bit |
| `flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q6_K.gguf` | 7.4 GB | 6-bit |
| `flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q8_0.gguf` | 9.5 GB | Closest to BF16 |
| `flux-3-image-klein-pup-BF16.gguf` | 17.9 GB | Unquantized |
| `mmproj-F16.gguf` | 0.9 GB | Vision projector, needed for edits with reference images |
| `mmproj-BF16.gguf` | 0.9 GB | Vision projector, BF16 |
| `system_prompts.json` | | Black Forest Labs' system prompts (`t2i`, `i2i`, `t2i_bbox`, `i2i_bbox`), unchanged |

We rendered the hard poses (backflip, handstand, stretch, violin, a group of five on a couch, a hugging couple) on FLUX 3 Image Klein from the Q4_K_M, Q8_0 and original BF16 captions with the same seeds, and saw no anatomy difference between them.

## Quantization

Accuracy against BF16, measured as KL divergence on the upsampler's own captions (96 requests, assistant tokens only):

| File | Mean KLD vs BF16 |
|---|---|
| Q4_K_M | 0.0194 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL | 0.0119 |
| Q6_K | 0.0025 |

The files hold up across request types: the bbox system prompt, Chinese, Japanese, Spanish and German requests, very long and very short requests, and unusual ones (typos, lists, negations, text in the image), and the files loop no more often than BF16. Q4_K_M and Q6_K keep the tensor types, size and speed of the earlier files. UD-Q4_K_XL uses the Unsloth Dynamic layout of Qwen3.5-9B UD-Q4_K_XL, at 6% more bytes than Q4_K_M.

## Usage with llama.cpp

```bash
llama-server -m flux-3-image-klein-pup-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf \
    -ngl 99 -c 16384 --jinja
```

Then send the `t2i` system prompt from `system_prompts.json` and the request as the user message, with thinking off and greedy decoding. These are the settings of the official ComfyUI FLUX 3 Image Klein templates:

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "<t2i system prompt>"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "a gymnast doing a backflip"}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 3584,
  "temperature": 1.0,
  "top_k": 1,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "min_p": 0.0,
  "presence_penalty": 1.5,
  "repeat_penalty": 1.0,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}
}
```

For edits, use the `i2i` system prompt and `presence_penalty` 0, and put the reference images before this text in the user message:

```
Reference images follow in order (the first image, the second image, ...).
User request: <instruction>
Output the caption.
```

Pass the returned caption to FLUX 3 Image Klein as the prompt.

## License

Apache 2.0, the same as the original model. All credit for the model goes to Black Forest Labs; see the [original model card](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup) for training details and intended use.

# DINO-T2I SiT-XL ImageNet-256 checkpoint

This repository contains the final checkpoint from an 80-epoch ImageNet-1K
training run of a SiT-XL latent diffusion transformer conditioned on the
DINOv3 ViT-L/16 CLS representation of an input image.

## Checkpoint

- File: `ep-00080.pt`
- Epoch: 80
- Optimizer step: 200,160
- Size: 7,345,316,757 bytes
- SHA-256: `d072ab59681882a21640319e4a2abeeaf4c020ba0f505f9d58da36af364ffdd3`
- Contents: training model, EMA model, optimizer state, arguments, epoch, and step

## Training setup

- Dataset: ImageNet-1K training split, 1,281,167 images with 25 held out
- Resolution: 256 x 256
- Model: SiT-XL with SwiGLU, RMSNorm, RoPE, and shared adaLN
- Latent autoencoder: FLUX.2 VAE
- Condition: frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 CLS token
- Global batch size: 512 on 4 NVIDIA H200 GPUs
- Precision: BF16
- Epochs: 80
- Learning rate: 2e-4
- EMA decay: 0.9995
- Prediction target: velocity (`v`)
- Path type: linear

The exact launch arguments are included in `args.json`. The source worktree was
based on DINO-T2I commit `af221902608ec61204b57fc8b8f791cd58614ef1`.

## Final held-out result

At step 200,160, the recorded 25-image held-out DINOv3-CLS similarity was
0.61471. This metric measures agreement between the DINOv3 CLS embeddings of
the conditioning images and generated images; it is not an ImageNet FID score.

## Notes

The checkpoint is an image-representation-conditioned generator, not a
standalone text-to-image pipeline. Loading and sampling require the matching
DINO-T2I source code, FLUX.2 VAE, and DINOv3 ViT-L/16 encoder.

# MiniMax-H3-Image for MLX (bf16)

![Six images generated with this port](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/hero.jpg)

[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) for Apple Silicon. It does text-to-image and image editing with a 33B model, at up
to ~16 MP, in 6 steps. Runner: [felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx](https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx). Unofficial and not affiliated with MiniMax.
Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image.

| | |
|---|---|
| Download | 94 GB |
| Memory | 5 GB at 2048×2048, 15 GB at 4736×3552 |
| Time (M4 Pro Mac mini, 48 GB) | 3 min at 2048×2048, 17 min at 4736×3552 |

These are the original bf16 weights, not quantized, in MLX format. They are read from disk one transformer block at a time.

## Usage

Accept the licence on this page, then:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx
hf auth login
minimax-h3-mlx @prompt.txt --size 4736x3552 --seed 42 -o out.png
minimax-h3-mlx @edit.txt --image ref.png --size 4096x4096 --seed 1234 -o edit.png
```

The second command edits `ref.png`; the prompt refers to it as `<Picture 1>`. The model expects long, detailed
English prompts ([examples](https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/tree/main/examples/prompts)). Sizes under 4 MP are generated at 4 MP and scaled
down, as in MiniMax's pipeline.

## Accuracy

- **float32:** output matches the PyTorch reference (diffusers / transformers) to within 3e-5 after 6 steps.
- **bf16:** output differs from the reference about as much as PyTorch's own bf16 backends differ from each other.
- **Seeds:** they match MiniMax's pipeline. Their published seed-42 example gives the same image (left: MiniMax,
  right: this port).

![MiniMax's published seed-42 image next to this port's](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/seed_parity.jpg)

Full measurements: [VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/blob/main/docs/VALIDATION.md).

## Why there is no 8-bit version

On an M4 Pro it gave the same image quality but ran slower: 218 s against 193 s at 2048×2048. Unless streamed, it
also needed 27 GB of memory. Its only advantage would be a smaller download. For quantized weights, see
[mlx-vlm](https://github.com/Neywa-Labs/mlx-vlm), which supports MiniMax-H3-Image at
[8-bit](https://huggingface.co/nativ-community/MiniMax-H3-Image-8bit) and
[4-bit](https://huggingface.co/nativ-community/MiniMax-H3-Image-4bit).

## Examples

Generated at ~16 MP with this repository and shown downscaled. The prompts are in [examples](https://github.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/tree/main/examples/prompts).

| | |
|---|---|
| ![portrait](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/portrait.jpg) | ![poster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/poster.jpg) |
| ![painting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/painting.jpg) | ![street](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/street.jpg) |
| ![landscape](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/landscape.jpg) | ![macro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felix-ab/minimax-h3-image-mlx/main/docs/macro.jpg) |

- The transformer and text encoder are split into one file per block or layer.
- Each block's AdaLN projection is replaced by its precomputed output for the 7 timesteps the sampler uses. The
  results are identical.
- The text encoder ends after layer 49; the model only reads `hidden_sta

# MiniMax H3 Image — low VRAM files for Woovee Studio

Selected, unmodified [Comfy-Org repackaged weights](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image) of the official [MiniMax H3 Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), released November 10, 2026. This is the official six-step image model, distinct from Pruna P-H3-Image and from the H3 video models. Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image.

## Files

| File | Size | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `diffusion_models/minimax_h3_image_pruned_w4a8.safetensors` | 12.55 GB | Pruned image transformer, W4A8 |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors` | 15.69 GB | Original 32B encoder, NVFP4 AWQ |
| `vae/minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors` | 1.17 GB | Image VAE |

Total download: approximately 29.41 GB. Exact upstream revision and SHA256 values are in `source-manifest.json`. These quantized files are copied without modification; the selection and documentation are maintained by Woovee.

## Usage

Use ComfyUI commit `989d93d0d968e704c589ce0146bb18c77f6b50cc` or a compatible later release. Place each file in its matching `ComfyUI/models/` folder. Use `MiniMaxH3ImageConditioning`, `KSampler` with **6 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple**, and the included image VAE. Follow the [official ComfyUI templates](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/image_minimax_h3_image_t2i.json).

Start at **2048 × 2048 (4 MP)** for speed. The upstream model recommends around 16 MP for best detail, at greater memory and compute cost. Describe the entire image in detailed English. For editing, name references `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, etc., and specify both the desired change and what should remain. The Studio's optional prompt enhancement is separate; a large prompt expander is not included in this weight set.

The deployment targets 24–32 GB NVIDIA GPUs with dynamic offloading, loading the text encoder and diffusion model in stages. Runtime overhead, reference count, resolution, GPU kernels and CPU RAM also matter. W4A8/NVFP4 outputs can differ from full precision.

Measured on November 10, 2026 with six steps and 2048 × 2048 output:

| Test | Workflow time | Total handler time | Sampled peak VRAM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX 5090 (32 GB), first text-to-image | 46.90 s | 78.26 s | 28,162 MiB |
| RTX 5090 (32 GB), warm one-reference edit | 23.44 s | 24.25 s | 30,727 MiB |
| RTX 4090 (24 GB), first one-reference edit | 26.35 s | 50.61 s | 22,975 MiB |

All returned valid images; edits changed a blue teapot to green or orange while retaining composition. Workflow time includes component loading and output encoding; total handler time includes model hash verification and server startup. Provider queue and container startup are excluded. These are individual observations, not throughput guarantees or minimum-memory requirements. 24 GB and 32 GB tests passed at 4 MP with one reference. Higher resolutions, four simultaneous references and the other configured GPU types have not been benchmarked.

## License and access

Read the included **MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement**, which differs from the older H3 license. It excludes the EU, UK, Republic of Korea and USA under its standard grant. Separate prior written authorization from MiniMax is required for third-party hosted services or annualized revenue above USD 1 million. This repository distributes weights; it does not grant a hosted-service license or override the upstream terms. Do not use the model outside the license's applicable territory without authorization. The Studio deployment is intended for its owner's private use.

The original model, architecture and license belong to MiniMax; Comfy-Org produced these repackaged quantized files. See `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`.

# MiniMax-H3 Prompt-Rewriter (Qwen3.8-27B)

Prompt-rewriter models built on [Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B):

- [lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-FL2VA](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-FL2VA)
- [lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-Qwen3.8-27B-Ref2VA)

[Qwen3.5-9B](https://huggingface.co/nynxz/Qwen3.5-9B) lora versions can be found here

## Using in ComfyUI

### Option 1 — Native "Generate Text" node (recommended)

Both FL2VA and Ref2VA rewriter loras can be used directly with ComfyUI's native **Generate Text** (`TextGenerateV2`) node — no extra custom node packs are needed.

The [`comfy/`](https://huggingface.co/siraxe/lightx2v_MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter_loras/tree/main/comfy) directory of this repo contains everything for this setup:

- **Loras** (converted for the native node's `LoadLoraTextEncoder` loader):
  - `lightx2v_minimax_h3_FL2VA_PR-Q3.8-27B_rank32_bf16_comfy.safetensors`
  - `lightx2v_minimax_h3_Ref2VA_PR-Q3.8-27B_rank32_bf16_comfy.safetensors`
- **Example workflow**: [`comfy/H3_FL2VA_prompt_gen_27B_9B.json`](https://huggingface.co/siraxe/lightx2v_MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter_loras/blob/main/comfy/H3_FL2VA_prompt_gen_27B_9B.json)

The workflow loads the Qwen3.8-27B text encoder with `CLIPLoader` (e.g. `qwen3.8_27b_w4a8.safetensors`), attaches the lora through **Load Lora (Text Encoder)** (`LoadLoraTextEncoder`), and runs prompt generation in **Generate Text** (`TextGenerateV2`). A switch also lets you flip between the 27B and a 9B encoder variant.

The loras are converted on the fly during runtime, so just point the loader at the `.safetensors` file.

### Option 2 — ComfyUI-QwenVL nodes

These models can also be used with the [ComfyUI-QwenVL](https://github.com/siraxe/ComfyUI-QwenVL) (separate branch with changes) nodes as prompt enhancers via the **QwenVL (GGUF)** node, or any other LLM lora loaders.

An example workflow is available here: [Q3.8_27B_H3_promt_enhance.json](https://github.com/siraxe/ComfyUI-QwenVL/blob/main/example_workflows/Q3.8_27B_H3_promt_enhance.json).

# MiniMax-H3-Image GGUF

Quantized GGUF builds of [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image),
made for ComfyUI. Tested on an RTX 5060 Laptop 8GB.

| File | Size | 512x512 / 6 steps |
|---|---|---|
| `minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16-Q3_K_M.gguf` | 8.81 GB | ~60 s |
| `minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16-Q4_0.gguf` | 14.22 GB | ~80 s |

(bf16 original: 40.2 GB, ~110 s)

## What else you need

- `text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors` (from [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image)) — 27 GB.
  A Qwen3-VL-32B file whose keys start with `model.language_model.` / `model.visual.`
  must be renamed to `model.` / `visual.`, otherwise ComfyUI detects it as the 8B model
  and fails with `5120 vs 4096`.
- `vae/minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors` — the **image** VAE, 1.09 GB.
  Do not use the video VAE.

## ComfyUI workflow

```
UnetLoaderGGUF          -> gguf\minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16-Q3_K_M.gguf
CLIPLoader              -> qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors, type = minimax
VAELoader               -> minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors
MiniMaxH3ImageConditioning   (clip + vae + prompt + width + height)
        -> positive, LATENT
KSampler                -> steps 6, cfg 1.0, euler, simple
        negative also comes from the same positive output (cfg 1 ignores it)
VAEDecode               -> SaveImage
```

## Gotchas

1. Use `MiniMaxH3ImageConditioning`, **not** `PH3ImageConditioning`
   (the latter is a different model, p-h3-image).
2. There is **no** `Empty*LatentImage` node — the latent comes out of the
   conditioning node.
3. `steps = 6`. This is a PDD-distilled model; more steps make it worse. `cfg = 1.0`.
4. Keep only one GGUF loader plugin. The older `ComfyUI-GGUF-Rebel` fork
   rejects `minimax_h3` with `Unexpected architecture type in GGUF file`.

## How these were made

- Q4_0: direct safetensors → GGUF with the `gguf` python library
  (`use_temp_file=True`, which is required or the writer runs out of RAM).
- Q3_K_M: safetensors → F16 GGUF (architecture spoofed as `llama` with the
  required metadata, `rope.dimension_count = 96`), then
  `llama-quantize` with `--tensor-type-file`.

**Important**: 106 tensors must stay unquantized —
`final_layer.*`, `*adaln_proj*`, `adaln_t_table`.
They are the PDD head bank. Quantizing them makes `GGMLTensor.dequantize()`
return `(576, 3024)` instead of `(576, 5376)`, and sampling dies on the first
matmul with `cannot be multiplied (256x5376 and 3024x96)`.

The stock checkpoint is step-distilled for its fixed 6-step PDD schedule; this LoRA lands a finished image in **2 denoising evaluations** on a plain flow-matching grid. This is the file for ComfyUI and other native-naming stacks. - `minimax_h3_image_pdmd_2step_bf16.safetensors` — the **one-file ComfyUI checkpoint**: Comfy-Org's pruned bf16 diffusion model with the pDMD LoRA pre-merged (208 deltas in fp32, base metadata preserved), verified loading and rendering in stock ComfyUI. No LoRA node needed. - `transformer/` — the **official MiniMax-H3-Image transformer pre-converted to diffusers layout** (sharded bf16 `MiniMaxH3Transformer3DModel`), so the stack below loads with a plain `from_pretrained(..., subfolder="transformer")` and no on-the-fly conversion. # **MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF**

> **MiniMax-H3-Image-PE** is MiniMax's prompt-expansion model for its MiniMax-H3-Image image generator. It is fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B and released in FP4. It turns a short request into a detailed image description and recommends an aspect ratio, returned as JSON with `expanded_caption` and `aspect_ratio`, with the output constrained to a schema by XGrammar. It runs with thinking on by default (`reasoning_effort` xhigh, 4,096 max tokens including reasoning), and the reasoning is returned separately. The weights cover text-to-image expansion. For image editing, the release provides only a task prompt and a message-assembly example for a vision-language model of your choice, and the card says editing support is still under development. In editing mode the model describes what is preserved and changed and returns a `target_aspect_ratio`. It can be served with SGLang (0.5.23 or later) or run locally through the Modular Diffusers blocks, where the FP4 weights use about 19 GiB of GPU memory. The Diffusers path runs activations in bf16, so its outputs differ slightly from the SGLang deployment. The card gives no benchmarks. The license is the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement, not Apache 2.0, and some uses need separate written authorization from MiniMax. The Qwen3.8-27B base is Apache 2.0.

> [!NOTE]
> MTP — Speculative Decoding: Yes

> [!NOTE]
Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) GGUF is a specialized GGUF model file format extension that integrates speculative decoding directly into the model weights to significantly accelerate local inference.  Unlike traditional speculative decoding which requires a separate, smaller "draft" model, MTP GGUF files include additional output heads within the main model architecture that predict multiple future tokens in a single forward pass.

## Model Files

| File Name | Quant Type | File Size | File Link | Description |
|-----------|------------|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP.gguf | NVFP4 (with MTP) | 17.9 GB | [Link](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF/blob/main/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP.gguf) | NVFP4 quantization with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP). Highly optimized for **NVIDIA Blackwell** hardware accelerators **(e.g., RTX Pro 6000, RTX 50-series, B200, B300)**, offering native hardware-accelerated FP4 Tensor Core speeds and faster generation. |
| MiniMax-H3-Image-PE.mmproj.gguf | mmproj | 931 MB | [Link](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF/blob/main/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE.mmproj.gguf) | Multimodal projection file. Used for vision/image capabilities. |

---

## Without MTP vs. With MTP Decoding

| Benchmark | Without MTP | With MTP |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Model | [MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-GGUF) | [MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF) ✱ |
| File Size | 17 GB | 17.9 GB |
| Average Generation Speed | 74.94 tokens/s | 112.64 tokens/s |
| Speculative Decoding | Disabled | MTP (`draft_n_max=2`) |
| MTP Tensors | Not Preserved | Preserved |
| Test Runs | 5 | 5 |

### Performance Improvement

| Metric | Result |
|:--|--:|
| Speed Improvement | +37.70 tokens/s |
| Relative Performance Gain | **+50.3%** |
| Generation Speed Multiplier | **1.50×** |

MTP speculative decoding delivers approximately **50.3% faster generation**, increasing throughput from 74.94 to 112.64 tokens/s across five benchmark runs.

---

## NVFP4 Test Run

Tested `MiniMax-H3-Image-PE-NVFP4-MTP.gguf` on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU with `96 GB` of VRAM, using `llama-cli` with full GPU offloading and MTP speculative decoding.

# MiniMax-H3-Image — OrbitQuant W4A8

[OrbitQuant](https://github.com/iamwavecut/OrbitQuant) 4-bit weights for [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), MiniMax's 33.1B text-to-image and image-editing model that makes images of up to 16 megapixels in 6 steps.
The diffusion transformer and the MiniMax-H3 Qwen3-VL text encoder both run 8-bit activations over 4-bit weights. The 4-bit codes were chosen with GPTQ rounding against calibration prompts that are not in the evaluation set.
The runtime is the official MiniMax-H3-Image modular pipeline of [Diffusers](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/15230) with fused OrbitQuant kernels, and the [ComfyUI-OrbitQuant](https://github.com/iamwavecut/ComfyUI-OrbitQuant) nodes.
The download is 27.5 GB. The original needs 135.4 GB: the 66.3 GB transformer and the 66.7 GB MiniMax-H3 text encoder.

**On one RTX PRO 6000 a 4096×4096 image takes 13.5 s with a 29.8 GiB device peak, and a 2048×2048 image takes 2.4 s. The BF16 original needs 22.4 s and 4.4 s for the same work even when each of its models is resident alone.
