# MiniMax H3 Image (INT6 W6A8 & INT4 W4A8 GPTQ) for ComfyUI

Low-bit GPTQ quantizations of the **MiniMax H3 Image** diffusion transformer, packaged as single files for ComfyUI.

- Original model: [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)
- Official ComfyUI repackage (pruned INT8 ConvRot model, VAE): [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image)

Both files were quantized from the pruned BF16 weights (`minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16.safetensors`) used by the ComfyUI repackage.

## Files

| File | Format | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minimaxh3_image_W6A8_GPTQ.safetensors` | INT6 W6A8, GPTQ | 15.61 GB | Highest quality |
| `minimaxh3_image_W4A8_GPTQ.safetensors` | INT4 W4A8 + W6A8 tail, GPTQ | 12.77 GB | Smallest. Last 20 blocks kept at W6A8 |
| `*_quant_report.json` | — | — | Per-layer quantization reports, for reference only |

**W6A8 GPTQ:** all transformer blocks are stored at 6-bit weights (group size 32) with 8-bit activations.

**W4A8 GPTQ (mixed):** blocks 0–29 are stored at 4-bit weights (asymmetric codebook, group size 16). The **last 20 blocks (30–49) are kept at W6A8** (group size 16). That adds size over a pure 4-bit file but keeps the late blocks, where 4-bit error is largest, close to the W6A8 file.

### Text encoder and VAE

These are not included here. The text encoder is shared with MiniMax H3:

* Text encoder: [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 › text_encoders](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/text_encoders), for example `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors`
* VAE: `vae/minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors` from [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image)

## Model storage paths

```text
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
│   │   ├── minimaxh3_image_W6A8_GPTQ.safetensors
│   │   └── minimaxh3_image_W4A8_GPTQ.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 text_encoders/
│   │   └── qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
│   └── 📂 vae/
│       └── minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors
```

You only need the diffusion model file you plan to use.

Load the diffusion model with ComfyUI's **Load Diffusion Model** node, the same way as the Comfy-Org file. The quantization settings are stored in ComfyUI's native `_quantization_metadata` header, so no extra loader is needed. Requires `comfy-kitchen >= 0.2.37` on ComfyUI v0.38.0 or newer.

## Conversion details

The transformer has 50 blocks (0–49). Each has four large linear layers: `attn.qkv_proj`, `attn.out_proj`, `mlp.fc1` and `mlp.fc2`. These are the layers being quantized. Small, sensitive parts such as embedders, modulation, output layer and norms stay at full precision. Converted with my [ComfyUI-INT8-Fast (fork)](https://github.com/tsolful/ComfyUI-INT8-Fast).

| Setting | W6A8 GPTQ | W4A8 GPTQ |
|---|---|---|
| Weight format | Symmetric INT6 | Asymmetric INT4 codebook, W6A8 on blocks 30–49 |
| Group size | 32 | 16 (both the INT4 and W6A8 parts) |
| Scale dtype | FP8 E4M3 | FP8 E4M3 |
| GPTQ-calibrated layers | 192 | 200 (includes the token refiner) |
| Token refiner | Not quantized | INT8 |
| GPTQ settings | 2 passes, damp 0.02, act-order, sequential | Same |
| Calibration tokens per layer | 75,648 | 75,648 |

### Layer-level improvement from GPTQ

The mean output error per layer is measured against BF16 on the calibration data. GPTQ is compared with plain rounding (RTN) at the same bit width.

| Format | Plain rounding (RTN) | GPTQ | Reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| W6A8 | 0.0190 | **0.0060** | 68 % |
| W4A8 (mixed) | 0.0385 | **0.0113** | 71 % |

GPTQ cuts per-layer error to roughly a third of plain rounding for both files.

### End-to-end error per denoising step

This is the relative RMSE of the full denoiser output vs BF16 at each sampling step (lower is better).

| Step | Sigma | W6A8 GPTQ | W4A8 GPTQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1.000 | 0.035 | 0.040 |
| 1 | 0.968 | 0.086 | 0.070 |
| 2 | 0.888 | 0.043 | 0.051 |
| 3 | 0.750 | 0.029 | 0.031 |
| 4 | 0.534 | 0.011 | 0.013 |
| 5 | 0.233 | 0.004 | 0.004 |
| **Mean** | | **0.035** | **0.035** |

Cosine similarity with BF16 stays at 0.996 or higher at every step for both files.

* **Both files track BF16 closely.** The error is largest in the first, noisiest steps and drops below 1.3 % by step 4.
* **The mixed W4A8 file is almost level with W6A8 end to end** while being 2.8 GB smaller. Keeping the last 20 blocks at W6A8 recovers most of the 4-bit loss.

# MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned — OrbitQuant W4A8

[OrbitQuant](https://github.com/iamwavecut/OrbitQuant) 4-bit weights for [MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned](https://huggingface.co/WaveCut/MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned), the [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) checkpoint without the weights its inference never reads. MiniMax-H3-Image is MiniMax's text-to-image and image-editing model; it makes images of up to 16 megapixels in 6 steps.
The diffusion transformer and the Qwen3-VL text encoder both run 8-bit activations over 4-bit weights. The 4-bit codes were chosen with GPTQ rounding against calibration prompts that are not in the evaluation set.
The transformer is the stock Diffusers `MiniMaxH3ImageTransformer2DModel` of the pruned checkpoint: it computes its AdaLN modulation with the stock forward pass (a one-hot timestep code and 8-column projections, kept in BF16), so this release needs no modulation table.
The runtime is the MiniMax-H3-Image modular pipeline of [Diffusers](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers) with fused OrbitQuant kernels, and the [ComfyUI-OrbitQuant](https://github.com/iamwavecut/ComfyUI-OrbitQuant) nodes.
The download is 27.5 GB, against 95.1 GB for the BF16 pruned checkpoint and 135.4 GB for the original.

**On one RTX PRO 6000 a 4096×4096 image takes 13.6 s with a 29.9 GiB device peak, and a 2048×2048 image takes 2.5 s. The BF16 pruned checkpoint needs 27.6 s and 5.8 s for the same work with all its models on the GPU (92.8 GiB peak). With model offload the release also runs in 23.4 GiB of free device memory (a simulated 24 GB card).**

The [first release](https://huggingface.co/WaveCut/MiniMax-H3-Image-OrbitQuant-W4A8) applies the same recipe to the original checkpoint. On the same machine both releases have the same speed, memory and download size (the chart). This release keeps the stock Diffusers transformer of the pruned checkpoint; the first release replaces the AdaLN projections with a table of their outputs.

# MiniMax H3-Image GGUF

GGUF files of the pruned diffusion transformer of [MiniMax H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), for [stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp) and [Hearthscale](https://hearthscale.com). MiniMax H3-Image is a model for text-to-image and picture editing, up to 16 megapixels, distilled to 6 steps.

The files are converted from `minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16.safetensors` in [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image) with the converter of stable-diffusion.cpp `master-1088-32d516c`. They load in stable-diffusion.cpp from `master-1088`, the first build that reads MiniMax H3-Image, with no patch.

<Gallery />

Every picture above comes from the Q4_K_M file with seed 42, the Q2_K_M text encoder and stable-diffusion.cpp's own `master-1088-32d516c` release build. The edit takes the portrait as its reference.

## Files

| File | Size | Block weights | Graphics memory to hold the whole model | Quality |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q8_0.gguf](minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q8_0.gguf) | 21.4 GB | Q8_0 | 24 GB | Closest to the bf16 weights. |
| [minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q5_K_M.gguf](minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q5_K_M.gguf) | 13.9 GB | Q5_K | 16 GB | Very close to Q8_0. |
| [minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q4_K_M.gguf](minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q4_K_M.gguf) | 11.4 GB | Q4_K | 16 GB | **Recommended.** Lettering and fine detail hold. |
| [minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q3_K_M.gguf](minimax_h3_image_pruned-Q3_K_M.gguf) | 8.8 GB | Q3_K | 12 GB | Softer detail. The smallest file that keeps lettering right. |

With less graphics memory, the weights stream from system memory at each step. Every file runs on a 10 GB graphics card with 32 GB of system memory, at the times below. A 2-bit file is not published: at Q2_K, lettering and detail break.

In every file, the attention and MLP weights of the 50 blocks and of the token refiner take the type in the name. The AdaLN projections stay in F16, the norms and the condition projection in BF16, and the output heads in F32. The input projection is F32, except in the Q8_0 file, where it is Q8_0. # Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo with AtomicChat's abliterated text encoder, IQ8R — radiance container

[Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) with the abliterated Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder
of AtomicChat's [Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Uncensored](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Uncensored-GGUF),
as a single `.rad` container for the [radiance](https://codeberg.org/StillDeadcode/radiance) inference engine
(AMD RDNA4, ROCm).

It replaces [StillDeadcode/radiance-qwen-image-2.1-turbo-uncensored-fp8](https://huggingface.co/StillDeadcode/radiance-qwen-image-2.1-turbo-uncensored-fp8),
with the same eight bits a weight.

## What differs from Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo

Only the conditioning network's language model: the `o_proj` and `down_proj` weights of all 36 layers and the token
embedding, which AtomicChat's abliteration rewrote (scale 0.75, per their GGUF's metadata). The diffusion transformer,
the vision tower and the VAE are the stock Turbo model's.

What that does to pictures is small. The stock pipeline has no content filter, and AtomicChat's own test found no
image outcome changed over 45 prompts; in the FP8 container a picture moved by about as much as the FP8 conversion
moved it (39.7 dB PSNR from the stock container at 1024x1024). The Turbo diffusion transformer itself has no
uncensored fine-tune on Hugging Face.

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `qwen-image-2.1-turbo-uncensored-iq8r.rad` — 16.13 GiB |
| Weights | the conditioning network's (Qwen3-VL-8B) and the diffusion transformer's linears int8 (codes −127..127) with a u8 scale per row and 256 of K under a bf16 scale a row, each 128 of K rotated by the unnormalised Hadamard, round to nearest; the vision tower, the small linears, the norms and the VAE bf16 |
| Activations | int8 under the same rotation (W8A8) |
| Steps | 8, fixed by the model |
| Needs | radiance built from main after 1.17.0: IQ8R at one scale a 256 of K is not in 1.17.0 and comes with the next release |

## Serve

```yaml
# radiance.yaml
server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8000
models:
  qwen-image:
    model: qwen-image-2.1-turbo-uncensored-iq8r.rad
    tp: 2
```

```sh
radiance --config radiance.yaml
```

`tp: 1` serves it on one card. The server speaks OpenAI's Images API: `POST /v1/images/generations` and
`POST /v1/images/edits` (JSON, or multipart with `image` / `image[]` and `mask`, as OpenAI's SDKs send them).
Pictures come back as `b64_json` (png, jpeg or webp; `response_format: url` is refused). Also: `n`, `size`
(`WxH` or `auto` = 2048x2048), `seed`, streaming with `partial_images`, `background: transparent`; edits take
1 to 10 reference pictures and a mask. `/v1/models` lists the model.

On one Radeon AI PRO R9700 a 1024x1024 picture takes 4.5 s (the FP8 container: 4.4 s). From the same noise its
four test pictures are 25.7 dB from the FP8 container's on average (19.6 to 33.2). Not measured against a bf16
container of this model; on Qwen-Image 2.1 itself the same recipe is 32.6 dB from bf16 where FP8 is 28.1.

## How this file was made

```sh
python extract_atomic.py Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1/text_encoder AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Uncensored/text_encoder
rad-convert AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Uncensored --recipe qwen-image-2.1-iq8r.recipe -o qwen-image-2.1-turbo-uncensored-iq8r.rad
```

`extract_atomic.py` (in this repository) reads AtomicChat's BF16 GGUF by HTTP range and writes the 73 tensors that
differ from the stock text encoder as `abliterated.safetensors`, with a `model.safetensors.index.json` that points
those names at it and every other name at the stock shards (linked beside it). `AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Uncensored`

# LTX-2.5, IQ8R — radiance container

[LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers) — video with a synchronized stereo
soundtrack from text, or from text and a first frame — as a single `.rad` container for the
[radiance](https://codeberg.org/StillDeadcode/radiance) inference engine (AMD RDNA4, ROCm). It replaces
[StillDeadcode/radiance-ltx-2.5-fp8](https://huggingface.co/StillDeadcode/radiance-ltx-2.5-fp8), with the
same eight bits a weight.

This is not an official Lightricks release and is not endorsed by Lightricks.

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `ltx-2.5-iq8r.rad` — 36.86 GiB |
| Weights | the Gemma 4 text encoder's, the text connectors' and the diffusion transformer's linears int8 (codes −127..127) with a u8 scale per row and 256 of K under a bf16 scale a row, each 128 of K rotated by the unnormalised Hadamard, round to nearest; the vocoders f32; everything else (the video and audio VAEs, the latent upsampler, the duration head, the diffusion decoder, the small linears and norms) as released, bf16 |
| Activations | int8 under the same rotation (W8A8) |
| Steps | 30 by default (`num_inference_steps`, up to 64), each up to four evaluations of the DiT (classifier-free, spatio-temporal and modality guidance; the defaults are the release's: video 3, 1, 3 with rescale 0.7, audio 7, 1, 3 with rescale 0.7) |
| Needs | radiance built from main after 1.17.0: LTX-2.5 on IQ8R is not in 1.17.0 and comes with the next release |

## Serve

```sh
radiance --model ltx-2.5-iq8r.rad --vision-tower-placement ram
```

LTX-2.5 runs on one card (`--tp` above 1 is refused). The text encoder (13 GiB at eight bits a weight) does not fit a
32 GB card beside the DiT: `--vision-tower-placement ram` keeps it in pinned host memory, read once a
prompt.

The server speaks OpenAI's video API: `POST /v1/videos` queues a job (JSON, or multipart as OpenAI's SDKs
send it), `GET /v1/videos/{id}` reports its progress and `GET /v1/videos/{id}/content` downloads the MP4
(H.264 and 48 kHz stereo AAC).

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "prompt": "A red fox trots through fresh snow at golden hour, snow crunching under its paws",
  "size": "960x544", "seed": 7}'
```

- **`seconds`**: rounded up to steps of 8 frames at 24 a second, 17 to 161 frames. Left out (or `"auto"`),
  the release's duration head chooses the length the prompt implies, as diffusers does when `num_frames`
  is omitted.
- **`size`**: sides multiples of 32 from 256, at most 1920x1088 of area (121 frames at that size), at most
  3:1; 960x544 by default. A frame larger than 960x544 is decoded in diffusers' VAE tiles.
- **`input_reference`**: a first frame (image to video), resized to `size` and put through H.264 at CRF 18
  first, as the release was trained.
- **`decoder`**: `"vae"` (the default) or `"diffusion"`, the release's diffusion decoder: neighbourhood-attention
  stages that upsample the latent, then one diffusion step over pixel patches, a tile at a time with
  diffusers' tiling. Frames up to 960x544 of area (a larger `size` is refused with it). Its weights stay in host memory with `--vision-tower-placement ram`.
- **Guidance**: `negative_prompt` (empty by default), `guidance_scale`, `stg_scale`, `modality_scale`, `guidance_rescale`, and the same prefixed `audio_` for the soundtrack. A scale of 1 (0 for `stg_scale`) drops that evaluation.

On one Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201) at the default 30 guided steps: 5 seconds (121 frames) at 960x544 in 310 to 316 s from the request to the finished video; an FP8 container of the same checkpoint took 306 to 314 s on the same card. The diffusion decoder was not timed again with this container.

The model was trained on long, single-paragraph captions describing the shot, the motion, the light and
the sound; short prompts give generic results.

## How this file was made

The full DiT is `transformer_full/` of the diffusers download, read as the pipeline's transformer, with the scheduler's shifting turned back on as the release's R

# MiniMax-H3-Image int8 + w4a8 hybrid for ComfyUI

`diffusion_models/minimax_h3_image_pruned_int8_w4a8_hybrid.safetensors` is a mixed-precision repack of the
[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image) diffusion model, sized for 16 GB
GPUs. It is a drop-in replacement in the official text-to-image workflow (ComfyUI 0.45.0 or newer).

| Part of the model | Format | Taken from |
|---|---|---|
| Blocks 0-29: `qkv_proj`, `out_proj`, `fc1`, `fc2` | `asym_w4a8_int8` | `minimax_h3_image_pruned_w4a8` |
| Blocks 30-49 and every other tensor | `int8_tensorwise` (ConvRot) | `minimax_h3_image_pruned_int8_convrot` |

The tensors are copied unchanged from the two Comfy-Org files; nothing was requantized. SHA-256:
`ea736af3b44f0f8be32e3ec632e375fea0449a8c0b2e05fe121ede5719a0137b`.

## Why this split

The last 20 blocks are the ones that suffer from 4-bit weights, so they stay int8. Measured against the bf16
model at 2048x2048, 6 steps:

| Model | Size | Output error per step | SSIM to bf16 image |
|---|---|---|---|
| int8 ConvRot (official) | 19.5 GiB | 3.5% | 0.888 |
| **this hybrid** | **14.8 GiB** | **5.2%** | **0.844** |
| w4a8 (official) | 11.7 GiB | 9.1% | 0.767 |

Output error is the relative error of the model's prediction when every variant is fed the bf16 model's own
inputs, averaged over 6 steps and 2 prompts. SSIM is the mean over 6 images (2 prompts, 3 seeds) generated with
the model's default attention.

## Speed

6 steps at 2048x2048 with the official workflow. The smaller files finish sooner because less has to be moved
onto the GPU: on the RTX 5060 Ti that shortens only the load before the first step, on the RTX 4060 Ti (slower
PCIe link) every step is faster too.

| GPU | int8 | hybrid | w4a8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB | 1.86 s/step, 21-23 s total | 1.85 s/step, 16-17 s total | 1.85 s/step, 16 s total |
| RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB | 2.72 s/step, 27-28 s total | 2.33 s/step, 20-21 s total | 2.27 s/step, 19-20 s total |

Totals are the six sampling steps including loading the model onto the GPU.

## Why there is no NVFP4 in it

NVFP4 was tested for every layer type and left out. On this model an NVFP4 layer loses 8-12% of its output on
real inputs, against about 1% for int8 ConvRot and 5-6% for w4a8, and half of that loss comes from NVFP4's 4-bit
activations, so better weight rounding or calibration cannot remove it. The best NVFP4 mix found (calibrated NVFP4
on `qkv_proj`, `out_proj` and `fc1` of blocks 0-29, int8 elsewhere) reached 8.1% output error at 15.5 GiB and only
runs fast on RTX 50 cards.

## Use

Put the file in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models` and select it in the workflow's diffusion model loader. It
uses ComfyUI's int8 kernels only, so it does not need FP4 hardware.

Original model: [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), under the MiniMax
H3 Image community license.

Totals are the six sampling steps including loading the model onto the GPU.

## Why there is no NVFP4 in it

NVFP4 was tested for every layer type and left out. On this model an NVFP4 layer loses 8-12% of its output on
real inputs, against about 1% for int8 ConvRot and 5-6% for w4a8, and half of that loss comes from NVFP4's 4-bit
activations, so better weight rounding or calibration cannot remove it. The best NVFP4 mix found (calibrated NVFP4
on `qkv_proj`, `out_proj` and `fc1` of blocks 0-29, int8 elsewhere) reached 8.1% output error at 15.5 GiB and only
runs fast on RTX 50 cards.

## Use

Put the file in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models` and select it in the workflow's diffusion model loader. It
uses ComfyUI's int8 kernels only, so it does not need FP4 hardware.

Original model: [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), under the MiniMax
H3 Image community license.

# MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned

[MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) without the weights its inference never needs:
135.3 GB → 95.1 GB on disk (transformer, text encoder and VAE). The stock Diffusers and Transformers classes load
it like the original, with no custom code and no `trust_remote_code`. Text-to-image results are bit-identical to the
original on the same GPU; edit results differ by a small margin (PSNR 43.3 dB on the test edit). Every kept tensor is a byte copy of the original;
nothing is quantized or retrained.

![Generation time, GPU memory and checkpoint size](assets/speed_memory_size.png)

![Samples: two text-to-image results, bit-identical to the original, and an edit](assets/samples.jpg)

| | Original | Pruned |
|---|---|---|
| Transformer | 66.3 GB, 33.1B parameters | 40.2 GB, 20.1B parameters |
| Text encoder (Qwen3-VL-32B) | 66.7 GB, 64 decoder layers | 52.5 GB, 51 decoder layers |
| VAE | 2.3 GB | 2.3 GB (unchanged) |

## Usage

```bash
pip install "diffusers @ git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers@875373ac7f5856071e345a3e394c74efccc6b9e6" \
  "transformers>=5.22" accelerate torchvision
```

```python
import torch
from diffusers import ComponentsManager, ModularPipeline

manager = ComponentsManager()
manager.enable_auto_cpu_offload(device="cuda")  # or skip this and call pipe.to("cuda") on a GPU with 96 GB or more

pipe = ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("WaveCut/MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned", components_manager=manager)
pipe.load_components(dtype=torch.bfloat16)

image = pipe(
    prompt="The image is a top-down photograph of ...",
    height=3552,
    width=4736,
    generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(42),
    output="images",
)[0]
```

This is the code of the [original card](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) with another repository
name. Editing: pass `image=reference` (or a list) and refer to the images as `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, ... in the
prompt. The prompting guidance of the original card applies unchanged: long, complete English descriptions;
recommended sizes from 4096×4096 (1:1) to 6272×2688 (21:9).

### Memory modes

`enable_auto_cpu_offload` moves a model off the GPU only when the next one does not fit. On a 96 GB card the pruned
models fit together, so after the first image nothing moves and the run is as fast as with everything on the GPU
(peak 92.7 GiB). For the lowest peak, keep one model on the GPU at a time; set the strategy after loading, because
adding the components resets it to the default:

```python
pipe.load_components(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
manager.set_offload_strategy(lambda hooks, **kwargs: hooks)  # move every other model off the GPU first
```

The peak is then 50-52 GiB, set by the text encoder (48.9 GiB of weights), and each image moves both models over
PCIe: about 72 s at 2048×2048 instead of 5.6 s (see Profiles).

The components also load alone with the stock classes: `MiniMaxH3ImageTransformer2DModel.from_pretrained(repo,
subfolder="transformer")` and `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(repo, subfolder="text_encoder")`.

## What was removed

- **AdaLN projection inputs (13.0B parameters).** Every block projects the timestep embedding to its modulation
  vectors, and the checkpoint samples on a fixed grid: six steps (one output head per step), plus t = 0.999 for the
  reference images of an edit. Seven timesteps need seven input columns, so `adaln_proj.linear` and `norm_out.linear`
  keep 8 of their 2688 input columns (`time_embed_dim: 8` in the config). The new `time_embedder` (16 hidden units)
  turns each grid timestep into a one-hot code, and column k holds the original projection's output for timestep k.
  The stock forward pass then returns the original modulation values exactly; the
  [GitHub repository](https://github.com/iamwavecut/MiniMax-H3-Image-Pruned) explains the construction.
- **Text encoder layers 51-63 and `lm_head`.** The transformer is conditioned on `hidden_states[50]` of the Qwen3-VL
  text encoder, the output of decoder layer 49. Layer 50 stays because the pipeline requires more than 50 layers; with
  51 layers, `hidden_states[50]` is still the output of layer 49. `lm_head` is tied to the input embedding, so loading
  allocates nothing for it.

## Text-to-image and edit

The original model computes the modulation for a step with one timestep row in text-to-image and with two rows (step
and reference) in an edit, and the matrix products round slightly differently in the two cases. The pruned
checkpoint stores one value per timestep: the text-to-image value for the six steps and the edit value for the
reference timestep.

- Text-to-image: bit-identical to the original.
- Edit: not bit-identical. 59,279 of the

# MiniMax-H3-Image-4bit

An MLX checkpoint converted directly from the original floating-point
[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image)
weights. It supports text-to-image generation and native image editing with up to
sixteen ordered reference images. Inference uses MLX on Apple silicon, without
PyTorch or Diffusers.

## Quantization

Eligible linear and embedding layers use **4-bit affine quantization with group
size 64**. Both the diffusion transformer and the Qwen3-VL conditioner are
quantized. The conditioner retains its vision tower for editing.

The VAE, transformer modulation layers, and transformer input/time/output
projections retain their released precision. Normalizations and convolutional
layers also retain their released precision.

| Component | Weight files | Size (GB, decimal) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-VL conditioner | 3 | 14.683 |
| Diffusion transformer | 8 | 37.445 |
| Image VAE | 1 | 2.337 |

The full checkpoint occupies approximately **54.5 GB (50.7 GiB)**, including its
tokenizer, configuration files, and weight indexes. No external image-model
components are required.

## Usage

Requires an `mlx-vlm` version with MiniMax-H3-Image support
([implementation PR](https://github.com/Neywa-Labs/mlx-vlm/pull/2702)). Until that
support is included in your installed release, install the implementation branch:

```sh
python -m pip install -U "git+https://github.com/lucasnewman/mlx-vlm.git@minimax-h3-image"
```

Replace `/path/to/MiniMax-H3-Image-4bit` with the local checkpoint directory or
this repository's Hugging Face ID after upload.

```sh
mlx_vlm.generate --output-modality image \
  --model /path/to/MiniMax-H3-Image-4bit \
  --prompt "A red ceramic teapot beside a white cup on a wooden table by a sunny window" \
  --size 4096x4096 --seed 42 --output teapot.png
```

```python
from mlx_vlm.generate import generate_image, load_image_generation_model

model = load_image_generation_model("/path/to/MiniMax-H3-Image-4bit")
result = generate_image(
    model,
    "A red ceramic teapot beside a white cup by a sunny window",
    width=4096,
    height=4096,
    seed=42,
    output_path="teapot.png",
)
```

For editing:

```sh
mlx_vlm.generate --output-modality image --task edit \
  --model /path/to/MiniMax-H3-Image-4bit \
  --image teapot.png \
  --prompt "Make the teapot in <Picture 1> blue, preserving its shape, the cup, and the lighting" \
  --size 4096x4096 --seed 42 --output blue-teapot.png
```

Reference images are ordered as `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, and so on. Sampling
is fixed at **six steps and guidance 1**. Small output requests are generated on
at least a 2048x2048-equivalent canvas before resizing. The conditioner is
released before diffusion, and the transformer caches fixed-schedule AdaLN
projections so their large weights can be released.

## Prompt expansion

Short prompts are expanded by default with the separately downloaded
[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image-PE)
model. Its released NVFP4 weights are separate from this 4-bit image checkpoint.
Prompt templates and request defaults are embedded in the MLX implementation.

For a detailed caption that is ready for the image model, disable expansion:

```sh
mlx_vlm.generate --output-modality image \
  --model /path/to/MiniMax-H3-Image-4bit \
  --prompt "A realistic still-life photograph of a glossy red ceramic teapot with a curved spout and lid, beside a plain white cup on a warm wooden table next to a sunny window. Soft morning light from the left, detailed glaze and wood grain, a beige wall in the background." \
  --gen-kwargs '{"upsample_prompt":false}' \
  --size 4096x4096 --seed 42 --output teapot.png
```

In Python, pass `upsample_prompt=False` when loading or generating. With
expansion disabled, this checkpoint can run fully offline after downloading.

## Validation

Validated with strict component loading and offline inference on an Apple M5 Max
with 128 GiB unified memory, using MLX 0.32.4. Both checks used seed 42, six steps,
guidance 1, and prompt expansion disabled. The edit used the generated 4K image
as its reference.

| Task | Output resolution | Total elapsed time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Generate | 4096×4096 | 180.1 s |
| Edit | 2048×2048 | 88.4 s |

## License

Weights and prompt templates use the
[MiniMax H3 Image Community License](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image/blob/main/LICENSE).
The reference Diffusers implementation is
[Apache-2.0](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/LICENSE).

# MiniMax-H3-Image fp8 scaled and NVFP4 (ComfyUI)

Two more precisions of the MiniMax-H3-Image diffusion transformer for
ComfyUI, alongside the bf16, int8 ConvRot and w4a8 files in
[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image).
They are drop-in replacements for those: same layout, same loader, same
workflow. GGUF versions are in
[LSDJesus/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/LSDJesus/MiniMax-H3-Image-GGUF).

> **Modified files.** These are quantized versions of MiniMax-H3-Image, made
> from Comfy-Org's `minimax_h3_image_pruned_bf16.safetensors`.
> MiniMax-H3-Image is licensed under the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License
> Agreement, Copyright © 2026 MiniMax. All Rights Reserved. See `LICENSE` and
> `NOTICE`. Among other terms, the license grants rights only outside the
> European Union, the United Kingdom, South Korea and the United States
> (sections I.5 and II), and it includes an acceptable use policy. Read it
> before downloading.

## Files

| File | Format | Size | Runs natively on | Speed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `minimax_h3_image_pruned_fp8_scaled.safetensors` | fp8 e4m3, one scale per weight tensor | 21.0 GB | RTX 40 and RTX 50 | 2.1 steps/s |
| `minimax_h3_image_pruned_nvfp4.safetensors` | NVFP4 (fp4 with fp8 scales per 16 values) | 12.5 GB | RTX 50 and other Blackwell | 3.4 steps/s |

Speed is sampling at 2048×2048 on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. On the same card
Comfy-Org's int8 ConvRot ran 2.6 steps/s and w4a8 2.5. On cards without
native support for a format, ComfyUI still runs it, more slowly.

## Requirements

- **ComfyUI with MiniMax-H3-Image support**, merged on 10 November 2026
  (ComfyUI 0.44).
- The text encoder (`qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq` or `_int8_convrot`) and
  the VAE (`minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16`) from
  [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image).

Put the file in `models/diffusion_models/`, open ComfyUI's **MiniMax H3
Image** template and choose it in Load Diffusion Model.

## What is quantized

The same 200 layers that Comfy-Org quantizes in its int8 and w4a8 files: the
fused `qkv_proj`, `out_proj`, `mlp.fc1` and `mlp.fc2` of the 50 transformer
blocks, 95.8% of the weights. The token refiner, the condition projection,
the adaLN time-curve basis, the patch and output projections and all norms
are kept as in the bf16 source, as are the per-block int8 attention setting
and the `config` metadata with the 6-step PDD schedule.

- **fp8 scaled**: e4m3 weights with one scale per tensor. `mlp.fc2` is tagged
  `full_precision_matrix_mult` (fp8 weights, matrix multiply in bf16), as in
  Comfy-Org's own MiniMax-H3 fp8 files. Its input has outliers that ComfyUI's
  on-the-fly per-tensor fp8 activation scale cannot hold: without the tag the
  render drifted far more than NVFP4 (the subject changed and text was
  misspelled). The other layers quantize their activations on the fly; there
  are no calibrated activation scales.
- **NVFP4**: E2M1 values with an e4m3 scale per block of 16 and one global
  scale per tensor, made with ComfyUI's comfy-kitchen quantizer.

## Quality

One render per file, seed 42, 2048×2048, 6 steps, compared with Comfy-Org's
int8 ConvRot render. Left: whole image; right: a 1:1 crop. A 6-step model
changes its composition a little with any change to the weights, so
differences in pose and layout are normal; look for broken texture and text.

The template's own prompt:

![Comparison on the template prompt](assets/compare_fox.jpg)

A held-out photographic prompt (a fruit market with signs):

![Comparison on a market prompt](assets/compare_market.jpg)

# MiniMax H3 Image — low VRAM files for Woovee Studio

Selected, unmodified [Comfy-Org repackaged weights](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3-Image) of the official [MiniMax H3 Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), released November 10, 2026. This is the official six-step image model, distinct from Pruna P-H3-Image and from the H3 video models. Powered by MiniMax-H3-Image.

## Files

| File | Size | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `diffusion_models/minimax_h3_image_pruned_w4a8.safetensors` | 12.55 GB | Pruned image transformer, W4A8 |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors` | 15.69 GB | Original 32B encoder, NVFP4 AWQ |
| `vae/minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors` | 1.17 GB | Image VAE |

Total download: approximately 29.41 GB. Exact upstream revision and SHA256 values are in `source-manifest.json`. These quantized files are copied without modification; the selection and documentation are maintained by Woovee.

## Usage

Use ComfyUI commit `989d93d0d968e704c589ce0146bb18c77f6b50cc` or a compatible later release. Place each file in its matching `ComfyUI/models/` folder. Use `MiniMaxH3ImageConditioning`, `KSampler` with **6 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple**, and the included image VAE. Follow the [official ComfyUI templates](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/blob/main/templates/image_minimax_h3_image_t2i.json).

Start at **2048 × 2048 (4 MP)** for speed. The upstream model recommends around 16 MP for best detail, at greater memory and compute cost. Describe the entire image in detailed English. For editing, name references `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, etc., and specify both the desired change and what should remain. The Studio's optional prompt enhancement is separate; a large prompt expander is not included in this weight set.

The deployment targets 24–32 GB NVIDIA GPUs with dynamic offloading, loading the text encoder and diffusion model in stages. Runtime overhead, reference count, resolution, GPU kernels and CPU RAM also matter. W4A8/NVFP4 outputs can differ from full precision.

Measured on November 10, 2026 with six steps and 2048 × 2048 output:

| Test | Workflow time | Total handler time | Sampled peak VRAM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RTX 5090 (32 GB), first text-to-image | 46.90 s | 78.26 s | 28,162 MiB |
| RTX 5090 (32 GB), warm one-reference edit | 23.44 s | 24.25 s | 30,727 MiB |
| RTX 4090 (24 GB), first one-reference edit | 26.35 s | 50.61 s | 22,975 MiB |

All returned valid images; edits changed a blue teapot to green or orange while retaining composition. Workflow time includes component loading and output encoding; total handler time includes model hash verification and server startup. Provider queue and container startup are excluded. These are individual observations, not throughput guarantees or minimum-memory requirements. 24 GB and 32 GB tests passed at 4 MP with one reference. Higher resolutions, four simultaneous references and the other configured GPU types have not been benchmarked.

Read the included **MiniMax-H3-Image Community License Agreement**, which differs from the older H3 license. It excludes the EU, UK, Republic of Korea and USA under its standard grant. Separate prior written authorization from MiniMax is required for third-party hosted services or annualized revenue above USD 1 million. This repository distributes weights; it does not grant a hosted-service license or override the upstream terms. Do not use the model outside the license's applicable territory without authorization. The Studio deployment is intended for its owner's private use.

# MiniMax-H3-Image — W4A4

An experimental **W4A4 quantization** of [MiniMax-H3-Image](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image), created using [PotatoForge](https://github.com/bakapotatolord/potatoforge-quantization).

## Why W4A4?

On my **GTX 1660 Super (6 GB)**, W4A8 inference was nearly **4× slower**, which motivated this W4A4 release.

The goal is to improve inference performance on older, resource-constrained GPUs while maintaining reasonable image quality (reasonable for an int4 quant).

# H3-LongVideos

Long MiniMax-H3 video with synchronised audio from a single prompt, in ComfyUI.

## What it does

H3 renders at most about 15 seconds at a time. H3-LongVideos takes a whole scene written
as beats, renders it shot by shot and joins the shots into one video with one soundtrack.
People and their clothes stay the same from shot to shot, and every spoken line is
lip-synced to whoever says it.

## How it works

1. **Plan.** Each paragraph of the prompt is a beat, and each beat becomes a shot as long
   as it takes in real life (at least 5.2 seconds). A beat that needs more than
   `shot_seconds` runs on into the next shot. The node reads who is in each beat, who says
   each line and what goes on or comes off whom, and carries that from shot to shot.
2. **Write.** Each shot's text is the scene, the characters and your beat, followed by
   notes that spell out each step of what goes on or comes off, keep everyone's clothes
   as they are and keep everyone whole and in frame.
3. **Render.** Each shot starts on the last frame of the shot before, so the scene runs on
   without a break. Reference pictures go into every shot their person is in.
4. **Sound.** Each spoken line gets its own stretch of sound, lip-synced to its speaker. A
   shot with no line is rendered silent and gets its sound from a second, audio-only pass.
5. **Join.** Each shot is matched to the one before in colour, contrast and sharpness, and
   the still background is carried over, so nothing drifts from shot to shot. The shots
   come out as one video with one soundtrack.

### The prompt

Characters go in `character_memory`, one per line. `<Picture 1>` … `<Picture 4>` beside a
name gives that person the picture wired into `ref_image_1` … `ref_image_4`:

```
Sarah <Picture 1>: a woman in her twenties, long brown hair, white blouse, black skirt
Dana: a woman in her thirties, short red hair, black blazer, blue shirt, grey trousers
```

The prompt is the scene, then one paragraph per beat. Anything in quotes is spoken:

```
A dim office at night.

Dana walks in and stops at Sarah's desk. "You're still here?" she asks.

Sarah looks up and smiles. "I was waiting for you."

Dana takes off her blazer and hangs it on the back of a chair.

Dana walks out of the room.
exit: Dana
```

- A first paragraph that names none of your characters and has no quotes is the scene,
  kept at the top of every shot. Text in `anchor` is kept there too.
- `cut` on its own line starts the next shot fresh instead of on the last frame.
- A `seconds: 12` line in a beat sets that shot's length.
- A tag line under a beat says outright what happens, instead of leaving it to the node to
  read:

| tag | |
|---|---|
| `hold: Name, item` | the item goes on in this shot and stays on |
| `release: Name, item` | the item comes off; `release: Name` takes everything off |
| `remove: Name, garment` | the garment comes off |
| `wear: Name, garment` | the garment goes on, or back into place |
| `lift: Name, garment` | the garment is pulled out of the way and stays on |
| `tear: Name, garment` | the garment is cut or torn off |
| `exit: Name` | the person leaves and is out of the shots after |

A `hold:` line in `character_memory` puts the item on from the first shot.

## How to wire it up

Copy this folder into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/` and restart the ComfyUI server. It needs
ComfyUI with native MiniMax-H3 support. Coming from an earlier version, right-click the
node → **Fix node (recreate)** and set your values again.

```
UNETLoader ──────── model ─────┐
CLIPLoader ──────── clip ──────┤
VAELoader (video) ─ vae ───────┼─> H3-LongVideos ─┬─ images ─┬─> Create Video ─> Save Video
VAELoader (audio) ─ audio_vae ─┤                  ├─ audio ──┘
text node ───────── prompt ────┘                  └─ info, script ─> Preview as Text
```

| `model` | a MiniMax-H3 model; a [hybrid fl2va/ref2va merge](https://huggingface.co/smhfacct/Minimax-H3-fl2va-ref2va-hybrid-models) works best |
| `clip` | H3's text encoder, loaded with type `minimax` |
| `vae` | the full H3 video VAE; a decoder-only VAE cannot start a shot on the last frame |
| `audio_vae` | the H3 audio VAE, a separate file (the converted one) |
| `prom

# MiniMax-H3, int8 — radiance container

[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) — video with a synchronized stereo
soundtrack from text — as a single `.rad` container for the
[radiance](https://codeberg.org/StillDeadcode/radiance) inference engine (AMD RDNA4, ROCm). It replaces
[StillDeadcode/minimax-h3-fp8](https://huggingface.co/StillDeadcode/minimax-h3-fp8), with the same eight bits a
weight and no E4M3 weight left.

The MiniMax H3 Community License does not cover the European Union, the United Kingdom, the
Republic of Korea or the United States of America; see [License](#license).

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `minimax-h3-i8.rad` — 62.79 GiB |
| Weights | int8 throughout: the text encoder's linears (the 50 layers of Qwen3-VL-32B the model reads) and the token refiner's IQ8R (codes −127..127, each 128 of K rotated by the unnormalised Hadamard, a u8 scale per row and 256 of K under a bf16 scale a row); the modulation projections the same rotation with a bf16 scale per row and 128; the DiT's 50 blocks' linears unrotated int8 with a bf16 scale per row and 128; the video decoder bf16; the audio decoder f32 |
| Activations | int8 (W8A8), rotated where the weight is |
| Latent upscaler | [LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler) v1 (3D conv, 345M parameters, bf16; Apache-2.0) |
| Output | MP4: H.264 at 24 fps, up to 1344x768, 5.17 to 14.4 s; AAC at 32 kHz stereo |
| Needs | radiance built from main after 1.17.0 (the text encoder's, the refiner's and the modulation projections' int8 forms are not in 1.17.0 and come with the next release); two 32 GB cards and about 39 GiB of pinned host memory |

## Serve

```sh
radiance --model minimax-h3-i8.rad --tp 2 --vision-tower-placement ram --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "prompt": "A red fox trotting through a snowy pine forest, snow crunching underfoot",
  "seconds": "5", "size": "1344x768", "seed": 7}'          # -> {"id": "video_...", "status": "queued", ...}
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos/video_...            # poll until "status": "completed"
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos/video_.../content -o fox.mp4
```

The server speaks OpenAI's video jobs API (`POST /v1/videos`, `GET /v1/videos/{id}`,
`GET /v1/videos/{id}/content`, list and delete), and SGLang's `target` field:

- `prompt` is read as written, up to 2048 tokens; the model follows long structured descriptions
  (the shot, its soundscape, its music) best.
- `seconds` is rounded up to the model's length steps (17 frames): 5.17 to 14.4 s. `size` is
  `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, multiples of 32, at most 1344x768 pixels of area.
- `seed` makes a video repeatable on the same deployment; `num_inference_steps` counts sigma grid
  points as diffusers does (50 by default, at most 65). The model is guidance-distilled: no guidance
  scale, no negative prompt.
- Text to video and audio only; the image- and reference-conditioned forms are not in this file.

On two Radeon AI PRO R9700s (gfx1201) the FP8 container's 5.17 s clip at 1344x768 takes about 8.8
minutes at the default 50 steps; a step of this container takes about 7% longer (measured below,
at 768x448). The text encoder and the modulation projections are read from pinned host memory,
which `--vision-tower-placement ram` selects. For the eight-step distillation, see
[StillDeadcode/fasth3-8-step-v2-i8](https://huggingface.co/StillDeadcode/fasth3-8-step-v2-i8).

Against the FP8 container on the same two cards, same prompt and seed, a 5.17 s clip at 768x448: 40 s against 38 s at 12 steps and 116 s against 108 s at 36, so a step of the int8 DiT takes about 7% longer; two runs of this container give the same video byte for byte, and its frames show the FP8 container's shot (PSNR 22.7 dB between the two at 12 steps). Not measured against diffusers' bf16 pipeline.

## Latent upscaling

The container carries LBH-123-AI's latent upscaler. A request with `"latent_upscale": 2` runs its
first steps at half the size (672x384 for 1344x768), the upscaler enlarges the clean latent, and the
last `upscale_refine_steps` (12 by default) run at the full size from a re-noised copy of it:

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "prompt": "...", "seconds": "5", "size": "1344x768", "seed": 7, "latent_upscale": 2}'
```

# FLUX 3 Image Klein — Uncensored Text Encoder (Qwen3-VL-4B, Q6_K)

GGUF **text encoder** for FLUX 3 Image Klein, built on an abliterated
[Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct). It is a drop-in

# **flux-3-image-klein-pup-MTP-Repacked (Prompt Upsampler)**

> FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler is Black Forest Labs’ 9B vision-language model, fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-9B with a frozen vision tower. It transforms short requests into detailed, FLUX 3 Image Klein-optimized prompts across three modes: text-to-image, image editing (up to 10 references), and layout generation with optional bounding boxes. It uses supervised fine-tuning followed by preference tuning based on generated image quality. Outputs cover style, scene, lighting, camera, materials, colors, and spatial positioning. It integrates with the official inference code, ComfyUI, and Diffusers. Limitations include English-only outputs, Klein-specific prompt optimization, and potential inaccuracies with small reference-image details. Released under Apache 2.0 with 19.3 GB bfloat16 weights.

> [!NOTE]
> MTP — Speculative Decoding: Yes | GGUF — [flux-3-image-klein-pup-MTP-Repacked(GGUF)](https://huggingface.co/prithivMLmods/flux-3-image-klein-pup-MTP-Repacked/tree/main/GGUF)

> [!NOTE]
Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) GGUF is a specialized GGUF model file format extension that integrates speculative decoding directly into the model weights to significantly accelerate local inference.  Unlike traditional speculative decoding which requires a separate, smaller "draft" model, MTP GGUF files include additional output heads within the main model architecture that predict multiple future tokens in a single forward pass.

# **flux-3-image-klein-prompt-upsampler-GGUF**

> **FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler** is Black Forest Labs' 9B vision-language model, a full fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B with the vision tower frozen, that expands a short image request into the detailed prompt FLUX 3 Image Klein works best with. The card says Klein is not meant to run without an upsampler in front of it, because short prompts sent as typed give generic output. One model covers three modes, selected by the system prompt: text-to-image, editing with up to 10 reference images, and layout with optional bounding boxes. Output prompts spell out medium and style, scene, lighting and camera, and each subject's colors, materials and position, with any text to render kept verbatim in quotes. For edits it looks at the references and writes the instruction around what is in them, covering what changes and what stays. Bounding boxes are kept exactly, in a box table after the prompt, and the prompt cites each box by id. Training had two stages: supervised training on pairs of short requests and expanded prompts, then preference tuning on pairs of the model's own prompts, rendered with FLUX 3 Image Klein at the same seed and ranked on the resulting image. The card gives no benchmark numbers. Its one example turns "A man walking with his dog, afternoon sun" into a 220-word prompt. It is loaded by default in the official inference code and has an `enable_prompt_upsampler` switch in ComfyUI. With Diffusers, you run the Transformers block yourself and pass the caption as `prompt`. The limitations section says output is English only, though the request can be in any language, the prompts are tuned only for FLUX 3 Image Klein, and references are downscaled (at most 1 MP for one), so small details can be described wrongly. The model does not refuse requests, and the inference code offers optional prompt and image safety checks (`--safety`). The weights, a 18.8 GB bfloat16 file, are released under Apache 2.0.

> [!NOTE]
> MTP — Speculative Decoding: No

# Molmo2 H3 Encoder + MolmoPoint Tracking

Community packages for two separate jobs: Molmo2-8B INT8 ConvRot as an experimental MiniMax H3 encoder, and MolmoPoint-8B point tracking for video segmentation. This is not an official Ai2 or MiniMax release.

The single weight file `molmo2_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors` totals **9.29 GB** (decimal); 302 eligible linear layers are quantized. The complete package including the projector is about **9.65 GB**.

The full model is included: language and vision weights, multimodal adapter, tokenizer, processor and original model code. Eligible linear layers use symmetric per-output-channel INT8 weights with regular block-Hadamard ConvRot rotations (blocks 256, 64 or 16) and dynamic per-token INT8 activations. Embeddings, normalization, biases and unsupported shapes retain BF16. The separate H3 projector retains its original precision. No original BF16 weight download is required.


## Which model to use

| Task | Package | Node | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H3 text/visual conditioning | Root `Molmo2-8B-Minimax-H3` INT8 ConvRot + `projections/` | Auto Download & Load Molmo2 (H3 Encoder) | H3-compatible CLIP |
| Locate and track subjects | `molmopoint_8b_int8_convrot/` | Auto Download & Load MolmoPoint-8B | Native point tokens and object IDs |
| Lower-memory point tracking on Blackwell | `molmopoint_8b_nvfp4_awq/` | MolmoPoint loader, NVFP4 AWQ option | Same point format |

The MolmoPoint packages are **separate models**. They do not use the H3 projection or replace the H3 text encoder. The ComfyUI [Molmo2-H3 nodes](https://github.com/alisson-anjos/ComfyUI-Molmo2-H3) expose points for `MolmoH3DrawPoints` and for the BFS Video Segment Picker. In the picker, connect `point_model`, choose `MolmoPoint-8B` as `propagation_method`, select a subject, and use **Apply fix**. MolmoPoint supplies sparse, identity-aware points; SAM 3.1 turns selected points/masks into per-frame segmentation. Clear subject descriptions and correct anchors still matter, especially across camera cuts.

The INT8 ConvRot point package quantizes 144 language linear layers and retains the visual backbone and point prediction head in BF16. The NVFP4 AWQ point package uses ModelOpt activation-aware calibration on video prompts for the same language layers, with native NVFP4 weights and AWQ pre-quantization scales. Both need their included loaders; standard Transformers `from_pretrained` does not interpret these custom quantized weights.

### Tracking evidence from Ai2

The [original MolmoPoint-8B](https://huggingface.co/allenai/MolmoPoint-8B) generates point tokens tied to visual patches and decodes them with pointing metadata, a constrained logits processor, and `extract_video_points`. Ai2 reports +5.7 J&F on Molmo2-Track versus Molmo 2 (8B), and state-of-the-art results on MeViS. These are **upstream full-precision results**, not scores for the INT8 or NVFP4 packages here. See the [Ai2 technical write-up](https://allenai.org/blog/molmopoint).

[![Ai2 MolmoPoint benchmark figure](https://www.datocms-assets.com/64837/1773843436-ai2-molmo-point-graphs-development-v9-05-1.png?fit=max&h=810&w=1550)](https://allenai.org/blog/molmopoint)

### Local validation of the quantized trackers

Both packages loaded and generated the same five tracking points with a consistent object ID on an eight-frame penguin clip. NVFP4 also passed inference through 144 ComfyUI native quantized layers on RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell. This is a smoke test, not a tracking accuracy benchmark. Approximate package sizes: INT8 9.8 GiB; NVFP4 AWQ 6.9 GiB. The NVFP4 loader adapts ModelOpt nibble order and block scales to ComfyUI native layout at load time. Execution uses the current ComfyUI process and model manager.

### Current H3 projection limitation

The Molmo2 → H3 projection can be used experimentally for **fl2va** and **t2v**. It sometimes works for **ref2va**, but identity and video quality are not yet consistent or as good as desired. The projection needs further task-specific training, particularly with multiple reference images and paired target videos. This limitation concerns the H3 projection; it is separate from MolmoPoint's pointing and SAM 3.1 segmentation roles.

## Load the complete quantized model

Use Python with PyTorch supporting your NVIDIA CUDA GPU, transformers 4.57.1 or later (checked with 4.57.1, 5.17 and 5.22.1), accelerate, safetensors, pillow, numpy, einops and molmo_utils. Video processing may require the upstream video dependencies.

# Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo, IQ8R — radiance container

[Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) — the 8-step distillation of Qwen-Image 2.1,
text to image and image editing — as a single `.rad` container for the
[radiance](https://codeberg.org/StillDeadcode/radiance) inference engine (AMD RDNA4, ROCm).

It replaces [StillDeadcode/radiance-qwen-image-2.1-turbo-fp8](https://huggingface.co/StillDeadcode/radiance-qwen-image-2.1-turbo-fp8),
with the same eight bits a weight.

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `qwen-image-2.1-turbo-iq8r.rad` — 16.13 GiB |
| Weights | the conditioning network's (Qwen3-VL-8B) and the diffusion transformer's linears int8 (codes −127..127) with a u8 scale per row and 256 of K under a bf16 scale a row, each 128 of K rotated by the unnormalised Hadamard, round to nearest; the vision tower, the small linears, the norms and the VAE bf16 |
| Activations | int8 under the same rotation (W8A8) |
| Steps | 8, fixed by the model (a request's `num_inference_steps` is refused) |
| Needs | radiance built from main after 1.17.0: IQ8R at one scale a 256 of K is not in 1.17.0 and comes with the next release |

## Serve

```yaml
# radiance.yaml
server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8000
models:
  qwen-image:
    model: qwen-image-2.1-turbo-iq8r.rad
    tp: 2
```

```sh
radiance --config radiance.yaml
```

`tp: 1` serves it on one card. The server speaks OpenAI's Images API: `POST /v1/images/generations` and
`POST /v1/images/edits` (JSON, or multipart with `image` / `image[]` and `mask`, as OpenAI's SDKs send them).
Pictures come back as `b64_json` (png, jpeg or webp; `response_format: url` is refused). Also: `n`, `size`
(`WxH` or `auto` = 2048x2048), `seed`, streaming with `partial_images`, `background: transparent`; edits take
1 to 10 reference pictures and a mask. `/v1/models` lists the model.

4.3 seconds a 1024x1024 picture on one Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), where the FP8 container takes 4.2.

From the same noise its four test pictures (1024x1024) are 26.3 dB from the FP8 container's on average (23.2 to
31.9). Not measured against a bf16 container of this model; on Qwen-Image 2.1 itself the same recipe is 32.6 dB
from bf16 where FP8 is 28.1.

## How this file was made

```sh
rad-convert Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo --recipe qwen-image-2.1-iq8r.recipe -o qwen-image-2.1-turbo-iq8r.rad
```

`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo` is the diffusers download of that repository with `text_encoder/` taken from
Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 (the two releases share it byte for byte).

The recipe (`qwen-image-2.1-iq8r.recipe` in this repository) names what is quantised; everything it does not
name is the checkpoint's own dtype:

```
te.blk.*.attn_qkv.weight             rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
te.blk.*.attn_output.weight          rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
te.blk.*.ffn_gate_up.weight          rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
te.blk.*.ffn_down.weight             rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.attn_qkv.weight            rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.attn_output.weight         rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.ffn_gate_up.weight         rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.ffn_down.weight            rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
vae.*                                cast dtype=bf16
```

## License

Built with Qwen. Qwen-Image 2.1 is licensed under the Qwen RESEARCH LICENSE AGREEMENT
(non-commercial; `LICENSE` in this repository), and `NOTICE` carries its attribution. This container is a
modified copy: its linear weights are re-encoded as rotated int8 (see above).

| Steps | 40 by default (`num_inference_steps`, or `quality`: low / medium / high) |
| Needs | radiance built from main after 1.17.0: IQ8R at one scale a 256 of K is not in 1.17.0 and comes with the next release |

## Serve

```yaml
# radiance.yaml
server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8000
models:
  qwen-image:
    model: qwen-image-2.1-iq8r.rad
    tp: 2
```

```sh
radiance --config radiance.yaml
```

`tp: 1` serves it on one card. The server speaks OpenAI's Images API: `POST /v1/images/generations` and
`POST /v1/images/edits` (JSON, or multipart with `image` / `image[]` and `mask`, as OpenAI's SDKs send them).
Pictures come back as `b64_json` (png, jpeg or webp; `response_format: url` is refused). Also: `n`, `size`
(`WxH` or `auto` = 2048x2048), `seed`, streaming with `partial_images`, `background: transparent`; edits take
1 to 10 reference pictures and a mask. `/v1/models` lists the model.

Seconds a 1024x1024 picture at 20 steps on Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201): 10.5 on one card and 6.8 on two (the
FP8 container: 10.2 and 6.6).

Against radiance's bf16 container of the same model from the same noise (four 1024x1024 pictures, 20 steps), PSNR
32.6 dB on one card and 34.1 dB on two; the FP8 container is at 28.1 and 28.6 dB.

## How this file was made

```sh
rad-convert Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 --recipe qwen-image-2.1-iq8r.recipe -o qwen-image-2.1-iq8r.rad
```

`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` is the diffusers download of that repository.

The recipe (`qwen-image-2.1-iq8r.recipe` in this repository) names what is quantised; everything it does not
name is the checkpoint's own dtype:

```
te.blk.*.attn_qkv.weight             rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
te.blk.*.attn_output.weight          rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
te.blk.*.ffn_gate_up.weight          rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
te.blk.*.ffn_down.weight             rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.attn_qkv.weight            rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.attn_output.weight         rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.ffn_gate_up.weight         rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
dit.blk.*.ffn_down.weight            rtn  codes=i8 group=256 scale=u8 scale2=bf16 block2=1x* transform=fwht128 clamp=sym rule=search
vae.*                                cast dtype=bf16
```

The 3D release has no such control (its sharpness sits at roughly 2D tier 1). Neural latent-space upscaler for **Minimax H3** video generation. Works directly on Minimax H3's **24-channel VAE latents** to upscale spatial resolution (H×W) while preserving the time dimension. ## Purpose This model is designed to **accelerate high-resolution H3 video generation**: 1. Generate video at low resolution — far fewer latent tokens, much faster. 2. Upscale the latent in-place with this learned upscaler. 3. Re-sample / refine at the target resolution to recover detail. By skipping the expensive `decode → pixel upscale → encode` round-trip through Minimax H3's heavy ~5B-parameter VAE, this pipeline saves a significant amount of generation time. It also avoids the **ghosting / double-image artifacts** that naive latent interpolation (bilinear/bicubic) introduces. ## 📸 Examples **Video upscale comparison** — click to play: *(If the player doesn't render, [download the video here](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler/resolve/main/examples/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler_001.mp4).)* **Image upscale comparison**: ![Minimax H3 latent upscale comparison](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler/resolve/main/examples/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler_002.jpg) ## 2D v1 vs 3D v1 **Test setup**: 2,500 validation pairs (the same frozen split used during training); latent-domain metrics computed on the normalized latents; pixel metrics decoded through the actual Minimax H3 VAE. Uncensored anime on Qwen Image 2.1: soft light, clean color, and full nudity when the scene calls for it. Built with Qwen.

**The full gallery with prompts, the int4, fp8, bf16 and fp16 files and the reviews are on Civitai: [Noct Q Anime](https://civitai.com/models/2967534).**

## What it does well

- Anime illustration, from close portraits to wide background paintings
- Adult characters dressed, in lingerie or nude, and explicit scenes
- Long, detailed prompts followed closely: two characters, poses and camera angles as written

| file | size | use |
|---|---|---|
| `NoctQA_V1_int8_convrot.safetensors` | 7.3 GB | 8 to 12 GB cards, ComfyUI 0.37 or newer, core nodes only |
| `NoctQ_Anime_V1_workflow.json` | | drag it into ComfyUI |

The model goes in `models/diffusion_models`.

## Settings

25 steps, euler, simple, cfg 3 with the negative prompt from the workflow.

- Text encoder: [`qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors) in `models/text_encoders`

Start with "An anime illustration of…" and describe the scene in full sentences. Without the word "anime" you get a photo. No trigger word.

Code and results for the causal teacher-forcing LoRA experiments in `code/tutorial.md`.

# Qwen3-VL-32B Heretic (MiniMax-H3 text encoder) — NVFP4

**The uncensored MiniMax-H3 text encoder, in 15.7 GB — it fits on a single 16 GB card.**

This is a mixed-precision **NVFP4** re-quantization of
[ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-32B-Ultra-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-ComfyUI-INT8-ConvRot](https://huggingface.co/ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-32B-Ultra-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-ComfyUI-INT8-ConvRot),
the Heretic (uncensored) text encoder for [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)
video generation.

| build | size | fits 16 GB card? |
|---|---|---|
| Heretic INT8-ConvRot (upstream) | 26.4 GB | no (needs offload) |
| **Heretic NVFP4 (this repo)** | **15.7 GB** | **yes** |
| Comfy-Org NVFP4 (censored) | 15.7 GB | yes |

Same size as Comfy-Org's official NVFP4 encoder, so it is a **drop-in replacement**:
point `CLIPLoader` at this file instead and the rest of your MiniMax-H3 workflow is unchanged.

## Why

80 GB cards always had the choice. This is for the people who don't have one.
Creative work shouldn't require datacenter hardware — that's the whole point of quantizing it.

## Measured

Generated 6 s of 480×864 vertical video with audio, MiniMax-H3 `fl2va` pruned INT8 diffusion model,
`res_multistep` 20 steps, ComfyUI 0.30.0, Sage Attention on:

| | value |
|---|---|
| GPU | 1× RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell (16 GB, sm_120) |
| peak VRAM during generation | **~9.9 GB** |
| encoder staged in VRAM | 14.9 GB (dynamic loading) |
| system RAM used by the ComfyUI process | ~36 GB |

Output was compared against the upstream INT8-ConvRot build on identical prompt and seed.
The two are visually equivalent — the quantization does not change what the encoder will describe.

## Files

```
qwen3vl_32b_heretic_minimax_h3_nvfp4.safetensors   15.7 GB
```

Place in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` and select it in `CLIPLoader` (type: `minimax`).
You still need the diffusion model and VAEs from
[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3).

## How it was made (and the trap you must avoid)

**The upstream weights are rotated.** Its `comfy_quant` metadata reads:

```json
{"format": "int8_tensorwise", "convrot": true, "convrot_groupsize": 256, "per_row": true}
```

ConvRot stores each weight already multiplied by a normalized Hadamard matrix
(`W_stored = W @ Hᵀ`, per 256-wide group) and rotates activations to match at runtime.
If you dequantize those weights and re-quantize them to plain NVFP4 **without undoing the
rotation**, you get a file that loads, runs, and produces *completely unrelated video* —
in our first attempt a prompt for a war-torn street rendered a speedboat on open water.
Nothing errors. The conditioning is simply meaningless.

Because the Hadamard is orthogonal, the fix is to multiply by `H` again before re-quantizing:

```python
from comfy_kitchen.backends.eager.convrot_w4a4 import _build_hadamard

def unrotate(w, gs=256):                      # w: dequantized [out, in]
    out_f, in_f = w.shape
    h = _build_hadamard(gs, device=w.device, dtype=torch.float32).to(w.dtype)
    return torch.matmul(w.reshape(out_f, in_f // gs, gs), h).reshape(out_f, in_f)
```

**Mixed precision.** 350 linear layers are NVFP4 (`TensorCoreNVFP4Layout`, group size 16).
`model.embed_tokens` (151936 × 5120 = 778 M params) is **left as INT8** — the same choice
Comfy-Org made in the official NVFP4 build. Quantizing it gives little size benefit and it is
the one layer whose temporaries will OOM a 16 GB card during baking. ComfyUI reads per-layer
`comfy_quant` metadata, so the mixed file loads with no special handling.

The bake runs on a single 16 GB GPU in about two minutes.

## Provenance

- Uncensoring / Heretic work: **[ethanfel](https://huggingface.co/ethanfel)**
- Original encoder: **Qwen3-VL-32B** (Alibaba / Qwen team), as adapted for MiniMax-H3
- MiniMax-H3: **[MiniMaxAI](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)**
- ComfyUI packaging conventions and quantization layouts: **[Comfy-Org](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)**
- This NVFP4 re-quantization: **Lna-Lab** ([@Tono_Ken3](https://x.com/Tono_Ken3))

Licensing follows the upstream repositories; the MiniMax-H3 model weights themselves are
subject to the MiniMax H3 Community License.

## Notes

- Re-quantizing INT8 → NVFP4 means this build inherits the upstream INT8 rounding.
  A bake straight from BF16 would be marginally cleaner; we did not have those weights.
- Blackwell (sm_120) was used for both baking and inference. NVFP4 needs hardware support.
- If output looks unrelated to your prompt rather than merely lower quality, suspect a
  rotation mismatch, not the quantization.

# MiniMax-H3 x Z-Image Hybrid

A custom hybrid version of **MiniMax-H3** combining the **FL2VA** and
**REF2VA** branches of the model.

The model uses different branches for different transformer blocks:

```text
B00-B24  -> FL2VA
B25-B49  -> REF2VA
B50+     -> FL2VA
````

This hybrid layout was constructed at the raw safetensor payload level.
No tensor conversion was performed when constructing the BF16 hybrid.

## Files

### BF16

```text
minimax_h3_hybrid_fl2va_ref2va_zs05_b25-49_bf16.safetensors
```

Approximately 37.46 GiB.

This is the full-precision BF16 hybrid model.

The B25-B49 tensors were copied byte-for-byte from the REF2VA ZS05 BF16
model, while the remaining tensors come from the FL2VA ZS05 BF16 model.

### INT8

The repository also contains an INT8 version of the same hybrid model.

The INT8 model follows the same conceptual hybrid layout:

```text
B00-B24  -> FL2VA
B25-B49  -> REF2VA
B50+     -> FL2VA
```

## Verification

The BF16 hybrid was verified at tensor level.

Results:

```text
Tensor count                 : 532
Expected source matches      : 532/532
Payload failures             : 0
Wrong-source tensors         : 0

B00-B24 : FL2VA
B25-B49 : REF2VA
B50+    : FL2VA

Tensor set       : PASS
dtype            : PASS
shape            : PASS
payload sizes    : PASS
Payload hashes   : PASS
```

All B25-B49 payloads were verified to be byte-exact copies from the
REF2VA source.

No tensor conversion was performed during hybrid construction.

## Why this hybrid exists

The purpose of this model is to experiment with a mixed FL2VA/REF2VA
architecture where only the middle transformer blocks use REF2VA.

The selected layout is:

```text
FL2VA
  |
  +-- B00-B24
  |
REF2VA
  |
  +-- B25-B49
  |
FL2VA
  |
  +-- B50+
```

This allows the model to be tested as a single hybrid model without
requiring separate model files for the two branches.

## Related model

For the original/native Z-Image implementation and the REF2VA BF16
model, see:

[https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/MiniMax-H3-x-Z-Image-native](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/MiniMax-H3-x-Z-Image-native)

Please refer to the original repository for the native model structure,
configuration and usage information.

## GGUF

A GGUF conversion of the BF16 hybrid is provided separately:

[https://huggingface.co/hoidhxd/MiniMax-H3-x-Z-Image-hybrid-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/hoidhxd/MiniMax-H3-x-Z-Image-hybrid-GGUF)

The GGUF version is intended for use with GGUF-compatible ComfyUI
workflows and loaders.

## Disclaimer

This is an experimental custom hybrid model.

It is not an official MiniMax release.

The hybrid block selection was created for experimentation and testing.

# Noct Q: Qwen Image 2.1 Uncensored Realism

Qwen Image 2.1, uncensored: nudes and explicit scenes render without a LoRA. Built with Qwen.

**The full gallery with prompts, the int4, fp8, bf16 and fp16 files and the reviews are on Civitai: [Noct Q](https://civitai.com/models/2958896).**

## What it does well

- Full-body nudes in daylight, flash and night scenes
- Explicit scenes with a partner: V4 renders them as asked three times as often as V3
- Readable text on signs and labels
- Anime and painted illustration
- Plain-caption prompts: who, what she does, where, the light
- Image editing with the same files, in ComfyUI's Qwen Image 2.1 edit template

## Files

| file | size | use |
|---|---|---|
| `NoctQ_V4_int8_convrot.safetensors` | 7.3 GB | V4: 8 to 12 GB cards, ComfyUI 0.37 or newer, core nodes only |
| `NoctQ_V3_base_int8_convrot.safetensors` | 7.3 GB | V3, the previous version |
| `NoctQ_V4_workflow.json` | | drag it into ComfyUI |

The model goes in `models/diffusion_models`.

## Settings

25 steps, euler, simple, cfg 3 with the negative prompt, all set in the workflow. cfg 1 runs about twice as fast and then ignores the negative prompt. 1024x1536 portrait works well.

- Text encoder: [`qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors) in `models/text_encoders`
- VAE: [`qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1/blob/main/vae/qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors) in `models/vae`

## How to prompt

Write full sentences, like a caption of the finished photo: the kind of shot, then the person with an adult age ("a woman in her twenties"), what she does, where, the light and the framing. Qwen Image 2.1 reads prose, not tag lists. No trigger word.

# ⚡ LightVAE **Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders** Wan2.1 · Wan2.2 · MiniMax-H3 [📄 Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.14726) · [💻 Code](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE) · [🧩 ComfyUI](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE/tree/main/comfyui) · [⚡ LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V)
LightVAE compresses video autoencoders while preserving their original latent interfaces, allowing compressed components to be paired with the corresponding original components. - **Wan2.1 / Wan2.2:** Pro and Lite decoders, paired with the original encoder. Pro retains the original decoder depth with temporal low-rank compression; Lite adds block pruning. - **MiniMax-H3:** independently block-pruned Lite encoder and decoder, with native ComfyUI integration. - **Optional ConvRot-INT8:** a quantized H3 Lite decoder for ComfyUI. Download the components you need from [Files and versions](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/LightVAE/tree/main). Keep checkpoints matched to their backbone. > **Wan2.2 model selection:** 14B models use the **Wan2.1 VAE**; TI2V-5B uses the **Wan2.2 VAE**. ## 🧩 ComfyUI · MiniMax-H3 The **Load H3 LightVAE** node reuses ComfyUI’s native H3 VAE. No separate LightVAE package installation, TLR or custom Triton kernels are needed. The current node supports **H3 only**. ### 1. Install Use a ComfyUI version with native MiniMax-H3 support. Run these commands in the Python environment that starts ComfyUI: ```bash cd /path/to/ComfyUI git clone https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE.git LightVAE python LightVAE/comfyui/install.py --comfy-root . python -m pip install huggingface_hub hf download lightx2v/LightVAE \ lightvae-lite-h3-decoder.safetensors \ lightvae-lite-h3-encoder.safetensors \ --local-dir models/vae/LightVAE ``` Already cloned? Run `git -C LightVAE pull`, then rerun the installer. The installer creates `custom_nodes/ComfyUI-LightVAE/` automatically. **Do not clone the entire repository directly into `custom_nodes`.** The original H3 video VAE is required. Download it if needed: ```bash hf download Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 \ vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors \ --local-dir models ``` ### 2. Connect Restart ComfyUI and search for **Load H3 LightVAE**. Load the **original H3 video VAE** with the standard **Load VAE** node and connect it to **`base_vae`**. Select Lite components in **Load H3 LightVAE**, not in the standard Load VAE node. - **FL2V:** replace only the decoder. Leave `encoder = none`, keep the original VAE connected to first/last-frame encoding, and use LightVAE for **VAE Decode**. - **REF2V:** replace the encoder, decoder, or both. Connect LightVAE to reference encoding and **VAE Decode**. - **`none`:** use the corresponding original component. **The audio VAE stays unchanged.** Standard H3 checkpoints and our previous `*-h3-*-comfy.safetensors` exports are both accepted; downloading both formats is unnecessary. ### 3. Load a workflow Download a workflow JSON and drag it into ComfyUI: [🎞️ First + last frame](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE/blob/main/comfyui/workflows/h3_fl2v_lightvae.json) · [🖼️ Image references](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE/blob/main/comfyui/workflows/h3_ref_image_lightvae.json) · [🎬 Video reference](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE/blob/main/comfyui/workflows/h3_ref_video_lightvae.json) Select your model files, upload the inputs and run. These are base-model workflows, not 4-/8-step turbo-LoRA workflows. See the [workflow guide](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE/tree/main/comfyui/workflows) for required diffusion models, text encoders and input preparation. ### Optional · ConvRot-INT8 decoder Update LightVAE, rerun the installer and download the quantized decoder: ```bash hf download lightx2v/LightVAE \ lightvae-lite-h3-decoder-int8-convrot.safetensors \ --local-dir /path/to/ComfyUI/models/vae/LightVAE ``` Restart ComfyUI and select this file in **Load H3 LightVAE → decoder**. Keep `base_vae`, encoder selection and audio VAE unchanged. Native NVIDIA CUDA acceleration requires a **CUDA 13.0+ PyTorch build** and a compatible driver. Backend support and performance depend on your environment. > This INT8 checkpoint is **ComfyUI-only**. Use standard, non-INT8 checkpoints with the standalone Python scripts. ## 🐍 Python · Video Reconstruction Example: **original Wan2.1 encoder + LightVAE-Lite decoder**. ```bash git clone https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE.git cd LightVAE python -m pip install -r requirements.txt hf download lightx2v/LightVAE \ lightvae-lite-wan21-decoder.safetensors \ --local-dir weights/LightVAE hf download Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B \ Wan2.1_VAE.pth --local-dir weights/Wan2.1 python infer.py \ --model wan21 --variant lite \ --encoder weights/Wan2.1/Wan2.1_VA
