## Introduction We are excited to introduce **Qwen-Image-Layered**, a model capable of decomposing an image into multiple RGBA layers. This layered representation unlocks **inherent editability**: each layer can be independently manipulated without affecting other content. Meanwhile, such a layered representation naturally supports **high-fidelity elementary operations**-such as resizing, reposition, and recoloring. By physically isolating semantic or structural components into distinct layers, our approach enables high-fidelity and consistent editing. ## Quick Start 1. Make sure your transformers>=4.51.3 (Supporting Qwen2.5-VL) 2. Install the latest version of diffusers ``` pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install python-pptx ``` ```python from diffusers import QwenImageLayeredPipeline import torch from PIL import Image pipeline = QwenImageLayeredPipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-Layered") pipeline = pipeline.to("cuda", torch.bfloat16) pipeline.set_progress_bar_config(disable=None) image = Image.open("asserts/test_images/1.png").convert("RGBA") inputs = { "image": image, "generator": torch.Generator(device='cuda').manual_seed(777), "true_cfg_scale": 4.0, "negative_prompt": " ", "num_inference_steps": 50, "num_images_per_prompt": 1, "layers": 4, "resolution": 640, # Using different bucket (640, 1024) to determine the resolution. For this version, 640 is recommended "cfg_normalize": True, # Whether enable cfg normalization. "use_en_prompt": True, # Automatic caption language if user does not provide caption } with torch.inference_mode(): output = pipeline(**inputs) output_image = output.images[0] for i, image in enumerate(output_image): image.save(f"{i}.png") ``` ## Showcase ### Layered Decomposition in Application Given an image, Qwen-Image-Layered can decompose it into several RGBA layers: ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片1.JPG) After decomposition, edits are applied exclusively to the target layer, physically isolating it from the rest of the content, and thereby fundamentally ensuring consistency across edits. For example, we can recolor the first layer and keep all other content untouched: ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片2.JPG) We can also replace the second layer from a girl to a boy (The target layer is edited using Qwen-Image-Edit): ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片3.JPG) Here, we revise the text to "Qwen-Image" (The target layer is edited using Qwen-Image-Edit): ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片4.JPG) Furthermore, the layered structure naturally supports elemetary operations. For example, we can delete unwanted objects cleanly: ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片5.JPG) We can also resize an object without distortion: ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片6.JPG) After layer decomposition, we can move objects freely within the canvas: ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片7.JPG) ### Flexible and Iterative Decomposition Qwen-Image-Layered is not limited to a fixed number of layers. The model supports variable-layer decomposition. For example, we can decompose an image into either 3 or 8 layers as needed: ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片8.JPG) Moreover, decomposition can be applied recursively: any layer can itself be further decomposed, enabling infinite decomposition. ![Example Image](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/layered/幻灯片9.JPG) ## License Agreement Qwen-Image-Layered is licensed under Apache 2.0. ## Citation We kindly encourage citation of our work if you find it useful. ```bibtex @misc{yin2025qwenimagelayered, title={Qwen

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

# heretic-ara-seed2-t116-Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I — ConvRot INT8

INT8 ConvRot quantization of
[rockerBOO/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I-heretic-ara-seed2-t116](https://huggingface.co/rockerBOO/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I-heretic-ara-seed2-t116),
a Heretic ARA-decensored [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I)
(the image-editing prompt rewriter for Qwen-Image-2.1), as a single safetensors file for ComfyUI.

Built with Qwen. **Non-commercial use only** (see License).

## Files

| File | Size | Description |
| :--- | :--: | :---------- |
| `qwen_image_2.1_pe_i2i_heretic_ara_seed2_t116_convrot_int8.safetensors` | 11.9 GB | INT8 ConvRot language model, rest BF16 |
| `layer_config.json` | – | Per-layer routing used for the quantization |
| `system_prompt.txt` | – | Upstream prompt-rewriting system prompt |

Source (BF16): 18.8 GB.

## Layout

- **INT8 ConvRot, group size 256, per-row scale** (200 tensors): all language-model attention
  (`self_attn` q/k/v/o, `linear_attn` in_proj_qkv / in_proj_z / out_proj) and MLP
  (`gate_proj` / `up_proj` / `down_proj`) weights
- **BF16**: embeddings, `lm_head`, norms, `in_proj_a` / `in_proj_b`, conv1d, vision tower

## Hardware

Any recent NVIDIA GPU with INT8 tensor cores; no Blackwell requirement. ~12 GB VRAM to hold
fully, less with ComfyUI offloading. Requires ComfyUI with quantized-checkpoint (`comfy_quant`)
support.

## Usage

Put the file in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/`, load it with `CLIPLoader` (type `moss_image`), and
use it with the `TextGenerate` node. For edit-prompt rewriting as upstream intends, pass
`system_prompt.txt` as the system prompt.

## Quality

Checked for functional correctness only: it loads in ComfyUI and produces coherent prompt
rewrites closely matching the BF16 source on a small prompt set (greedy decoding). No benchmark
evaluation has been run.

## Quantization

[`convert_to_quant`](https://github.com/silveroxides/convert_to_quant), learned rounding (default):

```
ctq -i qwen_image_2.1_pe_i2i_heretic_ara_seed2_t116_bf16.safetensors \
    -o qwen_image_2.1_pe_i2i_heretic_ara_seed2_t116_convrot_int8.safetensors \
    --int8 --scaling-mode row --convrot --convrot-group-size 256 \
    --layer-config layer_config.json \
    --comfy_quant --save-quant-metadata
```

ConvRot: [arXiv:2512.03673](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03673).

## License

[Qwen Research License Agreement](./LICENSE), inherited from
[Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-I2I) — research and
evaluation (non-commercial) use only. Attribution and modification notices are in `NOTICE`.
These weights are modified from the original: decensored with Heretic, then quantized.

# Minimax H3 Latent Upscaler (3D) — MAXQUALITY / NEXORA

This repository contains several checkpoints derived from the **MiniMax H3 3D Latent Upscaler** by [LBH-123-AI](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler).

It includes the original repository's BF16 conservative re-quantized checkpoint and two FP16 NEXORA checkpoints fine-tuned for latent upscaling on paired image and video latent data.

> **Important:** The FP16 NEXORA checkpoints are fine-tuned versions of the existing upscaler. They are not models trained from scratch, and they are not LoRA adapters.

## 📥 Checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Training stage | Saved format | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `minimax_h3_bf16_CONSERVATIVE_v5.safetensors` | Re-quantization | BF16 + FP16 fallback | Conservative mixed-precision checkpoint described below |
| `Minimax_h3_NEXORA_LatentUpscaler_FP16_Steps400.safetensors` | 400 steps | FP16 | NEXORA Expanded fine-tuning checkpoint |
| `Minimax_h3_NEXORA_LatentUpscaler_FP16_Steps6056.safetensors` | 6,056 steps in final stage | FP16 | NEXORA Full-data fine-tuning checkpoint |

The two NEXORA files were saved as FP16. During training, model parameters were held in FP32, forward computation used FP16 autocast, the loss was calculated in FP32, and the final state dictionaries were converted to FP16 for saving.

## 🆕 NEXORA FP16 fine-tuning

### What is NEXORA?

NEXORA is an experimental fine-tuning series built on the existing MiniMax H3 3D latent upscaler architecture. The objective was to adapt the upscaler using paired low-resolution guide latents and high-quality target latents from both images and videos.

The training objective was supervised latent-space fine-tuning:

1. Prepare corresponding guide and target media.
2. Encode the media into latent representations using the VAE workflow.
3. Feed the normalized low-resolution guide latent to the 3D upscaler.
4. Compare the predicted upscaled latent with the normalized high-quality target latent.
5. Calculate the training loss and update the model weights through backpropagation.

The training data was stored as prepared latent pairs, so the VAE encoding did not need to be repeated for every optimization step.

### Training stages

The NEXORA checkpoints were produced in successive stages:

| Stage | Steps | Learning rate | Starting point / purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Pilot | 40 | `2e-6` | Initial short fine-tuning experiment from the original upscaler |
| Expanded | 400 | `2e-6` | Expanded-data fine-tuning; checkpoint published as `Minimax_h3_NEXORA_LatentUpscaler_FP16_Steps400` |
| Full-data | 6,056 | `5e-7` | Further fine-tuning from the Expanded checkpoint; checkpoint published as `Minimax_h3_NEXORA_LatentUpscaler_FP16_Steps6056` |

The 6,056-step Full-data stage is the final stage's step count. It is not 6,056 epochs. The 400-step checkpoint is an earlier checkpoint and was not overwritten by the Full-data run.

### Full-data dataset

The final training run used the prepared full-data latent-pair dataset:

| Split | Image pairs | Video pairs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Training | 4,724 | 111 |
| Validation | 275 | 10 |
| **Total** | **4,999** | **121** |

To avoid the much smaller video subset being overwhelmed by image examples, the final training schedule used each training image once and each training video twelve times:

- Images: `4,724 × 1`
- Videos: `111 × 12`
- Total optimization steps: `4,724 + 1,332 = 6,056`

This corresponds to 6,056 optimization steps with an effective batch size of 1, not 6,056 epochs.

The prepared latent data used a 4× scale setting. The project history identifies 512 px as the preparation resolution; exact per-sample dimensions and media provenance are not specified in this README.

### Training configuration

The recorded Full-data training configuration was:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Optimizer | AdamW |
| Learning rate | `5e-7` |
| Weight decay | `1e-4` |
| Loss | Smooth L1 |
| Smooth L1 beta | `0.1` |
| Gradient clipping | `1.0` |
| Effective batch size | `1` |
| Forward precision | FP16 autocast |
| Model parameter dtype during training | FP32 |
| Loss calculation | FP32 |
| Gradient scaling | CUDA GradScaler enabled |
| Scale | `4×` |
| Training GPU recorded in project history | NVIDIA Tesla T4 |

The training loop checked that the loss and gradient norm remained finite. Gradients were unscaled before clipping, then the optimizer and GradScaler were stepped.

No EMA weights, LoRA training, or training-from-scratch stage are documented for these checkpoints. A learning-rate scheduler is not specified in the recorded final training configuration.

![PiD 1.5 qwenimage NVFP4, ComfyUI-ready decoder, by BennyDaBall](banner.png)

**Follow me on X [@BennyDaBall_OG](https://x.com/BennyDaBall_OG) !**

**The first quantized PiD decoder on HF.** 2.61 GB → **1.09 GB**, drops straight into a stock
`UNETLoader`, and decodes a 33 MP master in **16 s** on a 5090 (bf16 takes 20). No custom
loader. No core patches. No Blackwell requirement either — this runs anywhere the bf16 file
runs.

## 🧠 What is this?

NVIDIA's [PiD v1.5](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/PiD) decoder for the qwen-image latent
family — the 4-step pixel-diffusion decode that replaces your VAE decode and hands back **4×
the resolution**. Same decoder, 42% of the size, a little faster.

Everyone else ships this model in bf16 only. Not anymore.

## 👀 Same seed, same latent, both builds

![full frame](ab_full_frame.jpg)

100% crops — faces, lettering, bokeh all hold:

![face](ab_face_100.jpg)

![lettering](ab_lettering_100.jpg)

![bokeh](ab_bokeh_100.jpg)

## 📋 Specs

| Attribute | Details |
|---|---|
| Base | `nvidia/PiD` v1.5 qwenimage (4-step distill), via the Comfy-Org/PixelDiT repackage |
| Quantization | NVFP4 (group 16), quality-critical layers kept bf16 |
| File size | 1.09 GB (bf16: 2.61 GB) |
| Requirements | ComfyUI ≥ 0.32 (tested on 0.33.0) · any GPU that runs PiD bf16 |
| Text encoder | `gemma_2_2b_it_elm_bf16.safetensors` from Comfy-Org/PixelDiT (CLIPLoader type `pixeldit`) |

## 💻 Usage

Drop the model in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`, select it in `UNETLoader`, done. Two
workflows included:

**Simple (core nodes only)** — `PiD-1.5-qwenimage-nvfp4_simple_1mp_to_16mp.json`. Stage-1
render at ~1MP → single-shot PiD 4× → **5376×3072**, built from nothing but core nodes
(`PiDConditioning` + a 4-step KSampler). Drop the included `pixel_space_vae.safetensors` into
`ComfyUI/models/vae/` for the final decode step. Keep this one near its trained envelope —
single-shot PiD collapses past ~4K output.

**Tiled (the big guns)** — `PiD-1.5-qwenimage-nvfp4_tiled_2mp_to_33mp.json`. Stage-1 →
seam-free **7680×4352** in one queue via
[ComfyUI-Latent-Tiled-PiD](https://github.com/BennyDaBall930/ComfyUI-Latent-Tiled-PiD):
install from **ComfyUI Manager** (search "Latent-Tiled-PiD") or the
[Comfy Registry](https://registry.comfy.org/publishers/bennydaball).

Every included workflow was executed through the actual ComfyUI frontend against this exact
file before upload. qwen-family latents only — the FLUX.2 build is
[here](https://huggingface.co/BennyDaBall/PiD-1.5-flux2-nvfp4-comfy).

Smallest working 22B on the board — **18.7GB, ~2.8GB lighter than the official comfy-int8** — and the same-seed output holds up frame for frame.

Image-to-video with this checkpoint, 50fps — the sign text stays legible the whole clip.

Same seed, same prompt, both quants:
Official comfy-int8-convrot (21.5GB) NVFP4 — this repo (18.7GB)
Top row: text-to-video. Bottom row: **image-to-video** from a single keyframe — same start image, same seed, both quants. Native synced audio on all four (yes, the disco clips come with their own disco track). ## The problem Lightricks ships an NVFP4 export of the 2.5 distilled DiT, but it's a raw TensorRT-ModelOpt export. Load it through ComfyUI's UNETLoader and you get: ``` mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (6820x4096 and 2048x4096) ``` That `2048x4096` is a packed 4-bit weight being read as raw bytes — exactly half the width it should be. The funny part: the file's scale tensors (`weight_scale`, `weight_scale_2`, `input_scale`) already match ComfyUI's nvfp4 spec name-for-name. The only thing missing is the per-layer `.comfy_quant` marker tensor ComfyUI uses to detect quantized layers. Official "comfy-" packs have them; the NVFP4 export doesn't. ## The fix This repo is the official NVFP4 file with a `{"format": "nvfp4"}` marker stamped onto all **1,176 quantized layers**. No requantization, no math — the weight bytes are untouched. It just tells ComfyUI what it's looking at. | | | |---|---| | Base | [Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-nvfp4` | | Quant | NVFP4 (group 16, ModelOpt scales), 1,176 layers | | Size | 18.7GB (vs 21.5GB comfy-int8-convrot) | | Needs | ComfyUI ≥ v0.32.0, **Blackwell GPU** (RTX 50-series) for the FP4 kernels | ## Usage Drop it in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/` and pick it as `unet_name` in the stock **LTX-2.5 Text to Video / Image to Video** templates (ComfyUI ships them natively — no custom nodes). ### 🧠 What is this?
This is a merged model based on **Qwen3 (specifically the 4B-Instruct-2507 variant)**, fine-tuned to enhance user image prompts. It excels at adding detail, maintaining stylistic consistency, and transforming brief ideas into rich, descriptive prose without the robotic "AI feel" of standard assistants. It knows about "Positive Constraints," it hates negative prompts (because they don't work), and it really, really wants you to describe skin texture so your portraits don't look like plastic dolls.

#### Key Use Cases
- **✨ Prompt Enhancement:** A lightweight, low-VRAM solution to create, edit, and enrich simple image ideas into detailed narratives.

- **⚡ Hybrid Power:** Use it to expand a prompt, then use the model itself as the encoder for the generation stage.

### 📉 The "Heretic" Touch
We took the base Qwen3 model (which loves to say "I cannot assist with that") and gave it the [Heretic](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic) treatment by targeting image generation refusals. 
- **Refusal Rate:** Dropped from a prudish **100/100** to a chill **23/100** on our benchmarks.
- **KL Divergence:** Minimal. We lobotomized the censorship without breaking the brain.

### 🔬 V1 vs V2: The Training Evolution

The leap from V1 to V2 isn't just about training time—it's about a fundamental shift in how we generated the synthetic training data.

#### 1. The "Camera" Fix
In V1, the training seeds included specific camera bodies (e.g., "Shot on Canon R5"). This confused the model, causing it to occasionally hallucinate a literal camera appearing *inside* the generated image.
**V2 Improvement:** We stripped all camera brand references from the seed data, focusing purely on **lens specifications** (e.g., "85mm f/1.2") and optical characteristics. The model now understands photography physics without trying to render the hardware.

#### 2. From Cloud API to Local Swarm Intelligence
- **V1 (Legacy Pipeline):** The original version was trained on data generated by lighter, faster models with simple instructions. It produced good volume, but the seeds were often simple combinations of concept + style.
- **V2 (Advanced Swarm):** For V2, we upgraded to a swarm of **LFM2-8B-A1B** models running a complex "Persona" system prompt with **few-shot examples**. 
    - **Outcome:** The V2 data features significantly more complex sentence structures, better "sentence fragments" for pacing, and a deeper understanding of lighting and spatial relationships. It doesn't just list tags; it weaves them into a scene.

#### 3. Strict Quality Control
V2 introduced a rigorous validation loop. While V1 just checked for word count, V2's generation pipeline actively rejected thousands of outputs that didn't meet strict criteria for **lens preservation**, **texture density**, and **spatial precision**. If a generated prompt was "tag salad," it was discarded and regenerated.

#### 4. Multi-Turn Retention
Thanks to the new base model (Instruct-2507) and the diverse conversation samples in the dataset, V2 has significantly better context retention. You can have a back-and-forth conversation to refine a prompt (e.g., "make it darker," "change the lens to wide angle") without the model losing the original subject details.

- **V1 (Legacy Pipeline):** The original version was trained on data generated by lighter, faster models with simple instructions. It produced good volume, but the seeds were often simple combinations of concept + style.
- **V2 (Advanced Swarm):** For V2, we upgraded to a swarm of **LFM2-8B-A1B** models running a complex "Persona" system prompt with **few-shot examples**. 
    - **Outcome:** The V2 data features significantly more complex sentence structures, better "sentence fragments" for pacing, and a deeper understanding of lighting and spatial relationships. It doesn't just list tags; it weaves them into a scene.

#### 3. Strict Quality Control
V2 introduced a rigorous validation loop. While V1 just checked for word count, V2's generation pipeline actively rejected thousands of outputs that didn't meet strict criteria for **lens preservation**, **texture density**, and **spatial precision**. If a generated prompt was "tag salad," it was discarded and regenerated.

#### 4. Multi-Turn Retention
Thanks to the new base model (Instruct-2507) and the diverse conversation samples in the dataset, V2 has significantly better context retention. You can have a back-and-forth conversation to refine a prompt (e.g., "make it darker," "change the lens to wide angle") without the model losing the original subject details.

# Hy-Nomas x LTX-2.5 Audio Workflows

![Hy-Nomas x LTX-2.5 Audio Workflows](banner.png)

**Follow me on X [@BennyDaBall_OG](https://x.com/BennyDaBall_OG) !**

**Want to support my work? Buy me a coffee on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/bennydaball) !**

Tencent's **Hy-Nomas** is an 8B video world model: you write a world, it renders it segment by segment, and you can keep extending it or drive it with WASD. It has **no audio**.

These two ComfyUI workflows give it a soundtrack with the stock **LTX-2.5 distilled** model. **No training, no new models.** LTX-2.5 is a joint audio-video model, so I freeze the Hy-Nomas frames inside LTX's latent and let it generate only the audio. Because the audio attends to the frozen video, the sound follows the picture: hoofbeats while the horse gallops, a deep burner roar the moment the flame fires.

## Examples (straight out of the workflows)

**Hot air balloon over Giza**: Text to World with Audio, 1280x704, 10 s, seed 7 (the workflow ships with 42; for this one set Sample segment 1 to 7, Sample segment 2 to 8 and the LTX Seed to 7)

<video controls src="https://huggingface.co/BennyDaBall/Hy-Nomas-x-LTX-2.5-Audio-Workflows/resolve/main/examples/hot_air_balloon_over_giza_with_ltx_audio.mp4"></video>

Calm breeze over the desert, then the deep burner roar lands right as the view tilts up to the flame.

**Dragon raid**: Add Audio to Any Video, on a Hy-Nomas clip, 1280x704, 10 s, seed 42

<video controls src="https://huggingface.co/BennyDaBall/Hy-Nomas-x-LTX-2.5-Audio-Workflows/resolve/main/examples/dragon_raid_with_ltx_audio.mp4"></video>

Regular hoofbeats through the gallop, then a broadband blast exactly when the wall of fire erupts. With the video switched off (same prompt, LTX's audio-only mode) you just get one flat roar from frame 0, so the frames really are steering it.

World prompts and sound prompts for both are in [`examples/`](examples).

## The workflows

### 1. Add Audio to Any Video: `workflows/hynomas_x_ltx25_add_audio_to_video.json`
Core ComfyUI nodes only. Load a Hy-Nomas world, a saved Hy-Nomas Drive, or any clip, write a sound prompt, run. The video is saved untouched with the new audio track.

![Add Audio to Any Video](images/workflow_add_audio_to_video.png)

### 2. Text to World with Audio: `workflows/hynomas_x_ltx25_text_to_world_with_audio.json`
Writes a 2-segment Hy-Nomas world (stock T8 settings: 8 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1) and scores it with LTX-2.5 in one run. Ships with the hot air balloon world as the default.

![Text to World with Audio](images/workflow_text_to_world_with_audio.png)

## How it works
1. Pad the clip to LTX's frame grid (8n+1) by holding the last frame, all in-graph, so any length works.
2. Encode the frames with LTX's own video VAE at half size (the same size the stock LTX template's first stage uses).
3. **Freeze** that video latent (`LTXV Freeze Latent`, noise mask 0) so LTX cannot change a single frame.
4. Join it with an empty LTX audio latent and sample with the stock distilled sigmas (euler ancestral, CFG 1).
5. Decode with the LTX audio VAE and mux it onto the original full-resolution frames.

## Speed on my RTX 5090 (32 GB, ComfyUI 0.44.0)
| | Time | Peak VRAM |
|---|---:|---:|
| Add Audio to a 10 s 1280x704 clip | ~20 s warm, 41 s with first model load | ~31 GiB |
| Text to World with Audio, 10 s at 1280x704 | 103 s (132 s with first model loads) | ~31 GiB |

No offload in any run.

**RAM:** Text to World loads Hy-Nomas and LTX-2.5 in one run and peaked at about 62 GB of system RAM on my 64 GB box. It works, but it's at the limit. With 64 GB, close other apps, or render the world first and score it with workflow 1 in a second run.

## What you need
- ComfyUI 0.43 or newer (tested on 0.44.0).
- **LTX-2.5** files from [Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) (gated, accept the license first):
  - `diffusion_models/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors`
  - `text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors`
  - `vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors`
  - `vae/ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors`
- **Workflow 2 only:** the [Comfyui-HY-Nomas-T8](https://github.com/T8mars/Comfyui-HY-Nomas-T8) node pack (ComfyUI-Manager: "Hy-Nomas T8") and its three files from [t8star/HY-Nomas-Comfy](https://huggingface.co/t8star/HY-Nomas-Comfy): `hy_nomas_distil_int8.safetensors` (diffusion_models), `hy_nomas_pixelumm_fp8.safetensors` (vae), `qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors` (text_encoders).

- The raw audio comes out hot (around -9 LUFS). Normalize it in your editor if you need broadcast levels.

Uses **3 evaluations per chunk**, 8 chunks (24 evaluations per clip), CFG 1.
Use the included chunked sampler, not a stock H3 pipeline with only its step count changed.

## Quick start

Use Python 3.12 and a compatible CUDA-enabled PyTorch environment.
The tested environment uses PyTorch 2.11.0/CUDA 13.0; `requirements.txt` pins the Diffusers revision.
A high-memory GPU is required; consumer-GPU offloading and quantization are not validated.

```bash
hf download Perflow-Shuai/MiniMax-H3-3Step-LoRA --local-dir ./h3-3step
hf download MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
  --revision fa9c8ab1eaa21c8ae25e7e40b83b2e6002f340af \
  --local-dir ./h3-base --exclude "transformer/*"
cd h3-3step
pip install -r requirements.txt
python infer.py --base ../h3-base --prompt-file examples/tokyo-car.txt \
  --output ./output --seed 20262020
```

Output: `output/video.mp4`, including generated audio.
The script automatically loads the complete merged transformer from this repository.
Its approximately 66.28 GB of weights are stored as 14 Safetensors shards plus an index;
these shards form one full transformer checkpoint, not separate LoRAs.
No standalone adapter weights are included or loaded. Use a fresh local directory if upgrading.
The original H3 download supplies the unchanged text encoder, VAEs and supporting components.
Replace the example prompt with your own UTF-8 text file.
Rerun the same command/output directory to resume an interrupted clip.

**中文：下载本仓库和 H3 的非 transformer 组件后，直接执行上述推理命令即可。视频下方附完整英文 Prompt 和中文翻译；实际输入使用英文。**

## Python integration

```python
from h3_inference import load_base, ChunkedH3Runtime, ChunkGeometry, generate_sample

model = load_base("/path/to/h3-3step")
runtime = ChunkedH3Runtime(model, checkpoint_blocks=False)
video_rows, audio_rows = generate_sample(
    runtime, ChunkGeometry(), {"prompt_embeds": prompt_embeds},
    seed=20262020, nfe=3,
)
```

`prompt_embeds` is the positive H3 text-encoder output **before** the token refiner,
shape `[1, text_length, text_dim]`. See `infer.py` for text encoding and VAE decoding,
and `inference_config.json` for the chunk boundaries and paired audio/video schedules.
The current interface is first-clip text-to-audio/video, not long-video continuation.

## Video cases

These videos were generated with the **merged transformer** and the included 3-step-per-chunk sampler.
Native BF16/FP32 weights are retained. Merging introduces floating-point rounding,
so outputs can change in composition and are not pixel-identical to separate FP32 adapter inference.

# Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 - masked repaint with crop/paste-back (tutorial)

Editing a small region of a large image with a diffusion model normally forces you to downscale the whole picture and lose the detail you cared about. This graph takes the opposite route: paint a mask, crop that region out with padding information, repaint only the crop - with a reference image if you want object transfer - then paste the result back at full resolution.

**This repository ships the English tutorial plus the parsed parameter table.** The workflow JSON itself stays with the episode release; values quoted here were read from it.

## Contents

- `README.md` - this tutorial
- No JSON, no weights, no covers: the graph is available through the episode release / RunningHub page

## What it covers

- You need to change one object in a high-resolution image without downscaling it.
- You want to put an object from a reference image into a masked region ("everything transfer").
- You want a reusable paste-back step rather than manual compositing.

## How it works

1. Load the image, paint the mask, write the prompt.
2. The graph crops a padded square; repaint that block (add a reference image for object transfer).
3. Paste back using the stored padding info at full resolution.
4. Keep the longest edge at 2048 and the 4-step accelerator on.

# InfiniteTalk on ComfyUI - single/dual lip-sync loops and near-infinite length (tutorial)

InfiniteTalk is a Wan 2.1-based lip-sync method, and ComfyUI now supports it natively - the author says faster and better than the earlier KJ implementation, with only minor degradation for two-person shots. The interesting part is the loop: feed the rendered clip back as the next segment's first frame, compute the iteration count from the audio length, and you get near-infinite duration. The episode also updates the LTX-2 distilled talking-head graph.

**This repository ships the English tutorial plus the parsed parameter table.** The workflow JSON itself stays with the episode release; values quoted here were read from it.

## Contents

- `README.md` - this tutorial
- No JSON, no weights, no covers: the graph is available through the episode release / RunningHub page

## What it covers

- You need a talking clip longer than the ~3-second first window.
- You have one portrait and one audio track and want a repeatable loop.
- You want two characters alternating lines from a single image.

## How it works

1. Single: load image + audio, set audio start second and length, width and height, run.
2. Take the first 81 frames, then loop by feeding the clip back; compute iterations from audio ms.
3. Dual: two audios, one image, paint two masks; upscale with FlashVSR afterwards.
4. LTX-2 distilled: load image, set size and frame count, keep Camera Control LoRA enabled.

No UNET/CLIP/VAE sampler chain in this graph - it is a processing or composite graph. Node inventory: `FlashVSRNode`, `VHS_LoadVideo`, `VHS_VideoCombine`, `LayerUtility: ImageScaleByAspectRatio V2` (4 nodes).

# Seedance 2.0 post-production - watermark removal + interpolation + upscale (tutorial)

Seedance 2.0 clips come out of Xiaoyunque with a corner watermark and a modest frame rate. This episode chains two ComfyUI graphs to fix both: a MiniMax remover built on the early Wan 2.1 work to take the watermark out by masking it, then a GIMM interpolation pass and a FlashVSR upscale. The author reports the watermark is "almost gone" and the upscaled result reaches roughly 2K after a 960-pixel constraint.

**This repository ships the English tutorial plus the parsed parameter table.** The workflow JSON itself stays with the episode release; values quoted here were read from it.

## Contents

- `README.md` - this tutorial
- No JSON, no weights, no covers: the graph is available through the episode release / RunningHub page

## What it covers

- You generate clips yourself and want them clean and high-frame-rate before editing.
- Your delivery target wants 32 or 60 fps from a 16 fps source.
- You need a repeatable post chain instead of a one-off manual fix.

## How it works

1. Remove watermark: load clip, freeze first frame if needed, paint mask, prompt the masked area, run.
2. Interpolate + upscale: load clip, 2x interpolation, 3x upscale after 960 px constraint.
3. Both graphs are separate; chain them by feeding the cleaned clip into the second graph.

## Parameters

#### **minimax remover 视频去水印** - 26 nodes
No UNET/CLIP/VAE sampler chain in this graph - it is a processing or composite graph. Node inventory: `MaskToImage`, `WanVideoEncode`, `PreviewImage`, `VHS_VideoCombine`, `WanVideoMiniMaxRemoverEmbeds`, `LoadWanVideoT5TextEncoder`, `GrowMaskWithBlur`, `WanVideoVAELoader` (26 nodes).

#### **视频补帧+放大** - 7 nodes

This episode tests ControlNet 2.1 on Base, then repairs the aesthetics by splitting sampling: Base drives the high-noise half, Turbo takes the low-noise half and pulls quality back. # Z-Image Turbo - enhanced encoder + Flow-DPO + Ultra Real (tutorial notes)

Notes for the fixed-seed A/B of three Z-Image Turbo add-ons, and what happens when the winners are pushed into ControlNet segmented rendering.

## Contents

- `README.md` - this tutorial

## Graph facts (from the shipped JSON)

**Comparison test (47 nodes)** — four branches of `KSampler` at **9 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, denoise 1**.

- UNET `z_image_turbo_bf16.safetensors`
- CLIP `qwen_3_4b.safetensors` (qwen_image) and GGUF `Qwen3-4b-Z-Image-Engineer-V4-F16.gguf`
- VAE `ae.safetensors`
- LoRA `zit_fdpo_v1` at 1.0 / 0.8 / 0.72 and `lenovo__z` at 1.0 / 0.72

**Full comparison (180 nodes)** — same stack, plus a second `qwen_3_4b` loaded as `lumina2`, `ImageScaleBy` lanczos 1.5 on four branches, `CFGGuider` 1 throughout.

## Findings as reported

- Enhanced encoder fixes prompt adherence: without it the prompted tea set is absent; with it the table objects are correct.
- Flow-DPO gives the most satisfying colour and light of the four.
- Ultra Real at weight 1.0 degrades the image and reduces detail; the author recommends lowering it.
- Recommended daily stack: enhanced encoder + Flow-DPO at weight 0.8-0.7.

## ControlNet behaviour

The enhanced encoder breaks pose control in segmented CN rendering; the 2602 Turbo CN model in the high-noise segment locks the shape instead. Gain LoRAs only act in the low-noise segment, which runs 5 steps, so weight 1.0 is safe there.

## Limits

One prompt, one seed, four images. The "+60% data" claim is the encoder author's. Step counts and weights are coupled — retest if you change the low-noise step count.

# Anima Preview 2 - four ComfyUI graphs + the Anima-Enhancer node (tutorial notes)

Notes for the Anima Preview 2 episode: text-to-image, image-to-image, tiled upscale, a batch artist-style test, and the community enhancement node.

## Contents

- `README.md` - this tutorial

## Stack

- UNET `anima-preview2.safetensors`
- CLIP `qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors` (type `stable_diffusion`)
- VAE `qwen_image_vae.safetensors`

## Parameters from the shipped JSON

| Graph | Nodes | Sampler settings |
|---|---|---|
| Text-to-image | 14 | 20 steps / CFG 2.5 / denoise 0.65 and 30 steps / CFG 3 / denoise 1; `dpmpp_2m_sde_gpu`, `sgm_uniform`; scale 1.6 |
| Image-to-image | 13 | 40 steps / CFG 3 / denoise 0.75; scale 1.0486 |
| Tiled upscale | 25 | 20 steps / CFG 2 / denoise 0.25; `4x_NMKD-Siax_200k`; 3 MP lanczos |
| Batch style test | 16 | 30 steps / CFG 3 / denoise 1 and 20 steps / CFG 2.5 / denoise 0.65 |

## Anima-Enhancer defaults

`block_indices` 345, denoise 0.5 -> 1 (or 0.95/0.9), `enable_spectrum` off, spectrum 0.2/0.22, 8-12, 0.5, warm-up 6.

## Note on a conflict

The video recommends 30-50 steps and CFG 4-5; the JSON ships 20-40 steps and CFG 2.5-3. Reproduce from the JSON.

## Limits

1024-class model; quality collapses above ~1 megapixel. Artist tags need the `@` prefix. High denoise in tiled upscale causes seams.

## Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo

The official [Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) checkpoint is available as single-file WanGP weights:

- [BF16](qwen_image_21_turbo_7B_bf16.safetensors): original transformer tensors, merged without dtype conversion.
- [INT8 ConvRot](qwen_image_21_turbo_7B_int8_convrot.safetensors): quantized with WanGP's shared ConvRot converter.

Use **8 steps**, **CFG 1**, and WanGP's **Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo** scheduler. It uses the release's fixed sigmas `[1.0, 0.978453, 0.95418, 0.926626, 0.89508, 0.845148, 0.704534, 0.414568]`, followed by zero, with no dynamic shift or terminal remapping. Ordinary FlowMatch schedules are not the release's evaluated schedule. No acceleration LoRA is needed. The existing Qwen Image 2.1 text encoder and VAE are reused.

[Upstream license](qwen_image_21/turbo/LICENSE), [original model card](qwen_image_21/turbo/UPSTREAM_README.md), and [conversion provenance and checksums](qwen_image_21/turbo/provenance.json) are included. Packaging and scheduler checks were performed on CPU; full image generation was not tested in this packaging session.

# ✨ FLUX 3 Image Klein – Native 4-Channel RGBA Transparency Suite (Text-to-RGBA & Foreground Extraction LoRAs)

![Text-to-RGBA Showcase Banner](assets/civitai_cover_flux3_transparent_wide.png)
![Foreground Extraction Showcase Banner](assets/civitai_cover_flux3_extract_wide.png)

Complete **native 4-channel RGBA transparency suite** for **FLUX 3 Image Klein (5.6B)** in ComfyUI — featuring **two specialized LoRAs** and a **4-channel RGBA `AutoencoderKLFlux2` VAE**:

1. **🎨 `flux3_klein_transparent_lora.safetensors` (Text-to-Transparent-Image LoRA):** Generate brand-new 32-bit RGBA PNG assets directly from text prompts with native alpha transparency (`0.000` background alpha).
2. **✂️ `flux3_klein_extract_lora.safetensors` (Foreground-Extraction & Matting LoRA):** Extract subjects from existing RGB images directly into clean 4-channel RGBA cutouts using FLUX 3's native `ReferenceLatent` (`image_cond`) conditioning — either automatically or guided by your text prompt!

---

## 📦 Files Included in This Repository

| File | Target Folder in ComfyUI | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`flux3_klein_transparent_lora.safetensors`** | `ComfyUI/models/loras/` | **Part 1:** Rank-32 Text-to-Transparent-RGBA LoRA for FLUX 3 Image Klein (240 MB) |
| **`flux3_klein_extract_lora.safetensors`** | `ComfyUI/models/loras/` | **Part 2:** Foreground-Extraction & Matting RGBA LoRA using `ReferenceLatent` (87 MB) |
| **`vae/flux2_3_rgba_vae.safetensors`** | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` | Original 4-Channel RGBA `AutoencoderKLFlux2` VAE by **[trmz/flux2-klein-alpha](https://huggingface.co/trmz/flux2-klein-alpha/tree/main/vae)** (320 MB) |
| **`vae/flux3_ultra_rgba_vae.safetensors`** | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` | **Post-Trained 4-Channel RGBA VAE:** Decoder fine-tuned for cleaner transparent edges, reduced hidden-background color bleed (`-55%`), and higher foreground PSNR (`32.7 dB -> 39.3 dB`) |
| **`vae/flux3_ultra_rgb_vae.safetensors`** | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` | **Experimental 3-Channel RGB Photo VAE:** Pure 3-channel `ae_flux_3` decoder post-trained on 2K DSLR (`DIV2K`) & editorial (`Vogue Runway`) photography with phase-coherent YCbCr luminance-wavelet distillation (`~+18%` subtle micro-contrast on pores/hair, `0.00%` color shift) |
| **`workflows/Flux3_Klein_Transparent_RGBA.json`** | Drag & drop into ComfyUI | Ready-to-run ComfyUI workflow for **Text-to-RGBA Generation** |
| **`workflows/Flux3_Klein_Extract_RGBA.json`** | Drag & drop into ComfyUI | Ready-to-run ComfyUI workflow for **RGBA Foreground Extraction & Matting** |

---

## 🔧 Required ComfyUI Custom Nodes

Because standard ComfyUI VAE nodes only encode/decode 3 channels (`RGB`), install **[DenRakEiw_Nodes](https://github.com/DenRakEiw/DenRakEiw_Nodes)** to load, encode, and decode all 4 channels (`RGBA`):

```bash
cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/DenRakEiw/DenRakEiw_Nodes.git
```

### Included Nodes:
* **`🔧 Flux 2/3 RGBA VAE Loader *DRE`** – Loads `flux2_3_rgba_vae.safetensors` with dropdown selection and optional auto-download.
* **`🔍 Flux 2/3 RGBA VAE Decode *DRE`** – Decodes FLUX 2 / FLUX 3 128-channel latents into `rgba_image` (`[B, H, W, 4]`), `rgb_image` (`[B, H, W, 3]`), and `alpha_mask` (`MASK`).
* **`📥 Flux 2/3 RGBA VAE Encode *DRE`** – Encodes RGB/RGBA images into 128-channel latents (used with `ReferenceLatent` for Foreground Extraction).
* **`👁️ Preview Transparent Image`** – Live Checkerboard / White / Black background preview in ComfyUI.
* **`💾 Save Transparent Image`** – Saves true 32-bit RGBA PNGs with intact alpha channel.
* **`📊 Transparent Image Info`** – Alpha statistics & grayscale `alpha_preview` output.

---

## 🎨 LoRA 1: Text-to-Transparent-Image (`flux3_klein_transparent_lora.safetensors`)

| Elven Sorceress (Translucent Silk) | Steampunk Mechanical Owl | Cute Astronaut Red Panda | 3D Glossy Toy Robot |

Include the trigger phrase at the start or end of your prompt:
* **`RGBA transparent background, isolated foreground object`** *(recommended)*
* **`transparent background`**

```text
RGBA transparent background, isolated foreground object, an enchanting cute elven sorceress with pointed ears and emerald eyes, wearing a fitted white and gold silk dress with sheer translucent sleeves, glowing magical butterflies around her hands, long platinum hair, soft rim light, masterpiece character art, transparent background.
```

# Qwen-Image-2.1 — [GEN]图片生成v2.1

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README_CN.md)

## 1. Overview

Qwen-Image-2.1 text-to-image model: a prompt goes in, a 512×512 image comes out.

This repository ships the RK182x deployment artifacts (RKNN graphs +
weights) **together with the wdnwebui worker manifest**
(`qwenimage21.json`).

The pipeline is split across **three** compute devices:

| Stage | Device | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text encoder (TE) + DiT head | EP card 0 (RK182x) | RKNN3 |
| DiT, 4 segments | EP card 1 (RK182x) | RKNN3 |
| VAE decode (and VAE encode, for image-to-image) | the host RK3588's own NPU | RKNN2 |

Because the VAE is physically separate from the DiT, everything stays
resident: **the generation loop performs zero `model_init`**. A second
image costs only the sampling steps plus the decode.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model ID | `wardner/Qwen-Image-2.1` |
| Display name | Qwen-Image-2.1 |
| Model type | T2I (text-to-image) |
| Compute target | RK182x (×2) + host RK3588 NPU |
| Host platform | RK3588 |
| Runtime | RKNN3 + RKNN2 |
| Capabilities | `swcap_text_to_image` |
| Worker factory | `qwen_image_21_512` |

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

# MiniMax-H3 bX-49 — full hybrid teachers

Full (non-pruned) MiniMax-H3 checkpoints built the same way as the popular
`b25-49` pruned hybrids: **FL2VA is the base for the whole network**, and the
`adaln_proj` of **blocks X-49** is taken from **Ref2VA**.

Why: a pruned bX-49 file cannot be recorded from — it has no `time_embedder` and
its AdaLN is an 8-wide curve — so the exact modulation has to be reconstructed.
These files carry the whole AdaLN branch at full width. One recording pass on
one of them yields that hybrid's native modulation, and gives a **bitwise
end-to-end reference**: pruned bX-49 + table recorded here reproduces this file
exactly.

## Files

| file | split | replaced tensors | size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minimax_h3_hybrid_fl2va_ref2va_b5-49_full_int8.safetensors` | 5 | 180 | 31.7 GiB | `5100ee083264653c8f49dd5fdccd8a591a454810b565f64ac2e323c9e80f79a5` |
| `minimax_h3_hybrid_fl2va_ref2va_b20-49_full_int8.safetensors` | 20 | 120 | 31.7 GiB | `bae89706229fda2d6523a9ad028b2729f53b36be0cf224fe641c9a4993e84427` |
| `minimax_h3_hybrid_fl2va_ref2va_b25-49_full_int8.safetensors` | 25 | 100 | 31.7 GiB | `35a57db840bebe701b151cb9ea8c563db5b2d267927b283ad54162ee6418f84f` |
| `minimax_h3_hybrid_fl2va_ref2va_b30-49_full_int8.safetensors` | 30 | 80 | 31.7 GiB | `7f3e72d1479ded3b9880a10d838e22a3791e1c3be9a137fd5cb19a3f7f3550d5` |
| `minimax_h3_hybrid_fl2va_ref2va_b45-49_full_int8.safetensors` | 45 | 20 | 31.7 GiB | `e6538c349820db0d97c4e74c5ae8ba4f970e5a32fe100f6a2bcfa28a7562f5f6` |

Every file is a byte copy of `fl2va_int8_convrot` with the AdaLN block range
swapped in from `ref2va_int8_convrot` (4 tensors per block: `weight` I8,
`weight_scale` F32, `bias` BF16, `comfy_quant` U8). Tensor shapes and all
`data_offsets` entries are unchanged, so the FL2VA header stays valid.

Sources: [`Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3).

## Verification (byte level, every file)

- every replaced tensor is byte-identical to the Ref2VA source
- every other byte of the body is byte-identical to the FL2VA source
- `sha256` above

## End-to-end test

b25-49, both chains with the same LoRA, 8-step `simple`, shift 12/2, 832x480x39:

```
A: full b25-49 hybrid (native)
B: pruned b25-49 + table recorded on A
samples__part0: equal=True max_abs=0.000e+00 psnr=inf
samples__part1: equal=True max_abs=0.000e+00 psnr=inf
VERDICT: PASS - bitwise identical
```

## Which split should I use?

Pick the one that matches the pruned file you already run. A pruned bX-49 keeps
the base teacher's body and only adopts the donor's AdaLN from block X on, so
the split is a property of that file, not a quality dial:

- low X (5, 20) — most of the network modulated by Ref2VA: strongest reference
  conditioning, largest deviation from pure FL behaviour;
- 25 — the common `b25-49` recipe;
- high X (30, 45) — only the tail adopts Ref2VA, closest to plain FL.

## This is NOT the same target as the two-teacher merge

Recording FL2VA and Ref2VA separately and merging the tables gives a different
table for the tail blocks: FL and Ref do not share a `time_embedder`
(`proj_out.weight` differs by up to `0.104`), so the merged tail is Ref's
modulation computed with Ref's own embedding, while the tail blocks of a real
hybrid see the base teacher's embedding. Measured on b25-49: blocks 0-24 and
`final_layer` bitwise identical, blocks 25-49 differ by up to `0.19`; applying
the merged table to the pruned file and comparing against this model gives
`psnr=22.20 dB` / `31.10 dB`.

To reach the same target without a merged checkpoint, record Ref2VA full with
`H3AdaLNRecord.time_embedder_from = <FL2VA checkpoint>` and merge that table —
it matches these files bitwise (25/25 tail projections, 51/51 after the merge).

## Usage

1. `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`; the stock MiniMax-H3 loader accepts them
   (int8 convrot, same as the official full builds).
2. With [`ComfyUI-H3-ExactAdaLN`](https://github.com/bingling360/ComfyUI-H3-ExactAdaLN):
   load one (+ your LoRA) -> `H3 AdaLN Record` before the guider -> run the
   schedule you will use -> `H3 Exact AdaLN Save Table` -> on the matching
   pruned bX-49, `H3 Exact AdaLN Apply`. One teacher, one recording, no merge.

A table recorded with one LoRA reproduces the model with a **different**
non-AdaLN LoRA bitwise; only LoRAs that touch `time_embedder` / `adaln_proj`
(acceleration / distillation LoRAs) need a re-record.

## Limits

- A table is a function of (weights, LoRA stack and strengths, sigma grid,
  shifts, packed layout); change any of them and it must be re-recorded.
- `out_dtype` is fixed at recording time; these models run bf16 maths.
- Derivative of MiniMax H3: the merge and quantisation are Apache 2.0, the
  underlying weights remain under MiniMax's own license.

# FLUX 3 Image Klein — Multiple Angles LoRA

Camera-control LoRA for [FLUX 3 Image Klein (base)](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base): re-render a subject from a new camera pose — 8 azimuths × 5 elevations × optional distance — using fal's `<mva>` prompt grammar (the one from the Qwen-Image multiple-angles LoRAs).

Full 360° orbit around a dog, a cat and a person, driven by the same `<mva>` azimuth prompts:

![360 degree camera orbit around a dog, a cat and a person](./angles_lora_orbit.gif)

## Usage (diffusers)

```python
import torch
from diffusers.modular_pipelines import Flux3AutoBlocks

blocks = Flux3AutoBlocks()
blocks.sub_blocks.pop("prompt_upsampler", None)  # important: LoRA expects raw prompts
pipe = blocks.init_pipeline("black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base")
pipe.load_components(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
pipe.to("cuda")
pipe.load_lora_weights("akhaliq/flux-3-image-klein-angles-lora")

image = pipe(
    prompt="<mva> right side view, elevated shot",
    image=input_image,            # your reference image (PIL)
    num_inference_steps=50,
    generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(0),
    output="images",
)[0]
```

## Prompt grammar

```
<mva> {azimuth} view, {elevation} shot[ close-up]
```

| Azimuths | Elevations | Distance |
|---|---|---|
| front view | low-angle shot | (none) |
| front-right / front-left quarter view | eye-level shot | close-up |
| right / left side view | elevated shot | |
| back-right / back-left (quarter) view | high-angle shot | |
| back view | top-down shot | |

## Training details

- **Base model:** `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base` (undistilled, trained via the public mirror)
- **Script:** [diffusers `train_dreambooth_lora_flux3_klein_img2img.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/examples/dreambooth/train_dreambooth_lora_flux3_klein_img2img.py) (i2i DreamBooth)
- **Dataset:** [akhaliq/flux3-multiple-angles-train-4k](https://huggingface.co/datasets/akhaliq/flux3-multiple-angles-train-4k) (4,000 synthetic render pairs, fal `<mva>` grammar)
- **Config:** rank 16 / alpha 16, bf16, 512px, lr 1e-4 constant, 8-bit AdamW, 2000 steps on A100 (checkpoints at 500/1000/1500/2000 in the repo)
- Trained 2026-10-16, the day after the FLUX 3 Image Klein open-weights release

## Limitations

Trained on **synthetic 3D renders**, so it generalizes unevenly to real photos: people and animals re-angle reliably, but plain objects can be replaced by hallucinated subjects or scenes on some prompts. A v2 mixing in real multi-view photo data is planned.

## Demo

Try it: [akhaliq/flux3-klein-angles-demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/akhaliq/flux3-klein-angles-demo)

## License

Trained on top of FLUX 3 Image Klein — weights subject to the [FLUX Kommunity License](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base/blob/main/LICENSE.md).

## 🚀 Updates

**2025.11.09 - Version 2.5.5**

- 💾 **Memory: Fixed RAM leak for long videos** - On-demand reconstruction with lightweight batch indices instead of storing full transformed videos, fixed release_tensor_memory to handle CPU/CUDA/MPS consistently, and refactored batch processing helpers

**2025.11.08 - Version 2.5.4**

- 🎨 **Fix: AdaIN color correction** - Replace `.view()` with `.reshape()` to handle non-contiguous tensors after spatial padding, resolving "view size is not compatible with input tensor's size and stride" error
- 🔴 **Fix: AMD ROCm compatibility** - Add cuDNN availability check in Conv3d workaround to prevent "ATen not compiled with cuDNN support" error on ROCm systems (AMD GPUs on Windows/Linux)

- **Global Model Cache**: Models now shared across multiple upscaler instances with automatic config updates - no more redundant loading
- **ComfyUI V3 Migration**: Full compatibility with ComfyUI V3 stateless node design
- **RGBA Support**: Native alpha channel processing with edge-guided upscaling for clean transparency
- **Improved Memory Management**: Streaming architecture prevents VRAM spikes regardless of video length
- **Flexible Resolution Support**: Upscale to any resolution divisible by 2 with lossless padding approach (replaced restrictive cropping)
- **Enhanced Parameters**: Added `uniform_batch_size`, `temporal_overlap`, `prepend_frames`, and `max_resolution` for better control

### 🖥️ CLI Enhancements

- **Batch Directory Processing**: Process entire folders of videos/images with model caching for efficiency
- **Single Image Support**: Direct image upscaling without video conversion
- **Smart Output Detection**: Auto-detects output format (MP4/PNG) based on input type
- **Enhanced Multi-GPU**: Improved workload distribution with temporal overlap blending
- **Unified Parameters**: CLI and ComfyUI now use identical parameter names for consistency
- **Better UX**: Auto-display help, validation improvements, progress tracking, and cleaner output

# MiniDF pixel map — Qwen Image 2.1 LoRA (final A)

Turns an oblique 3D map render of Brasília into the isometric pixel-art look of the [MiniDF map](https://cadeoflavio.marceloeduardo.com/), which Codex paints frame by frame. Image-to-image LoRA; winner of the first training round (7 Nov 2026). Training log: [marceloeduardo.com/pixel-lora-training.html](https://marceloeduardo.com/pixel-lora-training.html).

## Use

```python
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline
from PIL import Image

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda")
pipe.load_lora_weights("handful/mndf-pixel-qwen-image-2.1")
render = Image.open("render.jpg").convert("RGB")          # 1024x1024 oblique 3D render
out = pipe(image=render, prompt="Repaint this 3D map render as mndfstyle isometric pixel-art map of Brasília, keeping every road, building and tree in place",
           width=1024, height=1024, num_inference_steps=28).images[0]   # no guidance (pipeline default)
```

## Training

diffusers `train_dreambooth_lora_qwenimage21_img2img.py` · rank 16 · alpha 16 · lr 1e-4 constant · random flip · 1024 px · batch 1 · 3,750 steps (~100 min on one RTX PRO 6000) · 188 Brasília pairs.

## Evaluation

Round-1 judge (32 held-out Brasília frames): LPIPS 0.416. On the later five-group test set: 0.410 (Brasília 0.401, landmarks 0.409, São Paulo 0.396, Rio 0.412, world 0.429).

## Limitations and data

- **Training data:** ~2,000 pairs of (oblique 3D render of a 1024 px map frame → Codex painting of the same frame), mostly Brasília, plus São Paulo, water/shorelines and 42 world-landmark frames. The 3D inputs are renders of **Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles**; Google's Map Tiles terms do not allow using their content to train models. This LoRA is shared as a research experiment; check those terms before using it for anything beyond that.
- **Look:** water comes out brighter than the target's deep teal; very fine lattices (e.g. the Torre de TV) only appear when the 3D render shows them.
- **Input:** works best on renders like the training ones: 1024×1024, ~30° oblique, ~3.4 px per metre.

# LTX 2.5 Stubelius Remix

## v1 update (2026-10-07)

The remix is out of beta. v1 is beta 2 plus one thing I tested properly before baking it in: OmniNFT, a reinforcement-learning fine-tune that rewards video and audio quality, merged in at its trained strength. Everything else is the same as beta 2. It's still mainly meant for NSFW work but can do SFW (name the clothing in SFW prompts, or you may get unwanted nudity), and the distilled LoRA is still baked in.

![Beta 2 vs v1, same prompt and seed, 100% crop](images/compare_beta2_v1.jpg)

What changed, measured against beta 2 on my test prompts:
- **Sharper fine detail: +55%.** Faces, hair, fabric and backgrounds come out crisper.
- **A bit more motion: +15%.**
- **Same remix.** Prompt following, loudness and dialogue unchanged; dialogue lines still come out word for word. Colour is the same on average, though a few scenes come out less saturated.
- **Blind A/B:** in a blind, AI-judged comparison of full-resolution frames, OmniNFT at the strength v1 bakes in won 29 to 9 against beta 2, with 10 ties.
- I tested VBVR too. It cost motion and didn't improve prompt following, so it isn't in.

### Files

| File | Size | |
|---|---|---|
| `ltx2.5-Stubelius_remix_v1_int8_convrot.safetensors` | 21.5 GB | **v1, the one to use** (ComfyUI int8) |
| `ltx2.5-Stubelius_remix_v1_bf16.safetensors` | 42 GB | v1 in bf16, for merging and your own conversions |
| `ltx2.5-Stubelius_remix_v1_nvfp4.safetensors` | 14.4 GB | v1 in NVFP4 for RTX 50-series (Blackwell) cards, **experimental** (see below) |
| `ltx2.5-Stubelius_remix_v1_Q4_K_S.gguf` | 12.5 GB | v1 as GGUF Q4 for low-VRAM cards, **experimental**, fixed 8 Nov 2026 (see below) |
| `ltx2.5-Stubelius_remix_beta2_int8_convrot.safetensors`, `ltx2.5-Stubelius_remix_beta2_bf16.safetensors` | 21.5 / 42 GB | beta 2 |
| `ltx2.5-Stubelius_remix_beta1.safetensors` | 42 GB | beta 1 |

### How to run v1

- Put it in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models` and load it with Load Diffusion Model, or pick it in the Models node of Stubelius Ultimate LTX 2.5.
- CFG 1, 8 steps (plus 3–4 steps if you run an upscale pass). The distilled LoRA and OmniNFT are already baked in, so don't add either.
- Text encoder: `gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors`. Lightricks re-uploaded it in mid-August; download it again if your copy is older. VAEs: `ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16` and `ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16`.
- The int8 file needs a ComfyUI recent enough to load Comfy-Org's int8 LTX 2.5 files. LTX 2.5 LoRAs load on it the same way as on stock LTX 2.5.

### NVFP4 (experimental)

A smaller 4-bit version of the same v1 weights for RTX 50-series cards: transformer blocks 0–41 in NVFP4, the last 6 blocks and the text connectors in int8. That's Lightricks' own layer choice for their NVFP4 file, with int8 where they kept bf16.

- Same settings as int8: CFG 1, 8 steps. Load it the same way.
- It's only fast on RTX 50-series (Blackwell) cards, with a recent ComfyUI (0.32 or newer) and PyTorch built for CUDA 13. Older cards can run it, but slower than the int8 file, so stay on int8 there.
- It's new. The weights check out: every 4-bit layer is within normal NVFP4 rounding, and the OmniNFT change is kept. I haven't finished comparing its renders against int8 yet, though, so if something looks off, switch to int8 and tell me.

### GGUF Q4 (experimental)

The smallest version, for low-VRAM cards: the transformer's big layers in Q4_K, the small, sensitive ones (the timestep and adaLN layers, the input and output layers, the gates) in BF16, as in the int8 file.

- **Fixed on 8 November 2026. If you downloaded this file before then, download it again.** The first upload stored three small weights (the text connectors' register tokens and the keyframe marker) in BF16, which ComfyUI-GGUF can't use outside its layers, so sampling stopped with "Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 1. Expected size 4096 but got size 8192". The new file stores those three in F32, which loses nothing; every other weight is byte for byte the same.
- Needs [ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF). Load it with Unet Loader (GGUF), or pick it in the Models node of Stubelius Ultimate LTX 2.5. Same settings as int8: CFG 1, 8 steps.
- On 8 GB cards ComfyUI keeps the part that doesn't fit in VRAM in system RAM, so more RAM helps.
- Tested on 8 November 2026 in Stubelius Ultimate LTX 2.5 (RTX 5090): text only, first / middle / last frames, and Licon MSR with three Cast references all render, and the same-seed renders match the int8 file closely in composition, motion and detail.

# MCNL v1 — Multi Concept NSFW LoRA for Qwen Image Edit

A LoRA adapter for the [Qwen-Image-Edit-2511](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511) diffusion pipeline, enabling NSFW content generation and editing capabilities.

## Model Details

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Base Model** | Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 |
| **Architecture** | QwenImageTransformer2DModel (MMDiT) LoRA |
| **File Size** | ~563 MB |
| **Format** | safetensors |
| **License** | OpenRAIL++ |

## Usage

### With the ScottzillaSystems Image Editor Space

The easiest way to use this LoRA is through the [ScottzillaSystems Image Editor](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ScottzillaSystems/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-LoRAs-Fast) — select "🔥 MCNL-NSFW-v1" from the adapter dropdown.

### Programmatic Usage

```python
from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline
import torch

pipe = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).to("cuda")

# Load this LoRA
pipe.load_lora_weights(
    "ScottzillaSystems/qwen-image-edit-plus-nsfw-lora",
    weight_name="qwen-image-edit-plus-nsfw-lora.safetensors",
    adapter_name="mcnl-nsfw-v1"
)
pipe.set_adapters(["mcnl-nsfw-v1"])

# Edit an image
from PIL import Image
image = Image.open("input.jpg").convert("RGB")
result = pipe(
    image=image,
    prompt="nsfw",
    num_inference_steps=40,
    true_cfg_scale=4.0,
    negative_prompt=" ",
).images[0]
result.save("output.jpg")
```

## Trigger Words

Use these concepts in your prompts to activate specific capabilities:

`nsfw` `nipples` `vagina` `penis` `missionary` `cowgirlout` `reversecowgirlpov` `blowjob` `cum_on_face` `creamp1e` `l1ck`

# MiniMax-H3 FL2VA 8-Step Turbo (Permanently Baked GGUF Suite)

This repository hosts standalone, permanently baked **8-step distilled Turbo** versions of the **MiniMax-H3 FL2VA** foundation model (generating high-definition video with native synchronized stereo audio).

### Why Baked GGUFs?
In standard workflows, MiniMax-H3 requires 50 steps and loading separate LoRA adapters at runtime. Applying runtime adapters to quantized GGUF integer weights causes either massive VRAM dequantization spikes (triggering OOM crashes on consumer GPUs) or slow dual-branch execution.

These models were created by permanently fusing the official **MiniMax-H3 8-step Turbo LoRA** (`minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_comfyui_bf16.safetensors`) directly into the base weights offline via **FP32 matrix fusion**:

$$W_{\text{baked}} = \text{Quantize}\left(\text{Dequantize}(W_{\text{base}}) + \frac{\alpha}{r}(B \times A)\right)$$

Zero runtime LoRA overhead, zero extra VRAM required, and 8-step generation works out of the box.

---

Lowest memory footprint (~3.1 GB headroom on 12GB GPUs) with near-Q4 fidelity. |

# Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo · Siliconed SQ4

The transformer (DiT) of [Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo), by Qwen (Hangzhou Tongyi Laboratory), quantized to
**SQ4**, the 4-bit weight format of [Siliconed](https://github.com/gwenn-ha-dev/Siliconed), a text-to-image app for Apple silicon written in Swift and
Metal. Each linear is at 4, 5 or 8 bits, 4.72 bits per weight on average. This is the transformer of Siliconed's
**Light** version, from Siliconed 0.21: one self-contained file of 4.39 GB, against 14.23 GB for the
publisher's bf16.

It is closer to the full-precision model than the published GGUF Q4_K_M it replaces, at every layer
and at the model's output (below), and on Siliconed it runs at about the speed of the 8-bit Compact, with less memory.

**Only Siliconed reads it.** It is not a GGUF and loads in neither diffusers nor ComfyUI: the format is specified below,
and its decoder is open source with the app (`Sources/Siliconed/SQ.swift`). The text encoder and the VAE are not in this
repository; Siliconed takes them from their publishers.

## Files

| File | Bytes | sha256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `qwen-image-2.1-turbo-sq4.safetensors` | 4,385,824,160 | `d289920998192edc414b447f26e83230de1afd820bcad5bce559b7e4ec666e57` |

225 linears of the transformer: 184 SQ4, 32 SQ5, 7 SQ8, 2 BF16. Every other tensor (74 tensors: 74 BF16) is the publisher's,
bit for bit. The metadata name the base model's repository, revision, files and their sha256.

## Why another 4-bit format

GGUF's Q4_K carries a float scale every 32 weights along K, so a product with int8 activations has to be cut into
32-wide partial sums, each multiplied by its own float. SQ keeps **one float per output row**: every group's code
decodes to an exact int8, and

```
y[t, n] = s[n] · Σ_k (x·R)[t, k] · v[n, k]        v[n, k] ∈ [−128, 127], an integer
```

so the whole K reduction is one integer (int8 × int8, activations rotated and quantized per token) or float × int8 dot
product: the route Siliconed's 8-bit Compact already runs, Metal on the GPU. The 16-weight groups and the Hadamard
rotation (the one of Comfy's int8 *convrot*) make up for the coarser scale.

## Accuracy

Judged against the exact value, never against another quantization. **Distance** is the relative error channel by
channel (per output channel, the L2 of the error over the L2 of the exact output, floored at 1 % of the median
channel), reported as the worst channel / the median channel. The exact value is a float64 witness of the reference
pipeline (diffusers) where one was computed, else the float32 oracle on the publisher's bf16 weights (within 10⁻³
of the witness). Judge prompts and seeds are disjoint from the calibration's.

- **Layers.** At every block linear (225), on its real inputs, the error of the quantized weight against the exact
  float64 product: SQ4's is smaller than the Q4_K_M's at **all 225**.
- **Output.** One evaluation of the whole transformer per point, model output against the exact value:

# SeedVR2-3B Snapdragon NPU conversion (experimental, unofficial)

This is a modified deployment conversion of [ByteDance SeedVR2-3B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR2-3B), not a newly trained model. The transformer was split into 32 static 256-token ONNX graphs and quantized with mixed group-wise W4/W8 weights and A16 activations; the image VAE uses W8A16. RMS normalization was rewritten with ONNX Runtime SimplifiedLayerNormalization to avoid observed quantization instability. The head and tail include fixed conditioning and the single-step inference components. This is a single-image inference conversion, not a general video model export.

## Compatibility and limitations

The complete conversion was tested through a custom Android pipeline on a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 (SM8550, HTP v73, 8 GB RAM), using ONNX Runtime 1.29.0, ONNX Runtime QNN execution provider 2.7.0 and QAIRT 2.51.0, with CPU fallback disabled for accelerator graphs. The baseline conversion was also exercised on one Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 phone (SM8650). Other devices and runtimes are untested. The transformer graphs use an ONNX Runtime-specific SimplifiedLayerNormalization operator; they are not a drop-in general ONNX model and require a compatible runtime and supporting code. Static shapes are 256 video tokens, 58 text tokens and 2560 hidden dimensions. These files alone do not include a ready-to-use application, tile processing pipeline, NPU runtime or inference script.

The device used SoC-specific precompiled QNN contexts. **Those contexts and Qualcomm runtime libraries are not included in this initial release.** The ONNX files here are the corrected patched graphs, whereas the current prototype app expects separate on-device context files and does not yet download this repository. They cannot be copied into a stock app to make it work. Generating compatible contexts requires the matching Qualcomm tooling and validation. Support beyond those two tested phones is not established.

The model can produce tile seams, tonal shifts, and invented or altered detail. This is experimental; no quantitative quality claim across a representative dataset is made. On the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, one portrait took 267 seconds to produce a 1992 × 2560 output; performance varies with image dimensions, device state, and thermal conditions. These measurements do not establish hardware maximum utilization. The upstream model is for restoration; not all generated details reflect the source.

## Optional faster decoder (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 experiment)

`onnx/vae/decoder_256_w8a16_groupnorm.onnx` is an additional W8A16 decoder graph. It replaces 30 decomposed normalization sequences with ONNX GroupNormalization while preserving the original boundary quantization scales. It removes intermediate quantization roundings, so results are not bit-identical. The original decoder remains available.

A single Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 phone (SM8650 / HTP v75) was tested with ONNX Runtime 1.29.0, ONNX Runtime QNN EP 2.7.0 and QAIRT 2.51.0. A custom QNN HTP context was compiled from this exact ONNX graph using those tools, with CPU fallback disabled. For three latent tiles, the optimized decoder measured 276–278 ms per tile versus 464–469 ms for a QNN context compiled from the baseline `onnx/vae/decoder_256_w8a16.onnx` on the same phone and runtime. One full 1992 × 2560 portrait completed in 165 seconds versus 189 seconds in a separate prior run; output PSNR versus the output of the earlier 189-second run was 55.7 dB (8-bit peak 255, maximum per-channel difference 4/255). Only the decoder was changed; these were separate runs, not a controlled end-to-end A/B trial. The three raw decoder tile comparisons were 61.4–63.0 dB PSNR on a [-1,1] signal with peak range 2. Results may vary by image, thermal state and runtime; these are not broad quality or compatibility claims. The optimized decoder was not validated on Gen 2.

The file SHA-256 is `fa55e9f0f3bba65566caf72279eb550f2c507e5622e9befa4be3ba3dd6474359`; size is 52,830,295 bytes. The graph uses ONNX opset 21 and Microsoft-domain quantization operators and is validated with the runtime versions above; it is not a precompiled QNN context or a guarantee of compatibility with arbitrary ONNX runtimes. Compiling and deploying it requires a compatible QNN runtime, tooling and application; the current prototype does not download model files. No Qualcomm runtime or proprietary context is included.

## Files

- `onnx/dit/block00_256.onnx` through `block31_256.onnx`: quantized, modified transformer blocks in execution order.
- `onnx/vae/`: quantized single-frame encoder, baseline decoder, and optional `decoder_256_w8a16_groupnorm.onnx`.
- `onnx/pipeline/`: fixed-shape head and tail graphs, including fixed conditioning.
- `SHA256SUMS`: checksums for model ar

> **Language**: English | [中文](README_CN.md)

## 9.20 GiB less after load (46.4%) · text-to-image 2.43× faster · editing 2.02× faster

FP4 on an RTX 5090, compared with the BF16 transformer.

4-bit weight-and-activation quantization of the Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo transformer, rank 32, for inference with Nunchaku. Combat Base V2 is no longer just a combat LoRA — it now works for both action and dialogue scenes, adding richer body movement, finer sound details, and stronger shot-to-shot continuity to character performance.

Core Physics & Motion Logic / 核心物理与动作逻辑
Combat Base V2 moves away from "attack → reset" loops into a continuous physical chain where missed strikes carry momentum, blocks change direction smoothly, and limbs separate cleanly without sticking.

Hit reactions now persist and accumulate—sustained torso bending, lowered guards, and impaired mobility directly build toward convincing heavy finishers.

受击状态具备持续性与累计效应，躯干弯曲、护架变慢及移动受限等伤害会自然保留，让最后的重击终结更加合理成立。

Upgrades include continuous rotational kicks, sustained grappling and takedowns, dynamic 3-stage environmental collisions, and multi-phase fall trajectories.
