Quantized GGUF versions of [WarmBloodAban/Minimax-H3 Singularity](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity), optimized for [ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF).

---

## 📁 Available GGUF Files & Sizes

| Filename | File Size | Quantization Type | Recommended VRAM / Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Minimax-h3-Singularity-ref2va-v2-Pruned-Q3_K_M.gguf` | **8.9 GB** | `Q3_K_M` (3-bit Medium) | Low-VRAM systems (12 GB–16 GB VRAM) |
| `Minimax-h3-Singularity-ref2va-v2-Pruned-Q4_K_M.gguf` | **11.6 GB** | `Q4_K_M` (4-bit Medium) | **Sweet Spot** for standard GPUs (16 GB–24 GB VRAM) |
| `Minimax-h3-Singularity-ref2va-v2-Pruned-Q5_K_M.gguf` | **14.1 GB** | `Q5_K_M` (5-bit Medium) | High fidelity for 24 GB+ VRAM |
| `Minimax-h3-Singularity-ref2va-v2-Pruned-Q6_K.gguf` | **16.7 GB** | `Q6_K` (6-bit) | Near-lossless quality |

---

## 🛠️ Engineering & Pruning Details

- **Curve-Pruned AdaLN Architecture:** The 51 unpruned AdaLN modulation modules (`[Out, 2688]`) from the original 34GB checkpoint were projected onto the canonical rank-8 Ref2VA subspace (`adaln_basis` + `adaln_mean`), reducing parameters by **13.03 Billion** and saving ~26 GB of disk space.
- **Lossless Precision Guards:** All normalization layers (`RMSNorm`, `LayerNorm`), timestep embeddings (`adaln_t_table`), and modality input/output heads (`video_patch_proj`, `audio_patch_proj`, `final_layer.video_out`, `final_layer.audio_out`) are preserved in **lossless FP32**.
- **ConvRot Un-Rotation:** Source INT8 weights were accurately un-rotated using ComfyUI's exact **Regular Hadamard ($H_4^{\otimes 4}$)** transform in `float64` before K-quantization, eliminating quantization artifacts and color shifts.
- **LoRA Compatibility:** Includes the canonical `adaln_affine.safetensors` curve basis, ensuring 100% compatibility with the ComfyUI pruned H3 LoRA and PowerLoRA stack ecosystem.

---

## 🚀 How to Use in ComfyUI

1. Place your chosen `.gguf` file into your ComfyUI models folder:
   `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`
2. Load the model using **`UnetLoaderGGUF`**.
3. Pair it with the Qwen3-VL text encoder and MiniMax-H3 Video + Audio VAEs.

---

# SANA-Video 2.0 5B 4-step: Style Video-to-Video LoRA (c20)

A rank-32 LoRA for NVIDIA's **SANA-Video 2.0 5B 720p 4-step** model that restyles a video into one of **20 looks**. It takes the source video
and a styled version of its first frame, and **keeps the look for the whole clip** while following the source's motion. The look is set by the
styled frame and a one-sentence look prompt. Without this LoRA, the 4-step model holds the styled first frame for a moment and then slides back
to the photographic source. c20 was trained only on **pairs that SANA-Video 2.0's own 4-step model generated and that were then verified**:
cycle pairs of a styled clip and its photographic twin with the same motion. No other video model and no real video were used. On 200 held-out
restyles (10 source videos x 20 looks), the clip keeps its look in **191 / 200** (CLIP) against 95 / 200 with the same recipe minus the style
training. With the **s2x** schedule, which follows the source's motion more closely and is recommended for 17 of the 20 looks, it keeps the
look in **171 / 200** against 30 / 200. c20 was grown from the first-frame LoRA [f3](#lineage) and still does picture-to-video. All numbers are reproducible with
[`eval/`](eval/).

# SANA-Video 2.0 5B 4-step: First-Frame LoRA (f3)

A rank-32 LoRA for NVIDIA's **SANA-Video 2.0 5B 720p 4-step** model that teaches it two picture-conditioned tasks it was not trained for:
**picture to video** (the clip starts on your picture and stays on it) and **first + last frame** (the clip starts on one picture and lands on
another). NVIDIA released the 4-step model as a text-to-video research preview, *"not intended for first-frame image conditioning"*. The
transformer does take a timestep per latent frame, though, so a picture can be held in place ("pinned") while the rest of the clip is
generated. Without training, the student often drifts off a pinned picture, and with two pinned pictures it tends to hold still and then snap to the end.
f3 was trained **only on clips that SANA-Video 2.0's own 4-step model generated and that were then verified** (self-distillation: the model is
its own teacher). No other video model and no real video were used. On 100 held-out pictures it stays on the subject more often (CLIP), and
on first + last frame it lands closer to the target with **42 % more motion and a much smaller end snap**. All of these numbers are reproducible
with the scripts and inputs in [`eval/`](eval/).

# Qwen symbolic thinking: image training

Teaching a Qwen3.5 vision-language model to think about a picture in writing, the way the rows of
[thought-symbolic-image-captions](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AbstractPhil/thought-symbolic-image-captions) do: a short
chain of plain-language thoughts, one step each (`see`, `count`, `light`, `mood` ...), ending in a caption.

```
see: One man in an apron stands in front of two ovens.
place: A working kitchen; pans hang on the wall behind him.
mood: A kitchen at work reads as warm and busy.
caption: A man in an apron standing by two ovens in a kitchen.
```

The code lives at [github.com/AbstractEyes/qwen-symbolic-thinking](https://github.com/AbstractEyes/qwen-symbolic-thinking);
this repository holds the data files, the screens and the adapters.

## What is here

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `screens/inputs/screen_v1.json` | the behaviour screen's rows: 60 picture rows (COCO 2017 images named by id, fetched from the COCO site at run time) and 40 specification rows, with two worked examples per depth |
| `sft/sft_v1.json` | the first fine-tune set: 978 picture rows outside the screen and 978 specification rows (1,956 items) |
| `screens/<stamp>/` | a screen's answers (`results.jsonl`: the text, the parse and the reads per answer), per-model summaries, `summary.md`, `env.json` |
| `screens/<stamp>_throughput*/` | a throughput sweep: rows an hour, seconds a row, tokens a second and peak memory per batch size |
| `lora/<model>/r<rank>/<stamp>_<arm>/` | LoRA adapters shipped during and after training (`step_N/`, `final/`), with `train_summary.json` |
| `sft/pictures_v2.json`, `sft/drawn_deep_v2.json`, `synth/` | the whole-row training sets and the synthetic rows (below) |
| `runs/queue_lane*.json`, `runs/done/*.json` | the queues the cards worked through unattended, and each run's record |

## The base models, screened

Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-4B, shown a picture and asked plainly (an RTX PRO 6000, greedy decoding, thinking off). Reads per
answer: the form held (`step: text` lines and a caption), the number of thoughts against the depth asked for, the share of
the row's specification said, and two habits the dataset bans (defining a word instead of looking; remarking on the task).

| model | form | format held | thoughts in range | spec words said | s a row (batch 4) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | instructions + two examples | 1.00 | 0.98 | 0.43 | 0.56 |
| Qwen3.5-9B | instructions only | 1.00 | 0.43 | 0.47 | 1.42 |
| Qwen3.5-4B | instructions + two examples | 1.00 | 0.62 | 0.37 | 0.91 |

# Koharu NVFP4 GGUF (Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo transformer)

A GGML **NVFP4** quantization of the
[Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) diffusion
transformer, made for [stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp)
and the [Koharu](https://github.com/koharu-rs/koharu) manga translator's text-cleanup stage.
NVFP4 runs on the native FP4 tensor cores of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (RTX 50 series, B-series).

Built with Qwen.

> **License: Qwen RESEARCH LICENSE AGREEMENT. Non-commercial use only**
> (research or evaluation). Commercial use needs a separate license from the Qwen team
> (model-business@notice.qwencloud.com). See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE).

## Files

| File | Size | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen-image-2.1-turbo-NVFP4.gguf` | 5.69 GB | Diffusion transformer only |
| `nvfp4_repack.py` | | The conversion script |
| `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` | | License and attribution |

sha256 `0ac8acb9cfe4e85bbc2272416e31f1d92a89e272553e827770ef7f2ff7efdd80`

The text encoder and VAE are not included. Use them from the usual sources, for example
the [Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF)
(with its `mmproj`) and `vae/qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors` from
[unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-FP8](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-FP8).

## Modifications

This file is a modified version of the original model:

- Source: `qwen-image-2.1-turbo-F16.gguf` from
  [unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF),
  revision `5d1f9f7` (sha256 `4f2241cb…7e80f`).
- 144 transformer weight matrices are quantized to GGML NVFP4 (block of 64, one UE4M3
  scale per 16 weights). The other 121 tensors keep the source F16/BF16 data unchanged.
- Which matrices are NVFP4 follows the selective layout of
  [BennyDaBall/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/BennyDaBall/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-NVFP4),
  but the weights are quantized directly from F16 rather than repacked from that file.
  GGML NVFP4 has no per-tensor scale, so repacking would round twice.
- Per 16-weight block, the converter tries several UE4M3 scales near `amax / 6` and keeps
  the one with the lowest squared error. Mean relative weight error is 0.088 (max 0.092).
  For comparison, the ComfyUI NVFP4 file measured 0.094 against the same F16 weights.

Reproduce with:

```bash
python nvfp4_repack.py convert-f16 qwen_image_2.1_turbo_nvfp4.safetensors qwen-image-2.1-turbo-F16.gguf qwen-image-2.1-turbo-NVFP4.gguf
```

(The ComfyUI checkpoint is read only for its list of quantized layers.)

## Measurements

These numbers come from an RTX 5090 running stable-diffusion.cpp `master-1043-3be2378`.
The test was manga text inpainting with 8 steps, strength 1.0 and Flash Attention:

| Transformer | Steady sampling speed | Mean pixel diff vs F16 (masked) |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K_M | ~12 it/s | 0.50 |
| F16 | ~13.8 it/s | 0 |
| **NVFP4 (this file)** | **~19 it/s** | 0.64 |

On a 13-page manga cleanup job, the full job took 127 s with this file against 136 s with
Q4_K_M, and the outputs looked the same. It was only tested on Blackwell. On GPUs without
native FP4 support, a K-quant is likely the better choice.

# MiniMax H3 — NVFP4

NVFP4 quantizations of the **MiniMax-H3** diffusion transformer for ComfyUI — both task
variants, `ref2va` (reference images → video) and `fl2va` (first/last frame → video).

- Original model: https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3
- ComfyUI repackage these derive from: https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3

**NVFP4 requires an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU** (RTX 50-series, RTX PRO 6000, B200). On Ada,
Hopper or older the NVFP4 path is emulated — use Comfy-Org's `int8_convrot` files instead.

## Which file do I want?

First pick the **task**, then the file:

- **`ref2va`** — up to 9 reference images (+ videos/audio) → video. Identity-driven.
- **`fl2va`** — first and/or last frame → video. Interpolates between endpoints; also how
  you chain clips past one generation by feeding the previous clip's last frame in.

| file | size | s/it | VRAM (DiT) | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_nvfp4.safetensors`** | **12.5 GB** | **1.90** | 11.9 GB | smallest/fastest ref2va |
| **`minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_nvfp4.safetensors`** | **12.5 GB** | — | ~11.9 GB | smallest/fastest fl2va |
| `minimax_h3_ref2va_nvfp4_mixed.safetensors` | 24.4 GB | 1.92 | ~20 GB | from unpruned bf16 |
| `minimax_h3_ref2va_nvfp4_full.safetensors` | 18.7 GB | 1.91 | ~16 GB | experimental |
| `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_nvfp4_convrot_int8.safetensors` | 20.1 GB | — | ~20 GB | **mixed-precision, by [rockerBOO](https://huggingface.co/rockerBOO/minimax-h3-nvfp4)** |
| `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_nvfp4_convrot_int8.safetensors` | 20.1 GB | — | ~20 GB | **mixed-precision, by [rockerBOO](https://huggingface.co/rockerBOO/minimax-h3-nvfp4)** |

Take a **`pruned_nvfp4`** file when footprint and speed matter: half the size of the
alternatives at equal-or-better speed, with the modulation path left at full precision. If
you have VRAM to spare and want maximum fidelity, read "Honest limitations" first — 4-bit
weights appear to cost some motion quality relative to Comfy-Org's 8-bit `int8_convrot`.

The two `_convrot_int8` files are **not ours** — they are
[rockerBOO](https://huggingface.co/rockerBOO/minimax-h3-nvfp4)'s work, mirrored here for
convenience under the same MiniMax community license. A mixed-precision profile quantized in
a single pass from bf16: NVFP4 for `blocks.2-46` mlp, FP8 for `attn.qkv_proj`/`adaln_proj`,
BF16 left on the layers stored F32 upstream, and `attn.qkv_proj` swapped to INT8 ConvRot
quantized fresh rather than restacked. Bigger than ours, better motivated on fidelity.
Original repo: https://huggingface.co/rockerBOO/minimax-h3-nvfp4

The two pruned files are the same size and were produced by the same script over the same
200 quantized layers — they differ only in task head. `fl2va` s/it is unmeasured but should
match `ref2va`; the architectures are identical.

## Why the pruned base is the right one to quantize

Comfy-Org's `pruned` checkpoint is not lossily pruned — it is a **structural refactor of
AdaLN**, and understanding it explains the whole table above.

In the bf16 model, AdaLN modulation dominates the parameter count:

| group | bf16 | pruned |
|---|---|---|
| `adaln_proj` | **13.04B (39.4%)** | **0.04B (0.2%)** |
| `mlp` | 12.02B | 11.56B |
| `attn` | 8.02B | 7.71B |
| token_refiner / norms / embedders | 0.05B | 0.80B |
| **total** | **33.12B** | **20.11B** |

The bf16 model projects a 5376-dim conditioning vector into modulation parameters per block.
The pruned model replaces this with an 8-dim timestep table (`adaln_t_table`, shape
`[1025, 8]`) feeding `adaln_proj.linear` of shape `[96768, 8]`. Because modulation depends
only on the timestep, that 5376-wide projection was almost entirely redundant — 13.04B
parameters collapse to 0.04B, a ~326x reduction.

This matters for quantization because AdaLN is the part you least want to quantize: it emits
the scale and shift applied to every residual stream, so error there is multiplicative and
compounds across all 50 blocks and every sampling step. In the bf16 model you face a bad
choice — protect AdaLN and produce a ~36 GB file (larger than the 34 GB int8 it should beat),
or quantize 39% of the model and hope. **In the pruned model the problem disappears**: AdaLN
is already tiny, so you keep it at full precision for free and quantize only attn+mlp, which
are error-tolerant.

Comfy-Org's `pruned_int8_convrot` quantizes exactly those 200 attn/mlp layers to
int8_convrot and leaves everything else alone. `pruned_nvfp4` takes that same set to NVFP4.

## Measured

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB), ComfyUI 0.30.0, ref2va, 864x480, 39 frames, 20 steps,
`res_multistep` / `beta`, three matched seeds. **These are speed/size numbers only** — the
quality comparison from the sam

In a continuous 360 orbit. output: url: media/hero.webp --- # MiniMax-H3 360° Orbit LoRA (first–last frame) **A LoRA for [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) (FL2VA variant) that turns one photo into a frozen-time 360° camera orbit, and lands back on the exact frame it started from.**

Give the model the same image as the first and the last keyframe, and the LoRA orbits the camera all the way around the subject while the scene stays frozen. The clip closes on its own first frame, so orbits can be chained or stitched into longer shots without a visible seam. ## Results Each comparison shows three renders of the same input with the same seed, prompt, resolution and step count: | left | middle | right | |---|---|---| | base model, first frame only | base model, first + last frame | **base + this LoRA, first + last frame** |

The previews are downscaled animated WebP. Full-resolution MP4s: comparisons [skate](media/skate_comparison.mp4) · [man2](media/man2_comparison.mp4) · [girl2](media/girl2_comparison.mp4) · [man](media/man_comparison.mp4); LoRA-only clips [skate](media/skate_lora.mp4) · [man2](media/man2_lora.mp4) · [girl2](media/girl2_lora.mp4) · [man](media/man_lora.mp4). ### About the comparisons - **Base, first + last frame:** when both keyframes are the same image, the base model reads the clip as a still and barely moves. - **Base, first frame only:** the camera moves, but drifts away and never returns to the starting view. - **With the LoRA:** the camera travels the full orbit and returns to the starting frame, with smooth motion and no cuts. ## Why this LoRA? Reference-to-video (Ref2VA) treats its input images as loose appearance references, so clips don't end on a known frame and can't be joined cleanly. First–last-frame generation (FL2VA) pins both ends, but out of the box it freezes when both ends are the same image. This LoRA teaches the model a real, geometry-consistent orbit, while FL2VA keyframe pinning at inference keeps both ends exact. ## Prompt Use this prompt verbatim. ```text One frozen instant. Only the camera moves. In a continuous 360 orbit. Preserve every person and object in exactly the same world position, orientation, shape and pose throughout the shot. Airborne objects remain suspended at the captured height and angle: no wobbling, shaking, spinning, drifting, falling or continued action. Keep faces, hands, clothing, liquids and the background motionless while retaining their natural appearance. Camera parallax is the only source of apparent movement. No cuts, zoom, morphing or added objects. ``` ## Recommended settings | setting | value | |---|---| | base weights | MiniMax-H3 FL2VA, pruned ([Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3) int8 ConvRot repack) | | keyframes | the same image as first **and** last frame, for a full 360° loop | | resolution | 768 × 768 | | frames | 73 (about 3 s at 24 fps) | | steps | 28 | | guidance | none. MiniMax-H3 is guidance-distilled, so there is no CFG or negative prompt | | LoRA strength | 1.0 | | audio | off | ## Usage These weights were trained and tested with [ostris/ai-toolkit](https://github.com/ostris/ai-toolkit) and its `minimax_h3` model extension.

# Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-T2I — BF16 single-file ComfyUI repack (unofficial)

**Unofficial community lossless single-file repack of Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-T2I for ComfyUI. Packaging publisher: kosmozoo.**
Not affiliated with or endorsed by the upstream authors or Hangzhou Tongyi Laboratory Technology Co., Ltd.

**Modified-container notice:** four official original BF16 shards were merged into one native checkpoint. Only container header/offset/provenance metadata changed. All760tensor names, shapes, BF16dtypes and payload bytes remain unchanged. This is **not a new fine-tune, quality upgrade, quantization or INT8 dequantization**.

## Exact model and task

- Source: [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-T2I](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-T2I), immutable revision `f3ed7985c788ad75b3ab7223e0c4c51e2a43545b`.
- Task: text-to-image **prompt rewriting** for Qwen Image2.1. This is the T2I fine-tune, **not** the separate PE-I2I image-editing enhancer, a generic base LLM, the FLUX prompt upsampler, or the image-generation DiT.
- Upstream describes a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-VL9B. Config identifies `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`,32text layers,4096hidden width,248320vocabulary and an untied output head. Actual packaged count:9,409,813,744parameters.
- Weight filename: `qwen3.5_9b_qwen_image_2.1_pe_t2i_bf16.safetensors`.
- Bytes: **18,819,722,624**.
- Full SHA256: **`5c93236acbcf73b17cad77e8a5479e15893987a34844dc653c639faff91c1a91`**.

## Native ComfyUI use

1. Place the exact checkpoint under your existing `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` model directory and verify its full hash against SHA256SUMS.
2. In the author's matching T2I workflow, choose the filename in the **prompt-enhancer CLIPLoader feeding TextGenerate**, or its exposed enhancer model selector. It is not the main image encoder or image-generator selector.

# Introduction
FlagOS is a fully open-source system software stack for heterogeneous AI chips. It unifies the model–system–chip layers to enable a "develop once, run anywhere" workflow, eliminating the fragmentation among vendor-specific software stacks and substantially lowering the cost of porting AI workloads across accelerators.
In this release, Qwen-Image-2.1 leverages the FlagOS software stack to provide direct multi-chip support. By integrating the Triton-based operator library FlagGems via the Torch-FL plugin, FlagOS enables seamless adaptation of the Diffusers library across chip platforms; the usage experience remains identical to that on NVIDIA, requiring zero code modifications. Inference accuracy across all platforms has been aligned with the official implementation.

### Integrated Deployment
- Out-of-the-box inference scripts with pre-configured hardware and software parameters
- Released **FlagOS-Ascend** container image supporting deployment within minutes
### Consistency Validation
- Rigorously evaluated through benchmark testing: Performance and results from the FlagOS software stack are compared against native stacks on multiple public.

# SeedVR2 VAE TensorRT Engines for NVIDIA Blackwell

High-performance, pre-compiled **NVIDIA TensorRT** engine plans (`.rtxplan`) built for the official **SeedVR2 VAE** (`seedvr2_ema_vae_fp16`), specifically compiled and optimized for the **NVIDIA Blackwell** GPU architecture (**RTX 5090**, **RTX 5080**, **RTX 5070**, **RTX 5060**, **RTX 5050**, and Blackwell workstation / data center GPUs, Compute Capability `sm_100` / `sm_120`).

## 🚀 Usage in ComfyUI
These TensorRT engine plans (`.rtxplan`) are directly loaded and executed via the dedicated custom node:
- **Loader & Node Repository:** [ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT](https://github.com/ussoewwin/ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT)

### 1. Installation
Clone the custom node repository into your ComfyUI `custom_nodes/` directory:

```bash
cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/ussoewwin/ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT.git
```

### 2. Engine Placement
Place the downloaded `.rtxplan` engine files into either of the following supported directories:

```
ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT/tensorrt_backend/artifacts/
```
or
```
ComfyUI/models/tensorrt/seedvr2/
```

Upon launching ComfyUI, all detected `.rtxplan` files will automatically populate the `engine_frames` and `engine_tile` dropdown lists of the respective loader nodes:
- `vae_decoder_tile_*_*f.rtxplan` populates **`SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Decoder`**
- `vae_encoder_*f_tile*.rtxplan` populates **`SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Encoder`**

### 3. Node Integration
Connect both loader nodes directly to the **`SeedVR2 Video Upscaler`** node:
- Connect the `SEEDVR2_VAE` output of **`SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Encoder`** to the **`vae_encode`** input.
- Connect the `SEEDVR2_VAE` output of **`SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Decoder`** to the **`vae_decode`** input.

```
+------------------------------------+
| SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Encoder  |
| [engine_frames: 21 / 45 / 1]       |--(SEEDVR2_VAE)---+
| [engine_tile: 512 / 1024]          |                  |
+------------------------------------+                  |
                                                        v [vae_encode]
                                         +----------------------------+
                                         |   SeedVR2 Video Upscaler   |
                                         +----------------------------+
                                                        ^ [vae_decode]
+------------------------------------+                  |
| SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Decoder  |                  |
| [engine_frames: 21 / 45 / 1]       |--(SEEDVR2_VAE)---+
| [engine_tile: 512 / 1024]          |
+------------------------------------+
```

### 4. Workflow Examples
#### Complete Video Upscaler Workflow (TensorRT VAE & Quantized Models)
Workflow JSON: [`example_workflows/SeedVR2_tensorrt_decode.json`](https://github.com/ussoewwin/ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT/blob/main/example_workflows/SeedVR2_tensorrt_decode.json)

![Usage Example - Full Workflow](docs/usage_01.png)

#### TensorRT VAE Decoder & Encoder Node Integration
Connect the `SEEDVR2_VAE` outputs from **`SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Decoder`** and **`SeedVR2 Load TensorRT VAE Encoder`** directly into the **`SeedVR2 Video Upscaler`** node:

![Usage Example - TensorRT VAE Nodes](docs/usage_02.png)

# FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler

FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler is a 9B vision-language model that expands an image editing, text-to-image or layout request into the detailed prompt [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) works best with. It takes the request, up to 10 reference images and an optional list of bounding boxes, and returns one prompt. It is a fine-tune of [Qwen3.5-9B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B).

Always run a prompt upsampler with FLUX 3 Image Klein, for editing, text-to-image and layout alike. This one is tuned for it, see [Training](#training). Any other LLM can do the job with the system prompts in `system_prompts.json`. The inference code in [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) loads it by default. The Diffusers modular pipeline runs it automatically; the [Transformers block](#with-transformers) below shows how to run it on its own. In ComfyUI, the text-to-image templates on [flux-3-image-klein-comfy](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy) have an `enable_prompt_upsampler` switch.

**Request**

> A man walking with his dog, afternoon sun

**Prompt**

> Full-color outdoor photograph, eye-level medium-wide shot in late afternoon sunlight, showing a man walking his dog along a neighborhood sidewalk. The low sun shines from the upper right, casting long shadows across the pavement and lighting the man's face and clothing with warm side light. Slightly left of center, a white man in his thirties with fair skin, short brown hair, and light stubble walks toward frame-left at an easy pace. He wears a faded olive overshirt over a plain grey T-shirt, dark blue jeans, and worn brown leather shoes. [...]

220 words in full, with the image it made, in [examples/base/man_dog.json](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/blob/main/examples/base/man_dog.json).

# Key Features

1. One model for editing with reference images, text-to-image and layout with bounding boxes. The system prompt selects the mode.
2. Prompts with everything the image model needs decided: medium and style, scene, lighting and camera, each subject with its colors, materials and position in the frame. Text to render stays verbatim, in quotes.
3. For an edit it looks at the references and writes the instruction around what is in them: what changes, what stays, by appearance.
4. Bounding boxes you pass are kept exactly, as a box table after the prompt; the prompt cites each box by id, so the image model places that element where the box says.
5. Released under the Apache License 2.0.

# Training

A full fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B with the vision tower frozen, in two stages: supervised training on pairs of short requests and their expanded prompts, then preference tuning on pairs of the model's own prompts, rendered with FLUX 3 Image Klein at the same seed and ranked on the resulting image.

# Files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `model.safetensors` | the model, bfloat16, 18.8 GB |
| `system_prompts.json` | the four system prompts: `t2i`, `i2i`, `t2i_bbox`, `i2i_bbox` |
| `config.json`, `generation_config.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `chat_template.jinja`, `processor_config.json`, `preprocessor_config.json` | Transformers configuration, tokenizer, chat template, image processor |

# Usage

## With the FLUX 3 inference code

```sh
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup --local-dir weights/pup
python scripts/cli.py "A man walking with his dog, afternoon sun" --out out.png
```

The upsampler is on by default; `--no-pup` sends the prompt as typed. To upsample without generating: `python -m flux3.pup --prompt "..." --out caption.txt`. Install, references and the box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein).

## With Transformers

```python
import json

import torch
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration

model_id = "black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup"
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto").eval()

## 使用技巧

- **素材怎么配最好**：全身换全身、半身换半身。
- **半身换全身**：可能会穿上原图人物的下装，在提示词里写明下装穿什么。
- **遮罩（可选，90% 以上的图不需要）**：替换后人物超出了原图人像的范围，或者全身换半身时姿势对不上，就右键图2 → 在"遮罩编辑器"中打开 → 画笔颜色调成纯黑、不透明度 0.7 → 涂满要替换的人物区域（包括手臂）。这样能限制区域，帮助模型理解。
- **单人场景**：直接写"使用图1的人物替换图2的人物"就可以，也可以要求"使用图2的服装"或"保留图1人物的服装"。

# MiniMax-H3 on a single AMD RDNA2 GPU (Windows)

Deployment, profiling and optimization notes for running **MiniMax-H3** (33B omni
video+audio diffusion transformer) on an **AMD RX 6900 XT** under **Windows**, using
[stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp) with the
ROCm/HIP backend.

Everything here was measured on one machine. The numbers are reproducible with the
included scripts; the analysis documents explain *why* they are what they are.

**Result: 3707 s → 183 s for a 480p / 2.3 s clip (20.3×)**, with a documented
breakdown of where the remaining time goes.

> **Unofficial project. No model weights are distributed here.**
> MiniMax-H3 is **not** open source — it is governed by the

> Excluded Territories** requiring a separate license. Downloading or using the model
> is your agreement to those terms. This repository ships only PowerShell scripts and
> documentation; `stable-diffusion.cpp` is MIT.

## What is in here

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/gen.ps1` | Main generator. Presets `draft` / `fast` / `quality` / `longhd`, backend selection, automatic VRAM budgeting. |
| `scripts/serve.ps1` | Local web UI (sd-server on 127.0.0.1:1234). |
| `scripts/bench.ps1` | Benchmark harness (per-step timing, log parsing). |
| `scripts/extract_rocm.ps1` | Admin-free extraction of the ROCm runtime from AMD's HIP SDK installer. |
| `scripts/build_hip.bat` | Build stable-diffusion.cpp with the HIP backend (MSVC + clang from the ROCm SDK). |
| `docs/PITFALLS.md` | 40+ traps hit during the work: network, ROCm deployment, ggml behaviour, measurement methodology. |
| `docs/KERNEL-ANALYSIS.md` | Operator-level analysis: where the time goes, what RDNA2 can and cannot do, and the measured effect of every knob. |
| `docs/FRAME56-CLIFF.md` | Case study of a 2.8× cliff caused by WDDM silently demoting allocations to shared memory. |
| `docs/ATTENTION-KERNEL-BENCH.md` | Standalone HIP attention kernel: 8.76 TFLOPS on gfx1030 (18–19% of peak). |

Mirrors:
- Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/kylinfires/minimax-h3-rdna2-windows
- ModelScope: https://modelscope.cn/models/kylinfires/minimax-h3-rdna2-windows

Model weights are **not** included. The scripts download them from ModelScope /
Hugging Face.

---

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11
- AMD GPU with ROCm/HIP support (tested: RX 6900 XT, gfx1030, 16 GB)
- 64 GB system RAM recommended (mmap + offload keeps RSS around 23–28 GB)
- ~31 GB disk for the models

## Quick start

```powershell
# 1. Download the models (~31 GB)
.\scripts\download_models.ps1

# 2. Extract the ROCm runtime (no admin required)
.\scripts\extract_rocm.ps1

# 3. Generate
.\gen.ps1 -Prompt "<at least 25 words, details help>" -Preset fast
```

Presets:

| Preset | Resolution | Frames | Steps | Measured |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fast` | 864×480 | 22 (0.9 s) | 8 | **67.2 s** |
| `draft` | 512×288 | 56 (2.3 s) | 8 | **72.2 s** |
| `quality` | 864×480 | 22 (0.9 s) | 20 | **138.5 s** |
| `longhd` | 864×480 | 56 (2.3 s) | 8 | **183.0 s** |

---

## The three findings that mattered

### 1. WDDM silently demotes large allocations to shared memory (2.8×)

On Windows, once ~11.4 GB of weights are resident, activation tensors larger than
~600 MB no longer fit the effective VRAM budget and the OS transparently pages them
to shared memory. `ggml` still sees them as device memory, so nothing in the logs
says "spilling" — but elementwise ops drop from 240 GB/s to 5–12 GB/s.

Fix: cap the staged weight VRAM so activations stay resident.

```
--max-vram ROCm0=11
```

The cap is bounded on **both** sides (measured at 56 frames): 9 GB → 147 s,
11 GB → 145 s, 12 GB → 145 s, **13 GB → 400 s**. The rule is *leave 4–5 GB for
activations*, i.e. roughly `VRAM − 5 GB` on other cards.

### 2. The text encoder was 20% of every run

The TE stage cost 18 s regardless of prompt length — pure weight staging for the
17 GB Qwen3-VL encoder. Switching to the 12.5 GB Q2_K_M quant cut it to 6.4 s
(**−15% end-to-end**), with no visible quality difference in A/B frames.

### 3. On Vulkan, `GGML_PREC_F32` disables the fast attention path (2.4×)

`stable-diffusion.cpp` forces `GGML_PREC_F32` on the attention QK^T matmul. In the
Vulkan backend, `ggml_vk_get_mul_mat_mat_f16acc()` requires `prec == GGML_PREC_DEFAULT`,
so that single line forces a pure-f32 shader GEMM — measured at **0.8 TFLOPS (1.7% of
peak)**. Turning on flash attention fixes it: 94.1 → 38.9 s/step, **2.4×**.

## Introduction **Four-step image generation and editing. Built with Qwen.** This model is the reinforcement-learning-refined version of LightX2V Lightning v2, distilled from [Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1). It supports text-to-image generation, single-reference image editing, and multi-reference image generation with **4 denoising steps** and **CFG = 1.0**. RL training was performed with [LightX2V RL](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/tree/main/lightx2v_rl). ## Model files The release provides the **full transformer weights** in a single `diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors` file, together with `config.json`. The weights are stored in FP32 and can be loaded in BF16 for inference. `inference_config.json` records the base model, four sampling sigmas, guidance scale, KV cache setting, and scheduler parameters. It is a release-specific configuration file, explicitly read by the example below; Diffusers does not load it automatically. The inference files are: ```text config.json diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors inference_config.json README.md assets/img_lightx2v.png assets/wechat.jpg assets/comparison/ ``` `merge_manifest.json` is a local export audit record, is not used for inference, and can be excluded when uploading. Load the processor, text encoder, and VAE from the original Qwen-Image-2.1 pipeline, then replace its transformer as shown below. This checkpoint is not a LoRA adapter or a standalone pipeline bundle. ## Quick start Install a recent Diffusers version with `QwenImage21Pipeline` support: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers.git pip install "transformers>=5.17.0" accelerate safetensors pillow ``` Run the following code from the downloaded model directory, or change `MODEL_DIR` to its local path. The base pipeline components will be downloaded from Hugging Face when needed. ### Load the model ```python import json from pathlib import Path import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import ( FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler, QwenImage21Pipeline, QwenImage21Transformer2DModel, ) MODEL_DIR = "." with (Path(MODEL_DIR) / "inference_config.json").open(encoding="utf-8") as f: inference_config = json.load(f) SIGMAS = inference_config["sample_sigmas"] transformer = QwenImage21Transformer2DModel.from_pretrained( MODEL_DIR, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, ) pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( inference_config["base_model"], transformer=transformer, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, ) # The four sigmas are already shifted. Do not apply dynamic shifting again. pipe.scheduler = FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler( **inference_config["scheduler"], ) pipe.to("cuda") def generate(prompt, image=None, seed=42): return pipe( prompt=prompt, image=image, width=1024, height=1024, sigmas=SIGMAS, num_inference_steps=len(SIGMAS), true_cfg_scale=inference_config["true_cfg_scale"], use_kv_cache=inference_config["use_kv_cache"], generator=torch.Generator("cpu").manual_seed(seed), ).images[0] ``` Use this exact sigma schedule for all three tasks. The terminal sigma of zero is appended by the scheduler. Setting only `num_inference_steps=4` does not reproduce this schedule. ### Text-to-image ```python image = generate( "A ceramic teapot beside a small bowl of oranges on a wooden table, " "soft morning window light, detailed glaze, natural colors." ) image.save("t2i.png") ``` ### Single-reference editing ```python reference = Image.open("reference.png").convert("RGB") image = generate( "Change the jacket to dark green. Preserve the person's face, pose, " "and the rest of the scene.", image=[reference], ) image.save("edit.png") ``` ### Multi-reference generation Pass reference images in the same order used by the prompt: ```python references = [ Image.open("person.png").convert("RGB"), Image.open("jacket.png").convert("RGB")

# Noct Q Anime: Qwen Image 2.1 Uncensored Anime

Uncensored anime on Qwen Image 2.1: soft light, clean color, and full nudity when the scene calls for it. Built with Qwen.

**The full gallery with prompts, the int4, fp8, bf16 and fp16 files and the reviews are on Civitai: [Noct Q Anime](https://civitai.com/models/2967534).**

## What it does well

- Anime illustration, from close portraits to wide background paintings
- Adult characters dressed, in lingerie or nude, and explicit scenes
- Long, detailed prompts followed closely: two characters, poses and camera angles as written

## Files

| file | size | use |
|---|---|---|
| `NoctQA_V1_int8_convrot.safetensors` | 7.3 GB | 8 to 12 GB cards, ComfyUI 0.37 or newer, core nodes only |
| `NoctQ_Anime_V1_workflow.json` | | drag it into ComfyUI |

The model goes in `models/diffusion_models`.

## Settings

25 steps, euler, simple, cfg 3 with the negative prompt from the workflow.

- Text encoder: [`qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors) in `models/text_encoders`
- VAE: [`qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1/blob/main/vae/qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors) in `models/vae`

## How to prompt

Start with "An anime illustration of…" and describe the scene in full sentences. Without the word "anime" you get a photo. No trigger word.

Noct Q Anime is a derivative work of Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 with modified transformer weights (see `NOTICE`), free for non-commercial use only under the Qwen Research License Agreement (`LICENSE`). All characters are adults. No real people.

# SO-101 Bench: ImageWAM (FLUX.2 klein 4B) full fine-tune

**Paper:** [SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.36420)  
**Project:** [https://so101-bench.github.io/](https://so101-bench.github.io/)  
**Code:** [https://github.com/5hadytru/so101_bench](https://github.com/5hadytru/so101_bench)

ImageWAM is an image-editing world-action model: a FLUX.2 [klein] base 4B editing backbone predicts the future
camera canvas while a mixture-of-transformers action DiT predicts the action chunk. This checkpoint is a full
fine-tune of `yuyangalin/ImageWAM-FLUX.2-4B-InternData-A1-EE` on the SO-101 Bench simulated teleop dataset
`5hadytru/so101_bench_sim` (3,629 episodes, 1,996,120 frames; overhead + wrist cameras).

- **Official checkpoint: step 30000** of a 33,000-step run on 4x A100-80GB (global batch 128 = 8 per GPU x 4 GPUs x
  4 accumulation, AdamW 2.5e-5, weight decay 0.01, 5% warmup then cosine to 0, bf16; ~2.1 epochs).
- Files: `model.pt` (MoT backbone + action DiT + proprio encoder weights), `config.yaml` (the run's resolved
  config), `dataset_stats.json` (normalization stats).

## Validation

SO-101 Bench validation set (`real_gr00t_val_v2`, 39 closed-loop episodes in Isaac Sim across named-bin, four-object bin,
next-to, between and move tasks, seen and unseen objects):

| Step | 3k | 6k | 9k | 12k | 15k | 18k | 21k | 24k | 27k | **30k** | 33k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Success /39 | 1 | 4 | 6 | 9 | 11 | 16 | 15 | 7 | 15 | **15** | 14 |

Step 30000 scores 15/39 (38.5%). It was picked from the 15-16/39 plateau of steps 18k-30k; those
scores are within the noise of a 39-episode set.

## Inputs and outputs

- **Cameras:** one 288x256 canvas. The overhead view is 192x256 on top, the wrist view 96x128 bottom-left, and the bottom-right is black.
- **Proprio and actions:** the SO-101's 6 joints are padded into the pretrain checkpoint's 16-D end-effector layout
  (arm in slots 0-4, gripper in slot 7). Actions are absolute joint targets in LeRobot units.
- **Chunking:** chunks of 32 actions at 30 Hz, of which the client executes 16 before replanning.
- **Language:** the task instruction is encoded with Qwen3-4B, as in training.

## Running it

The checkpoint holds the fine-tuned backbone weights. The FLUX.2 autoencoder (`ae.safetensors`) and the Qwen3-4B text
encoder are loaded from their upstream repos, following ImageWAM's setup instructions.

- **Code:** yuyangalin/ImageWAM @ `5d4a341`.
- **SO-101 adapter, recipe, configs and server:** in the SO-101 Bench repo (`scripts/ImageWAM_fine_tuning/`,
  `scripts/imagewam_server.py`).

## License

MIT, following ImageWAM and its pretrain checkpoint. The backbone derives from FLUX.2 [klein] base 4B (Apache-2.0).

# FLUX 3 Image Klein

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

![Teaser](./teaser.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the distilled checkpoint for generation and image editing. For fine-tuning, LoRA training and research, use [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, [flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup), which the reference code loads by default, or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours). Diffusers runs neither on its own; see [Prompt upsampling](#prompt-upsampling).

This repository includes the BF16 transformer and [FP8](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/fp8r) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/nvfp4) variants, together with the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder and image autoencoder.

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

## Download

Download the root BF16 distilled package, including its text encoder and image autoencoder, without downloading the quantized variants:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

snapshot_download(
    repo_id="black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein",
    local_dir="weights/flux-3-image-klein",
    allow_patterns=[
        "model.safetensors", "config.json", "manifest.json",
        "ae.safetensors", "text_encoder/*",
        "README.md", "LICENSE.md", "NOTICE.md",
    ],
)
```

To download a quantized distilled transformer instead, replace the three root transformer patterns (`model.safetensors`, `config.json`, and `manifest.json`) with `variants/fp8r/*` or `variants/nvfp4/*`. Keep `ae.safetensors` and `text_encoder/*` for the other components.

These files contain the model package, not a complete inference application. Use an inference implementation that supports flow-map sampling and this checkpoint format. Quantized packages need a loader that supports their format; their file size is not a measure of total GPU memory use.

## Using with reference code

The distilled checkpoint is served on the [BFL API](https://bfl.ai) as FLUX 3 Image Klein. The reference inference code is [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein).

From the reference implementation checkout, install the package and download the two components the CLI loads besides this checkpoint. The CLI reads its weights from `weights/` (set `WEIGHTS_DIR` for another root), where the download above puts this repository.

```bash
pip install -e .

# safety classifier, always loaded
hf download Falconsai/nsfw_image_detection --local-dir weights/nsfw-classifier
# prompt upsampler (18.8 GB), on by default; --no-pup sends the prompt as typed, for captions written by another LLM
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-k

# Qwen-Image-2.1 2-step DMD2 LoRA

A **2-step** distillation LoRA for [Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1), trained with **DMD2** (Distribution Matching Distillation). It turns the base model's 20-step sampling into a 2 forward-pass run while keeping instruction editing and text-to-image quality close to the full-step teacher, which makes it suitable for real-time and interactive pipelines.

- **Base model:** Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
- **Method:** DMD2 (on-policy distribution matching, no regression/GAN loss), teacher CFG guidance
- **LoRA:** rank 32, alpha 32, **attention-only** (`to_q`, `to_k`, `to_v`, `to_out.0`)
- **Inference:** 2 steps, fixed sigmas `[1.0, 0.5]`, `true_cfg_scale=1.0`
- **Training:** multi-aspect (~1 MP) DMD2, 2000 steps on a single H100

> **2026-10-30:** New **V1.5** checkpoint available, with improved prompt adherence and edit fidelity. Load it by passing `weight_name="pytorch_lora_weights_v1_5.safetensors"` to `load_lora_weights` (all other settings below are unchanged).

## Editing: 2 steps vs base 20 steps

The official Qwen-Image-2.1 demo edits (sketch-to-photo, hairstyle, expression, photo restoration), same input, prompt and seed. Middle column is this LoRA at 2 steps; right column is the base model at 20 steps.

![2-step vs 20-step editing comparison](assets/edit_space_examples.png)

## Multi-reference composition

Qwen-Image-2.1 takes a **list** of condition images, referred to as "Picture 1", "Picture 2", ... in the prompt, and the LoRA keeps this working at 2 steps:

```python
image = pipe(
    prompt="Place the cat from Picture 1 on the beach from Picture 2.",
    image=[cat, beach],          # a list of condition images
    num_inference_steps=2,
    sigmas=[1.0, 0.5],
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
).images[0]
```

## Usage

This model uses the `QwenImage21Pipeline`, which needs a `diffusers` build with Qwen-Image-2.1 support (currently the dev branch, not yet on PyPI):

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers.git@qwenimage21-lora-training"
```

### Image editing

```python
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline, FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler
from diffusers.utils import load_image

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda")

# this LoRA was trained with fixed sigmas (no dynamic shifting)
pipe.scheduler = FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler.from_config(
    pipe.scheduler.config, use_dynamic_shifting=False, shift=1.0, shift_terminal=None
)
pipe.load_lora_weights("linoyts/Qwen-Image-2.1-DMD2-2steps", weight_name="pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors")

image = load_image("input.png")
out = pipe(
    prompt="Turn this into a claymation character of colorful clay.",
    image=image,
    num_inference_steps=2,
    sigmas=[1.0, 0.5],
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(0),
).images[0]
out.save("edited.png")
```

### Text to image

Drop the `image` argument and keep everything else the same:

```python
out = pipe(
    prompt="a cute 3d render of a baby dragon made of jelly, soft shadows",
    num_inference_steps=2,
    sigmas=[1.0, 0.5],
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(0),
).images[0]
```

## Notes

- The `[1.0, 0.5]` sigma schedule is the schedule the LoRA was trained on. Because it was trained with fixed sigmas, set `use_dynamic_shifting=False` and `shift=1.0` on the scheduler so the nodes are used exactly as given, rather than being resolution-shifted.
- No CFG at inference (`true_cfg_scale=1.0`): the LoRA bakes the teacher's guidance into the student, so a single conditional pass per step is enough.
- Attention-only adaptation keeps conditioning fidelity high for editing; it preserves the input image more faithfully than adapting the feed-forward blocks as well.

# MiniMax-H3 FL2VA and Ref2VA (pruned) 4-step DMAD: INT8 ConvRot

These are the pruned MiniMax-H3 FL2VA and Ref2VA transformers from [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)
with the full-rank [DMAD](https://huggingface.co/ZhengmingYu/DMAD) `full_critic` 4-step LoRA merged in, quantized to
INT8 ConvRot. Both were made the same way and differ only in the base model:

| File | Base model | Same layout as (Comfy-Org `diffusion_models/`) |
|---|---|---|
| `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_dmad_4step_int8_convrot.safetensors` | FL2VA | `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` |
| `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_dmad_4step_int8_convrot.safetensors` | Ref2VA | `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` |

The tensor names and order, dtypes, shapes, data offsets and `.comfy_quant` descriptors all match the Comfy-Org file. The
difference is that the distillation is baked in, so you don't need a LoRA loader.

**Modified files:** the weights differ from the MiniMax-H3 release, as described under [How they were made](#how-they-were-made).

**Layout:** every block linear (`blocks.N.attn.{qkv_proj,out_proj}`, `blocks.N.mlp.{fc1,fc2}`) is INT8 and has its own
`.comfy_quant` tensor (`{"format": "int8_tensorwise", "convrot": true, "convrot_groupsize": 256}`) and a per-row F32
`weight_scale`. Everything else keeps the Comfy-Org dtype. 

**Not trained on Ref2VA:** DMAD was trained on the text-to-audio-video transformer, and the Ref2VA weights differ from
it. The DMAD authors state that the LoRA loads on the Ref2VA partition but don't publish results for it.

## Examples

### FL2VA

| Steps | CFG | Size | Frames | Seed | Sampler | Shift (video / audio) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1.0 | 1344×768 | 124 at 24 fps | 42 | DMAD | 12 / 2 |

> A cinematic view of an ancient floating city suspended above a sea of cumulus clouds. The camera begins in a wide establishing shot and slowly dollies in toward the city, gliding forward through the soft pastel cloudscape as its intricate, hand-drawn architecture comes into view. A waterfall cascades from the city's edge into the clouds, while shafts of golden sunlight break through the cumulus clouds and illuminate the ultra-detailed digital painting.

This render used SageAttention with sparse attention at density 0.15 (first step dense) as described [here](https://noxengine.dev/blog/sparse/). 

### Ref2VA

<video src="https://huggingface.co/Spectrallic/MiniMax-H3-DMAD-4step-int8-convrot/resolve/main/samples/stormy_boat_1344x768_seed42.mp4" controls width="672"></video>

| Steps | CFG | Size | Frames | Seed | Sampler | Shift (video / audio) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1.0 | 1344×768 | 124 at 24 fps | 42 | DMAD | 12 / 2 |

> A close-up of a small wooden fishing boat in a stormy green sea at night, rain lashing the deck, while the floating city from <Picture 1> hangs in the sky far above and lightning flashes behind it. Handheld camera. Loud thunder and crashing waves.

`<Picture 1>` is the first frame of the FL2VA example above, scaled to match the output size. This render used the same setup as the FL2VA example: SageAttention with sparse attention at density 0.15 (first step dense).

## Sampling

Use the DMAD student's own operating point: **4 steps**, CFG 1 (no classifier-free guidance), video time shift 12 and
audio shift 2. Workflows are in the [DMAD repository](https://huggingface.co/ZhengmingYu/DMAD).

Both examples were rendered in Nox with the DMAD sampler. For Ref2VA, refer to references in the prompt as `<Picture i>`,
`<Video k>` and `<Audio j>`.

## How they were made

`<variant>` below is `fl2va` or `ref2va`.

1. **Source:**

# MCNL v1 — Multi Concept NSFW LoRA for Qwen Image Edit

A LoRA adapter for the [Qwen-Image-Edit-2511](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511) diffusion pipeline, enabling NSFW content generation and editing capabilities.

## Usage

### With the ScottzillaSystems Image Editor Space

The easiest way to use this LoRA is through the [ScottzillaSystems Image Editor](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ScottzillaSystems/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-LoRAs-Fast) — select "🔥 MCNL-NSFW-v1" from the adapter dropdown.

### Programmatic Usage

```python
from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline
import torch

pipe = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).to("cuda")

# Load this LoRA
pipe.load_lora_weights(
    "ScottzillaSystems/qwen-image-edit-plus-nsfw-lora",
    weight_name="qwen-image-edit-plus-nsfw-lora.safetensors",
    adapter_name="mcnl-nsfw-v1"
)
pipe.set_adapters(["mcnl-nsfw-v1"])

# Edit an image
from PIL import Image
image = Image.open("input.jpg").convert("RGB")
result = pipe(
    image=image,
    prompt="nsfw",
    num_inference_steps=40,
    true_cfg_scale=4.0,
    negative_prompt=" ",
).images[0]
result.save("output.jpg")
```

## Trigger Words

Use these concepts in your prompts to activate specific capabilities:

`nsfw` `nipples` `vagina` `penis` `missionary` `cowgirlout` `reversecowgirlpov` `blowjob` `cum_on_face` `creamp1e` `l1ck`

# Qwen-Image 2.1 PE — Heretic · W4A8 (ComfyUI native)

English | [中文](#中文说明)

---

## English

### What this is

W4A8-quantized builds of the **Qwen-Image 2.1 prompt encoder** (base architecture
**Qwen3.5-9B**), packaged as native ComfyUI `asym_w4a8_int8` checkpoints. Two variants
are provided:

| File | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `qwen_image_2.1_pe_t2i_heretic_w4a8.safetensors` | Text-to-image |
| `qwen_image_2.1_pe_i2i_heretic_w4a8.safetensors` | Image editing / image-to-image |

These are **text encoders, not diffusion models**. They supply conditioning for the
Qwen-Image 2.1 DiT; you still need the diffusion model and the VAE.

### Works with the official ComfyUI workflow out of the box

ComfyUI's official **Qwen-Image 2.1 Text-to-Image** workflow already supports these
files. There is no patch, no custom node and no workflow edit — you drop the file in
place and pick it from the list.

**Step 1 — put the file where ComfyUI looks for it.**

```
ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/
```

That is the only location. Files elsewhere will not appear in the loader.

**Step 2 — open the workflow and select the model.**

Load the official template (Home → Templates → Qwen-Image 2.1, or
`Workflow → Browse Templates`), then click the `CLIPLoader` node — inside the
**Text to Image (Qwen Image 2.1)** subgraph — and choose the file from the `clip_name`
dropdown:

| Loader field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `clip_name` | `qwen_image_2.1_pe_t2i_heretic_w4a8.safetensors` |
| `type` | `qwen_image` — leave as the template sets it |
| `device` | `default` |

For image editing, use the editing template and select
`qwen_image_2.1_pe_i2i_heretic_w4a8.safetensors` in the same way.

No other node needs to change. Leave everything else in the template — sampler, steps,
VAE, and the diffusion-model loader — exactly as shipped, and queue the prompt.

Both files load and encode successfully through this path with nothing but the stock
`CLIPLoader`, verified against ComfyUI 0.43.2.

### At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Base architecture | Qwen3.5-9B (4096 hidden, 32 layers, hybrid linear + full attention) |
| Vocabulary | 248320 tokens |
| Source precision | FP8 E4M3FN mixed with BF16 |
| Quantization | `asym_w4a8_int8` (4-bit weights, ConvRot INT8 activations) |
| Size | **6.38 GB** |
| Tensors | 1764 (from 760) |
| Required | ComfyUI with a `comfy-kitchen` installation that registers `asym_w4a8_int8` |

### How the layers were treated

| Treatment | Count | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W4A8 `asym_w4a8_int8` | 250 | All 2-D LM linear layers with `in_features % 256 == 0` |
| Kept floating point | 510 | RMSNorm, `conv1d`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`, `pos_embed`, the output head, and all 111 vision-layer linears |

W4A8 parameters: `group_size=16`, `convrot_groupsize=256`.

- **The 111 vision-layer linears stay in FP8.** Their `in_features` is 1152 or 4304,
  neither divisible by the 256 required by ConvRot, so they cannot use this kernel.
  The vision tower itself has 27 blocks; its `merger` linears (4608-dim) do quantize,
  which is why the W4A8 count is 250 rather than 248.

### Usage

Place the file in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/`, then point a stock **CLIPLoader** at it:

```
CLIPLoader
  clip_name : qwen_image_2.1_pe_t2i_heretic_w4a8.safetensors
  type      : qwen_image
  device    : default
```

Then wire the `CLIP` output into `TextEncodeQwenImage21` exactly as you would with the
unquantized file. No custom node is required — `CLIPLoader` reads the embedded
`.comfy_quant` metadata and builds the quantized runtime on its own.

### License and attribution

Derived from the Heretic Qwen-Image 2.1 prompt encoders. **This build introduces no new
terms — the upstream license governs.** Verify the exact terms at the original source
before redistributing or using commercially. Qwen-Image and Qwen3-VL carry their own
licenses from their respective publishers.

Quantization format and runtime by [comfy-kitchen](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen)
and [ComfyUI](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI). ConvRot from
[*ConvRot*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03673).

# Cobijada MiniMax-H3 Hybrid (Pruned, Uncensored)

![Cobijada MiniMax-H3 Hybrid](https://huggingface.co/Winnougan/Cobijada_Minimax-H3_Hybrid_Pruned_ComfyUI/resolve/main/H3_Hybrid.png)

A merged variant of MiniMax H3, a joint audio+video diffusion transformer (DiT) for ComfyUI, combining the strengths of the two source conditioning modes — first/last-keyframe (FL) and reference-driven (REF) — into a single checkpoint.

## Why this merge exists

MiniMax H3 ships two distinct training regimes with identical architecture and tensor layout:

- **FL (first/last-keyframe conditioning)** — higher raw visual and audio output quality, but no support for reference-driven generation.
- **REF (reference conditioning)** — adds image/video/audio reference-driven generation, but at a real cost to output quality, even on non-reference tasks.

A tensor-by-tensor comparison of the two checkpoints shows the large majority of weights — attention projections, MLPs, norms, patch projections, rotary embeddings, and the token refiner — are effectively identical between them. The meaningful differences are concentrated almost entirely in the per-block `adaln_proj` weights: the AdaLN modulation projections that route conditioning signal into the residual stream at each transformer block.

That made a targeted, non-training weight-selection merge viable rather than a lossy compromise.

## What this model is

This hybrid uses the **FL checkpoint as the base** for the entire network, with the **`adaln_proj` weights for transformer blocks 25–49 (the later half of the network) taken from the REF checkpoint** instead. Everything else — including the earlier-block `adaln_proj` weights, the final AdaLN projection, attention, MLPs, norms, and output heads — remains on FL throughout.

The intent is to keep REF's reference-conditioning pathway, which is expressed primarily through those later-block AdaLN weights, while retaining FL's higher-fidelity weights everywhere else in the network.

No additional training, fine-tuning, or gradient-based optimization was performed — this is a weight-selection merge at the tensor level, not a fine-tune. Both source checkpoints were the uncensored, pruned variants before merging.

## Files

| File | Format | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Cobijada_H3_Hybrid_Uncensored_pruned_hybrid_BF16_pruned.safetensors` | BF16 | Full-precision merge output; base for the quantized variants below |
| `Cobijada_H3_Hybrid_Uncensored_pruned_hybrid_int8_convrot_pruned.safetensors` | INT8 (ConvRot) | Quantized from the BF16 hybrid |
| `Cobijada_H3_Hybrid_Uncensored_pruned_hybrid_w4a8_convrot_pruned.safetensors` | W4A8 (ConvRot) | Quantized from the BF16 hybrid |

All three are pruned variants.

## Usage (ComfyUI)

1. Download the format you want and place it in `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`.
2. Load it with your normal MiniMax H3 checkpoint loader — architecture and tensor layout are unchanged from the source models, so no custom node is required to load the hybrid itself.
3. Reference-conditioned workflows (image/video/audio reference input) and standard first/last-keyframe workflows both work with this single checkpoint.

## Intended use

- Text/image/video/audio-to-video generation where you want reference conditioning while keeping output quality closer to the FL checkpoint.
- A drop-in replacement for the REF checkpoint in reference-conditioned workflows, for users who found REF's raw output quality lacking.

This model is not expected to exceed the FL checkpoint's quality on non-reference-conditioned generation, since the large majority of its weights are shared with FL to begin with.

## License

This merge, the quantized conversions, and this repository are released under **Apache 2.0**. The underlying MiniMax H3 weights remain subject to MiniMax's own original license terms — please review those separately before use.

## Credits

Merged and quantized by [Winnougan](https://huggingface.co/Winnougan). Built on the officially released MiniMax H3 FL and REF checkpoints.

# Qwen-Image-2.1 on RunPod

Hugging Face hosts these scripts. A RunPod GPU Pod runs the model and API.
Based on vladlen-beilik/ltx-2.3-runpod; separate runtime and model cache.

## Setup

1. Create a Hugging Face **model repository** named `qwen-image-2.1-runpod` and upload bootstrap.sh, requirements.txt, server.py and this README.
2. Use a RunPod PyTorch template with Python 3.10+ and CUDA-capable PyTorch. Start with 48 GB VRAM and at least 64 GB system RAM as a conservative initial configuration; actual requirements must be measured. Model offload is enabled by default. Reserve at least 80 GB disk space for weights, dependencies and temporary files. Full weights total about 33.1 GB.
3. Expose HTTP port 8000. Configure environment variables:

```text
HF_BOOTSTRAP_REPO=vladlen-beilik/qwen-image-2.1-runpod
QWEN_API_KEY=your-long-random-key
QWEN_OFFLOAD=model
QWEN_STORAGE_ROOT=/workspace
```

Set QWEN_STORAGE_ROOT to your actual persistent volume mount. This does not require `/workspace-global`. Keep HF_TOKEN in environment only if needed for model access. The bootstrap repository download currently assumes a public repository.

4. In the Pod terminal:

```bash
curl -fsSL --retry 3 https://huggingface.co/vladlen-beilik/qwen-image-2.1-runpod/resolve/main/bootstrap.sh -o /workspace/qwen-bootstrap.sh
bash /workspace/qwen-bootstrap.sh
```

These commands work after you upload the files. First launch installs dependencies and downloads weights. Later launches reuse the cache. The server loads the model once; only one request runs on the GPU at a time. No runtime archive is required. Dependencies follow upstream minimum versions and Diffusers main; record/pin working versions after your first verified run.

## API

Swagger: `https://POD_ID-8000.proxy.runpod.net/docs`
Health: `GET /health`

```bash
export QWEN_URL=https://POD_ID-8000.proxy.runpod.net
curl --fail-with-body "$QWEN_URL/generate" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $QWEN_API_KEY" \
  -F 'prompt=Photorealistic ancient Egyptian village at sunrise, cinematic documentary still' \
  -F 'width=1376' -F 'height=768' -F 'steps=40' -F 'seed=42' \
  --output result.png
```

For editing, add `-F 'image=@first-frame.png'` and describe the requested change in prompt. PNG output preserves alpha when the model produces it. For native transparency, use the model's recommended RGBA prompt format. For higher resolution, try width=2752 and height=1536; increase only after the initial generation succeeds.

`QWEN_OFFLOAD=none` keeps the pipeline on GPU; `sequential` uses more aggressive, slower offload. CPU offload requires sufficient system RAM. The default 1376x768 approximates 16:9 while using dimensions divisible by 16.

## Verification and limitations

Python and shell syntax checked locally. GPU inference, dependency installation and RunPod deployment have not been executed. This package has not been uploaded to your Hugging Face account. A proxy timeout may terminate the HTTP request during long generations; this synchronous API has no job polling. Use a job-based API for long production workloads.

Official model instructions: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
Model license: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1/blob/main/LICENSE

# SeedVR2 DiT — ConvRot INT8 & W4A8 Quantization (`asym_w4a8_int8` & `int8_tensorwise`)

This repository provides the official **ConvRot INT8** and **ConvRot W4A8 (`asym_w4a8_int8`)** quantized diffusion transformer (DiT) weights for [SeedVR2](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/SeedVR) / [ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT](https://github.com/ussoewwin/ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT).

It brings the original **15.35 GB** FP16 7B DiT down to **4.44 GB** (~71.1% memory & disk reduction) for W4A8, and **8.53 GiB** VRAM footprint for INT8, enabling native low-bit inference directly inside ComfyUI with comprehensive VRAM savings.

---

## Available Models & Checkpoint Specifications

| Model Checkpoint | Architecture | Precision / Layout | Disk Size | Peak VRAM | Hugging Face Direct URL |
|:---|:---|:---|:---:|:---:|:---|
| **`seedvr2_7b_convrot_w4a8.safetensors`** | 7B DiT Base | `asym_w4a8_int8` + ConvRot | **4.44 GB** | **5.69 GiB** | [Download](https://huggingface.co/ussoewwin/SeedVR2-ConvRot-INT8-and-w4a8/resolve/main/seedvr2_7b_convrot_w4a8.safetensors) |
| **`seedvr2_7b_sharp_convrot_w4a8.safetensors`** | 7B DiT Sharp | `asym_w4a8_int8` + ConvRot | **4.44 GB** | **5.69 GiB** | [Download](https://huggingface.co/ussoewwin/SeedVR2-ConvRot-INT8-and-w4a8/resolve/main/seedvr2_7b_sharp_convrot_w4a8.safetensors) |
| **`seedvr2_3b_convrot_w4a8.safetensors`** | 3B DiT Base | `asym_w4a8_int8` + ConvRot | **2.21 GB** | **5.69 GiB** | [Download](https://huggingface.co/ussoewwin/SeedVR2-ConvRot-INT8-and-w4a8/resolve/main/seedvr2_3b_convrot_w4a8.safetensors) |
| **`seedvr2_7b_convrot_int8.safetensors`** | 7B DiT Base | `int8_tensorwise` + ConvRot | **8.12 GB** | **8.53 GiB** | [Download](https://huggingface.co/ussoewwin/SeedVR2-ConvRot-INT8-and-w4a8/resolve/main/seedvr2_7b_convrot_int8.safetensors) |
| **`seedvr2_7b_sharp_convrot_int8.safetensors`** | 7B DiT Sharp | `int8_tensorwise` + ConvRot | **8.12 GB** | **8.53 GiB** | [Download](https://huggingface.co/ussoewwin/SeedVR2-ConvRot-INT8-and-w4a8/resolve/main/seedvr2_7b_sharp_convrot_int8.safetensors) |
| **`seedvr2_3b_convrot_int8.safetensors`** | 3B DiT Base | `int8_tensorwise` + ConvRot | **4.08 GB** | **5.69 GiB** | [Download](https://huggingface.co/ussoewwin/SeedVR2-ConvRot-INT8-and-w4a8/resolve/main/seedvr2_3b_convrot_int8.safetensors) |

---

## Technical Specifications (W4A8 Architecture)

| Parameter | Specification |
|:---|:---|
| **Base Architectures** | SeedVR2 7B / 3B NaDiT (ByteDance Seed) |
| **Quantization Format** | ComfyUI Native `asym_w4a8_int8` (`AsymW4A8Int8Layout`) |
| **Weight Precision** | INT4 packed into `torch.int8` storage (`[out_features, in_features // 2]`) |
| **Orthogonal Rotation** | **ConvRot** normalized Hadamard transform ($H_{256} \cdot H_{256}^T = I$) |
| **ConvRot Group Size** | `256` channels |
| **Weight Group Size** | `16` channels |
| **Scale Hierarchy** | **2-Level**: Per-channel scale (FP32) $\times$ Per-group relative scale (FP8 `e4m3fn`) |
| **Quantized Layers (7B)** | **288** Core Transformer Block Attention & MLP 2D Projection Weights |
| **Preserved Layers (7B)** | **842** Sensitive Layers strictly kept in **FP16** (Norms, Biases, RoPE, Embeddings, Output Heads) |
| **VRAM Reduction (7B)** | **~71.1%** weight footprint reduction |

---

## Trajectory Comparison & Empirical Benchmarks

Extensive multi-seed trajectory benchmarking across 25 deterministic seeds (`42` to `99999`) using [`benchmark/seedvr2_w4a8_traj_compare.py`](https://github.com/ussoewwin/ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT/blob/main/benchmark/seedvr2_w4a8_traj_compare.py) and [`seedvr2_int8_traj_compare.py`](https://github.com/ussoewwin/ComfyUI-SeedVR2-VideoUpscaler-with-TensorRT/blob/main/benchmark/seedvr2_int8_traj_compare.py):

Numbers are per-frame image statistics averaged over the clip; "detail vs step 1500" is the median per-frame ratio of the Laplacian variance (fine detail) to the step-1500 clip. | White cat 360 | Orbit step 750 (old, not in this repo) | CardSpin v1 (750 + 50) | **ORB360 step 1500** | CardSpin v2 (1500 + 50) | |---|---|---|---|---| | Fine detail (Laplacian variance) | 30.2 | 19.8 | **56.1** | 20.7 | | Detail vs step 1500 | 0.54x | 0.34x | **1.00x** | 0.35x | | Edge energy (Tenengrad) | 1098 | 809 | **1343** | 841 | | High-frequency share | 0.0035 | 0.0028 | **0.0050** | 0.0029 | | First frame vs the photo, PSNR / SSIM | 28.0 dB / 0.87 | 24.5 dB / 0.85 | **28.5 dB / 0.87** | 22.5 dB / 0.77 | ![Same frames from the four LoRAs, native-pixel crops](https://huggingface.co/MATLOWAI/MiniMax-H3-ORB360-CardSpin/resolve/main/assets/whitecat_orbit_detail_4way.jpg) - The high-resolution training nearly doubles the fine detail (step 750 -> step 1500: 1.85x, higher in all 124 frames). - **The 50 card-spin steps soften everything**, whichever orbit LoRA they start from: both CardSpin files keep only about a third of step 1500's fine detail and drift further from the photo in the first frame. The single card-spin training clip is a soft generated video, and 50 steps on it most likely pull the whole look towards it. - So: **step 1500 for orbits, CardSpin only for the card trick.** ## The original v1 videos CardSpin v1 (`minimax_h3_orb360_cardspin_step50.safetensors`), card-spin prompt:

To experience the latest model, please visit [Qwen Chat](https://qwen.ai) and select the "Image Editing" feature. Compared with Qwen-Image-Edit released in August, the main improvements of Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 include: * **Multi-image Editing Support**: For multi-image inputs, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 builds upon the Qwen-Image-Edit architecture and is further trained via image concatenation to enable multi-image editing. It supports various combinations such as "person + person," "person + product," and "person + scene." Optimal performance is currently achieved with 1 to 3 input images. * **Enhanced Single-image Consistency**: For single-image inputs, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 significantly improves editing consistency, specifically in the following areas: - **Improved Person Editing Consistency**: Better preservation of facial identity, supporting various portrait styles and pose transformations; - **Improved Product Editing Consistency**: Better preservation of product identity, supporting product poster editing； - **Improved Text Editing Consistency**: In addition to modifying text content, it also supports editing text fonts, colors, and materials； * **Native Support for ControlNet**: Including depth maps, edge maps, keypoint maps, and more. ## # Minimax-h3_Singularity-x-10Eros-Max_PRISM Merge of two Minimax-H3 Ref2VA finetunes with a custom algorithm (**PRISM**, no mergekit): * A: `WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity` / `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_bf16.safetensors` * B: `TenStrip/10Eros-Max` / `10Eros_Max_h3_8stepTURBO_beta6/7.safetensors` (8-step turbo) Weights: `Minimax-h3_Singularity_x_10Eros-Max_PRISM_b_fp16.safetensors` (fp16). Licence follows the source models - check them before use. ## Method 1. **Spectral denoise** - D=B-A split by randomised SVD into structured part L (rank<=64) and diffuse remainder R; B' = A + L + gamma\*R with adaptive gamma in [0.92, 1]. 2. **Polar geodesic** - per output row, direction by SLERP, magnitude by log-domain (geometric) interpolation. 3. **Sign-conflict mediation** - salient opposite-sign elements are pulled toward the weighted winner. 4. **Magnitude re-anchor** - rows rescaled to the geometric target norm. # ⚠️ **UPD1:** Test of the new version: 10Eros_Max_h3_8stepTURBO_beta7_SingularityV2_int8HQ.safetensors # ✨ **UPD2:** Test of the classic mix: 10Eros_Max_h3_TURBO-hybrid_beta5_Singularity_v1.3_int8.safetensors # 💝 **UPD3:** Test of the PIKA 1.00-strength mix: 10Eros_Max_SingularityV2_PikaFlex_1.00_int8HQ.safetensors # 💘 **UPD3:** Test of the PIKA 0.85-strength mix: 10Eros_Max_SingularityV2_PikaFlex_0.85_int8HQ.safetensors # 💖 **UPD4:** Test of the PRISM+PIKA 0.85-strength mix: 10Eros_Max_SingularityV2_PRISM2_PikaFlex_0.85_int8HQ.safetensors [🔗 My CivitAI Model Mirror](https://civitai.red/models/3019421/singularity-v2-x-10eros-max "Go to my CivitAI Mirror")

# MiniMax-H3 — combined (LoRA-fused · 8-bit conditioner · AoTI)

Joint video **and** synchronized soundtrack from a single denoising pass, packaged as a
deployment build of [`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)
(diffusers modular layout). This repo is tuned for **Hugging Face ZeroGPU Spaces**: the whole
checkpoint is ~112 GB on the Hub (under the 150 GB per-Space storage quota), and each half of
the split pattern fits the 95 GiB ZeroGPU card with room to spare — so it runs comfortably and
fast, at ~40 s for a 5 s clip instead of the 5+ minutes a 30-step base run pays.

Full, unmodified bf16 partitions (including the 62 GiB bf16 conditioner) remain available in the
private backup [`addlabsviral/minimax-h3-combined-bkup`](https://huggingface.co/addlabsviral/minimax-h3-combined-bkup).

## Repo layout

| Folder | Content | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `transformer/` | 50-block MiniMax-H3 transformer, **bfloat16, LoRA-fused** | 14 shards + index; the Turbo LoRA is *folded into the weights* (not a runtime adapter) |
| `text_encoder/` | Qwen3-VL conditioner, **8-bit** | single 34.9 GB safetensors + `quantization_config` in `config.json` |
| `vae/` + `audio_vae/` | video and audio autoencoders, **float32, unquantized** | joint video + soundtrack decode |
| `aoti/` | **AoTI-compiled transformer-block package** | `aoti/package/submodules/transformer_blocks/package.pt2` |
| `lora/` | the Turbo LoRA checkpoint kept for reference | already folded — loading it again is not needed |
| `scheduler/`, `audio_scheduler/`, `tokenizer/`, `processor/` | small configs | untouched from base |
| `model_index.json`, `modular_model_index.json` | diffusers modular indexes | point at `transformer/` and `text_encoder/` as-is |

## `transformer/` — LoRA-fused, 4-step inference

The
[`larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora`](https://huggingface.co/larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora)
Turbo checkpoint (`minimax_h3_turbo_4step_ema_ckpt850`, the final EMA round, sharp at 4 steps)
is baked into the bf16 weights at conversion time — `scale * (lora_B @ lora_A)` is added into
every targeted projection (fused-QKV thirds, SwiGLU gate/value swap, AdaLN rows), so an adapter
wrap at load time is unnecessary and the checkpoint serves 4-step inference out of the box.

- **4 steps** is the design point; 6 is a comfort setting, 28 is the unturbo fallback.
- Guidance-distilled: no CFG, no negative prompt — every step is one forward pass.
- 24 fps, `num_frames` of the form `17 * n + 5` (2–15 s).

## `text_encoder/` — 8-bit bitsandbytes

The 62 GiB bf16 Qwen3-VL conditioner is served from a single safetensors file with a
bitsandbytes **LLM.int8** `quantization_config` (`load_in_8bit: true`, threshold 6.0, no skip
modules). `from_pretrained` applies the quantization automatically at load, so the conditioner
runs in about a third of the memory and there is no manual quantize step. Requires
`bitsandbytes` and `transformers==5.8.0`.

## `aoti/` — compiled transformer blocks

One AOT-Inductor `MiniMaxH3TransformerBlock` package, shared byte-identically by all 50 blocks,
exported with a **dynamic sequence dimension** (original key `bf16/torch2.11/sm120/dynamic`,
flattened to `aoti/`, with the loader layout `aoti/package/submodules/transformer_blocks/`
preserved). It removes ~0.5 s/step of kernel-launch and epilogue overhead and is
card-specific: built for the ZeroGPU pool's RTX PRO 6000 (sm120) cards with torch 2.11.
Everything else falls back to eager safely.

## Usage

```python
import torch
from diffusers import MiniMaxH3ModularPipeline

pipe = MiniMaxH3ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("addlabsviral/minimax-h3-combined")
pipe.load_components()          # text encoder quantizes to 8-bit per its config

state = pipe(
    prompt="a cinematic drone shot over a neon city at night",
    height=544, width=960,
    num_frames=124,             # 17 * n + 5
    num_inference_steps=4,      # the Turbo LoRA's design point
    generator=torch.Generator("cpu").manual_seed(42),
)
```

For the *split* ZeroGPU pattern (conditioner Space + denoiser/reconstructor Space), point
`H3_MODEL_REPO` at this repo and `H3_AOTI` at the `aoti/` package; `modular_model_index.json`
already resolves `transformer/` and `text_encoder/`, so `load_components` fetches exactly the
subfolders each half declares.
