# SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-8step-ComfyUI

**8-step SMD reference-conditioned generation with synchronized audio, using native ComfyUI nodes.** Includes the converted LoRA, ready-to-run workflows and reproducible example inputs.

[Original checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-8step) · [SMD code](https://github.com/zjwfufu/SMD)

<video controls poster="https://huggingface.co/zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-8step-ComfyUI/resolve/main/examples/poster.webp" src="https://huggingface.co/zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-8step-ComfyUI/resolve/main/examples/preview.mp4" width="100%"></video>

[Generated video with audio](examples/sample.mp4) · [Prompt and inputs](case.json)

## Run

New to ComfyUI? Download this repository with the first three commands below, then follow [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) for the tested Linux/NVIDIA installation. If ComfyUI is already installed, run all four commands using its Python environment. No custom nodes or SMD source checkout are needed.

```bash
python -m pip install -U huggingface-hub
hf auth login
hf download zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-8step-ComfyUI --exclude '*.safetensors' --local-dir SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-8step-ComfyUI
python SMD-MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-8step-ComfyUI/download_models.py --comfyui /path/to/ComfyUI
```

The installer verifies the model files, copies example inputs, and adds the complete workflow to ComfyUI's default user library.

1. Start ComfyUI and open its browser interface (normally `http://127.0.0.1:8188`).
2. Click **Workflows** in the left sidebar, expand **SMD**, and double-click **H3-Ref2VA-8step-Compact**. Refresh the page if it was already open. Alternatively, drag the downloaded [`workflow.json`](workflow.json) file onto the canvas.
3. Confirm the workflow contains **Load LoRA** and **Save Video**, then click **Run** with the supplied settings. This loads the complete graph; no manual node connections are needed.
4. When the job completes, play the result in **Save Video** and enable sound. The MP4 is also saved under `ComfyUI/output/`.

The example generates about five seconds of video with audio. After your first successful run, edit the prompt or the seed in **RandomNoise**. To switch between 4 and 8 steps, install and open the corresponding repository's workflow and LoRA.

Use this repository's complete workflow. Substituting H3 weights into ComfyUI's default image template can fail with errors such as `audio_scale` missing. See [setup and troubleshooting](SETUP.md#troubleshooting).

The two source images condition subject appearance independently; replace them in the Load Image nodes and keep their order aligned with `<Picture 1>` and `<Picture 2>` in the prompt.

## Model profiles

| Profile | Workflow | Downloads |
|---|---|---:|
| Compact (default; example above) | [workflow.json](workflow.json) | 42.0 GB |
| Unpruned BF16 transformer | [workflow_bf16.json](workflow_bf16.json) | 101.2 GB |

The compact profile uses the official pruned INT8 transformer, NVFP4-AWQ text encoder and INT8 video VAE. The BF16 profile uses an INT8 text encoder and FP16 video VAE. Both use the FP32 audio VAE and the same BF16 SMD LoRA. Shared files are downloaded once and verified by SHA-256; the base files come from [Comfy-Org](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3). **4-step SMD for video and audio generation.** The student adapters, standalone inference code and reproducible examples are included. Upstream base components are downloaded separately.

[Training code](https://github.com/zjwfufu/SMD) · [SMD collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/zjwfufu/smd-6ac5f4b53c26548a75672189)

## Example

An ivory spacecraft marked SMD lifts off from a desert landing pad at blue hour.

<video controls poster="https://huggingface.co/zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-T2VA-4step/resolve/main/examples/poster.png" src="https://huggingface.co/zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-T2VA-4step/resolve/main/examples/sample.mp4" width="100%"></video>

[Download video with audio](examples/sample.mp4)

**Seed:** 42. **Size:** 1344 × 768. **Frames:** 124 at 24 fps. **Steps:** 4.

[Full prompt and case settings](examples/case.json) · [Generation receipt](examples/generation.json)

## Models

| Variant | Weights | Steps | Size |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| default | LoRA | 4 | 1.38 GB |

## Run

For a native ComfyUI workflow on a single GPU, use the corresponding [SMD-MiniMax-H3-T2VA-4step-ComfyUI](https://huggingface.co/zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-T2VA-4step-ComfyUI). It includes a Compact profile and a BF16 transformer profile. The Python runner below uses two GPUs.

Base: [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3).

Use Linux, Python 3.12, Git and two NVIDIA GPUs with CUDA support. The requirements install Diffusers from a pinned Git revision. The included inference code does not import the SMD training repository.

```bash
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install huggingface-hub
# Sign in to Hugging Face.
hf auth login
hf download zjwfufu/SMD-MiniMax-H3-T2VA-4step --local-dir SMD-MiniMax-H3-T2VA-4step --exclude "lora/adapter_model.safetensors"
cd SMD-MiniMax-H3-T2VA-4step
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python infer.py --output outputs
```

The runner requires two CUDA GPUs and launches two processes with FSDP2. It was tested on **2 × A100 80 GB**, with 433 GiB of host RAM. It downloads only the selected transformer plus shared encoders, decoders and processor files to the Hugging Face cache. The selected base components occupy approximately **144 GB (134 GiB) per workflow**; keeping both workflows reuses the shared components and requires approximately **210 GB (196 GiB)** in total. Loading and fusing these weights can take longer than the sampling steps. `--base` selects a complete local upstream snapshot, and `--case` selects another case JSON.

The runner prefers `smd_lora.safetensors` at the repository root and falls back to the retained `lora/adapter_model.safetensors` path. Both files have identical bytes. The download command excludes the legacy duplicate; adapter fusion and sampling settings are unchanged.

## Sampling

The released sampler uses raw final-segment scale **0.5**. The raw grid is built before the model-specific time shift. The included runner follows `sampling.json`; changing only an upstream pipeline's step count does not reproduce the student.

Video shift is 12; audio shift is 3. LoRA scale is 1.0. The default case uses 124 frames at 24 fps and joint video/audio generation.

The supplied loader validates and applies all LoRA matrices and saved replacement tensors, with the recorded merge precision. Omitting replacement tensors or using a different base can change the result.

# Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-step32000-GGUF

Quantized with **ComfyUI-GGUF** `tools/convert.py` (molbal fork, commit `61843db580f8549a85b0a1ed850d550079fadfee`), LoRA fused at **strength 0.8**.

- Base: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` ComfyUI single-file transformer (265 tensors, `img_mlp.gate_up` + `out`), SHA256 `89f4158d066cc33906a199fca85634f766892dd78f49b6698dabf187ac86c4bc`.
- Adapter: `qwen21_full1024_r128-step00032000-comfy-fused.safetensors` (192 targets, rank 128, alpha 128), SHA256 `3bb604a1f73f8a51fd1f5e88ec541c935dccb9adee673f69c2cc1fc0bc4d6924`.
- Merge accumulation: FP32; quantizer input for merged weights: FP32.

## Files

| File | Size | Tensor types |
|---|---:|---|
| `qwen21_step32000_lora0p8-F16.gguf` | 14.23 GB | 192 × F16 + 8 × BF16 + 65 × F32 |
| `qwen21_step32000_lora0p8-Q8_0.gguf` | 7.69 GB | 192 × Q8_0 + 8 × BF16 + 65 × F32 |
| `qwen21_step32000_lora0p8-Q5_K_M.gguf` | 5.21 GB | 128 × Q5_K + 64 × Q6_K + 8 × BF16 + 65 × F32 |

All three have **265 tensors**. SHA256SUMS is included.

## ComfyUI

```text
ComfyUI/models/
├── diffusion_models/    qwen21_step32000_lora0p8-Q5_K_M.gguf
├── text_encoders/       qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors  (or qwen3vl_8b_bf16.safetensors)
└── vae/                 qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors
```

Text encode: `CLIPLoader` (`type=qwen_image`) + `TextEncodeQwenImage21`.
Recommended eval settings: 1728×1728, 25 steps, cfg 4.0, `er_sde`/`simple`, seed 42.

## Reproducibility

These files are bit-identical (SHA256) to the `lora0p8` reference exports produced by the same script from the same base/adapter at strength 0.8.

# LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Sandstorm

**Sandstorm** for **LTX-2.5-22B**. A clear clip goes in as the reference. The same shot comes back with a sandstorm. Density is a line in the prompt, not the LoRA strength.

Based on [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5).

## Example outputs

Same shot, same framing. **Top:** the clear plate. **Bottom:** that same video at step 2000, strength 1. Five examples are a heavy sandstorm. The desert road is near whiteout.

<Gallery />

| Example | Scene | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `examples/highway_30134225_sbs.mp4` | Mountain highway. The road stays. The mountains fade. | Heavy |
| `examples/street_39746014_sbs.mp4` | Town street. The houses stay readable. | Heavy |
| `examples/dune_6573940_sbs.mp4` | A person on a dune. The person stays. | Heavy |
| `examples/town_36182372_sbs.mp4` | Town from above. The nearest roofs stay. | Heavy |
| `examples/desert_4457802_sbs.mp4` | Desert road. The distance is buried. The car and the road stay. | Whiteout |
| `examples/crowd_34762053_sbs.mp4` | City crowd. The people stay readable. | Heavy |

Clear plates are Pexels videos: [30134225](https://www.pexels.com/video/30134225/), [39746014](https://www.pexels.com/video/39746014/), [6573940](https://www.pexels.com/video/6573940/), [36182372](https://www.pexels.com/video/36182372/), [4457802](https://www.pexels.com/video/4457802/), [34762053](https://www.pexels.com/video/34762053/).

## Model files

| File | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| **`ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-sandstorm.safetensors`** | **Release** (training **step 2000**) |

Trained on `ltx-2.5-22b-dev`. For inference, use the distilled transformer with `ICLoraPipeline`, stage 1 only. Keep the strength at **1.0**.

## Model details

- **Base model:** LTX-2.5-22B
- **Training type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video)
- **Control:** a clear reference video. The adapter adds the sandstorm to that shot
- **Trigger:** `ADD SANDSTORM` in every prompt
- **Density:** the next sentence. Light dust haze, blowing sand, heavy sandstorm, or near whiteout
- **Text encoder:** Gemma 4 (`gemma4-12b-ltx-v1`)
- **Audio:** this adapter does not generate sound

## How to prompt

Always include `ADD SANDSTORM`, then one density line.

```text
ADD SANDSTORM. Light dust haze. The same <scene>. The shot is still clear up close. A thin veil sits in the distance.
```

```text
ADD SANDSTORM. Heavy sandstorm. The same <scene>. The air is filled with sand. Far shapes fade. Near subjects stay sharper than the background.
```

```text
ADD SANDSTORM. Near whiteout. The same <scene>. The distance is buried. A heavy wall of sand leaves only the nearest shapes.
```

`<scene>` is a short description of the reference, such as `mountain highway` or `town street sunny`.

## Inference

Stage 1 of `ICLoraPipeline` runs at half the requested resolution, and stage 2 drops the LoRA. Request double the training resolution and pass `--skip-stage-2` so the adapter runs at the native training size, 960×544.

```bash
python -m ltx_pipelines.ic_lora \
  --transformer-path /path/to/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-bf16.safetensors \
  --text-encoder-path /path/to/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-bf16.safetensors \
  --video-vae-path /path/to/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors \
  --audio-vae-path /path/to/ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors \
  --spatial-upsampler-path /path/to/ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-b

# FLUX.3 Image Klein · Natural Facial Skin Texture LoRA

**Add natural facial skin texture to portraits.**

> **Workflow update — October 29, 2026:** The new [Natural Facial Texture workflow](flux3_image_klein_%E7%9C%9F%E5%AE%9E%E8%84%B8%E9%83%A8%E7%BA%B9%E7%90%86.json) is now recommended. In the author's tested images, it resolved the positional drift observed with the previous workflow, avoided the previously observed Chinese-text corruption, and substantially improved overall quality. The previous workflow remains available. Reported 4K generation time is approximately **3 minutes** with the new workflow, compared with **1 minute 40 seconds** previously. See the workflow comparison and performance sections below.

![Natural Facial Skin Texture LoRA cover](cover.png)

## Model overview

This image-editing LoRA adds natural-looking facial skin texture, subtle pores, and fine microtexture to portraits with overly smooth, untextured, or weakly textured skin. Its goal is to introduce natural skin detail while retaining the subject's identity, facial features, expression, skin tone, lighting, and composition as closely as possible.

- **Training base:** [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base).
- **Model type:** An image-editing LoRA adapter. A compatible base model and its supporting components must be loaded separately.
- **Weight format:** Safetensors, BF16, rank 64, exported with AI Toolkit.
- **Available checkpoints:** 14 training checkpoints are currently available.
- **Recommended checkpoints:** **5,000 and 5,600 training steps** are the author's recommendations and the versions tested most extensively. Other checkpoints have received less testing. The degree of fit differs across training stages, so their results may vary; they are provided as alternatives rather than equally validated recommendations. A later training step does not necessarily produce a better result; compare them for your input and preferred texture intensity.
- **Trigger words:** No additional custom trigger word is required. Describe the desired edit in natural language.

## Example results

These images were supplied by the author. In the comparison images, **the input is on the left and the texture-enhanced result is on the right**. The medium-shot example also includes matching facial close-ups. The cover is a presentation image and does not establish an input/output direction.

# LTX-2.5 for MLX (dynamic 8-bit)

An Apple Silicon (MLX) port of [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) by Lightricks: text to video
and image to video (a start image), the distilled two-stage pipeline, with **dynamic 8-bit** weights. No PyTorch, no
CUDA.

- **Ported line by line** from the [official code](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2) (v1.5.0, commit `e98f6d9`):
  tokenizer, Gemma 4 text encoder, feature extractor and connectors, the 48-block audio-video transformer, the
  ancestral sampler and its noise order, the x2 latent upsampler, the tiled conv VAE decoder and the H.264 file;
  for image to video the still's loading and H.264 re-compression, the VAE encoder, the per-token timesteps and the
  pinning of the first frame in both stages.
- **Proven against the official model** at its own precision (bf16) before quantizing: in fp32 every part matches the
  official fp32 output (strict gates); in bf16 every part is as accurate as the official bf16 against the exact
  answer (ratio 0.98-1.00); the whole sampling chain reproduces the official run bit for bit.
- **Dynamic 8-bit** (in the spirit of Unsloth's dynamic quants): every one of the 1,771 large weight matrices was
  quantized on its own and its effect measured (fp32, real denoising states); whole recipes were then compared on
  held-out data against the official 16-bit model's own rounding error. The most sensitive tensors stay 16-bit (48 in
  the transformer, mostly in its last blocks; 48 in Gemma, the token embeddings and the early layers' feed-forwards),
  the rest is 8-bit, group size 32. Result: **45.8 GB instead of 66 GB, as fast as 16-bit, and within about 5% of
  the official 16-bit model's own error** (below).

Independent port; not an official Lightricks release. See `NOTICE.md`.

## Quickstart

Requirements: an Apple Silicon Mac (tested on an M5 with 24 GB; a clip peaks at 9.3 GB), Python 3.14, ffmpeg on the
PATH, 46 GB of disk.

```bash
hf download zero0303/ltx-2.5-mlx-dynamic-8bit --local-dir ltx-2.5-mlx
cd ltx-2.5-mlx
uv venv --python 3.14 .venv
VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv uv pip install "mlx==0.32.2" "numpy==2.4.6" "tokenizers==0.23.3" "av==19.0.2" "pillow==13.0.0"
.venv/bin/python generate.py "Night, heavy rain on an empty city street ..." -o clip.mp4 --seed 7
```

Options: `--width 1024 --height 576` (multiples of 64), `--frames 121` (8k + 1; 121 = 5.04 s), `--fps 24`, `--seed`,
`--image start.png` (the clip starts from this image; `--image-strength`, default 1.0), `--models` (this pack by
default, or a folder with Lightricks' 16-bit release). The output is an H.264 MP4 (BT.709, crf 19), no sound.

From Python:

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "ltx-2.5-mlx")
from ltx25.pipeline import generate

generate("A lighthouse on a cliff at dusk, waves below, the camera slowly circles.", "out.mp4", seed=42,
         width=1024, height=576, num_frames=121, models="ltx-2.5-mlx/models/ltx-2.5-mlx-8bit")
```

## Speed and memory (M5, 24 GB)

One 5-second clip at 1024 x 576 (121 frames): **440 s** (7.3 min). Prompt encoding 17 s, stage 1 (8 steps at
512 x 288) 16 s a step, stage 2 (3 steps at 1024 x 576) 72 s a step, the 16-bit model's speed; decoding 70 s.
**Peak memory 9.3 GB** for the whole process (MLX's own peak 7.6 GB, in the prompt encoding): the weights are streamed
one transformer block or Gemma layer at a time, and the decoder works through each tile a few frames at a time.

## Accuracy

Error of one denoising call against the exact fp32 model (Lightricks' weights), on real full-size inputs, as a multiple
of the official-precision 16-bit runtime's own error:

| | stage 1 (2,304 tokens) | stage 2 (9,216 tokens) |
|---|---|---|
| 16-bit (official precision) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| **dynamic 8-bit** | 1.05 video, 1.04 audio | 1.06 video, 1.07 audio |

Measured on its own (fp32), the quantization adds about 0.4 of the 16-bit rounding error in the
transformer and 0.48-0.61 in the text encoder. Plain 8-bit (every weight 8-bit) adds 0.72-1.48 in the text encoder,
up to more than 16-bit itself: errors in Gemma's early layers grow through its 48 layers. Keeping the sensitive tensors
16-bit is what fixes that.

| `models/ltx-2.5-mlx-8bit/diffusion_models/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-8bit.safetensors` | 26.0 GB | the transformer (1,296 block matrices and the 96 connector linears 8-bit; 48 block matrices, norms, gates, AdaLN, patchify and output layers as shipped) |

# Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo — v0.3

**Built with Qwen.** A few-step distilled version of [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)
by Viggle. Text-to-image and instruction-driven editing with 1–3 reference images in **6 steps instead of 40**, with
**no classifier-free guidance**.

<video controls autoplay muted loop playsinline width="100%"
  src="https://huggingface.co/Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo/resolve/main/assets/viggle_turbo_promo.mp4"></video>

About **5× faster** than the 40-step base model end to end, and very competitive with it in quality: on the official
Qwen examples the two are hard to tell apart on most prompts. The clearest gaps are small, dense text and complicated
edits ([Known limitations](#known-limitations)). Compare them yourself in the **Comparison** tab of the
[demo Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo).

## v0.3 (2026-09-29)

* **6 steps, a different balance.** Against v0.2.1: less grain and cleaner surfaces, fine texture a little softer;
  diversity (still close to the base model's) and small-text accuracy about the same. It is not a strict upgrade: if
  you prefer the crisper look, v0.2.1 is still in the repository.
* **New 9-step mode:** 7 turbo steps, then the LoRA is switched off and the base model finishes the last two.
  Finer detail, and small text comes out right more often (not always). It takes about 1.4–1.5× as long as 6 steps
  (still about 3.5× faster than the base model). It works in diffusers and the demo Space only ([9 steps](#9-steps)).
* **We think 6 steps is close to its capacity.** Since v0.2.1, every gain we found at 6 steps cost something
  elsewhere: sharper came with more grain, less grain came with a softer look. Beyond this point, quality most likely
  has to be paid for with steps, which is what the 9-step mode does.

| file | |
|---|---|
| `Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo-v0.3-6step-lora-r256.safetensors` | **v0.3 LoRA** (rank 256, bf16, 1.3 GB), loaded on the base transformer at runtime. **Use this.** |
| `Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo-v0.3-6step-lora-r128.safetensors` | the same adapter cut to rank 128 (0.7 GB), used by the [ComfyUI workflows](#comfyui) |
| `peft_v0.3/` | the v0.3 adapter in peft key format |
| `...-{v0.3,v0.2.1}-6step-{int8_convrot,fp8_e4m3fn}.safetensors`, `...-{Q8_0,Q6_K,Q5_K_M,Q4_K_M}.gguf` | the LoRA merged into the base transformer, one file per format, for ComfyUI ([single-file transformers](#single-file-transformers)) |
| `comfyui/` | ComfyUI custom nodes, text-to-image / edit workflows, example inputs |
| `scheduler/` | the base scheduler config with `shift_terminal: null` |
| `...-v0.2.1-6step-lora-r256/r128.safetensors`, `peft_v0.2.1/` | v0.2.1 (2026-09-24), same usage |
| `...-v0.2-5step-lora-r256/r128.safetensors`, `peft_v0.2/` | v0.2 (2026-09-23), same usage (6 steps) |

## Install

```bash
pip install -U torch "transformers>=5.17,<6" accelerate safetensors peft pillow
pip install "git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers.git@80c7ed262aeffbeb43ef13ae04baeb9b84515a69"
```

`QwenImage21Pipeline` is not in a released `diffusers` yet, hence the pinned git install. `peft` is required.

## Usage

```python
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline, FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
pipe.load_lora_weights(
    "Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo",
    weight_name="Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo-v0.3-6step-lora-r256.safetensors",
)
pipe.scheduler = FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler.from_pretrained(
    "Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo", subfolder="scheduler"
)
pipe.to("cuda")

STEPS, SIGMAS = 6, [1.0, 0.9375, 0.875, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25]   # pass both to every call

    true_cfg_scale=1.0,                                   # no CFG (also the default)

image.save("out.png")
```

# FLUX 3 Image Klein

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

![Teaser](./teaser.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the distilled checkpoint for generation and image editing. For fine-tuning, LoRA training and research, use [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, [flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup), which the reference code loads by default, or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours). Diffusers runs neither on its own; see [Prompt upsampling](#prompt-upsampling).

This repository includes the BF16 transformer and [FP8](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/fp8r) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/nvfp4) variants, together with the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder and image autoencoder.

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

## Download

Download the root BF16 distilled package, including its text encoder and image autoencoder, without downloading the quantized variants:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

snapshot_download(
    repo_id="black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein",
    local_dir="weights/flux-3-image-klein",
    allow_patterns=[
        "model.safetensors", "config.json", "manifest.json",
        "ae.safetensors", "text_encoder/*",
        "README.md", "LICENSE.md", "NOTICE.md",
    ],
)
```

To download a quantized distilled transformer instead, replace the three root transformer patterns (`model.safetensors`, `config.json`, and `manifest.json`) with `variants/fp8r/*` or `variants/nvfp4/*`. Keep `ae.safetensors` and `text_encoder/*` for the other components.

These files contain the model package, not a complete inference application. Use an inference implementation that supports flow-map sampling and this checkpoint format. Quantized packages need a loader that supports their format; their file size is not a measure of total GPU memory use.

## Using with reference code

The distilled checkpoint is served on the [BFL API](https://bfl.ai) as FLUX 3 Image Klein. The reference inference code is [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein).

From the reference implementation checkout, install the package and download the two components the CLI loads besides this checkpoint. The CLI reads its weights from `weights/` (set `WEIGHTS_DIR` for another root), where the download above puts this repository.

```bash
pip install -e .

# safety classifier, always loaded
hf download Falconsai/nsfw_image_detection --local-dir weights/nsfw-classifier
# prompt upsampler (18.8 GB), on by default; --no-pup sends the prompt as typed, for captions written by another LLM
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-k

It also works with `--fp16-vae`. **🧨 Diffusers** ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline, AutoencoderKLQwenImage21 vae = AutoencoderKLQwenImage21.from_pretrained("madebyollin/texture-fix-vae-for-qwen-image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16) pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", vae=vae, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda") ``` # Mechanism ## Fixing Checkerboard Artifacts Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-2.1 was cured of checkerboard artifacts by finetuning the highest-resolution blocks briefly using the adversarial recipe developed for [TAESD](https://github.com/madebyollin/taesd). The TAESD recipe, like most image autoencoder training recipes, uses a mix of PSNR-focused (MSE/MAE), LPIPS, and adversarial (GAN) loss terms. Whenever precise details can't be reconstructed, MSE/MAE loss encourages blurring, LPIPS loss encourages blurring+checkerboarding (among other artifacts), and adversarial loss encourages generating sharp/plausible (but fake) detail without obvious artifacts. This figure from [DC-AE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10733) shows the importance of including adversarial (GAN) loss: ![Demo of the effects of adversarial loss, courtesy of the DC-AE paper](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/630447d40547362a22a969a2/uj9vJSR34LyZEkQeL-VOU.png) Figure: from *Deep Compression Autoencoder for Efficient High-Resolution Diffusion Models* (Chen et al., 2024, [arXiv:2410.10733](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10733)), licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); cropped to the first two rows. I suspect the original Qwen-Image-2.1-VAE was trained without a working adversarial loss term. ## Fixing NaNs in FP16 Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-2.1 runs fine in fp16, whereas the original Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE decoder often produces NaNs (the 🟪 magenta-highlighted regions below): | Qwen-Image-2.1-VAE (bf16) | ⚠️ Qwen-Image-2.1-VAE (fp16) | Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-2.1 (fp16) | | --- | --- | --- | | ![](./images/fp16-demo-official-bf16.png) | ![](./images/fp16-demo-official-fp16.png) | ![](./images/fp16-demo-texture-fix-fp16.png) | The original VAE decoder mostly produces NaNs in fully-transparent regions, but they bleed into surrounding content. You can reproduce this visualization with [`fp16_demo.py`](./fp16_demo.py). Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-2.1 was cured of the NaNs-in-FP16 issue by: 1) Finetuning the decoder weights to keep outputs the same while reducing activation magnitudes (like [SDXL-VAE-FP16-Fix](https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/sdxl-vae-fp16-fix)) 2) Manually shrinking certain weights to further reduce the scale of the residual stream (every residual branch starts with

# Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-step90000

Merged LoRA checkpoint of **Qwen-Image-2.1**, step 90000.

## Merge info

```json
{
  "base": "Qwen-Image-2.1",
  "lora": "qwen21_full1024_r128-step00090000.safetensors",
  "scale": 1.0,
  "modules": 224,
  "network_dim": "128",
  "network_alpha": "128.0"
}
```

## Contents

- `transformer/` — diffusers `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` (bf16, sharded)
- `text_encoder/` — `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` (bf16)
- `vae/` — `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21`
- `processor/`, `scheduler/`, `model_index.json`
- `merged/` — single-file merged transformer (`qwen_image_2.1_step90000_merged_bf16.safetensors`)

## Usage

```python
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline
import torch

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained(
    "chatrlabs/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-step90000",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)
pipe.to("cuda")
image = pipe(prompt="a cinematic film still", num_inference_steps=25, guidance_scale=1.0).images[0]
```

For ComfyUI GGUF, see `chatrlabs/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-step90000-GGUF`.

## Verification

- 297 tensors, 32 blocks, bf16; `img_in`, `txt_in`, `attn.norm_q/k` preserved.
- Quantized versions: see the GGUF repo (Q8_0 ~0.565% relative RMSE, Q4_0 ~8.3%).
- s32000 is the recommended step; s90000 is known to be less stable on text rendering.

# Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-step90000-GGUF

GGUF quantizations of the merged LoRA checkpoint **Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-step90000**.

Source: `qwen_image_2.1_step90000_merged_bf16.safetensors` (14.23 GB, 297 tensors, 32 blocks).
Architecture: `qwen_image21`, key names kept in diffusers form (`img_in.weight`, `transformer_blocks.N.attn.to_q.weight`, `img_mlp.gate_layer/proj`, ...).

## Files

| File | Size |
|---|---:|
| `qwen-image-2.1-s90000-BF16.gguf` | 14.23 GB |
| `qwen-image-2.1-s90000-Q8_0.gguf` | 7.59 GB |
| `qwen-image-2.1-s90000-Q6_K.gguf` | 5.88 GB |
| `qwen-image-2.1-s90000-Q5_K_M.gguf` | 5.22 GB |
| `qwen-image-2.1-s90000-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 4.60 GB |
| `qwen-image-2.1-s90000-Q4_0.gguf` | 4.15 GB |

Recommended: **Q4_K_M**.

## Quantization rules

| Variant | Rule |
|---|---|
| BF16 | original |
| Q8_0 | all non-protected tensors Q8_0 |
| Q6_K | all non-protected tensors Q6_K |
| Q5_K_M | `attn.to_v` / `img_mlp.out` Q6_K, rest Q5_K |
| Q4_K_M | `attn.to_v` / `img_mlp.out` Q6_K, rest Q4_K |
| Q4_0 | `img_mlp.out` Q4_1, rest Q4_0 |

Protected layers kept BF16 in every variant: `img_in.*`, `txt_in.*`, all `attn.norm_q/norm_k` (68 tensors).

## Verification

Full 297-tensor dequantized comparison against the bf16 source (global relative RMSE):

| Variant | RMSE |
|---|---:|
| BF16 | bit-identical |
| Q8_0 | 0.565 % |
| Q6_K | 1.808 % |
| Q5_K_M | 3.167 % |
| Q4_K_M | 6.062 % |
| Q4_0 | 8.321 % |

Protected layers are bit-identical to the source in both checkpoints. `SHA256SUMS` is included.

## ComfyUI

Requires ComfyUI with Qwen-Image-2.1 support and [ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF) (arch list includes `qwen_image21`).

```text
ComfyUI/models/
├── diffusion_models/    qwen-image-2.1-s90000-Q4_K_M.gguf
├── text_encoders/       qwen3vl_8b_bf16.safetensors
└── vae/                 qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors
```

Sampler: `euler` + `simple`, 25–40 steps, cfg 1.0, denoise 1.0. Resolution 1024×1024 and up (multiples of 32).

# dznpen — handwriting LoRA for Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo

Compact, irregularly joined handwriting (EN / FR / ES). Trigger: **`dznpen`**. Preferred strength: **0.75**.

Trained for OCR-style single-line crops (1024×256). Not a verified writer-ID model. Numerals, euro signs, and multi-line scenes are weaker.

## Examples

Real train reference:

![Real handwriting](assets/real-fountain-reference.png)

Adapter outputs (requested text ≠ certified label):

| | |
|---|---|
| ![FR](assets/r512_s9600-line_00.png) | `Préparer le dossier avant jeudi.` |
| ![EN](assets/r512_s9600-line_05.png) | `Two screws and a spare washer.` |
| ![ES](assets/r512_s9600-line_08.png) | `Total pagado: 14,25 €.` |

Base alone (descriptive prompt, unmatched probe):

![Untouched base](assets/base-descriptive-french.png)

## Use

```python
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo",
    revision="fc13ba1986fcb905854dc8de2f52eee395f49b5b",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
).to("cuda")
adapter = snapshot_download("domenzain/dznpen-qwen-image-2.1-lora")
pipe.load_lora_weights(adapter, adapter_name="dznpen")
pipe.set_adapters("dznpen", adapter_weights=0.75)

prompt = (
    'A single line in dznpen, the personal compact connected handwriting style, '
    'in dark fountain pen on plain white paper. Uneven joins and natural spacing. '
    'Write exactly: "Remember the keys."'
)
image = pipe(
    prompt=prompt, width=1024, height=256, use_kv_cache=True,
    generator=torch.Generator("cpu").manual_seed(9020),
).images[0]
```

Do not treat the prompt string as ground truth for OCR — read the pixels.

## Training (short)

| | |
|---|---|
| Base | `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo` @ `fc13ba1986fcb905854dc8de2f52eee395f49b5b` |
| Data | [`domenzain/dznpen-qwen-image-data`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/domenzain/dznpen-qwen-image-data) — 59 train lines, 12 val |
| LoRA | rank/alpha 512, attention only, BF16, ~537M adapter params |
| Steps | 9,600 cumulative (warm-start 3,200 + 6,400; Adam/RNG reset at 3,200) |
| File | `pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors` |

# MiniMax H3 Ref2VA — ComfyUI weights (BF16)

Exact, unpruned weights for the native MiniMax H3 Ref2VA workflow in ComfyUI:
one diffusion model, one text/visual encoder, and the video and audio VAEs.
Mirrored here so a deployment can be pulled and reproduced without depending
on upstream repositories staying available.

No quantized, pruned, or re-exported variants are included. Each file is
byte-identical to its upstream original; the SHA256 values below are the
upstream ones.

## Contents

| File | Role | Precision | Size |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| `diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_bf16.safetensors` | video main | BF16 | 66.3 GB |
| `text_encoders/H3/qwen3vl_32b_h3_ultra_uncensored_heretic_bf16.safetensors` | text/visual encoder | BF16 | 51.5 GB |
| `vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors` | video VAE | FP16 | 5.2 GB |
| `vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors` | audio VAE | FP32 | 605 MB |

Total 123.6 GB. Paths are relative to `ComfyUI/models/`.

## Pull

```bash
pip install -U "huggingface_hub[hf_xet]"
python pull_weights.py /path/to/ComfyUI          # verifies size + SHA256
```

`manifest.json` lists every file with its size, SHA256, and upstream
repository/revision. The script skips files that are already correct and
re-downloads anything that is not. Use `--dry-run` to only plan,
`--only SUBSTR` to pull a subset, and `--no-verify` to skip hashing.

The same manifest works with the CLI:

```bash
hf download gwd200/minimax-h3-weights diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_bf16.safetensors \
  --local-dir /path/to/ComfyUI/models
```

## Provenance

| File | Upstream repository | Revision |
|:--|:--|:--|
| diffusion model, video VAE, audio VAE | `Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3` | `e5eb578a89295337b8ff433a035929ce0279e0b6` |
| text/visual encoder | `sasoriiii/test-v2` | `c5f79b74854c10757f31b771a887c818f670d236` |

Use is governed by the upstream model terms and by any terms attached to the
original repositories; this repository only mirrors the files. The encoder
came from a gated upstream repository and is provided here for reproducibility
of an internal deployment, not as a new distribution with new rights.

## Deployment

This repo pairs with the private deployment record
`gwd200/minimax-h3-tests` (ComfyUI job scripts, workflows, UI, and run logs).
`infra/model_spec.json` there holds the same file list, sizes, and hashes.

Qwen-Image's text encoder, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, with its refusal direction projected out: a drop-in --llm for stable-diffusion.cpp next to our Turbo denoiser GGUFs. Below, exactly which part is uncensored and what that does to the pictures. The measurements are public.

  • As a chat model, the encoder's refusals fall from 88.9% to 1.2% on held-out English prompts. MMLU is unchanged: 77.35% before and after.
  • On images it changes nothing we could measure. The stock Qwen-Image pipeline has no filter and already draws all 9 sensitive categories we tested, and with this encoder not one of 45 prompts changed outcome. See where exactly this is uncensored.
  • Generate images locally in Atomic Chat. It runs stable-diffusion.cpp, the engine these files were built and checked with.
## Where exactly this is uncensored Qwen-Image 2.1 makes a picture with three parts. Only one of them is changed here. | Part | Does it refuse or filter? | In this repo | |---|---|---| | Safety checker | Qwen-Image ships none. The open weights have no content filter; moderation exists only in Qwen's hosted service. | nothing to remove | | **Text encoder**, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct | As a chat model, yes: it refused 88.9% of harmful English requests. Inside Qwen-Image it generates no text, so it cannot refuse. It draws what its training data taught it, and Qwen filtered NSFW images out of the pretraining data. | **unchanged** | The stock pipeline already blocks nothing. This release changes only how the encoder represents prompts it would refuse as a chat model. What the denoiser never learned to draw, no encoder can add. BFL's prompt upsampler for FLUX 3 Image Klein (a 9B Qwen3.5 fine-tune) with its refusal direction projected out, as GGUF for llama.cpp, plus the same edit as a LoRA for the stock files. Klein's text encoder without refusals is in FLUX-3-Image-Klein-TE-Uncensored-GGUF. The measurements are public.

  • Built by the team behind Atomic Chat, the app that runs open-weight models locally and offline.
  • As a chat model, refusals fall from 63% to 0% on held-out English prompts. MMLU goes from 74.15% to 73.95%.
  • As Klein's upsampler, under BFL's t2i system prompt, the stock model refuses none of our requests but softens 2 of 35 sensitive ones in its captions; this one keeps them. The image model draws neither of the two in any build, so on Klein's pictures we measured no uncensoring effect; the open pipeline already draws the sensitive categories (the per-category table).

# MiniMax-H3-FL2VA-FP8 (Optimized & Quantized)

This repository provides an optimized, pre-quantized **FP8** version of the **MiniMax-H3** Text-to-Video & Image-to-Video (`FL2VA` / `T2VA`) partition, structured natively for seamless high-performance serving with **vLLM-Omni** (`vllm serve --omni`). 

Tailored specifically to run efficiently on single-GPU enterprise setups (such as an NVIDIA A100 40GB), it leverages native FP8 weights and layer-wise offloading (`--enable-layerwise-offload`) to fit heavy multimodal requirements into strict VRAM budgets.

---

## 🔗 References & Credits
- **Original Model Base:** [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)
- **Architecture:** MiniMax-H3 Omni Multimodal Architecture (Dense 33B Diffusion Transformer with AdaLN caching, Qwen3-VL text/vision encoder backend, and Visual VAE components).

---

## ⚖️ License & Compliance Notice
- **License Agreement:** This model is a derivative work based on `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` and is governed by the **MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement**. 
- **Commercial Terms:** The community license permits royalty-free use provided your commercial products and services generate no more than $20 million in yearly revenue (refer to the official [License Document](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/LICENSE) for full details and territory compliance terms).
- **Attribution Requirement:** In compliance with Section IV of the license, any application, commercial product, or public service utilizing this work must prominently display **"MiniMax H3"** on its user interface.

---

## ⚠️ Requirements & Installation Note

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This model requires `vllm >= 0.32.0` and `vllm-omni >= 0.32.0`. 
> As of today, `vllm-omni` for this specific architecture may be in pre-release status and should be installed directly from source or via pre-release channels if not yet fully published on PyPI.

---

## 🚀 How to Serve with vLLM-Omni

You can serve this model directly using `vllm` with the multi-modal omni backend:

```bash
vllm serve "ParisNeo/MiniMax-H3-FL2VA-FP8" \
  --host "127.0.0.1" \
  --port "8002" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --init-timeout 1200 \
  --stage-init-timeout 1200 \
  --omni \
  --task-type fl2va \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --vae-use-slicing \
  --vae-use-tiling \
  --enable-layerwise-offload \
  --cache-backend cache_dit

```

---

## 📋 MiniMax-H3 Parameter Rules

When calling the vLLM-Omni endpoint for MiniMax-H3, ensure your request adheres to the model's strict validation constraints:

| Parameter | Required Value / Format | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fps` | `24` | **Fixed strictly at 24 FPS** by the MiniMax-H3 architecture. |
| `aspect_ratio` | `"16:9"`, `"9:16"`, `"1:1"`, `"4:3"`, `"21:9"` | **Mandatory** for text-to-video (`t2va`). |
| `duration` | `4.0` to `15.0` | Passed inside `extra_params` as decimal seconds (e.g. `15.0` = 360 frames at 24 FPS). |
| `task` | `"t2va"` or `"fl2va"` | Passed inside `extra_params`. Must match your target generation mode. |
| `input_reference` | `@file;type=image/png` | Field name for **single image** input (I2V mode). |
| `input_references` | Repeated `@file` fields | Field name for **multiple images** (First/Last frame interpolation). |
| `frame_indices` | `[0, -1]` | Array passed inside `extra_params` to explicitly anchor first and last frames. |

---

## 🔌 API Usage (Synchronous vs. Asynchronous Modes)

vLLM-Omni provides two distinct interaction models for generating videos:

### Mode 1: Synchronous API (`/v1/videos/sync`)

Best for short interactive scripts, testing, and benchmarks. It blocks execution until rendering completes and returns raw video bytes directly.

> **💡 Pro-Tip for Long Generations (up to 15s):**
> Rendering long videos (e.g., `duration: 15.0`) takes significant compute time. Always pass an extended socket timeout (e.g., `--max-time 900` in `curl`) to prevent socket drops from cancelling the request mid-render.

```bash
curl --max-time 900 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/videos/sync \
  -F "prompt=A cinematic tracking shot of a mountain lake at sunrise, highly detailed" \
  -F "aspect_ratio=16:9" \
  -F "fps=24" \
  -F "num_inference_steps=30" \
  -F 'extra_params={"task":"t2va","duration":15.0}' \
  -o t2v_output_15s.mp4

```

---

### Mode 2: Asynchronous Job Queue API (`/v1/videos`)

**Recommended for production workflows and long 15-second generation runs.** This decouples request submission from execution, avoiding HTTP timeout drops by handling processing in a background job queue.

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

# MiniMax-H3, AdaLN-pruned (Cloned from "multimodalart/MiniMax-H3-Pruned")

[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) in diffusers format with the AdaLN input
projections reduced to their reachable rank. **52 GB smaller** across the two DiT partitions, no visible change in
output, and every published H3 LoRA loads - pruned-trained ones natively, released-trained ones projected.

| | released | this repo |
|---|---|---|
| `transformer/` | 66.28 GB | **40.24 GB** |
| `transformer_ref/` | 66.28 GB | **40.24 GB** |
| DiT parameters, per partition | 33.14 B | 20.11 B |
| `text_encoder/` | 66.71 GB | **52.48 GB** |

The conditioner is hosted here too, truncated: MiniMax-H3 conditions on the *unnormalized* hidden state after the
Qwen3-VL conditioner's 50th decoder layer (`hidden_states[50]`), so decoder layers 51-63 and the language-model head
can never reach the conditioning and are dropped. `text_encoder/` ships decoder layers 0-50 - the 51st is kept so
`hidden_states[50]` stays a pre-norm intermediate rather than the final-norm output - and its embeddings are **bitwise
identical** to the released conditioner's, text-only and vision-bearing presentations alike. It stays bfloat16; a
quantized conditioner is planned as a separate variant, pending its own quality measurement.

Both VAEs, both schedulers, the tokenizer and the processor are *not* duplicated here. `modular_model_index.json`
points those at `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`, so loading this repo pulls only the pruned partitions, the truncated
conditioner, and the released components you already have.

## What was removed, and why it is safe

Each of the 50 blocks holds `adaln_proj.linear`, a `Linear(2688 -> 96768)`, and `norm_out.linear` adds one more.
Together that is **13.03 B parameters, 39.3% of the checkpoint**. All 51 of them read the same vector,
`silu(time_embedder(t))`, which is a function of the scalar timestep alone - so however wide it is, the set of
values it ever takes is a one-dimensional curve in `R^2688`.

An 8-dimensional affine subspace covers that curve to a relative RMS error of **1.45e-5**. One bfloat16 rounding step
of the weights those projections are stored in is about **3.9e-3** - roughly 250x larger. So the projections are
folded onto that subspace: `W @ x + b` with `x = mean + c @ basis` becomes `(W @ basis.T) @ c + (b + W @ mean)`, the
timestep MLP is replaced by a 1025-entry table of the coordinates `c(t)` (linearly interpolated), and every AdaLN
projection takes an 8-wide input instead of a 2688-wide one.

### Measured fidelity

Every folded projection, evaluated over 200 off-grid timesteps against an exact float64 evaluation of the released
weights. "Released" is the released checkpoint running its own bfloat16 arithmetic; "pruned" is this checkpoint
running its.

| | `transformer` | `transformer_ref` |
|---|---|---|
| rank-8 subspace residual (no storage rounding) | 1.51e-5 | 1.29e-5 |
| **pruned** vs exact float64, worst of 51 modules | **1.715e-3** | **1.715e-3** |
| **released** vs exact float64, worst of 51 modules | 1.751e-3 | 1.758e-3 |
| modules where pruned is closer to exact than released | **51 / 51** | **51 / 51** |
| pruned vs released, worst of 51 modules | 1.35e-3 | 1.41e-3 |

The approximation error is ~100x below the arithmetic the released checkpoint already runs at, which is why the
pruned model lands *closer* to the exact answer than the released one does, at every single projection.

handed to each VAE. A 10-step video diffusion trajectory amplifies *any* bfloat16-level perturbation, so the number
that matters is not the raw divergence but how it compares to a perturbation that is definitionally harmless. The
control is the **released** model against **itself**, run once with FlashAttention-3 and once with the native
backend: mathematically the same computation, differing only in the order bfloat16 sums are accumulated.

| video latents | cosine | relative L2 | max abs |

| released (native) vs pruned (FA3) | 0.99274 | 0.1205 | 7.71 |

# PBR maps LoRA for Qwen-Image-Edit-2511

Turns a lit photo of an object into one of its PBR maps, one instruction each:

* `Turn this photo into its albedo map: the base colour of every surface, with all lighting, shadows and reflections removed.`
* `Turn this photo into its roughness map: grayscale, black where the surface is glossy, white where it is rough.`
* `Turn this photo into its metallic map: white where the surface is bare metal, black everywhere else.`

Made for the PBR option of the projection-texturing Space: each generated view of a model is decomposed, and the
maps are projected and baked like the colour. Best with the Lightning 4-step LoRA
(`lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning`), at 768 px.

## Training

* Data: 2,820 synthetic views rendered in Blender Cycles: primitives, assemblies and 74 untextured meshes of
  everyday objects, with MatSynth materials (`gvecchio/MatSynth`, CC0 / CC-BY; metals three times as likely) and
  plain PBR materials (paint, plastic, ceramic, bare metal), under Poly Haven (CC0) and Blender studio HDRIs. For
  each view the exact base colour, roughness and metallic of every pixel are rendered with the same camera.
* v1 (`pbr/step-4230`): DiffSynth-Studio, rank 32, learning rate 1e-4, 2 epochs over 8,460 pairs (4x H200, 2 h).
* v2 (`pbr2/step-4215`, recommended): 2,800 more views in which a quarter of the materials are glossy paint, prints
  and lacquer that are never metal; 1 epoch over all 16,860 pairs. It stops reading glossy paint as metal.

## Benchmark

42 HDRI-lit views of 14 Khronos glTF sample assets (not in the training data) with exact ground truth:

| Method | albedo si-RMSE | roughness MAE | metallic MAE | metallic acc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| naive (photo, roughness 0.5, no metal) | 0.171 | 0.257 | 0.283 | 0.72 |
| Marigold-IID appearance v1-1 | 0.133 | 0.192 | 0.444 | 0.50 |
| RGB<->X | 0.143 | 0.247 | 0.442 | 0.56 |
| v1 + Lightning, 4 steps (DiffSynth) | **0.108** | **0.191** | **0.251** | **0.75** |
| v1 + Lightning, 4 steps (diffusers) | 0.114 | 0.196 | 0.268 | 0.72 |
| v2 + Lightning, 4 steps (diffusers) | **0.108** | 0.218 | 0.255 | 0.74 |

With diffusers, load the file's keys under `transformer.` without `.default` (DiffSynth saves PEFT keys of the
bare transformer): `{"transformer." + k.replace(".default", ""): v}`.

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the model files repackaged for [ComfyUI](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI): the distilled and base transformers in BF16, int8 and NVFP4, the text encoder in BF16 and int8, the prompt upsampler in BF16, int8 and w4a8, and the image autoencoder. The original model repositories are [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein), [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) and [FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, the `qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors` file in this repository, which the workflows run by default (see [Using with ComfyUI](#using-with-comfyui)), or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours).

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

# QwenImage2.1_Lora_BuildingExtraction_I2I_1.0

## Description

An experimental LoRA for Qwen-Image-2.1 that extracts and simplifies building footprints from satellite imagery, aiming to produce building shapes on a transparent background.

**Note:** This lora is trained by 1km*1km satellite images in 1024 resolution. To get the same output quality, you might need to use the same image input setup. 

## Visual Showcase

![Showcase1](images/Page1.png)
![Showcase2](images/Page2.png)

## Trigger Word

Use `BuildingExtraction` in your prompt to activate the intended usage.

## Intended Use

Designed for preliminary architectural site analysis, urban-context mapping, and simplified building-footprint visualization.

**Scope and limitations:**
- Building detection and boundaries may be inaccurate or incomplete.
- Non-building objects may be incorrectly detected, and some buildings may be missed.
- Transparency and spatial alignment are not guaranteed.
- Outputs require visual inspection and correction before GIS analysis. This model does not produce authoritative building data.

## ComfyUI Workflow

**Parameters Suggestion**
- cfg: 3.0
- steps: 40
- sampler: euler
- schduler: simple
- lora_strength: 1.00

**Workflow Template:**

测试发现：同一镜头包含打斗和台词时，必须先完整完成击打动作再说台词，否则容易退回底模的慢动作表现。

About This LoRA｜关于这个 LoRA
先说明一下：这不是一个魔法 LoRA，也不会自动帮你编排完整的武打动作。

如果你只写 two people fighting、a woman fights a man 之类非常简单的 Prompt，模型很可能只是让两个人高速乱挥拳，最后变成一段很快但没有逻辑的“王八拳”。

Prompt 负责决定“他们怎么打”，LoRA 负责增强“这些动作怎么表现”。

这个 Combat LoRA 前后训练和测试了好几个版本，也尝试过不同的数据比例、战斗速度、受击反应以及终结动作训练方向。

有些旧版本确实能让战斗明显变快，但高权重下也容易破坏 H3 本身不错的动作流畅度，让视频出现倍速感、模糊或者没有恢复过程的连续乱打。

目前发布的这一版，是我实际测试下来相对最平衡、也比较好用的一版。

它不再单纯追求“打得更快”，而是重点强化 连续战斗、命中反馈、身体失衡、后仰、踉跄、击倒、终结逻辑以及攻击产生的实际结果。

我的目标是尽量保留 H3 本身已经不错的动作连续性，同时让每一次有效攻击看起来更有重量、更有反馈，也更有“打中了以后真的发生了什么”的感觉。

Trigger Words｜触发词
prfight1 — 普通战斗
普通战斗只需要使用 prfight1。

prfight1, prfin1 — 终结 / 击倒
当这一段战斗需要一个明确的终结、KO、击倒或决定性收尾时，在 prfight1 后加入 prfin1。

prfight1, prfin1, prslow1 — 慢镜终结
需要在最后一击加入短暂的慢动作强调时，再加入 prslow1。

注意：只加入 prslow1 并不代表模型一定会自动产生慢动作。

你还需要在 Prompt 里明确告诉模型：最后一击在命中瞬间进入短暂慢动作，然后恢复正常速度。

最简单的高质量提示词写法
如果你不想自己手动写复杂的动作编排，一个非常简单的方法是直接使用 MiniMax H3 官方的两个 Prompt Writing Guide 文件。

把这两个官方提示词模板文件一起上传给 Gemini。

然后告诉 Gemini：按照这两个官方文件的规则，用六段式结构为 H3 编写视频提示词，并告诉它视频长度、剧情和你想要的战斗内容。

通常你只需要告诉 Gemini：几秒、什么剧情、谁打谁、最后想怎么结束，它就可以按照官方模板帮你扩展成一段完整得多的 H3 武打提示词。

这也是我目前比较推荐的使用方式：不要让模型自己猜怎么打，而是先让 Gemini 帮你完成动作编排，再把结果交给 H3 + Combat LoRA。


Compatibility｜兼容性说明
目前我只在 MiniMax H3 FL2VA 上完整测试过这个 LoRA。

其他 H3 模型、不同生成模式或其他工作流我暂时没有进行系统性测试。

所以在非 FL2VA 环境中能否获得相同的效果，我目前无法保证。

# matrixportalx/flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q4_0-GGUF
This model was converted to GGUF format from [`black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup) using llama.cpp via the ggml.ai's [GGUF-my-repo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ggml-org/gguf-my-repo) space.
Refer to the [original model card](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup) for more details on the model.

## Use with llama.cpp
Install llama.cpp through brew (works on Mac and Linux)

```bash
brew install llama.cpp

```
Invoke the llama.cpp server or the CLI.

### CLI:
```bash
llama-cli --hf-repo matrixportalx/flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q4_0-GGUF --hf-file flux-3-image-klein-pup-q4_0.gguf -p "The meaning to life and the universe is"
```

### Server:
```bash
llama-server --hf-repo matrixportalx/flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q4_0-GGUF --hf-file flux-3-image-klein-pup-q4_0.gguf -c 2048
```

Note: You can also use this checkpoint directly through the [usage steps](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp?tab=readme-ov-file#usage) listed in the Llama.cpp repo as well.

Step 1: Clone llama.cpp from GitHub.
```
git clone https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp
```

Step 2: Move into the llama.cpp folder and build it with `LLAMA_CURL=1` flag along with other hardware-specific flags (for ex: LLAMA_CUDA=1 for Nvidia GPUs on Linux).
```
cd llama.cpp && LLAMA_CURL=1 make
```

Step 3: Run inference through the main binary.
```
./llama-cli --hf-repo matrixportalx/flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q4_0-GGUF --hf-file flux-3-image-klein-pup-q4_0.gguf -p "The meaning to life and the universe is"
```
or
```
./llama-server --hf-repo matrixportalx/flux-3-image-klein-pup-Q4_0-GGUF --hf-file flux-3-image-klein-pup-q4_0.gguf -c 2048
```

**NSFW Wan 14B T2V** is a massive, 14 billion parameter text-to-video generation model, specifically fine-tuned for generating Not Safe For Work (NSFW) content. This model was created using a unified training methodology to build a solid understanding across the entire NSFW spectrum and generate videos with coherent motion natively.

The primary goal of this model is to provide a research and creative tool capable of generating thematically relevant short video clips based on text prompts within the adult content domain. It aims to understand and render a wide array of NSFW scenarios, aesthetics, and actions described in natural language with high fidelity and temporal consistency.

## Model Details
*   **Architecture:** Text-to-Video Transformer Architecture
*   **Parameters:** 14 Billion
*   **Type:** Text-to-Video (T2V)
*   **Specialization:** NSFW Content Generation
---

## Training Methodology
Unlike previous multi-phase approaches, the 14B model was trained using a single, unified configuration from the ground up to ensure maximum quality and stability from the very first epoch.

*   **Mixed Dataset:** The model was trained on a mixed dataset of **30k video clips and 20k still images simultaneously**. This method provides constant spatial regularization, preventing the anatomical drift and quality collapse that can occur in phased training. The model learns aesthetics and motion in parallel.
*   **Stable Configuration:** The entire 15-epoch run used a stable learning rate with an initial warmup, batch sizes optimized for the 14B architecture, and a training schedule designed for steady, progressive learning.
*   **Training Specifications:** The training was conducted on 17-frame video clips at a resolution of 480p.
*   **Outcome:** The result is a series of 15 high-quality, coherent checkpoints. The model demonstrates vastly improved spatial quality, stable motion, and reliable NSFW fidelity without the legacy artifacts associated with older training methods.

**We strongly recommend using `wan_14B_e15.safetensors` for all general use cases and LoRA training.** This final checkpoint represents the most refined state of the model.

## Training Data

The model was trained on a dataset comprising the top 1,000 posts from approximately 1,250 distinct NSFW subreddits. This dataset was carefully curated to capture a broad spectrum of adult themes, visual styles, character archetypes, specific kinks, and actions prevalent in these online communities. The video portion of the dataset was sourced from similar communities.

The captions associated with the training data leveraged the language and tagging conventions found within these subreddents. For insights into effective prompting strategies for specific styles or content, please refer to the `prompting-guide.json` file included in this repository.

**Note:** Due to the nature of the source material, the training dataset inherently contains explicit adult content.

## Files Included

*   `wan_14B_e1.safetensors`
*   ... (and all intermediate epochs)
*   `wan_14B_e15.safetensors`
*   `prompting-guide.json`: This crucial JSON file contains an analysis of common keywords, phrases, and descriptive language associated with the content from various source subreddits. It is designed to help users craft more effective prompts.

## How to Use

This model is intended for generating short video clips (typically a few seconds) from descriptive text prompts.

1.  **Select a Checkpoint:** **We recommend using the final `wan_14B_e15.safetensors` checkpoint** for the best balance of training and quality.
2.  **No Helper LoRA Needed:** The model generates motion natively. You do not need to use any external motion LoRAs.
3.  **Craft Your Prompt:** Utilize natural language to describe the desired scene, subjects, actions, and style.
4.  **Consult `prompting-guide.json`:** For best results, especially when targeting specific sub-community styles or niche fetishes, refer to the `prompting-guide.json`. This guide will provide insights into the terminology and phrasing most likely to elicit the desired output.
5.  **Generate:** Use your preferred inference pipeline compatible with this model architecture.

# Qwen-Image Sharp VAE [Anima / Krea-2]

## TL;DR

**EN**

- A sharper, clearer drop-in replacement for the Qwen-Image VAE: crisper lines, eyes and hair, with no overexposure.
- **3 strengths** (pick from the download dropdown): **x0.5** (subtle) / **Default** (x1.0) / **x1.5** (strongest).

---

**Crisper lines, eyelashes and hair strands, just by swapping the VAE. The difference is biggest with hires fix.**

A drop-in replacement for `qwen_image_vae` for **Anima** and **Krea-2**. No trigger words, no extra nodes, no retraining. Same colors, same exposure, sharper details.

![Backlit beach: Original vs Qwen-Image Sharp](images/hero_04_backlight.png)
![Portrait: Original vs Qwen-Image Sharp](images/hero_02_portrait.png)
![Summer festival: Original vs Qwen-Image Sharp](images/hero_06_multi.png)

Same prompt, same seed, same settings. Only the VAE is different.

| Scene | Original: sharpness / clipped | **Qwen-Image Sharp**: sharpness / clipped | Sharpness gain |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Angel ¹ | 6.48 / 3.04% | **11.26 / 1.60%** | +74% |
| Miku | 6.87 / 4.31% | **11.21 / 1.82%** | +63% |
| Portrait | 3.89 / 19.89% | **7.65 / 17.49%** | +97% |
| Lineart classroom | 6.21 / 15.75% | **9.01 / 14.33%** | +45% |
| Backlit beach | 2.45 / 8.70% | **3.67 / 8.26%** | +50% |
| Castle scenery | 3.81 / 1.80% | **5.78 / 0.05%** | +52% |
| Summer festival | 8.72 / 0.94% | **14.08 / 0.70%** | +61% |

Every scene gets sharper, and every scene also has **fewer** blown-out highlights than the original.

- *Sharpness* = mean luminance gradient (higher = crisper edges).
- *Clipped* = share of pixels with any channel ≥ 254.
- Settings: SilvermoonMix-Anima29B-Evolved-V2.3, Forge Neo, Euler a, Simple, 28 steps, CFG 3, Shift 3, 832×1216. Hires fix: 1.5×, `4x-AnimeSharp`, denoise 0.15, 8 hires steps, hires CFG 3, hires Shift 3.
- ¹ Angel: same settings, but 14 hires steps and ADetailer (face_yolov8n, denoise 0.15).
![Angel](images/hero_01_angel.png)
![Castle scenery](images/hero_05_scenery.png)

## Why the VAE matters so much in hires fix

In hires fix, the VAE is not only used at the very end. It also sits in the middle of the pipeline:

1. The first pass produces a small latent.
2. **The VAE decodes it into an image.** ← Qwen-Image Sharp gives a crisper image here.
3. The upscaler (e.g. `4x-AnimeSharp`) enlarges that image. Clean edges in, clean edges out.
4. The enlarged image is encoded back into a latent and the model resamples it at the chosen denoise strength.
5. The VAE decodes the final image.

So the VAE decides what the second pass starts from. With a low denoise strength, the second pass mostly keeps that starting image, and the extra detail from step 2 carries all the way to the final result. That is why only swapping the VAE makes such a large difference in hires fix.

## Effect of denoise strength

Same seven scenes, hires fix with denoise 0.15 / 0.30 / 0.45 (everything else unchanged):

| Scene | 0.15 | 0.30 | 0.45 |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Angel ¹ | +74% | +63% | +53% |
| Miku | +63% | +56% | +46% |
| Portrait | +97% | +88% | +78% |
| Lineart classroom | +45% | +39% | +36% |
| Backlit beach | +50% | +40% | +31% |
| Castle scenery | +52% | +37% | +26% |
| Summer festival | +61% | +53% | +42% |

*(Sharpness gain of Qwen-Image Sharp over the original VAE at the same denoise.)*

![Denoise sweep: Angel](images/denoise_01_angel.png)
![Denoise sweep: castle scenery](images/denoise_05_scenery.png)

- **Lower denoise keeps more of what the VAE decoded**, so the gain is largest at 0.15.
- **Higher denoise lets the model redraw more**, so the gap narrows, but it is still +26% to +78% at 0.45.
- Qwen-Image Sharp had fewer clipped highlights than the original in all 21 scene/denoise combinations.

## Not your taste? Try x0.5 or x1.5

If the default feels too sharp or not sharp enough, two more strengths are included:

# MCNL v1 — Multi Concept NSFW LoRA for Qwen Image Edit

A LoRA adapter for the [Qwen-Image-Edit-2511](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511) diffusion pipeline, enabling NSFW content generation and editing capabilities.

## Model Details

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Base Model** | Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 |
| **Architecture** | QwenImageTransformer2DModel (MMDiT) LoRA |
| **File Size** | ~563 MB |
| **Format** | safetensors |
| **License** | OpenRAIL++ |

## Usage

### With the ScottzillaSystems Image Editor Space

The easiest way to use this LoRA is through the [ScottzillaSystems Image Editor](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ScottzillaSystems/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-LoRAs-Fast) — select "🔥 MCNL-NSFW-v1" from the adapter dropdown.

### Programmatic Usage

```python
from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline
import torch

pipe = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).to("cuda")

# Load this LoRA
pipe.load_lora_weights(
    "ScottzillaSystems/qwen-image-edit-plus-nsfw-lora",
    weight_name="qwen-image-edit-plus-nsfw-lora.safetensors",
    adapter_name="mcnl-nsfw-v1"
)
pipe.set_adapters(["mcnl-nsfw-v1"])

# Edit an image
from PIL import Image
image = Image.open("input.jpg").convert("RGB")
result = pipe(
    image=image,
    prompt="nsfw",
    num_inference_steps=40,
    true_cfg_scale=4.0,
    negative_prompt=" ",
).images[0]
result.save("output.jpg")
```

## Trigger Words

Use these concepts in your prompts to activate specific capabilities:

`nsfw` `nipples` `vagina` `penis` `missionary` `cowgirlout` `reversecowgirlpov` `blowjob` `cum_on_face` `creamp1e` `l1ck`

# MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA — few-step audio-video generation

A LoRA for [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3) that renders
joint **video + synchronized stereo audio** in as few as **4 sampling steps**
instead of the usual ~20 — a ~5× sampling speedup — and keeps getting better as
you add steps.

## Which checkpoint — `v4` (step 600) or `v1` (850)?

For **most** work, use **`minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors`**. It's the
strongest checkpoint we've released: much better static and small-motion shots,
markedly better micro-detail (faces, fingers, fine texture), and the
over-sharpening / plastic look of the earlier `v1` (~850) line is **fully
resolved**.

v4 introduced a **static-frame enhancement** — a big win for static and
small-motion content. The one trade-off shows up **only at 4 steps with large,
fast motion**, where v4 can produce **motion-smear / trailing ghosting** (we're
actively fixing this). Two things address it:

- **Use 6–8 steps.** This **largely removes the smear** and is where v4 looks its
  best. v4 also tolerates higher step counts better than v1, which tends to
  over-sharpen at high steps + strength 1.0.
- For the specific case of **4 steps *and* heavy motion**, the older **`v1` ~850**
  checkpoint can still be the friendlier pick.

```
Using 6–8 steps?        ── yes ──►  v4-600  (recommended)
   │ no (4 steps)
   ▼
Heavy / fast motion?    ── no  ──►  v4-600  (recommended)
   │ yes
   ▼
                                    v1-850  (friendlier at 4-step heavy motion)
```

Still a preview — training continues; the two areas still being improved are
**audio** and **behaviour under fast, intense motion**.

## Steps and strength — read this

- **4 steps is the recommended *minimum*; 4–8 is the useful range.** 6–8 steps
  look noticeably better than 4, so add steps if you can afford them. Past **8
  steps** it stops helping and can start to introduce **over-sharp artifacts** —
  there's no benefit to going higher, so stay in **4–8**.
- **Keep strength at `1.0`.** It's tuned for 1.0 and holds up well across the 4–8
  step range. Only reach for the strength dial if a *specific* clip misbehaves —
  then **blurry ghosting / smear → nudge up** (`~1.05–1.2`), **over-sharp grain →
  nudge down** (`~0.8–0.95`).
- Keep the scheduler on `simple`.

## Use it in ComfyUI (recommended)

Custom nodes: **[Larryvrh/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo](https://github.com/Larryvrh/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo)**
— or search **"MiniMax-H3 Turbo"** in ComfyUI-Manager. (Keep the node updated; it
evolves alongside these weights.)

1. Install the nodes (Manager, or `git clone` into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes`) and put
   a `.safetensors` from this repo into `ComfyUI/models/loras/`. You also need the
   base MiniMax-H3 model, VAEs and text encoder — see the
   [MiniMax-H3 tutorial](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3).
2. Start from the official MiniMax-H3 workflow (t2v or i2v) and make two changes:
   - insert **MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA** between the model loader and the sampler;
   - feed `SamplerCustomAdvanced` from **MiniMax-H3 Turbo Sampler**, and set the
     scheduler to `simple` at **≥ 4 steps**.

Everything else stays as in the official graph, so both text-to-video and
image-to-video work. A ready-made t2v workflow ships in the
[node repo](https://github.com/Larryvrh/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-Turbo/tree/main/example_workflows)
(and here as `minimax_h3_t2v_turbo.json`) — drag it in.

- **Base model**: any MiniMax-H3 base — full (`bf16`, `int8_convrot`) **and the
  pruned/curve variants** (`pruned_int8`, `pruned_fp8`). The node auto-detects a
  pruned base and re-injects the time-conditioning at run time, so **one LoRA file
  covers every base**.
- **`low_vram`** switch: **off** applies the LoRA at run time (sharpest,
  recommended); **on** merges it into the weights for the lowest peak VRAM (a bit
  softer on quantized bases). Turn it on only if you run out of memory.
- The custom sampler **auto-adapts to your ComfyUI version**: MiniMax-H3 runs
  video and audio on two different flow schedules; recent ComfyUI handles that
  natively (`ModelSamplingAV`) and older ComfyUI doesn't — the Turbo Sampler
  detects which and does the right thing either way, so nothing to change when you
  update ComfyUI.

## Weights

All bf16, ~744 MB, applied as a plain low-rank update
(`W_eff = W + lora_B @ lora_A`, alpha = rank, so no extra scaling). **Prefer the
EMA files**; the non-EMA ones are for comparison.

| file | notes |
|---|---|
| **`minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors`** | **recommended — current best.** Strong static/small-motion, good micro-detail, no over-sharpening. |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600.safetensors` | v4-600 non-EMA (comparison). |
| `minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step150_ema.safetensors` | earlier v4 checkp

# Veda-MiniMax-H3 R2VA (Preview) [Demo](https://veda.hanxiao.run/) · [Project Page](https://veda-sparse.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/veda-sparse/Miowtion/tree/main) · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30325) · [Deployment Guide](AGENTS.md) ## Introduction **Veda** is a learned sparse-attention method for video diffusion models. This checkpoint brings Veda to [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) reference-to-audio-video generation. It selects visual reference and generated video tiles independently; text, VLM conditioning, and audio attention remain dense. The predictor is not a LoRA and leaves the backbone weights unchanged. This preview was fine-tuned for 600 updates from the T2VA predictor on 5.17-second R2VA clips. It uses the MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA for eight-step generation, with up to 32 visual-reference tiles and 32 current-video tiles per query tile and head. The predictor is stored in FP8 and dequantized to BF16 when loaded. ### Highlights - **Learned sparse attention.** Visual reference and generated-video attention are selected independently; text, VLM conditioning, and audio stay dense. - **Fixed visual budgets.** The released preview uses 32 reference tiles and 32 current-video tiles per query tile and head. - **Plug-and-play predictor.** The FP8 predictor is separate from the H3 backbone and Turbo LoRA weights. ## Samples The examples below use the same seed, prompt, geometry, and Turbo LoRA for Dense and Veda. Each generated output is 1344×768, 124 frames, and about 5.17 seconds. Dense (left) and Veda (right) are stitched into one synchronized comparison video, with attention and denoising speedups in its top title bar. Each comparison uses the original Dense audio track.
