# UltraTex Qwen-Image 2.1 port

This is a port of [UltraTex](https://github.com/yiboz2001/UltraTex) (MIT, Yibo Zhang) to the Qwen-Image 2.1 backbone, trained by Atlas 3D ([orwelian84](https://huggingface.co/orwelian84)). The released UltraTex weights only cover FLUX.1-dev and FLUX.2-Klein, so this is, to our knowledge, the first Qwen-Image multi-view texture LoRA.

Code: [github.com/Atlas3DSS/UltraTex](https://github.com/Atlas3DSS/UltraTex) (fork of upstream with the Qwen-Image 2.1 and Krea 2 backbones on the default branch). The `code/` folder here is a snapshot of the same files.

The method is UltraTex's. This release is the backbone port (`code/`) plus the trained weights (`qwen21/`) and samples.

## Files

| Path | Size | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen21/lora/dit_lora.safetensors` | 608 MiB | Multi-view texture LoRA, checkpoint-15000 |
| `qwen21/lora/train_args.json` | 1.5 KiB | Training arguments for the LoRA |
| `qwen21/decoder_step1200.safetensors` | 988 MiB | Foreground-aware RGBA decoder, step 1200 |
| `qwen21/decoder_train_log.jsonl` | 89 KiB | Decoder training log |
| `qwen21/text_cond.safetensors` | 64 KiB | Cached empty-prompt text conditioning |
| `qwen21/text_cond.json` | 122 B | Metadata for the text conditioning cache |
| `code/` | ~0.2 MiB | Qwen-Image 2.1 backbone and pipeline changes, scripts, tools, tests (apply on top of upstream UltraTex) |
| `code/README.md` | 15 KiB | UltraTex README as of this port |
| `samples/eval_grid_ckpt15000.webp` | 495 KiB | Evaluation grid, checkpoint-15000 |
| `samples/albedo_canvas_ckpt15000.webp` | 651 KiB | Albedo canvas output, checkpoint-15000 |
| `samples/fox_flux2_left_vs_qwen21_right.glb` | 21 MiB | Fox comparison: stock FLUX.2-Klein UltraTex (left) vs this LoRA (right) |
| `samples/qwen21_ckpt15000_side_by_side.glb` | 101 MiB | Side-by-side GLB, this LoRA at checkpoint-15000 |
| `samples/fox_adventurer_v2_skinned.glb` | 12 MiB | Skinned sample mesh |
| `samples/axolotl_suit_skinned.glb` | 14 MiB | Skinned sample mesh |
| `samples/robot_companion_skinned.glb` | 12 MiB | Skinned sample mesh |

## Training

- LoRA rank 64, alpha 64
- 15,000 steps, 1024 px per view, batch 1
- lr 5e-5, constant; bf16; seed 42
- Sparse attention top-k 0.2
- Trained on G-buffer TexVerse ([YiboZhang2001/G-buffer-TexVerse](https://huggingface.co/datasets/YiboZhang2001/G-buffer-TexVerse), gated)
- Foreground-aware RGBA decoder fine-tuned for 1,200 steps; foreground PSNR 38.65 dB
- Text conditioning is the cached empty prompt from Qwen3-VL-8B

## Usage

1. Clone [Atlas3DSS/UltraTex](https://github.com/Atlas3DSS/UltraTex) (or apply `code/` on top of upstream [UltraTex](https://github.com/yiboz2001/UltraTex)).
2. Put `qwen21/` at `checkpoints/qwen21/`.
3. Set the paths in `scripts/mv_env.sh` to a ComfyUI checkout with Qwen-Image 2.1 support.
4. Run multi-view inference:

```bash
BACKBONE=qwen21 LORA=checkpoints/qwen21/lora DECODER_CKPT=checkpoints/qwen21/decoder_step1200.safetensors bash scripts/inference_mv.sh
```

Or run one mesh end to end:

```bash
BACKEND=qwen21 bash scripts/skin_mesh.sh MESH.glb REF.png OUT_DIR
```

Base weights are not included: Qwen-Image 2.1 (bf16), its VAE, and Qwen3-VL-8B must be obtained separately.

## Samples

![Evaluation grid, checkpoint-15000](samples/eval_grid_ckpt15000.webp)

The GLBs are TRELLIS meshes generated from Krea 2 concept art, textured with this LoRA. The fox comparison GLB has stock FLUX.2-Klein UltraTex on the left and this LoRA on the right.

## Credits

Method: UltraTex, by Yibo Zhang and contributors (MIT), [github.com/yiboz2001/UltraTex](https://github.com/yiboz2001/UltraTex). Qwen-Image 2.1 port, training, and weights: Atlas 3D.

It supports unified understanding of multimodal contexts composed of text, images, video, and audio, and can generate video with native stereo audio at resolutions up to 2K and durations of up to 15 seconds. Thanks to its task-generalization-oriented system design, H3 already possesses broad multimodal context understanding and generation capabilities at the pre-training stage, enabling outstanding performance in following complex multimodal instructions. H3 supports the following input and output specifications: | Category | Specification | |---|---| | Output duration | 4–15 seconds | | Output aspect ratio | Supports a wide range of aspect ratios, including but not limited to 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, and 9:16 | | Output resolution | Supports various resolution dimensions. The shorter side is set to 768 pixels by default. 2K \| generation can be achieved with H3-Regenerate-2K | | Output frame rate | 24 FPS | | Output audio | 32 kHz stereo | | Supported dialogue languages | Stable support for 11 languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish. Additional languages are also supported to varying degrees | ### Model Variants and Input Specifications | Model Variant | Input Mode | Specifications | |---|---|---| | H3-Base-FL2VA | First-and-last-frame mode | Supports zero, one, or two input images.

- No image input: Text-to-video mode
- One image input: First-frame-to-video or last-frame-to-video generation
- Two image inputs: First-and-last-frame-to-video generation | | H3-Base-Ref2VA | Omni-reference mode | Supports multi-modal reference inputs:

- **Images:** ≤ 9 images
- **Videos:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds
- **Audio:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds

### Example usage

#### SGLang (✅ verified)

Install the FLUX configuration plugin included in `tiny-random/flux-3-image-klein-comfy`. It reads text/VAE dimensions through official diffusion hooks; the installed SGLang files are unchanged. CUDA Graph warmup covers 64×64 text-to-image; reference-image signatures use SDPA outside captured graphs.

```bash
hf download tiny-random/flux-3-image-klein-comfy --local-dir ./flux-3-image-klein-comfy
python -m pip install --no-deps ./flux-3-image-klein-comfy/runtime
```

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path tiny-random/flux-3-image-klein-comfy \
  --model-type diffusion \
  --num-gpus 4 \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --ulysses-degree 1 \
  --ring-degree 1 \
  --attention-backend torch_sdpa \
  --enable-breakable-cuda-graph \
  --warmup-resolutions 64x64
```

#### Diffusers (✅ verified)

Use Diffusers from commit aaf57d03a3edfbd9de457d2872417a92f149a91d or a release containing FLUX 3. The repo includes the native Diffusers component layout for standard pretrained loading.

```python
def run_diffusers(model_id: str):
    import torch
    from PIL import Image
    from diffusers import ModularPipeline

    pipe = ModularPipeline.from_pretrained(model_id)
    pipe.load_components(
        pretrained_model_name_or_path=model_id, dtype={"default": torch.bfloat16, "vae": torch.float32}
    )
    pipe.to("cuda")
    image = pipe(
        prompt="Combine these scenes into a red and green illustration.",
        image=[Image.new("RGB", (64, 64), "blue"), Image.new("RGB", (64, 64), "green")],
        height=64,
        width=64,
        num_inference_steps=2,
        max_new_tokens=10,
        text_encoder_out_layers=tuple(range(1, 9)),
        generator=torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(42),
        output="images",
    )[0]
    image.save("flux3-output.png")
    print(pipe.transformer)
    print(image.size)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_diffusers(model_id="tiny-random/flux-3-image-klein-comfy")
```

Rank-reduced (`fro90_ceil256`) distillation LoRA for few-step ("turbo") sampling. Same key format as
the source, drop-in wherever the original loads; the trade against the full 8.9 GB rank-450
file is file size, not compatibility.

|---|---|
| Source | `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-lora-450-bf16.safetensors` (via `ibyteohdear/Lightricks-LTX-2`) |

| Median kept Frobenius energy | 0.900 |
| 5th percentile / worst | 0.815 / 0.767 |
| Global kept energy / error | 0.870 / 0.361 |
| File size | 4.01 GB |

Per module the delta `B @ A` is truncated by factored SVD (QR of both factors + core SVD
— the optimal rank-k approximation), singular values kept until **90%
Frobenius energy**, capped at **rank 256**, with a small condition safeguard. Same key
format as the source, drop-in wherever the original loads. Typical usage: weight ~0.8 with
the official 8-step sigma schedule.

# MiniMax-H3 PTD adapters for ComfyUI (shrunk)

EPFL VITA Lab's **PTD** few-step adapters for MiniMax-H3
([epfl-vita/PTD-weights](https://huggingface.co/epfl-vita/PTD-weights)), converted from the released
DCP training checkpoints to ComfyUI safetensors and made 2–4.5× smaller. The per-hop adapters are the
only thing PTD adds to the base model, so these files are all you need besides the
original MiniMax-H3 transformer, text encoder and VAEs.

It also has int8 versions of taobao-content-ai's **Ref2VA** PTD adapters
([taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-LoRAs](https://huggingface.co/taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-LoRAs),
4 and 8 steps, reference images → video + audio), and of their 8- and 6-step **RefAsymOPD** sibling
([taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-RefAsymOPD-LoRAs](https://huggingface.co/taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-RefAsymOPD-LoRAs),
same format, trained for better backgrounds and sharpness), at half the size of their bf16 releases.

Put the files in `ComfyUI/models/ptd/`.

| File | Size | vs. original | Adapter error (max / mean) | Loader |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `ptd/ptd_h3_4step_bf16.safetensors` | 5.55 GB | 48% | 0.23% / 0.19%, identical at runtime¹ | official **or** compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_4step_int8.safetensors` | 2.83 GB | 25% | 1.13% / 0.85% | compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_4step_int8_r5.safetensors` | 2.52 GB | 22% | 5.17% / 4.88% | compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_6step_bf16.safetensors` | 8.32 GB | 48% | 0.23% / 0.19%, identical at runtime¹ | official **or** compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_6step_int8.safetensors` | 4.25 GB | 25% | 1.10% / 0.87% | compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_6step_int8_r5.safetensors` | 3.89 GB | 23% | 5.17% / 4.83% | compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_ref2va_4step_int8.safetensors` | 2.86 GB | 51%² | 0.93% / 0.44% | compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_ref2va_8step_int8.safetensors` | 5.68 GB | 51%² | 1.18% / 0.47% | compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_ref2va_refasymopd_8step_int8.safetensors` | 5.68 GB | 51%² | 0.90% / 0.52% | compact |
| `ptd/ptd_h3_ref2va_refasymopd_6step_int8.safetensors` | 4.24 GB | 51%² | 0.86% / 0.47% | compact³ |

Originals: 11.5 GB (4-step), 17.2 GB (6-step), float32. Adapter error is the relative Frobenius error
`‖ΔW' − ΔW‖ / ‖ΔW‖` of every per-hop delta `ΔW = B·A` against the original float32 checkpoint,
measured on all 1248 (4-step) / 1872 (6-step) adapters after loading each file the way ComfyUI does.
The dense output-head adapters and the reference head buffers are kept float32 and exact in every file.

¹ The official ComfyUI hook casts each block's factors to the block's compute dtype (bf16) before use,
so bf16 storage rounds them earlier but gives the same numbers.

² Of taobao-content-ai's bf16 files (5.58 GB / 11.11 GB); error measured the same way against them, over
1248 / 2496 / 1872 adapters (4 / 8 / 6 steps; the RefAsymOPD 8-step file is 11.11 GB, the 6-step 8.31 GB).
Their PDD output-head banks are kept unchanged.

³ The RefAsymOPD 6-step file was first released with `pdd_num_steps: 32, pdd_block_size: 4`, the 8-step
file's values, though it holds a 6-row head bank (one head per hop), so no loader accepted it. We reported it
([discussion #3](https://huggingface.co/taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-RefAsymOPD-LoRAs/discussions/3)) and
taobao-content-ai corrected it to `pdd_num_steps: 6, pdd_block_size: 1` in commit `d1f88c8`; the tensors are
unchanged. This file carries the same corrected values, so it matches their current release. The 6-step has
not yet been render-compared against taobao's node the way the 4- and 8-step Ref2VA files were.

**Which one?** `int8` is the recommended default. It's a quarter of the original size, needs a quarter
of the host RAM, and its error sits far below the margins discussed below. `int8_r5` saves a further 11%
for about 5× the error. `bf16` is the one the unmodified official nodes can load. For Ref2VA, use
`ptd_h3_ref2va_4step_int8`, or an 8-step file for sharper detail at twice the steps;
`ptd_h3_ref2va_refasymopd_8step_int8` is taobao's improved 8-step at the same cost, and
`ptd_h3_ref2va_refasymopd_6step_int8` its faster 6-step.

## Install

1. Clone the official PTD pack into `custom_nodes`:

   ```sh
   cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
   git clone --branch release/comfyui-inference --single-branch https://github.com/vita-epfl/PTD-inference ComfyUI-PTD
   ```

2. Clone the compact loader next to it:

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/Nynxz/ComfyUI-PTD-Compact
   ```

3. Put the adapter files in `ComfyUI/models/ptd/`.

At inference each checkpoint is **structurally identical to a [plain PTD LoRA](https://huggingface.co/taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-LoRAs)**: one independent low-rank adapter per inference step, applied on top of the per-interval output heads introduced by Parallel Decoding Distillation (PDD). BFL's prompt upsampler for FLUX 3 Image Klein (a 9B Qwen3.5 fine-tune) with its refusal direction projected out, as GGUF for llama.cpp, plus the same edit as a LoRA for the stock files. Klein's text encoder without refusals is in FLUX-3-Image-Klein-TE-Uncensored-GGUF. The measurements are public.

  • As a chat model, refusals fall from 63% to 0% in English and from 29% to 1% in Russian on held-out prompts. MMLU goes from 74.15% to 73.95%.
  • As Klein's upsampler, under BFL's t2i system prompt, the stock model refuses none of our requests but softens 2 of 35 sensitive ones in its captions; this one keeps them. The image model draws neither of the two in any build, so on Klein's pictures we measured no uncensoring effect; the open pipeline already draws the sensitive categories (the per-category table).
  • Against the other uncensored upsamplers on our stand, prithiv's measures the same as this one, and Sakura's still refuses 22% in English.

# LightX2V × MicroDuck — FastWAM navigation inference bundle

Deployment files for [fuheaven/LightX2V-microduck](https://github.com/fuheaven/LightX2V-microduck), including the trained MicroDuck navigation checkpoint and its minimal Wan inference dependencies.

**This release contains simulation development weights. It has not passed independent full capability acceptance or real-hardware validation.** It is a task-specific high-level controller, not a general-purpose autonomous robot brain.

本仓库提供 MicroDuck 视觉寻球模型的完整推理文件。使用代码仓库的 Docker 环境即可运行推理测速、MuJoCo 仿真与独立 MicroDuck Studio 页面；无需先训练 TinyVLA、安装 ROS2 或取得作者私有权重。

## Included model and behavior

- Model: `clear-room-realtime-control-pilot-v1 / step 250`.
- Model SHA256: `8ea7793290f0a22bff56ec4e44168232564ec5d57a9e21515a8a8c4a989114ea`.
- Inputs: head-camera RGB history, a supported target instruction, and 48-dimensional robot state.
- History: control-tick offsets `[300, 150, 50, 0]`, composed into a 512 × 512 image.
- Output: `32 × 5` high-level action chunk: forward velocity, lateral velocity, turning, head yaw, and standing.
- Supported instructions/tasks: `find_red_ball`, `find_blue_ball`, `find_yellow_ball`.
- The official ONNX locomotion policy executes walking/balancing at 50 Hz; this FastWAM checkpoint does not directly generate joint angles.
- Tested deployment family: a single NVIDIA H200, BF16, 20 flow-sampling steps. Consumer-GPU compatibility is not established by the on-disk size.

## Files

The ten required model files total **26,244,309,246 bytes (26.24 GB / 24.44 GiB)**. Downloading the `models/` directory directly into your deployment data directory preserves the expected paths.

```text
models/
  microduck/
    model.pt                          # 12.04 GB; complete trained task weights
    dataset_stats.json                # original training-set normalization
    navigation_checkpoint.json        # exact checkpoint/history/statistics binding
  Wan2.2-TI2V-5B/
    config.json
    models_t5_umt5-xxl-enc-bf16.pth     # 11.36 GB
    Wan2.2_VAE.pth                     # 2.82 GB
    google/umt5-xxl/
      special_tokens_map.json
      spiece.model
      tokenizer.json
      tokenizer_config.json
```

`model-files.lock.json` and `SHA256SUMS` specify byte counts and hashes. The checkpoint receipt retains its original training provenance paths; the deployment code resolves model files from your local data directory and does not require access to those original server paths.

Training data, optimizer/DeepSpeed states, unused Wan diffusion shards, TinyVLA checkpoints, and later experimental navigation candidates are not included or required for this inference release.

## Download and deploy

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fuheaven/LightX2V-microduck.git
cd LightX2V-microduck
docker build -f deploy/microduck/fastwam/Dockerfile \
  -t lightx2v-microduck:fastwam-v1 .
export FASTWAM_DATA=/absolute/path/to/microduck-data

# Download the inference bundle; no GPU required.
GPU_ID=none deploy/microduck/fastwam/run.sh python -c \
  'from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download; snapshot_download("lightx2v/microduck", local_dir="/data", allow_patterns=["models/**", "model-files.lock.json", "SHA256SUMS", "NOTICE.md", "licenses/**"])'

# Fetch the pinned official robot and ONNX policies from their original sources.
GPU_ID=none deploy/microduck/fastwam/run.sh \
  python scripts/microduck/fastwam_handoff.py fetch --component sim

# Verify the exact checkpoint, normalizer, receipt, and backbone hashes.
GPU_ID=none deploy/microduck/fastwam/run.sh \
  python scripts/microduck/fastwam_handoff.py verify

# Select an available GPU and start the independent visualization service.
export GPU_ID=0
WEB_BIND=0.0.0.0 WEB_PORT=8770 deploy/microduck/fastwam/web.sh
```

Open `http://YOUR_SERVER_IP:8770/`. The gallery includes recorded successes and failures; live simulation loads the model on request. The code repository pins releases for repeatable downloads. If manually using `snapshot_download`, record and reuse the full Hugging Face commit with `revision="FULL_COMMIT_SHA"`.

See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/fuheaven/LightX2V-microduck/blob/main/docs/microduck/deployment.md), [visualization guide](https://github.com/fuheaven/LightX2V-microduck/blob/main/docs/microduck/visualization.md), and [optimization guide](https://github.com/fuheaven/LightX2V-microduck/blob/main/docs/microduck/optimization.md).

# Qwen-Image-2.1-GGUF

云碩（xCloudinfo）自製的Qwen-Image-2.1 GGUF量化版本，底模 [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)。

## 這個repo解決什麼問題

llama.cpp生態（含ComfyUI-GGUF）原本不支援量化Qwen-Image-2.1——`llama-quantize` 遇到這個架構會直接報
`unknown model architecture: 'qwen_image21'`。我方在 [leejet的ComfyUI-GGUF fork](https://github.com/leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF)
補上了 `qwen_image21` 架構的**量化支援**（C++ 端五處：架構列舉、名稱對照表、tensor map、
metadata略過規則、量化排除規則），重新編譯 `llama-quantize` 後產出完整六階量化。
ComfyUI端的**讀取**支援leejet fork其實已經內建（`qwen_image21` 已列在其 `loader.py` 的
`IMG_ARCH_LIST`），本次補的是「產出」這一側的缺口。

## 內含檔案

- `Qwen-Image-2.1-{Q8_0,Q6_K,Q5_K_M,Q4_K_M,Q3_K_M,Q2_K}.gguf` —— DiT主體，六個量化階
- `text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_bf16.safetensors` —— Qwen3-VL-8B文字編碼器，bf16，單一檔案。
  **權重與官方 `text_encoder` 的四個分片逐位元相同**（750個張量全部比對，無任何差異）。
  差別只在封裝：合併成單檔，且語言模型張量的鍵名由官方的 `model.language_model.layers.*` 改為
  `model.layers.*`。這不是Qwen官方發布的檔案形式，是為了單檔載入而重新封裝的版本。
- `vae/qwen_image_2.1_vae.safetensors` —— 官方 `vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors`，內容未修改，
  上傳時僅更改檔名。

## 量化方法

邊界層（`img_in.` / `txt_in.` / `time_text_embed.` / `modulation.` / `norm_out.` / `proj_out.weight`）
維持bf16不量化，逐層注意力與MLP矩陣依量化階梯轉換，1D正規化層（`norm_q`/`norm_k`）自動保留f32
——沿用llama.cpp對FLUX、SD3等既有diffusion架構的既定處理方式。

**沒有IQ4_XS / IQ2_M**：llama.cpp（含此fork）目前對所有image-model架構統一禁用I-quant系列
（`Invalid quantization type for image model (Not supported)`），FLUX/SD3等既有架構一樣不能轉I-quant。
這是上游程式碼現有的限制，不是這次轉檔特有的問題。最小的可用量化階是Q2_K。

## 誠實揭露

- **已做結構驗證**：297個張量數量與命名對齊原始f16、邊界層確認未被量化、輸出檔案能被
  gguf reader正常解析。
- **未做端到端生圖驗證**：轉檔環境沒有安裝完整ComfyUI，沒有實際跑一次生圖比對輸出品質。
  建議初次使用先用較高量化階（Q8_0/Q6_K）跑一張對照圖確認品質，再視需求換更小的階。
- 使用需要支援 `qwen_image21` 架構的ComfyUI-GGUF節點；目前建議用
  [leejet的fork](https://github.com/leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF)，vanilla city96版尚未收錄此架構。

## 使用方式（ComfyUI）

1. 安裝 [leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF) 到 `custom_nodes/`。
2. DiT GGUF放 `models/diffusion_models/`，用UNET Loader (GGUF) 節點載入。
3. 文字編碼器放 `models/text_encoders/`，VAE放 `models/vae/`，分別用對應的原生節點載入。

## 授權

繼承 [Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) 原廠授權（Apache 2.0）。

## 關於云碩科技

云碩科技（xCloudinfo Corp. Limited）專注於地端私有化人工智慧解決方案。xVITA是云碩自研模型的品牌名稱。

其他模型請見 [https://hf.co/xCloudinfo](https://hf.co/xCloudinfo)。

# Qwen-Image-2.1-GGUF — English

A GGUF quantized version of Qwen-Image-2.1 made by xCloudinfo (云碩), with the base model [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1).

## What problem this repo solves

The llama.cpp ecosystem (including ComfyUI-GGUF) originally did not support quantizing Qwen-Image-2.1: `llama-quantize` fails on this architecture with
`unknown model architecture: 'qwen_image21'`. In [leejet's ComfyUI-GGUF fork](https://github.com/leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF) we added
**quantization support** for the `qwen_image21` architecture (five places on the C++ side: the architecture enum, the name mapping table, the tensor map,
the metadata skip rules, and the quantization exclusion rules), recompiled `llama-quantize`, and produced the full set of six quantization tiers.
**Loading** support on the ComfyUI side is in fact already built into the leejet fork (`qwen_image21` is already listed in the
`IMG_ARCH_LIST` of its `loader.py`); what we filled in this time is the gap on the "producing" side.

## Included files

- `Qwen-Image-2.1-{Q8_0,Q6_K,Q5_K_M,Q4_K_M,Q3_K_M,Q2_K}.gguf`: the DiT body, in six quantization tiers
- `text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_bf16.safetensors`: the Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder, bf16, as a single file.
  **The weights are bit-for-bit identical to the four shards of the official `text_encoder`** (all 750 tensors compared, with no differences).
  The only difference is the packaging: the shards are merged into a single file, and the key names of the language-model tensors are changed from the official `model.language_model.layers.*` to
  `model.layers.*`. This is not a file form that Qwen officially publishes; it is a repackaged version made for single-file loading.
- `vae/qwen_image_2.1_vae.safetensors`: the official `vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors`, with its content unmodified;
  only the file name was changed on upload.

## Quantization method

The boundary layers (`img_in.` / `txt_in.` / `time_text_embed.` / `modulation.` / `norm_out.` / `proj_out.weight`)
stay in bf16 and are not quantized; the per-layer attention and MLP matrices are converted according to the quantization tier, and the 1D normalization layers (`norm_q`/`norm_k`) are automatically kept in f32.
This follows llama.cpp's established handling of existing diffusion architectures such as FLUX and SD3.

**No IQ4_XS / IQ2_M**: llama.cpp (including this fork) currently disables the I-quant family for all image-model architectures

# ComfyFix GGUF for Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo (Q8_0, fixed for ComfyUI)

Repo: [skyzer4ever/ComfyFix-GGUF-for-Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/skyzer4ever/ComfyFix-GGUF-for-Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo)

> **Modified file.** This is AtomicChat's [`Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Q8_0.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF) with one change: the 64 QK-norm weights are stored as F32, so it loads in ComfyUI with [city96/ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF). Built with Qwen. Licensed under the Qwen Research License, for **non-commercial use only** (see `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`).

All credit for the quantization goes to **[AtomicChat](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat)**. All credit for the model goes to **[Qwen](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo)**. If AtomicChat re-uploads a ComfyUI-compatible Q8_0, use theirs instead. Bug report: see the [AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF discussion #2](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF/discussions/2).

Model chain: [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) → [AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-GGUF) (Q8_0) → [skyzer4ever/ComfyFix-GGUF-for-Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/skyzer4ever/ComfyFix-GGUF-for-Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo) (norm fix).

## What was wrong
In the upstream Q8_0 file, `transformer_blocks.{0..31}.attn.norm_q.weight` and `.attn.norm_k.weight` (shape `[128]`) are quantized to Q8_0. That's a side effect of `sd-cli -M convert`, which quantizes any tensor whose row length divides the block size. stable-diffusion.cpp handles it, but ComfyUI-GGUF has no quantized RMSNorm, so sampling fails on step 1:

```
RuntimeError: Expected weight to be of same shape as normalized_shape,
but got weight of shape [136] and normalized_shape = [128]
```

(128 values = 4 Q8_0 blocks × 34 bytes = 136.) AtomicChat's BF16 and AD-Q*_K files keep these norms in BF16 and already work in ComfyUI, so only the Q8_0 needed fixing.

## What changed
- The 64 tensors above were dequantized from Q8_0 to F32, which reproduces exactly the values the original file encodes.
- Every other tensor (BF16 ×4, Q8_0 ×197) and the header metadata are **byte-identical** to the upstream file. Nothing was requantized.
- ComfyUI log: `gguf qtypes: BF16 (4), Q8_0 (197), F32 (64)`.

| File | Size | sha256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Q8_0-comfyfix.gguf` | 7,591,577,312 B | `8d74ae0be534df394ea2d29f04b77f879318c9e0df20a3e208e6bedbf89b4159` |
| source: AtomicChat `Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Q8_0.gguf` | 7,591,554,784 B | (see upstream repo) |

Quality is the same as upstream Q8_0: per AtomicChat's card, LPIPS 0.037 vs BF16. At seed 42, this file and another Q8_0 build with F32 norms gave almost the same image (PSNR 38.7 dB, mean abs diff 0.82/255).

## Usage in ComfyUI
Files:
- `models/unet/` (or `diffusion_models/`): `Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-Q8_0-comfyfix.gguf`
- `models/text_encoders/`: Qwen3-VL-8B, e.g. `qwen3vl_8b_bf16.safetensors` from [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1)
- `models/vae/`: `qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors` from [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1)

Graph: `UnetLoaderGGUF` → `CLIPLoader` (type `qwen_image`) → `TextEncodeQwenImage21` → `SamplerCustom` (cfg **1.0**) with `KSamplerSelect` = **euler** and `ManualSigmas` → `VAEDecode`. A ready-made API workflow is in `workflow_atomicchat_turbo_api.json`.

**Recommended settings (Turbo, from the AtomicChat and Qwen cards):**
- 8 steps, CFG 1.0, euler, sampler shift 1.0
- Sigmas (the checkpoint's `sample_sigmas` plus a final 0):
  ```
  1.0, 0.978453, 0.95418, 0.926626, 0.89508, 0.845148, 0.704534, 0.414568, 0.0
  ```
- Don't use a default 20–30-step scheduler. Turbo was distilled for this schedule only.
- 1024×1024 works well. Qwen recommends about 2 MP (2048×2048 at 1:1).

Measured speed on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell: about 2.2–2.7 s per 1024² image, end to end.

[`fix_atomicchat_gguf.py`](https://huggingface.co/skyzer4ever/ComfyFix-GGUF-for-Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo/blob/main/fix_atomicchat_gguf.py) makes the same fix on any GGUF with quantized 1-D tensors (e.g. other sd.cpp Q8_0/Q5_0/Q4_0 exports). It never overwrites its input, and it verifies the output.

# MiniMax-H3 FL2VA - SVDQuant MXFP4

This is a self-contained FL2VA checkpoint of
[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) with the
50-block diffusion transformer quantized using **SVDQuant MXFP4**. The text
encoder, tokenizer, processor, video VAE, and audio VAE remain in their original
BF16/full-precision form.

The checkpoint was exported with AutoRound at `iters=0` (RTN residuals) and unit
smoothing. It is **not** a ConvRot checkpoint.

![Validation frames for SVDQuant MXFP4 W4A4](assets/preview_mxfp4_w4a4.png)

## Quantization

- Diffusion transformer: SVDQuant MXFP4, rank 32, `act_unsigned=false`
- 208 quantized SVD linear layers
- 58 BF16 pass-through modules
- 1,367 transformer tensors
- Transformer weights: 34.58 GiB
- Full FL2VA repository: 107.03 GiB
- Other FL2VA components: original BF16 weights and support files

The checkpoint keeps both critical SVD components: the low-rank correction
(`proj_down`/`proj_up`) and the quantized residual (`qweight`/`wscales`), plus
the smoothing factor. No reference BF16 transformer is needed at inference.

## Runtime requirements

Use a vLLM-Omni build containing the SVDQuant MXFP4 runtime and H3 serialized-QKV
reorder fix from
[vllm-omni-fork PR #13](https://github.com/yiliu30/vllm-omni-fork/pull/13),
specifically commit
[`66e56e62f`](https://github.com/yiliu30/vllm-omni-fork/commit/66e56e62ffaff9351cc101b8ef5e54d8332c8507)
or a later release containing it.

The H3 QKV reorder fix is mandatory. Without it, the serialized QKV rows are
loaded in the wrong order and the generated video will be noise.

Validated environment:

- NVIDIA B200, SM100, 183 GiB
- One GPU for inference; about 89.7 GiB GPU memory after model loading
- vLLM 0.32.0 with the vLLM-Omni `feat/svdquant-mxfp4` runtime
- CUDA build with FlashInfer MXFP4 support

The kernel is selected automatically from the transformer
`quantization_config.json`; do **not** pass `--quantization`.

- FlashInfer CuTe-DSL MXFP4 available: `FlashInferMxFp4LinearKernel` (W4A4)
- Otherwise: `MarlinMxFp4LinearKernel` (W4A16 fallback)

## Run with vLLM-Omni

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 vllm serve Yi30/MiniMax-H3-FL2VA-SVD-MXFP4 \
  --omni \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8091 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --task-type fl2va \
  --num-gpus 1 \
  --diffusion-attention-backend TRTLLM_ATTN \
  --cache-backend cache_dit \
  --cache-config '{"Fn_compute_blocks":1,"Bn_compute_blocks":0,"max_warmup_steps":4,"residual_diff_threshold":0.04,"max_continuous_cached_steps":1,"enable_taylorseer":false,"scm_steps_mask_policy":null}' \
  --enable-cache-dit-summary
```

The first request also triggers the model's lazy regional `torch.compile`.
After the server is ready, submit a text-to-video-plus-audio request:

```bash
curl -sS --fail-with-body -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8091/v1/videos/sync \
  -F 'prompt=A cinematic shot of a starship bridge.' \
  -F 'width=1344' \
  -F 'height=768' \
  -F 'aspect_ratio=16:9' \
  -F 'fps=24' \
  -F 'num_inference_steps=50' \
  -F 'flow_shift=12' \
  -F 'seed=0' \
  -F 'extra_params={"task":"t2va","duration":10,"audio_flow_shift":3.0}' \
  -o output.mp4
```

For first-frame conditioning, add
`-F 'input_reference=@first_frame.png;type=image/png'` and keep
`"task":"fl2va"` in `extra_params`.

## Validation

Request: 1344x768, 243 frames, 24 fps, 10 seconds, 50 steps, seed 0,
Cache-DiT enabled, using the model-card prompt.

| Transformer kernel | Engine time | Output | PSNR vs BF16 | SSIM vs BF16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FlashInfer MXFP4 W4A4 | 382.9 s | 12.29 MB | 10.85 dB | 0.386 |
| Marlin MXFP4 W4A16 | 449.9 s | 10.57 MB | 11.12 dB | 0.376 |

Both outputs are end-to-end coherent with synchronized audio. Generated video is
stochastic and the quantized path changes the sampled trajectory, so these
pixel-wise PSNR/SSIM values compare runs rather than representing a lossless
reconstruction.

## Download

```bash
hf download Yi30/MiniMax-H3-FL2VA-SVD-MXFP4 \

```

The repository root is the complete FL2VA model directory. Serve that directory
or the Hub repository ID directly.

## Scope and limitations

- This repository contains FL2VA only; it does not add Ref2VA.

# phygenhand MiniMax-H3 HOT3D ControlNet

日期：2026-10-24

- 模型：MiniMax-H3 FL2VA 的 Fun-ControlNet-Union 分支（5 个注入块，3.40B 参数）从 PAI 权重全量继续训练，同时训练 DiT LoRA（rank 32，`attn.qkv_proj, attn.out_proj, mlp.fc1, mlp.fc2`）。
- 控制输入：物理通道图，打包成一个 RGB 视频：R = 深度（近亮远暗），G = 手 255 / 物体 128 / 背景 0，B = 接触强度。
- 数据：HOT3D train_aria 全部 1516 个 clip 渲染的（真实视频, 通道图）配对，1441 训练 / 75 验证；832×480，24 fps，124 帧。视频无音频，音频损失权重为 0。
- 训练：5 个 epoch，LR 1e-4，AdamW（weight decay 0.01），有效 batch 8（4 卡 × 梯度累积 2）。
- 配置：4×H200，BF16，DeepSpeed ZeRO-2，梯度检查点开启，DiffSynth-Studio 6b3c254；每个 epoch 约 66 分钟，峰值显存约 110 GB/卡。
- 状态：训练完成；尚未用训练后的权重做推理评测。

## 文件

每个 epoch 两个文件，sha256 见 `training_config.json`：

| epoch | ControlNet | DiT LoRA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `epoch-0-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-0-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 1 | `epoch-1-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-1-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 2 | `epoch-2-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-2-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 3 | `epoch-3-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-3-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |
| 4 | `epoch-4-controlnet.safetensors`（6.34 GiB） | `epoch-4-lora.safetensors`（296 MiB） |

## 加载

ControlNet 是 DiffSynth 的内部格式（q/k/v 已融合为 `qkv_proj`），不是 PAI 原始格式。先照常加载 PAI ControlNet（经 DiffSynth 转换），再用这里的权重覆盖；开启显存管理时 norm 层的键名会多一层 `.module.`，需要映射：

```python
import torch
from diffsynth import load_state_dict

# pipe = MiniMaxH3Pipeline.from_pretrained(..., model_configs=[...,
#     ModelConfig(model_id="PAI/MiniMax-H3-Fun-Controlnet-Union", origin_file_pattern="MiniMax-H3-Fun-Controlnet-Union.safetensors", **vram_config)])
trained = load_state_dict("epoch-4-controlnet.safetensors", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cpu")
names = {k: k.replace(".module.", ".") for k in pipe.controlnet.state_dict()}
pipe.controlnet.load_state_dict({k: trained[v] for k, v in names.items()}, assign=True)
pipe.load_lora(pipe.dit, "epoch-4-lora.safetensors")
```

首帧条件（FL2VA 关键帧）与 ControlNet 同时使用时需要 DiffSynth 的一行补丁。代码、补丁和数据渲染见 [phygenhand](https://github.com/Nicous20/phygenhand) 的 `cvm-physics-proxy` 分支（`scripts/cvm_hand/`，`scripts/reproduce/run_h3_scenarios.py`）。

For best clarity and motion definition, I recommend one of the following setups:

Option A

Sampler: res_multistep

Scheduler:simple

Option B

Sampler: euler

Scheduler: beta

Other sampler / scheduler combinations may produce noticeably blurrier or softer results.

Core Physics & Motion Logic / 核心物理与动作逻辑
Combat Base V2 moves away from "attack → reset" loops into a continuous physical chain where missed strikes carry momentum, blocks change direction smoothly, and limbs separate cleanly without sticking.

Combat Base V2 摆脱了“攻击 → 复位”的回合制循环，形成持续的运动链，招式落空可延续动量，格挡可自然顺势变向，且接触点脱离干净不黏连。

Hit reactions now persist and accumulate—sustained torso bending, lowered guards, and impaired mobility directly build toward convincing heavy finishers.

受击状态具备持续性与累计效应，躯干弯曲、护架变慢及移动受限等伤害会自然保留，让最后的重击终结更加合理成立。

Combat Skillset & Staging / 动作技法与镜头调度
Upgrades include continuous rotational kicks, sustained grappling and takedowns, dynamic 3-stage environmental collisions, and multi-phase fall trajectories.

全面升级连续旋转腿法、持续近身缠抱摔投、三阶段环境碰撞（人体→环境→材质），以及拥有完整轨迹的特技跌落表现。

Supports cinematic 1vMany choreography via staggered attacker entrances, spatial lane control, continuous protagonist-centered tracking, and motivated cross-cut motion continuity.

支持电影级“一对多”围攻调度，利用交替切入、环境通道压迫、主角中心跟随镜头以及跨镜动作连贯性提升画面表现。

Dialogue Performance & Benchmarks / 文戏表现与测试数据
Internal same-seed dialogue tests revealed +19.5% in-shot motion, +34.2% audio RMS, and +22.4% edge sharpness, significantly enhancing physical acting, breathing, and vocal dynamics outside of fight scenes.

同 Seed 文戏测试显示镜内动作量增加 +19.5%、Audio RMS 提升 +34.2%、边缘锐度提升 +22.4%，大幅增强了武戏之外的肢体表演、呼吸与声音动态。

Workflow & Trigger Usage / 工作流与触发词使用
For optimal flow, structure prompt timing as ACTION → DIALOGUE; start with No Trigger for maximum anatomical accuracy, add prfight2 for higher intensity, or prfight2, prfin1 for heavy stunt impact.

建议将提示词结构设为“动作 → 对白”；优先使用 No Trigger 换取最稳动作与人体，需要强攻击性时加入 prfight2，重终结/特技受击则使用 prfight2, prfin1。

Includes two specialized combat-director workflows (General & 1vMany) with Chinese instructions that support prompt output in any target language.

附带“通用”与“一对多”两个专用武戏导演工作流，内置中文说明并支持生成任意语言的最终 Prompt。

Direct the fight first. Write the prompt second. 先把战斗导演好，再去写提示词。

Upgrade Notes：

测试发现：同一镜头包含打斗和台词时，必须先完整完成击打动作再说台词，否则容易退回底模的慢动作表现。

Test finding: When combat and dialogue are in the same shot, complete the attack before the dialogue, or the motion may revert to the base model’s slower behavior.

About This LoRA｜关于这个 LoRA
先说明一下：这不是一个魔法 LoRA，也不会自动帮你编排完整的武打动作。
First of all: this is not a magic LoRA, and it will not automatically choreograph a complete fight for you.

如果你只写 two people fighting、a woman fights a man 之类非常简单的 Prompt，模型很可能只是让两个人高速乱挥拳，最后变成一段很快但没有逻辑的“王八拳”。
You still need to tell the model who attacks first, what they do, where the strike lands, how the opponent dodges or reacts, and why the next attack can naturally follow.

Prompt 负责决定“他们怎么打”，LoRA 负责增强“这些动作怎么表现”。
The prompt decides what the fighters do, while the LoRA enhances how those actions are performed.

*BUNNY Motion Repair V2 — High-Difficulty Motion Shouldn't Be a Lottery.*

Recommended Usage / 推荐使用

Standalone use: around 0.9 is currently recommended.

单独使用时，目前推荐权重约为 0.9。

When used alone, Motion Continuity Repair needs a relatively high weight to produce a clear effect on motion continuity / slow-motion tendency / missing transitions / prompt-following.

因为 Combat 已经提供了较强的动作速度和打击感，此时 Motion Continuity Repair 只需要中等权重来修正动作衔接 / 协调性 / 动作逻辑，避免过度接管整个动态。

What does it do? / 它主要做什么？

Ever had a great clip ruined by less than one second of strange motion? A sudden slowdown / a missing action / an awkward limb trajectory / a broken interaction can easily make an otherwise usable clip unusable.

你是否遇到过这种情况：一段视频明明整体很好，却偏偏有不到 1 秒突然慢下来 / 漏掉一个动作 / 肢体轨迹变得诡异 / 交互突然断掉，最后整段素材因此报废？

This LoRA is designed around repairing those moments rather than simply making every motion stronger.

这个 LoRA 的重点就是修复这些“突然掉链子”的瞬间，而不是粗暴地把所有动作统一增强。

Current A/B testing shows improvements in unwanted slow-motion behavior / missing motion transitions / abnormal limb trajectories / action coordination / prompt-following / interaction continuity / and some mismatched motion-feedback events.

目前 A/B 测试中已经观察到对 异常慢动作 / 动作断链 / 诡异肢体轨迹 / 动作协调性 / 提示词遵循度 / 交互连续性 / 部分错误动作反馈 的改善。

When H3 already handles a scene well, the difference may be very small / when the base model begins to struggle, the difference can become much more obvious.

当 H3 本来就很擅长某段动态时，开启前后的区别可能非常小 / 当底模开始掉速、断动作或失去逻辑时，差异反而会明显很多。

It doesn't simply make H3's strengths stronger — it tries to keep its weaker motion states from falling apart.

它不是单纯让 H3 的强项更强，而是尽量不让 H3 在弱项动态里突然掉下去。

Different weights can progressively change motion intensity and eventually begin reshaping the overall motion rhythm.

# MiniMax H3 Ref2VA FP8 for Radiance

[中文模型卡](README.zh-CN.md) · [Experimental engine and documentation](https://codeberg.org/Bunsei/radiance-h3-fullref)

An **experimental, preconverted `.rad` container** for the MiniMax H3 Ref2VA path in Bunsei's Radiance full-reference fork. It packages an existing pruned FP8-scaled checkpoint for that runtime. It is **not a newly trained model** and is not an official MiniMax release.

Use the matching fork for image, video, audio and mixed-reference conditioning. A `.rad` file alone does not add full-reference support to an arbitrary upstream Radiance build. It cannot be loaded directly by ComfyUI, Transformers or Diffusers.

## Artifact and provenance

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| File | `minimax-h3-fullref-experimental-fp8.rad` |
| Size | 26,863,880,192 bytes (26.86 GB; 25.02 GiB) |
| SHA-256 | `6d886c33067f81a3e6cc435351b42702b64a2c0ddfd81aa1387b87f4bd46f1a8` |
| Original model | [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) |
| Ref2VA checkpoint | [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3), `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_fp8_scaled.safetensors` |
| Container base | [StillDeadcode/minimax-h3-fp8](https://huggingface.co/StillDeadcode/minimax-h3-fp8) |
| Runtime source snapshot | `41ded9231759d28ef095338aa103ce997be73a85`, branch `h3-fullref` |

The Ref2VA source checkpoint SHA-256 is `f86f2f79ebd2d76eb8eeb46091e83982e6ff51d255747e7b16e92834b392b8e9`; recorded source revision: `e5eb578a89295337b8ff433a035929ce0279e0b6`.

The importer replaces the refiner/DiT components, adapts scale layout while preserving the source Ref2VA FP8 codes and scales, and carries over the base container's decoders and vocabulary. Existing FP8 quantization and pruning were inherited from the upstream conversions. This repack adds no training, fine-tuning, calibration or further quantization. The container includes mixed-precision components; “FP8” does not mean every tensor or operation is FP8.

**No acceleration LoRA is merged. No user images, reference videos, music, prepared latents or credentials are embedded.** The tested imported weights were not subsequently adjusted. See [MODEL-MANIFEST.json](MODEL-MANIFEST.json), [NOTICE](NOTICE), and the original [base-model notice](licenses/NOTICE-base-model.txt).

## Runtime requirements

The demonstrated configuration is Linux x86-64, two AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 GPUs (32 GiB each, `gfx1201`), tensor parallelism with an operational PCIe P2P path, and host memory offload. Two cards do not behave as a single unified 64 GiB GPU: some allocations are replicated and CPU memory is still used.

The accompanying experimental runtime was exercised on Ubuntu 26.04.1 / glibc 2.43. That is the prebuilt runtime's tested platform, not an intrinsic operating-system requirement of the weights. Other hardware, driver combinations and single-card deployment are not validated here. The full-reference benchmark reached roughly 34.6 GB of process resident memory in addition to GPU allocations; allow host-memory headroom. Runtime ABI is 28: build the engine and its plugins together.

**Raw-media preprocessing still requires external ComfyUI encoders.** The native Radiance refiner/DiT/decoders perform generation after preparation. This file is not the complete raw-media encoding stack.

## Download and verify

After accepting this repository's access terms, authenticate with a Hugging Face account that has access:

```bash
hf auth login
hf download Bunsei/MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-FP8-Radiance --local-dir /path/to/h3-rad
sha256sum /path/to/h3-rad/minimax-h3-fullref-experimental-fp8.rad
```

Keep all accompanying licenses and notices when redistributing the model. This download is already converted; the source Ref2VA safetens

We release an **8-step** and a **4-step** accelerator for the Ref2VA task. > [!TIP] > **Want better quality or lower latency?** Check out [`MiniMax-H3-PTD-RefAsymOPD-LoRAs`](https://huggingface.co/taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-RefAsymOPD-LoRAs) — the upgraded sibling trained with **PTD + RefAsymOPD** (Reference-Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation). > It ships an **8-step** and a new **6-step** variant, both delivering noticeably better **background plausibility, sharpness and realism** — surpassing the plain PTD checkpoints in this repo as well as the base model at 40 NFE. > Same checkpoint format and the same `apply_ptd_lora` call — a one-line filename swap. Unlike a single shared acceleration LoRA, PTD trains **one independent low-rank adapter per inference step** ("per-hop" LoRA) on the diffusion backbone, on top of the per-interval output heads introduced by Parallel Decoding Distillation (PDD). # MiniMax-H3-Pruned-full (self-contained mirror)

A self-contained re-packaging of the pruned MiniMax H3 checkpoint published by `multimodalart`, with the components that
the pruned index borrows from the base release copied in, so that one repository holds everything the diffusers modular
pipeline needs. This exists because some serving platforms mount exactly one Hugging Face repository per endpoint.

| Component | Source | Pinned commit |
|---|---|---|
| `text_encoder` (Qwen3-VL, 51 layers), `transformer`, `transformer_ref`, remote code `modeling_minimax_h3_pruned.py` | `multimodalart/MiniMax-H3-Pruned` | `1a0ef5e65b639e84af81d883817968532180e9c7` |
| `vae`, `audio_vae`, `tokenizer`, `processor`, `scheduler`, `audio_scheduler`, `LICENSE` | `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` | `9ac0dd7aabc2c651fcf0ace4c00b2bffd9c8c8a6` |

`modular_model_index.json` is the upstream pruned index with every `pretrained_model_name_or_path` rewritten to
`lightweight/MiniMax-H3-Pruned-full`; no component resolves to another repository at load time. All weights are byte-identical to the sources.

# MiniMax-H3 DaSiWa Hybrid V4, FP8 — radiance container

The DaSiWa community fine-tune of
[MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) — video with a synchronized
stereo soundtrack, from text, from pictures, or between two keyframes — as a single `.rad`
container for the [radiance](https://codeberg.org/StillDeadcode/radiance) inference engine
(AMD RDNA4, ROCm).

This is **not** the stock FP8 container. The denoiser is the DaSiWa `dasiwaHybridV4` fine-tune and
the text encoder is llmfan46's uncensored `qwen3vl_32b_h3_ultra_uncensored_heretic` CLIP — the
same two models the community's DaSiWa reference clips were rendered with. The file also carries
every conditioning component, so all forms are served from this one container: text, first frame,
last frame, first+last keyframe completion, and reference images/video/audio.

The MiniMax H3 Community License does not cover the European Union, the United Kingdom, the
Republic of Korea or the United States of America; see [License](#license).

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `minimax-h3-dasiwa-fp8.rad` — 50.07 GiB, RAD2, 3273 tensors |
| Denoiser | DaSiWa `DasiwaMinimaxH3_dasiwaHybridV4_int8` (the fine-tuned UNet), dequantised and re-encoded as FP8 E4M3 per 128×128 block (bf16 scales); its curve-form timestep modulation — the 1025×8 table and the per-block K=8 ada projections — stays bf16, unquantised |
| Text encoder | llmfan46's `qwen3vl_32b_h3_ultra_uncensored_heretic` (a Qwen3-VL-32B fine-tune): the 50 language layers and the full vision tower incl. deepstack taps; linears FP8 E4M3, tower bf16 |
| Other weights | token refiner FP8 E4M3; video VAE (encoder + decoder) bf16; audio VAE encoder bf16 / decoder f32; latent upscaler bf16 with f32 embedding MLP |
| Latent upscaler | [LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler) v1 (3D conv, 345M parameters, bf16; Apache-2.0) |
| Output | MP4: H.264 at 24 fps, up to 1344x768, 5.17 to 14.4 s; AAC at 32 kHz stereo |
| Needs | a radiance build with curve-form modulation and reference conditioning (see [Serve](#serve)); two 32 GB cards; pinned host memory for the text encoder and vision tower |

## Capabilities

One container, every conditioning form (all device-verified):

| Form | Request |
|---|---|
| T2VA | `prompt` alone |
| I2VA | a `first_frame` picture part — animate one image |
| L2VA | a `last_frame` picture part |
| FL2VA | `first_frame` + `last_frame` — generative completion between two keyframes (endpoints are pinned; the motion between them is the model's) |
| REF2VA | `ref_image_1 … ref_image_9` (≤9 pictures), `ref_video_1 … ref_video_3` with their `ref_video_audio_N` soundtracks, `ref_audio_1 … ref_audio_3` (≤3 standalone audio clips) |

Keyframes and reference media are mutually exclusive: a request either completes between two pinned
frames or conditions on references. All parts arrive as multipart file parts on `POST /v1/videos`
(`curl -F first_frame=@start.png -F last_frame=@end.png -F prompt=...`).

## Serve

Curve-form modulation (the fine-tune's ada tables) and reference conditioning are newer than any
upstream release: serve this file with a radiance build that carries both.

```sh
radiance --model minimax-h3-dasiwa-fp8.rad --tp 2 --vision-tower-placement ram \
         --max-model-len 4096 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "prompt": "A red fox trotting through a snowy pine forest, snow crunching underfoot",
  "seconds": "5", "size": "1344x768", "seed": 7, "sampler": "res_multistep"}'
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos/video_...            # poll until "status": "completed"
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos/video_.../content -o fox.mp4
```

The server speaks OpenAI's video jobs API (`POST /v1/videos`, `GET /v1/videos/{id}`,
`GET /v1/videos/{id}/content`, list and delete):

- `prompt` is read as written, up to 2048 tokens; the model follows long structured descriptions
  (the shot, its soundscape, its music) best — the DaSiWa workflow prompts in particular.
- `seconds` is rounded up to the model's length steps (17 frames): 5.17 to 14.4 s. `size` is
  `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, multiples of 32, at most 1344x768 pixels of area.
- `seed` makes a video repeatable on the same deployment. `num_inference_steps` counts sigma grid
  points as diffusers does, so the reference's 25 forwards correspond to 26 here.
- The model is guidance-distilled: no guidance scale, no negative prompt.
- `sampler`: `"res_multistep"` is what the DaSiWa reference clips were rendered with
  (`re

# MiniMax H3 Singularity ref2va v2, pruned

Pruned and quantized versions of the ref2va v2 release of
[WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity),
in the same layout as ComfyUI's own pruned MiniMax H3 releases. Load them in ComfyUI with
**Load Diffusion Model**, with `weight_dtype` left at `default`.

| File | Size | Built from | Transformer blocks | Token refiner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_pruned_int8_convrot_r2.safetensors` | 21.0 GB | bf16 release | int8 convrot | bf16 |
| `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_pruned_w6a8_r2.safetensors` | 16.0 GB | bf16 release | w6a8, group 32 | int8 convrot |
| `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_pruned_w4a8.safetensors` | 11.8 GB | int8 release | w4a8, group 16 | int8 convrot |

## Build r2

The int8 and w6a8 files are built from `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_bf16.safetensors`. The
first build started from the int8 release. Measured against the bf16 release:

| | r2 | r1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| int8 weight error, sampled layers | 0.87% to 1.10% | 1.30% to 1.48% |
| Timestep modulation error | 0.02% | 0.3% to 0.6% |
| int8 render, mean PSNR over four seeds | 26.1 dB | 24.6 dB |
| w6a8 render, mean PSNR over four seeds | 24.4 dB | 23.9 dB |

The w4a8 file is unchanged. Built from bf16 it rendered further from the bf16 release on every seed
tested (20.2 dB against 21.5 dB), so the build from the int8 release stays.

The r1 int8 and w6a8 files remain in the repository history at commit
[`ad7eb66`](https://huggingface.co/WAS/Minimax-h3_Singularity_v2_pruned/tree/ad7eb66157ff5fbe3429ef4413921fb0c7c9323f).

## What was pruned

The timestep embedder and the full-width adaLN projection in each of the 50 transformer blocks,
13 billion weights in all, are replaced by a 1025 x 8 `adaln_t_table` and 8-wide adaLN weights:
the curve layout of ComfyUI's own `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot`. ComfyUI loads it
natively. In the r2 files the table comes from the bf16 release's own timestep embedder, and the
modulation it produces is within 0.03% of the bf16 release's at every timestep tested.

The r2 int8 file quantizes the transformer block linears from bf16 with each row's scale set for
the lowest error. The w6a8 file quantizes the block linears and `final_layer.video_out`, with the
token refiner in int8 convrot, as ComfyUI's pruned w6a8 release does.

## Comparison

![The bf16 release and the pruned files, first, middle and last frame](comparison/contact_sheet.png)

1344 x 768, 124 frames at 24 fps, euler, simple, 6 steps, DMAD 4-step LoRA at 0.7, PyTorch
attention, `minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot` and the Qwen3-VL 32B MiniMax H3 text encoder. Mean
PSNR of every frame against the bf16 release rendered with the same seed:

| File | Seed 42 | Seed 43 | Seed 44 | Seed 45 | Mean | Render, seed 42 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| bf16 release | | | | | | [reference_bf16.mp4](comparison/reference_bf16.mp4) |
| pruned int8 convrot r2 | 23.3 | 24.9 | 28.2 | 28.0 | 26.1 dB | [pruned_int8_convrot_r2.mp4](comparison/pruned_int8_convrot_r2.mp4) |
| pruned w6a8 r2 | 23.5 | 24.2 | 24.3 | 25.8 | 24.4 dB | [pruned_w6a8_r2.mp4](comparison/pruned_w6a8_r2.mp4) |
| pruned w4a8 | 21.9 | 21.1 | 21.7 | 21.4 | 21.5 dB | [pruned_w4a8.mp4](comparison/pruned_w4a8.mp4) |

The bf16 release rendered twice with the same settings is identical frame for frame, so every
difference in the table comes from the weights. A single seed can rank two close files either way;
the mean over four is the comparison.

LoRAs without adaLN or timestep-embedder keys apply unchanged, including the source card's
recommended `minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1`.

## Modified files

These files are modified versions of WarmBloodAban's Singularity ref2va v2 release (MiniMax H3
Community License Agreement, Section III.2): the int8 and w6a8 files of
`Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_bf16.safetensors`, the w4a8 file of
`Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_int8.safetensors`. The timestep path is replaced as described
above and the transformer weights are quantized. Each file's safetensors metadata states the same.

## Credits

Fine-tune: [WarmBloodAban](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban). Base model:
[MiniMax H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) by MiniMax.

## Introduction We are excited to open-source **Qwen-Image-2.1**, a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model in the Qwen family. With just **7B parameters in its visual generation component** (32 Single-Stream DiT layers), Qwen-Image-2.1 balances generation quality, inference efficiency, and versatility. Four key improvements define this release: - **Compact and Efficient** — A lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. - **Native Transparency, Unified Creation and Editing** — Generate regular or transparent (RGBA) images from text, edit transparent layers, and extract subjects from photographs—all in one model. - **Versatile Editing** — Support up to **10 reference images**, specify local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks, and preserve identity for people and products. - **Realistic Textures and Refined Aesthetics** — Improved typography, portrait lighting, and fine details for more visually compelling results.

For more details, see the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) and [Blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1). ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install torch>=2.4.0 pip install transformers>=5.17 pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers pip install accelerate pillow ``` ### Text-to-Image ```python import torch from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") image = pipe( prompt="A neon shop sign that reads \"QWEN IMAGE 2.1\", rainy night, reflections on wet pavement", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("t2i_example.png") ``` ### Image Editing ```python import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ).to("cuda") input_image = Image.open("input.png") image = pipe( prompt="Change the background to a sunset beach", image=input_image, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("edit_example.png") ``` ### Transparent Image Generation (RGBA) Use the recommended prompt format for transparent images: ```python image = pipe( prompt="This is an RGBA image with transparency. A cute cartoon dragon sticker. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent.", width=2048, height=2048, num_inference_steps=40, generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("transparent_example.png") ``` ### Supported Aspect Ratios ```python aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (2048, 2048), "4:3": (2400, 1792), "3:4": (1792, 2400), "3:2": (2528, 1696), "2:3": (1696, 2528), "16:9": (2752, 1536), "9:16": (1536, 2752), } ``` ### Memory Optimization ```python pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained( "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() ``` ## Showcase

# FLUX.3 Image Klein — ROCmFPX GGUF

The diffusion transformer of [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein)
quantized to [ROCmFPX](https://github.com/charlie12345/ROCmFPX) formats for
[stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp).

> These files need stable-diffusion.cpp built against the ROCmFPX fork of ggml. Stock sd.cpp, ComfyUI-GGUF and
> other runners do not know these types. The patch is in this repo (`sdcpp-rocmfpx.patch`, 29 lines).
>
> Not an official Black Forest Labs release. Non-commercial use under the FLUX Kommunity License (see `LICENSE.md`
> and `NOTICE.md`).

![BF16 vs quants, same seed](comparison.jpg)

## Files and measured quality

8 prompts, 1024×1024, 16 steps, Euler, same seed per prompt. Every image is compared with the BF16 image of the same
prompt and seed. PSNR (dB) and SSIM: higher is closer. LPIPS: lower is closer (perceptual distance).
For scale: the same BF16 weights run in BF16 math instead of F32 already give PSNR 42.3,
SSIM 0.994, LPIPS 0.004. Diffusion amplifies small weight changes over the steps, so
quantized images keep the prompt and composition but differ in detail.

| File | Size | PSNR | SSIM | LPIPS | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `flux-3-image-klein-Q8_0_ROCMFPX.gguf` | 5.5GB | 30.4 | 0.969 | 0.025 | ROCmFPX 8-bit (UE4M3 block scales) |
| `flux-3-image-klein-Q6_K_ROCMFPX.gguf` | 4.4GB | 26.2 | 0.922 | 0.070 | ROCmFPX 6-bit |
| `flux-3-image-klein-Q4_0_ROCMFP4.gguf` | 3.1GB | 19.4 | 0.783 | 0.177 | ROCmFP4 4-bit |
| `flux-3-image-klein-Q4_0_ROCMFP4_FAST.gguf` | 2.9GB | 20.2 | 0.794 | 0.175 | ROCmFP4 4-bit, one scale per block (speed layout) |
| `flux-3-image-klein-Q4_0_ROCMI4.gguf` | 2.9GB | 19.6 | 0.777 | 0.188 | signed 4-bit integers with UE4M3 scale |
| `flux-3-image-klein-Q3_0_ROCMFPX.gguf` | 2.5GB | 17.6 | 0.693 | 0.280 | ROCmFP3 3-bit (preview format), visible quality loss |
| Q8_0 (stock ggml, baseline only) | 5.6GB | 34.6 | 0.984 | 0.011 |  |
| Q4_K (stock ggml, baseline only) | 3.1GB | 20.7 | 0.816 | 0.154 |  |
| Q4_0 (stock ggml, baseline only) | 3.1GB | 19.1 | 0.787 | 0.171 |  |

The 6-bit file is named `flux-3-image-klein-Q6_K_ROCMFPX.gguf` so that Hugging Face lists it as a 6-bit quant. Its weights are the ROCmFPX `Q6_0_ROCMFPX` type, not a stock llama.cpp `Q6_K`, and it needs the same fork as the other files.

**Honest comparison:** on this model `Q8_0_ROCMFPX` scores below stock `Q8_0` of about the same size; `Q4_0_ROCMFP4` scores below stock `Q4_K` of about the same size. The ROCmFPX formats are built for fast AMD kernels; their speed for image models on AMD has not been measured yet.

Not published: `Q2_0_ROCMFPX` (LPIPS 0.72, images no longer follow the reference).

Sizes are the diffusion transformer only (BF16: 11.1 GB). Layers that sd.cpp keeps in full precision for FLUX
(input/output projections, time embedding, biases, norms) stay BF16.

## How these were made

1. stable-diffusion.cpp (`b13a482`) built on the ROCmFPX ggml (`fb08d7c`) with `sdcpp-rocmfpx.patch`.
2. Importance matrix from the BF16 model over 16 calibration prompts (different from the test prompts), 1024², 16 steps.
3. `sd-cli -M convert --type <type> --imat-in imatrix.dat`.
4. Quality measured on GPU with every quantized weight expanded back to F32 at load time, so the numbers measure the
   stored weights. The fork's own GPU kernels for these types were not used (they are wrong on NVIDIA). On AMD GPUs the
   native kernels may round differently; **these files have not been tested on AMD hardware yet.**

## Run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/charlie12345/ROCmFPX
git clone https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp sdcpp && cd sdcpp && git checkout b13a482
git submodule update --init --recursive && git apply ../sdcpp-rocmfpx.patch
cmake -B build -DSD_USE_UPSTREAM_GGML=ON -DSD_GGML_SOURCE_DIR=$PWD/../ROCmFPX/ggml -DSD_ROCMFPX=ON -DSD_VULKAN=ON
cmake --build build -j
build/bin/sd-cli --diffusion-model flux-3-image-klein-Q4_0_ROCMFP4_FAST.gguf --llm Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf \
  --vae ae.safetensors -p "a lovely cat holding a sign that says hello" --cfg-scale 1.0 --steps 16 --sampling-method euler
```

Text encoder: [Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-GGUF).
VAE: `ae.safetensors` from the original repo.

--- license: apache-2.0 base_model: Qwen/Qwen-Image library_name: diffusers tags: - vae - qwen-image - qwen-image-edit - krea-2 --- # Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-1-and-Krea-2 Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-1-and-Krea-2 is the [Qwen-Image VAE](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image/tree/main/vae), but finetuned to produce cleaner textures with minimal checkerboarding or blur. This results in sharper, cleaner rendering of fur and skin (comparison courtesy [Green-Sky](https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/texture-fix-vae-for-qwen-image-1-and-krea-2/discussions/1)): ...as well as improvements in foliage, stone, etc.:
Comparison Settings The cleaner, sharper decoding is most noticeable in detailed, photo-style images with stochastic textures. The latents for the comparison image below were generated by Krea 2 (Turbo, 1024², 8 steps, guidance 0, seed 0) from the prompt: > Landscape photograph of a subalpine wildflower meadow in the Pacific Northwest in midsummer: a clear mountain stream winding over mossy boulders through purple lupine and red paintbrush, dense old-growth Douglas fir and western red cedar forest behind, a snow-capped volcano in the distance, golden late-afternoon light, highly detailed Zoomed crops are 128² regions upscaled 4x (nearest-neighbor).
| Qwen-Image VAE ([full-res](./images/decode-qwen-image-vae-full.png)) | 🪄 Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-1-and-Krea-2 🪄 ([full-res](./images/decode-texture-fix-vae-full.png)) | | --- | --- | | ![](./images/decode-qwen-image-vae-zoomed-1.png) | ![](./images/decode-texture-fix-vae-zoomed-1.png) | | ![](./images/decode-qwen-image-vae-zoomed-2.png) | ![](./images/decode-texture-fix-vae-zoomed-2.png) | | ![](./images/decode-qwen-image-vae-zoomed-3.png) | ![](./images/decode-texture-fix-vae-zoomed-3.png) | | ![](./images/decode-qwen-image-vae-full.png) | ![](./images/decode-texture-fix-vae-full.png) | # Compatibility Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-1-and-Krea-2 works with any image model that uses the Qwen Image (1) VAE, notably: - **[Qwen-Image](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image)** - **[Krea-2-Raw](https://huggingface.co/krea/Krea-2-Raw)** and **[Krea-2-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/krea/Krea-2-Turbo)** - **[Qwen-Image-Edit](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit)** For Qwen-Image 2.1, see [Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/texture-fix-vae-for-qwen-image-2.1). # Usage **ComfyUI** Download [`texture_fix_vae_for_qwen_image_1_and_krea_2_bf16.safetensors`](./texture_fix_vae_for_qwen_image_1_and_krea_2_bf16.safetensors) into `ComfyUI/models/vae/`. Then select it in the `Load VAE` node in place of `qwen_image_vae.safetensors`. You can also use the alternate 2D checkpoint [`texture_fix_vae_for_qwen_image_1_and_krea_2_2d_bf16.safetensors`](./texture_fix_vae_for_qwen_image_1_and_krea_2_2d_bf16.safetensors) via the [`anzhc-qwen2d-comfyui`](https://github.com/Anzhc/anzhc-qwen2d-comfyui) node. This checkpoint collapses the designed-for-video 3D conv layers into simpler/cheaper 2D conv layers that (for images) produce identical results. **🧨 Diffusers** ```python import torch from diffusers import AutoencoderKLQwenImage, QwenImagePipeline # for Qwen-Image: vae = AutoencoderKLQwenImage.from_pretrained("madebyollin/texture-fix-vae-for-qwen-image-1-and-krea-2", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16) pipe = QwenImagePipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image", vae=vae, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda") # or, for Krea 2: # from diffusers import Krea2Pipeline # pipe = Krea2Pipeline.from_pretrained("krea/Krea-2-Raw", vae=vae, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda") ``` # Mechanism Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-1-and-Krea-2 was created by briefly finetuning the highest-resolution decoder blocks with the adversarial recipe developed for [TAESD](https://github.com/madebyollin/taesd). The original Qwen Image VAE decoder was trained without adversarial loss (per the [official tech report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02324v1), section 2.3) which encourages the decoder to create blurry/artifacty outputs wherever fine details can't be precisely reconstructed from the latent. ![image](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/630447d40547362a22a969a2/I3F6SbqvcSRAs8Z-3fPdJ.png) Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-1-and-Krea-2 was only finetuned in the highest-resolution VAE decoder blocks (and within those, only the current-frame weights used in image decoding, not the multi-frame/video weights), so its encoder is unchanged, and the decoder differences are generally only visible at high resolution (when zoomed in). # Metrics Texture-Fix-VAE-for-Qwen-Image-1-and-Krea-2 makes perceptual quality metrics (rFID) much better and reconstruction accuracy metrics (LPIPS/PSNR) somewhat worse. This is an expected tradeoff, since we're generating plausible details

This tiny model is intended for debugging. It is randomly initialized using the configuration adapted from [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3).

# Nunchaku Lite INT4 r32 + BNB4 — quantized from Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo

**Built with Qwen.** A complete Diffusers pipeline converted from
[`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo/tree/fc13ba1986fcb905854dc8de2f52eee395f49b5b)
using [`diffuse-compressor`](https://github.com/rootonchair/diffuse-compressor).
Supports text-to-image generation and image editing with the checkpoint's saved **8-step schedule, CFG 1**.

The transformer uses **INT4 SVDQuant, rank 32, GPTQ, group size 64**:
224 SVDQ W4A4 targets and one INT4 AWQ W4A16 target (`modulation.1`). Other transformer tensors retain their source precision.
Eligible linear layers in the `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` text/vision encoder use
**BitsAndBytes NF4**, BF16 compute, without double quantization. The original Turbo VAE is retained.
The weights are serialized in their quantized formats and load through ordinary `from_pretrained` calls.

[Companion NVFP4 repository](https://huggingface.co/lite-infer/qwen-image-2.1-turbo-nunchaku-lite-nvfp4-r32).

## Run

Tested with PyTorch 2.11.0 + CUDA 12.8, Transformers 5.19.0, BitsAndBytes 0.50.2,
and the Diffusers build pinned below, which supports QwenImage21 and Nunchaku Lite.
NVFP4 requires a Blackwell or newer NVIDIA GPU.
The compatible native kernels are loaded through the Hugging Face `kernels` package.


```python
import os
os.environ["DIFFUSERS_TRUST_REMOTE_KERNELS"] = "true"

import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained(
    "lite-infer/qwen-image-2.1-turbo-nunchaku-lite-int4-r32",
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
).to("cuda")

image = pipe(
    prompt="A capybara wearing a wizard hat reading a book by candlelight, oil painting.",
    width=1024,
    height=1024,
    num_inference_steps=8,
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    use_kv_cache=True,
    generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42),
).images[0]
image.save("output.png")
```

For image editing, pass a PIL image through `image=`:

```python
from PIL import Image

pipe.vae.enable_tiling(
    tile_sample_min_height=1024, tile_sample_min_width=1024,
    tile_sample_stride_height=768, tile_sample_stride_width=768,
)
edited = pipe(
    prompt="Change her hairstyle to long, loose, voluminous wavy hair falling over her shoulders. Keep her face, makeup, necklace, black top, and the street background exactly the same.",
    image=Image.open("input.png").convert("RGBA"),
    output_resolution=1024,
    num_inference_steps=8,
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    use_kv_cache=True,
    generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(20261088),
).images[0]
edited.save("edited.png")
```

The saved `sample_sigmas` schedule is used automatically. Explicit call-time `sigmas` override it.
For larger outputs, use the pipeline's VAE tiling support as appropriate for available memory.

## Peak VRAM

| Final pipeline | Peak PyTorch allocated VRAM |
| --- | ---: |
| NVFP4 r32 + BNB4 | 17.53 GiB |
| INT4 r32 + BNB4 | 17.32 GiB |

1024×1024, 8 steps, CFG 1, KV cache enabled, all components resident on GPU, no CPU offload.

## Blog fidelity comparison

Six editing cases: three portraits and three products, using inputs from the
[Qwen-Image-2.1 blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1).
The BF16 column was generated with the **same Turbo source checkpoint**; it is not the original blog's output.
Both quantized columns were regenerated with their **final BNB4 encoder pipelines**.
Each row uses the same input, prompt, seed, dimensions, eight-step schedule, CFG 1, and KV-cache setting.
VAE tiling uses a 1024-pixel minimum and 768-pixel stride; 1024 × 1024 images remain untiled.
Click an image to inspect its original resolution.

# Nunchaku Lite NVFP4 r32 + BNB4 — quantized from Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo

**Built with Qwen.** A complete Diffusers pipeline converted from
[`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo/tree/fc13ba1986fcb905854dc8de2f52eee395f49b5b)
using [`diffuse-compressor`](https://github.com/rootonchair/diffuse-compressor).
Supports text-to-image generation and image editing with the checkpoint's saved **8-step schedule, CFG 1**.

The transformer uses **NVFP4 SVDQuant, rank 32, GPTQ, group size 16**:
224 SVDQ W4A4 targets and one INT4 AWQ W4A16 target (`modulation.1`). Other transformer tensors retain their source precision.
Eligible linear layers in the `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` text/vision encoder use
**BitsAndBytes NF4**, BF16 compute, without double quantization. The original Turbo VAE is retained.
The weights are serialized in their quantized formats and load through ordinary `from_pretrained` calls.

[Companion INT4 repository](https://huggingface.co/lite-infer/qwen-image-2.1-turbo-nunchaku-lite-int4-r32).

## Run

Tested with PyTorch 2.11.0 + CUDA 12.8, Transformers 5.19.0, BitsAndBytes 0.50.2,
and the Diffusers build pinned below, which supports QwenImage21 and Nunchaku Lite.
NVFP4 requires a Blackwell or newer NVIDIA GPU.
The compatible native kernels are loaded through the Hugging Face `kernels` package.


```python
import os
os.environ["DIFFUSERS_TRUST_REMOTE_KERNELS"] = "true"

import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline

pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained(
    "lite-infer/qwen-image-2.1-turbo-nunchaku-lite-nvfp4-r32",
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
).to("cuda")

image = pipe(
    prompt="A capybara wearing a wizard hat reading a book by candlelight, oil painting.",
    width=1024,
    height=1024,
    num_inference_steps=8,
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    use_kv_cache=True,
    generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(42),
).images[0]
image.save("output.png")
```

For image editing, pass a PIL image through `image=`:

```python
from PIL import Image

pipe.vae.enable_tiling(
    tile_sample_min_height=1024, tile_sample_min_width=1024,
    tile_sample_stride_height=768, tile_sample_stride_width=768,
)
edited = pipe(
    prompt="Change her hairstyle to long, loose, voluminous wavy hair falling over her shoulders. Keep her face, makeup, necklace, black top, and the street background exactly the same.",
    image=Image.open("input.png").convert("RGBA"),
    output_resolution=1024,
    num_inference_steps=8,
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    use_kv_cache=True,
    generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(20261088),
).images[0]
edited.save("edited.png")
```

The saved `sample_sigmas` schedule is used automatically. Explicit call-time `sigmas` override it.
For larger outputs, use the pipeline's VAE tiling support as appropriate for available memory.

# Qwen3-VL-32B Heretic (MiniMax-H3 text encoder) — NVFP4

**The uncensored MiniMax-H3 text encoder, in 15.7 GB — it fits on a single 16 GB card.**

This is a mixed-precision **NVFP4** re-quantization of
[ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-32B-Ultra-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-ComfyUI-INT8-ConvRot](https://huggingface.co/ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-32B-Ultra-Heretic-MiniMax-H3-ComfyUI-INT8-ConvRot),
the Heretic (uncensored) text encoder for [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)
video generation.

| build | size | fits 16 GB card? |
|---|---|---|
| Heretic INT8-ConvRot (upstream) | 26.4 GB | no (needs offload) |
| **Heretic NVFP4 (this repo)** | **15.7 GB** | **yes** |
| Comfy-Org NVFP4 (censored) | 15.7 GB | yes |

Same size as Comfy-Org's official NVFP4 encoder, so it is a **drop-in replacement**:
point `CLIPLoader` at this file instead and the rest of your MiniMax-H3 workflow is unchanged.

## Why

80 GB cards always had the choice. This is for the people who don't have one.
Creative work shouldn't require datacenter hardware — that's the whole point of quantizing it.

## Measured

Generated 6 s of 480×864 vertical video with audio, MiniMax-H3 `fl2va` pruned INT8 diffusion model,
`res_multistep` 20 steps, ComfyUI 0.30.0, Sage Attention on:

| | value |
|---|---|
| GPU | 1× RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell (16 GB, sm_120) |
| peak VRAM during generation | **~9.9 GB** |
| encoder staged in VRAM | 14.9 GB (dynamic loading) |
| system RAM used by the ComfyUI process | ~36 GB |

Output was compared against the upstream INT8-ConvRot build on identical prompt and seed.
The two are visually equivalent — the quantization does not change what the encoder will describe.

## Files

```
qwen3vl_32b_heretic_minimax_h3_nvfp4.safetensors   15.7 GB
```

Place in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` and select it in `CLIPLoader` (type: `minimax`).
You still need the diffusion model and VAEs from
[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3).

## How it was made (and the trap you must avoid)

**The upstream weights are rotated.** Its `comfy_quant` metadata reads:

```json
{"format": "int8_tensorwise", "convrot": true, "convrot_groupsize": 256, "per_row": true}
```

ConvRot stores each weight already multiplied by a normalized Hadamard matrix
(`W_stored = W @ Hᵀ`, per 256-wide group) and rotates activations to match at runtime.
If you dequantize those weights and re-quantize them to plain NVFP4 **without undoing the
rotation**, you get a file that loads, runs, and produces *completely unrelated video* —
in our first attempt a prompt for a war-torn street rendered a speedboat on open water.
Nothing errors. The conditioning is simply meaningless.

Because the Hadamard is orthogonal, the fix is to multiply by `H` again before re-quantizing:

```python
from comfy_kitchen.backends.eager.convrot_w4a4 import _build_hadamard

def unrotate(w, gs=256):                      # w: dequantized [out, in]
    out_f, in_f = w.shape
    h = _build_hadamard(gs, device=w.device, dtype=torch.float32).to(w.dtype)
    return torch.matmul(w.reshape(out_f, in_f // gs, gs), h).reshape(out_f, in_f)
```

**Mixed precision.** 350 linear layers are NVFP4 (`TensorCoreNVFP4Layout`, group size 16).
`model.embed_tokens` (151936 × 5120 = 778 M params) is **left as INT8** — the same choice
Comfy-Org made in the official NVFP4 build. Quantizing it gives little size benefit and it is
the one layer whose temporaries will OOM a 16 GB card during baking. ComfyUI reads per-layer
`comfy_quant` metadata, so the mixed file loads with no special handling.

The bake runs on a single 16 GB GPU in about two minutes.

## Provenance

- Uncensoring / Heretic work: **[ethanfel](https://huggingface.co/ethanfel)**
- Original encoder: **Qwen3-VL-32B** (Alibaba / Qwen team), as adapted for MiniMax-H3
- MiniMax-H3: **[MiniMaxAI](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)**
- ComfyUI packaging conventions and quantization layouts: **[Comfy-Org](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)**
- This NVFP4 re-quantization: **Lna-Lab** ([@Tono_Ken3](https://x.com/Tono_Ken3))

Licensing follows the upstream repositories; the MiniMax-H3 model weights themselves are
subject to the MiniMax H3 Community License.

## Notes

- Re-quantizing INT8 → NVFP4 means this build inherits the upstream INT8 rounding.
  A bake straight from BF16 would be marginally cleaner; we did not have those weights.
- Blackwell (sm_120) was used for both baking and inference. NVFP4 needs hardware support.
- If output looks unrelated to your prompt rather than merely lower quality, suspect a
  rotation mismatch, not the quantization.

# MiniMax H3 ## News Offical skills to improve prompt writing: [skills on github](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/skills) ## Online API Use MiniMax\-H3 directly via API\. - Global: [platform\.minimax\.io](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) \| CN: [platform\.minimaxi\.com](https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create) ## Online App Use MiniMax\-H3 directly via App\. - WebApp Global: [hailuoai\.video](https://hailuoai.video/tools/minimax-h3) \| CN: [hailuoai\.com](https://hailuoai.com/) - Desktop Global: [hub\.minimax\.io](https://hub.minimax.io/) \| CN: [hub\.minimaxi\.com](https://hub.minimaxi.com/) ## System Overview MiniMax H3 is a general-purpose, omni-modal generative system. It supports unified understanding of multimodal contexts composed of text, images, video, and audio, and can generate video with native stereo audio at resolutions up to 2K and durations of up to 15 seconds. Thanks to its task-generalization-oriented system design, H3 already possesses broad multimodal context understanding and generation capabilities at the pre-training stage, enabling outstanding performance in following complex multimodal instructions. H3 supports the following input and output specifications: | Category | Specification | |---|---| | Output duration | 4–15 seconds | | Output aspect ratio | Supports a wide range of aspect ratios, including but not limited to 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, and 9:16 | | Output resolution | Supports various resolution dimensions. The shorter side is set to 768 pixels by default. 2K \| generation can be achieved with H3-Regenerate-2K | | Output frame rate | 24 FPS | | Output audio | 32 kHz stereo | | Supported dialogue languages | Stable support for 11 languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish. Additional languages are also supported to varying degrees | ### Model Variants and Input Specifications | Model Variant | Input Mode | Specifications | |---|---|---| | H3-Base-FL2VA | First-and-last-frame mode | Supports zero, one, or two input images.

- No image input: Text-to-video mode
- One image input: First-frame-to-video or last-frame-to-video generation
- Two image inputs: First-and-last-frame-to-video generation | | H3-Base-Ref2VA | Omni-reference mode | Supports multi-modal reference inputs:

- **Images:** ≤ 9 images
- **Videos:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds
- **Audio:** ≤ 3 clips; each clip must be 2–15 seconds long; total duration ≤ 15 seconds
- **Mixed inputs:** Maximum number of files across all input types is 12 | ![Image](assets/overview.p
