Diffusers-compatible transformer weights extracted from [Phr00t/Qwen-Image-Edit-Rapid-AIO-V4](https://huggingface.co/Phr00t/Qwen-Image-Edit-Rapid-AIO/blob/main/Qwen-Rapid-AIO-v4.safetensors) for 4-step accelerated Qwen Image Edit inference.

## **Quick Start with Diffusers🧨** 

```
pip install -U torch transformers diffusers
```

```py
import torch
from diffusers.models import QwenImageTransformer2DModel
from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline
from diffusers.utils import load_image

transformer = QwenImageTransformer2DModel.from_pretrained(
    "prithivMLmods/Qwen-Image-Edit-Rapid-AIO-V4",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
)

pipeline = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511", # (or) 2509
    transformer=transformer,
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
)
pipeline.to("cuda")

image1 = load_image("grumpycat.png")
prompt = "turn the cat into an orange cat"

inputs = {
    "image": [image1],
    "prompt": prompt,
    "generator": torch.manual_seed(42),
    "true_cfg_scale": 1.0,
    "negative_prompt": " ",
    "num_inference_steps": 4,
    "guidance_scale": 1.0,
    "num_images_per_prompt": 1,
}

output = pipeline(**inputs)
output_image = output.images[0]
output_image.save("output_image_edit_plus.png")
```

# LTX-2.5 Gemma 4 12B text encoder, abliterated (int8 ConvRot)

This is a drop-in replacement for `text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors` from
[Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5), with refusal-direction abliteration applied. It uses the same
layout, the same `comfy_quant` format and the same loader.

## Why not the existing "uncensored LTX-2.5 Gemma" files

LTX-2.5's encoder (`gemma_version: gemma4-12b-ltx-v1`) is a Lightricks fine-tune, not stock `google/gemma-4-12B-it`:
- layers 0-10 match stock;
- from layer ~11 on, tensors differ from stock by 1-11% relative norm (11% at L12 `q_proj`, 1.2% at L47 `up_proj`).

The abliterated LTX encoders published before this one are stock Gemma with LTX's projection attached, some with the
pre-2026-08-17 projection. They lose the fine-tune the DiT was trained against.

## How it was made

- `igorls/gemma-4-12B-it-heretic-v1@192d14f` (0/100 refusals, KL 0.028) differs from `google/gemma-4-12B-it@707f0a3` in exactly
  22 tensors: `mlp.down_proj` in layers 22-34 and `self_attn.o_proj` in layers 29-37. Each difference is rank-1 (98-99% of its
  energy).
- Each difference was added to the official bf16 encoder (`Lightricks/LTX-2.5@49b093a`) and requantized to int8 ConvRot: fp32
  256-wide Hadamard rotation, per-row absmax/127, round. This recipe reproduces Lightricks' own int8 file exactly: 100% of int8
  values on the layers checked, scales to 1.9e-7.
- The refusal direction's output norm keeps the same share on the LTX weights as heretic left on stock: 29% / 45% / 43% at
  L22 `down_proj`, L30 `o_proj` and L37 `o_proj`, against 29% / 44% / 43% on stock.
- The other 1298 of 1342 tensors are byte-identical to the official int8 file.

`build.py` rebuilds the file from the three pinned sources.

## Notice of modification and licence

This file is a modified version of an LTX-2.x component. Its modified tensors are the 22 weights listed above and their 22
scales. The safetensors `__metadata__.modified` key records the same change.

LTX-2.x and Derivatives of LTX-2.x are subject to the **LTX-2.x Community License Agreement** (`LICENSE`), including Section 4
and Attachment A in their entirety: all use restrictions and acceptable use policies. By using or redistributing this file you
agree to that licence.

The Gemma 4 weights it contains are © Google, released under Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE-GEMMA-APACHE-2.0`). The abliteration comes from
[igorls/gemma-4-12B-it-heretic-v1](https://huggingface.co/igorls/gemma-4-12B-it-heretic-v1), made with
[Heretic](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic).

--- license: apache-2.0 base_model: - easygoing0114/qwen_image_clear_vae - Felldude/Qwen-Image-HDR-VAE tags: - merge - Anima - VAE - QwenImage - HDR - Clear --- # Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE
**An Optimized VAE Exclusively for Anime Illustration Generation** [![Model Type](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Type-VAE-blue)](https://huggingface.co/Rikunarita-ORG/Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE) [![Base Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Base%20Model-Qwen--Image-green)](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-orange)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)
![Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE_00002_](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/693bb65fb81c865cbc5f4fcd/daQdLGBaaTKlaGOoM5Dsv.png)
--- ## Overview This is a **custom VAE designed specifically for Qwen-Image**, optimized for anime illustration generation. By merging two VAEs with distinct characteristics, it successfully combines the "vibrant colors" of Qwen-Image-HDR-VAE with the "noise-free, natural line art" of Qwen-Image-Clear-VAE. It is specifically optimized for use with models specialized in anime illustration generation (2D/2.5D). --- ## Features ### Comparison of Base Models | Base Model | Pros | Cons | |------|---------|---------| | **Qwen-Image-HDR-VAE** | High dynamic range delivers **vibrant colors** (especially enhanced blues). Ideal for anime illustrations. Also offers **high resolution resilience**. | Excessive edge sharpness causes ringing artifacts, resulting in an **unnatural appearance**. | | **Qwen-Image-Clear-VAE** | Resistant to unwanted **artifacts**. Produces natural lines with a **hand-drawn feel**. | Colors can appear flat and sometimes **washed out or dull**. | ### Merge Results | Characteristic | Base Model | Result in This VAE | |------|---------|--------------| | **Color Vibrancy** | HDR-VAE (30%) | Vibrant colors (enhanced blue tones) and expanded dynamic range | | **Natural Line Art / Noise Resistance** | Clear-VAE (70%) | Retains hand-drawn texture while suppressing excessive sharpness / Eliminates fine graininess for smooth gradients | ### Technical Approach - **Merge Method**: Linear Merge (weighted_sum) - **Ratio**: Clear-VAE 70% : HDR-VAE 30% - **Tools Used**: ComfyUI-KJNodes - **Architecture**: Fully compatible with Qwen-Image-VAE --- ## Workflow Availability ### Full Disclosure for Reproducibility We have fully disclosed the **merge procedure** and **testing methodology** for this model. - **Merge Workflow**: [Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE/ComfyUI-Workflows](https://huggingface.co/Rikunarita-ORG/Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE/blob/main/ComfyUI-Workflows/Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE_Merge-Workflow.json) - **Test Generation Workflow**: [Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE/ComfyUI-Workflows](https://huggingface.co/Rikunarita-ORG/Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE/blob/main/ComfyUI-Workflows/VAE-Test_Workflow.json) By importing these workflows into ComfyUI, you can **reproduce the exact same merge under identical conditions**. --- ## Recommended Use Cases ### Suitable Applications - **Anime illustration generation** - Achieving both **vibrant colors** and **natural line art** - Use with anime-specialized models such as **Anima** and **illustrious-SDXL** - Supports **high-resolution generation (2048² and above)** - Compatible with any **Qwen-Image-VAE supported model**, including *Anima*, *Qwen-Image*, and *Krea.2* series ### Important Notes **Quality is not guaranteed for photorealistic (3D) image generation models.** --- ## Detailed Article on note ***[Introducing Anima-illustron-Qwen-Image-VAE: A Dedicated Anime VAE at the Golden 7:3 Ratio](https://note.com/rikunarita/n/n4f345d4cdb6f)*** --- ## Credits ### Base Models - **easygoing0114/qwen_image_clear_vae** - Provides clear image quality - **Felldude/Qwen-Image-HDR-VAE** - Provides vibrant colors ### Tools Used - **ComfyUI** - Generative AI workflow engine - **ComfyUI-KJNodes** - VAEMergeKJ --- ## License This model is released under the **Apache 2.0 License**, in accordance with the license of the base models. --- ## Feedback We welcome artworks generated using this model, as well as suggestions for improvement. Feel free to reach out via the **👏 Community** tab! --- ## Related Projects & Models in Development This VAE was created as a companion to **"Anima-illustron,"** an anime-specialized diffusion model currently under development. "Anima-illustron" itself is developed by merging multiple models, and this VAE has been optimized to maximize its potential. **The main model (Anima-illustron) will be released soon!** A link will be shared on this page once it becomes available.

# Introduction This September, we are pleased to introduce Qwen-Image-Edit-2509, the monthly iteration of Qwen-Image-Edit. To experience the latest model, please visit [Qwen Chat](https://qwen.ai) and select the "Image Editing" feature. Compared with Qwen-Image-Edit released in August, the main improvements of Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 include: * **Multi-image Editing Support**: For multi-image inputs, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 builds upon the Qwen-Image-Edit architecture and is further trained via image concatenation to enable multi-image editing. It supports various combinations such as "person + person," "person + product," and "person + scene." Optimal performance is currently achieved with 1 to 3 input images. * **Enhanced Single-image Consistency**: For single-image inputs, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 significantly improves editing consistency, specifically in the following areas: - **Improved Person Editing Consistency**: Better preservation of facial identity, supporting various portrait styles and pose transformations; - **Improved Product Editing Consistency**: Better preservation of product identity, supporting product poster editing； - **Improved Text Editing Consistency**: In addition to modifying text content, it also supports editing text fonts, colors, and materials； * **Native Support for ControlNet**: Including depth maps, edge maps, keypoint maps, and more. ## Quick Start Install the latest version of diffusers ``` pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers ``` The following contains a code snippet illustrating how to use `Qwen-Image-Edit-2509`: ```python import os import torch from PIL import Image from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline pipeline = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16) print("pipeline loaded") pipeline.to('cuda') pipeline.set_progress_bar_config(disable=None) image1 = Image.open("input1.png") image2 = Image.open("input2.png") prompt = "The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square." inputs = { "image": [image1, image2], "prompt": prompt, "generator": torch.manual_seed(0), "true_cfg_scale": 4.0, "negative_prompt": " ", "num_inference_steps": 40, "guidance_scale": 1.0, "num_images_per_prompt": 1, } with torch.inference_mode(): output = pipeline(**inputs) output_image = output.images[0] output_image.save("output_image_edit_plus.png") print("image saved at", os.path.abspath("output_image_edit_plus.png")) ``` ## Showcase **The primary update in Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 is support for multi-image inputs.** Let’s first look at a "person + person" example: ![Person + Person Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8719.JPG#center) Here is a "person + scene" example: ![Person + Scene Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8720.JPG#center) Below is a "person + object" example: ![Person + Object Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8721.JPG#center) In fact, multi-image input also supports commonly used ControlNet keypoint maps—for example, changing a person’s pose: ![ControlNet Keypoint Example](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8722.JPG#center) Similarly, the following examples demonstrate results using three input images: ![Three Images Example 1](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/edit2509/%E5%B9%BB%E7%81%AF%E7%89%8723.JPG#center) ![Three Images Example 2](htt

## Introduction We are thrilled to release **Qwen-Image**, an image generation foundation model in the Qwen series that achieves significant advances in **complex text rendering** and **precise image editing**. Experiments show strong general capabilities in both image generation and editing, with exceptional performance in text rendering, especially for Chinese. ![](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/bench.png#center) ## News - 2025.08.04: We released the [Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02324) of Qwen-Image! - 2025.08.04: We released Qwen-Image weights! Check at [huggingface](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image) and [Modelscope](https://modelscope.cn/models/Qwen/Qwen-Image)! - 2025.08.04: We released Qwen-Image! Check our [blog](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen-image) for more details! ## Quick Start Install the latest version of diffusers ``` pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers ``` The following contains a code snippet illustrating how to use the model to generate images based on text prompts: ```python from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline import torch model_name = "Qwen/Qwen-Image" # Load the pipeline if torch.cuda.is_available(): torch_dtype = torch.bfloat16 device = "cuda" else: torch_dtype = torch.float32 device = "cpu" pipe = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(model_name, torch_dtype=torch_dtype) pipe = pipe.to(device) positive_magic = { "en": ", Ultra HD, 4K, cinematic composition.", # for english prompt "zh": ", 超清，4K，电影级构图." # for chinese prompt } # Generate image prompt = '''A coffee shop entrance features a chalkboard sign reading "Qwen Coffee 😊 $2 per cup," with a neon light beside it displaying "通义千问". Next to it hangs a poster showing a beautiful Chinese woman, and beneath the poster is written "π≈3.1415926-53589793-23846264-33832795-02384197". Ultra HD, 4K, cinematic composition''' negative_prompt = " " # using an empty string if you do not have specific concept to remove # Generate with different aspect ratios aspect_ratios = { "1:1": (1328, 1328), "16:9": (1664, 928), "9:16": (928, 1664), "4:3": (1472, 1140), "3:4": (1140, 1472), "3:2": (1584, 1056), "2:3": (1056, 1584), } width, height = aspect_ratios["16:9"] image = pipe( prompt=prompt + positive_magic["en"], negative_prompt=negative_prompt, width=width, height=height, num_inference_steps=50, true_cfg_scale=4.0, generator=torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(42) ).images[0] image.save("example.png") ``` ## Show Cases One of its standout capabilities is high-fidelity text rendering across diverse images. Whether it’s alphabetic languages like English or logographic scripts like Chinese, Qwen-Image preserves typographic details, layout coherence, and contextual harmony with stunning accuracy. Text isn’t just overlaid—it’s seamlessly integrated into the visual fabric. ![](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/s1.jpg#center) Beyond text, Qwen-Image excels at general image generation with support for a wide range of artistic styles. From photorealistic scenes to impressionist paintings, from anime aesthetics to minimalist design, the model adapts fluidly to creative prompts, making it a versatile tool for artists, designers, and storytellers. ![](https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-Image/s2.jpg#center) When it comes to image editing, Qwen-Image goes far beyond simple adjustments. --- license: apache-2.0 library_name: comfyui pipeline_tag: text-to-image tags: - qwen-image - qwen-image-2.1 - taesd - tiny-autoencoder - vae - comfyui - preview --- # TAE Qwen-Image 2.1 · AcademiaSD

Tiny AutoEncoder (TAESD-style decoder) for fast, sharp live previews of Qwen-Image 2.1 in ComfyUI.

![Original · TAE · Latent2RGB](comparison.jpg)

Left: Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE · Center: TAEQwenImage21_AcademiaSD · Right: Latent2RGB (ComfyUI's default preview for this model)

ComfyUI previews Qwen-Image 2.1 only with Latent2RGB, a linear 64→3 color projection that looks blurry and blocky. This decoder is distilled from the Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE: it turns the sampler's latents into a real preview image in about 15 ms, with no need for the full VAE. | | | | :--- | :--- | | File | `TAEQwenImage21_AcademiaSD.safetensors` | | Size | 3.3 MB (fp16) | | Parameters | 1.63 M | | Input | Qwen-Image 2.1 latents, 64 channels, as the sampler sees them (`x0`) | | Output | RGB at 16× the latent resolution, range [0, 1] | | Decode time | ~15 ms for a 1024×1024 preview (RTX 5080, fp16) | | Validation PSNR | **30.1 dB** vs 20.9 dB for Latent2RGB | --- ## 🚀 Usage in ComfyUI 1. Download `TAEQwenImage21_AcademiaSD.safetensors` to `ComfyUI/models/vae_approx/`. 2. Install [ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes). 3. Add the **Model Preview Override** node between your Qwen-Image 2.1 model and the sampler. 4. In its `tiny_vae` input, choose `TAEQwenImage21_AcademiaSD.safetensors`. > ComfyUI's built-in **TAESD** preview method does not pick up this file: core has no tiny decoder entry for Qwen-Image 2.1 and its TAESD loader only supports 8× decoders. Use the KJNodes node. ## 🔧 Training details - **Teacher:** Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE (`qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors`). - **Architecture:** flat TAESD decoder, `Clamp → conv → 4 × (3 blocks + 2× upsample + conv) → block → conv`, width 64. - **Latent space:** latents normalized with ComfyUI's `QwenImage21` latent format (mean/std), the same space as the sampler's `x0`, so no extra scaling is needed. - **Data:** 4,072 varied images, 512×512 crops, encoded once with the real VAE. - **Training:** 30,000 steps, batch 8, 256×256 tiles, AdamW LR 5e-4 with cosine decay, L1 + FFT loss, EMA 0.999, latent noise augmentation for stable previews on the noisy `x0` of the first steps. ## ⚠️ Limitations - Preview only: use the real VAE for the final decode. - Decoder only, there is no encoder. - RGB only: the Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE also decodes an alpha channel, which this decoder skips. --- # 🇪🇸 Español Tiny AutoEncoder (decoder tipo TAESD) para previsualizar **Qwen-Image 2.1** en ComfyUI con nitidez y en tiempo real. Sustituye a Latent2RGB, la previsualización por defecto, borrosa y pixelada. Destilado del VAE de Qwen-Image 2.1: decodifica una previsualización de 1024 px en unos 15 ms, con 30,1 dB de PSNR frente a 20,9 dB de Latent2RGB. **Uso:** 1. Descarga `TAEQwenImage21_AcademiaSD.safetensors` en `ComfyUI/models/vae_approx/`. 2. Instala [ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes). 3. Pon el nodo **Model Preview Override** entre el modelo de Qwen-Image 2.1 y el sampler. 4. En su entrada `tiny_vae`, elige `TAEQwenImage21_AcademiaSD.safetensors`. El método de previsualización **TAESD** que trae ComfyUI no lo usa, porque no tiene entrada para Qwen-Image 2.1. Usa el nodo de KJNodes. Solo sirve para previsualizar: la imagen final se decodifica con el VAE real. --- ## 🙏 Credits - TAESD architecture: [madebyollin/taesd](https://github.com/madebyollin/taesd) - Model Preview Override node: [kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes) - Qwen-Image 2.1: Qwen team ## 🔗 AcademiaSD [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Academia_SD) · [X / Twitter](https://twitter.com/Academia_S_D) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/Syuaduy678) · [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/academiasd)

# Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 + Multiple-Angles LoRA (merged, scale 0.8)

[Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511) with [fal/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Multiple-Angles-LoRA](https://huggingface.co/fal/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Multiple-Angles-LoRA) merged into the transformer weights at scale **0.8**, saved as a full Diffusers directory in bf16.

This is the base model used to train the OakInk2 ego→exo LoRAs (`OakInk2_Ego2Exo_Qwen2511_MultiAngle_0p8_*`). Load those LoRAs on top of this model, not on plain Qwen-Image-Edit-2511.

## Merge

| | |
|---|---|
| Base | Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 |
| LoRA | `qwen-image-edit-2511-multiple-angles-lora.safetensors` (rank 16, alpha 16) |
| Scale | 0.8 (W = W₀ + 0.8 · B·A) |
| dtype | bfloat16 |
| Changed | transformer only; text encoder, VAE, tokenizer and processor are unchanged from the base |

Check on `transformer_blocks.0.attn.add_k_proj.weight`: cosine of the merged delta against the expected 0.8 · B·A is 1.0006 (bf16 rounding). See `merge_manifest.json` and `validation_report.json`.

## Usage

```python
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImageEditPlusPipeline
from PIL import Image

pipe = QwenImageEditPlusPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "wrc1415691977/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-MultiAngle-merged-0.8", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).to("cuda")
image = pipe(
    image=[Image.open("input.png").convert("RGB")],
    prompt="<sks> back-right quarter view elevated shot medium shot",
    true_cfg_scale=4.0,
    num_inference_steps=40,
).images[0]
```

The multi-angle prompt format (`<sks> [azimuth] [elevation] [distance]`, 96 poses) is documented in the [fal LoRA card](https://huggingface.co/fal/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Multiple-Angles-LoRA). Because the LoRA is baked in at 0.8, do not load it again on top.

## ComfyUI

`comfyui/qwen_image_edit_2511_multiangle_merged_0.8_bf16.safetensors` is the same merged transformer as one ComfyUI file (40.9GB, bf16, includes the 2511 `__index_timestep_zero__` marker).

| File | ComfyUI folder | Node |
|---|---|---|
| `comfyui/qwen_image_edit_2511_multiangle_merged_0.8_bf16.safetensors` | `models/diffusion_models/` | Load Diffusion Model |
| [`qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/HunyuanVideo_1.5_repackaged/tree/main/split_files/text_encoders) | `models/text_encoders/` | Load CLIP (type `qwen_image`) |
| [`qwen_image_vae.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI/tree/main/split_files/vae) | `models/vae/` | Load VAE |

Use it in place of `qwen_image_edit_2511_bf16.safetensors` and remove the Multiple-Angles LoRA node. Checked against plain 2511 bf16 + the LoRA at 0.8 in ComfyUI (same image, seed, Lightning 4-step): mean pixel difference 3/255, visually identical. Of 1,933 transformer tensors, 836 differ from Comfy-Org's 2511 bf16 file and the rest are bit-identical.

## Download in China

```bash
export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com
./hfd.sh wrc1415691977/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-MultiAngle-merged-0.8 --tool aria2c -x 8 -j 4
# ComfyUI file only:
./hfd.sh wrc1415691977/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-MultiAngle-merged-0.8 --include "comfyui/*" --tool aria2c -x 8
```

## License

Apache 2.0, inherited from both Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 and the fal Multiple-Angles LoRA. Credit: Qwen team (base model) and Lovis Odin / fal (Multiple-Angles LoRA).

# Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo (Nunchaku SVDQuant NVFP4 Rank-128 with Channel-Wise Macro Scaling) 🌟🚀

This repository provides the high-fidelity **SVDQuant NVFP4 (Rank 128, 32 Alternating SVD Iterations)** quantized transformer for Alibaba's **[Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo)**. Forged with **channel-wise Level-0 macro scaling (`wcscales`)** and optimized low-rank error absorption, it enables ultra-fast 8-step flow-matching generation and in-context image editing with **[Nunchaku](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/nunchaku)** on NVIDIA Blackwell (`sm_120`), Ada Lovelace, and Hopper architectures.

---

## ⚡ Highlights

* **100% Resident VRAM Execution on Consumer 16GB GPUs**:
  * Weights compressed from **30.2 GB (BF16)** down to **4.54 GB (NVFP4)** — a **6.65x reduction** in transformer memory footprint!
  * Runs entirely resident in VRAM on consumer GPUs (e.g. NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, RTX 4080 16GB, RTX 4090 24GB) with over **11 GB free VRAM headroom** on a 16GB card.
* **Rank-128 SVD Quantization Conquers Complex Facial Distortion**:
  * Quadrupled the SVD low-rank capacity from standard Rank 32 to **Rank 128**, trained over **32 alternating SVD error compensation iterations**.
  * Slashed relative $L_2$ projection reconstruction residual by **-44.7%** (from $0.1305$ down to **$0.07219$**) and elevated Cosine Similarity to **$0.99740$** across all 224 NVFP4 linear layers.
  * Completely eliminates the smeared eyes, smudged foreheads, and distorted facial geometry that lower-rank (Rank 32) models encounter during complex multi-subject in-context photo edits (e.g., adding multiple children in front of adults in high-resolution family photos).
* **Blazing Fast 8-Step Flow-Matching Latency**:
  * 8-step Text-to-Image (1024x1024) in **~12–14 seconds** (1.65 it/s) on a single RTX 5060 Ti — over **3x faster** than 25-step base models.
  * Multi-subject in-context image editing in **12.08 seconds** (1024x576, 8 steps).
* **Channel-Wise Level-0 Macro Scaling (`wcscales`)**:
  * Incorporates 224 channel-wise scale vectors across all transformer blocks, protecting outlier activation channels and eliminating color bleed and subscale saturation.
* **Procedural Geometry Excellence**:
  * Benchmarked on solid geometric primitives (e.g. red square on solid cyan studio background): achieves a background Laplacian variance of **$12.56$** (target $< 15.0$) with zero cobblestone or tiling artifacts.
* **Diffusers PR #14950 Flow-Matching Compatibility**:
  * Fully integrated with Diffusers flow-matching schedulers, automatically handling `sample_sigmas` for 8-step distilled generation.
* **Designed for Pairing with Heretic Text Encoder**:
  * Perfectly complements **`Qwen21_Text_Encoder_Heretic`** to eliminate false refusals, vector deflection, and unnatural anatomical postures.

---

# MiniMax H3 — Pruned INT8 ConvRot + Image Training Adapter (Fused)

**Unofficial experimental derivative; not affiliated with or endorsed by MiniMax, Comfy-Org, or CircleStone Labs.**

This project combines the **MiniMax H3 FL2VA pruned INT8 ConvRot** diffusion checkpoint from Comfy-Org with **CircleStone Labs' MiniMax H3 Image Training Adapter**, with the adapter fused into the model weights.

Its intended purpose is to simplify setup for **image-focused LoRA training** by avoiding a separate adapter fusion step at training time. It is not a newly trained base model.

## Sources and attribution

- **Original model:** [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)
- **Base checkpoint:** [Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3), file `diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`
- **Image-training adapter:** [circlestone-labs/MiniMax-H3-Image-Training-Adapter](https://huggingface.co/circlestone-labs/MiniMax-H3-Image-Training-Adapter)

## What was changed

The CircleStone Labs image-training adapter was merged into Comfy-Org's preexisting pruned INT8 ConvRot FL2VA checkpoint to create a single derivative `.safetensors` checkpoint. The base model and adapter remain the work of their respective creators; this repository documents only the fusion.

## Status

**Fused model weights are available through gated access.**

- Fusion completed.
- Preliminary file/reload sanity checks passed.
- End-to-end image-training results have been validated.
- MiniMax has confirmed authorization to use MiniMax H3 under its Community License Agreement, subject to continued compliance.

These statements reflect preliminary preparation checks, not a guarantee of training correctness or performance.

## Intended use and caveats

The fused checkpoint is intended for experimentation with **image-only LoRA training** in workflows that support the corresponding MiniMax H3 FL2VA checkpoint format.

- **Do not apply the CircleStone adapter again** when training with a checkpoint that already contains its weights.
- As the adapter author explains, image training with this adapter should use ordinary training rather than CFG-augmented/guidance-preservation training.
- The adapter author recommends using the regular base model, **without the image-training adapter**, for inference.
- Compatibility with a specific training framework or configuration should be verified before use; this is not a plug-and-play general inference release.

See the upstream adapter's [usage notes](https://huggingface.co/circlestone-labs/MiniMax-H3-Image-Training-Adapter).

# Qwen-Image-2.1 Uncensored — MIXED 4.39 GB (GGUF)

A per-layer mixed-precision quantisation of
[abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Quantized](https://huggingface.co/abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Quantized),
built from its BF16 GGUF (14.23 GB).

**4.391 GB · 4.94 bits/weight · relative weight error 0.0636**

Every one of the 297 tensors was quantised independently, with all other
tensors held at full precision, and the format was then chosen per tensor to
minimise total reconstruction error under a size budget. Result: Q4_K quality
budget, ~10 % better fidelity than uniform Q4_K, at 4.39 GB instead of 4.00 GB.

![preview](preview.png)

<sub>Generated with this file: 1024×1024, 20 steps, euler, CFG 6.0, seed 42. No reference image.</sub>

## Files

| file | size | bpw | rel. weight error | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen-image-2.1-UC-MIXED-4.39G.gguf` | 4.391 GB | 4.94 | **0.0636** | this model — recommended |
| `qwen-image-2.1-UC-Q4K-4.00G.gguf` | 4.003 GB | 4.50 | 0.0829 | uniform Q4_K, for comparison |

Composition of the mixed build: **Q4_K ×126, Q5_K ×105, F16 ×66**. The 66 F16
tensors are the block RMS norms plus two odd-shaped tensors (`ne0 = 64`), which
cannot be block-quantised; they are ~0.01 % of the file.

## How the bits were assigned

For each tensor, five encodings were built and the true error
`||W − W_q||_F²` measured. Formats were then allocated globally to minimise

```
sum_tensors ||W − W_q||_F^2     subject to     total size <= budget
```

which is the expected output-perturbation energy under an isotropic-input
assumption. The allocation is a Lagrangian λ-sweep over the measured
per-tensor byte/error pairs.

![per-block precision](chart_precision.png)

Sensitivity is nearly flat across depth (block-level relative error 0.043–0.084),
so most of the gain comes from choosing better formats for a subset of tensors
rather than from redistributing bits. Early blocks and the most sensitive late
`attn.to_v` / `modulation.1` tensors receive Q5_K; the rest run Q4_K.

![size vs fidelity](chart_pareto.png)

## Quality

Measured by actually rendering, not only in weight space.

Engine `stable-diffusion.cpp` (`master-975-95b3090`, CUDA 12), RTX 4070 Laptop
8 GB with `--offload-to-cpu`, 1024×1024, 20 steps, euler, CFG 6.0.

| subject (same seed per row) | mixed vs BF16 | uniform Q4_K vs BF16 |
|---|---|---|
| elderly fisherman portrait | 26.56 dB | 23.21 dB |
| snowy alpine village | 18.05 dB | 19.12 dB |
| car at night | 31.45 dB | 29.18 dB |
| astronaut on the moon | 20.96 dB | 18.25 dB |
| **mean** | **24.25 dB** | **22.44 dB** |

The mixed build wins on 3 of 4 subjects. At 1:1 crop, skin pores, hair and
fabric weave are indistinguishable between BF16 and both quantised builds.

![detail comparison](detail.png)

Differences between the two quantised builds at image level are mostly the
sampler amplifying sub-percent latent drift, not structural damage; the
weight-space numbers above are the reliable comparison.

## Usage

### stable-diffusion.cpp

```bash
sd-cli.exe \
  --diffusion-model qwen-image-2.1-UC-MIXED-4.39G.gguf \
  --vae qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors \
  --llm Qwen3VL-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -p "a weathered stone lighthouse on a basalt cliff during a storm at blue hour" \
  --cfg-scale 6.0 --sampling-method euler --steps 20 \
  -W 1024 -H 1024 --seed 42 --offload-to-cpu -o out.png
```

Needs the Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE and a Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder; both are available
from [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1).

### ComfyUI

Drop into `models/diffusion_models/`, load with **Unet Loader (GGUF)** from
[ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF), and set the CLIPLoader
type to `qwen_image`.

## Notes and caveats

- **Use 1024 or larger.** At 512×512 this model produces noise — including from
  the pristine BF16 weights. It is a 1024-class model.
- Dimensions should be divisible by 32.
- The error metric assumes isotropic inputs; activation-aware allocation would
  need calibration data and was not used.
- Q4_K is the lowest format implemented here, so 4.00 GB is the floor for
  uniform builds. Q3_K/Q2_K are not included.
- Generated samples inherit the uncensored behaviour and biases of the base
  model. You are responsible for how you use it.

## Credits

- Base: [abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Quantized](https://huggingface.co/abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Quantized)
- Upstream: [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)
- Engine: [leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp)

Quantisation, measurements and samples produced locally. Licence follows the
base model (`other`); check its terms

```python
import torch
from PIL import Image

# Qwen-Image Nunchaku Lite FP4 R32 with BNB4 Text Encoder

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Experimental:** This Nunchaku Lite quantized Qwen-Image checkpoint is experimental. APIs and loading behavior may change.

This repository contains a full Diffusers pipeline for [Qwen/Qwen-Image](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image) with:

- a Nunchaku Lite quantized diffusion transformer
- a prequantized bitsandbytes 4-bit NF4 `text_encoder`
- inherited tokenizer, scheduler, and VAE from the Qwen-Image release

## Quantization

The transformer uses a compact Nunchaku Lite quantization config stored in `transformer/config.json`.

| Component | Method | Precision | Group size | Rank | Targets |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Transformer `svdq_w4a4` | Nunchaku Lite | `fp4` | 16 | 32 | 720 |
| Transformer `awq_w4a16` | Nunchaku Lite | `int4` | 64 | - | 120 |
| Text encoder | bitsandbytes | `nf4` 4-bit | - | - | 358 modules |

## Requirements

This checkpoint requires a Diffusers version that includes `NunchakuLiteQuantizationConfig` and the Nunchaku Lite loader path.

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers
pip install kernels bitsandbytes
```

Use a CUDA-capable PyTorch environment. The quantized transformer uses kernels from the Hugging Face `kernels` package, and the text encoder uses bitsandbytes 4-bit modules.

## Usage

```python
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImagePipeline

pipe = QwenImagePipeline.from_pretrained(
    "lite-infer/Qwen-Image-nunchaku-lite-nvfp4-r32",
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,

# MiniMax-H3 PTD Ref2VA LoRAs: Pruned for ComfyUI

Smaller, rank-reduced versions of the **MiniMax-H3 PTD Ref2VA** few-step accelerator LoRAs, made to be lighter to download and load in ComfyUI.

> **All the real work belongs to the original authors.** These are derivative files. Original repo and full documentation: **[taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-LoRAs](https://huggingface.co/taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-LoRAs)**
>
> Same license and terms as the original apply. Check the original repo.

---

## What are these?

PTD (Parametric Trajectory Distillation) turns MiniMax-H3's Ref2VA task (reference image → video + audio) into a few-step generator.

Instead of one shared acceleration LoRA, PTD trains **one LoRA per denoising step** ("per-hop"):

- **4-step file:** 4 hops, 4 transformer evaluations
- **8-step file:** 8 hops, 8 transformer evaluations

Each step uses its own adapter plus its own output head.

## What I changed

The originals are rank 128 and big. I used **per-hop SVD rank reduction** to cut each hop's LoRA down to rank 64 or 32.

- Every hop and every module is truncated on its own, so hops are never mixed
- `lora_alpha` is set equal to the new rank, so alpha/rank stays 1.0, same as the originals
- `proj_out` and `audio_proj_out` (the per-step output heads) are **untouched**
- Still **BF16**. This is rank pruning, not quantization.
- The metadata (`ptd_num_hops`, `pdd_num_steps`, `lora_rank`, `lora_alpha`, etc.) is kept and updated

## Files

| File | Hops | Rank | Approx. size | Energy retained (mean / min) |
|------|------|------|--------------|------------------------------|
| `MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-PTD-4Step_r64.safetensors` | 4 | 64 | ~2.6 GB | 0.989 / 0.921 |
| `MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-PTD-4Step_r32.safetensors` | 4 | 32 | ~1.3 GB | 0.975 / 0.814 |
| `MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-PTD-8Step_r64.safetensors` | 8 | 64 | 5.2 GB | 0.985 / 0.865 |
| `MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-PTD-8Step_r32.safetensors` | 8 | 32 | ~2.6 GB | 0.965 / 0.724 |

Originals are rank 128: the 8-step is 10.35 GB.

**Energy retained** is how much of each LoRA's weight signal survives the rank cut. The mean is across all hop-modules, and the min is the worst single module. It's a rough guide, not a quality score.

## Which one should I pick?

- **Want the safest option?** Use a **r64** file.
- **Short on disk or VRAM?** Try **r32**, and compare against r64 before trusting it.
- **8-step r32** has the weakest worst-case module (min 0.72), so test it first.
- Few-step distilled models are touchy. If you see drift in **motion, lip sync or identity**, step up to r64 or use the original.

## How to use (ComfyUI)

1. Drop the `.safetensors` into `ComfyUI/models/loras/`
2. Install the ComfyUI nodes from the **original repo** (`comfyui_node/ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-PTD/`), plus **ComfyUI-PTD**, which they depend on
3. Use the **original, unpruned Ref2VA transformer** as the base. Pruned, Turbo, PDD and quantized base models are not valid for these adapters.
4. Load the LoRA with the PTD loader node at weight **1.0**, and set the step count to match the hop count (4 or 8)

Full setup and the example workflow are in the original repo's ComfyUI README.

## Notes

- The nodes read rank and alpha from the file metadata. If a loader hardcodes rank 128, the strength will be wrong.
- Pruning is lossy. The original files are the reference.
- These pruned files are community-made and not endorsed by the original authors.

## Credits

- **Original LoRAs:** [taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-LoRAs](https://huggingface.co/taobao-content-ai/MiniMax-H3-PTD-LoRAs)
- **PTD:** Lan Feng et al., *Parametric Trajectory Distillation for Few-Step Video Generation*, arXiv:2610.11498 (2026). [Project page](https://alan-lanfeng.github.io/PTD/)
- **PDD:** Neta Shaul et al., *Parallel Decoding Distillation for Fast Image and Video Generation*, arXiv:2607.26004 (2026)
- **Base model:** [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)
- **Pruning:** Winnougan

# LTX-2.5 22B LoRA Slow Motion Control

This is a **Slow Motion Control** LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**, which turns
**physical motion speed** into a controllable knob — real-time through extreme slow-motion —
while the **output video stays at original fps**.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

<Gallery />

## Model Files

`ltx-2.5-22b-lora-slow-motion-control-1.0.safetensors`


## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** standard LoRA
- **Control Type:** a `speed` conditioning value that decouples motion frame rate from playback frame rate
- **Modality:** image-to-video
- **Pipeline details:** no external models and no preprocessing at inference — one LoRA plus a
  pipeline that exposes the speed knob.

## Intended Use & Out-of-Scope

**Intended use:** image-to-video generation where you want **controllable slow-motion** of physical
action — splashes, punches, body shakes, spins, cloth and hair motion, falling liquids — at a fixed
provided fps playback rate.

**Out of scope:** arbitrary video restyling, and any use without the speed / dual-fps wiring. With a
generic loader that ignores the speed value you get a plain LoRA and none of the intended motion
control.

## How It Works

Unlike a normal LTX run, which uses a single frame rate for both the model and the output file, this
LoRA needs **two** values:

| Knob | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Playback fps (`frame_rate`) | Always **24** — the rate the mp4 plays at |
| Motion speed (`speed`) | The slow-motion knob. The pipeline derives `motion_fps = frame_rate / speed` |

Keeping `frame_rate = 24`:

| `speed` | Motion fps | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `1.0` | 24 | real-time |
| `0.5` | 48 | 2× slow |
| `0.2` | 120 | 5× slow |
| `0.1` | 240 | 10× slow |
| `0.05` | 480 | 20× slow |
| `0.025` | 960 | 40× slow |

Without the LoRA, pushing motion fps high mostly produces smearing and ghosting. With it, you get
genuine high-speed-camera-style slow-motion.

**Prompting:** write a normal image-to-video caption. There is **no trigger word** and no special
phrasing — do not add "slow motion", "high fps", or any speed wording. The speed value alone drives
the effect, and the same caption should be reused across every speed.

## Usage

### 🔌 ComfyUI

1. Copy `ltx-2.5-22b-lora-slow-motion-control-1.0.safetensors` into `models/loras`.
2. Load [`LTX-2.5_I2V_Speed_Control_flow.json`](LTX-2.5_I2V_Speed_Control_flow.json) from this repo — it wires the
   LoRA and the speed knob for you, and lists the LTX-2.5 models it needs in its own note.
3. Set the **`speed`** node (ships at `0.2`) to taste and keep the frame rate at **24**.

# Cinemagraph

Transforms still images into smooth, looping cinemagraphs with selective motion while keeping the rest of the scene frozen.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

## Example Outputs

<Gallery />

## Model Files

`ltx-2.5-22b-lora-cinemagraph-0.9.safetensors`

## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** LoRA
- **Modality:** image-to-video

## Intended Use & Out-of-Scope

**Intended use:** Creating cinemagraph videos from still images — producing looping videos with selective motion (water, light, elements) while keeping the rest of the scene static. Ideal for creating animated wallpapers, social media content, and artistic motion pieces.

**Out of scope:** Scenes with camera movement, character/body movement, complex dynamic scenes, videos with multiple moving subjects. The LoRA is optimized for static-camera, single-element-motion scenarios.

## How It Works

This LoRA fine-tunes LTX-2.5 to generate cinemagraph-style videos from still images. It excels at creating smooth, continuous-loop animations where only specific elements move (water flowing, neon lights pulsing, rain falling, reflections shimmering) while the rest of the frame remains completely frozen. The model learns to respect spatial isolation — keeping backgrounds, people, and static objects completely still while animating only the designated element.

The training dataset consisted of "no moving people" scenarios with locked-off cameras, so the LoRA strongly respects composition and avoids unwanted motion outside the intended subject.

## Usage

### 🔌 ComfyUI

1. Copy the LoRA weights into `models/loras`.
2. Load the **LTX-2.5-22B** base model.
3. Add `ltx-2.5-22b-lora-cinemagraph-0.9.safetensors` as the LoRA.
4. Use the [T2V/I2V workflow](https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo/blob/master/example_workflows/2.5/LTX-2.5_T2V_I2V_Single_Stage_Distilled.json) from the [ComfyUI-LTXVideo repository](https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo/).
5. Start with LoRA strength `1.0–1.2` (the sweet spot) and adjust within `0.5–1.5` per generation.
6. Include the trigger word `CINEMAGRAPH_MOTION` in the positive prompt.

## Recommended Settings

- **LoRA strength / weight:** `0.5–1.5` (sweet spot: `1.0–1.2`)
- **Spatial Guidance (STG):** Use `stg_v` mode, scale `1.0`, targeting block `29` for enhanced motion control and boundary preservation.
- **Inference steps:** 30 (from training validation)
- **Guidance scale:** 4.0
- **Prompting:** See examples below. The model responds well to explicit descriptions of what should move and what should remain still. Emphasize "locked-off static camera" and "seamless natural loop" for best results.

```

# LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Water Simulation

This is a **Water Simulation** IC-LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**, which adds water to a clip — rivers, surf, rain, waterfalls, floods, splashes, spray, and wet-surface specularities — while keeping the subject's identity, clothing, pose, camera framing, and background geometry identical to the reference.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

<Gallery />

## Model Files

`ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-water-simulation-0.9.safetensors` — the released checkpoint (training step 3000). Trained on the `-dev` base; recommended inference on the `-distilled` base.

## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video, reference-conditioned)
- **Control Type:** Reference video conditioning — a "dry" reference clip drives a re-render of the same shot with water added.

# LTX Restore IC-LoRA

An In-Context LoRA that restores old and damaged footage: it takes archive video (low-resolution web rips, low-bitrate broadcast transfers, tape, sepia or black-and-white film scans) as its reference and renders the same shot as a clean, colour, high-resolution capture, removing compression damage, tape and sepia casts, flicker, dirt and scratches.

It was trained on the [LTX-2.3](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3) foundation model and has been tested on [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5), where it works well unchanged: every example and every number on this card was produced on the LTX-2.5 distilled transformer through the LTX-2.5 tiled workflow.

<Gallery />

Three public-domain archive clips restored with this LoRA and then refined (the two-stage ladder in Pipeline Details), from 640x480 or 720x544 scans to 2880x2176: a 1954 family meal (Prelinger Archives), the Lumière brothers' train arriving at La Ciotat (1896) and the Hindenburg at its mooring mast (1937). Each gallery clip is a 1:1 crop comparison (the scan lanczos-upscaled on the left, the result on the right, 800x800 result pixels); full-frame wipes: [family meal](examples/restore_family_meal_1954_wipe.mp4), [train](examples/restore_train_1896_wipe.mp4), [Hindenburg](examples/restore_hindenburg_1937_wipe.mp4). The prompts shown are the restoration-stage prompts as run. Negative for all three: `blocky compression, banding, mosquito noise, ringing, blurry, smeared, ghosting, low resolution`; the train additionally carried the prohibitions `shipping containers, logos, signage, lettering, ladders, modern vehicles, graffiti, modern buildings`. On that clip the station side of the frame holds almost no information in the scan, so the model rebuilds it: the buildings, the hillside and the porter's cart on the left are period-plausible reconstructions, not recovered detail. The locomotive and the crowd on the right are.

## Model Files

`ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-restore-1.0.safetensors`

Final checkpoint (step 4000) of the training run described below.

## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.3-22B Video (trained on the 2.3 dev base with the Gemma-3 12B text encoder). Tested on LTX-2.5: runs on the LTX-2.5 distilled transformer with the LTX-2.5 video VAE and the Gemma-4 text encoder at strength 1.0, with no change to the weights.
- **Training Type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video)
- **Control Type:** reference video (the archive clip, frame-aligned); optional reference image at the -1 token; optional prefix frames for chaining windows
- **Reference Downscale Factor:** 1
- **Pipeline details:** restoration pass at 1440 wide, then the [Detail Refine IC-LoRA](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Refine-Details) (see Pipeline Details)
- **Audio:** Not trained for audio generation

## Intended Use & Out-of-Scope

**Intended use:** restoring and colourising archive footage for delivery at HD to 4K class: silent-era and newsreel film scans, mid-century broadcast, tape-era video, low-resolution low-bitrate web uploads; recovering the mid-band texture that heavily compressed broadcast video has lost.

**Out of scope:** footage that is already clean (the pass is a switch, not a gentle enhancer); faithful recovery of a creative colour grade from a monochrome source (colour is inferred from content, or from a reference image); deinterlacing (deinterlace before restoring).

## Control Signal Requirements

- **Control signal type:** the archive clip, resized (lanczos) to the working canvas

# LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Pixel Spatial Upscaler

This is a **Pixel Spatial Upscaler** IC-LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**, currently available in a **2x** variant. It creatively upscales a low-resolution video, synthesizing fine detail rather than simply interpolating — making it a generative upscaler rather than a refiner.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

## Model Files

- `ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-pixel-spatial-upscaler-x2-1.0.safetensors` — the 2x upscaler checkpoint.

## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video, reference-conditioned)
- **Control Type:** Low-resolution reference video drives a 2x high-resolution re-render with synthesized spatial detail.
- **Adapter Rank:** 32
- **Precision:** BF16

## How It Works

The model is an in-context LoRA: instead of taking only a text prompt, it also consumes a **reference video** in context alongside the noisy latents being denoised. During training, the reference is a downscaled version of the target clip, so the model learns to map a low-resolution reference onto a higher-resolution rendering of the same scene.

At inference the reference is your low-resolution clip. The model does not upsample it pixel-wise; it re-renders the scene at the higher resolution, inventing plausible fine detail (texture, edges, micro-contrast) that was never present in the reference. Composition, motion and subject identity are carried over from the reference, while high-frequency detail is generated.

## Control Signal Requirements

- **Control signal:** a low-resolution video clip (the reference).
- **Reference downscale factor:** `2`. The reference is expected at half the linear resolution of the target output; the model's metadata carries `reference_downscale_factor: 2` so compatible tooling can derive this automatically.
- **Framing:** the reference must cover the same shot, duration and framing as the intended output. This is not an inpainting or reframing model — changing the aspect ratio or crop between reference and target degrades results.
- **Source quality:** the reference should be a clean low-resolution render, not a heavily compressed or degraded clip. See *Intended Use* — artifact removal is out of scope.

## Usage

### 🔌 ComfyUI

1. Copy the LoRA weights into `models/loras`.
2. Load the **LTX-2.5-22B** base model and add `ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-pixel-spatial-upscaler-x2-1.0.safetensors` as the LoRA.
3. Use an IC-LoRA (video-to-video) workflow from the [LTX-2 ComfyUI repository](https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo/blob/master/example_workflows/2.5/LTX-2.5_V2V_ICLoRA_Single_Stage_Distilled.json). Connect your low-resolution clip as the reference video.

## Recommended Settings

- **LoRA strength:** `1.0`. The weights ship pre-scaled so that full strength is the intended default.
- **Reference downscale factor:** `2` (see *Control Signal Requirements*).
- **Recommended flow:** generate your video at a low base resolution (~280p) until you are satisfied with composition and subject motion, then feed that clip as the reference and run the 2x upscaler to produce the final high-resolution output.

The level of fidelity to the original can be traded off via generation parameters (guidance and step count in particular). Fewer steps and lower guidance keep the output closer to the reference; more steps and higher guidance allow more creative hallucination of detail.

## Intended Use

**Intended use:** Creative upsampling as part of a generation flow. The recommended workflow is to generate a draft at a very low base resolution (e.g. ~280p) to nail composition and motion, then run the upscaler to produce a high-resolution result with synthesized detail.

**Out of scope:** This is not a blind denoiser or a compression-artefact remover. The model synthesizes new detail rather than faithfully preserving the reference — use it as a creative step, not a pixel-accurate refiner. It is also not intended for upscaling live-action footage where factual fidelity to the source matters.

- **Code:** [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2)
- **ComfyUI:** [ComfyUI-LTXVideo](https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo/

# LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Layout to Render

This is a **Layout to Render** IC-LoRA trained on top of [LTX-2.5-22B](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5). It turns a 3D viewport animation into a finished shot. Give it a grey clay viewport, or a blocky playblast of simple shapes, from Blender, Unreal, or a similar 3D tool, carrying the camera move and the objects. Give it a first frame that sets the art direction. It returns a video that moves like the layout and looks like that first frame.

It keeps the camera path and the placement of objects from the layout. It is suited to workflows that value that alignment and that precision.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

## Example Outputs

<Gallery />

## Model Files

- `ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-layout-to-render-1.0.safetensors`.
- `LTX-2.5_ICLoRA_Layout_To_Render_Two_Stage_Distilled.json` — the ComfyUI workflow for this model.

## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video, reference-conditioned), rank 128, BF16
- **Control Type:** a 3D viewport animation or playblast supplies the camera, the motion, and where objects sit. It can be a detailed clay render or a blocky animation of simple shapes, from Blender, Unreal, or a similar 3D tool. 
                    A first frame and possibly more additional keyframes supply the art direction and details.
- **Pipeline details:** See Pipeline Details at [ic_lora.py](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2/blob/main/packages/ltx-pipelines/src/ltx_pipelines/ic_lora.py).

## Intended Use

Turn a 3D viewport animation into a finished shot without re-lighting or re-texturing the scene. The layout can be a clay viewport render or a blocky playblast of simple shapes. Use it for look development and camera-accurate shot iteration. It is suited to workflows that value alignment and precision.

## Control Signal Requirements

- **Control signal type:** A 3D viewport animation or playblast, for example from Blender or Unreal. This can be a detailed clay render, or a blocking animation built from simple shapes. A detailed clay render is not required.
- **Expected input:** The driving clip. It supplies the camera and the movement. Prefer 24 fps. Width and height must divide by 64. 1920×1088 is a known good size.
- **Keyframes:** The picture (or pictures) that sets the art direction: palette, lighting, and materials. Take the first frame of the clay animation and give it to any image model to generate the visual you want. Those images go in as keyframes. Do not use the grey clay frame itself.
- **Preprocessing:** Frame count is snapped to 8×k+1. A 72-frame, 3-second, 24 fps clip becomes 65 frames. That trim is part of the recipe.
- **Alignment:** The output keeps the camera and where objects sit, including the motion of simple shapes in a blocking animation.

## How It Works

The layout clip sets the camera, the motion, and the framing, and it keeps objects in place. The image sets palette, lighting, and materials.

A clay viewport render works as the layout. A blocky playblast of simple shapes works too, from Blender, Unreal, or a similar 3D tool, and the model keeps that movement and that camera. A detailed clay render is not required.

The camera path and the placement of objects stay aligned through the shot.

# LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Decompression

This is a **Decompression** IC-LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**, which removes compression artifacts from low bit-rate / heavily-compressed video — macroblocking, chroma bleed, ringing, and banding — while preserving subject identity, framing, and geometry.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

<Gallery />

`ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-decompression-0.9.safetensors` — the single released checkpoint (used for the published inference samples).

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video)
- **Control Type:** Video-to-video — a heavily-compressed, low bit-rate input (reference) video drives a clean, artifact-free output video.

**Intended use:** Improving **low bit-rate / heavily-compressed video** — removing compression artifacts such as macroblocking, chroma bleed, ringing, and banding from low-bitrate sources, restoring sharp detail and clean edges while keeping the original subject and composition.

**Out of scope:** This is **not** a general restoration model. It is specifically not designed for: out-of-focus / defocus blur, motion blur, noise / grain removal, super-resolution / upscaling, or colorization. It targets compression-artifact removal only; content far outside the training distribution may underperform.

- **Control signal type:** Low bit-rate / heavily-compressed source video (visible macroblocking, chroma bleed, ringing).

This is a **Deblur** IC-LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**, which restores sharpness to out-of-focus / defocused video by conditioning on the blurry clip and regenerating it in sharp focus while preserving the original subject, framing, and scene geometry.

This is a **Day-to-Night Relighting** IC-LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**, which re-renders a daytime video as the same shot at night while preserving composition, framing, camera movement, and subject motion frame-for-frame.

# LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Colorization

This is a **Colorization** IC-LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**, which restores natural color to grayscale, monochrome, or desaturated video while keeping subject identity, framing, and geometry untouched — only the color information changes.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

<Gallery />

## Model Files

`ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-colorization-0.9.safetensors` — the single released checkpoint (used for the published inference samples).

## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video)
- **Control Type:** Video-to-video — a grayscale/monochrome input (reference) video drives a color-restored output video.
- **Reference Downscale Factor:** 1 (the reference is encoded at 1× the output resolution).
- **Pipeline details:** No special pre/post color transform — the reference video is VAE-encoded as the control signal and the model predicts the colorized result.

## Intended Use & Out-of-Scope

**Intended use:** Colorizing black-and-white, monochrome, or heavily desaturated footage — restoring plausible, natural color to a clip while preserving the original subject, composition, motion, and background geometry.

**Out of scope:** Any task other than colorization (it is not a deblur, denoise, decompression, or upscaling model); relighting or scene re-composition; and content far outside the training distribution. Generating far above the 960×544 training bucket can weaken the colorization effect.

## Control Signal Requirements

- **Control signal type:** Grayscale / monochrome / desaturated source video.
- **Expected input:** A reference video (`.mp4` / `.mov` / `.mkv` / `.webm` / `.avi`).
- **Preprocessing:** None required — the reference is VAE-encoded directly. The reference is used at 1× the output resolution (downscale factor 1).
- **Alignment:** The output matches the reference frame count, FPS, resolution, and aspect ratio. Best results at the 960×544×121 @ 24fps training bucket

# LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Alpha Gen

This is an **Alpha Gen** IC-LoRA trained on top of **LTX-2.5-22B**. It takes an ordinary RGB ("beauty") video and generates a matching **alpha matte** for it, with no green screen, masks, or prompt required. It handles hard subjects as well as soft and semi-transparent elements such as hair, fur, smoke, fire, sheer fabric, glass, and water.

It is based on the [LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) foundation model.

<Gallery />

## Model Files

`ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-alpha-gen-0.9.safetensors`: the released checkpoint (training step 25000). Recommended inference on the `-distilled` base.

## Model Details

- **Base Model:** LTX-2.5-22B Video
- **Training Type:** IC-LoRA (video-to-video, reference-conditioned)
- **Control Type:** Reference video: the RGB clip to be matted. The model outputs a grayscale alpha matte (white = foreground, black = background) aligned frame-for-frame with the input.
- **Reference Downscale Factor:** 1 (the reference is processed at the same resolution as the output).
- **Prompt:** Always empty. The RGB video is the only guide.

## Intended Use & Out-of-Scope

**Intended use:** Pulling an alpha matte from live-action or generated footage for compositing and VFX: isolating people, animals, objects, logos, and characters so they can be placed over new backgrounds, including shots with soft or semi-transparent edges that are hard to key or rotoscope.

**Out of scope:** Clips longer than **145 frames**: above that, RGB content starts leaking into the matte, so trim or split longer clips. Resolutions above **1920×1088**. Choosing *which* object to matte: there is no prompt or mask control, and the model decides the foreground on its own.

## Control Signal Requirements

- **Control signal type:** The RGB clip to be matted (the "beauty" pass).
- **Expected input:** A single video at up to 1920×1088 and up to 145 frames.
- **Preprocessing:** Pad (don't stretch) the clip to dimensions divisible by 32 and a frame count of `8n+1` (e.g. 1920×1080 → 1920×1088; 145 frames already fits). No extractor or normalization is needed; the RGB clip is VAE-encoded directly.
- **Alignment:** The matte is generated at the same size and length as the reference and is frame-aligned with it.
- **Mask support:** Not supported. The model predicts the foreground for the whole frame.

## How It Works

The IC-LoRA conditions on the latents of the RGB reference video and generates the corresponding alpha matte as a video, with an **empty text prompt**. Because the reference stays attached for the entire denoise (stage-1-only inference at native resolution), the matte stays aligned with the source down to fine edges.

To composite, use the matte as the alpha channel of the **original** RGB clip:

```
out = rgb * alpha + background * (1 - alpha)
```

## Usage

### 🔌 ComfyUI

1. Copy `ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-alpha-gen-0.9.safetensors` into `models/loras`.
2. Load the **LTX-2.5-22B** distilled base model and add the LoRA.
3. Use the [IC-LoRA (video-to-video) workflow](https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo/blob/master/example_workflows/2.5/LTX-2.5_V2V_ICLoRA_Single_Stage_Distilled.json) from the [LTX-2 ComfyUI repository](https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo/). Select this LoRA in the IC-LoRA loader node, connect your RGB clip as the reference video, and **leave the prompt empty**.
4. Use LoRA strength `1.0`.
5. The output video is the alpha matte. Combine it with your original clip as its alpha channel (e.g. in your compositor, or export RGBA / ProRes 4444).

Use the IC-LoRA video-to-video pipeline (`python -m ltx_pipelines.ic_lora`) from [LTX-2](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2) with an empty prompt, `--skip-stage-2`, and `--width`/`--height` set to **2× the source size**, so the stage-1 render comes ba

# LTX-2 19B LoRA - Camera Control (Dolly Right)

This is a camera-motion control **LoRA** trained to bias generations toward a **dolly-right** camera move (camera translates laterally to the right, revealing content on the right side of the scene and changing parallax) on top of an **LTX-2 19B** base video model.

## Model Details

- **Developed by**: Lightricks
- **Base model**: LTX-2 19B
- **Training type**: LoRA finetune for camera motion (dolly right)

## Recommended Prompting

To get the best results with Motion Camera LoRAs, describe the **destination of the movement** and the **hidden parts of the scene** so the model knows what to reveal as the frame shifts.

# Minimax-H3 Singularity V2 (Pruned Safetensors)

Pruned and optimized `.safetensors` versions of [WarmBloodAban/Minimax-H3 Singularity](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity), formatted for native ComfyUI custom nodes (such as `comfyui-mixed-quantizer` and native INT8 loaders).

## 📁 Available Safetensors Files & Sizes

| Filename | File Size | Quantization / Format | Recommended Use Case / Hardware |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_Pruned_int8.safetensors` | **21.0 GB** | **INT8 Backbone** + Lossless Pruned AdaLN | **100% Lossless Quality** (Direct INT8 copy with 13B AdaLN parameters pruned) |
| `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_Pruned_w4a8.safetensors` | **12.5 GB** | **Asym W4A8 INT8** (ComfyUI `asym_w4a8_int8`) | **Low-VRAM Hardware** (Fitted 16-level Lloyd-Max codebook) |

## 🛠️ Engineering & Pruning Details

* **Curve-Pruned AdaLN Architecture:** The 51 unpruned AdaLN modulation modules (`[Out, 2688]`) from the original 34GB checkpoint were projected onto the canonical rank-8 Ref2VA subspace (`adaln_basis` + `adaln_mean`), removing **13.03 Billion parameters** and saving \~13 GB of disk space without affecting motion dynamics.
* **Lossless Precision Guards:** All normalization layers (`RMSNorm`), timestep embeddings (`adaln_t_table`), and modality input/output heads are preserved in **lossless FP32 / BF16**.
* **Regular Hadamard Un-Rotation ($H_4^{\otimes 4}$):** Source ConvRot-256 weights were accurately un-rotated using ComfyUI's exact butterfly transform in `float64` before re-quantization to eliminate color shifts and grid artifacts.
* **LoRA Compatibility:** Fully compatible with the canonical `adaln_affine.safetensors` curve basis, ensuring 100% compatibility with the ComfyUI pruned H3 LoRA and PowerLoRA stack ecosystem.

---

1. Place your chosen `.safetensors` file into your ComfyUI models folder:
   `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/`
2. Load the model using your preferred native ComfyUI loader or mixed-quantizer custom nodes.
3. Pair it with the Qwen3-VL text encoder and MiniMax-H3 Video + Audio VAEs.

# LTX-2.5 22B dev, uncensored text encoder — ROCmFPX GGUF

[Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5) dev for
[stable-diffusion.cpp](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp), with its Gemma 4 12B text encoder
de-censored by the [Heretic](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic) refusal edit. The video transformer is in
`Q4_0_ROCMFP4`, the 4-bit [ROCmFPX](https://github.com/charlie12345/ROCmFPX) format for AMD GPUs; the text encoder
is in a ROCmFPX format. Everything needed besides the VAE is here.

> The diffusion file needs stable-diffusion.cpp built against the ROCmFPX fork of ggml. Stock sd.cpp, ComfyUI-GGUF
> and other runners do not know its type. The patch is in this repo (`sdcpp-rocmfpx.patch`).
>
> Not an official release of Lightricks, Google or the Heretic authors. Use is subject to the LTX-2.x Community
> License Agreement (`LICENSE.txt`, `NOTICE.md`), including its use restrictions (Attachment A); "uncensored" does not
> change them. Commercial Entities with annual revenues of at least USD 10 million need a paid license from
> Lightricks for commercial use.

## What "uncensored" means here

LTX-2.5 reads prompts through Gemma 4 12B. Gemma's refusal behaviour can weaken or partly ignore prompts it would
refuse in a chat. [llmfan46/gemma-4-12B-it-uncensored-heretic](https://huggingface.co/llmfan46/gemma-4-12B-it-uncensored-heretic)
removes that behaviour (6 of 100 refusals instead of 99, KL divergence 0.12) by editing only the attention output
projections of layers 24-39.

- **What it does:** the text encoder no longer steers away from prompts Gemma would refuse.
- **What it does not do:** the video model is unchanged. It cannot generate anything it did not learn in training;
  no NSFW LoRA or fine-tune is merged.
- **Why it is built this way:** Lightricks ships its own tuned copy of Gemma: many of its tensors differ from
  Google's release (the projections edited here by 3-11 %). Dropping in the whole
  Heretic model, as other uncensored LTX encoders do, would throw that tuning away. Here only the Heretic *change*
  (heretic minus Google's original) is added to Lightricks' weights, in FP32, for the 16 edited tensors
  (relative size of the change 1.4-7.0 %); every other tensor, including the LTX
  video and audio projections, is Lightricks' own, bit for bit.
  The script is `build/build_uncensored_te.py`, its per-tensor numbers `build/te_delta_stats.json`.

![Lightricks text encoder vs uncensored, middle frame, same seed](comparison.jpg)

## Measured quality

4 prompts, 768×448, 33 frames, Euler, 20 steps, CFG 3.0, the negative prompt below, same seed per prompt. Every frame is compared with the frame of the same prompt, seed and index from the reference (132 frames per row). PSNR (dB) and SSIM: higher is closer. LPIPS: lower is closer (perceptual distance). Diffusion amplifies small weight changes over the steps, so a quantized model can give a different take of the same prompt (pose, composition) without any loss of quality.

| Compared | Reference | PSNR | SSIM | LPIPS |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Floor of this test: same BF16 DiT and encoder loaded directly | BF16 DiT, Lightricks encoder | 41.1 | 0.988 | 0.015 |
| **Uncensored encoder instead of Lightricks' (both BF16)**, on ordinary prompts | BF16 DiT, Lightricks encoder | 36.3 | 0.982 | 0.021 |
| Floor of the encoder path: uncensored encoder as BF16 GGUF | BF16 DiT, uncensored encoder | 40.8 | 0.987 | 0.014 |
| **This repo:** `LTX-2.5-22B-dev-Q4_0_ROCMFP4.gguf` + `gemma4-12b-heretic-with-proj-ltx-2.5-Q8_0_ROCMFPX.gguf` | BF16 DiT, uncensored encoder | 25.6 | 0.879 | 0.130 |
| For comparison: `LTX-2.5-22B-dev-Q4_0_ROCMFP4.gguf` + Lightricks' BF16 encoder | BF16 DiT, Lightricks encoder | 24.6 | 0.871 | 0.147 |

On ordinary prompts the edit moves the videos a little more than the floor of the test (see the LPIPS column): mostly a different take of the same prom

# Minimax-h3 Singularity ref2va **v2** — pruned int8 (curve form)

A **pruned** build of [WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity)
`Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_int8.safetensors`. That repo ships v2 only in full form (34.0 GB); this is the same
model in the pruned "curve" layout, **21.05 GB**, which loads natively in ComfyUI exactly like the official
`minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot` and the author's own pruned v1.3.

All credit for the model goes to **WarmBloodAban** (fine-tune) and **MiniMax** (MiniMax-H3). This repo only changes the
storage layout of the timestep-modulation path. Licence: Apache-2.0, as the source.

| file | size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_pruned_int8.safetensors` | 21.05 GB | `c75cba0d4a7587166303ac038befc0b4f4aaea16686315cccecc16f9ca0c1519` |
| source: `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_int8.safetensors` | 34.00 GB | `db3ec568863db6f5ec1840210d41653afef73d4df7b0cb489c52ad458b6f8a7f` |

**Use:** put it in `models/diffusion_models/` and pick it in the UNET loader, in place of the full v2. ComfyUI detects the
curve form from the `adaln_t_table` key. Needs a ComfyUI recent enough to load pruned MiniMax-H3 checkpoints.

## What "pruned" means here

Only the timestep path changes; every attention / MLP weight is copied **byte for byte** (200 layers, int8 tensorwise
convrot, group size 256).

| | full v2 | this file |
|---|---|---|
| `time_embedder.*` | present | removed |
| each of 50 `blocks.N.adaln_proj.linear.weight` | `[96768, 2688]` int8 (~260 MB) | `[96768, 8]` fp32 (3 MB) |
| `final_layer.adaln_proj.linear.weight` | `[10752, 2688]` | `[10752, 8]` fp32 |
| `adaln_t_table` | — | `[1025, 8]` fp32 |

The timestep `t` is one number in [0, 1], so what the adaLN layers consume, `silu(time_embedder(t))`, traces a 1-D curve
in 2688-dim space. Sampled on a 1025-point grid, that curve lies **exactly** in an 8-dim subspace (SVD residual energy
0.0 at k = 8). So: table = curve coordinates in that basis, and each adaLN weight is pre-multiplied into the basis
(`W' = W·Vₖᵀ`, `b' = b + W·mean`). ComfyUI interpolates the table at runtime.

## Fidelity

Error of the adaLN output vs the full model's own weights, over the whole 1025-point t grid, relative to the
t-dependent part of the output:

| | blocks (50) | final layer |
|---|---|---|
| this file (v2) | 1.4e-4 – 1.7e-4 | 2.3e-4 |
| same method on v1.3 | 1.9e-4 – 2.0e-4 | 2.7e-4 |
| for reference: the author's pruned v1.3 vs their full v1.3 | 3.5e-2 – 2.0e-1 | 1.5e-2 |

The 8-wide weights are stored in **fp32** deliberately: bf16 storage raises the error to ~2.5e-2.

**Renders.** On a fast 4-step test of a 15 s action sequence (fixed seed), each model is perfectly deterministic. This
file, the full v2, and the full v2 with its adaLN stored bf16 instead of int8 all differ from one another by about the
same amount (17.5–18.1 dB PSNR): the sampler amplifies any change in adaLN numerics, including just int8 vs bf16
storage in the original. A genuinely different model (Singularity v1.3) sits at 12.9 dB. Judge quality by eye, as with
any re-quantisation.

## Reproduce

`curve_prune.py` (+ `curve_prune_io.py`) converts any full-form MiniMax-H3 checkpoint, streaming, CPU only (~2 min for
this file); `curve_check.py` verifies keys/shapes against a reference pruned header and reports per-layer error. Run
with ComfyUI's Python from inside a ComfyUI install (uses `comfy_kitchen` for int8 convrot dequantisation).

```
python -s curve_prune.py Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_int8.safetensors Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_pruned_int8.safetensors
python -s curve_check.py Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_int8.safetensors Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_pruned_int8.safetensors
```

Note: HyperFlow on a pruned base needs a curve refit (ComfyUI-HyperFlow-H3 "Create HyperFlow H3 Curve Fit").

# Model Card for FLUX 3 Image Klein — Apple Core AI, int8 weights / fp16 activations (W8A16)

[`black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) (distilled checkpoint, 16 steps, text-to-image, single- and multi-reference editing) converted to Apple **Core AI** (`.aimodel`) with 8-bit integer weights in blocks of 32 and fp16
activations, for on-device generation on Apple silicon: Qwen3-VL-4B text encoder (up to layer 32), the 5.5B DiT and the VAE, all as assets. Tested on macOS 27.2 (Apple M5, 24 GB) with the Core AI Python runtime; **not tested on iOS**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Licensed under the FLUX Kommunity License v1.0** (non-commercial use, with a commercial exception for Qualifying Users): see `LICENSE.md` and `NOTICE`. **This is a modified version of the FLUX Model** (quantized and re-authored; see "License and Attribution").
> **Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. The upsampler from the same release, converted the same way, is
> [`silv4souz4/flux-3-image-klein-pup-coreai-w8a16`](https://huggingface.co/silv4souz4/flux-3-image-klein-pup-coreai-w8a16) (text, edits with up to 10 references, bounding boxes).

## Model Details

### Model Description

- **Original model developed by:** Black Forest Labs (`black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein`); text encoder Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (Qwen team, Alibaba Cloud, Apache-2.0).
- **Conversion by:** silv4souz4 (independent; not affiliated with or endorsed by Black Forest Labs, Alibaba/Qwen or Apple).
- **Model type:** flow-map distilled diffusion transformer with a VLM text encoder and a convolutional VAE.
- **Relation to base:** quantized (int8 weights) and re-authored for Core AI; same math; no retraining or fine-tuning.
- **Included:** the distilled Klein checkpoint only (not Klein Base); the FP8/NVFP4 variants are not included. Text encoder: the text path only (up to layer 32), no vision tower.
- **License:** FLUX Kommunity License v1.0 for the FLUX Model and this Derivative; the text encoder is Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE_Qwen3-VL.txt`).

### Assets (10.7 GB, flat layout)

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `te_block{0..7}_w8a16.aimodel` (411 MB each; block 1 is `te_block1_w8a16p.aimodel`, 478 MB) | text encoder, 4 layers per asset, one function per text lane (`flux3klein_te_b{b}_l{320,640,1280}_…`); each returns one of the 8 hidden states the DiT consumes |
| `te_embed_int8.npz` (389 MB) | token embedding table, int8 per row + fp16 scale (the host does the gather) |
| `dit_mod_w8a16.aimodel` | time embeddings → all modulations |
| `dit_img_w8a16.aimodel`, `dit_cond_w8a16.aimodel`, `dit_txt_w8a16.aimodel` | the 5 double-mode blocks of the image (1024/4096 tokens), reference (1024/2048/4096) and text (320/640/1280) streams |
| `dit_single{0..6}_w8a16.aimodel` (522 MB each) | the 28 single-stream blocks in groups of 4 (the last one also applies the final layer); 16 functions each: {text-to-image, edit} × image lane × (reference lane) × text lane, same weights |
