# Model Card for FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler — Apple Core AI, int8 weights / fp16 activations (W8A16)

[`black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup) (Qwen3.5-9B fine-tune that expands a short image request into the full caption FLUX 3 Image Klein works best with) converted to Apple **Core AI**
(`.aimodel`) with 8-bit integer weights in blocks of 32 and fp16 activations, **vision tower included**, for on-device use on Apple silicon. One model, four modes selected by the system prompt:
`t2i`, `i2i` (up to 10 reference images), `t2i_bbox`, `i2i_bbox`. Tested on macOS 27.2 (Apple M5, 24 GB) with the Core AI Python runtime; **not tested on iOS**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The context window is **4,096 positions** (K/V ring cache), against 8,192 in the official vLLM setup. The host refuses a request whose prompt plus generation would not fit. With one 1 MP reference
> the prompt is ~1,600 tokens (the `i2i` system prompt alone has 548); ten references use ~3,100. This is the upsampler for [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/silv4souz4/flux-3-image-klein-coreai-w8a16) in Core AI, but it works on its own.

## Model Details

### Model Description

- **Original model developed by:** Black Forest Labs (`black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup`), a full fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B (Qwen team, Alibaba Cloud) with the vision tower frozen.
- **Conversion by:** silv4souz4 (independent; not affiliated with or endorsed by Black Forest Labs, Alibaba/Qwen or Apple).
- **Model type:** vision-language model: 27-layer ViT (patch 16, 2×2 merge, 2D rope) + decoder-only language model, hybrid 24 Gated DeltaNet + 8 full-attention layers; multimodal RoPE (3 axes).
- **Relation to base:** quantized (int8 weights); same math, re-authored for Core AI; no retraining or fine-tuning.
- **Language:** English output; the request can be in any language (inherited).
- **License:** Apache License 2.0, inherited from `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup` and `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`.

### Assets (10.0 GB)

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `pup_block{0..7}_w8a16.aimodel` (921 MB each) | layers 4b..4b+3 = Gated DeltaNet ×3 + attention, each with its MLP; functions `pupklein_b{b}_decode_w8a16_g32` (1 token per call) and `pupklein_b{b}_prefill_w8a16_g32` (64 tokens per call) |
| `pup_head_w8a16.aimodel` (1.08 GB) | final RMSNorm + `lm_head` (4096 → 248,320), function `pupklein_cabeca_w8a16_g32` |
| `pup_vision_w8a16.aimodel` (485 MB) | the ViT: functions `pupklein_visao_n{256,1024,2048,4096}_w8a16_g32` (one per patch-count lane; real patches are a masked prefix) → image tokens `[N/4, 4096]` |
| `pup_embed_int8.npz` (1.02 GB) | token embedding table, int8 per row + fp16 scale (the host does the gather) |
| `pup_vision_pos_embed.npy` | the learned 48×48 position table of the vision tower (fp32), resampled by the host per image |
| `system_prompts.json` | the four system prompts (`t2i`, `i2i`, `t2i_bbox`, `i2i_bbox`), unchanged from `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup` |
| `host/pup_coreai_host.py`, `host/flux3_bbox.py` | self-contained reference host (numpy, Pillow, `tokenizers`, Core AI runtime): reference preprocessing, vision position embedding and 2D rope, mRoPE, masks, states, chat template, sampling; `flux3_bbox.py` is an unmodified copy of the official box helper |
| `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `chat_template.jinja` | unchanged from `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup` |

### Model Sources

- **Original model:** https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup
- **Inference code (reference):** https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein
- **Base model:** https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B

## Uses

### Direct Use

Turning a short request (with optional reference images and bounding boxes) into the detailed caption FLUX 3 Image Klein expects, locally on Apple silicon.

### Out-of-Scope Use

- Use as a general chat or vision-language assistant: the fine-tune is specialised and does not refuse requests (the official inference code wraps it with optional safety checks that are not part of these assets).
- Image models other than FLUX 3 Image Klein (not part of the training).
- Contexts above 4,096 positions.

# FLUX.3 Image Klein on your Mac

**Local image generation and editing with MLX. Five model choices. Download only the one you need.**

![Actual Q8 quality outputs: photography, product composition, typography and reference-image editing](images/release/showcase.jpg)

*Q8 quality, 16 steps. These are existing benchmark outputs, resized for this overview. [Full prompts, seeds, inputs and original PNGs](gallery/README.md).*

An independent Apple Silicon port of Black Forest Labs' distilled [FLUX.3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein), published by [Devin Lai](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai). Includes the inference runtime, ready-to-run weights, exact presets, benchmark data and original comparison images. The image transformer has 5.6B parameters; the text encoder is separate.

**Start with Q8 quality.** On the tested MacBook Pro M5 / 32 GiB, its 16-step preset measured **38.75 s** across four workloads, **7.46 GiB** maximum process footprint, and **4.16×** the speed of the strict MLX FP32 reference. Its 11-step preset measured **29.69 s** in a later round. These are workload aggregates, not promises for every image size or Mac. [Measurement details](reports/macbook-pro-32gb.md).

## Choose your download

This repository holds the runtime, documentation and gallery. Each linked variant repository contains one complete model configuration, including its text encoder, tokenizer, VAE and image-editing components. No other variant is needed.

| Model | Download¹ | Local time² | Peak memory² | Choose it for |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **[Q8 quality](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/flux-3-image-klein-mlx-q8-quality)** | **12.73 GiB** | **38.75 s** | **7.46 GiB** | Recommended balance of fidelity and storage; Q8 transformer + BF16 text |
| [Q8](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/flux-3-image-klein-mlx-q8) | 9.58 GiB | 36.65 s | 7.43 GiB | Smaller download; Q8 transformer + Q8 text |
| [Mixed 4/8-bit](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/flux-3-image-klein-mlx-mixed) | 8.23 GiB | 34.91 s | 6.07 GiB | Lower memory, with larger visual changes |
| [Q4](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/flux-3-image-klein-mlx-q4) | 7.40 GiB | 33.75 s | 5.53 GiB | Smallest download, with stronger fidelity tradeoffs |
| [BF16](https://huggingface.co/devin-lai/flux-3-image-klein-mlx-bf16) | 17.40 GiB | 40.34 s | 12.47 GiB | Unquantized weight control |

¹ Model components and weight licenses; small repository metadata is additional. Download size is different from runtime memory. ² 16 steps on M5/32 GiB; geometric mean of four per-workload median launch times, three fresh-process repeats per case. Peak memory is the maximum process lifetime footprint. Tested canvases range from 640 × 640 to 1024 × 1024 and include one reference-image edit. **A minimum supported Mac memory capacity has not been established.**

Q4 changed object counts in the typography example. Inspect the [image comparisons](gallery/README.md) and [model selection guide](MODEL_SELECTION.md) when choosing a compact model.

## Generate your first image

Use an **Apple Silicon Mac and Python 3.12**, preferably in a fresh virtual environment. Install the small runtime once; the generation command downloads only Q8 quality on its first run.

```sh
python3.12 -m venv .flux-env
source .flux-env/bin/activate
python -m pip install "huggingface_hub>=1,<3"

hf download devin-lai/flux-3-image-klein-mlx \
  --include "flux_klein_mlx/*" --include "pyproject.toml" \
  --include "LICENSE-runtime.txt" --include "examples/*" \
  --local-dir flux-klein-runtime
python -m pip install "./flux-klein-runtime[hub]"

flux-klein --download q8-quality --model-dir ./flux-models/q8-quality \
  --preset q8-quality-16 --prompt-file ./flux-klein-runtime/examples/teapot.json \
  --width 768 --height 512 --seed 1937 --out ./flux-output/teapot.png
```

After downloading, omit `--download` to run locally. Use `--preset q8-quality-11` for the faster tested preset, or `--download q8 --model-dir ./flux-models/q8 --preset q8-16` for the smaller Q8 package. Use a separate directory for each variant.

For editing, add `--image /path/to/reference.png` and supply a full scene caption describing the desired result. This CLI sends captions as provided; it does not run a prompt upsampler or bundle content filtering. Review generated outputs before sharing and follow the [upstream license](LICENSE.md). [Installation, offline use and editing guide](USAGE.md).

## Limitations and provenance

Quantization and accelerated arithmetic can change outputs. Inspect the matched comparison images; similarity to a reference is not an aesthetic quality rating.

This release repacks/quantizes existing weights; it adds no pretraining or fine-tuning dataset. # ImageWAM FLUX.2 C-Pred — LIBERO, epoch 5

Complete inference weights and the corresponding source snapshot for the five-epoch
state-free-visual C-Pred experiment. Checkpoint **epoch 5 / step 10850**.

This is the native **Gaussian flow-matching** experiment, not an I2I/A2A Delta-flow
checkpoint. The visual branch receives current images and pure instruction tokens,
with **no numerical state input**. A pose head predicts current state from shared
visual features. Its detached prediction conditions the action expert through an
additive hidden projection. Action gradients through visual KV remain enabled.

## Downloads

- [Epoch-five inference weights](weights/epoch_005.pt) — 9,085,602,105 bytes.
- [Code, configuration, text caches and inference instructions ZIP](imagewam_flux2_cpred_epoch005_code.zip) — excludes weights and external base models.
- [Inference instructions](INFERENCE.md) and [portable evaluation launcher](run_libero_eval.py).
- [Verified evaluation scores](results/metrics.json) and [file checksums](manifest.json).

The checkpoint contains the complete trained MoT and pose head. It contains **no
optimizer state, training RNG state or training dataset**. The external FLUX.2 base
transformer and autoencoder are still required by the unmodified native constructor;
they are not redistributed here. The 40 bundled Qwen caches are pure instruction
embeddings for standard LIBERO, not numerical state tokens.

Download the full repository with `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download`, or unpack
the code ZIP and separately place the checkpoint at `weights/epoch_005.pt`.
Follow [INFERENCE.md](INFERENCE.md) for external assets and the actual runtime
versions; the archived upstream `pyproject.toml` does not describe this environment
exactly. This is a native PyTorch checkpoint, not an `AutoModel.from_pretrained` model.

## LIBERO

Final checkpoint, predicted state, 40 tasks × 25 trials = **1,000 rollouts**.

| Suite | Successes / rollouts | Success rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Spatial | 237 / 250 | 94.80% |
| Object | 243 / 250 | 97.20% |
| Goal | 239 / 250 | 95.60% |
| Long | 209 / 250 | 83.60% |
| Overall | 928 / 1000 | **92.80%** |

## LIBERO-Plus

The same final checkpoint, predicted state, **10,030 benchmark instances**, one
rollout per instance with benchmark initial-state index 0.

| Perturbation | Successes / rollouts | Success rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Camera viewpoints | 847 / 1599 | 52.97% |
| Robot initial states | 712 / 1550 | 45.94% |
| Language instructions | 1014 / 1537 | 65.97% |
| Lighting | 840 / 1142 | 73.56% |
| Background textures | 752 / 1076 | 69.89% |
| Sensor noise | 1114 / 1601 | 69.58% |
| Object layouts | 1040 / 1525 | 68.20% |
| Overall | 6319 / 10030 | **63.00%** |

These are actual completed rollouts, not extrapolated from a subset. The bundled
launcher is for **standard LIBERO**, not LIBERO-Plus. The latter also needs its own
benchmark checkout, full instance list and instruction caches; the 40 base-task
caches alone do not reproduce this score.

## Training and inference protocol

- Five completed epochs, 10,850 optimizer updates, seed 42.
- Eight GPUs, microbatch 8 per GPU, gradient accumulation 2, global batch 128.
- Learning rate 1e-4; original 21,700-update schedule and 1,085 warmup updates
  retained. Training stopped after five epochs, not after completing that schedule.
- Visual FM weight 0.5, action FM weight 1.0, pose loss weight 1.0.
- Native Gaussian sources; I2I, A2A and endpoint-consistency losses disabled.
- Two 224×224 camera images concatenated to 224×448; context length 128.
- Ten solver updates, predict 16 local-delta 7D actions and execute 12 per replan.
- Thirty initial no-op control steps, control limits 400 for Spatial/Object/Goal
  and 700 for Long; per-call source-noise reseeding enabled.

The separate inference-time GT-state substitution is not the configuration in the
tables above and is not an independently retrained baseline. No matched baseline
was trained for this pilot, so these numbers do not establish a causal gain from
C-Pred alone. The release has not been validated on a physical robot.

## Provenance and licenses

Checkpoint SHA-256:
`e6b438a4760e3cb6a18d4a5cc874a1636d6996aa0375c4af9cd614e1e28c8f60`.

The original ImageWAM source license and copyright are preserved at
[code/LICENSE](code/LICENSE) (MIT, including its third-party exception). This source
license is not a claim that every upstream pretrained asset has the same license.
External FLUX.2, Qwen and LIBERO assets remain subject to their respective upstream
terms; they are not included in the code ZIP. Source files and configuration are
recorded in `manifest.json` with file hashes. The original training YAML contains
archived machine paths; use the portable launcher to set local inference paths.

  --prompt "A puffin standing on a cliff" \
  --width 1024 \
  --height 1024 \
  --seed 42 \

```bash

# FLUX.3 Image Klein — EntroPack Pre-Quantized Models

We provide pre-quantized weight packages produced by [**EntroPack**](https://github.com/modelscope/entropack) for **FLUX.3 Image Klein** ([black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein)), which can be used with the quantization features of [**DiffSynth-Studio**](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio).

Both the **DiT** and the **text encoder** are provided at three compression rates (3 / 4 / 6 bit), and the DiT additionally ships **FP8 GEMM** variants:

* **`3bit`** (lowest VRAM) — mixed-bit: the most sensitive layers (embeddings, time / modulation and final layers, 15 layers) keep **4.0 bpp**, while the remaining 258 layers use **2.9482 bpp** (weighted target 3.0 bpp);
* **`4bit`** (balanced) — uniform entropy coding at 4 bits per weight;
* **`6bit`** (highest precision) — uniform entropy coding at 6 bits per weight; the accuracy is close to FP8 quantization;
* **`fp8_3bit`** / **`fp8_4bit`** / **`fp8_6bit`** (DiT only) — weights are first **FP8 W8A8-quantized**, then entropy-coded by EntroPack down to 3 / 4 / 6-bit storage; the forward pass uses **FP8 GEMM** for faster inference.

All packages are entropy-coded from the original BF16 weights directly. Every `*.safetensors` ships with a same-named `*.json` that records its quantization config. `actual bpp = 8 × Σ storage bytes / Σ numel` is measured on the package artifacts.

## DiT

| name | file | actual bpp | size | preview |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dit_3bit (mixed-bit) | `models/dit_3bit.safetensors` | 3.021 | 2.10 GB | ![](assets/dit_3bit.jpg) |
| dit_4bit | `models/dit_4bit.safetensors` | 4.024 | 2.79 GB | ![](assets/dit_4bit.jpg) |
| dit_6bit | `models/dit_6bit.safetensors` | 6.053 | 4.20 GB | ![](assets/dit_6bit.jpg) |
| dit_fp8_3bit (FP8 GEMM, mixed-bit) | `models/dit_fp8_3bit.safetensors` | 3.030 | 2.10 GB | ![](assets/dit_fp8_3bit.jpg) |
| dit_fp8_4bit (FP8 GEMM) | `models/dit_fp8_4bit.safetensors` | 4.032 | 2.80 GB | ![](assets/dit_fp8_4bit.jpg) |
| dit_fp8_6bit (FP8 GEMM) | `models/dit_fp8_6bit.safetensors` | 6.049 | 4.20 GB | ![](assets/dit_fp8_6bit.jpg) |

## Text Encoder

| name | file | actual bpp | size |
|---|---|---|---|
| text_encoder_3bit | `models/text_encoder_3bit.safetensors` | 3.023 | 2.46 GB |
| text_encoder_4bit | `models/text_encoder_4bit.safetensors` | 4.027 | 3.02 GB |
| text_encoder_6bit | `models/text_encoder_6bit.safetensors` | 6.058 | 4.14 GB |

## Usage

### Install

```bash
# DiffSynth-Studio
git clone https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio.git
cd DiffSynth-Studio && pip install -e .

# EntroPack (pick the extra matching your CUDA version: cuda13 / cuda12)
git clone https://github.com/modelscope/entropack.git
cd entropack && pip install -e '.[cuda13]'
```

### Example scripts

* Inference: [standard](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio/blob/main/examples/flux3/model_inference/flux-3-image-klein-EntroPack.py) / [low VRAM](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio/blob/main/examples/flux3/model_inference_low_vram/flux-3-image-klein-EntroPack.py)
* LoRA training: [train](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio/blob/main/examples/flux3/model_training/lora/flux-3-image-klein-entropack.sh) / [validation](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio/blob/main/examples/flux3/model_training/validate_lora/flux-3-image-klein-entropack.py)

`dit_package` and `text_encoder_package` are chosen independently: any combination works (e.g. `dit_fp8_6bit` with `text_encoder_4bit`). `dit_4bit` and `text_encoder_4bit` are pre-registered in DiffSynth-Studio, so they load with a plain `ModelConfig`; the helper below registers any package's json sidecar before loading:

```python
import json

from diffsynth.configs import MODEL_CONFIGS
from diffsynth.pipelines.flux3_image import Flux3ImagePipeline, ModelConfig

prequant_model_id = "DiffSynth-Studio/flux-3-image-klein-entropack"
dit_package = "models/dit_4bit.safetensors"
text_encoder_package = "models/text_encoder_4bit.safetensors"


def make_package(pattern):
    package = ModelConfig(model_id=prequant_model_id, origin_file_pattern=pattern)
    package.download_if_necessary()
    sidecar = ModelConfig(model_id=prequant_model_id, origin_file_pattern=pattern.replace(".safetensors", ".json"))
    sidecar.download_if_necessary()
    with open(sidecar.path) as handle:
        entry = json.load(handle)
    if not any(config.get("model_hash") == entry["model_hash"] for config in MODEL_CONFIGS):
        MODEL_CONFIGS.append(entry)
    return package


pipe = Flux3ImagePipeline.from_pretrained(
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device="cuda",
    model_configs=[
        make_package(dit_package),
        make_package(text_encoder_package),
        ModelConfig(model_id="black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein", origin_file_pattern="vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors"),
    ],
    processor_config=ModelConfig(model_id="black-forest-labs/flux-3

# FLUX 3 Image Klein, mflux 4bit

An Osaurus 4bit [mflux](https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux) quantization of
[FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) for Apple Silicon (5.0 GB, smallest).
This is not an official Black Forest Labs release and is not endorsed, approved or validated by Black Forest Labs.

FLUX 3 Image Klein is the 16-step distilled model: a 5.6B-parameter transformer with a Qwen3-VL-4B text encoder. One
bundle does **text-to-image** and **reference editing** (one to ten reference images). It also reads bounding boxes
in the prompt and renders text inside images.

## Variants

| bundle | size | 1024² generation (16 steps) | 1024² edit (1 reference) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8bit | 9.2 GB | 44.8 s | 89.7 s |
| 6bit | 7.1 GB | 42.9 s | 102.7 s |
| 4bit | 5.0 GB | 40.8 s | 82.2 s |

Times are end to end, including the model load, on an Apple M5 Max (mflux).

## Changes from the original (attribution notice: modified)
- Transformer and text-encoder linear layers re-saved with mflux and quantized to MLX affine 4-bit, group size 64.
  Norms, modulation, embeddings and biases are kept in bf16.
- The VAE is kept in bf16 except its 8 mid-block attention projections, which use the same 4-bit quantization.
- The text encoder holds the 32 Qwen3-VL language layers the model reads (it takes text features from layers 4 to 32);
  reference images are encoded by the VAE, so the vision tower is not included.
- No fine-tuning or other change.

## Prompting
Write full scene captions: framing, subject, background, lighting. For edits, describe the whole target image with
the change folded in. 16 steps, no guidance. Width and height must be multiples of 16.

# Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-INT8

An INT8 conversion of **Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo** for LightX2V's `int8-metal` backend on Apple M5 or M6. It supports text-to-image generation and image editing with the Turbo model's 8-step sampling schedule.

This directory contains the complete model. Set LightX2V's `model_path` to this directory; a separate copy of the original BF16 model is not required. Quantization applies only to selected DiT Linear weights. The text encoder, VAE, and other components retain their original contents.

## `apple_silicon_metal/`

**This folder provides the precompiled GPU kernels required by LightX2V's `int8-metal` backend.** Keep it alongside the model when deploying on Apple M5 or M6.

Kernel source code is available in [LightX2V / lightx2v_kernel / apple](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/tree/main/lightx2v_kernel/apple).

```text
apple_silicon_metal/
├── int8_k4096_n4096.metallib
├── int8_k4096_n12288.metallib
└── int8_k12288_n4096.metallib
```

These files contain the Metal kernels for online activation quantization and INT8 matrix multiplication. The kernels take BF16 activations, quantize them to INT8 per token, multiply them by the INT8 weights, and produce BF16 output after applying the activation and weight scales.

Model weights and scales are stored separately under `transformer/`. The `.metallib` files contain GPU code and do not contain model weights.

### What each file covers

For `X[M,K] @ W[K,N]`, K is the input feature dimension, N is the output feature dimension, and M is the number of activation rows.

| Library | K | N | DiT Linear layers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `int8_k4096_n4096.metallib` | 4096 | 4096 | Attention Q, K, V, and output projections |
| `int8_k4096_n12288.metallib` | 4096 | 12288 | MLP up and gate projections |
| `int8_k12288_n4096.metallib` | 12288 | 4096 | MLP down projection |

All three libraries are required to cover this model's quantized DiT layers. Each library is shared across Transformer blocks with the same `(K,N)` dimensions.

**M remains dynamic.** Different image resolutions change the activation row count M without changing the layer dimensions K and N, so a new library is not needed for each resolution.

## Usage with LightX2V

### Requirements

- Apple M5 or M6 with PyTorch MPS enabled.
- macOS 26.4 or later. The included `.metallib` files target a minimum deployment version of 26.4.
- Python 3.10 or later and PyTorch 2.14 or later, with `torch.mps.load_metallib` available.
- LightX2V code containing the `int8-metal` backend, Qwen-Image-2.1 MPS configuration, and launch scripts.

Clone LightX2V and enter the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V.git
cd LightX2V
```

Install LightX2V's inference dependencies according to its project instructions. Then install the Apple kernel package from the **LightX2V repository root**, using the same Python environment:

```bash
pip install ./lightx2v_kernel/apple
```

Before running either script below, update `lightx2v_path` and `model_path` in the script to your local paths. Adjust `--prompt` and, for image editing, `--image_path` as needed.

### Text-to-image

```bash
bash scripts/platforms/mps/qwen_image_21_turbo_t2i_int8.sh
```

### Image editing

```bash
bash scripts/platforms/mps/qwen_image_21_turbo_i2i_int8.sh
```

## Rebuilding the Metal libraries

The included libraries have been validated on Apple M5. Other chip and OS combinations require separate validation. To rebuild the libraries, install the Metal Toolchain and run this command from the LightX2V repository root:

```bash
python lightx2v_kernel/apple/python/lightx2v_kernel_apple/int8_gemm/compile_metallib.py \
    4096x4096 4096x12288 12288x4096 \
    --output-dir /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo-INT8/apple_silicon_metal
```

# FLUX 3 Image Klein

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

![Teaser](./teaser.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the distilled checkpoint for generation and image editing. For fine-tuning, LoRA training and research, use [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, [flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup), which the reference code loads by default, or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours). Diffusers runs neither on its own; see [Prompt upsampling](#prompt-upsampling).

This repository includes the BF16 transformer and [FP8](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/fp8r) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/nvfp4) variants, together with the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder and image autoencoder.

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

## Download

Download the root BF16 distilled package, including its text encoder and image autoencoder, without downloading the quantized variants:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

snapshot_download(
    repo_id="black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein",
    local_dir="weights/flux-3-image-klein",
    allow_patterns=[
        "model.safetensors", "config.json", "manifest.json",

# FLUX 3 Image Klein Base

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

![Teaser](./teaser.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the undistilled base checkpoint, for fine-tuning, LoRA training and research. You can find the distilled checkpoint here: [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, [flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup), which the reference code loads by default, or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours). Diffusers runs neither on its own; see [Prompt upsampling](#prompt-upsampling).

This repository includes the BF16 transformer and [FP8](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base/tree/main/variants/fp8r) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base/tree/main/variants/nvfp4) variants, together with the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder and image autoencoder.

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

)

# FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler SDNQ INT8

| bf16 | INT8 |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![bf16](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OzzyGT/diffusers-examples/resolve/main/flux3_image_klein/pup_bf16_s7.png) | ![INT8](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OzzyGT/diffusers-examples/resolve/main/flux3_image_klein/pup_int8_s7.png) |

*Left: original bf16 upsampler · Right: this INT8 upsampler (same request and seed, both generated with the bf16 FLUX 3 Image Klein).*

This is a dynamic 8-bit quantized version of [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup), the prompt upsampler of FLUX 3 Image Klein, using [SDNQ](https://github.com/Disty0/sdnq). The language model, the vision tower and the token embeddings are quantized; `lm_head` stays in bf16.

Note: You need SDNQ v0.2.8 or superior and a diffusers version with the FLUX 3 prompt upsampler block.

## Usage

You can find ready-to-use scripts in the [diffusers-recipes](https://github.com/asomoza/diffusers-recipes/blob/main/models/flux3_image_klein/README.md) repository. For 16 GB GPUs and up, use [sdnq_prompt_upsampler_model_cpu_offload.py](https://github.com/asomoza/diffusers-recipes/blob/main/models/flux3_image_klein/scripts/sdnq_prompt_upsampler_model_cpu_offload.py); for 12 GB GPUs, use [sdnq_prompt_upsampler_two_stage.py](https://github.com/asomoza/diffusers-recipes/blob/main/models/flux3_image_klein/scripts/sdnq_prompt_upsampler_two_stage.py), which writes the caption first and then generates the image.

The upsampler replaces the `prompt_upsampler` component of the FLUX 3 Image Klein pipeline. Import `sdnq` before loading so the quantized weights are registered. Decoding is slower than with the bf16 upsampler (about 22 vs 70 tokens/s on an RTX 5090).

For the system prompts, layout boxes and image editing, see the [original model card](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup).

## Sample image

The INT8 image above was generated with the following request and settings (seed `7`):

```python
import sdnq  # noqa: F401
import torch
from diffusers import ModularPipeline
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration


upsampler_id = "OzzyGT/Flux_3_Image_Klein_pup_sdnq_dynamic_8bit"

pipe = ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein")
pipe.update_components(
    prompt_upsampler=Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(upsampler_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
    prompt_upsampler_processor=AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(upsampler_id),
)
pipe.load_components(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
pipe.to("cuda")

prompt = "A small neighborhood pet shop: a tabby cat on the counter, a golden retriever in a wicker basket and a scarlet macaw perched above an aquarium. The sign over the door reads WHISKERS & WAGS."

output = pipe(
    prompt=prompt,
    height=1152,
    width=2048,
    generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(7),
    output=["images", "prompt"],
)
print(output["prompt"])  # the caption written by the upsampler
output["images"][0].save("flux3_klein_pup_int8.png")
```

# Camera Motion LoRA — 使用指南
---
重新收集素材专门为训练运镜的LORA，稍微弥补MINIMAX H3模型的一些缺失的运镜方式。

## 一、触发词（必须）

```
camera motion
```

**必须放在 prompt 开头**。它是激活本 LoRA 运镜控制能力的开关，后面接具体运镜 + 场景。

## 二、文件版本

| 1000步文件 | 3000步文件 |
|---|---|
| `camera_motion_h3_lora_v1_1000_pruned.safetensors` | `camera_motion_h3_lora_v1_3000_pruned.safetensors` |


## 三、安装与加载

1. `_pruned` 文件放入 ComfyUI `models/loras/`
2. **LoraLoader** 加载，`strength_model` 建议 **0.8 ~ 1.0**
   - 0.8 运镜温和；1.0 运镜明确；>1.2 可能画面不稳
3. 底膜用 MiniMax-H3 视频工作流（pruned + int8 + convrot 版本）

## 四、提示词用法（核心）

### 素材提示词结构

训练素材的标注格式（也是本 LoRA 最匹配的写法）：

```
camera motion, [主体], [场景], [运镜描述], [光线/风格], [画质]
```

### 直接使用素材提示词（推荐）

`camera_motion_提示词库.md` 里有 **55 条从训练素材原样提取的完整提示词**，
按 9 类运镜组织（推近/拉远/推拉结合/环绕/跟拍/航拍/升降/摇镜/微距），
**直接复制粘贴即可**，效果与训练数据最接近。例如：

```
camera motion, a woman and a man in athletic wear, engaged in a dynamic rooftop martial arts fight with punches and defensive blocks, nighttime urban cityscape background, slow push-in to medium shot transitioning to slight pull-back as the woman falls, cinematic teal-orange grading, water droplet effects, sharp 4k, high production quality
```

### 换场景，保留运镜

把素材提示词里的 `[主体], [场景]` 换成你的内容，**保留逗号后面的运镜短语**：

```
camera motion, [你的主体], [你的场景], slow push-in with subtle lateral tracking, cinematic color grading, 4k, high quality
```

### 换运镜，保留场景

只替换运镜短语（如 `slow push-in` → `slow orbit`），其余不动。

### 完整示例（不同类型，直接可用）

**① 推近 Push-in（武术/夜景）**
```
camera motion, a woman and a man in athletic wear, engaged in a dynamic rooftop martial arts fight with punches and defensive blocks, nighttime urban cityscape background, slow push-in to medium shot transitioning to slight pull-back as the woman falls, cinematic teal-orange grading, water droplet effects, sharp 4k, high production quality
```

**② 拉远 Pull-back（工业/体积光）**
```
camera motion, two men in a dynamic martial arts fight, exchanging kicks and punches with defensive blocks and dodges, inside a vast abandoned industrial warehouse with crumbling pillars and dramatic shafts of sunlight, slow pull-back combined with gentle orbit around the fighters revealing the full scale of the environment, cinematic gritty texture, natural volumetric lighting, high production quality
```

**③ 环绕 Orbit（古风/雪景）**
```
camera motion, two martial artists in white and dark robes, dueling with sword and fan atop a snow-covered pavilion surrounded by swirling vortex energy, misty mountain landscape with weeping willow, dynamic pull-back from close-up vortex to wide establishing shot revealing the full rooftop confrontation, cinematic wuxia fantasy style, ethereal atmospheric lighting, 4k, high quality
```

**④ 手持跟拍 Handheld（动作/雨夜霓虹）**
```
camera motion, a man and woman in athletic wear, engaged in intense martial arts combat with punches kicks and takedowns, nighttime rooftop with wet pavement reflecting neon city skyline, dynamic handheld camera with push-in and slight tracking following action, cinematic teal-orange color grading, sharp 4k, high quality
```

**⑤ 航拍 Aerial（自然/山川）**
```
camera motion, majestic green mountain peaks and misty valleys, aerial drone descending over cloud-wrapped ridges, low-angle water-level shot of splashing stream, two hikers crossing stone bridge, mountain forest with flowing creek, slow aerial push-in, water-level tracking, static wide, cinematic natural lighting, 4k, high quality
```

**⑥ 微缩造景（微距/桌面 diorama）**
```
camera motion, a miniature seasonal village diorama on a desk, transforming through autumn, winter, and spring with changing foliage and weather effects, office desk environment with computer monitor and stationery, slow push-in dolly glide across the diorama surface revealing each season transition, whimsical miniature aesthetic, soft natural lighting, 4k, high quality
```

# LTX-2.5 22B — quantised for a 16 GB card

LTX-2.5 generates picture and sound in one pass. It is also 42 GB of bf16
weights, and the text encoder beside it is another 26 GB. This repo is the set
of weights that make it run on a card that does not have that.

Two families, because ComfyUI has two loaders and people are split across them:

- **`.gguf`** — for **ComfyUI-GGUF** (city96). The familiar Q-ladder.
- **`comfy-*.safetensors`** — for **stock ComfyUI 0.32+**, no custom nodes. These
  use ComfyUI's own quantisation system (`comfy_quant` + the comfy-kitchen
  kernels), the same machinery Lightricks' official `int8-convrot` build uses.
  The 4-bit ones are the smallest way to run this model without a custom node in
  the graph.

## What fits

Sizes are measured, not estimated. "Fits 16 GB" assumes the text encoder is not
resident at the same time — ComfyUI frees it before sampling — and tiled VAE
decode. File sizes are decimal GB (bytes / 10^9); card capacities are the usual
binary GiB, so a 15.9 GB file occupies 14.8 GiB of a 16 GiB card. The gap is
real and it is where your activation pool lives.

| file | GB | 12 GB | 16 GB | 24 GB |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| `LTX25-distilled-DiT-comfy-w4a4.safetensors` | 11.2 | tight | **yes** | yes |
| `LTX25-distilled-DiT-comfy-w4a8.safetensors` | 12.5 | — | **yes** | yes |
| `LTX25-distilled-DiT-Q2_K.gguf` | 7.9 | **yes** | yes | yes |
| `LTX25-distilled-DiT-Q3_K_M.gguf` | 10.6 | tight | **yes** | yes |

which on a 16 GB card means the encoder alone owns the machine for the one step
that just makes an embedding. **No GGUF of the LTX-2.5 encoder exists** —
ComfyUI-GGUF gates text encoders on `TXT_ARCH_LIST`, which carries `gemma3` but
not `gemma4`, so LTX-2.3's gemma3 encoder does have GGUFs and this one cannot.
The open request ([#450](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF/issues/450),
2026-05-28) has not been picked up — but comfy-native quantisations of it do exist and landed the
same day as ours (Winnougan's w4a8-convrot at 10.6 GB, DmitryDB's nvfp4 at 11.2,
vonkaiser's nvfp4-torchao at 8.9). Ours is w4a8 at 10.60 GB, within 2 MB of
Winnougan's — the same format at the same size, published independently. Treat it
as a mirror, not a first.

2. `gemma4-12b-ltx25-comfy-w4a8.safetensors` for the text encoder

   (1.5 GB and 0.4 GB; quantising them is not worth what it costs, see below)
4. tiled VAE decode: `tile_size` 512, `temporal_size` 32
5. the distilled schedule: 9 steps then 4, `video_cfg` and `audio_cfg` at 1.0

Every quant is cut from Lightricks' bf16 originals, never from another quant.

**GGUF.** An F16 master with `general.architecture = "ltxv"` and the
`model.diffusion_model.` prefix stripped, then `llama-quantize`. Two findings
worth writing down:

- **K-quants are legal on essentially the whole model.** 4041 of 4349 tensors
  have a last dimension divisible by 256. Of the 308 that do not, 306 are bias
  vectors that stay F16 like every other bias — 304 gate-logit biases of length
  32, plus `proj_out.bias` and `audio_proj_out.bias` at length 128 — and
  **two are real weight matrices**: `patchify_proj.weight` and
  `audio_patchify_proj.weight`, whose 128-wide axis cannot take a K-quant. Those
  two fall back to F16, which is what you want anyway since they are the input
  projections. (MiniMax-H3, for comparison, cannot K-quant at all: its 2688-wide
  tensors rule it out everywhere.)
- **IQ-quants are not.** `llama-quantize` refuses them for this class of file:
  `failed to quantize: Invalid quantization type for image model (Not supported)`.

# FLUX 3 Image Klein, 4-bit and 8-bit export for SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML

**This is a modified (quantised) copy of [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein). It is not an official Black Forest Labs release and BFL has not endorsed or validated it.
It is licensed to you by Black Forest Labs under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md): non-commercial use, or use of outputs as a Qualifying User. Read `LICENSE.md` and `NOTICE` before using it.**

The weights are repacked so the model fits in a browser tab and runs on the [SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML](https://github.com/LostBeard/SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML) engine (C# kernels compiled to WebGPU, CUDA and OpenCL; no PyTorch, no ONNX Runtime).
Large matrices are quantised to 4-bit (or, in the q8 files, 8-bit) blocks; nothing else about the model is changed. All credit for the model goes to Black Forest Labs.

| file | what | size |
|---|---|---|
| `text_encoder_q4.safetensors` | the text tower of Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, first 32 of 36 layers (the model reads hidden states 4, 8, ... 32) + embeddings | 2.26 GB |
| `transformer_q4.safetensors` | the 5.6B flow-map transformer | 3.47 GB |
| `text_encoder_q8.safetensors`, `transformer_q8.safetensors` | the same stages in 8-bit blocks (near lossless; for desktop GPUs) | 4.07 GB + 6.24 GB |
| `vae_decoder.onnx` | the autoencoder's decoder (post_quant_conv + decoder), fp32, dynamic spatial size | 199 MB |
| `vae_encoder.onnx` | the autoencoder's encoder (encoder + quant_conv, mean), for reference images | 138 MB |
| `vae_norm.json` | the 128-channel batch-norm statistics applied to the packed latents | |
| `tokenizer.json` | the Qwen tokenizer | |

Quantisation format: every weight matrix `[N, K]` with `K % 32 == 0` and at least a million elements is cut along `K` into blocks of 32 and stored as `int32` words `[N, K/32*5]` (q4) or `[N, K/32*9]` (q8):
word 0 = fp16 scale `d` (low half) and fp16 offset `m` (high half), then 4 words of 8 nibbles (q4) or 8 words of 4 bytes (q8); value = `d * q + m`. Norm weights and small tensors stay bf16.
`tools/unirig-harness/reference/flux3/` in the engine's repo has the scripts that wrote these files (`quantize_flux3.py`, `quantize_flux3_text.py`, `export_flux3_vae.py`).

## Use

```csharp
var pipe = await Flux3Pipeline.CreateAsync(accelerator, modelSource, "LostBeard/flux-3-image-klein-q4-ILGPU");
var image = await pipe.RunAsync(new Flux3Request { Caption = fullSceneCaption, Seed = 1, Width = 1024, Height = 1024 });
```

FLUX 3 Image Klein is trained on full scene captions: a short prompt gives generic pictures. Write the caption (or have an LLM expand your prompt with BFL's system prompts) before you draw.
Text to image, 16 steps; checked against the reference implementation (bf16, same prompt and start noise, 512 px): the q8 files give the same picture at 31.9 dB PSNR, the q4 files the same scene with small differences in detail at 23.2 dB (about 8% relative error per 4-bit matrix).

Live demo: https://lostbeard.github.io/SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML/generate

# LTX-2.5, FP8 — radiance container

[LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers) — video with a synchronized stereo
soundtrack from text, or from text and a first frame — as a single `.rad` container for the
[radiance](https://codeberg.org/StillDeadcode/radiance) inference engine (AMD RDNA4, ROCm).

This is not an official Lightricks release and is not endorsed by Lightricks.

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `ltx-2.5-fp8.rad` — 36.73 GiB |
| Weights | the Gemma 4 text encoder's, the text connectors' and the diffusion transformer's linears FP8 E4M3 per 128×128 block (bf16 scales); the vocoders f32; everything else (the video and audio VAEs, the latent upsampler, the duration head, the diffusion decoder, the small linears and norms) as released, bf16 |
| Steps | 30 by default (`num_inference_steps`, up to 64), each up to four evaluations of the DiT (classifier-free, spatio-temporal and modality guidance; the defaults are the release's: video 3, 1, 3 with rescale 0.7, audio 7, 1, 3 with rescale 0.7) |
| Needs | radiance built from main after 1.8.1 — LTX-2.5 support is not in 1.8.1 and comes with the next release |

## Serve

```sh
radiance --model ltx-2.5-fp8.rad --vision-tower-placement ram
```

LTX-2.5 runs on one card (`--tp` above 1 is refused). The text encoder (13 GiB in FP8) does not fit a
32 GB card beside the DiT: `--vision-tower-placement ram` keeps it in pinned host memory, read once a
prompt.

The server speaks OpenAI's video API: `POST /v1/videos` queues a job (JSON, or multipart as OpenAI's SDKs
send it), `GET /v1/videos/{id}` reports its progress and `GET /v1/videos/{id}/content` downloads the MP4
(H.264 and 48 kHz stereo AAC).

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/videos -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "prompt": "A red fox trots through fresh snow at golden hour, snow crunching under its paws",
  "size": "960x544", "seed": 7}'
```

- **`seconds`**: rounded up to steps of 8 frames at 24 a second, 17 to 161 frames. Left out (or `"auto"`),
  the release's duration head chooses the length the prompt implies, as diffusers does when `num_frames`
  is omitted.
- **`size`**: sides multiples of 32 from 256, at most 1920x1088 of area (121 frames at that size), at most
  3:1; 960x544 by default. A frame larger than 960x544 is decoded in diffusers' VAE tiles.
- **`input_reference`**: a first frame (image to video), resized to `size` and put through H.264 at CRF 18
  first, as the release was trained.
- **`decoder`**: `"vae"` (the default) or `"diffusion"`, the release's diffusion decoder: neighbourhood-attention
  stages that upsample the latent, then one diffusion step over pixel patches, a tile at a time with
  diffusers' tiling. Frames up to 960x544 of area (a larger `size` is refused with it). Its weights stay in host memory with `--vision-tower-placement ram`.
- **Guidance**: `negative_prompt` (empty by default), `guidance_scale`, `stg_scale`, `modality_scale`, `guidance_rescale`, and the same prefixed `audio_` for the soundtrack. A scale of 1 (0 for `stg_scale`) drops that evaluation.

On one Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201) at the default 30 guided steps: 3 seconds (73 frames) at 768x512 in about 112 s, 5 seconds (121 frames) at 960x544 in about 262 s. `"decoder": "diffusion"` adds about 22 s at 960x544 (121 frames) over the VAE's 2.

The model was trained on long, single-paragraph captions describing the shot, the motion, the light and
the sound; short prompts give generic results.

## How this file was made

The full DiT is `transformer_full/` of the diffusers download, read as the pipeline's transformer, with the scheduler's shifting turned back on as the release's README does:

```sh
mkdir ltx-2.5-full && ln -s Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers/* ltx-2.5-full/
rm ltx-2.5-full/transformer ltx-2.5-full/transformer_full
ln -s Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers/transformer_full ltx-2.5-full/transformer
rad-convert ltx-2.5-full --recipe ltx-2.5-fp8.recipe -o ltx-2.5-fp8.rad \
    --set scheduler.use_dynamic_shifting=1 --set scheduler.shift_terminal=0.1
```

# Qwen-Image-Lightning

Qwen-Image-Lightning provides distilled LoRA weights for Qwen-Image,
enabling image generation with fewer inference steps.

**[Create Online — LightX2V Studio](https://x2v.light-ai.top/)**
· **[GitHub — Qwen-Image-Lightning](https://github.com/ModelTC/Qwen-Image-Lightning/)**
· **[GitHub — LightX2V Framework](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V)**

## Method 1: LightX2V Studio — Online Image Creation

[**LightX2V Studio**](https://x2v.light-ai.top/) is an online AI avatar
and multimodal content production platform built on the LightX2V video
generation inference framework. With AI avatar video creation at its
core, it supports video, image, and audio creation, plus workflow
orchestration and reuse.

Studio supports **text-to-image** and **image-to-image** creation
directly in your browser, without local installation or GPU setup.

### Quick Start

1. Open [LightX2V Studio](https://x2v.light-ai.top/), sign in, and
   choose text-to-image or image-to-image.
2. Enter a prompt, upload an image if required, and configure settings.
3. Review the credit cost, submit, then preview and download the result.

### Current Online Model and LoRA

- **Model:** Qwen-Image-2512
- **LoRA:** Lightning 8-step V1.0, FP32
- **Source:** [lightx2v/Qwen-Image-2512-Lightning](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Qwen-Image-2512-Lightning)

> The online deployment differs from the original Qwen-Image setup
> shown below. Available models and versions may change over time.

[Open LightX2V Studio](https://x2v.light-ai.top/)
· [Pricing](https://x2v.light-ai.top/pricing)

## Method 2: Local Inference with Diffusers

For model versions, usage instructions, workflows, and evaluation
results, see the
[Qwen-Image-Lightning GitHub repository](https://github.com/ModelTC/Qwen-Image-Lightning/).

For inference and deployment with the LightX2V framework, see the
[LightX2V GitHub repository](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V).

The following example uses
`Qwen-Image-Lightning-8steps-V1.0.safetensors`.

use with diffusers 🧨:

make sure to install diffusers from `main` (`pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers.git`)
```
from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline, FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler
import torch 
import math

# From https://github.com/ModelTC/Qwen-Image-Lightning/blob/342260e8f5468d2f24d084ce04f55e101007118b/generate_with_diffusers.py#L82C9-L97C10
scheduler_config = {
    "base_image_seq_len": 256,
    "base_shift": math.log(3),  # We use shift=3 in distillation
    "invert_sigmas": False,
    "max_image_seq_len": 8192,
    "max_shift": math.log(3),  # We use shift=3 in distillation
    "num_train_timesteps": 1000,
    "shift": 1.0,
    "shift_terminal": None,  # set shift_terminal to None
    "stochastic_sampling": False,
    "time_shift_type": "exponential",
    "use_beta_sigmas": False,
    "use_dynamic_shifting": True,
    "use_exponential_sigmas": False,
    "use_karras_sigmas": False,
}
scheduler = FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler.from_config(scheduler_config)
pipe = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen-Image", scheduler=scheduler, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
).to("cuda")
pipe.load_lora_weights(
    "lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning", weight_name="Qwen-Image-Lightning-8steps-V1.0.safetensors"
)

prompt = "a tiny astronaut hatching from an egg on the moon, Ultra HD, 4K, cinematic composition."
negative_prompt = " "
image = pipe(
    prompt=prompt,
    negative_prompt=negative_prompt,
    width=1024,
    height=1024,
    num_inference_steps=8,
    true_cfg_scale=1.0,
    generator=torch.manual_seed(0),
).images[0]
image.save("qwen_fewsteps.png")
```

5.6B [FLUX.3 Image Klein model](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/337337621b8526e120f2275d250242f4a6bedd75).

## Checkpoints

| Folder | Linear bits | Effective DiT bpw | Safetensors GB | BF16-relative NMSE ↓ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [3bit](3bit) | 3 | 3.647574 | 2.530172 | 0.0065190011 |
| [4bit](4bit) | 4 | 4.598320 | 3.189595 | 0.0016975493 |
| [5bit](5bit) | 5 | 5.549066 | 3.849018 | 0.0004679566 |

Each folder includes 258 quantized block Linear layers, one retained high-precision
tensor file, transformer config, checksummed `quantization.json`, license and notice.
Effective bpw includes retained high-precision tensors and quantization scales.
Sizes are decimal GB including publication headers. Text encoder, VAE and prompt
upsampler (PUP) are fetched separately; they are not quantized in this release.
The DiT/text encoder compute in BF16; the VAE uses FP32. EXL3 weights are restored
in bounded workspaces for matrix multiplication, without expanding the whole DiT.

These are custom checkpoints for the [EXL3 engine](https://github.com/jyohukuchan/rocm_exl3_forme/tree/0d879e7a7b6aadd3c08508240ade6db87332bafe),
not standard Diffusers `from_pretrained()` folders. Hugging Face hosted inference
is not configured. The source is the distilled Klein model, not a Base model;
the official schedule is **16 flow-map steps, shift 6.93**, with `target_timestep`.
Output is RGB.

## Inference

Use Python 3.12, a compatible ROCm PyTorch installation/toolchain and a built
native EXL3 extension. Validated GPUs are a single Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201)
and a single Radeon PRO V620 (gfx1030). CUDA and other GPUs have not been validated
with this release. Measured environment: PyTorch 2.12.0+rocm7.2, HIP compiler
7.14.60850, Transformers 5.17.0, Accelerate 1.15.0, safetensors 0.8.0, and Diffusers
commit `b800f828f3951c4d206e154411bcbfa693cd322e`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jyohukuchan/rocm_exl3_forme.git
cd rocm_exl3_forme
git checkout 0d879e7a7b6aadd3c08508240ade6db87332bafe

# Install compatible ROCm torch first and point ROCM_PATH at the SDK.
# Use gfx1030 for V620; gfx1201 for R9700.
EXL3_BACKEND=rocm PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1201 MAX_JOBS=8 \
  python -m pip install --no-build-isolation '.[diffusion]'
python -m pip install 'huggingface-hub==1.31.0' 'safetensors==0.8.0'
python -c 'import exllamav3_ext'
```

See [build requirements](https://github.com/jyohukuchan/rocm_exl3_forme/blob/0d879e7a7b6aadd3c08508240ade6db87332bafe/README.md#requirements)
and the [tested environment](r9700-environment.json). Validation reused existing
compiled GPU extensions, with binary hashes recorded in the environment files;
their original build commits are unknown. A clean rebuild of those exact binaries
was not demonstrated. Do not rely on automatic CUDA-style JIT compilation on ROCm.

Accept the upstream model's access conditions on Hugging Face and authenticate
with `hf auth login` as needed. Download the pinned text encoder/VAE without
downloading the original dense DiT:

```bash
python rocm_tools/flux3.py download --components-only --output models/flux3-components
```

# Flux.3-Image-Klein · MFlux Q4

This is a **Q4** **MFlux** version of [**flux-3-image-klein**](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein).

[**MFlux**](https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux) runs the latest state-of-the-art generative image models locally on your Mac in native MLX. MFlux is open source and free.

> [!NOTE]
> Community conversion by [MFlux-Community](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community) -- not an official release from the original model's authors. The original model's license applies unchanged, see [License](#license).

### MFlux versions of flux-3-image-klein
|   QUANT   | GB  | Repo |
| :--: | :-: | --- |
| BF16 | 18.5 | [mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-bf16](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-bf16) |
| Q8 | 9.9 | [mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q8](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q8) |
| Q6 | 7.6 | [mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q6](https://huggingface.co/mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q6) |
| Q5 | -- | -- |
| **Q4** | 5.3 | this repo |
| Q3 | -- | -- |

Converted with MFlux 0.23.0 on 2026-10-19.

Standard MFlux quantization uses MLX affine quantization (4-bit) across the text encoder, transformer and VAE. The quantization level is stored in the weights, so no `--quantize` flag is needed.

## Usage

**Install MFlux**
```bash
uv tool install --upgrade mflux
```

**Generate an image using flux-3-image-klein Q4:**
```bash
mflux-generate-flux3 \
  --model mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q4 \
  --base-model flux3-image-klein \
  --prompt "A puffin standing on a cliff" \
  --width 1024 \
  --height 1024 \
  --seed 42 \
  --output image.png
```

The weights are downloaded from this repo on first use. To keep a local copy instead:
```bash
hf download mflux-community/flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q4 --local-dir ./flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q4
```
then pass `--model ./flux-3-image-klein-mflux-q4`.

# FLUX 3 Image Klein — Q4_K_M GGUF

Community quantization of the distilled [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) transformer (5.6B). The BF16 Comfy checkpoint was converted with [molbal/ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/molbal/ComfyUI-GGUF) to architecture `flux3`, file type `MOSTLY_Q4_K_M`.

This is a modified derivative. It is not an official Black Forest Labs product.

| File | Quant | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flux3_image_klein-Q4_K_M.gguf` | Q4_K_M | 2.91 GB |

270 weight tensors are Q4_K. 87 small tensors stay F32. `emb_in.image.weight` and `emb_in.image_cond.weight` stay BF16 because their inner dimension is below the 256-value quant block.

Use an up-to-date ComfyUI build with FLUX 3 support and the [molbal ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/molbal/ComfyUI-GGUF) loader (`UnetLoaderGGUF`). This file is only the diffusion transformer.

# SeedVR2 1.4B MLX Q4

Unofficial MLX affine 4-bit / group-32 conversion of
[lvladikov/SeedVR2-1.4B](https://huggingface.co/lvladikov/SeedVR2-1.4B), a community
six-block distillation of ByteDance SeedVR2 7B. This is a complete still-image
upscaling package: Q4 transformer, unmodified FP16 VAE, and fixed positive text
embeddings. No text encoder is required. This checkpoint requires the six-block,
3072-wide architecture with normal GELU MLPs; a standard SeedVR2 3B loader cannot
load it. Quantization changes the model's predictions; sample comparisons and
measured results are in validation.json and the examples directory.

Native Swift/MLX inference and the macOS model selector are available in
[zimageapp/zimage](https://github.com/zimageapp/zimage), on the seedvr2 branch:

```sh
swift build -c release --product ZImageCLI
.build/release/ZImageCLI seedvr2 --model-path /path/to/package \
  --input input.png --output output.png --resolution 2x --steps 1 \
  --tile-size 512 --tile-overlap 64 --seed 42
```

Use one step, without approximate prediction reuse. The VAE uses overlapping
tiles for larger images; the transformer attends over the whole latent image.
Peak memory therefore grows with output resolution. Supported app scales are
2x and 4x. The 3B model remains available separately.

The original Apache-2.0 license applies. Credit to ByteDance Seed and lvladikov;
this derivative is not an official release from either author. conversion.json
records the pinned upstream revision, source hashes, and quantization details;
package-manifest.json records the distributed file hashes.

# LTX-2.5 Distilled — complete base SDNQ pipeline

**Complete base video/audio checkpoint; GPU generation and output quality are not yet validated.**
The repository name retains `Transformer` for existing links, but the main revision
now contains the complete single-stage distilled/convolutional-VAE pipeline.
No additional model repositories are needed for this base graph after download.

Полный базовый комплект для генерации видео со звуком из одного репозитория.
Квантован **только трансформер**; остальные компоненты скопированы из закреплённого
официального checkpoint без повторного квантования. Генерация на GPU пока не проверена.

## Weight inventory

- Transformer: SDNQ dynamic INT8 setting, 20 shards, 19,516,366,360 bytes.
- Text encoder (Gemma4Unified), connectors, video VAE, audio VAE and vocoder:
  original floating-point weights from the official Diffusers snapshot.
- Matching tokenizer, scheduler and component configurations are included.
- All weights combined: **51,597,450,102 bytes** (51.60 GB / 48.05 GiB).
- `bundle_manifest.json` and `SHA256SUMS` record exact source files and hashes.

The optional native prompt enhancer, duration predictor, diffusion decoder,
upscalers, SFT transformer and LoRAs are not included or required for this base
single-stage pipeline. Their disabled entries are explicit in `model_index.json`.
This is not a mirror of every optional official recipe.

## Quantization and compatibility

Transformer conversion used adapted SDNQ 0.2.8+ai.manager.1, Diffusers
`d42ebf9c6e0b46103b74283f5324357a67acaa04`, Torch 2.11.0+cu129.
Dynamic `weights_dtype=int8`, group_size=0, FP32 dequantization; no SVD/Hadamard,
no convolution/embedding quantization, quantized matmul disabled. Packed storage
may vary per layer; this does not claim every tensor is INT8 or native INT8 compute.
See `ai_manager_quantization.json` and `quantize_ltx25_transformer.py`.

Requires an SDNQ-enabled Diffusers runtime with LTX-2.5 support and Transformers
providing `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (older releases cannot import
this pipeline). AI Server Manager's LTX adaptation supplies hardware placement
and distilled scheduling. No automatic package installation is performed here.
CMP50 uses FP16, CMP170 can use BF16; CPU offload or multiple GPUs may be needed.
Disk size is not peak inference RAM/VRAM. No one-card fit or speed claim is made.

Structural checks: pinned source file sizes and SHA-256 values; all local
safetensors shard headers and indexed tensor names; complete component graph.
The earlier tiny CPU/CUDA transformer quantize-save-reload smoke passed.
**Full-model video/audio inference, quality and performance tests remain pending.**

## Sources, modifications and terms

Original transformer: [Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5),
revision `49b093a39c19169a8a81721dcc541e07e945232f`; the original BF16 file is retained
on the preparation host. The modified transformer uses Diffusers naming, including
the 12 prompt AdaLN renames, dynamic quantization and sharded serialization.
All other pipeline weights/configs are unmodified from
[Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers),
revision `da0b690960026eab794b8ceaf841233cf7064478`. `model_index.json` is modified only for the repository
identity and disabled optional components. This was not a fine-tuning run.

LTX weights and derivatives remain under the **LTX-2.x Community License**,
including Attachment A and the Acceptable Use Policy. See LICENSE,
ACCEPTABLE_USE_POLICY.pdf and NOTICE.md. Commercial revenue thresholds,

# ltx-2.5-distilled-lora-450-reduced-ceil96

Rank-reduced (`fro90_ceil96`) distillation LoRA for few-step ("turbo") sampling on
GPUs where the full 8.9 GB rank-450 file does not fit next to the model.

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | [`pyros-vault/ltx-2.5-distilled-lora-450-reduced`](https://huggingface.co/pyros-vault/ltx-2.5-distilled-lora-450-reduced) |
| Recipe | fro90_ceil96 |
| Modules | 1660 |
| Rank | 256 -> 77.6 mean (ceiling 96) |
| Ceiling-capped modules | 69% |
| Median kept Frobenius energy | 0.763 |
| 5th percentile / worst | 0.532 / 0.451 |
| File size | 1.67 TB |

Per module the delta `B @ A` is truncated by factored SVD (QR of both factors +
core SVD - the optimal rank-k approximation), singular values kept until
**90% Frobenius energy**, capped at **rank 96**, with a small
condition safeguard. Same key format as the source, drop-in wherever the
original loads. Typical usage: weight ~0.8 with the official 8-step schedule.

Numbers are copied verbatim from `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-lora-450-bf16_fro90_ceil96_report.json` (see that file for the
per-module breakdown).

# LTX-2.5 22B Alpha-Gen — fp8, LoRA fused

A single-file build of the LTX-2.5 22B distilled transformer with the [IC-LoRA Alpha-Gen 0.9](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Alpha-Gen) fused in and the large Linear layers stored as fp8. It is made for alpha matting from a reference video, as used by the **LTX Alpha** matting model in the Sammie-Roto 2 panda fork ([lukaszomasta/Sammie-Roto-Panda](https://github.com/lukaszomasta/Sammie-Roto-Panda)).

It saves you building this yourself, which needs about 65 GB of gated downloads (bf16 transformer, LoRA and the Gemma 4 text encoder), about 32 GB of RAM and two build steps.

> **Not an official Lightricks release.** It is a modified Derivative of LTX-2.x, distributed under the [LTX-2.x Community License](LICENSE-2_x). Organizations with annual revenue of USD 10M or more need a paid license from Lightricks.

## Files

| File | Size | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-alpha-gen-0.9-fp8-fused.safetensors` | 21.9 GiB | Transformer with the Alpha-Gen LoRA fused in, fp8 Linears |
| `empty_prompt_embeddings.safetensors` | 12 MB | The empty text prompt, pre-encoded, so the 24 GiB Gemma 4 text encoder is never needed |
| `LICENSE-2_x` | | The LTX-2.x Community License Agreement, with Attachment A |
| `tools/` | | The scripts that built both files, to reproduce or audit them |
| `SHA256SUMS` | | Checksums: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` |

You also need `ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors` and `ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors` from [Lightricks/LTX-2.5](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5). They are not modified, so they are not mirrored here.

## Modifications (LTX-2.x Community License, Section 3.3)

These files were changed from Lightricks' originals as follows:

- **Transformer.** Built from `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-bf16.safetensors` and `ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-alpha-gen-0.9.safetensors` with `tools/build_ltx_fp8_fused.py`:
  - All 480 LoRA deltas, `(B × 1.0) @ A`, were added to the base weights in fp32.
  - The 2,592 weights and biases that LTX-2's own `fp8_cast` policy converts at load time (`transformer_blocks.*` `to_q`, `to_k`, `to_v`, `to_out.0`, `ff.net.0.proj`, `ff.net.2`) are stored as `float8_e4m3fn` (a plain cast, no scales). No value exceeded the fp8 range.
  - Every other tensor, every key name and the original checkpoint metadata (model config and license) are unchanged. The build is recorded in the `ltx_alpha_fused` metadata key.
- **Embedding.** `empty_prompt_embeddings.safetensors` is the output of LTX-2.5's prompt encoder (`gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-bf16.safetensors` plus the transformer's embeddings connector) for the empty prompt `""`. It was made with `tools/encode_ltx_empty_prompt.py`.
- **Code.** Built with [LTX-2](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2) at commit `be6d6d0` (v1.4.2 + 2 commits).

## Quality

Measured against the unfused bf16 transformer + LoRA (with LTX-2's runtime fp8 cast), on a 25-frame clip at 576p:

- Mean absolute matte difference: 0.5–0.7 / 255; 99th percentile: 7–8 / 255.
- Soft edge pixels: 2.7 / 255 on average.
- Frame-to-frame stability, including across batch crossfades: unchanged.

Rounding happens once instead of twice: at runtime LTX-2 fp8-casts first, then fuses the LoRA and rounds again.

**With Sammie-Roto (panda fork).** Put both `.safetensors` files and the two VAEs in `checkpoints/ltx_alpha/`, then choose **LTX Alpha** on the Matting tab. Sammie finds the fused file automatically.

# MiniMax-H3 T2VA Prompt Rewriter LoRA

[![LightX2V](https://img.shields.io/badge/Inference-LightX2V-ff6b35)](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V)
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/ModelTC/LightX2V?style=social)](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V)
[![MiniMax-H3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Base%20Generator-MiniMax--H3-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)

An open, local prompt rewriter for **text-to-audio-video (T2VA)** generation with
[MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3), fine-tuned as a LoRA
adapter on top of [Qwen3.6-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B).

> **Generate the final audio-video with
> [LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V).** LightX2V provides optimized local
> MiniMax-H3 inference, including T2AV and other H3 tasks, memory offloading, tensor and
> sequence parallelism, quantized checkpoints, optimized attention/RMSNorm/RoPE kernels,
> and feature caching. If this project is useful, please consider giving
> **[ModelTC/LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V) a star**.

The complete local workflow is:

```text
Short prompt ──► this Prompt Rewriter LoRA ──► structured H3 prompt
                                                        │
Official MiniMax-H3 weights ──► LightX2V inference ◄─────┘
                                      │
                                      ▼
                          synchronized video + audio
```

The [official MiniMax-H3 repository](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3)
provides the upstream model weights. **LightX2V is the recommended inference entry
point for the workflow documented here.**

## What it does

The adapter turns a short prompt plus the requested aspect ratio and duration into a
structured audio-video description:

```text
Original prompt + aspect ratio + duration
                    │
                    ▼
          Qwen3.6-27B + this LoRA
                    │
                    ▼
integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] ...
overall_soundscape: ...
non_diegetic_music: ...
```

The rewritten prompt expands shot structure, timing, composition, camera motion,
physical action, continuity, synchronized diegetic sound, and non-diegetic music while
preserving the original intent.

| Component | Purpose | Model |
|---|---|---|
| Inference framework | Runs MiniMax-H3 locally and generates the final synchronized video and audio | **[ModelTC/LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V)** |
| Generator weights | Upstream MiniMax-H3 model weights consumed by LightX2V | [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) |
| Base language model | General instruction-following backbone | [Qwen3.6-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B) |
| LoRA adapter | H3-oriented T2VA prompt rewriting | [lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-LoRA](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-LoRA) |

## Status and roadmap

- [x] T2VA prompt rewriting
- [ ] First/last-frame-to-audio-video (FL2VA) prompt rewriting
- [ ] Reference-to-audio-video (Ref2VA) prompt rewriting

## Installation

Clone this repository and install the inference dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-LoRA
cd MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-LoRA
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

The 27B base model is not included in this adapter repository and will be downloaded
from Hugging Face on first use. Ensure that the machine has enough GPU/CPU memory for
Qwen3.6-27B. `device_map="auto"` is used to distribute the model over available devices.

## Rewrite one prompt

```bash
python infer.py \
  --prompt "Epic space-opera teaser: a captain watches the last fleet jump away, leaving her alone." \
  --duration 10 \
  --resolution 16:9 \
  --greedy
```

Local paths are supported as well:

```bash
python infer.py \
  --base-model /path/to/Qwen3.6-27B \
  --adapter /path/to/MiniMax-H3-Prompt-Rewriter-LoRA \
  --prompt "A red fox walks through a snowy forest at dawn." \
  --duration 15 \
  --resolution 21:9 \
  --output rewritten_prompt.json
```

Use `--output result.txt` for plain text or a `.json` path for a record containing
the original prompt, conditions, model IDs, and rewritten prompt.

To run the base-model baseline without the LoRA:

```bash
python infer.py \
  --base-only \
  --prompt "A red fox walks through a snowy forest at dawn." \
  --duration 15 \
  --resolution 21:9 \
  --greedy
```

For fair comparisons, use the same decoding mode and seed for every rewriter. Greedy
decoding is the simplest deterministic setting; sampling is enabled when `--greedy`
is omitted.

# Wan2.1-T2V-14B-CausVid

## Overview

Wan2.1-T2V-14B-CausVid is an advanced text-to-video generation model built upon the Wan2.1-T2V-14B foundation, enhanced with CausVid's causal diffusion approach. This integration enables the model to generate high-quality, temporally consistent videos from text prompts. By leveraging causal diffusion, our model excels at producing coherent long-form videos through an autoregressive generation process, addressing the temporal consistency limitations commonly found in traditional diffusion models. This approach also allows the model to generate videos with significantly fewer inference steps, substantially reducing video generation time while maintaining high quality outputs.

## Training

Our training code is modified based on the [CausVid](https://github.com/tianweiy/CausVid) repository. We extended support for the Wan2.1-14B-T2V model and performed a 9-step distillation process. For training data, we utilized the OpenSora dataset, selecting approximately 15,000 prompt-video pairs with 81 frames each. The modified code is available at [CausVid-Plus](https://github.com/GoatWu/CausVid-Plus).

## Inference (Legacy)

This checkpoint was developed for an earlier LightX2V CausVid integration. The current LightX2V main branch no longer includes the original CausVid inference scripts and configuration.

For historical reference, the following files are preserved at commit `79842681ae93ff2bff3b72e7fa7316b381050a09`:

## Overview Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Moe-Distill-Lightx2v is an advanced image-to-video generation model built upon the Wan2.2-I2V-A14B foundation. This approach allows the model to generate videos with significantly fewer inference steps (4 steps, 2 steps for high noise and 2 steps for low noise) and without classifier-free guidance, substantially reducing video generation time while maintaining high quality outputs. This version has the following features: 1. We found that the training challenge of Wan2.2 lies in high noise; therefore, we have focused on the two-step training for the high-noise model. Compared with the previous version, we have adopted several new strategies, which have improved the consistency and dynamics of the model. 2. We found that the low-noise model can achieve good results by directly using the LoRA from Wan2.1; thus, the low-noise model still adopts the old Wan2.1 LoRA. ## Inference Our inference framework utilizes [lightx2v](https://github.com/ModelTC/lightx2v), a highly efficient inference engine that supports multiple models. This framework significantly accelerates the video generation process while maintaining high quality output. Edit the [I2V launch script](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/blob/main/scripts/wan22/inference/distill/run_wan22_moe_i2v_distill.sh): set `lightx2v_path`, `model_path`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, and the input/output paths. For the full distilled checkpoints in this repository, use `configs/distill/wan22/wan_moe_i2v_distill_model.json`. Set `high_noise_original_ckpt` and `low_noise_original_ckpt` to the local files downloaded from `distill_models/high_noise_model/` and `distill_models/low_noise_model/`, respectively. Keep `model_path` pointed at the complete Wan2.2-I2V-A14B base model directory. Run from the LightX2V repository root: ```bash bash scripts/wan22/inference/distill/run_wan22_moe_i2v_distill.sh ``` We recommend using the **Euler scheduler** (default in lightx2v) with the following settings: - `shift=5.0` - `guidance_scale=1.0 (i.e., without CFG)` ## License Agreement The models in this repository are licensed under the Apache 2.0 License. Offline LoRA Merging (Recommended ⭐) **Offline LoRA merging provides best performance and supports quantization simultaneously.** #### 1.1 Download LoRA Models ```bash # Download both LoRAs (high noise and low noise) # Note: xxx represents version number, please check HuggingFace for actual filename huggingface-cli download lightx2v/Wan2.2-Distill-Loras \ wan2.2_i2v_A14b_high_noise_lora_rank64_lightx2v_4step_xxx.safetensors \ wan2.2_i2v_A14b_low_noise_lora_rank64_lightx2v_4step_xxx.safetensors \ --local-dir ./loras/ ``` #### 1.2 Merge LoRA (Basic Merging) **Merge LoRA:** ```bash cd LightX2V/tools/convert # For directory-based base model: --source /path/to/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B/high_noise_model/ python converter.py \ --source ./models/Wan2.2-Official-Models/wan2.2_i2v_A14b_high_noise_lightx2v.safetensors \ --output /path/to/output/ \ --output_ext .safetensors \ --output_name wan2.2_i2v_A14b_high_noise_lightx2v_4step \ --model_type wan_dit \ --lora_path /path/to/loras/wan2.2_i2v_A14b_high_noise_lora_rank64_lightx2v_4step_xxx.safetensors \ --lora_strength 1.0 \ --single_file # For directory-based base model: --source /path/to/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B/low_noise_model/ python converter.py \ --source ./models/Wan2.2-Official-Models/wan2.2_i2v_A14b_low_noise_lightx2v.safetensors \ --output /path/to/output/ \ --out
